title: consolidated: filter NON_TASK_LABELS from stampless interactive scan/recovery (shared-constants.sh Option B)
body:
_Supersedes #20021 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Extract a shared `NON_TASK_LABELS` constant into `shared-constants.sh` and a `_filter_non_task_issues` jq helper, then apply that helper at all three query sites that enumerate `origin:interactive` + self-assigned issues:

1. `pulse-prefetch.sh:934` (dispatch path — already correct, migrate to shared helper)
2. `interactive-session-helper.sh:237-279` `_isc_list_stampless_interactive_claims` (Site A — scan-stale Phase 1a)
3. `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:159-216` `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` (Site B — 24h autonomous unassign)

Add a regression test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stampless-non-task-filter.sh`.

## Why

`scan-stale` Phase 1a and the 24h `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` recovery path both identify stampless interactive claims by querying for:

```bash
gh issue list --repo <slug> --assignee <user> --label origin:interactive --state open
```

Neither applies a negative filter for `routine-tracking` or other "non-task" labels.

Routine-tracking issues are created by `init-routines-helper.sh:770-778` during `/routine` setup. They receive `origin:interactive` (interactive session context), self-assigned to the routine owner (intentional ownership signal), and no claim stamp (they are execution dashboards, not work claims). They tick every positive box for "stampless interactive claim" while being explicitly non-tasks.

Observed real-world impact:

1. **False positive in scan-stale Phase 1a** — session start surfaced a routine-tracking issue alongside a legitimate dead claim, prompting the agent to recommend `gh issue edit --remove-assignee` for the routine owner.
2. **Latent auto-damage** — the 24h `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` path uses the same unfiltered query and will execute `gh issue edit --remove-assignee` after `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD`. The routine itself keeps running (cron-driven via `routine-log-helper.sh`), but the ownership signal on the dashboard is silently stripped.

`pulse-prefetch.sh:934` (the dispatch path) already correctly excludes `routine-tracking`. This bug is label-filter drift between three sites that share the same intent. The same three-site duplication is what allowed the bug to hide in the first place.

## How

**Files to modify:**

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — add `NON_TASK_LABELS` array alongside `ISSUE_STATUS_LABELS` and `ORIGIN_LABELS`. Seed from `pulse-prefetch.sh:934`: `supervisor`, `contributor`, `persistent`, `quality-review`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `routine-tracking`, `on hold`, `blocked`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:237-279` `_isc_list_stampless_interactive_claims` — change `--json number,updatedAt` → `--json number,updatedAt,labels`, pipe `$json` through the new `_filter_non_task_issues` helper before the `updatedAt` scan.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:159-216` `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` — same: add `labels` to `--json` field list, apply `_filter_non_task_issues` before the `updatedAt` cutoff.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh:934` — migrate inline jq filter to `_filter_non_task_issues` (shared helper). Optional in same PR; prevents future three-site drift.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-stampless-non-task-filter.sh` — regression test (see Acceptance Criteria).

**Reference pattern:**

The existing jq idiom at `pulse-prefetch.sh:934` is the precedent:

```bash
filtered_json=$(echo "$issue_json" | jq '[.[]
    | select(.labels | map(.name)
    | (index("supervisor") or index("contributor") or index("persistent")
       or index("quality-review") or index("needs-maintainer-review")
       or index("routine-tracking") or index("on hold") or index("blocked"))
    | not)]')
```

The new shared helper wraps this idiom so all three sites reference one definition. Model on `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` patterns for `ISSUE_STATUS_LABELS` and `ORIGIN_LABELS`.

**Mandatory scope constraint (per @marcusquinn comment 2):** All three sites must migrate to the shared helper in the same PR. Leaving any site un-migrated recreates the original drift between call sites.

**Future extension point (do NOT build in this PR):** A `~/.aidevops/configs/non-task-labels-extra.txt` for repo-local custom non-task labels follows the `privacy-guard-extra-slugs.txt` pattern. Not in scope — one-line note in the brief is sufficient.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `shared-constants.sh` exports `NON_TASK_LABELS` containing at minimum: `supervisor`, `contributor`, `persistent`, `quality-review`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `routine-tracking`, `on hold`, `blocked`
- [ ] `_isc_list_stampless_interactive_claims` requests `labels` in its `--json` call and filters out issues carrying any `NON_TASK_LABELS` member before reporting Phase 1a candidates
- [ ] `_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive` requests `labels` in its `--json` call and skips issues carrying any `NON_TASK_LABELS` member before the 24h unassign execution
- [ ] `pulse-prefetch.sh:934` inline jq filter replaced by the new shared helper (or same-PR follow-up)
- [ ] Regression test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stampless-non-task-filter.sh` mocks `gh issue list` to return a mixed fixture (one real stampless interactive claim + one routine-tracking + one supervisor + one needs-maintainer-review); asserts both Site A (`_isc_list_stampless_interactive_claims`) and Site B (`_normalize_unassign_stampless_interactive`) emit only the real claim
- [ ] Manual verification on a repo with an active routine: `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale` produces no routine-tracking issue under Phase 1a
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all modified shell files

## Context & Decisions

**Root cause attribution:** The bug was introduced by t2148 (GH#19384/GH#19380) which added stampless-interactive detection with label predicate `origin:interactive` only. The brief for t2148 framed the target as "interactive session filed an issue and walked away without claiming" — routine-tracking issues share that exact shape. The `routine-tracking` label was not added to the query predicate at either new site, while the existing dispatch site (`pulse-prefetch.sh:934`) already had it.

**Option A vs Option B (per @marcusquinn review):** Option A (inline jq at the two new sites only) was rejected in favour of Option B (shared `NON_TASK_LABELS` constant + helper). Rationale: the three-site duplication is structurally what allowed this bug to hide; Option A fixes the symptom but does not prevent the next drift. Option B's incremental cost (one shared array + one helper) is trivial compared to the structural benefit.

**Multi-user safety (per @marcusquinn comment 2):** The fix is multi-user safe by construction. Both query sites scope by `--assignee "$runner_user"`. The `NON_TASK_LABELS` filter is framework-defined, not user-preference. Alice's pulse cannot strip Bob's routine assignment because the query is already scoped `--assignee alice`. The filter does not change cross-user isolation — only what counts as a stampless claim within the scoped set.

**Blast radius note (per @marcusquinn review):** `shared-constants.sh` is sourced by ~339 framework scripts. Any regression there has wide blast radius. For this reason `tier:standard` is recommended over `tier:simple` even though the diff is small.

**Related work:** #20012 (t2414) auto-releases Phase 1 dead stamps but does not touch Phase 1a (stampless) or the label-filter gap. This fix is independent.

## Contributors

@marcusquinn

title: t2426: conflict-feedback template — embed cherry-pick-first worker guidance
body:
## Problem

When `pulse-merge.sh` closes a PR for merge conflicts and routes a conflict-feedback comment back to the linked issue, the generated worker guidance reads:

1. Check out a fresh branch from `origin/main` (do NOT reuse the old PR's branch)
2. Re-implement the changes on top of the current `main`
3. The files listed above were modified by both this PR and concurrent merges — review `main` to understand what changed

"Re-implement" implies a full rewrite from scratch. In practice, the prior worker's commit is often correct-but-stale and cherry-picking it onto a fresh branch off current `main` is ~10x cheaper than rewriting. The cherry-pick itself reveals the actual semantic conflict surface to focus on, rather than making the worker re-derive it by eye.

**Evidence:** t2409 (PR #20039 closed, PR #20049 merged) — the re-implementation session saved ~20 minutes by cherry-picking the prior worker's commit `a8f3d59c3` onto a fresh branch rather than rewriting, then verifying tests pass. Memory stored: `mem_20260420023455_fa8089af`.

**Frequency:** 14 conflict-feedback issues in the last 5 days (~3/day). Token savings compound quickly.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh:267-285` — the `feedback_section` heredoc in the conflict-feedback case. Replace the 3-step guidance with the cherry-pick-first decision tree. Also fetch `pr_head_sha` from the closed PR so it can be interpolated into the template.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/prompts/build.txt:90-102` — the "Pre-implementation discovery (t2046 — MANDATORY before any non-trivial code change)" section. Add ONE bullet noting the cherry-pick-first pattern for `source:conflict-feedback` reroutes. Keep it short (system prompt budget).

### Reference pattern

- Existing template structure in `pulse-merge-feedback.sh` (the `feedback_section="## ..."` heredoc pattern). Follow the same heredoc + variable interpolation style.
- For the `pr_head_sha` fetch, `gh api repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/:num --jq '.head.sha'` — the commit remains reachable after PR close (not GC'd for at least 30 days).

### New guidance text (Change 1)

Replace `pulse-merge-feedback.sh:279-283` with:

```markdown
### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `${pr_head_sha}`. Before re-implementing:

1. **Try cherry-pick first** — cheap and catches the common case where `main` moved but the prior implementation was correct:

       git fetch origin pull/${pr_number}/head:recovered-${pr_number}
       git cherry-pick ${pr_head_sha}
       # run tests — if clean and CI passes, proceed to PR

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **Only rewrite from scratch** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check the prior PR's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `main`.
```

### New bullet (Change 3)

Add after the existing bullets at `prompts/build.txt:102` (before "Treat the codebase as a living system..."):

```
- For `source:conflict-feedback` reroutes, cherry-pick-first before rewriting. The prior PR's head commit is usually reachable (`gh api repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/:num --jq '.head.sha'`), and cherry-pick reveals the actual conflict surface. Rewriting from scratch is only correct when the prior approach was rejected in review, not when it simply went stale.
```

### Verification

1. ShellCheck clean on `pulse-merge-feedback.sh`:

       shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh

2. Template content verification — the conflict-feedback output should include:
   - `recovered-` and `cherry-pick` in the guidance text
   - `${pr_head_sha}` (or the rendered SHA) surfacing in the rendered comment
   - Original "do NOT reuse the old PR's branch" wording preserved

3. Live smoke test (manual):
   - Trigger `pulse-merge.sh` on a test conflict PR in a scratch repo OR
   - Extract the `feedback_section` variable and verify its rendered shape against the template above.

## Acceptance criteria

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh` conflict-feedback template leads with cherry-pick guidance, preserves `do NOT reuse the old branch` warning, interpolates `pr_head_sha`.
- `.agents/prompts/build.txt` has a single additional bullet under "Pre-implementation discovery" covering conflict-feedback reroutes.
- ShellCheck clean on modified shell script.
- No behaviour change to the CI-fix feedback path (lines ~165-170) — that's a separate scenario where rewrite IS appropriate.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20004 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20004

**Parent issue:** #20004 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2411: auto-admin-merge origin:interactive PRs from OWNER/MEMBER in pulse-merge.sh
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,pulse,origin:worker,tier:standard,framework,source:ci-feedback,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20004. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20004 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20004:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20004 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20004 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20004 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20004 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

- **Do NOT read #20004** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Problem

`pulse-merge.sh` currently auto-merges `origin:worker` PRs via `gh pr merge --squash --admin` at line 1255, but has NO auto-merge path for `origin:interactive` PRs. The only `origin:interactive` handling is at line 876-878: a STALENESS handover (applies `origin:worker-takeover` after 24h idle).

The framework rule documented in `AGENTS.md` ("PRs tagged `origin:interactive` from `OWNER`/`MEMBER` authors merge as soon as all required checks pass — typically 4-10 minutes") is ASPIRATIONAL, not implemented. Every `origin:interactive` PR from OWNER that passes checks sits indefinitely until someone runs `gh pr merge --admin` manually.

## Live evidence (2026-04-19)

- PR #19965 (`origin:interactive`, OWNER marcusquinn, all 32 required checks PASS, 0 failures, `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`) sat for ~90 minutes without auto-merge. Branch protection's `required_approving_review_count: 1` blocked native merge; no bot or pulse-level actor posted an approving review. Manual `gh pr merge 19965 --admin --squash --delete-branch` succeeded immediately.
- PR #19993 (successor to auto-closed #19983, same pattern) — currently awaiting same manual intervention.

## Impact

Every interactive session's PR needs a manual admin-merge step. At current cadence (~3-5 interactive PRs per working day), that's ~15-25 min/day of toil + context-switching cost. Compounds when session ends before checks finish — the PR strands overnight until next session.

More importantly: the pulse is supposed to close the loop on its own. When it doesn't, interactive sessions carry the cognitive load of "is my PR done yet? do I need to check-and-merge?" — which defeats the point of dispatching to a background system.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — this is the deterministic merge pass. Add a new eligible-PR scan branch for `origin:interactive` PRs, parallel to the existing `origin:worker` path. Criteria for auto-merge:
  1. Label `origin:interactive` present.
  2. PR author login matches a repo OWNER or MEMBER (use existing `_is_collaborator` helper — see `pulse-merge.sh:1272-1285`).
  3. All required status checks PASS or SKIPPED (mirror the logic at `pulse-merge.sh:751-800` that's already used for `origin:worker`).
  4. No `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review from a human reviewer (existing helper).
  5. PR is NOT draft.
  6. PR does NOT have the `hold-for-review` label (new label, document in the brief).
- **EDIT**: same file — when eligible, call the existing merge path at line 1255: `gh pr merge "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --squash --admin --delete-branch`. Respect the stacked-PR retargeting fix from t2412 (sister brief) — those land together or sequentially.
- **EDIT**: same file — emit a clear audit log line on auto-merge: `[pulse-merge] auto-merged origin:interactive PR #N (author=<login>, role=<role>)` to `$LOGFILE`.
- **EDIT**: `AGENTS.md` (user guide) under "Auto-merge timing" — upgrade the paragraph from aspirational to current: document the criteria (label + role + checks + no-changes-requested + not-draft + no hold-for-review).

### Reference pattern

- Existing `origin:worker` auto-merge path in `pulse-merge.sh` — copy the structure. The admin-merge call at line 1255 is already correct; the new code just needs to add `origin:interactive` PRs to the scan.
- `_is_collaborator` helper at `pulse-merge.sh:1272-1285` for role gating.

   - OWNER + `hold-for-review` label → no merge.
   - OWNER + draft PR → no merge.
   - OWNER + human CHANGES_REQUESTED → no merge.
2. Dogfood: file a test `origin:interactive` PR against a throwaway branch, label it, let the pulse cycle run, assert it merges within one pulse tick.

title: t2429: fix(full-loop-helper): merge command must fire _release_interactive_claim_on_merge (parity with pulse-merge.sh)
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` does NOT fire `_release_interactive_claim_on_merge` after a successful `gh pr merge`. That helper is only called from `pulse-merge.sh`. Result: interactive sessions that merge their own PR via `full-loop-helper.sh merge` leave a stale claim stamp in `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/` and a stale `status:in-review` label on the closed issue.

## Why

t2413 added auto-release on merge so that interactive ownership is cleaned up atomically with the merge. AGENTS.md states this as an operational guarantee: "PR merge is now automated (t2413): when pulse-merge.sh merges an origin:interactive PR with a Resolves #NNN link and a claim stamp exists, _release_interactive_claim_on_merge fires automatically." But the guarantee only holds for pulse-merge. Sessions using full-loop-helper (the canonical INTERACTIVE merge helper) get silently skipped, forcing manual `interactive-session-helper.sh release` or reliance on the next scan-stale cycle.

**Canonical failure:** Session completed t2422/PR#20054 at 2026-04-20 02:00:59Z via `full-loop-helper.sh merge --squash --admin`. The claim stamp `marcusquinn-aidevops-20028.json` persisted on disk and the `status:in-review` label persisted on issue #20028 until manual `interactive-session-helper.sh release 20028 marcusquinn/aidevops` at 02:01Z.

## How

1. Add a call to `_release_interactive_claim_on_merge <PR> <REPO>` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` cmd_merge(), immediately after a successful `gh pr merge` branch, guarded by same conditions as pulse-merge.sh.
2. The function lives in `pulse-merge.sh`. Preferred: EXTRACT `_release_interactive_claim_on_merge` into a new `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` sourced by both pulse-merge.sh and full-loop-helper.sh. Alternative: source pulse-merge.sh from full-loop-helper.sh (check for circular sourcing via shared-constants.sh first).
3. Guard with the same conditions pulse-merge.sh uses: PR has `origin:interactive` label AND `Resolves #NNN` in body AND a claim stamp exists. Non-interactive merges unaffected.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — in `cmd_merge()`, after gh pr merge success, call `_release_interactive_claim_on_merge "$pr_num" "$repo"`.
- REFERENCE: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — locate `_release_interactive_claim_on_merge` definition and its invocation site. Model on that pattern.
- NEW (preferred): `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` — house `_release_interactive_claim_on_merge` + future claim lifecycle helpers. Source from both pulse-merge.sh and full-loop-helper.sh.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-auto-release.sh` — regression test (see Acceptance).

## Acceptance

- After `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <slug>` on an `origin:interactive` PR with a `Resolves #NNN` link and an existing claim stamp at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/<slug>-<N>.json`, the stamp file is deleted AND the linked issue `status:in-review` label is removed (idempotently).
- Regression test covers: (a) stamp deleted on merge of origin:interactive PR, (b) no deletion on merge of origin:worker PR, (c) no deletion when `Resolves`/`Fixes`/`Closes` keyword absent, (d) idempotency on re-run.
- Existing `test-pulse-merge-interactive-release.sh` still passes (pulse-merge.sh path intact).
- AGENTS.md Git Workflow section updated: "PR merge auto-release (t2413)" bullet no longer pulse-merge-specific.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — one shared-lib extraction + one-line call-site insertion + regression test. Mirror existing pattern, no novel design.

## Session Origin

Discovered in t2422 interactive session merging PR #20054 via `full-loop-helper.sh merge --squash --admin`. Claim stamp `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/marcusquinn-aidevops-20028.json` remained after successful merge. `interactive-session-helper.sh release 20028 marcusquinn/aidevops` returned "not in status:in-review — no-op" but still deleted the stamp file (label was already auto-cleared by GitHub Resolves-keyword handler). The stamp was the only orphaned artefact.

title: t2430: fix(complexity-regression-helper): rewrite nesting-depth scanner (portable AWK or shfmt) to eliminate elif/prose/here-string false positives
body:
## What

`complexity-regression-helper.sh` (lines ~220–260) uses a naive AWK regex to detect max-nesting-depth per shell file: `/[[:space:]]*(if|for|while|until|case)[[:space:]]/` increments a GLOBAL counter, `/[[:space:]]*(fi|done|esac)[[:space:]]*$/` decrements. Four documented false-positive classes block legitimate refactors:

1. **`elif` matches `if`** — the leading `[[:space:]]*` can match zero characters, so `elif` contains a matching substring. Each elif increments without a matching decrement (only the terminal `fi` decrements once) → net inflation per elif chain.
2. **Prose containing bare keywords** — printf/echo/log strings like `"warn action for runner=%s"` contain ` for ` which matches the increment regex. Comment bodies and heredoc bodies with the same pattern trigger it too.
3. **`done <<<"$X"` not recognized as close** — the close regex requires `done` at EOL or followed by whitespace-to-EOL. `done <<<"..."`, `done | cmd`, `done > file` all have non-EOL trailing tokens → permanent +1 to the global counter for the rest of the file.
4. **Global counter never resets between functions** — so all false positives compound across the entire file. `headless-runtime-lib.sh` currently scans as depth=83, physically impossible (verified by manual inspection).

## Why

The scanner is both the PR CI gate (`code-quality.yml:502-508`) and the pre-push hook (`complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`). False positives:

- Actively penalize clean bash idioms (`done <<<X`, good log messages with natural prose)
- Block file-split refactors — see `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 for the `complexity-bump-ok` override flow that exists ENTIRELY because of these false positives
- Train workers to write awkward bash to avoid a broken linter instead of optimizing the linter
- Generate ratchet-debt that never pays down: PR #20054 baseline showed 292 files with "nesting >8"; a large uncertain fraction are false positives
- Canonical waste: t2422 session burned ~45min on two rewrites (`IFS=$'\\n'; for line in $rows; do ... done` and "warn action ON runner=" instead of "FOR runner=") to pass the scanner on clean code

Related closed issues (did NOT address the regex): t2159 #19459 (added per-function regression for FUNCTION_COMPLEXITY only), t2171 #19585 (extended per-function to nesting but kept the same AWK), t2228 umbrella #19734 (retrospective, no AWK fix).

## Root cause

AWK regex pattern matching is insufficient to parse bash lexical structure. Specifically:
- AWK has no notion of "is this inside a string literal, heredoc, or comment"
- AWK has no notion of "elif = else+if combined" (net 0, not +1)
- AWK has no notion of "done followed by redirect/pipe/subshell" as a valid close

Any regex-only solution will keep hitting edge cases. The systemic fix needs a real tokenizer.

## How — systemic fix

**Approach A (preferred): POSIX-AWK tokenizer.** Replace the scan pass with a state machine in POSIX awk that handles:
1. String-literal skipping (`"..."`, `'...'`, `$'...'`) — track quote state
2. Comment skipping (`# ...` to EOL)
3. Heredoc skipping — track `<<MARKER` / `<<-'MARKER'` opens, match close marker, suppress content
4. elif as no-op (both +1 and -1 inside the same iteration)
5. `done <<`, `done |`, `done >`, `done &`, `done ;` all count as close
6. Per-function reset (track function boundaries: `function NAME` / `NAME ()`)

Stays in POSIX awk: no `gensub`, no `FIELDWIDTHS`, no `asort`, no multi-char RS regex. Both BSD awk (macOS `/usr/bin/awk`) and gawk/mawk (Linux) must produce identical output on the same inputs.

**Approach B (fallback if A too complex):** Use `shfmt --tojson` (if installed) or `bash-language-server` to obtain a real bash AST. Iterate the AST for nesting depth. `shfmt` is a single Go binary, easy to provision in CI and locally via `brew install shfmt` / `apt install shfmt`. Check deployment cost vs. Approach A maintenance burden.

**Approach C (tactical minimum if A and B deferred):** Keep AWK but patch in priority order: (a) strip comments pre-scan, (b) strip string literals pre-scan, (c) treat `elif` as no-op, (d) recognize `done (<<|<|>|\\||&|;|$)` as close, (e) reset counter at `function` / `name ()` boundaries. Doesn't fix heredoc bodies but cuts 80%+ of false positives with minimal risk.

Architectural decision on A vs B vs C MUST be taken before implementation. This is why the task is tagged `#parent` and `tier:thinking`.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh:220-260` — replace inline AWK with a call to `scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.awk` (or `.py`/Go wrapper).
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml:502-508` — replace inline AWK with a call to the helper (single source of truth).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.awk` (or language-of-choice per approach) — tokenizer per Approach A/B/C.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` — fixtures for each false-positive class. Each fixture has known expected depth, verified by manual bash parser or `shfmt` cross-check.
- EDIT: `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 — note that the `complexity-bump-ok` override for nesting-depth is NO LONGER needed for per-function-stable splits after this fix.

## Portability

- Target: POSIX awk subset. Verify explicitly on both macOS BSD awk (`/usr/bin/awk` = nawk) AND Linux gawk/mawk.
- Test matrix in `test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh`: run `env AWK=/usr/bin/awk ...` and `env AWK=gawk ...` (+ mawk if available) with identical expected output for every fixture.
- Avoid external runtimes (Python, Go) UNLESS already in dev-deps (`shfmt` likely approved — check `aidevops.json` / `setup.sh` first).
- CI must test on both `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` matrix (code-quality.yml already does this for ShellCheck — mirror).

## Acceptance

- Scanner on `headless-runtime-lib.sh` reports depth <=12 (sanity: manual inspection shows real max ~5). Current: 83.
- Per-function reset: a file with 10 top-level functions, each max-depth 3, reports max=3 (not max=30).
- elif chain of 10 elifs + matching `fi`: net 0 (not +9).
- File containing only `echo "for all users, if it matches"` reports depth=0.
- `while read; do ...; done <<<"$rows"`: +1 enter, +1 exit = 1 (not stuck at +1 forever).
- Heredoc body containing `if`, `for`, `while` keywords reports 0 contribution.
- `test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` passes on macOS BSD awk AND Linux gawk/mawk (CI matrix both OSes).
- Baseline re-snapshot after fix: expect "nesting >8" count to drop from ~292 to a small number reflecting real deep control flow only.
- `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 updated to remove the `complexity-bump-ok` nesting-depth false-positive escape hatch.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — requires architectural judgment (A vs B vs C), POSIX-AWK subset verification, cross-OS portability testing, and re-baselining decisions. DO NOT auto-dispatch without A/B/C decision. This is a `#parent` task — decompose into sub-tasks after design phase.

## Session Origin

Discovered in t2422 session implementing PR #20054. Hit false-positive (4) (`done <<<"$rows"`) and (2) (prose `for` in printf message) within a single 300-line dispatch-claim refactor. Both required awkward rewrites to pass the pre-push hook. Three prior stored memories confirm same pattern in t2265, t2368 (large-file-split playbook), and unnamed prior session (83-depth headless-runtime-lib.sh). The `large-file-split.md` playbook documents the override flow; this task makes that section obsolete.

title: t2431: fix(tests): test harness silently broken after shared-gh-wrappers split (PR #20037) — source fails, exit 0, zero assertions
body:
## What

PR #20037 (GH#20018, merged 2026-04-20 00:25:49Z) extracted all `gh_*` wrappers (including `_gh_wrapper_auto_sig`) from `shared-constants.sh` into a new file `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. `shared-constants.sh:755` now does `source "${_SC_SELF%/*}/shared-gh-wrappers.sh"`. But `test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` (and ~20 other tests) copy only `shared-constants.sh` to their tmp dir and then source it. The source of `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` fails with:

```
tmp/shared-constants.sh: line 755: tmp/shared-gh-wrappers.sh: No such file or directory
```

The test continues and exits 0 because the source error is non-fatal and no assertion block runs. The test is **silently green** — a regression in the wrapper would not be caught.

Reproduced 2026-04-20:

```
$ bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh
=== _gh_wrapper_auto_sig tests (t2115) ===
/var/folders/.../tmp.XXX/shared-constants.sh: line 755: /var/folders/.../tmp.XXX/shared-gh-wrappers.sh: No such file or directory
exit=0
```

Zero PASS lines. Zero FAIL lines. Exit 0.

## Why

`_gh_wrapper_auto_sig` is the single enforcement point for signature footers on `gh_create_pr` and `gh_create_issue` (documented in `prompts/build.txt` §8 and AGENTS.md traceability rules). AGENTS.md states "every gh issue create, gh issue comment, and gh pr create body MUST end with the helper output". Without a working test:

- A future refactor of the wrapper could drop the auto-append silently
- Workers and interactive sessions would stop getting signature footers
- Audit trail (who/what/why) would degrade, breaking cost-budget aggregators (t2425 explicitly filters interactive footers from aggregators — depends on footer presence)
- Post-merge debugging loses telemetry

**Broader blast radius:** The same copy-constants-only pattern is used across ~20 test files. Full list:

```
tests/test-label-invariants.sh
tests/test-approval-wrappers-available.sh
tests/test-pre-commit-hook-duplicate-ids.sh
tests/test-repo-role-guard.sh
tests/test-fast-fail-age-out.sh
tests/test-pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh
tests/test-encryption-git-roundtrip.sh
tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh
tests/test-quality-sweep-serialization.sh
tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh
tests/test-tier3-simplified.sh
tests/test-pre-commit-hook-counter-monotonic.sh
tests/test-shell-init-pattern-check.sh
tests/test-claim-release-label-mutation.sh
tests/test-sandbox-passthrough-otel.sh
tests/test-issue-reconcile.sh
tests/test-comment-wrapper-marker-dedup.sh
tests/test-origin-label-exclusion.sh
tests/test-hot-deploy-flow.sh
tests/test-stats-functions-characterization.sh
tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh
```

Any test that invokes wrapper functions silently no-ops after the split. This is fleet-wide blast radius — every test file needs audit.

## Root cause

PR #20037 split `shared-constants.sh` → `shared-constants.sh` + `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, adding a bare `source` directive at line 755. Three contributing factors to the silent regression:

1. **No error trapping on source**: `shared-constants.sh:755` does `source "path/shared-gh-wrappers.sh"` with no `|| exit 1` and no `set -e` around it. A failed source is silent.
2. **Test files copy only one file**: Tests use `cp shared-constants.sh "$tmpdir/"` without knowing about the new dependency. When they source the copied file, the relative `source` path in it points to the (empty) tmpdir, fails, and the test continues.
3. **No CI guard against the split-incomplete pattern**: PR #20037 CI passed because no test exercises the "copy shared-constants.sh and use a wrapper" code path through CI (the tests that do are local-only; the CI only runs shellcheck + markdownlint + the specific tests other PRs rely on).

The systemic gap is: **file-split PRs have no CI guard that ensures co-dependency tests still run assertions.** A test that was green before a split is green after a split, even when every assertion silently skips.

## How — systemic fix (three layers)

**Layer 1 (immediate — unblock auto-sig test):**
Update `test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` (and all ~20 affected tests) to ALSO copy `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. Introduce a single helper `_test_copy_shared_deps(tmpdir)` in a new `tests/lib/test-helpers.sh` that knows the current dependency graph and is the one-stop-update point for future splits.

**Layer 2 (fail loud on source errors):**
Modify each affected test setup to:
```
set -euo pipefail
source "$tmpdir/shared-constants.sh" || {
    echo "FAIL: shared-constants.sh sourcing failed (missing dependency?)" >&2
    exit 1
}
```
Better: bake the error check into `_test_copy_shared_deps`.

**Layer 3 (CI guard against the class):**
Add a pre-commit / CI check that for every test file under `.agents/scripts/tests/` containing `cp .*shared-constants\\.sh`, also contains `cp .*shared-gh-wrappers\\.sh` in the same setup block. Alternatively: lint rule banning bare `cp shared-constants.sh` outside `_test_copy_shared_deps`. Implementation: a `.github/workflows/test-harness-deps.yml` action or extension of `shell-init-pattern-check.sh`.

**Layer 4 (preventive — reciprocal):**
Add a pre-commit check that when a NEW `source` directive is added to `shared-constants.sh` (or to any file frequently copied by tests), CI fails unless the new dependency is already in `_test_copy_shared_deps`. This catches the same class of regression at introduction time.

## Files to modify

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/lib/test-helpers.sh` — expose `_test_copy_shared_deps(tmpdir)` which copies `shared-constants.sh` + `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (+ any future deps) and sources both with error checking.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` — replace the bare `cp` block with `_test_copy_shared_deps "$tmpdir"`. Verify the test now runs actual assertions (should see multiple "PASS:" lines).
- AUDIT + EDIT: all 20+ tests listed above. Replace bare `cp .*shared-constants.sh` with `_test_copy_shared_deps`.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-test-helpers.sh` — meta-test that `_test_copy_shared_deps` copies all declared deps, sourcing succeeds, and known wrapper functions (`gh_create_pr`, `gh_create_issue`, `gh_issue_comment`) are callable after setup.
- NEW: `.github/workflows/test-harness-deps.yml` OR extend `code-quality.yml` — CI check that scans test files for bare `cp shared-constants.sh` usage outside the helper.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants-deps-check.sh` — called from pre-commit and CI to verify `_test_copy_shared_deps` covers every `source` directive in `shared-constants.sh`.
- EDIT: `reference/testing.md` (create if absent) — document the `_test_copy_shared_deps` pattern and the rule "do not copy shared-constants.sh without also copying its deps".
- REFERENCE: `shared-constants.sh:749-755` shows the sourcing pattern to cover; `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:280` is `_gh_wrapper_auto_sig` itself.

## Acceptance

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` prints at least 6 "PASS:" assertions and returns non-zero on any wrapper regression.
- Sanity-regression test: intentionally delete `_gh_wrapper_auto_sig` from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (in a scratch branch), run `test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh`, confirm it FAILS with a clear assertion message. Then revert.
- Grep shows zero bare `cp .*shared-constants\\.sh` outside of `tests/lib/test-helpers.sh` (all migrated to the helper).
- New CI check fails when a new test file is added that does bare `cp shared-constants.sh`.
- `shared-constants-deps-check.sh` passes on main and fails on a synthetic branch that adds a new `source` directive to `shared-constants.sh` without updating `_test_copy_shared_deps`.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — clear scope, mechanical migration for the 20+ test files after helper is written. No novel architecture; mirrors existing shared-lib test patterns elsewhere in the codebase.

## Session Origin

Discovered in t2422 session while triaging "gh_create_pr didn't auto-inject signature footer" as a potential bug. Ran `bash test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` to verify wrapper health. Test exited 0 with a single source error and zero assertions. Inspected `shared-constants.sh` → `_gh_wrapper_auto_sig` not present. Found function in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (created by PR #20037). Confirmed the test tmp dir lacks the new file. Verified: `tmp.../shared-gh-wrappers.sh: No such file or directory; exit=0`. Production wrapper IS functional (PR #20054 body has the sig marker); ONLY the test is broken.

title: t2433: fix(pulse): pull repo before large-file gate measures file size (false-positive debt issues)
body:
## What

The large-file simplification gate in `_issue_targets_large_files` measures `wc -l` on the **local** working copy of target files without first pulling from remote. When a split PR has merged on GitHub but the pulse runner's local repo has not yet pulled (which is common — the only `git pull` in the dispatch path runs _after_ the gate, inside `_dlw_actually_dispatch_worker`), the gate keeps firing on stale pre-split file sizes and creates new `file-size-debt` issues each cycle.

## Why

**Observed failure (2026-04-19, pulse-prefetch.sh):** PR #19973 split the 2286-line `pulse-prefetch.sh` into 4 sub-libraries at 21:37:31Z. Between 21:39:03Z and 23:53:47Z, the gate created **6 spurious `file-size-debt` issues** (#19964, #19982, #19988, #20003, #20010, #20023) claiming the file was still >2000 lines. It wasn't — it was 625. The gate was measuring a stale local copy.

**Systemic, not one-off.** Same root cause observed on:
- `headless-runtime-lib.sh` (actual 949 lines, claimed >2000): issues #19699, #19822
- `shared-constants.sh` (actual 1445 lines, claimed >2000): issues #20018, #20043

**Cost:** each false positive = 1 issue creation + label application + pre-dispatch validator cycle (t2367 closes them ~5-7 min later but pays tokens every time) + issue-tracker pollution. Gate correctness depends on remote-synced state; without the fix the validator will continue papering over the bug.

The pre-dispatch validator (t2367) is catching symptoms, not the disease.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add `_pulse_refresh_repo` helper and call it once per (cycle, repo) at the start of the dispatch + triage loops, before any gate invocation. Use a cycle-scoped sentinel (associative array keyed by repo_path) to avoid redundant pulls within a cycle.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:530-540` — remove the now-redundant `git pull --ff-only` block; the cycle-start refresh subsumes it. Keep the `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` safety guard inside the new helper.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh:595-645` — inside `_reevaluate_simplification_labels`, ensure the refresh has run for each `(slug, rpath)` before calling `_issue_targets_large_files`. If the helper hasn't been called this cycle, call it.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gate-pull-before-measure.sh` — test harness using a sandboxed git repo with a large file; rewrite the file to below threshold via simulated remote push; verify the gate measures the new state, not the stale local.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Add `_pulse_refresh_repo` in `pulse-wrapper.sh`.** Idempotent per cycle. Use a shell-level associative array `declare -A _PULSE_REFRESHED_THIS_CYCLE` reset at cycle start. On call: skip if already refreshed; otherwise `git -C "$repo_path" fetch --quiet origin && git -C "$repo_path" pull --ff-only --no-rebase`. Log failure with the existing "[pulse-wrapper]" prefix. Reset the sentinel at the top of the pulse main loop.

2. **Wire into dispatch.** In the dispatch loop (near line 1019, before `dispatch_with_dedup`), call `_pulse_refresh_repo "$repo_path"`. Must run BEFORE the gate at pulse-dispatch-core.sh:867.

3. **Wire into triage.** In `_reevaluate_simplification_labels` (pulse-triage.sh), before calling `_issue_targets_large_files`, call `_pulse_refresh_repo "$rpath"`. Since the triage loop iterates all pulse-enabled repos, the sentinel ensures each repo is pulled exactly once per cycle.

4. **Remove redundant pull.** Delete lines 530-540 in pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh. Verify the comment referencing GH#17584 is preserved as context on the new helper (the original motivation — "worker closes issue as Invalid because target file not yet pulled" — still applies, just earlier).

5. **Test.** New test harness: init a git repo, create a 2500-line file, commit; clone as bare-upstream; in the "local" clone, add a SHORTENED version of the file in the upstream bare; DO NOT pull locally yet; invoke `_issue_targets_large_files` and assert it does NOT gate (i.e., refresh fired, measured remote state 500 lines).

### Verification

```bash
cd ~/Git/aidevops
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gate-pull-before-measure.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-reeval-stale-continuation.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_pulse_refresh_repo` helper exists in pulse-wrapper.sh with cycle-scoped idempotency
- [ ] Dispatch loop refreshes BEFORE `dispatch_with_dedup`
- [ ] Triage re-evaluation refreshes BEFORE `_issue_targets_large_files`
- [ ] Redundant pull in pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:530-540 removed
- [ ] New test harness `test-gate-pull-before-measure.sh` passes
- [ ] Existing `test-reeval-stale-continuation.sh` still passes
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations on all modified files
- [ ] One cycle on the aidevops repo demonstrates no spurious `file-size-debt` issue creation after a merged split PR (verified manually by watching the next split PR merge)

## Session Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-20
- **Session:** Claude Code interactive (maintainer)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (marcusquinn)
- **Conversation context:** User asked why simplification issues kept being filed for `pulse-prefetch.sh` even after a split PR merged. Investigation traced 6 false-positive debt issues (#19964-#20023) all citing >2000 lines when the file was 625 lines post-split. Correlation with pull-timing in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:530-540` revealed the gate runs before the only pull in the path. Confirmed systemic: same pattern on headless-runtime-lib.sh and shared-constants.sh.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (add helper)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (call before gate)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` (remove redundant pull)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` (call before re-evaluation)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gate-pull-before-measure.sh` (new)

## Context & Decisions

- **Why cycle-scoped sentinel over per-call pull:** a pulse cycle touches 15+ repos and evaluates many issues per repo. Per-call pull would run git fetch dozens of times per cycle. Once per (cycle, repo) is sufficient because the gate only needs to see a consistent snapshot of the repo for the duration of that cycle.
- **Why `--ff-only`:** avoids the catastrophic failure mode where the pulse ends up on a rebase conflict and exits with the repo in a detached/conflicted state.
- **Why `git fetch` before `pull`:** makes the pull branchless — if the local is ahead for some reason, pull won't trigger a merge.
- **Rejected: measure via `git show origin/HEAD:<path> | wc -l`.** Would also work and avoid touching the working tree, but (a) requires remote metadata that still needs fetch, (b) creates divergence from how the worker will actually see the file, (c) more invasive change to the gate internals.

title: t2432: add recent-commit sweep to pre-dispatch eligibility gate
body:
**Status:** Deferred / conditional-trigger backlog. Do **not** dispatch a worker against this issue until the trigger condition below is met.

## Summary

Add a fourth eligibility check to `is_issue_eligible_for_dispatch()` in `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh` (new exit code `5`) that scans commits on the default branch within the last ~10 minutes and aborts dispatch if any commit message contains a valid closing keyword referencing this issue's number.

## Parent context

- **Parent:** #20030 (closed, resolved by #20064) — deployed a 3-check eligibility gate: CLOSED state, `status:done|resolved` label, linked PR merged within 5 min.
- **This follow-up:** the deferred 4th check (recent-commit sweep on default branch). Design and rationale captured in the brief: `todo/tasks/t2432-brief.md`.

## Trigger condition (implement only if this is true)

Check whenever investigating pulse churn — no schedule, no deadline, no auto-close:

```bash
grep -c "no_work skip-escalation" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log \
  | awk '{ if ($1 >= 1) print "TRIGGER: " $1 " events observed — implementation justified"; else print "Below threshold: " $1 " events — leave in backlog" }'
```

If the trigger fires, add `auto-dispatch` and proceed with implementation per the brief. If the count stays at zero, this issue sits in backlog indefinitely — project attention is variable and absence of observation is not evidence the underlying need has disappeared. The issue closes only on explicit maintainer decision (e.g., the 3-check gate's churn profile is accepted as-is, or the underlying churn pattern has been addressed another way).

## Deliverables (when implemented)

1. New helper `_check_recent_commit_closes_issue <issue_num> <repo_slug>` in `pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh`, patterned on `_check_recent_merge`.
2. New exit code `5 — recent-commit on default branch`.
3. Stats counter `pre_dispatch_aborts_recent_commit` in `pulse-stats-helper.sh`, surfaced in `aidevops status`.
4. Env override `AIDEVOPS_PREDISPATCH_RECENT_COMMIT_WINDOW` (default 600).
5. Test coverage: happy path, `Ref`/`For` negative case, different-issue negative case.
6. Regex MUST match `pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue` exactly: `grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`. `Ref #NNN` and `For #NNN` must NOT trigger the check.

## Why deferred rather than shipped with #20030

- The 3-check gate covers the observed churn pattern (stale prefetch cache after `pulse-merge.sh` auto-closes an issue). The 4th check adds cost and a new false-positive surface.
- Better to deploy, measure, and extend only if telemetry justifies it — the right time to add this is when `no_work skip-escalation` rate proves the 3-check gate insufficient.

## Full context

See `todo/tasks/t2432-brief.md` in this repo for full rationale, file references, tier justification, acceptance criteria with `verify:` blocks, and implementation approach.

## PR conventions

Leaf task. When implemented, the PR body uses `Resolves #<this-issue>` as normal.

title: bug: version-manager.sh release v3.8.82 — tag+GH release created but VERSION/CHANGELOG bump commit never landed
body:
## What

`v3.8.82` release is cosmetically broken: tag + GitHub release exist but `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md` bump never landed on `main`.

## Evidence

- `git rev-parse v3.8.82` → `eb27f01eac40b5387b6d754306d0ba6b2816a7fa` (annotated tag)
- Tag's underlying commit → `5ef404386` = `chore: claim t2430 [40543_4216]` (a pulse claim commit, not a release bump)
- `git show v3.8.82:VERSION` → `3.8.81` (not `3.8.82`)
- `git show v3.8.82:CHANGELOG.md | head -20` → `[Unreleased]` heading, no `[3.8.82]` entry
- `git log --oneline -- VERSION | head -5` → last bump is `872ef2633 chore(release): bump version to 3.8.81`; no `bump version to 3.8.82` commit exists
- GitHub release `v3.8.82` exists and is `isLatest`, published `2026-04-20T02:24:37Z`

## Why it matters

- `aidevops-update-check.sh` compares deployed `VERSION` to the latest tag; users may not see the update prompt correctly.
- Next invocation of `version-manager.sh release patch` will bump `3.8.81 → 3.8.82`, clashing with the existing tag.
- Audit trail is broken — no `chore(release): bump version to 3.8.82` commit exists.

## Suspected cause

Race between `version-manager.sh release patch` and concurrent pulse claim commits. Sequence from git metadata:

1. `02:22:21Z` — PR #20066 merges → `880ccb1e1`
2. `~02:22:50Z` — pulse pushes `chore: claim t2430` → `5ef404386`
3. `~02:23:58Z` — `version-manager.sh` tags `v3.8.82` pointing at `5ef404386` (not at a bump commit)
4. `02:24:37Z` — GitHub release published

The bump commit step either failed silently or was skipped (possibly a `git push` rejection due to the pulse pushing in-between, followed by a rebase that dropped the bump).

## Files to investigate

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/version-manager.sh:135`, `:297`, `:300` — release-commit handling
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/version-manager.sh` — the `release` subcommand flow (pre-tag commit sequence, push retry on rejection)
- Reference: `.github/workflows/release.yml` if any

## Acceptance

1. `version-manager.sh release` is atomic with respect to concurrent pushes: either the bump commit lands AND the tag points at it, or the release aborts cleanly.
2. If a release fails partway, no tag/GH release is created for the failed version.
3. One-shot recovery path documented for the existing broken `v3.8.82` tag (either retag on a new bump commit, or delete v3.8.82 and ship v3.8.83 with the proper commit).
4. Regression test covers the "pulse pushes during release window" scenario.

## Session origin

Discovered during t2427 post-merge verification (PR #20066 merged at 02:22:21Z, v3.8.82 tag/release created moments later). PR #20066 itself merged cleanly; this issue is downstream of the release process.

title: t2434: fix(upgrade-planning): _upgrade_todo drops tasks outside ## Backlog (141 Done rows lost)
body:
## Task

`_upgrade_todo` in `aidevops.sh:2604-2616` extracts tasks only from the `## Backlog` section. Tasks under `## Ready`, `## In Progress`, `## In Review`, `## Done`, and `## Declined` are silently dropped into `TODO.md.bak` and never merged into the new template.

## Why

Concrete impact (reproduced 2026-04-20): running `aidevops upgrade-planning` on <webapp> (v1.0→v1.1) dropped 141 completed `[x]` tasks from `## Done`. That is audit-trail data which is NOT reconstructable from GitHub alone — `actual:` session times and `est:` breakdowns live only in TODO.md. Data was recovered from `.bak` but the silent loss is the critical defect.

Adjacent prior fixes: GH#17804 (Format-section placeholder leakage) and GH#17806 (### subsection preservation inside Backlog). Both narrower in scope.

## How

1. EDIT: `aidevops.sh:2595-2669` — `_upgrade_todo()`.
   - Replace the single-section awk extraction at line 2604 with a per-section extraction loop covering all 6 sections: Ready, Backlog, In Progress, In Review, Done, Declined.
   - Replace the single-section TOON marker re-insertion at line 2646 with a loop that inserts each section's preserved content after its matching `<!--TOON:<tag>` marker (ready, backlog, in_progress, in_review, done, declined).
   - Preserve the existing `## Format` skip logic and code-block skip logic (per-section, not global).
   - Preserve the existing placeholder filter (`t[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*` regex, drop tXXX/tYYY/tZZZ).
   - Use bash 3.2-compatible syntax (no associative arrays, no `${var,,}`).

2. NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-upgrade-planning-sections.sh`
   - Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-init-scope.sh` (same directory pattern, same SCRIPT_UNDER_TEST convention).
   - Build a synthetic old-format TODO.md with tasks in all 6 sections, invoke `_upgrade_todo`, assert every task survives in the matching new-template section.
   - Cover edge cases: empty sections, sections with only subsection headers, Format-block placeholders must still be filtered.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_upgrade_todo` preserves tasks from all 6 sections (Ready, Backlog, In Progress, In Review, Done, Declined).
- [ ] Tasks land in the matching `<!--TOON:<tag>` marker in the new template, not all dumped into Backlog.
- [ ] `## Format` placeholders and tXXX-style template IDs are still filtered out.
- [ ] New regression test `test-upgrade-planning-sections.sh` passes and covers all 6 sections.
- [ ] `shellcheck aidevops.sh` clean.
- [ ] End-to-end verification: run `aidevops upgrade-planning` against <webapp>, task count unchanged (198 before, 198 after).

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` (function `_upgrade_todo`, around line 2595-2669)
- NEW:  `.agents/scripts/tests/test-upgrade-planning-sections.sh` (model on `tests/test-init-scope.sh`)

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-20 discovered the bug while running `aidevops upgrade-planning` on <webapp>. Restored from .bak before data loss was permanent. Filed and fixing interactively (not queuing to a worker — the reproduction context is fresh in this session).

title: t2435: make opus-4.7 context window user-configurable via AIDEVOPS_OPUS_47_CONTEXT env var
body:

## What

Make the registered context window for `claude-opus-4-7` in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs` configurable via the `AIDEVOPS_OPUS_47_CONTEXT` env var. Default stays 250000. Setting it to 1000000 (or any positive integer) overrides the cap.

- Console warning emitted at plugin init when override is active

title: t2436: fix: #parent TODO tag does not synchronously map to parent-task label at issue creation — pulse dispatch race window
body:
## What

The `#parent` TODO tag (alias: `#parent-task`, `#meta`) does NOT synchronously map to the `parent-task` label at issue creation time. The mapping only happens when `issue-sync-helper.sh push` runs AFTER a `TODO.md` push to `main` (via `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml`). This creates a race window between issue creation and label synchronisation during which the pulse (local OR a remote peer runner) can dispatch a worker on an issue that was intended to block dispatch via `parent-task`.

**Canonical failure (observed 2026-04-20):**

1. 02:35:51Z — interactive session created issue #20068 via `gh_create_issue` for `t2430` (scanner rewrite, tagged `#parent` in TODO entry, `tier:thinking`). `auto-dispatch` label applied by framework default.
2. 02:36:39Z (T+48s) — remote peer runner `alex-solovyev` dispatched a worker via `DISPATCH_CLAIM`. No `parent-task` label present to block dispatch.
3. 02:37:22Z — "Dispatching worker (deterministic). Worker PID: 32" posted on issue by the peer runner.
4. ~03:30Z — PR #20070 (which added the `#parent`-tagged TODO entry) merged to main.
5. ~03:34Z — maintainer manually applied `parent-task` label on #20068 (interactive intervention).
6. Maintainer intervention comment + `no-auto-dispatch` label forced the in-flight worker to release the claim; no PR was opened (lucky outcome — could easily have produced a contentious PR).

If the worker had produced a PR before intervention, the race would have cost: (a) wasted model tokens on an architectural decision a worker is not authorised to make, (b) a PR that must be closed with a "parent-task retroactively applied" rationale, (c) muddied git history and issue timeline.

## Why

The `parent-task` label is the framework canonical block for "this issue is planning/research-only, never auto-dispatch". AGENTS.md states this as an operational guarantee:

> `parent-task` Survives reconciliation — `_is_protected_label` in `issue-sync-helper.sh` prevents tag-derived label cleanup from stripping it. Blocks dispatch unconditionally — `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned` short-circuits with a `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED` signal whenever the label is present, regardless of assignees, status labels, or tier.

This guarantee fails when there is a TEMPORAL gap between issue creation and label sync. In a fleet with multiple pulse runners (t2422 multi-runner coordination), the gap is adversarial: the pulse may fire WITHIN the gap. The maintainer must always-manually apply `parent-task` before pushing any TODO entry tagged `#parent` — a bypass-inviting fragile manual step that contradicts the "tag in TODO = protected" contract.

## Root cause

Three interlocking causes:

1. **`claim-task-id.sh` issue creation path does not parse TODO tags.** The helper accepts `--labels "..."` but the caller must pass tag-derived labels explicitly. When it falls back to bare `gh issue create` (because a requested label does not exist), labels are silently dropped.
2. **`gh_create_issue` wrapper has no TODO-tag awareness.** It applies `origin:interactive` / `origin:worker` based on session context but does not scan TODO.md for the linked task ID and does not derive `parent-task` from `#parent`.
3. **Label sync is workflow-deferred.** `issue-sync-helper.sh push` is the authoritative tag → label mapper, but it runs only from `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` on a TODO.md push event. Between issue creation and the subsequent TODO.md push to main, the issue exists label-incomplete.

Compounding: the framework default auto-applies `auto-dispatch` to issues created via common code paths (observed on all three issues #20067, #20068, #20069 this session despite not requesting it). Combined with the missing `parent-task`, an intended-protected issue ends up dispatch-eligible immediately.

## How — fix options

**Approach A (preferred): synchronous TODO tag resolution at issue creation.**
Extend `claim-task-id.sh` and/or `gh_create_issue` to:
1. Accept an optional `--todo-tags "parent,multi-os,framework"` flag, OR
2. Auto-scan `TODO.md` for a matching task ID line and parse tags from it.
Map tags to labels using the same table `issue-sync-helper.sh` uses (single source of truth, likely already factored in `issue-sync-lib.sh`). Apply all derived labels atomically via the `--label` flag on issue creation. Protected labels like `parent-task` are applied BEFORE the pulse can see the issue.

**Approach B: creation-time "hydration window" on the dispatch side.**
Add a grace period (e.g., 30s) in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` / `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` that skips dispatch for issues less than N seconds old. Rationale: labels from `issue-sync-helper.sh` are eventually consistent; a short grace window lets reconciliation catch up. Trade-off: slows legitimate dispatch; does not fix peer-runner race where hydration may happen AFTER the window closes if TODO.md push is delayed.

**Approach C: defensive parent-task detection at dispatch time.**
Before dispatching, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` could scan the issue body for `#parent` / "Tagged `#parent`" / "this is a `#parent` task" markers and short-circuit as if `parent-task` were applied. Heuristic-only; brittle but fast.

**Recommended: Approach A + hold Approach B as a secondary safety net** (eventually-consistent TODO-sync is worth tolerating briefly; fixing the source-of-truth gap is the primary win).

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — when `--repo-path` points to a repo containing `TODO.md`, auto-scan for the claimed task ID line and derive tags → labels via `issue-sync-lib.sh` shared resolver. Apply ALL tags-derived labels at `gh issue create` time. Preserve `--labels` flag behaviour (additive).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` `gh_create_issue()` — optional parameter `--todo-task-id tNNN` to trigger TODO.md scan + label derivation. Callers that build issue body from a TODO entry pass the task ID.
- EDIT or NEW: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` — expose `_derive_labels_from_tags(tags) → labels[]` as a single shared resolver. Currently, the mapping lives inside `issue-sync-helper.sh`; extract it.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` (Approach B safety net) — add `DISPATCH_HYDRATION_WINDOW_S` (default 30) — skip dispatch on issues with `createdAt` within the window. Env var override to disable.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-tag-sync.sh` — fixtures covering: (1) `claim-task-id.sh --title X` with `#parent` in existing TODO entry applies `parent-task` at creation, (2) `gh_create_issue --todo-task-id tNNN` derives labels from TODO tags, (3) hydration-window dispatch skip fires for young issues.
- EDIT: `AGENTS.md` "Parent / meta tasks" section — note the hydration guarantee and the synchronous `parent-task` application at creation.

## Acceptance

- Creating an issue for a task with `#parent` in its TODO entry yields `parent-task` label present IMMEDIATELY at creation (before any subsequent TODO.md push). Verify by `gh issue view NNNN --json labels -q ".labels[].name" | grep parent-task` returning immediately.
- Peer-runner pulse cycle occurring within 30s of issue creation sees `parent-task` and short-circuits via `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED`. No `DISPATCH_CLAIM` comment posted.
- `test-parent-tag-sync.sh` passes: all three scenarios above produce expected labels without relying on workflow-triggered issue-sync.
- Reproduce t2430 failure mode: create an issue with a `#parent`-tagged TODO entry, run `pulse-wrapper.sh --dry-run --now` within 5s; confirm the pulse does NOT dispatch a worker. Currently fails.
- Label cleanup: re-running `issue-sync-helper.sh push` after creation is idempotent — does not duplicate `parent-task`, does not strip any other creation-time labels.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — scope is clear once Approach A selected, ~3 files + 1 test. If Approach B is added as a secondary safety net (recommended), +1 small file edit. No novel architecture — mirrors the existing `issue-sync-helper.sh` tag-to-label mapping, just moves the call site earlier in the lifecycle.

## Session Origin

Discovered 2026-04-20 while briefing t2429 / t2430 / t2431 (spin-offs from t2422 PR #20054 retrospective). The `#parent` tag on t2430 / issue #20068 did NOT produce a `parent-task` label at creation; peer runner `alex-solovyev` dispatched a worker 48s later. Intervention by maintainer (manual label + comment + `no-auto-dispatch`) released the claim before a PR was produced. Without this intervention, the race would have materialised as wasted worker tokens + a contentious PR to close. The race window is adversarial in multi-runner fleets — the exact environment t2422 added structured coordination for.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20068 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20068

**Parent issue:** #20068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2430: fix(complexity-regression-helper): rewrite nesting-depth scanner (portable AWK or shfmt) to eliminate elif/prose/here-string false positives
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,parent-task,no-auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,framework,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20068. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20068:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20068** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

`complexity-regression-helper.sh` (lines ~220–260) uses a naive AWK regex to detect max-nesting-depth per shell file: `/[[:space:]]*(if|for|while|until|case)[[:space:]]/` increments a GLOBAL counter, `/[[:space:]]*(fi|done|esac)[[:space:]]*$/` decrements. Four documented false-positive classes block legitimate refactors:

1. **`elif` matches `if`** — the leading `[[:space:]]*` can match zero characters, so `elif` contains a matching substring. Each elif increments without a matching decrement (only the terminal `fi` decrements once) → net inflation per elif chain.
2. **Prose containing bare keywords** — printf/echo/log strings like `"warn action for runner=%s"` contain ` for ` which matches the increment regex. Comment bodies and heredoc bodies with the same pattern trigger it too.
3. **`done <<<"$X"` not recognized as close** — the close regex requires `done` at EOL or followed by whitespace-to-EOL. `done <<<"..."`, `done | cmd`, `done > file` all have non-EOL trailing tokens → permanent +1 to the global counter for the rest of the file.
4. **Global counter never resets between functions** — so all false positives compound across the entire file. `headless-runtime-lib.sh` currently scans as depth=83, physically impossible (verified by manual inspection).

## Why

The scanner is both the PR CI gate (`code-quality.yml:502-508`) and the pre-push hook (`complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`). False positives:

- Actively penalize clean bash idioms (`done <<<X`, good log messages with natural prose)
- Block file-split refactors — see `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 for the `complexity-bump-ok` override flow that exists ENTIRELY because of these false positives
- Train workers to write awkward bash to avoid a broken linter instead of optimizing the linter
- Generate ratchet-debt that never pays down: PR #20054 baseline showed 292 files with "nesting >8"; a large uncertain fraction are false positives
- Canonical waste: t2422 session burned ~45min on two rewrites (`IFS=$'\\n'; for line in $rows; do ... done` and "warn action ON runner=" instead of "FOR runner=") to pass the scanner on clean code

Related closed issues (did NOT address the regex): t2159 #19459 (added per-function regression for FUNCTION_COMPLEXITY only), t2171 #19585 (extended per-function to nesting but kept the same AWK), t2228 umbrella #19734 (retrospective, no AWK fix).

## Root cause

AWK regex pattern matching is insufficient to parse bash lexical structure. Specifically:
- AWK has no notion of "is this inside a string literal, heredoc, or comment"
- AWK has no notion of "elif = else+if combined" (net 0, not +1)
- AWK has no notion of "done followed by redirect/pipe/subshell" as a valid close

Any regex-only solution will keep hitting edge cases. The systemic fix needs a real tokenizer.

## How — systemic fix

**Approach A (preferred): POSIX-AWK tokenizer.** Replace the scan pass with a state machine in POSIX awk that handles:
1. String-literal skipping (`"..."`, `'...'`, `$'...'`) — track quote state
2. Comment skipping (`# ...` to EOL)
3. Heredoc skipping — track `<<MARKER` / `<<-'MARKER'` opens, match close marker, suppress content
4. elif as no-op (both +1 and -1 inside the same iteration)
5. `done <<`, `done |`, `done >`, `done &`, `done ;` all count as close
6. Per-function reset (track function boundaries: `function NAME` / `NAME ()`)

Stays in POSIX awk: no `gensub`, no `FIELDWIDTHS`, no `asort`, no multi-char RS regex. Both BSD awk (macOS `/usr/bin/awk`) and gawk/mawk (Linux) must produce identical output on the same inputs.

**Approach B (fallback if A too complex):** Use `shfmt --tojson` (if installed) or `bash-language-server` to obtain a real bash AST. Iterate the AST for nesting depth. `shfmt` is a single Go binary, easy to provision in CI and locally via `brew install shfmt` / `apt install shfmt`. Check deployment cost vs. Approach A maintenance burden.

**Approach C (tactical minimum if A and B deferred):** Keep AWK but patch in priority order: (a) strip comments pre-scan, (b) strip string literals pre-scan, (c) treat `elif` as no-op, (d) recognize `done (<<|<|>|\\||&|;|$)` as close, (e) reset counter at `function` / `name ()` boundaries. Doesn't fix heredoc bodies but cuts 80%+ of false positives with minimal risk.

Architectural decision on A vs B vs C MUST be taken before implementation. This is why the task is tagged `#parent` and `tier:thinking`.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh:220-260` — replace inline AWK with a call to `scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.awk` (or `.py`/Go wrapper).
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml:502-508` — replace inline AWK with a call to the helper (single source of truth).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.awk` (or language-of-choice per approach) — tokenizer per Approach A/B/C.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` — fixtures for each false-positive class. Each fixture has known expected depth, verified by manual bash parser or `shfmt` cross-check.
- EDIT: `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 — note that the `complexity-bump-ok` override for nesting-depth is NO LONGER needed for per-function-stable splits after this fix.

## Portability

- Target: POSIX awk subset. Verify explicitly on both macOS BSD awk (`/usr/bin/awk` = nawk) AND Linux gawk/mawk.
