title: consolidated: t2411 auto-admin-merge origin:interactive PRs from OWNER/MEMBER in pulse-merge.sh
body:
_Supersedes #20004 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Extend `pulse-merge.sh` to auto-merge `origin:interactive` PRs from OWNER/MEMBER authors once all required checks pass. Today the pulse only auto-merges `origin:worker` PRs (at `pulse-merge.sh:1255`); `origin:interactive` PRs from maintainers sit indefinitely until someone runs `gh pr merge --admin` manually, despite the framework rule in `AGENTS.md` ("PRs tagged `origin:interactive` from `OWNER`/`MEMBER` authors merge as soon as all required checks pass — typically 4-10 minutes") being documented as current behaviour.

Closing the loop means an interactive session can file a PR, exit, and trust that the pulse will merge it once green — no manual admin-merge step, no end-of-session cognitive load.

## Why

- **Current behaviour does not match documented behaviour.** `AGENTS.md` describes auto-merge as current, but the implementation is absent. Every `origin:interactive` PR from OWNER requires manual `gh pr merge --admin --squash --delete-branch` to land.
- **Live evidence (2026-04-19).**
  - PR #19965 (`origin:interactive`, OWNER @marcusquinn, all 32 required checks PASS, 0 failures, `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`) sat for ~90 minutes without auto-merge. Branch protection's `required_approving_review_count: 1` blocked native merge; no bot or pulse-level actor posted an approving review. Manual `gh pr merge 19965 --admin --squash --delete-branch` succeeded immediately.
  - PR #19993 (successor to auto-closed #19983, same pattern) — currently awaiting the same manual intervention.
- **Cost of the toil.** At ~3-5 interactive PRs/day, that is ~15-25 min/day of manual check-and-merge plus context switching. Worse when sessions end before checks finish — the PR strands overnight until the next session.
- **The pulse is supposed to close the loop on its own.** Interactive sessions should be able to dispatch-and-forget just like worker sessions. Carrying the "is my PR done yet?" cognitive load defeats the point of the background merge system.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — the deterministic merge pass. Add a new eligible-PR scan branch for `origin:interactive` PRs, parallel to the existing `origin:worker` path. Criteria for auto-merge (ALL required):
  1. Label `origin:interactive` present.
  2. PR author login matches a repo OWNER or MEMBER (use existing `_is_collaborator` helper — see `pulse-merge.sh:1272-1285`).
  3. All required status checks PASS or SKIPPED (mirror the logic at `pulse-merge.sh:751-800` used for `origin:worker`).
  4. No `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review from a human reviewer (reuse existing helper).
  5. PR is NOT draft.
  6. PR does NOT have the `hold-for-review` label (the opt-out — this label already exists in the repo; document its purpose in `AGENTS.md`).
- **EDIT**: same file — when eligible, call the existing merge path at line 1255: `gh pr merge "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --squash --admin --delete-branch`. Respect the stacked-PR retargeting fix from t2412 (shipped in #20005) — call `_retarget_stacked_children` before merging, exactly as the `origin:worker` path already does.
- **EDIT**: same file — emit a clear audit log line on auto-merge: `[pulse-merge] auto-merged origin:interactive PR #N (author=<login>, role=<role>)` to `$LOGFILE`.
- **EDIT**: `AGENTS.md` (user guide) under "Auto-merge timing" — upgrade the paragraph from aspirational to current behaviour. Document the criteria (label + role + green checks + no CHANGES_REQUESTED + not draft + no `hold-for-review` label) and the `hold-for-review` opt-out.

### Reference pattern

- Existing `origin:worker` auto-merge path in `pulse-merge.sh` — copy the structure. The admin-merge call at line 1255 is already correct; the new code just needs to add `origin:interactive` PRs to the scan.
- `_is_collaborator` helper at `pulse-merge.sh:1272-1285` for role gating (OWNER or MEMBER).
- Review-bot-gate at `pulse-merge.sh:1003` — the `--admin` flag bypasses branch protection but the gate must still be enforced in code (same as `origin:worker`). Do not bypass the review-bot-gate.
- Stacked-PR retargeting: `_retarget_stacked_children` (landed via t2412 / #20005).

### Verification

1. Unit/integration: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-*.sh` — add `test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh` with fixtures for all six cases:
   - OWNER + all checks pass → merge.
   - COLLABORATOR + all checks pass → no merge (per framework rule: contributors go through the normal gate).
   - OWNER + 1 failing check → no merge.
   - OWNER + `hold-for-review` label → no merge.
   - OWNER + draft PR → no merge.
   - OWNER + human CHANGES_REQUESTED → no merge.
2. Dogfood: file a test `origin:interactive` PR against a throwaway branch, label it, let the pulse cycle run, assert it merges within one pulse tick. Then file a second test PR with the `hold-for-review` label and assert the pulse does NOT merge it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pulse-merge.sh` auto-merges `origin:interactive` + OWNER/MEMBER + green-checks + not-draft + no-`hold-for-review` PRs.
- [ ] `hold-for-review` label respected as an opt-out (documented in `AGENTS.md`).
- [ ] Audit log line written for each auto-merge (format: `[pulse-merge] auto-merged origin:interactive PR #N (author=<login>, role=<role>)`).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` "Auto-merge timing" section updated to match implementation (criteria documented: label + role + checks + no CHANGES_REQUESTED + not draft + no `hold-for-review`).
- [ ] Regression tests cover all six fixture cases above (`test-pulse-merge-origin-interactive-auto-merge.sh`).
- [ ] Stacked-PR retargeting (`_retarget_stacked_children`, from t2412/#20005) invoked before the admin-merge call on the `origin:interactive` path.

## Context & Decisions

- **Parent supersession.** This issue consolidates #20004. The two substantive comments on #20004 (`no-work-escalation-skip` from @alex-solovyev and `cost-circuit-breaker:fired` from @marcusquinn) were automation signals from failed prior dispatch attempts — they established cost and infrastructure context but did not add or modify constraints on the fix itself. The spec above is unchanged from the approved parent body.
- **Prior-attempt CI failures (from PR #20041).** The previous worker's PR had failing required checks and was auto-closed:
  - **Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate**: fail — [run 24642833216 / job 72050801523](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/24642833216/job/72050801523)
  - **Complexity Analysis**: fail — [run 24642833305 / job 72049773854](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/24642833305/job/72049773854)

  The next worker should (1) check out a fresh branch from `origin/main` (do NOT reuse the old branch), (2) read the failing check logs for specific errors, (3) fix issues in code — not in CI config, (4) verify all checks pass locally before pushing.
- **Prior dispatch cost.** Per Comment 2 (below): two `tier:standard` attempts spent 1,090K tokens (budget: 100K) without producing a merged PR, tripping the t2007 cost circuit breaker. Per Comment 1 (below): the root cause was `no_work` infrastructure failures during runtime setup (FD exhaustion / plugin init failure / branch naming race / auth refresh race), NOT task unsolvability. `tier:standard` is retained; the next attempt should succeed once runtime setup completes cleanly.
- **Sister brief t2412 has already shipped.** t2412 ("retarget stacked PRs before base-branch merge to prevent auto-close") is closed as COMPLETED in #20005 (2026-04-20T00:22:23Z). The `_retarget_stacked_children` helper referenced in the How section is available now — the `origin:interactive` auto-merge path MUST call it before merging, exactly as the `origin:worker` path does.
- **Maintainer approval carry-over.** Parent #20004 received a cryptographically-signed maintainer approval from @marcusquinn at 2026-04-20T01:42:11Z (`APPROVE:issue:marcusquinn/aidevops:20004:2026-04-20T01:42:09Z`). Because this consolidation preserves scope verbatim (no constraint changes), the approval intent carries over — but the signature itself is bound to issue 20004 and cannot be transferred. If the maintainer gate (`.github/workflows/maintainer-review-and-assignee-gate.yml`) requires a signed approval on this consolidated issue, run `sudo aidevops approve issue <THIS_NUM>` once filed.
- **Scope lock from parent.** The parent approval comment stated: _"This issue is now locked. To propose scope changes, open a new issue referencing this one."_ This consolidated issue inherits that lock — scope changes go through a new issue, not comment-driven drift on this one.
- **Auto-dispatch retained.** Parent had `auto-dispatch` and `status:available`. Both preserved on the consolidated issue so the pulse picks it up on the next tick.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

---

**Comment 1 attribution** — @alex-solovyev (2026-04-19T23:23:44Z, automated via `escalate_issue_tier` no_work skip in `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`, t2387): "Tier Escalation Skipped: Infrastructure Failure (no_work)" — established that prior failures were `no_work` crashes during runtime setup (FD exhaustion / plugin init failure / branch naming race / auth refresh race), not task-level blockers. Informed the decision to retain `tier:standard` rather than escalate to `tier:thinking`.

**Comment 2 attribution** — @marcusquinn (2026-04-20T00:41:30Z, automated via the t2007 cost circuit breaker): recorded cumulative spend of 1,090K tokens across 2 worker attempts against a 100K `tier:standard` budget. Established that cost overrun was driven by the infrastructure failures from Comment 1, not by an unsolvable brief, and applied `needs-maintainer-review` pending investigation.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20013 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20013

**Parent issue:** #20013 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2415: auto-claim interactive ownership on worktree creation
**Parent labels:** `auto-dispatch,origin:interactive,tier:standard,framework,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20013. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20013 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20013:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20013 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20013 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20013 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20013 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20013** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.

- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-19 evening — created a worktree for t2401 via `wt switch -c feature/t2401-dispatch-claim-version` to back PR #19993. The worktree creation does NOT automatically register an interactive claim on the linked issue #19968. In this session, the pulse had already assigned worker stamps to #19968 before the interactive claim was filed manually later. AGENTS.md already states "When an interactive session engages with a GitHub issue — opening a worktree for it, claiming a new task..." the agent "MUST immediately call `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`". This puts the burden on the agent to remember across every worktree creation. Automating it closes the race window between worktree creation and manual claim.

## What

When a new linked worktree is created via `wt switch -c`, `worktree-helper.sh add`, or `full-loop-helper.sh start` with a branch name that resolves to a GitHub issue number (`feature/tNNN-*` where `tNNN` claim file records `GH#NNN`, or directly `feature/gh-<N>-*`), automatically invoke `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug>` as part of the creation path.

## Why

- **Race window**: Pulse dispatch-dedup is `(active status) AND (non-self assignee)`. Between worktree creation and manual claim, the issue has neither — pulse can dispatch a worker.
- **Agent forgetfulness**: 90% of worktrees are created for a specific issue. The framework has enough information to infer the claim target; making the agent remember is a reliability hole.
- **Audit trail gap**: a worktree without a claim stamp is an orphaned stamp risk — if the session dies, `scan-stale` Phase 1 has no record to recover.

## How

1. **Parse branch name** in the worktree creation path:
   - Primary pattern: `^(feature|bugfix|hotfix|refactor|chore)/(t[0-9]+)(-.*)?$` → look up task ID → extract `ref:GH#NNN` from TODO.md entry OR from `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/task-claims/<task_id>.json`.
   - Secondary pattern: `^[^/]+/gh-([0-9]+)-.*$` → issue number direct from branch name.
   - Repo slug: `git -C <worktree> remote get-url origin` → normalise to `owner/repo`.

2. **Call claim** on successful worktree creation:
   ```bash
   if [[ -n "$linked_issue" && -n "$repo_slug" ]]; then
       "${AIDEVOPS_SCRIPTS_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/agents/scripts}/interactive-session-helper.sh" \
           claim "$linked_issue" "$repo_slug" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
           && echo "[worktree-helper] auto-claimed interactive ownership on ${repo_slug}#${linked_issue}" \
           || echo "[worktree-helper] claim skipped or failed (non-fatal)"
   fi
   ```

3. **Opt-out** via `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_AUTO_CLAIM=1` for scripted bulk worktree operations.

4. **Header parity**: apply the same logic in `full-loop-helper.sh start` (which also creates worktrees) so the behaviour is uniform regardless of entry point.

5. **Headless skip**: when `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=1` / `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1`, skip auto-claim — headless workers register their own claims via `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `worktree-helper.sh add|switch` auto-claims interactive ownership when branch name encodes a task ID OR direct issue number and session is not headless.
- [ ] `full-loop-helper.sh start` uses the same logic (shared helper `_resolve_linked_issue_from_branch` in `shared-constants.sh` or new `worktree-claim-helper.sh`).
- [ ] `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_AUTO_CLAIM=1` opts out.
- [ ] Headless detection (`FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS|AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS|Claude_HEADLESS|GITHUB_ACTIONS`) skips auto-claim.
- [ ] Failure to resolve branch→issue is non-fatal (log + continue).
- [ ] Regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-auto-claim.sh` covers: tNNN prefix with ref:GH#, gh-<N> prefix, unparseable prefix (no claim), headless env (no claim), opt-out flag (no claim).
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all touched files.
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Git Workflow" → "Worktree..." section updated to note auto-claim.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` — hook into `add` / `switch` subcommand exit path.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — `start` subcommand, post-worktree-creation.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — add `_resolve_linked_issue_from_branch` helper (or create `worktree-claim-helper.sh`).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-auto-claim.sh` — model on `test-parent-task-guard.sh`.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Git Workflow" → worktree paragraph.

## Reference pattern

Follow the existing post-creation integration at `worktree-helper.sh` localdev integration block (line ~200) — that block already runs AFTER successful worktree creation and handles exit-code-0-only side effects. Mirror that structure for the auto-claim call.

For branch-to-issue resolution, model on how `pulse-merge.sh:_extract_linked_issue` parses PR bodies — same logic for TODO.md entries is a ~10-line grep for `^- \[[ x]\] (tNNN) .*ref:GH#([0-9]+)`.

~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh remove ~/Git/aidevops-feature-tXXXX --force

## Consolidation target: #20068

**Parent issue:** #20068 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2430: fix(complexity-regression-helper): rewrite nesting-depth scanner (portable AWK or shfmt) to eliminate elif/prose/here-string false positives
**Parent labels:** `status:in-review,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,framework,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20068. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20068:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20068 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20068 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20068** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

`complexity-regression-helper.sh` (lines ~220–260) uses a naive AWK regex to detect max-nesting-depth per shell file: `/[[:space:]]*(if|for|while|until|case)[[:space:]]/` increments a GLOBAL counter, `/[[:space:]]*(fi|done|esac)[[:space:]]*$/` decrements. Four documented false-positive classes block legitimate refactors:

1. **`elif` matches `if`** — the leading `[[:space:]]*` can match zero characters, so `elif` contains a matching substring. Each elif increments without a matching decrement (only the terminal `fi` decrements once) → net inflation per elif chain.
2. **Prose containing bare keywords** — printf/echo/log strings like `"warn action for runner=%s"` contain ` for ` which matches the increment regex. Comment bodies and heredoc bodies with the same pattern trigger it too.
3. **`done <<<"$X"` not recognized as close** — the close regex requires `done` at EOL or followed by whitespace-to-EOL. `done <<<"..."`, `done | cmd`, `done > file` all have non-EOL trailing tokens → permanent +1 to the global counter for the rest of the file.
4. **Global counter never resets between functions** — so all false positives compound across the entire file. `headless-runtime-lib.sh` currently scans as depth=83, physically impossible (verified by manual inspection).

## Why

The scanner is both the PR CI gate (`code-quality.yml:502-508`) and the pre-push hook (`complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`). False positives:

- Actively penalize clean bash idioms (`done <<<X`, good log messages with natural prose)
- Block file-split refactors — see `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 for the `complexity-bump-ok` override flow that exists ENTIRELY because of these false positives
- Train workers to write awkward bash to avoid a broken linter instead of optimizing the linter
- Generate ratchet-debt that never pays down: PR #20054 baseline showed 292 files with "nesting >8"; a large uncertain fraction are false positives
- Canonical waste: t2422 session burned ~45min on two rewrites (`IFS=$'\\n'; for line in $rows; do ... done` and "warn action ON runner=" instead of "FOR runner=") to pass the scanner on clean code

Related closed issues (did NOT address the regex): t2159 #19459 (added per-function regression for FUNCTION_COMPLEXITY only), t2171 #19585 (extended per-function to nesting but kept the same AWK), t2228 umbrella #19734 (retrospective, no AWK fix).

## Root cause

AWK regex pattern matching is insufficient to parse bash lexical structure. Specifically:
- AWK has no notion of "is this inside a string literal, heredoc, or comment"
- AWK has no notion of "elif = else+if combined" (net 0, not +1)
- AWK has no notion of "done followed by redirect/pipe/subshell" as a valid close

Any regex-only solution will keep hitting edge cases. The systemic fix needs a real tokenizer.

## How — systemic fix

**Approach A (preferred): POSIX-AWK tokenizer.** Replace the scan pass with a state machine in POSIX awk that handles:
1. String-literal skipping (`"..."`, `'...'`, `$'...'`) — track quote state
2. Comment skipping (`# ...` to EOL)
3. Heredoc skipping — track `<<MARKER` / `<<-'MARKER'` opens, match close marker, suppress content
4. elif as no-op (both +1 and -1 inside the same iteration)
5. `done <<`, `done |`, `done >`, `done &`, `done ;` all count as close
6. Per-function reset (track function boundaries: `function NAME` / `NAME ()`)

Stays in POSIX awk: no `gensub`, no `FIELDWIDTHS`, no `asort`, no multi-char RS regex. Both BSD awk (macOS `/usr/bin/awk`) and gawk/mawk (Linux) must produce identical output on the same inputs.

**Approach B (fallback if A too complex):** Use `shfmt --tojson` (if installed) or `bash-language-server` to obtain a real bash AST. Iterate the AST for nesting depth. `shfmt` is a single Go binary, easy to provision in CI and locally via `brew install shfmt` / `apt install shfmt`. Check deployment cost vs. Approach A maintenance burden.

**Approach C (tactical minimum if A and B deferred):** Keep AWK but patch in priority order: (a) strip comments pre-scan, (b) strip string literals pre-scan, (c) treat `elif` as no-op, (d) recognize `done (<<|<|>|\\||&|;|$)` as close, (e) reset counter at `function` / `name ()` boundaries. Doesn't fix heredoc bodies but cuts 80%+ of false positives with minimal risk.

Architectural decision on A vs B vs C MUST be taken before implementation. This is why the task is tagged `#parent` and `tier:thinking`.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh:220-260` — replace inline AWK with a call to `scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.awk` (or `.py`/Go wrapper).
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml:502-508` — replace inline AWK with a call to the helper (single source of truth).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.awk` (or language-of-choice per approach) — tokenizer per Approach A/B/C.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` — fixtures for each false-positive class. Each fixture has known expected depth, verified by manual bash parser or `shfmt` cross-check.
- EDIT: `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 — note that the `complexity-bump-ok` override for nesting-depth is NO LONGER needed for per-function-stable splits after this fix.

## Portability

- Target: POSIX awk subset. Verify explicitly on both macOS BSD awk (`/usr/bin/awk` = nawk) AND Linux gawk/mawk.
- Test matrix in `test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh`: run `env AWK=/usr/bin/awk ...` and `env AWK=gawk ...` (+ mawk if available) with identical expected output for every fixture.
- Avoid external runtimes (Python, Go) UNLESS already in dev-deps (`shfmt` likely approved — check `aidevops.json` / `setup.sh` first).
- CI must test on both `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` matrix (code-quality.yml already does this for ShellCheck — mirror).

## Acceptance

- Scanner on `headless-runtime-lib.sh` reports depth <=12 (sanity: manual inspection shows real max ~5). Current: 83.
- Per-function reset: a file with 10 top-level functions, each max-depth 3, reports max=3 (not max=30).
- elif chain of 10 elifs + matching `fi`: net 0 (not +9).
- File containing only `echo "for all users, if it matches"` reports depth=0.
- `while read; do ...; done <<<"$rows"`: +1 enter, +1 exit = 1 (not stuck at +1 forever).
- Heredoc body containing `if`, `for`, `while` keywords reports 0 contribution.
- `test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` passes on macOS BSD awk AND Linux gawk/mawk (CI matrix both OSes).
- Baseline re-snapshot after fix: expect "nesting >8" count to drop from ~292 to a small number reflecting real deep control flow only.
- `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 updated to remove the `complexity-bump-ok` nesting-depth false-positive escape hatch.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — requires architectural judgment (A vs B vs C), POSIX-AWK subset verification, cross-OS portability testing, and re-baselining decisions. DO NOT auto-dispatch without A/B/C decision. This is a `#parent` task — decompose into sub-tasks after design phase.

## Session Origin

Discovered in t2422 session implementing PR #20054. Hit false-positive (4) (`done <<<"$rows"`) and (2) (prose `for` in printf message) within a single 300-line dispatch-claim refactor. Both required awkward rewrites to pass the pre-push hook. Three prior stored memories confirm same pattern in t2265, t2368 (large-file-split playbook), and unnamed prior session (83-depth headless-runtime-lib.sh). The `large-file-split.md` playbook documents the override flow; this task makes that section obsolete.

### Comment 3 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-20T03:25:32Z

## Approach selected: B (shfmt `--to-json` AST walker)

Proceeding with Approach B after reviewing the tradeoffs. Implementation starting now in a worktree at `~/Git/aidevops.feature-t2430-shfmt-nesting-scanner`.

### Decision matrix

| Axis | A (POSIX-AWK tokenizer) | **B (shfmt --to-json)** | C (tactical AWK patches) |
|------|-------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------|
| Correctness | Parser-like but imperfect — heredoc bodies, ANSI-C quoting, nested command substitutions each need new state | **Correct by construction** — shfmt uses `mvdan.cc/sh`, a real bash parser | 80% fix; heredocs still broken; elif fixed via no-op; `done <<<` fixed via regex widening |
| Code volume | 400-800 lines AWK state machine | **~100-150 lines jq + bash** | ~50 lines AWK |
| Maintenance | Perennial edge cases on new bash syntax | **Near zero** — upstream parser is maintained | Permanent band-aid; every new class of false-positive needs another patch |
| Dependency | None | shfmt (**already provisioned** by `setup.sh:1039,1061`, used by `linters-local.sh`) | None |
| Dev burden | High — BSD awk / gawk / mawk test matrix per fixture | **Low** — single Go binary, deterministic output across OSes | Low |
| False-positive coverage | Attempts all four classes via hand-rolled state | **All four classes solved by construction** (prose/elif/done-redirect/heredoc) | String-in-prose fixed (if comments pre-stripped); elif fixed; done-redirect fixed; heredoc NOT fixed |

### Why B is the right call

1. **shfmt is already a framework dev dep.** `setup.sh` installs it via `check_quality_tools`; `linters-local.sh` runs it as the fast pre-pass syntax check. We are not adding a new runtime — we are making better use of one that is already required.
2. **`shfmt --to-json` produces an AST with exactly the node types we need**: `IfClause`, `ForClause`, `WhileClause`, `CaseClause`, `FuncDecl`, `Block`. Computing max nesting depth is a direct AST walk.
3. **Every documented false-positive class disappears by construction**:
   - Prose containing bare keywords (`"for all users"`) — the lexer doesn't tokenize string-literal content as control flow.
   - `elif` chains — represented as `IfClause.Else.IfClause`, so depth is counted correctly (nested under the same block, not double-counted).
   - `done <<<"$x"` / `done | cmd` / `done > file` — just a normal `WhileClause` terminator, no regex shape matching needed.
   - Heredoc bodies — parsed as `Redirect.Hdoc`, not as control-flow source.
   - Per-function reset — `FuncDecl` nodes give us natural function boundaries; we compute per-function depth independently.
4. **The A-vs-B concern about "future edge cases"** cuts against A, not B: the parser handles them upstream.
5. **Scope correction:** the issue body cites `code-quality.yml:502-508` as a second scanner copy. That line range is now config-threshold read, not duplicate AWK (verified in situ). There is only ONE scanner location (`complexity-regression-helper.sh:245-251`). Fixing one place fixes everything.

### `parent-task` label treatment

The `#parent` tag was applied because genuine uncertainty existed on A/B/C and decomposition into "A-specific", "B-specific", "C-specific" child tasks might have been the right model for an async worker queue. With the decision made and the implementation scoped to a single ~150-line helper change + test fixtures + docs update, this is now a **single implementable unit**, not a decomposition epic. Per `AGENTS.md` "Parent / meta tasks" (t1986):

> Do not use for: issues that should eventually be implemented as a single unit — those are normal tasks.

The `parent-task` label is being removed as part of this PR's lifecycle. PR will use `Resolves #20068` (normal leaf-issue convention), not `For #20068`.

### Consolidation task #20084

The open `consolidation-task` child #20084 is obsolete once this issue is directly implemented. It will be closed with a rationale pointing at this PR.

### Scope of the PR (single unit)

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh` — shfmt-based scanner; fallback to the existing AWK when shfmt is unavailable (graceful degradation for minimal-dev environments).
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh:226-259` — replace inline AWK with call to the new scanner.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` — fixtures for all four false-positive classes + per-function reset + real deep-nesting positive case; asserts expected depths.
- **EDIT**: `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 — remove the `complexity-bump-ok` nesting-depth escape-hatch note, since the false-positive class no longer exists.

title: consolidated: auto-claim interactive ownership on worktree creation
body:
_Supersedes #20013 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## Session Origin

Interactive session 2026-04-19 evening — created a worktree for t2401 via `wt switch -c feature/t2401-dispatch-claim-version` to back PR #19993. The worktree creation did NOT automatically register an interactive claim on the linked issue #19968. In this session, the pulse had already assigned worker stamps to #19968 before the interactive claim was filed manually later. AGENTS.md already states that the agent MUST call `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` when opening a worktree for a GitHub issue, but this relies on the agent remembering across every worktree creation. Automating it closes the race window between worktree creation and manual claim.

## What

When a new linked worktree is created via `wt switch -c`, `worktree-helper.sh add`, or `full-loop-helper.sh start` with a branch name that resolves to a GitHub issue number (`feature/tNNN-*` where `tNNN` claim file records `GH#NNN`, or directly `feature/gh-<N>-*`), automatically invoke `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug>` as part of the creation path.

## Why

- **Race window**: Pulse dispatch-dedup is `(active status) AND (non-self assignee)`. Between worktree creation and manual claim, the issue has neither — pulse can dispatch a worker.
- **Agent forgetfulness**: 90% of worktrees are created for a specific issue. The framework has enough information to infer the claim target; making the agent remember is a reliability hole.
- **Audit trail gap**: A worktree without a claim stamp is an orphaned stamp risk — if the session dies, `scan-stale` Phase 1 has no record to recover.

## How

1. **Parse branch name** in the worktree creation path:
   - Primary pattern: `^(feature|bugfix|hotfix|refactor|chore)/(t[0-9]+)(-.*)?$` → look up task ID → extract `ref:GH#NNN` from TODO.md entry OR from `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/task-claims/<task_id>.json`.
   - Secondary pattern: `^[^/]+/gh-([0-9]+)-.*$` → issue number direct from branch name.
   - Repo slug: `git -C <worktree> remote get-url origin` → normalise to `owner/repo`.

2. **Call claim** on successful worktree creation:
   ```bash
   if [[ -n "$linked_issue" && -n "$repo_slug" ]]; then
       "${AIDEVOPS_SCRIPTS_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops/agents/scripts}/interactive-session-helper.sh" \
           claim "$linked_issue" "$repo_slug" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
           && echo "[worktree-helper] auto-claimed interactive ownership on ${repo_slug}#${linked_issue}" \
           || echo "[worktree-helper] claim skipped or failed (non-fatal)"
   fi
   ```

3. **Opt-out** via `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_AUTO_CLAIM=1` for scripted bulk worktree operations.

4. **Header parity**: Apply the same logic in `full-loop-helper.sh start` (which also creates worktrees) so the behaviour is uniform regardless of entry point.

5. **Headless skip**: When `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=1` / `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS=1`, skip auto-claim — headless workers register their own claims via `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` — hook into `add` / `switch` subcommand exit path (post-creation integration block ~line 200).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — `start` subcommand, post-worktree-creation.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — add `_resolve_linked_issue_from_branch` helper (or create `worktree-claim-helper.sh`).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-auto-claim.sh` — model on `test-parent-task-guard.sh`.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Git Workflow" → worktree paragraph.

## Reference pattern

Follow the existing post-creation integration at `worktree-helper.sh` localdev integration block (line ~200) — that block already runs AFTER successful worktree creation and handles exit-code-0-only side effects. Mirror that structure for the auto-claim call.

For branch-to-issue resolution, model on how `pulse-merge.sh:_extract_linked_issue` parses PR bodies — same logic for TODO.md entries is a ~10-line grep for `^- \[[ x]\] (tNNN) .*ref:GH#([0-9]+)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `worktree-helper.sh add|switch` auto-claims interactive ownership when branch name encodes a task ID OR direct issue number and session is not headless.
- [ ] `full-loop-helper.sh start` uses the same logic (shared helper `_resolve_linked_issue_from_branch` in `shared-constants.sh` or new `worktree-claim-helper.sh`).
- [ ] `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_AUTO_CLAIM=1` opts out.
- [ ] Headless detection (`FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS|AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS|Claude_HEADLESS|GITHUB_ACTIONS`) skips auto-claim.
- [ ] Failure to resolve branch→issue is non-fatal (log + continue).
- [ ] Regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-auto-claim.sh` covers: tNNN prefix with ref:GH#, gh-<N> prefix, unparseable prefix (no claim), headless env (no claim), opt-out flag (no claim).
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all touched files.
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Git Workflow" → "Worktree..." section updated to note auto-claim.

## Verification

```bash
# Unit:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-auto-claim.sh

# Manual:
# Seed a TODO.md entry mapping tXXXX → GH#YYYY
# Create worktree:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh add ~/Git/aidevops-feature-tXXXX feature/tXXXX-demo
# Confirm stamp exists:
ls ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/marcusquinn__aidevops__YYYY
# Confirm status:in-review on #YYYY:
gh issue view YYYY --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --json labels
# Teardown:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh release YYYY marcusquinn/aidevops
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh remove ~/Git/aidevops-feature-tXXXX --force
```

## Context & Decisions

- **Original spec** by @marcusquinn: Full implementation brief filed in interactive session 2026-04-19, covering branch-name parsing, auto-claim hook, opt-out env var, headless skip, and full-loop-helper parity.
- **Simplification gate cleared** (@marcusquinn, automated, 2026-04-20T00:36): Cited file references fall within scoped-range bypass or target file was simplified below 2000 lines. Issue cleared for dispatch.
- **Cost circuit breaker fired** (@alex-solovyev, automated, 2026-04-20T00:41): Worker accumulated 540K tokens (tier:standard budget 100K) on attempt 1. Applied `needs-maintainer-review`. Root cause: brief complexity or worker loop rather than scope error. No scope changes from this comment — the brief as written remains the implementation target.
- **Decision**: The two comments are automated pulse system events, not substantive scope modifications. The original spec from the parent body is preserved verbatim here with no removals.

## Tier

tier:standard — touches 2 entry points + shared helper, needs careful headless detection. Sonnet.

title: consolidated: t2430 rewrite nesting-depth scanner using shfmt --to-json AST walker (Approach B)
body:
_Supersedes #20068 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## Session Origin

Discovered in t2422 session implementing PR #20054 (per @marcusquinn). Hit false-positive (4) (`done <<<"$rows"`) and false-positive (2) (prose `for` in printf message) within a single 300-line dispatch-claim refactor. Both required awkward rewrites to pass the pre-push hook. Three prior stored memories confirm the same pattern in t2265, t2368 (large-file-split playbook), and an unnamed prior session (83-depth headless-runtime-lib.sh). The `large-file-split.md` playbook documents the override flow; this task makes that section obsolete.

## What

Replace the nesting-depth scanner in `complexity-regression-helper.sh` (lines 226–259) with a `shfmt --to-json` AST walker (Approach B, selected by @marcusquinn at 2026-04-20T03:25Z). The new scanner eliminates four documented false-positive classes that currently inflate nesting-depth reports (e.g., `headless-runtime-lib.sh` reports depth=83; real max is ~5) and block legitimate refactors.

**Selected approach: B — shfmt `--to-json` AST walker.** shfmt is already provisioned by `setup.sh:1039,1061` and used by `linters-local.sh` — no new dependency required.

## Why

The current scanner uses a naive AWK regex (`/[[:space:]]*(if|for|while|until|case)[[:space:]]/` increments, `/[[:space:]]*(fi|done|esac)[[:space:]]*$/` decrements) with four documented false-positive classes:

1. **`elif` matches `if`** — `[[:space:]]*` matches zero characters, so `elif` contains a matching substring. Each elif increments without a matching decrement (only the terminal `fi` decrements once) → net inflation per elif chain.
2. **Prose containing bare keywords** — printf/echo/log strings like `"warn action for runner=%s"` contain ` for ` which matches the increment regex. Comment bodies and heredoc bodies trigger it too.
3. **`done <<<"$X"` not recognized as close** — close regex requires `done` at EOL or whitespace-to-EOL; `done <<<"..."`, `done | cmd`, `done > file` have non-EOL trailing tokens → permanent +1 to the global counter for the rest of the file.
4. **Global counter never resets between functions** — all false positives compound across the entire file.

**Impact:**
- The scanner is both the PR CI gate (`code-quality.yml`) and the pre-push hook (`complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`). False positives actively penalize clean bash idioms.
- Blocks file-split refactors: `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 documents a `complexity-bump-ok` override that exists ENTIRELY because of these false positives.
- Trains workers to write awkward bash to avoid a broken linter instead of optimizing the linter.
- PR #20054 baseline: 292 files flagged "nesting >8"; a large uncertain fraction are false positives.
- Canonical waste: t2422 session burned ~45min on two rewrites to pass the scanner on clean code.

**Root cause:** AWK regex pattern matching is insufficient to parse bash lexical structure. AWK has no notion of "is this inside a string literal, heredoc, or comment", "elif = else+if combined (net 0, not +1)", or "done followed by redirect/pipe/subshell as a valid close". Any regex-only solution will keep hitting edge cases. The systemic fix needs a real tokenizer.

Related closed issues that did NOT address the regex: t2159 #19459, t2171 #19585, t2228 umbrella #19734.

## How

### Approach B rationale (per @marcusquinn decision matrix, 2026-04-20T03:25Z)

| Axis | A (POSIX-AWK tokenizer) | **B (shfmt --to-json)** | C (tactical AWK patches) |
|------|-------------------------|-------------------------|--------------------------|
| Correctness | Parser-like but imperfect — heredoc/ANSI-C/nested subshell each need new state | **Correct by construction** | 80% fix; heredocs still broken |
| Code volume | 400-800 lines AWK state machine | **~100-150 lines jq + bash** | ~50 lines AWK |
| Maintenance | Perennial edge cases on new bash syntax | **Near zero** — upstream parser maintained | Permanent band-aid |
| Dependency | None | shfmt (**already in `setup.sh:1039,1061`**) | None |
| Dev burden | High — BSD awk / gawk / mawk test matrix | **Low** — single Go binary, deterministic across OSes | Low |
| False-positive coverage | Attempts all four classes via hand-rolled state | **All four classes solved by construction** | Fixes 1–3; heredoc NOT fixed |

Key: `shfmt --to-json` produces an AST with exactly the node types needed: `IfClause`, `ForClause`, `WhileClause`, `CaseClause`, `FuncDecl`, `Block`. Computing max nesting depth = direct AST walk. `FuncDecl` nodes give natural function boundaries for per-function reset.

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh` — shfmt-based scanner. Falls back to existing AWK when shfmt is unavailable (graceful degradation for minimal-dev environments). Model on existing complexity helper in `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh`.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh:226-259` — replace inline AWK with a call to `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh` (single source of truth).
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` — fixtures for all four false-positive classes + per-function reset + real deep-nesting positive case; assert expected depths.
- **EDIT**: `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 — remove the `complexity-bump-ok` nesting-depth escape-hatch note, since the false-positive class no longer exists after this fix.

**Scope correction (per @marcusquinn):** The original issue body cited `code-quality.yml:502-508` as a second scanner location. That line range is config-threshold read, NOT duplicate AWK (verified in situ). There is ONE scanner location: `complexity-regression-helper.sh:226-259`. No `code-quality.yml` edit is needed.

### Implementation guidance

Run `shfmt --to-json <file>` to get a JSON AST; walk depth-first counting nesting blocks. Per @marcusquinn: every documented false-positive class disappears by construction:
- Prose containing bare keywords → string-literal content not tokenized as control flow
- `elif` chains → represented as `IfClause.Else.IfClause`, depth counted correctly (not double-counted)
- `done <<<"$x"` / `done | cmd` / `done > file` → normal `WhileClause` terminator, no regex shape matching needed
- Heredoc bodies → parsed as `Redirect.Hdoc`, not control-flow source
- Per-function reset → `FuncDecl` nodes give natural function boundaries; compute per-function depth independently

### Portability

- Test matrix in `test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh`: run under `env AWK=/usr/bin/awk ...` (macOS BSD awk = nawk) AND `env AWK=gawk ...` (Linux gawk/mawk) with identical expected output for every fixture.
- CI must test on both `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` matrix (mirror existing `code-quality.yml` ShellCheck matrix).
- Graceful degradation: when shfmt is unavailable, fall back to AWK with a warning; scan still completes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scanner on `headless-runtime-lib.sh` reports depth ≤12 (sanity: manual inspection shows real max ~5). Current: 83.
- [ ] Per-function reset: file with 10 top-level functions each max-depth 3 → reports max=3 (not max=30).
- [ ] elif chain of 10 elifs + matching `fi`: net 0 (not +9).
- [ ] File containing only `echo "for all users, if it matches"` → reports depth=0.
- [ ] `while read; do ...; done <<<"$rows"`: net depth=1 (not permanently stuck at +1).
- [ ] Heredoc body containing `if`, `for`, `while` keywords → reports 0 contribution.
- [ ] `test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` passes on macOS BSD awk AND Linux gawk/mawk (CI matrix: both OSes).
- [ ] Baseline re-snapshot after fix: "nesting >8" count drops from ~292 to a small number reflecting real deep control flow only.
- [ ] `reference/large-file-split.md` §4.1 updated to remove `complexity-bump-ok` nesting-depth false-positive escape hatch.
- [ ] Graceful degradation: shfmt unavailable → AWK fallback with warning, scan still completes.

## Context & Decisions

**Approach decision (per @marcusquinn, 2026-04-20T03:25Z):** Approach B (shfmt `--to-json` AST walker) selected over A (POSIX-AWK tokenizer, 400-800 lines, perennial edge cases) and C (tactical AWK patches, 80% fix, heredocs permanently broken). Key reason: shfmt already a framework dev dep; all four false-positive classes solved by construction; future edge cases handled upstream by the parser.

**parent-task label (per @marcusquinn):** Applied initially because A/B/C architectural decision was uncertain. With decision made and scope reduced to ~150-line helper + tests + docs update, this is a **single implementable unit** (not a decomposition epic). Per AGENTS.md t1986: "Do not use for issues that should eventually be implemented as a single unit." The `parent-task` label must NOT be applied to this consolidated issue.

**Decomposition nudge (per @alex-solovyev, automated, 2026-04-20T02:51Z):** `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` correctly identified the parent-task state (no children, blocked dispatch). However, the maintainer's Approach B selection and single-unit scoping superseded the decomposition path — this is now a leaf task.

**Scope correction (per @marcusquinn):** Original issue body cited `code-quality.yml:502-508` as a second scanner copy; verified to be config-threshold read, not duplicate AWK. One file to edit: `complexity-regression-helper.sh:226-259`.

**In-flight worker at time of parent-task label (per @marcusquinn comment 1, 2026-04-20T02:37Z):** A worker (@alex-solovyev runner) was dispatched before the parent-task label synced. Per maintainer: if a PR was opened, close it with rationale "parent-task retroactively applied; maintainer deferred architectural decision." This consolidated issue supersedes any prior work.

**Prior consolidation task #20084:** Was filed as a consolidation-task child for #20068. Already closed (state: not_planned) as of 2026-04-20T03:28Z. No action needed.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20072 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20072

**Parent issue:** #20072 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2432: add recent-commit sweep to pre-dispatch eligibility gate
**Parent labels:** `status:queued,no-auto-dispatch,origin:worker,tier:standard,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20072. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20072 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20072:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20072 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20072 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20072 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20072 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20072** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

**Status:** Deferred / conditional-trigger backlog. Do **not** dispatch a worker against this issue until the trigger condition below is met.

## Summary

Add a fourth eligibility check to `is_issue_eligible_for_dispatch()` in `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh` (new exit code `5`) that scans commits on the default branch within the last ~10 minutes and aborts dispatch if any commit message contains a valid closing keyword referencing this issue's number.

## Parent context

- **Parent:** #20030 (closed, resolved by #20064) — deployed a 3-check eligibility gate: CLOSED state, `status:done|resolved` label, linked PR merged within 5 min.
- **This follow-up:** the deferred 4th check (recent-commit sweep on default branch). Design and rationale captured in the brief: `todo/tasks/t2432-brief.md`.

## Trigger condition (implement only if this is true)

Check whenever investigating pulse churn — no schedule, no deadline, no auto-close:

```bash
grep -c "no_work skip-escalation" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log \
  | awk '{ if ($1 >= 1) print "TRIGGER: " $1 " events observed — implementation justified"; else print "Below threshold: " $1 " events — leave in backlog" }'
```

If the trigger fires, add `auto-dispatch` and proceed with implementation per the brief. If the count stays at zero, this issue sits in backlog indefinitely — project attention is variable and absence of observation is not evidence the underlying need has disappeared. The issue closes only on explicit maintainer decision (e.g., the 3-check gate's churn profile is accepted as-is, or the underlying churn pattern has been addressed another way).

## Deliverables (when implemented)

1. New helper `_check_recent_commit_closes_issue <issue_num> <repo_slug>` in `pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh`, patterned on `_check_recent_merge`.
2. New exit code `5 — recent-commit on default branch`.
3. Stats counter `pre_dispatch_aborts_recent_commit` in `pulse-stats-helper.sh`, surfaced in `aidevops status`.
4. Env override `AIDEVOPS_PREDISPATCH_RECENT_COMMIT_WINDOW` (default 600).
5. Test coverage: happy path, `Ref`/`For` negative case, different-issue negative case.
6. Regex MUST match `pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue` exactly: `grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`. `Ref #NNN` and `For #NNN` must NOT trigger the check.

## Why deferred rather than shipped with #20030

- The 3-check gate covers the observed churn pattern (stale prefetch cache after `pulse-merge.sh` auto-closes an issue). The 4th check adds cost and a new false-positive surface.
- Better to deploy, measure, and extend only if telemetry justifies it — the right time to add this is when `no_work skip-escalation` rate proves the 3-check gate insufficient.

## Full context

See `todo/tasks/t2432-brief.md` in this repo for full rationale, file references, tier justification, acceptance criteria with `verify:` blocks, and implementation approach.

## PR conventions

Leaf task. When implemented, the PR body uses `Resolves #<this-issue>` as normal.

For #20030

## Substantive comments (verbatim, in chronological order)

### Comment 1 — @marcusquinn at 2026-04-20T02:53:17Z

## Housekeeping — mechanism-only fix

Switched the "do not dispatch" block from accidental (stampless `origin:interactive` + self-assignment) to explicit (`no-auto-dispatch` label).

### Why

The prior state relied on `t2148` treating self-assigned `origin:interactive` issues as an active claim. That was incidental — the 24h autonomous recovery in `normalize_active_issue_assignments` would have eventually unassigned this issue, opening it up for dispatch against the author's stated intent ("do not dispatch until trigger condition met in 4 weeks").

`no-auto-dispatch` is the canonical mechanism for this intent. It is a stable block that does not rely on session-origin plumbing and is honoured independently of assignment state.

### Trigger condition (unchanged)

The original trigger — `no_work skip-escalation` events at ≥1/week rate over a rolling 4-week window — still gates whether this issue should be implemented. Remove `no-auto-dispatch` and self-assign at that point if the trigger fires.

### No code change

Mechanism-only cleanup. Discovered during post-merge cleanup of t2427.

title: t2432: add recent-commit sweep to pre-dispatch eligibility gate
body:
_Supersedes #20072 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Add a fourth eligibility check to `is_issue_eligible_for_dispatch()` in `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh` (new exit code `5`) that scans commits on the default branch within the last ~10 minutes and aborts dispatch if any commit message contains a valid closing keyword referencing the candidate issue's number.

**Status: Deferred / conditional-trigger backlog.** Do NOT dispatch a worker against this issue until the trigger condition below is met.

**Deliverables (when implemented):**

1. New exit code `5 — recent-commit on default branch` in `pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh`.
2. New helper `_check_recent_commit_closes_issue <issue_num> <repo_slug>` in `pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh`, patterned on `_check_recent_merge`.
3. Fourth check integrated into `is_issue_eligible_for_dispatch()`.
4. Stats counter `pre_dispatch_aborts_recent_commit` in `pulse-stats-helper.sh`, surfaced in `aidevops status`.
5. Env override `AIDEVOPS_PREDISPATCH_RECENT_COMMIT_WINDOW` (default 600), mirroring `AIDEVOPS_PREDISPATCH_RECENT_MERGE_WINDOW`.
6. Test coverage in `test-pre-dispatch-eligibility.sh`: happy path, `Ref`/`For` negative case, different-issue negative case.

## Why

**Trigger condition (implement only if true):**

```bash
grep -c "no_work skip-escalation" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log \
  | awk '{ if ($1 >= 1) print "TRIGGER: " $1 " events observed — implementation justified"; else print "Below threshold: " $1 " events — leave in backlog" }'
```

Trigger semantics: observed ≥1 `no_work skip-escalation` events in the pulse log since the 3-check gate deployed (PR #20064 / t2424). Measured whenever the maintainer chooses to check — no deadline, no expiry, no auto-close. The issue closes only on explicit maintainer decision.

**Why the 3-check gate may be sufficient:**

- The observed no_work churn pattern is "PR just merged, prefetch cache stale, pulse picks up the now-resolved issue". Check 3 (linked PR merged in last 5 min) catches this exact case.
- Direct-to-main planning commits that close issues (TODO.md edits with `Fixes #NNN`) are rare — `issue-sync.yml` closes the issue server-side before the pulse can see it.

**Why a 4th check adds cost:**

- One extra `gh api` call per candidate issue in the hot path of `dispatch_with_dedup`.
- New false-positive surface: `Ref #NNN` / `For #NNN` commits are planning-only references, not closes. The regex must be precise — same as `pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue`.
- Commits on non-default branches must be excluded (a WIP commit on a feature branch does not resolve the issue until its PR merges).

**Why deferred rather than shipped with #20030 (t2424):**

Deploy the 3-check gate first, observe telemetry, extend only if justified. The cheaper path is to measure first.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh:5-30` — add exit code 5 to the header comment table.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh:~130-210` — add `_check_recent_commit_closes_issue()` helper after the existing `_check_recent_merge`, and an invocation in `is_issue_eligible_for_dispatch()`. Model on `_check_recent_merge` exactly.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh` — add `pre_dispatch_aborts_recent_commit` counter, sibling to existing `pre_dispatch_aborts_*` keys.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-eligibility.sh` — add three new test cases following the existing pattern.

### Reference Patterns

- `_check_recent_merge` in `pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh` — closest model (time-windowed, uses `gh api`, fail-open on error).
- `_extract_linked_issue` in `pulse-merge.sh` — canonical closing-keyword regex: `grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`. Copy, don't reinvent. `Ref #NNN` and `For #NNN` must NOT match.
- `_run_eligibility_gate_or_abort` in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` — layer 6 caller; verify exit code 5 is handled or falls through to a generic abort (may not need a new `case` branch if existing code handles all non-zero uniformly).

### Implementation Steps

1. Read `_check_recent_merge` in `pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh` to match signature, error handling, and return convention.
2. Implement `_check_recent_commit_closes_issue()` using `gh api repos/{slug}/commits?sha={default_branch}&since={ISO-8601-window-ago}` (authoritative, survives shallow clones, consistent with `_check_recent_merge` approach).
3. Use the exact extraction regex from `_extract_linked_issue`: `grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`. Reject `Ref #NNN` and `For #NNN`.
4. Fail-open on `gh api` errors (network failure, auth expired) — log warning, return 0, allow dispatch to proceed. Identical to existing helpers.
5. Add stats counter and update `aidevops status` output.
6. Write tests with the same mock strategy as the existing test cases.

### Verification

```bash
# Shellcheck clean
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh \
  .agents/scripts/pulse-stats-helper.sh \
  .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-eligibility.sh

# All tests pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-eligibility.sh

# New counter visible in status
aidevops status | grep -q "pre_dispatch_aborts_recent_commit"
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `is_issue_eligible_for_dispatch()` returns exit code 5 when a commit on the default branch within `AIDEVOPS_PREDISPATCH_RECENT_COMMIT_WINDOW` seconds contains a valid closing keyword referencing the candidate issue number.
- [ ] `Ref #NNN` and `For #NNN` planning-reference commits do NOT trigger the new check (regex matches `pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue` exactly).
- [ ] Commits on non-default branches do NOT trigger the check.
- [ ] `pre_dispatch_aborts_recent_commit` counter increments when the new check fires and is surfaced in `aidevops status`.
- [ ] Three test cases cover: happy path, `Ref/For` negative case, different-issue negative case.
- [ ] Fail-open on `gh api` errors — gate returns 0 (allow) on network failure, matching existing helpers.
- [ ] Tests pass (`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-dispatch-eligibility.sh`) and shellcheck clean on all edited scripts.

## Context & Decisions

**Dispatch block mechanism (per @marcusquinn, comment on #20072):** The original issue used an accidental block — stampless `origin:interactive` + self-assignment — which relied on `t2148` treating this combination as an active claim. That was fragile: the 24h autonomous recovery in `normalize_active_issue_assignments` would have eventually unassigned the issue, opening it for dispatch against the author's intent. The block was switched to the explicit `no-auto-dispatch` label, which is the canonical mechanism for "do not dispatch until trigger condition met". It is stable, does not rely on session-origin plumbing, and is honoured independently of assignment state.

**Tier rationale:** `tier:standard` (not `tier:simple`). Three disqualifiers: (1) git log vs `gh api` design choice is a judgment call; (2) exit code 5 assignment needs verification against the existing contract; (3) regex precision is a known-risk area (t2204 — markdown-doesn't-shield-keywords). The pattern exists via the three sibling checks, but the worker needs to match tone and handle edge cases, not just transcribe.

**Non-goals / explicitly ruled out:**

- Scanning commits on non-default branches.
- Extending the window beyond ~10 minutes.
- Adding a commit-message check to the PR merge path (already exists in `pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue`).

**Prior art:** t2424 / GH#20030 / PR #20064 — deployed the 3-check gate. This task was deferred during that session's design phase.
