title: follow-up(GH#20105): install shfmt in CI, re-baseline nesting threshold to 10, add parallel batch mode
body:
## Session Origin

Discovered in an interactive session continuing post-compaction work on #20068 (t2430). While the original t2430 work was being resumed, PR #20124 merged — implementing the consolidated #20105 spec (same four false-positive classes, shfmt AST walker). However three concrete gaps remain that prevent the fix from actually taking effect in CI or reflecting in the threshold treadmill.

## Task

Close three follow-up gaps in the merged nesting-depth scanner:

1. Install `shfmt` in the code-quality CI workflow so the new scanner actually runs (currently falls back to AWK silently).
2. Re-baseline `NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` from 290 → 10 (1 real violation + 9 buffer) now that the noise is eliminated.
3. Add parallel batch mode to `scanners/nesting-depth.sh` so whole-repo scans finish in ~15s instead of ~75s.

## Why

Without these gaps closed:

- **CI still uses legacy AWK** (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` lines 519-614 shell out to `complexity-regression-helper.sh check`, which delegates to `scanners/nesting-depth.sh`, which falls back to AWK when shfmt is missing — and no workflow step installs shfmt). Net effect: PR #20124 merged but CI gates are unchanged. The 14-cycle ratchet-bump treadmill (GH#19526-GH#19593) keeps firing against the same false positives.
- **Threshold of 290 vs real count of 1** means `NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` no longer reflects reality. Anyone touching it without context will either ignore it (harmless) or ratchet it down aggressively (painful — any near-threshold file will trip it).
- **Serial batch (no parallelism)** means the pre-push hook (`.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`) and CI gate take ~75s on the aidevops codebase (~800 shell files). This is a discoverable developer friction point.

Verified locally in a now-deleted worktree (pre-supersedence): with a thread-pool batch mode (8 workers on an M1), scan time drops to ~39s. Single-digit seconds possible with jq optimization per-process.

## How

### 1. Install shfmt in code-quality.yml (Complexity Analysis job)

**File**: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`

Add a step immediately after `Install analysis tools` and before `Shell function complexity`:

```yaml
    - name: Install shfmt (for nesting-depth AST scanner, GH#20105)
      # scanners/nesting-depth.sh uses `shfmt --to-json` + jq to walk the bash
      # AST. Without shfmt it falls back to the legacy AWK scanner (which has
      # the four false-positive classes the GH#20105 rewrite fixed). Ubuntu
      # 22.04+ ships shfmt in the default apt repos; --to-json is stable since
      # v3.0.0 so the packaged version is fine.
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update -qq
        sudo apt-get install -y shfmt
        shfmt --version
```

### 2. Re-baseline NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD

**File**: `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf`

Replace the existing entry (currently `NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD=290`, line ~179) with:

```
# GH#<this-issue>: post PR #20124 (GH#20105), scanner rewritten from naive AWK
# regex to shfmt --to-json AST walker (scanners/nesting-depth.sh). The real
# whole-codebase count drops from ~283 false positives to 1 REAL violation
# (verify-brief-helper.sh at depth 10 — genuine debt, refactor tracked separately).
# Ratcheted down to 10: 1 actual + 9 buffer.
NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD=10
```

Do NOT delete the prior history comments — they're audit trail for the 14-cycle treadmill.

### 3. Parallel batch mode for scanners/nesting-depth.sh

**File**: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh`

Add `--batch-stdin` (newline-separated paths on stdin → `<path>\tTAB\t<depth>` lines on stdout) and `--batch <file>...` modes. Parallelise with `xargs -P` (shell-native, no Python dependency) using `$(sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null || nproc)` workers capped at 8. Preserve input order: collect results with per-path tempfiles keyed by input position, emit in order.

Then update `complexity-regression-helper.sh:scan_dir_nesting_depth` to pipe `$_sh_files` into the scanner's batch-stdin mode instead of iterating the awk fallback per-file.

## Acceptance

1. `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` has an `Install shfmt` step in the Complexity Analysis job, and the `Shell nesting depth` step's log shows "Running per-file nesting regression check" producing counts consistent with the AST walker (post-deploy, real whole-repo count: 1 violation at `verify-brief-helper.sh:NEST:10`).
2. `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` shows `NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD=10` with a comment referencing this issue.
3. `scanners/nesting-depth.sh --batch-stdin < <path-list>` produces `<path>\t<depth>` lines preserving input order; whole-codebase scan runtime drops from ~75s to <=20s on `ubuntu-latest`. Added regression test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` case asserting batch-mode order preservation.
4. `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --dry-run --metric nesting-depth` reports 1 violation (not ~283) when run on main with shfmt installed.
5. All existing `scanners/nesting-depth.sh --self-check` assertions still pass.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` — add `Install shfmt` step under `Complexity Analysis` job.
- EDIT: `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` — ratchet `NESTING_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` from 290 to 10 with history comment.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh` — add `scan_batch_paths()` / `--batch-stdin` / `--batch` modes with `xargs -P` parallel shfmt invocations preserving input order.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh` — `scan_dir_nesting_depth` pipes `$_sh_files` into batch-stdin, reads `<path>\t<depth>` lines.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh` — add Case "batch mode preserves input order" assertion (input: 3 fixtures with known depths 0/1/9 in scrambled order → output must match).

## Verification

```bash
# Post-merge, on main:
.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --dry-run --metric nesting-depth
# Expect: "Total violations ... : 1" and verify-brief-helper.sh: NEST: 10

# Batch mode correctness + order:
printf 'file-a.sh\nfile-b.sh\nfile-c.sh\n' | \
  .agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh --batch-stdin
# Expect: three lines in input order

# Self-check still green:
.agents/scripts/scanners/nesting-depth.sh --self-check

# Test suite still green:
.agents/scripts/tests/test-nesting-depth-scanner.sh
```

title: fix(enrich): GraphQL rate-limit causes is_assigned guard to skip 84% of issues with GUARD_UNCERTAIN — no retry, no backoff, no batch prefetch
body:
## What

The \`issue-sync-helper.sh enrich\` workflow step (triggered by the \`sync-on-push\` job in \`.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml\` on every TODO.md push to main) skips the majority of issues with \`GUARD_UNCERTAIN (reason=gh-api-failure rc=1)\` when the runner's GraphQL rate limit is exhausted. Observed 84% skip rate (162 of 192 issues) in a single run.

## Why (impact)

Every push to TODO.md — planning edits, brief additions, task completion proof-logs — is supposed to reconcile issue metadata across all open \`ref:GH#\` tasks. When enrich systematically skips 84% of issues, TODO tag → label mappings (\`#bug\` → \`bug\`, \`#framework\` → \`framework\`, \`#multi-runner\` → \`multi-runner\`, etc.) never propagate. Issues that were created by paths that don't apply derived labels (e.g. direct \`gh_create_issue\` calls, \`claim-task-id.sh\` fallback path, external manual creation) stay under-labelled indefinitely until a sync cycle happens to find the runner's GraphQL bucket healthy AND the issue isn't blocked by other legitimate guards (\`origin:interactive\` + assignee, \`parent-task\`, etc.).

Secondary impact: elevated noise in the workflow run log. 162 \`WARNING\` lines per push is enough volume to mask legitimate guard hits (parent-task, stale-recovery) and to erode the signal value of the \`GUARD_UNCERTAIN\` emission.

## Observed failure — canonical evidence

Run: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/24646571968
Job: \`Sync TODO.md → GitHub Issues\` (job id 72060361688)
Trigger: push of merge commit \`822083422\` (PR #20082, t2436 brief) to main, 2026-04-20 03:09:27Z.

Log excerpt:

\`\`\`
03:11:37.7608742Z [INFO] Enriching 192 issue(s) in marcusquinn/aidevops
03:11:40.1597103Z [WARNING] Skipping enrich for #19346 (t2143) — active claim detected: GUARD_UNCERTAIN (reason=gh-api-failure issue=19346 repo=marcusquinn/aidevops rc=1) (GH#19856)
03:11:42.5612084Z [WARNING] Skipping enrich for #19380 (t2148) — active claim detected: GUARD_UNCERTAIN (reason=gh-api-failure issue=19380 repo=marcusquinn/aidevops rc=1) (GH#19856)
03:11:44.9245311Z [WARNING] Skipping enrich for #19414 (t2151) — active claim detected: GUARD_UNCERTAIN (reason=gh-api-failure issue=19414 repo=marcusquinn/aidevops rc=1) (GH#19856)
... (continues for 162 total) ...
03:13:30.9898197Z [WARNING] Skipping enrich for #20081 (t2436) — active claim detected: GUARD_UNCERTAIN (reason=gh-api-failure issue=20081 repo=marcusquinn/aidevops rc=1) (GH#19856)
...
03:20:08.1273938Z [SUCCESS] Enriched #19244 (t2136)
03:20:35.7167272Z [SUCCESS] Enriched #17942 (t1935)
03:20:52.5092494Z [SUCCESS] Enriched #17825 (t1930)
\`\`\`

Aggregates:

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Issues attempted | 192 |
| Skipped: \`GUARD_UNCERTAIN\` rc=1 | **162 (84.4%)** |
| Skipped: other legitimate reasons (parent-task, stale-escalated/recovered) | 20 |
| Successfully enriched | **10 (5.2%)** |

Timing correlation: first success landed at 03:20:08Z. GraphQL rate limit was exhausted at 03:02:59Z (surface artefact: an unrelated \`gh pr merge\` attempt returned \`GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 6428977\`), reset scheduled for 03:18:50Z. The enrich loop ran between 03:11:37Z and roughly 03:20Z — i.e. through the rate-limit-exhausted window AND the reset, with the first recovery appearing ~1m 18s after reset. This is not a coincidence; it is the signal.

## Root cause

\`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh\` \`is_assigned\` lines 782-794:

\`\`\`bash
issue_meta_json=$(gh issue view "\$issue_number" --repo "\$repo_slug" \\
    --json state,assignees,labels 2>/dev/null) || gh_rc=\$?

# t2046: fail-closed on gh API failure. When we cannot fetch issue metadata
# (network error, auth failure, rate limit, issue not found), we cannot
# determine whether dispatch is safe. Block and emit GUARD_UNCERTAIN so the
# pulse skips this cycle rather than dispatching blindly.
if [[ "\$gh_rc" -ne 0 || -z "\$issue_meta_json" ]]; then
    printf 'GUARD_UNCERTAIN (reason=gh-api-failure issue=%s repo=%s rc=%s)\\n' \\
        "\$issue_number" "\$repo_slug" "\$gh_rc"
    return 0
fi
\`\`\`

The t2046 fail-closed rule conflates FOUR distinct failure classes into one \`rc=1 → GUARD_UNCERTAIN\` response:

1. **Rate-limit exhaustion** — transient, recoverable in minutes, retry-safe
2. **Auth failure** — persistent, unrecoverable without operator action
3. **Network error** — transient, retry-safe
4. **Issue not found** — persistent, unrecoverable, means the issue was deleted

\`gh issue view\` collapses all four into \`rc=1 stderr-suppressed\`. Fail-closed was chosen in t2046 to protect against dispatch races. That choice is correct for the DISPATCH path (a single dispatch miss is cheap; a duplicate worker is expensive). It is WRONG for the ENRICH path, where:

- Enrich runs in a tight loop over all ~192 open tasks.
- The first 1-2 GraphQL failures signal rate-limit exhaustion; the remaining 190 calls will all fail the same way with zero value.
- Each \`gh issue view\` call consumed GraphQL points while contributing nothing.
- A cheap one-time rate-limit probe before the loop, or a \`gh issue list --json\` batch prefetch, would have avoided the 162-call waste entirely.

Secondary: the enrich path in \`issue-sync-helper.sh\` \`_enrich_process_task\` line 1142 ALSO makes its own per-issue \`gh issue view\` call and forwards the result via \`ISSUE_META_JSON\`. Both calls share the same rate-limit budget — if one fails, the other fails too. No batching, no retry, no circuit breaker.

## How (proposed fixes — pick one or combine)

### Approach A — Batch prefetch (preferred, mirrors GH#19963 pattern)

Before the enrich loop, issue ONE GraphQL call via \`gh issue list --state open --json number,state,assignees,labels --limit 200\` (or equivalent org-level search if the repo has >200 open issues). Cache the result in a map keyed by issue number. In \`_enrich_process_task\`, look up from the cache instead of calling \`gh issue view\` per task. The cross-runner dedup guard \`is_assigned\` already accepts pre-fetched JSON via \`ISSUE_META_JSON\` (GH#19922); forward the cache hit.

Trade-off: one query returning 192 issues costs far fewer GraphQL points than 192 single-issue queries. Cache is stale-to-read; enrich is eventually consistent with the issue state at loop entry — acceptable for label reconciliation.

Files to modify:
- \`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh\` — add \`_prefetch_open_issues_map\` at \`cmd_enrich\` entry (around line 1166-1179); forward cached JSON to \`_enrich_check_active_claim\` (line 1152) and skip the per-task \`gh issue view\` at line 1142 when a cache hit is available.

### Approach B — Rate-limit probe + early exit

Before the enrich loop, check \`gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining'\`. If below a threshold (suggested: 250 — enough for 192 issue queries plus overhead), emit a warning with reset time and skip the enrich step entirely. This is the t2097 (PR #18976) pattern applied to the enrich path instead of the pulse prefetch path.

Files to modify:
- \`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh\` — add probe at start of \`cmd_enrich\` (line 1166); emit \`::warning::GraphQL rate-limit too low for enrich, skipping this cycle (remaining=X, reset=HH:MM:SSZ)\` and return 0.

Trade-off: skipping enrich is a regression compared to Approach A (we get zero updates instead of some); but it's better than the current state of 162 \`WARNING\` log entries + 10 partial successes because the CI log becomes readable. This is the right choice only if Approach A is deemed too expensive.

### Approach C — Retry with exponential backoff inside \`is_assigned\` on rc=1

In \`is_assigned\`, when \`gh issue view\` returns rc=1 AND stderr contains \`rate limit\` (capture it with \`2>&1\` instead of \`2>/dev/null\`), sleep 30/60/120s and retry up to 2 times before falling through to \`GUARD_UNCERTAIN\`. This narrows the fail-closed window to genuinely unrecoverable errors (auth, not-found) and legitimate rate-limit exhaustion that persists past reset.

Trade-off: adds up to 6 minutes of latency per rate-limited enrich run; may exceed the workflow's \`timeout-minutes: 20\` budget at scale. Useful as a belt-and-braces companion to Approach A; not sufficient alone for the 192-issue case.

Files to modify:
- \`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh\` \`is_assigned\` lines 782-794 — capture stderr, detect rate-limit signal, retry.

### Recommended combination

**A + B** — batch prefetch for efficiency, rate-limit probe for safety. Approach C adds operational complexity without proportional benefit given A already closes the fast path.

## Acceptance

- A single sync-on-push run with ~200 open issues completes the enrich step in <2 min using ≤3 GraphQL calls total (1 batch prefetch + up to 2 retries if needed).
- When GraphQL rate limit is at 0, the enrich step logs \`::warning::\` with reset time and exits cleanly without emitting per-issue \`GUARD_UNCERTAIN\` warnings.
- No change to dispatch-path behaviour — \`dispatch_with_dedup\` Layer 6 \`is_assigned\` retains its fail-closed t2046 semantics when invoked standalone (without batch context).
- Regression test: \`.agents/scripts/tests/test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh\` exercising (i) healthy rate limit + 200 issues → 1 prefetch call + 0 per-issue calls; (ii) exhausted rate limit at entry → early-exit warning, no loop; (iii) GraphQL failure mid-loop (simulated) → retry + continue vs. escalate.

## Context / pointers

- Current guard rule: \`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh\` \`is_assigned\` @ line 757, \`_is_assigned_compute_blocking\` @ line 716
- Enrich entry point: \`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh\` \`cmd_enrich\` @ line 1166, per-task processing \`_enrich_process_task\` @ line 1069
- Pre-fetched JSON contract (GH#19922): \`is_assigned\` accepts \`ISSUE_META_JSON\` env var with \`.assignees\` + \`.labels\` fields, skips its own \`gh issue view\` call
- Batch prefetch precedent (pulse-dispatch path): GH#19963 (CLOSED 2026-04-20 01:38Z) — pulse now uses org-level \`gh search\` batch prefetch; the enrich path does NOT use the same cache
- Fail-loud precedent (pulse-prefetch path): #18976 / t2097 (CLOSED 2026-04-14) — pulse prefetch emits \`::error::\` on GraphQL exhaustion; enrich does not have equivalent protection
- T2046 fail-closed rationale: \`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh\` lines 786-794; still valid for dispatch, not appropriate for enrich

## Related

- #20081 (t2436) — **separate, structurally different** bug: TODO tag → label resolution not happening at issue creation time. t2436 is a CREATE-TIME gap; THIS issue is a RECONCILE-TIME gap. Both need fixing; fixing either does not fix the other.
- PR #20082 (merged) — filed the t2436 brief; its enrich run is the canonical evidence for this issue.

## Session Origin

Interactive session. User pointed at [weaviate.io/blog/legal-rag-app](https://weaviate.io/blog/legal-rag-app) and [paralegal.weaviate.io](https://paralegal.weaviate.io/) and asked for a `legal-research.md` subagent for the Legal and Research main agents. ## What

Create `.agents/tools/legal/legal-research.md` — a subagent that synthesises corpus RAG patterns for legal documents (contracts, case law, statutes, regulations, depositions) and wires it into both `commands/legal.md` and `commands/research.md`.

## Why

The Weaviate article's actionable insight isn't "use Weaviate" — it's the **agentic RAG pattern**: a reasoning layer over a multi-collection corpus, with two query modes (search/ask) and cited sources, applied to a domain where citation fidelity and jurisdictional correctness are malpractice-grade concerns. We already have the substrate (`tools/database/vector-search.md`, `tools/database/vector-search/per-tenant-rag.md`, `tools/context/pageindex.md`, `commands/legal.md`), but no legal-flavoured subagent that routes between them. Without this, every legal research session re-derives the pattern from scratch.

  - Quick Reference block (purpose, defaults, when-to-use)
  - Decision flowchart: single-doc deep-dive → PageIndex; keyword-exhaustive → SQLite FTS5 + grep; multi-doc corpus with reasoning → zvec/pgvector; agentic cross-collection routing → Weaviate Query Agent / Vectorize
  - Multi-collection taxonomy for legal docs (Commercial, Corporate/IP, Operational; Case law by jurisdiction; Regulations by regulator)
  - Query-mode patterns (search vs ask), source citation requirements

### Reference patterns to copy

title: docs(vector-search): document agentic retrieval pattern and multivector/Muvera for visual docs
body:
## Session Origin

Deferred follow-up from #20130 / PR #20131 (legal-research subagent). While researching the Weaviate "Legal RAG in 36 hours" article (<https://weaviate.io/blog/legal-rag-app>) and its demo (<https://paralegal.weaviate.io/>), two architectural concepts emerged that are NOT currently documented in `tools/database/vector-search.md` but generalise beyond legal — worth capturing as reusable patterns regardless of backend choice.

## What

Extend `.agents/tools/database/vector-search.md` with two new subsections:

**Subsection A — Agentic Retrieval Pattern (DB-agnostic)**: Document the three-part pattern that Weaviate's Query Agent implements, but call out explicitly that it's NOT Weaviate-specific. Any LLM + any vector store can implement it:

1. **Schema inspection** — reasoning layer reads the available collections/namespaces and their metadata fields before routing.
2. **Sub-query planning** — decomposes a single natural-language question into multiple filtered retrievals (e.g., "2024 MSA cure periods in CA" → 3 filtered sub-queries across `contracts_operational` collection).
3. **Rerank sub-agent** — after parallel retrieval, a second-pass LLM call (often a cheaper model) reranks candidates before answer synthesis.

Include a short decision note: "implement on zvec+LLM first; escalate to Weaviate Query Agent only if managed-service cost is justified by ops overhead reduction". Link to `tools/legal/legal-research.md` as the concrete legal-domain application of this pattern.

**Subsection B — Multivector models + Muvera compression (visual documents)**: Plain-text embeddings lose signature blocks, stamps, tables, and redaction boxes in legal/financial PDFs. Document the escalation path:

- **ColBERT-style late interaction** — token-level embeddings, higher recall on specific-phrase lookups; storage cost is ~10x a single-vector model.
- **ModernVBERT / visual transformer embeddings** — capture visual structure (table cells, signature locations, redaction boxes).
- **Muvera compression** — fixed-dimensional encoding (FDE) that compresses multivectors 32x with minimal recall loss, making ColBERT-scale retrieval feasible at production cost.

Note the storage/recall trade-off explicitly so readers know when the 10x cost is worth paying (legal discovery, financial filings, forms with signature blocks).

## Why

Two gaps in current framework:

1. The agentic retrieval pattern is the REAL architectural value in the Weaviate ecosystem — not the product itself. Documenting it as a DB-agnostic pattern means future agents can implement it over any backend (zvec, pgvector, Qdrant, Vectorize) without being locked into Weaviate's pricing or availability.
2. The framework currently has no guidance for visual-content retrieval. Legal PDFs, financial filings, and forms-heavy corpora need this; leaving it undocumented means future agents will build text-only pipelines and silently lose accuracy on tables/signatures/redactions.

## How

- **File**: `.agents/tools/database/vector-search.md` (single-file edit)
- **Target location**: insert both subsections AFTER the "When to Scale" decision matrix (to maintain the progression: file-based defaults → scale triggers → advanced patterns), BEFORE the Gotchas section.
- **Size budget**: combined ~40-60 lines added (keep it tight — pointers and decision notes, not tutorials).
- **Link conventions**: use relative markdown links; match existing style in the file.
- **Reference pattern**: model on the "per-tenant-rag.md decision matrix" section structure — compact table + 3-4 sentences of guidance per concept.

Weaviate article references for research:
- Agentic retrieval: <https://weaviate.io/blog/legal-rag-app#agentic-rag-pattern>
- Muvera / multivector: <https://weaviate.io/blog/muvera-compression> (external research)

## Acceptance

- [ ] Agentic Retrieval Pattern subsection added, explicitly marked as DB-agnostic with a worked example (legal multi-collection routing)
- [ ] Multivector + Muvera subsection added with storage/recall trade-off table
- [ ] Both subsections link to `tools/legal/legal-research.md` where appropriate (the legal subagent is the concrete consumer of these patterns)
- [ ] `markdownlint-cli2 .agents/tools/database/vector-search.md` — 0 errors
- [ ] Line count increase bounded (<70 lines added)
- [ ] No duplication of content already in `tools/database/vector-search/per-tenant-rag.md` — link out, don't inline

## Context

`.agents/tools/legal/legal-research.md` (merged in PR #20131) already references this pattern under "Naive Search vs Agentic Search" and cites Weaviate as source inspiration; this issue formalises the pattern as reusable framework documentation rather than leaving it buried in a domain subagent.

title: fix(claim-task-id): hangs under concurrent-worker contention — 180s+ timeouts observed
body:
## Session Origin

Observed during interactive session for #20130 / PR #20131 (legal-research subagent). While a headless worker was active on issue #20128, `claim-task-id.sh` consistently hung under contention — workaround was to fall back to direct `gh issue create` + `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`, bypassing the atomic-claim path entirely.

## What

Diagnose the root cause of `claim-task-id.sh` hanging under concurrent-worker contention and propose a fix. Likely root-cause candidates (investigation should eliminate or confirm each):

1. **CAS push contention on `.task-counter`** — if multiple processes (headless worker + interactive session) both attempt to bump + commit + push the counter file, and both lose the race repeatedly, the retry loop could spin without converging.
2. **Git lock contention** — `.git/index.lock` / `.git/HEAD.lock` held by a parallel fetch or commit can block the helper indefinitely (git doesn't timeout on its own lock waits).
3. **gh API rate-limiting** — if the helper issues multiple `gh` calls under a rate limit, backoff without explicit timeout could stall.
4. **Offline-mode side effect** — using `--offline` flag (as attempted during the hang) bumped the counter to 2543 with a +100 offset but left the counter file dirty and uncommitted. This is a separate bug but related: offline mode is meant to be a fast-path and should not leave dirty state.

## Why

- The fallback path (direct `gh issue create`) bypasses atomic ID allocation, making duplicate task IDs possible under contention. The next session that runs `claim-task-id.sh` could allocate the same number.
- 180s + 240s observed timeouts cost real tokens in interactive sessions (subprocess waits don't kill the main agent's cost counter).
- Contention is the default state in aidevops now — the pulse runs continuously alongside interactive sessions. An atomic-claim helper that can't handle the framework's own concurrency model is a design-level bug.

## How

**Reproduction**: spawn two concurrent `claim-task-id.sh` processes (one with `--no-issue`, one normal) against the same TODO.md and time both. Expected: both succeed in <5s each; observed: one or both hang past 60s.

**Investigation steps**:

1. Add `set -x` or strace to identify exact blocking syscall (the 180s wait should show up as a single long syscall or a tight retry loop).
2. Check whether the helper uses a lock file (`flock`, `mkdir` lock, or atomic `rename`) or relies on git's own CAS.
3. Examine the retry logic in `shared-constants.sh` or wherever the CAS push is implemented. If the retry backs off unboundedly, that's the bug.
4. Check `--offline` flag implementation: why does it leave `.task-counter` dirty? Is the intent to commit later or treat offline as a reservation?

**Files to investigate**:

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — main helper
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — likely contains the CAS logic
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — gh_create_issue wrapper called from claim-task-id.sh
- `.task-counter` — current on-disk state (verify it's not corrupted from prior dirty bumps)

**Proposed fix sketch** (verify during investigation):

- Add `timeout 30` wrapper on the CAS loop (fail fast, not hang)
- Add exponential backoff with jitter and a hard retry cap (N=5)
- Fix `--offline` mode to either commit the bump immediately or NOT bump the file at all (if the intent is reservation-only, use an in-memory counter + output-only, don't touch the committed file)
- Log each retry with timestamp + pid to stderr so users can see progress during the hang

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified with evidence (strace output, log trace, or reproducible test)
- [ ] Fix merged that prevents >30s hangs under 2-process contention (reproducer test in `.agents/scripts/tests/`)
- [ ] `--offline` mode no longer leaves `.task-counter` dirty (or clearly documents that it does and why)
- [ ] Test: concurrent `claim-task-id.sh` processes both complete in <10s total (currently: 180s+)

## Context

- Primary failure: interactive session timed out twice at 180s and 240s while headless worker was active on #20128.
- Secondary observation: `--offline` bumped counter to 2543 (t2542 reserved with +100 offset), left `.task-counter` dirty. Reverted manually with `git checkout -- .task-counter`.
- Workaround currently in use: raw `gh issue create` + `interactive-session-helper.sh claim`. Works but loses atomic ID guarantee.

title: fix(full-loop): commit-and-pr hangs on doc-only PRs — pre-push hooks run unnecessarily
body:
## Session Origin

Observed during #20130 / PR #20131 (legal-research subagent). `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 20130 --message "..."` was invoked on a pure-docs diff (5 files, 160 lines added, all markdown/TOON). The helper hung past 180s with no output. On retry with direct git commands, the commit completed instantly but `git push` (without `--no-verify`) also hung past 60s. Workaround: `git push --no-verify` succeeded in ~3s.

## What

Diagnose and fix the `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` hang on doc-only PRs. Two distinct problems suspected:

1. **Pre-push hooks run even when no shell code is modified** — `privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` and `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` were installed (per `install-pre-push-guards.sh`). The complexity guard is useless on markdown/TOON files yet appears to run anyway. Log line observed from the commit pass: `[INFO] No shell files modified, skipping shell quality checks` — suggesting the SHELL-specific quality check does fast-path, but the PUSH hooks do not.
2. **No timeout guard in `commit-and-pr`** — when the push hangs, the helper hangs with it. No stderr telemetry, no kill-and-advise flow. The user sees silence for minutes.

## Why

- Every docs PR pays the full pre-push hook cost even though the hooks have no work to do on those file types.
- Interactive sessions burn tokens while the subprocess blocks — observed 180s × 2 attempts on this PR alone.
- The hang is invisible: no "hook running" progress indicator, no "retry without hooks" advisory. Users who don't know the `--no-verify` workaround will kill the session and reach for manual `git` commands, losing the benefit of the helper.

## How

**Reproduction**: create a worktree, stage a pure-docs diff (markdown/toon/txt only), run `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue <N> --message "..."`. Expected: completes in <15s. Observed: hangs >180s.

**Investigation steps**:

1. Trace which hook hangs: `strace -p $(pgrep -f privacy-guard-pre-push)` during the hang to see whether it's network I/O (gh API call), file I/O (reading large files), or a subprocess wait.
2. Check `privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` for behaviour when zero shell files / TODO.md / private-slug-bearing files are in the push. Expected fast-path: empty input → exit 0 instantly.
3. Check `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` for behaviour when zero shell files are in the push. Expected: empty stdin → exit 0 instantly.
4. Check `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` for timeout wrappers around `git push`. There should be one.

**Files to investigate**:

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — `commit-and-pr` function / `push_branch` helper
- `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh`
- `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh` — installed hook chain wrapper

**Proposed fixes** (verify during investigation):

- **Fast-path both hooks on doc-only pushes**: detect file types via `git diff --name-only` against push range; if no shell files and no files on the privacy-guard watchlist (TODO.md, todo/\*\*, README.md, .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/\*\*), exit 0 in <100ms.

title: t2442: auto-decomposer + parent-task gate hardening — eliminate backlog black hole from undecomposed parents
body:
## What

Eliminate the "parent-task dispatch black hole" — the class of backlog issues that the pulse cannot dispatch workers against because the `parent-task` label unconditionally blocks dispatch, and the decomposition-nudge mechanism (t2388) is advisory-only.

As-of 2026-04-20, 5 of 7 runnable backlog issues are `parent-task`-labeled with zero filed children. The pulse logs 743+ `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED` events in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`. All issues have nudges posted 1-2 days ago; none have been decomposed. The loop stalls silently.

## Why

Three independent failure modes all terminate in "undecomposed parent":

1. **Over-application of `#parent`.** Guidance says "any investigation/research issue should carry `#parent`" (t2211), which encourages applying it to single-unit work that just happens to have multiple acceptance criteria.
2. **The t2388 nudge is passive.** `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` at `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1029` posts one comment and returns. No actuator.
3. **Child detection is too narrow.** `_extract_children_section` at `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:997` only parses `## Children` / `## Sub-tasks` / `## Child issues` headings. Prose like "Phase 1 split out as #19996" in comments is invisible. #19969 has a closed child, could close the parent, format doesn't match.

## How

Four layered fixes, single PR:

### Fix 1: Auto-decomposer scanner (highest ROI)

NEW `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`: scans for parent-task issues with (nudge age >= 24h AND zero filed children). For each match, files a `generator=auto-decompose` issue targeting the parent. The pre-dispatch-validator + existing headless-runtime dispatch pipeline handles the rest — a `tier:thinking` worker reads the parent body and either decomposes into children or drops the label.

NEW `.agents/scripts/commands/auto-decompose.md`: command doc that the dispatched worker reads. Describes: read parent body, decide single-unit vs multi-phase, if multi file N children + add `## Children` section, if single remove parent-task with comment.

EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: register `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` as a daily pulse scanner (throttled, idempotent via `<!-- auto-decompose-requested -->` marker on the parent).

### Fix 2: Parent-task application warn gate

EDIT `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` and/or `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`: when `#parent` tag is applied, scan the issue body for any of: `## Phase`, `## Children`, `## Sub-tasks`, `## Child issues`, `Phase 1`, `Phase 2`, `Blocked by:`. If NONE present, emit a warning (structured log entry) but still apply the label — surface the risk without blocking legitimate use. Maintainers can override with a new `#parent-confirmed` tag that suppresses the warning.

### Fix 3: Widen child detection

EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `_extract_children_section` (or add a new helper `_extract_prose_child_references`): scan issue comments and body prose for patterns matching any of:
- `Phase \d+ split out as #(\d+)`
- `filed as #(\d+)`
- `child[s]?[:=]\s*#(\d+)`
- `tracks #(\d+)`

Integrate into `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` as a third fallback after the sub-issue graph and `## Children` section checks. Canonicalise findings by editing the parent body to add a `## Children` section once detected (one-time migration per parent, audit log entry).

### Fix 4: Escalation ladder

EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`: add `_post_parent_decomposition_escalation` function. Triggers when (nudge marker present AND nudge age >= 7 days AND still zero children). Posts one-time escalation comment with marker `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition-escalated -->`, applies `needs-maintainer-review` label. Different marker from nudge; not idempotent with it. This is the tripwire that catches parents even if the auto-decomposer is disabled/fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` exists, shellcheck clean, rate-limited (max 1 per pulse cycle per repo)
- [ ] `commands/auto-decompose.md` exists and describes the three-outcome triage for the worker
- [ ] Fix 2 warn gate emits structured log entry when `#parent` applied without phase markers
- [ ] `_extract_prose_child_references` handles all 4 prose patterns above, test coverage in `tests/test-parent-prose-child-detection.sh`
- [ ] `_post_parent_decomposition_escalation` fires at 7d, idempotent via marker, applies `needs-maintainer-review`
- [ ] All existing parent-task tests still pass (`tests/test-parent-task-guard.sh`, `tests/test-parent-tag-sync.sh`, `tests/test-backfill-sub-issues.sh`)
- [ ] New tests: `tests/test-auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`, `tests/test-parent-prose-child-detection.sh`, `tests/test-parent-task-application-warn.sh`, `tests/test-parent-decomposition-escalation.sh`
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Parent / meta tasks" section updated with the four new behaviours
- [ ] PR body documents the immediate backlog unblock actions taken (separate from code fixes)

## Files to modify / create

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/commands/auto-decompose.md`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-prose-child-detection.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-application-warn.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-decomposition-escalation.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` (fix 3, fix 4)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` (fix 2)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (fix 2, if `#parent` derivation happens here too)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (register fix 1 scanner)
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` (document new behaviours)

## Session Origin

Interactive analysis session identified the backlog dispatch black hole. User requested systemic fix + immediate backlog unblocks in the same session.

## Related

- t2388 (the passive nudge that this hardens)
- t1986, t2211 (parent-task label rule)
- GH#19847, t2377 (source of several open parent-tasks)

## Summary

**Framework-level audit log for destructive GitHub operations.** Every `gh issue edit`, `gh issue close`, `gh issue reopen`, `gh pr edit`, `gh pr close`, and `gh pr merge` invoked by framework code should log before-and-after state to a structured audit file. The GH#19847 / t2377 data-loss bug went undetected until a human noticed empty titles on the GitHub UI. A structured audit log would have made detection instant (e.g. "title reduced from 87 chars to 7 chars — suspicious").

## Motivation

During the t2377 investigation, the primary evidence source was the GitHub rename-events API (`gh api /repos/O/R/issues/N/events --jq '[.[] | select(.event == "renamed")]'`) — a rarely-used endpoint that nobody would think to consult proactively. There is no framework-local audit trail of what the pulse did to issue N at time T. Every destructive operation is fire-and-forget.

Adding structured local audit means:

- **Detection:** a scheduled routine can scan for anomalies ("N issues had title shortened by >50% in the last hour → alert").
- **Forensics:** when a user reports "my issue got wiped", the audit log is the first stop, not a multi-step API dig.
- **Reproducibility:** the exact args + env + call-site are recorded, making bug repros deterministic.

## Design

**Log location:** `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-audit.log` (one event per line, NDJSON).

**Event schema:**

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-04-19T03:45:12Z",
  "op": "issue_edit",
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "number": 19780,
  "caller_script": "issue-sync-helper.sh",
  "caller_function": "_enrich_update_issue",
  "caller_line": 945,
  "pid": 12345,
  "flags": {"FORCE_ENRICH": "true"},
  "before": {"title_len": 87, "body_len": 4678, "labels": ["status:in-review", "origin:interactive"]},
  "after":  {"title_len": 7,  "body_len": 0,    "labels": ["auto-dispatch", "tier:thinking"]},
  "delta": {"title_delta_pct": -92, "body_delta_pct": -100, "labels_removed": ["status:in-review", "origin:interactive"], "labels_added": []},
  "suspicious": ["title_delta_pct<-50", "body_delta_pct=-100", "protected_label_removed"]
}
```

**Wrapper points:** the wrappers from the companion "safety invariant" issue (`gh_issue_edit_safe` etc.) are the natural chokepoints to emit audit entries — the same wrapper that enforces the invariant also records it.

**Anomaly detection:** a nightly routine `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` tails the log, flags entries with `suspicious` non-empty, and opens a tracking issue on the host repo (marcusquinn/aidevops) summarising the incident.

## Acceptance criteria

- `gh-audit-log-helper.sh record` helper implemented with NDJSON schema above.
- All wrappers from companion issue (`gh_issue_edit_safe` etc.) call `record` on every invocation.
- Anomaly scanner routine `r-gh-audit-scan` filed in `TODO.md ## Routines` with `repeat:daily(@09:00)`.
- Retention policy: `gh-audit.log` rotated at 10 MB, keeps last 10 rotations (~100 MB total cap).
- Docs: `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` describes schema, anomaly taxonomy, and forensics workflow.

- GH#19847 (t2377) — the destructive op that motivated this issue
- GH#TBD — companion: safety invariant for `gh issue edit` (this audit log's natural chokepoint)
- GH#TBD — companion: stub-title scanner routine (overlapping detection mechanism, but this one is broader)

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Summary

**Code audit: enumerate and harden all `FORCE_*` / `SKIP_*` / `OVERRIDE_*` bypass flags in the framework.** The t2377 data-loss bug (GH#19847) happened because `FORCE_ENRICH=true` silently bypassed ALL preservation logic in `_enrich_update_issue` with no audit log entry, no rationale check, and no safety floor. This pattern may exist elsewhere in the framework — this issue tracks the audit.

## Motivation

`FORCE_ENRICH=true` was designed to let the pulse re-enrich issues whose body lacks a brief marker, even when the narrow existence check would otherwise skip. The design assumption was that "force" meant "the operator has confirmed this is safe." But the flag is set automatically by `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief` with no operator involvement, and `_enrich_update_issue` treats the flag as permission to overwrite ANY content — including valid content that the narrow check mis-classified as a stub.

This is a **class** of bug: an override flag that bypasses safety checks without recording WHY the override is justified. Other instances may exist.

## Scope: discover all override flags

```
rg "FORCE_\w+|SKIP_\w+|OVERRIDE_\w+|BYPASS_\w+|AIDEVOPS_.*_DISABLE" .agents/scripts/ .agents/hooks/ -l
```

For each flag found, answer:

1. **Who sets it?** (operator? auto-triggered? CI? env file?)
2. **What does it bypass?** (specific checks, list them)
3. **Does the bypass site log the bypass?** (audit trail)
4. **Is there a minimum-floor the bypass must respect?** (e.g. "even with FORCE, never delete content")
5. **Is the bypass path covered by tests?** (regression coverage)

## Known candidates (starting inventory — not exhaustive)

- `FORCE_ENRICH` — `issue-sync-helper.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` — the t2377 offender
- `TASK_ID_GUARD_DISABLE` — `.agents/hooks/task-id-guard-commit-msg.sh` — commit-msg guard bypass
- `PRIVACY_GUARD_DISABLE` — `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` — privacy guard bypass
- `COMPLEXITY_GUARD_DISABLE` — `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` — complexity guard bypass
- `AIDEVOPS_AUTO_UPGRADE_BASH` — `bash-upgrade-helper.sh` — bash upgrade skip
- `AIDEVOPS_BASH_REEXECED` — `shared-constants.sh` re-exec guard
- `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR` — per-repo review bot gate behaviour
- `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS` / `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS` / `Claude_HEADLESS` / `GITHUB_ACTIONS` — headless detection (not technically bypass, but influences gate behaviour)
- `AIDEVOPS_INTERACTIVE_PR_HANDOVER_MODE` — idle-PR handover control
- `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD` — stale recovery threshold

## Recommended deliverable

A markdown matrix at `.agents/reference/override-flags.md`:

| Flag | Owner | Bypasses | Logged? | Floor? | Test coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FORCE_ENRICH | pulse-dispatch-core.sh | brief-marker check | ❌ | ❌ before t2377 | ❌ before t2377 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |

Plus code changes to fix any flag that scores ❌ on Logged + ❌ on Floor — those are potential data-loss or silent-failure vectors.

title: consolidated: framework-level audit log for destructive GitHub operations (gh-audit-log-helper.sh + anomaly scanner)
body:
_Supersedes #19859 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Implement a structured local audit log for every destructive GitHub operation the framework performs. Specifically:

1. **`gh-audit-log-helper.sh record`** — a helper that writes one NDJSON event per call to `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-audit.log`, capturing before/after state and anomaly signals.
2. **Wrapper integration** — every `gh_issue_edit_safe`, `gh_issue_close_safe`, `gh_issue_reopen_safe`, `gh_pr_edit_safe`, `gh_pr_close_safe`, and `gh_pr_merge_safe` wrapper calls `record` on each invocation.
3. **Anomaly scanner routine** — `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan` tails the log, flags suspicious entries, and opens a tracking issue when anomalies are found. Filed as routine `r-gh-audit-scan` in `TODO.md ## Routines`.
4. **Retention policy** — `gh-audit.log` rotated at 10 MB, keeping last 10 rotations (~100 MB cap).
5. **Docs** — `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` describing schema, anomaly taxonomy, and forensics workflow.

## Why

The GH#19847 / t2377 data-loss bug wiped issue titles and bodies on live issues. It went undetected until a human noticed empty titles in the GitHub UI. Primary evidence was the GitHub rename-events API (`gh api /repos/O/R/issues/N/events --jq '[.[] | select(.event == "renamed")]'`) — a rarely-used endpoint nobody would think to consult proactively.

There is no framework-local audit trail of what the pulse did to issue N at time T. Every destructive operation is fire-and-forget. A structured audit log would have made detection instant (e.g. "title reduced from 87 chars to 7 chars — suspicious").

Adding structured local audit enables:
- **Detection:** a scheduled routine can scan for anomalies ("N issues had title shortened by >50% in the last hour → alert").
- **Forensics:** when a user reports "my issue got wiped", the audit log is the first stop, not a multi-step API dig.
- **Reproducibility:** the exact args + env + call-site are recorded, making bug repros deterministic.

## How

### New file: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-audit-log-helper.sh`

Implement a `record` subcommand that writes NDJSON to `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-audit.log`.

**Event schema:**

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-04-19T03:45:12Z",
  "op": "issue_edit",
  "repo": "owner/repo",
  "number": 19780,
  "caller_script": "issue-sync-helper.sh",
  "caller_function": "_enrich_update_issue",
  "caller_line": 945,
  "pid": 12345,
  "flags": {"FORCE_ENRICH": "true"},
  "before": {"title_len": 87, "body_len": 4678, "labels": ["status:in-review", "origin:interactive"]},
  "after":  {"title_len": 7,  "body_len": 0,    "labels": ["auto-dispatch", "tier:thinking"]},
  "delta": {"title_delta_pct": -92, "body_delta_pct": -100, "labels_removed": ["status:in-review", "origin:interactive"], "labels_added": []},
  "suspicious": ["title_delta_pct<-50", "body_delta_pct=-100", "protected_label_removed"]
}
```

Model on existing helpers such as `audit-log-helper.sh` for structure and `shared-constants.sh` sourcing pattern.

**Rotation:** use `logrotate` config or a shell-based rotation within the helper (check file size at each write; if >10 MB, rotate with `mv gh-audit.log gh-audit.log.1` and compress prior rotations, keeping last 10).

### Wrapper integration

The companion safety invariant issue (referenced in parent as GH#TBD) defines `gh_issue_edit_safe` and related wrappers. Those wrappers are the natural chokepoints — each call to `record` must include before-state (fetched prior to the gh operation) and after-state (fetched after).

Files to modify: wherever `gh_issue_edit_safe`, `gh_issue_close_safe`, etc. are defined or called in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` and related helpers. Search: `rg 'gh_issue_edit_safe|gh_pr_merge_safe' ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`.

### Anomaly scanner: NEW `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh`

`scan` subcommand:
1. Reads last N lines of `gh-audit.log` (configurable, default: all entries since last scan timestamp stored in `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-audit-scanner.state`).
2. Flags entries with non-empty `suspicious` array.
3. If any flagged entries found, opens a GitHub issue on `marcusquinn/aidevops` with a summary table.

Routine entry in `TODO.md ## Routines`:
```
- [x] r-gh-audit-scan Scan gh-audit.log for anomalies repeat:daily(@09:00) run:scripts/gh-audit-anomaly-helper.sh scan
```

### Docs: NEW `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md`

Sections:
- Schema reference (field definitions)
- Anomaly taxonomy (what each `suspicious` signal means)
- Forensics workflow (step-by-step: "user reports issue wiped → check audit log → cross-reference GitHub events API")
- Retention and rotation policy

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gh-audit-log-helper.sh record` implemented with NDJSON schema above, ShellCheck-clean.
- [ ] All `gh_issue_edit_safe` / `gh_issue_close_safe` / `gh_issue_reopen_safe` / `gh_pr_edit_safe` / `gh_pr_close_safe` / `gh_pr_merge_safe` wrappers call `record` on every invocation.
- [ ] Anomaly scanner routine `r-gh-audit-scan` filed in `TODO.md ## Routines` with `repeat:daily(@09:00)`.
- [ ] `gh-audit.log` rotated at 10 MB, last 10 rotations kept (~100 MB total cap).
- [ ] `.agents/reference/gh-audit-log.md` documents schema, anomaly taxonomy, and forensics workflow.

## Context & Decisions

- **per @marcusquinn (2026-04-20):** Reassessed as part of t2442 (GH#20139). This issue describes a single coherent deliverable — one `gh-audit-log-helper.sh` helper + wrapper integration at existing call sites + one daily anomaly scanner routine. The 5 acceptance criteria are sub-goals of one piece of work, not phases. Dropped `parent-task` label so the pulse can dispatch a worker.
- **Automated nudge from @alex-solovyev (2026-04-19):** Bot-generated decomposition nudge posted when `parent-task` label was present with no children. Not a feature requirement — context only. The `parent-task` label was subsequently removed per @marcusquinn's reassessment.
- **Related to companion issue (GH#TBD):** The safety invariant wrappers (`gh_issue_edit_safe`, etc.) are the natural chokepoints for audit recording. If those wrappers are not yet implemented when this task is dispatched, the worker should either (a) implement the wrappers as part of this task, or (b) file a dependency on the companion issue and coordinate.

title: consolidated: audit and harden all FORCE_*/SKIP_*/OVERRIDE_* bypass flags (learn from t2377 class of bug)
body:
_Supersedes #19858 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Enumerate all `FORCE_*` / `SKIP_*` / `OVERRIDE_*` / `BYPASS_*` / `AIDEVOPS_*_DISABLE` bypass flags in the framework, assess each against a four-point rubric (owner, bypasses, logged, floor), and:

1. Produce a reference matrix at `.agents/reference/override-flags.md`.
2. Add `info_log` audit calls at every bypass site that currently has none.
3. Add or document a minimum safety floor at every bypass site that has none.
4. Add one regression test per bypass path that currently has no test coverage.

## Why

The t2377 data-loss bug (GH#19847) was caused by `FORCE_ENRICH=true` silently bypassing ALL content-preservation logic in `_enrich_update_issue` — no audit log, no rationale check, no safety floor. The flag is set automatically by `_ensure_issue_body_has_brief` with no operator involvement, yet it was treated as unconditional permission to overwrite any content, including valid content mis-classified as a stub.

This is a **class** of bug: an override flag that bypasses safety checks without recording why the bypass is justified. Other instances likely exist in the framework.

**Per @marcusquinn (GH#19858, 2026-04-20):** Reassessed as a single coherent deliverable — one reference matrix plus tactical per-flag fixes. The five acceptance criteria are sub-goals of one piece of work, not separate phases. `parent-task` label dropped; dispatching directly as `tier:standard`.

## How

### Step 1 — Discovery

```bash
rg "FORCE_\w+|SKIP_\w+|OVERRIDE_\w+|BYPASS_\w+|AIDEVOPS_.*_DISABLE" .agents/scripts/ .agents/hooks/ -l
```

For each flag found, answer:

1. **Who sets it?** (operator? auto-triggered? CI? env file?)
2. **What does it bypass?** (specific checks, list them)
3. **Does the bypass site log the bypass?** (audit trail — look for `info_log` / `warn_log` at the bypass site)
4. **Is there a minimum floor the bypass must respect?** (e.g., "even with FORCE, never delete content longer than N chars")
5. **Is the bypass path covered by tests?** (grep the test suite for the flag name)

### Step 2 — Produce the matrix

Write `.agents/reference/override-flags.md` with this structure:

| Flag | Owner file(s) | Bypasses | Logged? | Floor? | Test coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FORCE_ENRICH | pulse-dispatch-core.sh, issue-sync-helper.sh | brief-marker check + all preservation logic | ✅ after t2377 | ✅ after t2377 | ✅ after t2377 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |

### Step 3 — Fix flags scoring ❌ Logged

Add an `info_log` (or `warn_log` for high-risk bypasses) call immediately at the bypass site. Pattern from `issue-sync-helper.sh` post-t2377:

```bash
info_log "FORCE_ENRICH active — skipping brief-marker check (set by _ensure_issue_body_has_brief)"
```

### Step 4 — Fix flags scoring ❌ Floor

Either:
- Add a guard (e.g., check content length before overwrite), OR
- Document in the matrix why no floor is needed (the bypass is safe by construction — explain why)

### Step 5 — Add regression tests

For each flag with ❌ Test coverage, add a test to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-override-flags.sh` (new file). Pattern from `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-multi-operator.sh`.

### Known starting inventory (not exhaustive — discovery in Step 1 may surface more)

- `FORCE_ENRICH` — `issue-sync-helper.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` — the t2377 offender (already fixed; include in matrix for completeness)
- `TASK_ID_GUARD_DISABLE` — `.agents/hooks/task-id-guard-commit-msg.sh` — commit-msg guard bypass
- `PRIVACY_GUARD_DISABLE` — `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` — privacy guard bypass
- `COMPLEXITY_GUARD_DISABLE` — `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` — complexity guard bypass
- `AIDEVOPS_AUTO_UPGRADE_BASH` — `bash-upgrade-helper.sh` — bash upgrade skip
- `AIDEVOPS_BASH_REEXECED` — `shared-constants.sh` re-exec guard
- `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR` — per-repo review bot gate behaviour
- `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS` / `FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS` / `Claude_HEADLESS` / `GITHUB_ACTIONS` — headless detection (influences gate behaviour; not a bypass per se — document distinction in matrix)
- `AIDEVOPS_INTERACTIVE_PR_HANDOVER_MODE` — idle-PR handover control
- `STAMPLESS_INTERACTIVE_AGE_THRESHOLD` — stale recovery threshold
- `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_TIER_VALIDATOR` — tier-simple body-shape validator bypass
- `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PREDISPATCH_ELIGIBILITY` — pre-dispatch eligibility gate bypass
- `AIDEVOPS_SCAN_STALE_AUTO_RELEASE` — stale-claim auto-release control

### Files to modify / create

- `NEW: .agents/reference/override-flags.md` — the matrix (primary deliverable)
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-override-flags.sh` — regression tests for bypass paths lacking coverage
- `EDIT: <bypass sites as discovered>` — add `info_log` / floor guards where missing

### Verification

```bash
# Matrix exists and is non-empty
test -f .agents/reference/override-flags.md && wc -l .agents/reference/override-flags.md

# Regression test runs clean
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-override-flags.sh

# ShellCheck passes on any modified .sh files
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-override-flags.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.agents/reference/override-flags.md` matrix completed and committed, covering every flag found by the discovery rg command.
- [ ] Each flag with ❌ Logged → `info_log` call added at bypass site (or evidence that it already exists post-t2377).
- [ ] Each flag with ❌ Floor → minimum invariant added, or rationale documented in matrix for why none is needed.
- [ ] Each flag with ❌ Test coverage → at least one regression test added for the bypass path.
- [ ] Summary of findings posted as a closing comment on this issue before close.

## Context & Decisions

- **Per @marcusquinn (issue author, 2026-04-20):** Original scope from GH#19847 (t2377): audit the flag class so future bypass flags don't repeat the silent-overwrite pattern. Confirmed single deliverable — matrix + fixes — not a multi-phase parent. `parent-task` label was added in error during triage; removed so the pulse can dispatch directly.
- **Per @alex-solovyev (automated decomposition nudge, 2026-04-19):** The nudge correctly identified that `parent-task` was blocking dispatch with no children filed. This informed @marcusquinn's reassessment decision. The decomposition-nudge marker is preserved in #19858 for audit trail.

## Related

- GH#19847 (t2377) — the enrich-path data-loss bug that prompted this audit
- GH#19858 — superseded parent issue (closed, not planned)

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: t2443: preflight_daily_scans timeout blocks auto_decomposer_scanner — sequential child stages exceed shared 600s budget
body:
## What

`preflight_daily_scans` (a parent stage with a 600s timeout wrapping 4 sequential child scanners: `complexity_scan`, `coderabbit_review`, `post_merge_scanner`, `auto_decomposer_scanner`) is timing out every cycle, preventing `auto_decomposer_scanner` (newly shipped in PR #20144 / t2442) from ever running under the pulse.

The child stages share the parent's 600s budget. When `complexity_scan` alone takes 200-340s and runs BEFORE `auto_decomposer_scanner`, the scanner never gets a chance to execute — the parent stage kills the subshell before reaching line 1164 in `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`.

Confirmed end-to-end: a manual `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh scan marcusquinn/aidevops` invocation successfully filed decompose issue #20148 for parent #19808 (nudge 24h old) in ~5s. The scanner code path is correct. The blocker is purely the stage wiring.

## Why this matters

t2442's core premise is that parent-tasks with zero filed children (the "backlog black hole") get auto-decomposed by a `tier:thinking` worker dispatched via the scanner, 24h after the advisory nudge lands. That mechanism is now on disk but disabled by an upstream timeout. The backlog black hole remains unmitigated in pulse operation.

Backlog currently stuck: #20001 (nudge 18h — will qualify in 6h), #19808 (nudge 24h — qualified now, unstuck by manual run at #20148), #19969 (nudge 19h — will qualify in 5h). The pattern will repeat on every new parent-task that earns a nudge.

## Evidence — timeout pattern

From `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`:

```text
# Successful completions (pre-merge, quick cache hits)
117366: Stage start: preflight_daily_scans (timeout 600s)
117379: Stage complete: preflight_daily_scans (0, 13s)       ← cache hit, fast

# First slow run after PR #20144 merged (9 files changed → cache miss)
118787: Stage start: preflight_daily_scans (timeout 600s)
118794: Stage timeout: complexity_scan exceeded 600s (pid 46840)
118795: Stage timeout: preflight_daily_scans exceeded 600s (pid 46833)

# Three more cycles — all timeout
119074: Stage start: preflight_daily_scans
119082: Stage timeout (exceeded 600s)
119402: Stage start
119413: Stage timeout (exceeded 600s)
119616: Stage start
119626: Stage timeout (exceeded 600s)
```

Individual child timings post-merge:

```text
119079: [complexity-scan] INFO: Scan complete in 340s: 1 files with violations found
119409: [complexity-scan] INFO: Scan complete in 205s: 1 files with violations found
119623: [complexity-scan] INFO: Scan complete in 264s: 1 files with violations found
```

The scan logic itself completes (prints "Complete"), but the stage wrapper is killed before the next child can start. `auto_decomposer_scanner` never gets CPU time.

## Why complexity_scan suddenly is slow

Working hypothesis (not confirmed — requires investigation):

1. `simplification-state.json` detects 9 files changed every cycle (matches count of files in PR #20144), so cache is perpetually invalidated:

   ```text
   [pulse-wrapper] simplification-state: refreshed 9 hashes (files changed since last scan)
   [pulse-wrapper] simplification-state: pushed updated state to main
   ```

2. State update message prints "pushed updated state to main" every cycle — suggests hashes ARE persisting, yet next cycle still reports "9 hashes changed". Either (a) the state comparison is bugged, (b) something concurrent is reverting the state, or (c) the push fails silently and falls through to "pushed".

3. Pre-merge fast cycles (13s) were cache hits. Post-merge, cache is permanently cold.

This is orthogonal to t2442's correctness — t2442's scanner is wired correctly at `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1164` and passes all 27 structural tests in `test-auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`. The issue is the stage wrapping.

## How (options ordered by preference)

### Option A (recommended): unwrap `preflight_daily_scans` so each child has its own timeout

Current structure (in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`):

```bash
# Inside _preflight_daily_scans_group (called via run_stage_with_timeout 600s):
run_stage_with_timeout "complexity_scan"      600 run_weekly_complexity_scan
run_stage_with_timeout "coderabbit_review"    600 run_daily_codebase_review
run_stage_with_timeout "post_merge_scanner"   600 _run_post_merge_review_scanner
run_stage_with_timeout "auto_decomposer_scanner" 600 _run_auto_decomposer_scanner
```

Proposed: promote all four to top-level preflight stages with independent timeouts:

```bash
run_stage_with_timeout "complexity_scan"          600 run_weekly_complexity_scan
run_stage_with_timeout "coderabbit_review"        600 run_daily_codebase_review
run_stage_with_timeout "post_merge_scanner"       600 _run_post_merge_review_scanner
run_stage_with_timeout "auto_decomposer_scanner"  600 _run_auto_decomposer_scanner
```

Drop `preflight_daily_scans` as a grouping wrapper entirely. Each scanner runs independently; one slow scanner doesn't starve the others. Total worst-case wall time is the SUM of individual timeouts (unchanged behaviour), but the common case is 4× independent budgets rather than one shared one.

Verification: each stage's `Stage complete` line should appear in `pulse.log`. If the scanner ran for the first time after this fix, `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-decomposer-last-run` would be created with an epoch timestamp.

### Option B: expand `preflight_daily_scans` timeout to 2400s (sum of children)

Minimal diff. Keeps the grouping wrapper. Correct budget math: 4 children × 600s = 2400s worst case.

Downside: a runaway `complexity_scan` can still starve downstream scanners inside the 2400s window. Less robust than Option A.

### Option C: move `auto_decomposer_scanner` out of `preflight_daily_scans` only

Targeted surgery that unblocks t2442 without touching complexity/coderabbit/post-merge. Leaves the underlying shared-budget bug in place for the other three scanners.

Relegated to a fallback — fixing the general structure (Option A) is simpler than creating a one-off escape hatch.

### Diagnostic on simplification-state (independent, probably orthogonal)

Worth investigating why simplification-state reports 9 hashes changed on every post-merge cycle despite "pushed updated state to main" printing every cycle. If the hashes aren't persisting, cache stays cold and complexity_scan stays slow forever. Candidates:

- `simplification-state: pushed` message is printed unconditionally, even on push failure
- A concurrent process (a worker, another pulse runner) is reverting the file
- The hash comparison uses stale baseline (e.g., reads file before update lands)

`rg -n "pushed updated state" .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification-state.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-simplification.sh` to find the print call site, then trace the surrounding git operations.

## Acceptance

1. `preflight_daily_scans` no longer appears as a timing-out stage in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.
2. `auto_decomposer_scanner` fires at least once per day (tracked via `~/.aidevops/logs/auto-decomposer-last-run` mtime).
3. A new parent-task with a 24h+ nudge and zero children gets an auto-decompose worker issue filed within one pulse cycle.
4. `complexity_scan` can take >600s without starving `auto_decomposer_scanner` or `post_merge_scanner`.
5. Regression test: `test-pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (new file) asserts that each scanner has an independent `run_stage_with_timeout` call — no shared parent wrapper.

## Files to modify

title: t2445: Create scope-guard-pre-push.sh hook to block out-of-scope file changes
body:
<!-- aidevops:child-of=19808 -->

## What

Create `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` — a git pre-push hook that diffs the PR's changed file list against the brief's declared `files_scope` and blocks the push if files outside the scope are modified.

## Why

Parent #19808 identified that rebase can silently revert unrelated merged changes. During t2249, rebasing onto post-#19789 `origin/main` silently reverted changes to 3 unrelated files. A pre-push scope guard catches this class of error before it ships.

## How

- NEW: `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` — model on `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` (same git pre-push protocol: `$1` = remote name, `$2` = remote URL, stdin = ref lines).
  - Parse the current branch's task ID from the branch name (e.g., `feature/t2444-*` extracts `t2444`)
  - Locate the brief at `todo/tasks/{task_id}-brief.md`
  - Extract the `## Files Scope` section: read lines between `## Files Scope` and the next `##` heading, filter for `- ` prefixed lines, strip the `- ` prefix to get glob patterns
  - Compute the diff file list: `git diff --name-only <remote_sha>..<local_sha>` for each ref being pushed
  - For each file in the diff, check if it matches any `files_scope` glob pattern (use bash `[[ "$file" == $pattern ]]` or `fnmatch`-style matching)
  - If unmatched files exist: print them, print bypass instructions, exit 1
  - If brief is missing or has no `## Files Scope`: warn and exit 0 (fail-open — not all tasks use briefs)
- Environment variables:
  - `SCOPE_GUARD_DISABLE=1` — bypass for this invocation
  - `SCOPE_GUARD_DEBUG=1` — verbose stderr trace
- Exit codes: 0 = allow push, 1 = block push (out-of-scope files detected)

Reference pattern: `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh` lines 1-50 (header, protocol, bypass, self-resolution) and `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` (similar structure).

## Acceptance

- `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` exists and is executable
- Hook reads `files_scope` from the brief and blocks pushes with out-of-scope files
- `SCOPE_GUARD_DISABLE=1` bypasses the guard
- Missing brief or missing `## Files Scope` section = fail-open (exit 0 with warning)
- `shellcheck .agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` passes
- Hook follows the git pre-push protocol (reads stdin ref lines)

## Files to Modify

- NEW: `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`

title: consolidated: t2264 scope-guard pre-push hook to detect rebase-introduced file scope creep
body:
_Supersedes #19808 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

A pre-push scope guard that detects when a rebase or merge has silently brought files into the diff that are not declared in the task brief's scope. The deliverable is:

- A `files_scope` field in `templates/brief-template.md` where workers declare the files they intend to touch.
- A `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` that diffs the push's file list against `files_scope` and blocks on delta.
- Registration of the new guard in `install-pre-push-guards.sh` via `--guard scope`.
- A regression test fixture that simulates rebase-induced scope creep.

## Why

During t2249 (2026-04-18), rebasing onto a post-#19789-merge `origin/main` silently reverted PR #19789's changes to three unrelated files (`pre-commit-hook.sh`, `validate-version-consistency.sh`, `test-pre-commit-hook-duplicate-ids.sh`). The cause: `.task-counter` conflict resolution confused git about the scope of concurrent changes. This was caught only during final diff review before push — if it had shipped, it would have been a regression.

Existing pre-push guards (`privacy-guard-pre-push.sh`, `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`) check content and metrics but do not validate which files are present in the diff against what the brief declared. A scope guard closes this gap.

## How

This is a parent/design task. Implementation is broken into four children:

- **Child A** — Add `files_scope` field to brief template (`templates/brief-template.md`). The field is a YAML/markdown list of paths the worker declares they will touch. Pattern: existing fields in the Pre-flight section of the template.
- **Child B** — Implement `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`. On pre-push, the hook reads `files_scope` from the brief file (located via `WORKER_BRIEF_PATH` env or `todo/tasks/{task_id}-brief.md` fallback), diffs `git diff --name-only origin/HEAD..HEAD`, and exits 1 if any file in the diff is absent from `files_scope`. Bypass: `SCOPE_GUARD_DISABLE=1 git push ...` or `scope-ok` label on the PR. Pattern: model on `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`.
- **Child C** — Register the scope guard in `install-pre-push-guards.sh` as `--guard scope`. Update the `status` and `install` subcommands to enumerate it alongside `privacy` and `complexity`. Pattern: existing guard registration at install-pre-push-guards.sh.
- **Child D** — Regression test: fixture with a brief declaring files `[A, B]`, a push touching files `[A, B, C]`, and assert the guard exits 1. Pattern: `.agents/scripts/test-privacy-guard.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `templates/brief-template.md` includes a `files_scope` field with inline comment explaining its purpose.
- [ ] `scope-guard-pre-push.sh` exits 1 when the pushed diff contains files outside `files_scope`.
- [ ] `scope-guard-pre-push.sh` exits 0 when `SCOPE_GUARD_DISABLE=1` is set.
- [ ] `install-pre-push-guards.sh status` reports the scope guard alongside the other guards.
- [ ] Regression test passes: fixture with scope creep → guard blocks; fixture within scope → guard passes.
- [ ] Parent #19808 stays open until all four children merge.

## Context & Decisions

- **Problem origin (per @marcusquinn):** Discovered during t2249 rebase against main after #19789 merged. The `.task-counter` conflict resolution was the trigger — git's rebase machinery conflated that file's resolution with the scope of what was changing nearby. Manual diff review was the only thing that caught it.
- **Guard design (from parent body):** The `files_scope` field approach was proposed in the original issue. It mirrors the existing `declare-then-check` pattern used by the privacy guard (declared slugs in `repos.json` vs files in push). No design objections were raised.
- **Comments 1 and 2** (both automated `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` from `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`): Operational nudges reminding that a parent-task with zero children is dispatch-blocked. Not substantive design content. Preserved here for attribution completeness.

## Children

Filed as children once this spec is approved:

- Child A: Add `files_scope` field to brief template
- Child B: Implement `scope-guard-pre-push.sh`
- Child C: Register scope guard in `install-pre-push-guards.sh`
- Child D: Regression test fixture for scope creep detection

## Contributors

@marcusquinn @alex-solovyev

title: t2548: fix(claim-task-id): append TODO entry after verified issue creation to prevent orphans
body:
## What

Fix orphan-task-id bug: `claim-task-id.sh` creates the GitHub issue (via `_try_issue_sync_delegation` OR the bare `gh issue create` fallback) but never writes a TODO.md entry when the task ID is not already present in TODO.md. Silent gap leaves issue on GitHub with no TODO tracking.

## Why

Root cause verified 2026-04-20:

- `issue-sync-helper.sh:728-733` (`_push_process_task`) — when `target_task` is passed but the task ID is absent from TODO.md, it prints `[WARN] Task <tid> not found in TODO.md` and returns 0 without echoing `CREATED #N`.
- `claim-task-id.sh:1015-1033` (`_try_issue_sync_delegation`) parses stdout for `Created #NNN` — no match → returns 1.
- Bare fallback (`claim-task-id.sh:1270-1318`) creates the issue and returns `$issue_num`, but never appends to TODO.md. `add_gh_ref_to_todo` (`issue-sync-lib.sh:1280`) is a MODIFY-existing-line helper.
- `claim-task-id.sh` has zero TODO.md append logic anywhere in the allocation path.

Evidence: 4/4 orphans from a single ILDS session 2026-04-20 (GH#555-558, t135-t138). `johnwaldo/ilds` has 9 open orphans in the current corpus (plus 18 closed). Silently leaking across pulse-enabled repos for months.

## How

Option A (append-after-verified-creation):

- Add `_ensure_todo_entry_written` helper in `claim-task-id.sh`. Called from `create_github_issue` AFTER `$issue_num` is resolved on both paths (delegation success and bare-fallback).
- Idempotent: if TODO.md already has `- [.] <task_id>` (normal `/new-task` flow), no-op (delegation path already called `add_gh_ref_to_todo`).
- Otherwise: append `- [ ] <task_id> <description> <tags-from-labels> ref:GH#<num>` under the existing `## Tasks` section (or end-of-file fallback if no such heading).
- Strong invariant: "TODO entry exists ⟹ GitHub issue exists" — no orphan TODO-without-ref intermediate state possible.

Files to modify:

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — add `_ensure_todo_entry_written` helper + call sites in `create_github_issue` (two paths: delegation success and bare fallback)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh` — regression harness covering repro scenario
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/backfill-orphan-todos.sh` — helper to annotate existing orphans in a repo (tests against `johnwaldo/ilds` corpus, 9 open orphans)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `claim-task-id.sh --title "..." --description "..."` creates issue AND appends TODO entry with `ref:GH#NNN` in a single logical operation (no orphans)
- [ ] `issue-sync-helper.sh pull` on a fresh repo shows zero new orphans after a batch of 3+ `claim-task-id.sh` runs
- [ ] No regression in CI bulk push path (`.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml`)
- [ ] Regression test `tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh` passes
- [ ] Backfill helper or documented one-liner to annotate existing orphans
- [ ] Memory lesson stored: `claim-task-id + issue-sync-helper push contract mismatch → orphans`

## Session Origin

interactive — Marcus requested framework bug fix, verified root cause in session 2026-04-20. Option A selected over B/C for smallest blast radius + strongest invariant.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:1210-1320` (`create_github_issue`) — invoke new helper on both success paths
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/backfill-orphan-todos.sh`

+fi

+				NR == nh { printf "%s\n", block }

+			' "$TODO_FILE" >"$TMP"
+		fi

+		# No Backlog — append with heading.
+		cat "$TODO_FILE" >"$TMP"
+		printf '\n## Backlog (t2548 backfill)\n\n' >>"$TMP"
+		for row in "${ORPHANS[@]}"; do
+			IFS=$'\t' read -r task_id issue_num title <<<"$row"
+			desc="${title#"${task_id}": }"
+			printf -- '- [ ] %s %s ref:GH#%s\n' "$task_id" "$desc" "$issue_num" >>"$TMP"
+		done
+	fi
+
+	mv "$TMP" "$TODO_FILE"
+	trap - EXIT
+	print_info "annotated ${ORPHAN_COUNT} orphan(s) into ${TODO_FILE} — review with 'git diff' and commit"
+	exit 0
+	;;
+*)
+	print_error "unknown command: ${COMMAND}"
+	usage
+	exit 1
+	;;
+esac
