title: t2564: docs(opencode): document project_id drift and /sessions session visibility recovery
body:
## Task

Add a `## Project ID drift — /sessions loses history` section to `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` documenting how opencode's `project_id` drift causes the TUI `/sessions` picker to hide historic sessions, and the SQL recipe to recover them.

## Why

Opencode 1.14.19 identifies git-tracked projects by a git commit SHA stored in `session.project_id`. When opencode regenerates this SHA (on binary update, git rebase, or certain reference events), all prior sessions orphan out of the TUI `/sessions` view — they are not deleted, just unreachable. A live diagnosis in the aidevops repo found 696 sessions orphaned on an old project_id after the opencode-ai binary updated on 2026-04-20. Remapping with a one-line SQL `UPDATE` restored full visibility. This recovery recipe should live in the canonical opencode-maintenance reference so the next hit is a 2-minute fix instead of a multi-hour diagnosis.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` — insert new section between line 120 (end of `## State` section, the `— append-only history` line) and line 121 (start of `## Related upstream issues`).

## How

Edit `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` with this exact replacement:

**oldString:**

````text
— append-only history

## Related upstream issues
````

**newString:**

````text
— append-only history

## Project ID drift — /sessions loses history

**Symptom:** The TUI `/sessions` picker shows only the current session (or a handful of recent ones), not the full history. Closing and reopening opencode does not help.

**Cause:** Opencode identifies git-tracked projects by a **git commit SHA** stored in `session.project_id`. The `/sessions` picker filters by the *current* session's `project_id`. When opencode regenerates this SHA (binary update, rebase, or certain git reference events), prior sessions orphan onto the old `project_id` and disappear from the picker. They are NOT deleted.

**Diagnose:** Close opencode TUI first, then inspect the DB:

```bash
# List project_ids seen for a given repo directory, ordered by session count
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT project_id, COUNT(*) FROM session
    WHERE directory='/absolute/path/to/repo'
    GROUP BY project_id ORDER BY 2 DESC;"
```

If two or more project_ids appear, the one with the highest count is the orphaned history; the one the TUI currently uses is whichever matches a new session (usually lower count).

**Fix:** Remap orphaned sessions to the current project_id. Close the opencode TUI first to avoid WAL lock contention:

```bash
# Replace OLD_SHA and NEW_SHA with the actual values from the diagnose step
sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "UPDATE session SET project_id='NEW_SHA' WHERE project_id='OLD_SHA';"
```

Reopen the TUI — `/sessions` now shows the full history.

**Archive DB:** `opencode-archive.db` is not read by the TUI regardless of `project_id`. No remap is needed there unless you are restoring archived sessions (in which case apply the same remap to the archive DB before running `opencode-db-archive.sh restore`).

## Related upstream issues
````

## Acceptance

- `.agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` contains a new `## Project ID drift — /sessions loses history` section between the existing `## State` section and the `## Related upstream issues` section.
- Section has four subsections: Symptom, Cause, Diagnose, Fix (with Archive DB note).
- The SQL commands use the DB path `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`.
- No other content in the file is modified.
- `npx --yes markdownlint-cli2 .agents/reference/opencode-maintenance.md` passes.

## Tier checklist

- [x] 1 file modified (≤2 required)
- [x] Target file under 500 lines (140 lines)
- [x] Exact oldString/newString blocks provided
- [x] No skeleton code blocks, no error/fallback logic to design
- [x] Estimate ≤1h
- [x] 5 acceptance criteria — single logical deliverable split by topic for clarity
- [x] No judgment keywords

title: consolidated: t2452 fix — revert t2449 mis-closure + CI guard against brief-enhancement PRs using closing keywords
body:
_Supersedes #20194 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Two-part correction to address the t2449 mis-closure and prevent the underlying anti-pattern from recurring:

1. **Revert t2449 completion marker** in `TODO.md` (around line 411): undo `[x] t2449 ... pr:#20185 completed:2026-04-20` back to `[ ]` — PR #20185 only enhanced the brief file (`todo/tasks/t2449-brief.md`), not the actual implementation. The symmetric auto-merge work remains unshipped.

2. **CI guard against brief-enhancement PRs using closing keywords**: if a PR only touches `todo/tasks/*.md` files (or other planning paths) AND uses closing keywords (`Closes`, `Fixes`, `Resolves`), the check must warn or block. This is the markdown foot-gun rule from `prompts/build.txt` (Traceability section) applied as a server-side enforcement gate.

## Why

PR #20185 was a brief-only PR (touching only `todo/tasks/t2449-brief.md`) but its body contained `Resolves #20164`, which auto-closed the implementation issue on merge. The actual t2449 implementation (symmetric auto-merge for `origin:interactive` PRs) was never shipped, but TODO.md was marked `[x]` as if it had been.

This is the markdown foot-gun anti-pattern documented in `prompts/build.txt` §Traceability: "Markdown formatting is INVISIBLE to the extraction regex." The same logic applies to brief-only PRs — the closing keyword in the PR body triggers both GitHub's auto-close machinery and the `issue-sync.yml` TODO completion path regardless of which files the PR touches.

A CI guard (modelled on `.github/workflows/parent-task-keyword-check.yml`) enforces this at push time rather than relying on contributor discipline.

## How

### Part 1: Revert t2449 completion in TODO.md

- **EDIT: `TODO.md`** — around line 411, change:
  ```
  [x] t2449 ... pr:#20185 completed:2026-04-20
  ```
  to:
  ```
  [ ] t2449 ...
  ```
  (strip `pr:#20185` and `completed:2026-04-20` suffixes, restore `[ ]`)

- PR body MUST use `For #20194` and `For #20164` (NOT `Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`) since the PR only touches planning files (`TODO.md`). Per `prompts/build.txt` Traceability rule.

**Status:** PR #20201 was opened by @marcusquinn for this part and is still open. Verify whether it has merged before re-implementing — if not yet merged, pick it up rather than duplicating.

### Part 2: CI guard — planning-pr-keyword-check.yml

- **NEW: `.github/workflows/planning-pr-keyword-check.yml`** — model on `.github/workflows/parent-task-keyword-check.yml`

  Logic:
  1. Trigger on `pull_request` event targeting the default branch (`main`)
  2. Get the list of changed files: `gh pr view ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} --json files -q '.files[].path'`
  3. If ALL changed files match planning paths (`todo/tasks/*.md`, `todo/**`, `TODO.md`, `PLANS.md`):
     - Scan the PR body for closing keywords: `grep -iE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`
     - If found: fail the check with a message explaining the foot-gun and linking to `prompts/build.txt` §Traceability
  4. Otherwise: pass (mixed diffs with code files are allowed to use closing keywords)

- **Reference pattern:** model on `.github/workflows/parent-task-keyword-check.yml` which already does PR-body keyword scanning with file-filter logic

- **Verification:** 
  ```bash
  # Should fail: brief-only diff with Resolves keyword
  # Should pass: brief-only diff with For #NNN keyword
  # Should pass: mixed diff (code + brief) with Resolves keyword
  ```

### Part 3 (follow-up — file as separate tasks)

Per @marcusquinn Comment 1 on #20194 — out of scope for this issue:

- **(B)** Harden stale-claim recovery to respect `Deferred` / `DO NOT dispatch` body markers
- **(C)** Worker prompt reinforcement on honouring body instructions

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `TODO.md` t2449 entry is reverted to `[ ]` with no `pr:` / `completed:` suffix (confirmed merged via PR #20201 or a new PR)
- [ ] `.github/workflows/planning-pr-keyword-check.yml` exists and triggers on `pull_request`
- [ ] The workflow fails a PR body containing `Resolves #NNN` when the diff is brief-only (`todo/tasks/*.md` only)
- [ ] The workflow passes a PR body containing `For #NNN` on a brief-only diff
- [ ] The workflow passes a PR body containing `Resolves #NNN` on a mixed diff (code + brief)
- [ ] No regression in existing `parent-task-keyword-check.yml` behaviour

## Context & Decisions

- **Root cause** (per @marcusquinn): PR #20185 was a brief-only PR that used `Resolves #20164`. GitHub's auto-close + `issue-sync.yml` TODO completion both triggered on merge, marking t2449 done despite the implementation being unshipped.

- **PR keyword strategy** (per @marcusquinn Comment 1 on #20194): planning-file-only PRs MUST use `For #NNN` or `Ref #NNN`, never `Closes/Resolves/Fixes`. Already documented in `prompts/build.txt` §Traceability; the CI guard makes it machine-enforced server-side.

- **Part 1 status** (per @marcusquinn Comment 1 on #20194): PR #20201 was opened for the TODO.md revert (title: "t2452: revert t2449 false-completion from PR #20185 miscarriage"). Still open as of consolidation. Pick it up rather than duplicating.

- **Implementation context gap** (per @alex-solovyev Comment 2 on #20194): two consecutive worker failures on #20194 were caused by the original issue body lacking file paths and implementation steps. This consolidated spec addresses that with explicit paths and a reference pattern.

## Contributors

cc @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn

title: bug: dispatch safety bypass + nudge loop on parent-task #20161 (3 cooperating factors)
body:
## What

Investigate and fix the cooperating dispatch-safety bugs that kept #20161 in an infinite `parent-needs-decomposition` nudge loop for 6+ hours until a triage session manually closed it.

## Why

#20161 carried every documented "do not dispatch" signal:

- `parent-task` label (rule t1986: unconditional dispatch block)
- No assignee (maintainer-gate pre-check GH#17810)
- Narrative `## Children` section (not parseable to `#NNNN` — correct per t2244, but interacts poorly with nudge fire)

Yet it was dispatched to at least one worker (the session that triaged and closed it on 2026-04-21 01:22 UTC). While open, two peer pulse runners (`@marcusquinn`, `@alex-solovyev`) posted 19+ identical `parent-needs-decomposition` nudge comments between 2026-04-20 18:32 and 2026-04-21 01:09 — roughly one every 20-30 minutes.

This pattern indicates at least two dispatch guards were silently bypassed and one nudge loop has no escape condition. The combination is expensive (token burn) and noisy (comment spam).

## How — three cooperating factors

### Factor 1: Parent-task dispatch guard bypass

- **Documented behaviour:** `parent-task` label unconditionally blocks dispatch via `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh is-assigned` returning `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED` (per t1986, `AGENTS.md` user guide).
- **Observed:** #20161 had `parent-task` label continuously since at least 2026-04-20 18:32 (first nudge timestamp) and was dispatched anyway.
- **Investigation needed:** audit `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` and every code path that dispatches a worker to find the one that bypassed the guard. Test: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-guard.sh` presumably covers the helper — if it passes, the bypass is in a caller.

### Factor 2: Nudge loop has no escape when narrative children are already implemented

- **Documented behaviour:** `_post_parent_task_decomposition_nudge` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` fires after 24h-since-`parent-task`-applied when children count is 0, with a dedup marker preventing re-post (per t2388).
- **Observed:** 19+ nudges on #20161 with the same `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` marker. Either dedup marker check is failing, OR the dedup marker was intentionally stripped, OR multiple peer runners are racing the dedup check.
- **Hypothesis:** the dedup marker check may be per-runner/per-machine rather than per-comment. With `@marcusquinn` and `@alex-solovyev` as concurrent peers on different hosts, each sees "no nudge from me yet" and posts. Investigate: does `_post_parent_task_decomposition_nudge` check the ENTIRE thread for the marker, or only comments authored by `$(gh api user)`?
- **Secondary missing escape:** even without the dedup bug, the nudge should ALSO check whether the described children have been implemented elsewhere (e.g., via commit message scanning for the child identifiers, or PR merge history). #20161's prose listed children that had already merged under predecessor #19808 — the nudge had no way to notice.

### Factor 3: No-assignee dispatch

- **Documented behaviour:** GH#17810 maintainer gate pre-check blocks dispatch when linked issue has no assignee. Both `full-loop-helper.sh start` and the pulse dispatch path are supposed to enforce this.
- **Observed:** #20161 has never had an assignee (confirmed via `gh api repos/.../issues/20161` — `assignees: []`), yet was dispatched.
- **Investigation needed:** audit the dispatch path for the code that should apply the no-assignee block.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified for Factor 1 (parent-task bypass). Regression test added covering the specific bypass path.
- [ ] Root cause identified for Factor 2 (dedup failure OR missing completion-aware escape). Fix implemented such that nudges stop after N posts (configurable) OR after detecting the described children are already merged.
- [ ] Root cause identified for Factor 3 (no-assignee bypass). Regression test added.
- [ ] Manual reproduction of the #20161 scenario against current `main` shows zero worker dispatches and at most one nudge comment.

## Reference evidence

- Closed parent: #20161 (closing comment has full timeline)
- Predecessor parent (where children actually shipped): #19808
- Children PRs (all merged): #20162, #20165, #20167, #20199 + follow-ups #20178, #20181
- Planning PR (filed children against 19808): #20159
- Nudge comment authors: `@marcusquinn`, `@alex-solovyev` (peer pulse runners)

## Files likely to need audit

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — `is-assigned` Layer 6, `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED` path
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — `_post_parent_task_decomposition_nudge`, dedup marker check
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — `start` subcommand maintainer gate pre-check
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — pre-dispatch eligibility layers
- `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh` — t2424 eligibility gate (is `parent-task` one of its checks?)

## Verification

Reproduce #20161 against local `main`: create a test issue with `parent-task` + `tier:thinking` + `origin:worker` + no assignee + narrative `## Children` section. Run the pulse against it. Expected: no dispatch, no nudge spam. Actual (pre-fix): at least one dispatch + repeating nudges.

title: t2567: harden collision guard to detect reuse without claim commit (Phase 1 of #20001)
body:
_Child of #20001 (Phase 1 of 3) — siblings: Phase 2 #20221, Phase 3 #20223._

## What

Harden `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` so that any commit referencing a `tNNN` ID requires a corresponding `chore: claim tNNN [nonce]` commit to exist on the current branch between `merge-base` and `HEAD`. This closes the reuse-without-claim gap exposed by the t2377 incident.

**Scope (Phase 1 only):**
- Modify `_check_message()` in `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh`.
- Add a `_check_branch_has_claim()` helper that walks `merge-base..HEAD` looking for `chore: claim <tid>` commits.
- Reject when a t-ID is cited but no matching claim exists on this branch AND no linked issue title confirms the ID.
- Add a test reproducing the t2377 pattern under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.

Phase 2 (mkdir mutex) and Phase 3 (audit log) are tracked as separate children — do NOT land them in this PR.

## Why

On 2026-04-19, two distinct tasks were filed under `t2377`:
- Session A legitimately claimed it via `claim-task-id.sh` (CAS commit `08741df4e`).
- Session B hardcoded `t2377` in an issue and brief commit without calling `claim-task-id.sh`.

The existing guard caught the "invention" case (t-ID > current counter) but missed the "reuse" case (t-ID ≤ counter but never claimed on THIS branch). Recovery required manual rename, audit trail cleanup, and memory updates — ~1h of wasted work for a single low-frequency incident.

**Gap:** `task-id-collision-guard.sh` checks "was this t-ID ever claimed?" (via counter + linked issues) but never checks "did THIS branch claim it?". Phase 1 adds exactly that check.

Per @marcusquinn's investigation on #19874: Phase 1 alone would have caught the t2377 incident. Phases 2-3 are defence-in-depth.

## How

**File to modify:** `EDIT: .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` (478 lines — note: the consolidated parent #20001 cited the wrong path `.agents/scripts/...`; the canonical location is `.agents/hooks/`).

**Target function:** `_check_message()` at lines 257-327. (Parent cited `_check_subject_ids()` — that name does not exist; the real function is `_check_message`.)

### Step 1 — Add a branch-claim scanner helper

After `_find_merge_base()` (line 132-148) and before `_extract_tids()` (line 154), add a new helper:

```bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Check whether a given t-ID has a matching claim commit on the current
# branch between merge-base and HEAD. The claim commit subject must match
# `chore: claim tNNN[..tMMM] [nonce]` (single or range form — see
# allocate_counter_cas in claim-task-id.sh lines 684-689).
#
# Returns 0 if a claim commit is found, 1 otherwise.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_branch_has_claim() {
	local tid="${1:-}"
	local base
	base=$(_find_merge_base)
	if [[ -z "$base" ]]; then
		_debug "merge-base empty — cannot verify branch claim, allowing"
		return 0
	fi
	# Match single claim: "chore: claim t001 [nonce]"
	# Match range claim:  "chore: claim t001..t003 [nonce]"
	# Use git log with %s (subject) and grep for the tid as word.
	local num
	num=$(printf '%s' "$tid" | tr -d 't')
	if ! [[ "$num" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
		return 1
	fi
	# Look for an exact single-ID claim first.
	if git log --format='%s' "${base}..HEAD" 2>/dev/null |
		grep -qE "^chore: claim t0*${num}( |\$|\\[)"; then
		return 0
	fi
	# Look for a range claim that covers num: chore: claim tA..tB
	local line low high
	while IFS= read -r line; do
		# Extract tA and tB from "chore: claim t00A..t00B [nonce]"
		if [[ "$line" =~ ^chore:\ claim\ t0*([0-9]+)\.\.t0*([0-9]+) ]]; then
			low="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
			high="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
			if ((10#$num >= 10#$low && 10#$num <= 10#$high)); then
				return 0
			fi
		fi
	done < <(git log --format='%s' "${base}..HEAD" 2>/dev/null)
	return 1
}
```

### Step 2 — Integrate into `_check_message()`

In `_check_message()` (lines 257-327), inside the `while IFS= read -r tid` loop (lines 294-319), replace the current "≤ counter means allowed" short-circuit:

**oldString (lines 302-308):**
```
		# Force base-10 (10#) so leading-zero IDs like "008", "068" don't trip
		# bash's octal parser. Same root cause as the _compute_counter_seed bug
		# in claim-task-id.sh — both fixed in this PR (GH#19620).
		if ((10#$num <= 10#$counter)); then
			_debug "$tid ≤ counter ($counter) — allowed"
			continue
		fi
```

**newString:**
```
		# Force base-10 (10#) so leading-zero IDs like "008", "068" don't trip
		# bash's octal parser. Same root cause as the _compute_counter_seed bug
		# in claim-task-id.sh — both fixed in this PR (GH#19620).
		if ((10#$num <= 10#$counter)); then
			# Phase 1 (t2567 / GH#20001): reuse-without-claim detection.
			# A t-ID ≤ counter exists globally, but must be claimed on THIS
			# branch. If no matching `chore: claim tNNN` commit is found on
			# merge-base..HEAD, fall through to the linked-issue check so the
			# worker can still authorise via `Resolves/Closes/Fixes/Ref/For
			# #NNN` (matching issue title). If neither claim commit nor
			# linked issue confirms, this becomes a violation (reuse).
			if _branch_has_claim "$tid"; then
				_debug "$tid claimed on this branch — allowed"
				continue
			fi
			_debug "$tid ≤ counter but no branch claim — verifying via linked issues"
			local verify_rc
			_verify_tid_via_issues "$tid" "$closing_issues"
			verify_rc=$?
			if [[ "$verify_rc" -eq 2 ]]; then
				return 2
			fi
			if [[ "$verify_rc" -eq 1 ]]; then
				violations="${violations}  ${tid} — ≤ counter ${counter}, but no 'chore: claim ${tid}' commit on this branch and no linked issue title contains ${tid}\n"
			fi
			continue
		fi
```

### Step 3 — Update the violation message

In `_report_violations()` at lines 235-248, tweak the "Subject references invented" header to also cover the reuse case. The tightest change:

**oldString (line 238):**
```
	printf '\n[task-id-guard][BLOCK] Commit subject references invented task ID(s):\n\n' >&2
```

**newString:**
```
	printf '\n[task-id-guard][BLOCK] Commit subject references invented or unclaimed task ID(s):\n\n' >&2
```

### Step 4 — Regression test

Create `.agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard-reuse.sh` modelled on the existing `test-task-id-collision-guard.sh`. It should:

1. Build a throw-away git repo with `.task-counter=100`.
2. Author `chore: claim t100 [sessA]` on a branch `sessA/foo` (simulates Session A).
3. Switch to a NEW branch `sessB/bar` off base (no claim on this branch).
4. Attempt to commit a file with subject `t100: do something` — the hook must reject.
5. Repeat on `sessA/foo` — hook must allow (claim commit exists on that branch).
6. Verify `TASK_ID_GUARD_DISABLE=1` still bypasses.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` (4 changes: new helper function, 2 substitutions in `_check_message`, 1 in `_report_violations`)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard-reuse.sh`

## Files Scope

- .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard-reuse.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_branch_has_claim()` helper added with single- and range-form claim detection.
- [ ] `_check_message()` rejects commits referencing a t-ID when neither a branch claim nor a linked-issue title confirms it.
- [ ] `TASK_ID_GUARD_DISABLE=1` bypass continues to exit 0 without running any of the new checks.
- [ ] Regression test reproduces the t2377 pattern and is blocked by the guard.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh` passes with zero violations.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-task-id-collision-guard-reuse.sh
# Manual smoke (must REJECT):
echo "t100: something" > /tmp/msg && TASK_ID_GUARD_DEBUG=1 \
  .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh /tmp/msg
# Manual smoke (must ALLOW — bypass):
TASK_ID_GUARD_DISABLE=1 .agents/hooks/task-id-collision-guard.sh /tmp/msg
```

## Context

- Parent: #20001 (this phase is the **only** change that would have caught the t2377 incident; Phases 2-3 are defence-in-depth).
- The existing `_verify_tid_via_issues()` at lines 185-227 already handles the cross-reference case (worker cites another person's task via `Resolves/Closes/Fixes/Ref/For #NNN`). Phase 1 adds the branch-history check as the preferred signal, falling back to issue verification.
- `_find_merge_base()` at lines 132-148 already picks origin/main as the base when available, so the branch-claim scan terminates at the right ancestry for feature branches and worktrees.
- Claim-commit subject format is fixed by `allocate_counter_cas()` in `claim-task-id.sh:684-689`: `chore: claim tNNN [nonce]` (single) or `chore: claim tNNN..tMMM [nonce]` (range). No other formats are valid.

## PR Conventions

- PR title: `t2567: harden collision guard to detect reuse without claim commit`
- PR body: use `Ref #20001` (parent is a `parent-task` — Phase 1 PR must NOT close it; only the final phase PR closes the parent per the t2046 rule).
- Labels: `bug`, `framework`, `tier:standard`, `auto-dispatch`.

title: t2568: add mkdir-based local mutex around claim-task-id CAS loop (Phase 2 of #20001)
body:
_Child of #20001 (Phase 2 of 3) — siblings: Phase 1 #20220, Phase 3 #20223._

## What

Wrap the `allocate_online()` retry loop in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` with a portable machine-local `mkdir`-based mutex, so concurrent agents on the same host serialise their CAS attempts at the fetch→read→commit→push boundary. The authoritative gate is still the git push (`--force-with-lease`-equivalent ref update on origin/main); this lock merely reduces wasted CAS commits and retry budget when two local sessions race.

**Scope (Phase 2 only):**
- Modify `allocate_online()` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (lines 705-760) to acquire/release a host-local `mkdir` lock.
- Choose a lock path under `~/.aidevops/locks/` so multiple repos on the same host still coordinate on the *claim* primitive.
- Bounded wait: give up after a configurable timeout (default 10s) and fall through to the usual retry loop — local lock MUST NOT become a deadlock.

Phase 1 (guard reuse detection) and Phase 3 (audit log) are separate children — do NOT land them in this PR.

## Why

The CAS implementation in `allocate_counter_cas()` is sound — `git push` returning non-zero on conflict is the authoritative gate. But when two agents on the same machine race, each one:

1. Runs `_cas_fetch_and_pin` (network round-trip).
2. Builds a commit (cheap).
3. Pushes (network round-trip; one wins, one loses).
4. Loser retries: fetch + push again.

Under observed contention in t2377-era worker storms, we saw >30 CAS attempts burn out the retry budget because two local workers kept colliding with each other AND with the pulse. A cheap host-local mutex cuts this dramatically: local workers serialise at step 1, only one network round-trip per slot, and the retry budget is spent on *real* cross-host contention (remote workflows, other machines).

`flock(1)` is the obvious choice but macOS lacks it in the default /usr/bin. `pulse-wrapper.sh` solves this with a `mkdir`-based lock pattern (atomic on all POSIX filesystems). Re-use that pattern here.

## How

**File to modify:** `EDIT: .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (2003 lines — parent #20001 cited "lines ~580-645" which is where `_cas_fetch_and_pin` / `_cas_build_and_push` live; the cleaner wrapping point is `allocate_online()` at lines 705-760, which contains the retry loop).

### Step 1 — Lock helpers

Add two helpers at the top of `claim-task-id.sh` (near the other private helpers, after the `log_*` section around line 180-220 — pick the nearest section boundary):

```bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Machine-local mutex for CAS serialisation (Phase 2 / t2568 / GH#20001).
# macOS has no flock(1); use atomic mkdir as the lock primitive.
# Location: ~/.aidevops/locks/claim-task-id.<counter_branch>.<remote>.lock/
# Shared across repos on the same host so local runners can't race.
# Returns 0 if lock acquired within timeout, 1 otherwise.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR="${CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/locks}"
CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S="${CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S:-10}"

_cas_local_lock_path() {
	local safe_remote safe_branch
	safe_remote=$(printf '%s' "${REMOTE_NAME:-origin}" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')
	safe_branch=$(printf '%s' "${COUNTER_BRANCH:-main}" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')
	printf '%s/claim-task-id.%s.%s.lock' "$CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR" "$safe_remote" "$safe_branch"
}

_cas_acquire_local_lock() {
	local lock_dir
	lock_dir=$(_cas_local_lock_path)
	mkdir -p "$CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
	local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S ))
	while (( $(date +%s) < deadline )); do
		if mkdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
			printf '%s' "$$" > "${lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null || true
			return 0
		fi
		# Stale-lock reclaim: if pid file points at a dead process, remove the lock dir.
		local lock_pid=""
		if [[ -r "${lock_dir}/pid" ]]; then
			lock_pid=$(cat "${lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null)
		fi
		if [[ -n "$lock_pid" ]] && ! kill -0 "$lock_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
			rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
			continue
		fi
		sleep 0.25
	done
	return 1
}

_cas_release_local_lock() {
	local lock_dir
	lock_dir=$(_cas_local_lock_path)
	rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
	return 0
}
```

### Step 2 — Wrap `allocate_online()`

Modify `allocate_online()` (lines 705-760) so the retry loop runs under the local lock. The exact shape: acquire at entry, ensure release on every exit path via a trap. If lock acquisition fails, FALL THROUGH (log a warning, proceed unlocked) — the git push remains authoritative, and we never want the lock to harden into a deadlock.

```bash
allocate_online() {
	local repo_path="$1"
	local count="$2"
	local attempt=0
	local first_id=""
	local start_epoch
	start_epoch=$(date +%s)

	# Phase 2 (t2568 / GH#20001): machine-local mutex.
	local have_local_lock=0
	if _cas_acquire_local_lock; then
		have_local_lock=1
		# shellcheck disable=SC2064  # intentional early expansion of the flag
		trap "[[ \"$have_local_lock\" -eq 1 ]] && _cas_release_local_lock" RETURN
	else
		log_warn "Could not acquire local CAS mutex within ${CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S}s — proceeding unlocked (git push remains authoritative)"
	fi

	while [[ $attempt -lt $CAS_MAX_RETRIES ]]; do
		# ...existing loop body unchanged...
	done

	log_error "Failed to allocate after ${CAS_MAX_RETRIES} attempts"
```

title: t2568: add mkdir-based local mutex around claim-task-id CAS loop (Phase 2 of #20001)
body:
_Child of #20001 (Phase 2 of 3) — siblings: Phase 1 #20220, Phase 3 #{{PHASE3}}._

## What

Wrap the `allocate_online()` retry loop in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` with a portable machine-local `mkdir`-based mutex, so concurrent agents on the same host serialise their CAS attempts at the fetch→read→commit→push boundary. The authoritative gate is still the git push (`--force-with-lease`-equivalent ref update on origin/main); this lock merely reduces wasted CAS commits and retry budget when two local sessions race.

**Scope (Phase 2 only):**
- Modify `allocate_online()` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (lines 705-760) to acquire/release a host-local `mkdir` lock.
- Choose a lock path under `~/.aidevops/locks/` so multiple repos on the same host still coordinate on the *claim* primitive.
- Bounded wait: give up after a configurable timeout (default 10s) and fall through to the usual retry loop — local lock MUST NOT become a deadlock.

Phase 1 (guard reuse detection) and Phase 3 (audit log) are separate children — do NOT land them in this PR.

## Why

The CAS implementation in `allocate_counter_cas()` is sound — `git push` returning non-zero on conflict is the authoritative gate. But when two agents on the same machine race, each one:

1. Runs `_cas_fetch_and_pin` (network round-trip).
2. Builds a commit (cheap).
3. Pushes (network round-trip; one wins, one loses).
4. Loser retries: fetch + push again.

Under observed contention in t2377-era worker storms, we saw >30 CAS attempts burn out the retry budget because two local workers kept colliding with each other AND with the pulse. A cheap host-local mutex cuts this dramatically: local workers serialise at step 1, only one network round-trip per slot, and the retry budget is spent on *real* cross-host contention (remote workflows, other machines).

`flock(1)` is the obvious choice but macOS lacks it in the default /usr/bin. `pulse-wrapper.sh` solves this with a `mkdir`-based lock pattern (atomic on all POSIX filesystems). Re-use that pattern here.

## How

**File to modify:** `EDIT: .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (2003 lines — parent #20001 cited "lines ~580-645" which is where `_cas_fetch_and_pin` / `_cas_build_and_push` live; the cleaner wrapping point is `allocate_online()` at lines 705-760, which contains the retry loop).

### Step 1 — Lock helpers

Add two helpers at the top of `claim-task-id.sh` (near the other private helpers, after the `log_*` section around line 180-220 — pick the nearest section boundary):

```bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Machine-local mutex for CAS serialisation (Phase 2 / t2568 / GH#20001).
# macOS has no flock(1); use atomic mkdir as the lock primitive.
# Location: ~/.aidevops/locks/claim-task-id.<counter_branch>.<remote>.lock/
# Shared across repos on the same host so local runners can't race.
# Returns 0 if lock acquired within timeout, 1 otherwise.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR="${CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/locks}"
CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S="${CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S:-10}"

_cas_local_lock_path() {
	local safe_remote safe_branch
	safe_remote=$(printf '%s' "${REMOTE_NAME:-origin}" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')
	safe_branch=$(printf '%s' "${COUNTER_BRANCH:-main}" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')
	printf '%s/claim-task-id.%s.%s.lock' "$CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR" "$safe_remote" "$safe_branch"
}

_cas_acquire_local_lock() {
	local lock_dir
	lock_dir=$(_cas_local_lock_path)
	mkdir -p "$CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
	local deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S ))
	while (( $(date +%s) < deadline )); do
		if mkdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
			printf '%s' "$$" > "${lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null || true
			return 0
		fi
		# Stale-lock reclaim: if pid file points at a dead process, remove the lock dir.
		local lock_pid=""
		if [[ -r "${lock_dir}/pid" ]]; then
			lock_pid=$(cat "${lock_dir}/pid" 2>/dev/null)
		fi
		if [[ -n "$lock_pid" ]] && ! kill -0 "$lock_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
			rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
			continue
		fi
		sleep 0.25
	done
	return 1
}

_cas_release_local_lock() {
	local lock_dir
	lock_dir=$(_cas_local_lock_path)
	rm -rf "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
	return 0
}
```

### Step 2 — Wrap `allocate_online()`

Modify `allocate_online()` (lines 705-760) so the retry loop runs under the local lock. The exact shape: acquire at entry, ensure release on every exit path via a trap. If lock acquisition fails, FALL THROUGH (log a warning, proceed unlocked) — the git push remains authoritative, and we never want the lock to harden into a deadlock.

```bash
allocate_online() {
	local repo_path="$1"
	local count="$2"
	local attempt=0
	local first_id=""
	local start_epoch
	start_epoch=$(date +%s)

	# Phase 2 (t2568 / GH#20001): machine-local mutex.
	local have_local_lock=0
	if _cas_acquire_local_lock; then
		have_local_lock=1

		trap "[[ \"$have_local_lock\" -eq 1 ]] && _cas_release_local_lock" RETURN
	else
		log_warn "Could not acquire local CAS mutex within ${CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S}s — proceeding unlocked (git push remains authoritative)"
	fi

	while [[ $attempt -lt $CAS_MAX_RETRIES ]]; do
		# ...existing loop body unchanged...
	done

	log_error "Failed to allocate after ${CAS_MAX_RETRIES} attempts"
	return 1
}
```

3. **Timeout fallthrough:** hold a lock for >`CAS_LOCAL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S` seconds, confirm the blocked call proceeds unlocked (not a hard error).

title: t2569: add structured audit log for CAS claims (Phase 3 of #20001)
body:
_Child of #20001 (Phase 3 of 3 — FINAL phase, closes parent) — siblings: Phase 1 #20220, Phase 2 #20221._

## What

Append one structured audit log line per successful CAS allocation to `~/.aidevops/logs/task-claim.log`. Fields: timestamp, pid, session_id (if available), claimed_id, nonce, attempt_number. This gives us a forensic trail for future incidents analogous to t2377 — when we see a duplicate claim at the remote, we can tell which local process allocated each ID.

## Why

The t2377 post-mortem on #19874 required manually reconstructing *when* each session claimed what, by grepping git log for `chore: claim tNNN` commits and cross-referencing their authored timestamps. That worked because the CAS mechanism happens to leave a git trail — but only because a commit is its side effect, not because we chose to instrument.

A structured log with pid + nonce + session_id gives:
- Instant correlation when two processes both believe they own a given tNNN (pid mismatch = we can tell which was real).
- Attempt counts visible for contention analysis (is the retry budget right?).
- Session ID lets the `session-miner` cross-reference claim events into the mined insights stream.

Phase 3 is the smallest of the three and the easiest to ship; it's also the highest signal for future incident response because it captures *every* claim with a single log append.

## How

**File to modify:** `EDIT: .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (2003 lines — the append site is at lines 740-745 inside `allocate_online()`, where the successful CAS path prints `log_success` and `echo "$first_id"`).

Add the log append between `log_success` and `echo "$first_id"`. Verbatim replacement block below.

### Step 1 — Locate the success branch

Find this block in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (currently lines 740-745):

**oldString:**
```
		case $cas_result in
		0)
			# go for it — CAS succeeded on this attempt
			log_success "Claimed $(printf 't%03d' "$first_id") (attempt ${attempt}, ${elapsed}s)"
			echo "$first_id"
			return 0
			;;
```

**newString:**
```
		case $cas_result in
		0)
			# go for it — CAS succeeded on this attempt
			log_success "Claimed $(printf 't%03d' "$first_id") (attempt ${attempt}, ${elapsed}s)"
			# Phase 3 (t2569 / GH#20001): structured audit log.
			_append_claim_audit_log "$first_id" "$attempt" "$elapsed"
			echo "$first_id"
			return 0
			;;
```

### Step 2 — Add the log helper

Add the helper near the other private helpers (around line 180-220 — pick the nearest section boundary). Use plain POSIX shell; no jq dependency.

```bash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Append a structured audit log line for a successful CAS claim.
# Format: ISO8601 \t pid \t session_id \t tNNN \t attempt \t elapsed_s
# (tab-separated so later tooling can parse without quoting concerns.)
# Log file: ~/.aidevops/logs/task-claim.log (created on first append).
#
# Phase 3 (t2569 / GH#20001): forensics for CAS-race or reuse incidents.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
_append_claim_audit_log() {
	local first_id="${1:-}"
	local attempt="${2:-1}"
	local elapsed="${3:-0}"

	[[ -z "$first_id" ]] && return 0

	local log_dir="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs"
	local log_file="${log_dir}/task-claim.log"

	mkdir -p "$log_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0

	local ts pid sid tid
	ts=$(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' 2>/dev/null)
	pid="${BASHPID:-$$}"
	sid="${AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ID:-${Claude_SESSION_ID:-${OPENCODE_SESSION_ID:-unknown}}}"
	tid=$(printf 't%03d' "$first_id")

	# Tab-separated; single append is atomic on POSIX filesystems for short writes.
	printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%ss\n' \
		"$ts" "$pid" "$sid" "$tid" "$attempt" "$elapsed" >> "$log_file" 2>/dev/null || true
	return 0
}
```

### Step 3 — Reference patterns

The `~/.aidevops/logs/` directory already has precedent — grep for `~/.aidevops/logs/` and `HOME/.aidevops/logs` in `.agents/scripts/` to find other append helpers. The `pulse-wrapper.sh` log append is a simple template; the `session-miner` helpers are more elaborate but overkill here. Single-line TSV append is sufficient.

### Step 4 — Log rotation

NOT part of this PR. Log rotation / size caps live in the aidevops update path and should be a follow-up. Append with `>>` is fine; the log will grow linearly with CAS frequency (<1MB/month at current rates).

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (one new helper `_append_claim_audit_log`, one call site insertion)

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_append_claim_audit_log` helper added and shellcheck-clean.
- [ ] `allocate_online()` success branch calls the helper between `log_success` and `echo "$first_id"`.
- [ ] Log directory `~/.aidevops/logs/` is created if missing; append fails open (no error on disk-full/perms).
- [ ] Log line contains ISO8601 timestamp, pid, session_id (or `unknown`), tNNN, attempt, elapsed.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` passes with zero violations.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh

# Manual smoke (on a throwaway repo with a valid counter):
.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh --no-issue --title "audit-log smoke"
tail -1 ~/.aidevops/logs/task-claim.log
# Expect one TSV line:  2026-04-21T02:34:12Z<TAB>12345<TAB>unknown<TAB>t2570<TAB>1<TAB>0s
```

## Context

- Parent #20001 + sibling Phase 1 #20220 + sibling Phase 2 #20221. Phase 3 is the **final** phase — its PR uses `Closes #20001` (per the t2046 rule: the final child closes the parent-task).
- Hygiene: log file is TSV, not JSON. Easier to append atomically, easier for shell tooling. If we later want JSON we can transform offline.
- Session ID fallbacks: `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ID` (framework-set), then runtime-specific env vars (`Claude_SESSION_ID` for Claude Code, `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` for OpenCode). Default to literal `unknown` if none set — the pid already disambiguates local processes.
- DO NOT log arbitrary env or secrets. The helper touches only the listed fields.

## PR Conventions

- PR title: `t2569: add structured audit log for CAS claims`
- **PR body MUST use `Closes #20001`** — this is the LAST phase child; the t2046 rule requires the final phase PR to close the parent, and this is the PR that does it.
- Labels: `bug`, `framework`, `tier:simple`, `auto-dispatch`.
- tier:simple is justified: single file, <500-line equivalent scope (one new ~25-line function + one 2-line edit), verbatim oldString/newString blocks above, 5 acceptance criteria (≤4 would be ideal but 5 is still within the soft bar).

### HIGH: gemini (gemini-code-assist[bot])
**File**: `.agents/hooks/privacy-guard-pre-push.sh:123`
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The logic for determining the default remote branch hardcodes `origin`, which will fail if the remote is named differently (e.g., `upstream`). Additionally, falling back to `HEAD` at line 123 is problematic for a privacy guard: if the remote base cannot be determined, `git merge-base "$_ls" HEAD` will likely return `$_ls` (if pushing the current branch), resulting in an empty diff and bypassing the scan. It is safer to leave `_default_remote_head` empty when unknown, which correctly triggers a full scan via the logic at line 139. Using `git symbolic-ref --short` also simplifies the extraction.

```suggestion
# Priority: remote/HEAD (repo-configured) → remote/main → remote/master.
_default_remote_head=$(git symbolic-ref --short "refs/remotes/${remote_name}/HEAD" 2>/dev/null)
if [[ -z "$_default_remote_head" ]]; then
	for _candidate in "${remote_name}/main" "${remote_name}/master"; do
		git rev-parse --verify "$_candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1
		_status=$?
		if [[ $_status -eq 0 ]]; then
			_default_remote_head="$_candidate"
			break
		fi
	done
fi
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In shell scripts, capture a command's exit code in a variable instead of using $? directly in conditionals. This aligns with ShellCheck SC2181 and improves clarity for multi-way branches.
2. To make git operations in scripts more robust, dynamically and explicitly determine the default branch instead of relying on the current checkout. Implement a fallback mechanism to find the branch, for example: try origin/HEAD, then common names like main/master, and finally HEAD.
3. In shell scripts, add guard clauses to check if a variable is empty before using it, especially when its value is derived from an external command that could fail or produce no output.
</details>

```shell
_compute_baseline() {
	local _remote
	_remote="${1:-origin}"
	local default_remote_head
	local baseline
	default_remote_head=$(git symbolic-ref "refs/remotes/$_remote/HEAD" 2>/dev/null | sed "s@^refs/remotes/$_remote/@@")

		for candidate in "$_remote/main" "$_remote/master" "HEAD"; do
			if git rev-parse --verify "$candidate" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
				default_remote_head="$candidate"
				break

		done

		printf '[%s] warning: no %s HEAD resolved; falling back to @{u}\n' "$GUARD_NAME" "$_remote" >&2
		git merge-base HEAD '@{u}'
		return $?
	fi
	baseline=$(git merge-base HEAD "$default_remote_head")
	local rc
	rc=$?
	if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] || [[ -z "$baseline" ]]; then
		baseline="$default_remote_head"
	fi
	printf '%s\n' "$baseline"
	return $rc
}
```

title: t2570: scanner — detect empty-compare foot-gun bash pattern
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive — post-t2559 follow-up. Filed after the 2026-04-20 canonical-trash incident was fully remediated (PR #20209, issue #20205, all four defensive layers live).

## What

Add a static scanner that detects the **empty-compare foot-gun** in bash shell scripts: a comparison of the form `[[ "$x" != "$y" ]]` (or `==`/`!=` variants, `[ ... ]` too) where `$y` is populated from command substitution or parameter expansion and the RHS lacks a prior non-empty assertion in the same function scope.

The failure mode: when `$y` resolves to the empty string, the compare reduces to `[[ $x != "" ]]` — always true for any real value of `$x`. Intent is silently inverted. This was the direct root cause of the t2559 canonical-trash incident at `worktree-helper.sh::cmd_clean:1591` (now fixed — that site lives behind the `_clean_preflight_main_worktree` guard extracted in the t2559 PR).

## Why

One failure site in this class **moved the canonical repo to Trash** and cost a full pulse-suspend + multi-phase recovery session. The same pattern is trivially reproducible in any shell script that populates a variable from a derived source (`git worktree list`, `jq`, parsed config, env lookup) and uses it as an anchor in a later compare. A repo-wide scan before the next incident is strictly cheaper than the next incident.

## How

New scanner at `.agents/scripts/empty-compare-scanner.sh`, modeled on the existing scanner helpers (`complexity-regression-helper.sh`, `qlty-new-file-gate-helper.sh` — similar tab-separated output, `--base <sha>` for CI use, `scan <path>` for local use).

Detection algorithm (regex-first pass, acceptable false-positive rate for CI warning; hard gate gated behind justification label):

1. Walk each `.sh` file under `.agents/` tracked by git.
2. Within each function body (track `^funcname\(\)` and `^}` boundaries — existing pattern in `complexity-regression-helper.sh` `_scan_file_function_complexity`):
   - Find variable assignments from derived sources: `var=$(...)`, `var="${...}"`, `var=$(jq ...)`, `var=$(git ...)`.
   - For each such `var`, find subsequent `!=` / `==` comparisons in the same function where `var` appears on either side.
   - Between the assignment and the compare, look for ANY of:
     - `[[ -z "$var" ]]` / `[ -z "$var" ]` with a `return`/`exit` in the then-branch
     - `[[ -n "$var" ]]` / `[ -n "$var" ]` with a `return`/`exit` in the else-branch
     - `: "${var:?...}"` or `: "${var:-...}"` with non-empty default
     - Explicit assignment to a known non-empty literal between derivation and compare
   - If none found, flag the compare site.
3. Output: `<file>\t<function>\t<assignment_line>\t<compare_line>\t<pattern>` tab-separated, plus an `--output-md` markdown report for PR comments.

title: t2572: fix gh api --slurp --jq anti-pattern causing duplicate parent-decomposition nudge comments
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive investigation after resolving #20001 manually. While diagnosing why 22 `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` nudge comments appeared on a single parent-task issue across ~30h from two pulse runners, the dedup check in `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` was reproduced and found to be 100% broken since introduction.

## What

Fix the invalid `gh api --paginate ... --slurp --jq "..."` invocation in `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` at `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1130-1133`. Sweep the rest of the framework for the same anti-pattern and repair each site.

## Why

`gh api` explicitly rejects combining `--slurp` with `--jq` or `--template`. The error message is `the --slurp option is not supported with --jq or --template`. The current code swallows that error with `2>/dev/null`:

```bash
existing=$(gh api --paginate "repos/${slug}/issues/${parent_num}/comments" \
    --slurp \
    --jq "[.[] | .[] | select(.body | contains(\"${marker}\"))] | length" \
    2>/dev/null) || existing=""
if [[ "$existing" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]; then
    return 1
fi
```

`existing=""` never matches `^[1-9]`, so every pulse cycle falls through and posts a duplicate nudge. This is NOT a rate-limit or API issue — it is an unconditional bug in the `gh` CLI contract. The comment above the query even asserts "re-runs are no-ops" — but the dedup check that enforces that has never succeeded.

Live evidence on #20001 (marcusquinn/aidevops): 22 nudge comments posted 2026-04-19 22:47 → 2026-04-21 01:28 from two pulse runners (`marcusquinn`, `alex-solovyev`). Expected: exactly 1.

This is filed as a standalone fix because the dedup failure is itself the noisy symptom operators see. The deeper gating issues (auto-decomposer timing, REST fallback) are separate tasks.

## How

1. Replace the broken call with a per-page streaming pattern (no `--slurp`):

   ```bash
   existing=$(gh api --paginate "repos/${slug}/issues/${parent_num}/comments" \
       --jq '.[] | select(.body | contains("'"$marker"'")) | .id' \
       2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
   ```

   `--paginate` concatenates per-page JSON arrays; the `--jq` expression runs per-page and prints one `.id` per matching comment; `wc -l` counts them. No `--slurp` needed.

2. Sweep the codebase for the same anti-pattern:

   ```bash
   rg -nS -- '--slurp' .agents/ | rg -- '--jq|--template'
   ```

   Fix each occurrence with the same streaming pattern, or pipe into a real `jq -s` process if slurping is genuinely needed.

3. Add a regression test that:
   - Stubs `gh api` with a response containing a marker comment
   - Calls `_post_parent_decomposition_nudge` twice
   - Asserts only ONE comment is posted (the second call's `gh_issue_comment` is never invoked)

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1130-1133` — replace the `--slurp --jq` call with the streaming pattern
- EDIT: any additional sites surfaced by the codebase sweep (expected: 0-3 sites based on a quick spot-check)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh` — regression test

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/**/*.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `rg -nS -- '--slurp' .agents/ | rg -- '--jq|--template'` returns zero matches
- [ ] Regression test posts one nudge on first call, zero on second call
- [ ] Test passes locally (`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh`) and in CI
- [ ] No new open parent-task issue accumulates >1 `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` comment after this lands

title: t2571: chore — remove sidelined pre-incident-20260420-2350 canonical clone (after 2026-05-20)
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive — post-t2559 follow-up. Retention period for the sidelined pre-incident canonical clone expires 2026-05-20 (30 days after the 2026-04-20 canonical-trash incident).

## What

Remove the sidelined pre-incident canonical clone at `~/Git/aidevops-pre-incident-20260420-2350/` once the retention window has passed. The sideline was created during t2559 Phase 1b recovery to preserve the original git packfile layout and reflog for any forensic need. With t2559 fully shipped (PR #20209 merged, four defensive layers deployed, pulse running fixed code), no further forensic access is anticipated.

## Why

Reclaim the ~400 MB of disk the sidelined clone occupies. Keep `~/Git/` free of stale recovery artefacts. The sideline is **not** in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` — it is not registered with the framework and therefore invisible to everything except manual browsing.

## How

```bash
# Precondition check — must be true before proceeding.
if [[ "$(date +%Y-%m-%d)" < "2026-05-20" ]]; then
  echo "[t2571] retention window has not yet expired; today=$(date +%Y-%m-%d), earliest=2026-05-20 — skipping"
  exit 0
fi

# Verify path exists and is the expected sideline (defense-in-depth — never delete a live worktree).
test -d ~/Git/aidevops-pre-incident-20260420-2350 || { echo "[t2571] sideline already removed, nothing to do"; exit 0; }

# Confirm it is NOT a registered canonical path.
if jq -r '.initialized_repos[].path' ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json | grep -Fxq ~/Git/aidevops-pre-incident-20260420-2350; then
  echo "[t2571] REFUSING: sideline path appears in repos.json — will not delete a registered repo" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Confirm it is NOT a registered git worktree.
if git -C ~/Git/aidevops worktree list --porcelain | grep -q "worktree $HOME/Git/aidevops-pre-incident-20260420-2350"; then
  echo "[t2571] REFUSING: sideline path is a registered worktree" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Safe to remove. Trash (not rm -rf) so recovery remains possible if this was premature.
mv ~/Git/aidevops-pre-incident-20260420-2350 ~/.Trash/
```

## Acceptance

1. `~/Git/aidevops-pre-incident-20260420-2350/` no longer exists.
2. `~/.Trash/` contains the moved directory (or the sideline was already removed by another operator — also acceptable).
3. Task closes without touching any registered repo or worktree.
4. `du -sh ~/Git/` shows the reclaimed disk.

## Files to modify

None. Operational task, no code or planning files.

## Context

- Root cause and recovery: t2559 / PR #20209 / issue #20205.
- Sideline created: 2026-04-21 ~00:15 UTC during Phase 1b.
- Orphan worktree audit from Phase 2: `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/aidevops/orphaned-worktrees-report-20260421.csv`.

title: t2573: tighten auto-decomposer gating: per-parent interval + 6h fresh-parent threshold
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive investigation after resolving #20001 manually. The auto-decomposer scanner (t2442) existed and worked correctly for one parent (#19808 → decomposer issue #20148, succeeded in 34 min) — but failed to fire for #20001 within the 54h window between label application and manual resolution. Root cause: gating thresholds are too coarse.

## What

Replace the global 24h interval gate for `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` with a per-parent gate. Reduce `SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS` default from 24h to 6h for parents that have zero prior non-nudge comments (fresh parents). Keep the 24h threshold for parents with existing activity.

## Why

Two gating issues combine to produce up to ~48h of "dispatch black hole" on fresh parent-tasks:

1. **Global 24h interval** (`AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL=86400`, `pulse-wrapper.sh:517`): the scanner runs at most once per 24h across ALL repos and ALL parents. `$AUTO_DECOMPOSER_LAST_RUN` is a single file, not per-repo or per-parent. If multiple parent-tasks need decomposition on the same day, only ONE decomposer issue is filed per 24h cycle.

2. **24h nudge-age threshold** (`SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS=24`, `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:55`): a parent must have a nudge comment at least 24h old before the decomposer will file a worker issue. For a parent labeled at T=0, the first nudge fires at T=0 or T+pulse-cycle, and the decomposer cannot fire until T+24h.

Concrete evidence from #20001 (marcusquinn/aidevops):

- Labeled `parent-task`: 2026-04-19 ~20:15 (inferred from first nudge)
- First nudge: 2026-04-19 22:47
- Global scanner last run: 1776717999 = 2026-04-20 21:46 (nudge was 23h old — skipped)
- Next eligible run would have been: 2026-04-21 21:46 (nudge would be ~47h old — eligible)
- Actual resolution: 2026-04-21 01:30 via manual session (beat automation by ~20h)
- Total black-hole window that would have been observed without manual resolution: ~47h

During that window, the nudge bot fired 22 comments (separate bug — see companion issue filed in this session). Operator friction: real.

Additionally, if a backlog of 5 parents needed decomposition simultaneously, the global interval means it takes 5 days to clear them — one per 24h.

## How

1. **Remove the global interval gate** in `pulse-simplification.sh:_run_auto_decomposer_scanner`:
   - Delete the `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_LAST_RUN` read/write block (lines 292-301 and 335).
   - Let the scanner run on every pulse cycle; its own per-parent dedup will handle idempotency.

2. **Add per-parent state** in `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`:
   - Introduce `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_PARENT_STATE="${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/auto-decomposer-parent-state.json"` — a JSON object `{"<slug>#<issue>": <last-filed-epoch>, ...}`.
   - Before filing a decomposer issue for a parent, check the state file — skip if last-filed < 7 days ago.
   - After filing, update the state file atomically (flock or write-then-rename).

3. **Introduce fresh-parent threshold** in `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`:
   - Add `SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS="${SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS:-6}"`.
   - In the eligibility check: if the parent has ZERO comments other than the `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` nudge, use `$SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS` (default 6h) instead of `$SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS` (default 24h).
   - Rationale: a fresh parent with no human activity is the purest form of dispatch black hole; 6h is enough time for the maintainer to notice if they wanted to intervene.

4. **Retire or repurpose `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL`**:
   - Remove the constant from `pulse-wrapper.sh:517` and its validation at `:575`, OR
   - Repurpose as a per-parent re-file interval (default 604800 = 7 days) and reference from the new state check.

5. **Regression tests**:
   - Test that the scanner runs on every pulse cycle (no global throttle).
   - Test that the same parent is not re-filed within 7 days.
   - Test that a fresh parent (0 non-nudge comments) with a 6-hour-old nudge triggers filing.
   - Test that a parent with existing activity requires 24h nudge age.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification.sh:288-340` — remove global interval gate
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` — add per-parent state + fresh-parent threshold
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:517,575` — remove or repurpose `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-decomposer-per-parent-gate.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Parent-task decomposition lifecycle (t2442)" section — update the description of the 4th mechanism (auto-decomposer scanner) to reflect per-parent gating

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-simplification.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-decomposer-per-parent-gate.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Global `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_LAST_RUN` file is no longer written by the scanner wrapper
- [ ] Per-parent state file prevents re-filing the same parent within 7 days (verified by running the scanner twice back-to-back)
- [ ] Fresh parent with 6h-old nudge gets a decomposer issue filed
- [ ] Aged parent (with prior comments) still requires 24h nudge age
- [ ] Regression tests pass
- [ ] AGENTS.md description updated to match the new behaviour

title: t2574: REST fallback for GraphQL-exhausted gh issue wrappers in shared-gh-wrappers.sh
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive investigation during #20001 resolution. Encountered live GraphQL rate exhaustion (0/5000 remaining, 4954/5000 after reset) while attempting to PATCH issue bodies, post comments, edit labels, and update assignees. Every `gh issue create/view/edit/comment` call failed; only raw `gh api` REST endpoints worked. A dispatched worker constrained to the framework's helper surface would have hit the same wall with no escape hatch.

## Why

`gh issue create|view|edit|comment` commands route through GitHub's GraphQL API internally. GraphQL has a dedicated 5000-point/hour budget separate from the core REST 5000 req/hour budget. When the pulse (and other cross-runner activity) saturates GraphQL, interactive operators can fall back to `gh api /repos/.../issues/...` REST endpoints — but the framework's wrappers (`set_issue_status`, `gh_issue_comment`, `gh_issue_edit`, `gh_issue_create`) do NOT have this fallback.

Observed 2026-04-21 ~01:00 UTC on marcusquinn/aidevops:

- `gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources'` → `graphql: {remaining: 0, used: 5000}`, `core: {remaining: 4974, used: 26}`
- `gh issue create --repo ...` → HTTP 403 "rate limit exceeded"
- `gh issue edit 20001 --repo ... --add-label status:in-review` → HTTP 403
- `gh api -X POST repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues` → HTTP 201 (success)
- `gh api -X PATCH repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20001 -f body=...` → HTTP 200 (success)

For workers this is an unrecoverable failure: `claim-task-id.sh` calls `gh issue create` (via `gh_create_issue` → auto-detection), `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` calls `gh issue edit` (via `set_issue_status`), `pulse-merge.sh` calls `gh pr comment`, etc. A worker dispatched during the exhaustion window would crash at step 1 and either emit a stuck-worker advisory or silently retry until watchdog kill.

The core REST budget (5000/hour) is almost always available when GraphQL is saturated, because REST doesn't share the point-per-query-complexity model GraphQL uses. Bots and cross-runner pulses tend to burn GraphQL faster than REST.

## What

Add automatic REST fallback to the four `gh issue *` wrappers in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`:

- `set_issue_status` → falls back to `gh api -X PATCH /repos/{slug}/issues/{N} -f labels[]=...`
- `gh_issue_comment` → falls back to `gh api -X POST /repos/{slug}/issues/{N}/comments -f body=@body.txt`
- `gh_issue_edit` → falls back to `gh api -X PATCH /repos/{slug}/issues/{N} -f ...`
- `gh_issue_create` → falls back to `gh api -X POST /repos/{slug}/issues -f title=... -f body=@body.txt -F labels[]=... -F assignees[]=...`

The fallback activates when:

1. The primary `gh issue *` call fails AND
2. `gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining'` returns a value ≤ 10

Emit `[INFO] gh-wrapper: GraphQL exhausted, falling back to REST for {endpoint}` when the fallback fires so operators see the symptom in logs.

## How

1. **Introduce a shared helper** `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`:

   ```bash
   _gh_should_fallback_to_rest() {
       local remaining
       remaining=$(gh api rate_limit --jq '.resources.graphql.remaining' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
       [[ "$remaining" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || remaining=0
       [[ "$remaining" -le 10 ]]
   }
   ```

2. **Refactor each wrapper** to:
   - Try the `gh issue *` call first.
   - On non-zero exit, check `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest`.
   - If exhausted, retry via `gh api` REST equivalent.
   - Log the fallback with `[INFO]`.

3. **`gh_issue_comment` REST fallback specifics**:
   - Body can contain newlines, shell metacharacters, unicode → use `-f body=@file` with a temp file, not `-f body="$body"`.

4. **`set_issue_status` REST fallback specifics**:
   - Label PATCH via REST requires sending the FULL label array (not `--add-label`/`--remove-label` deltas). Read current labels, compute the target set, send via `-f labels[]=<label>` repeated.

5. **`gh_issue_create` REST fallback specifics**:
   - Map `--label a,b,c` → `-F labels[]=a -F labels[]=b -F labels[]=c`.
   - Map `--assignee u` → `-F assignees[]=u`.
   - Map `--milestone N` → `-f milestone=N`.

6. **Regression tests**:
   - Stub `gh` to return rate-limit-exhausted on GraphQL calls.
   - Stub `gh api rate_limit` to return `{"resources":{"graphql":{"remaining":0}}}`.
   - Assert each wrapper logs the fallback message and returns success.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — add `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` + refactor 4 wrappers (~80-120 lines added)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh` — unit tests with `gh` stubs
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — add a brief mention under "Cross-runner coordination" or "Pulse scope" about the GraphQL/REST fallback

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 4 wrappers (`set_issue_status`, `gh_issue_comment`, `gh_issue_edit`, `gh_issue_create`) fall back to REST when GraphQL remaining ≤ 10
- [ ] Fallback emits a `[INFO]` log line so the symptom is visible
- [ ] Regression tests pass with a mocked `gh` stub
- [ ] Passing `body` containing newlines, quotes, backticks, unicode via the REST fallback survives round-trip intact
- [ ] `gh_issue_create` REST fallback preserves labels, assignees, milestone flags

title: t2575: isolate pre-push hook stdout from claim-task-id.sh CAS command substitutions
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive investigation during #20001 resolution. Observed a transient `claim-task-id.sh` failure where the CAS loop emitted `"2565: arithmetic syntax error: operand expected (error token is 'Pre-push Quality Validation')"` and then `CAS_EXHAUSTED: online allocation failed after 30 attempts`. Bypassed by manual CAS via git plumbing. After recovery, `claim-task-id.sh --dry-run` worked cleanly — confirming the failure was caused by hook output interfering with script parsing, not by the helper itself.

## What

Ensure `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` (and the pre-push banner it prints) routes ALL informational output to stderr, never stdout. Audit `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`'s CAS loop for command substitutions around `git push` and ensure hook stdout can never bleed into parsed values.

## Why

The observed error token `'Pre-push Quality Validation'` is a banner string printed by the pre-push hook. The arithmetic error indicates that the banner text was consumed by a `$(( ... ))` expression or a `[[ "$x" -eq N ]]` test — meaning the hook's stdout was captured into a variable that was then used in arithmetic context.

Working hypothesis based on code inspection:

- `claim-task-id.sh`'s CAS loop calls something like `PUSH_OUT=$(git push ... 2>&1)` to capture the result.
- When the pre-push hook runs (it does on every push), its banner output goes to stdout.
- `PUSH_OUT` accumulates `"Pre-push Quality Validation\n..."` plus the actual push output.
- Later code does `if (( PUSH_OUT < 0 ))` or parses via `echo "$PUSH_OUT" | awk ...` with a numeric expectation.
- The non-numeric banner text fails arithmetic with the exact error observed.

Symptom was transient in this session because it co-occurred with GraphQL exhaustion — during the normal case, a `set -e` elsewhere likely masks the failure, or the captured output happens to not include the banner. But the brittleness is real: the hook should never speak on stdout during `git push`, period.

This is separate from task 3 (REST fallback) because the helper runs entirely within git — no `gh` calls during the CAS loop itself. It is also separate from t2228 (task-counter monotonic guard) which enforces counter forward-progress but not hook hygiene.

## How

1. **Audit `pre-commit-hook.sh` for stdout writes**:

   ```bash
   rg -n '^\s*(printf|echo)\b[^>]*$' .agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh
   ```

   Each hit that does NOT end in `>&2` should be changed to `>&2`.

2. **Route all banners to stderr**:
   - `"Pre-push Quality Validation"` banner → stderr
   - Per-check progress indicators (shellcheck, markdownlint, secretlint, etc.) → stderr
   - Final summary line ("N checks passed") → stderr if the hook succeeded silently, otherwise still stderr (don't write to stdout)

3. **Audit `claim-task-id.sh` CAS loop for fragile captures**:

   ```bash
   grep -n '\$(git push' .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
   grep -n 'PUSH_OUT\|push_output\|push_result' .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
   ```

   For each capture of `git push` output:
   - Isolate from stdout: use `git push ... 2>/dev/null >/dev/null` and inspect `$?` instead, OR
   - If the output is genuinely needed, pipe through a filter that strips known hook banners: `| grep -v '^Pre-push'`, OR
   - Better: parse only the last line via `| tail -1`.

4. **Add a regression test** that:
   - Installs a test hook that prints 100 lines of banner to stdout.
   - Runs a `claim-task-id.sh` cycle.

5. **Consider a pre-hook-install lint** (optional): add a check in `install-hooks-helper.sh install` that warns if any registered hook writes to stdout during push.

title: t2578: pulse-wrapper: detect and break stale mkdir lock after crashed/killed instance
body:
## Task

Fix the multi-instance pulse lock race where a `pkill + nohup` restart leaves two or more pulse processes running simultaneously: the old instance still holds the mkdir lock (no longer active but not cleared), and new instances log `Another pulse instance holds the mkdir lock ... exiting immediately` on every cycle. Observed live 2026-04-21 with three concurrent PIDs (35834, 52848, 91825) visible via `pgrep -f pulse-wrapper.sh`.

## Why

The existing GH#4513 mkdir-lock guard is correct for the "second instance attempts start while first is actively running" case, but fails to detect the "stale lock from a crashed/force-killed instance" case. Symptoms:

- `pgrep -f pulse-wrapper.sh` shows multiple live PIDs.
- `~/.aidevops/locks/` is empty (no lockfile visible on disk).
- Log shows `[pulse-wrapper] Another pulse instance holds the mkdir lock (PID X, age Ns) — exiting immediately` repeatedly with `age` growing unbounded.
- Pulse work stalls because cycles exit immediately instead of processing the queue.

## What

Audit the instance-lock mechanism in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` for:

1. **Staleness detection**: the lock should include the owner's PID and a heartbeat; another instance starting up should verify the owner is still alive (`kill -0`) and crash-recover if not. Today the `age Ns` number is reported but not acted on for staleness.
2. **On-disk lock reality check**: the log says "holds the mkdir lock" but `~/.aidevops/locks/` is empty. Either the lock dir is non-standard, or the detection path is checking a different location than the cleanup/removal path.
3. **Restart contract**: document whether `pkill + nohup` is a supported restart pattern. If so, add the stale-lock breaking logic. If not, reject the pattern in the restart helpers and direct users to a graceful stop.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — identify the lock path, add liveness check (`kill -0 "$lock_pid"` → if dead, remove stale lock directory, reacquire).
- Reference pattern: `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` has similar claim-stamp liveness logic; model after it.
- Verification: (a) start pulse normally, (b) `kill -9` the pulse PID (simulate crash), (c) nohup-start a new pulse, (d) confirm it acquires the lock and processes a cycle instead of exiting.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Stale lock from crashed/killed instance is detected and reclaimed on next pulse start
- [ ] `pgrep -f pulse-wrapper.sh` returns at most 1 PID during steady-state operation
- [ ] Log transitions cleanly from "Another instance holds" → "Stale lock (PID X dead), reclaiming" → "Instance lock acquired"
- [ ] No regression: genuine concurrent-start race still detected and rejected

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`

## Session Origin

Interactive session, t2574 live-verification (2026-04-21). Discovered while confirming the REST fallback deploy — pulse-wrapper.log showed three live PIDs with empty lock dir and repeating "exiting immediately" messages.

## Context

Tier: `tier:standard` — lock/liveness work needs care to avoid introducing races. Not tier:simple because the fix requires reasoning about PID recycling, stale-detection windows, and interaction with the existing GH#4513 guard. Straightforward pattern available (dispatch-dedup-helper.sh) but merits standard tier for judgment.

title: t2579: make aidevops update auto-restart pulse + consolidate restart logic
body:
## Task

Make `aidevops update` (and `setup.sh --non-interactive`) automatically restart the pulse after deploying new scripts, so users pick up pulse-sourced code changes without manual `pkill + nohup` steps. Consolidate the duplicated restart logic currently living only in `_hotfix_auto_apply` into a shared `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`.

## Why

AGENTS.md (user-facing doc) already states:

> `setup.sh` and `aidevops update` handle this automatically via `_restart_pulse_if_running`. Interactive sessions deploying hotfixes via `cp` must restart manually.

But **the `_restart_pulse_if_running` function does not exist anywhere in the repo** — verified via `rg -n "_restart_pulse_if_running"` returning nothing. The claim is aspirational; the implementation is missing. Consequences:

- **Stale in-memory pulse code**: bash processes load `source` files at startup only. Updated `.sh` files deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` don't take effect until the pulse is restarted. Pulse fixes (lock races, rate-limit handling, dispatch logic) sit inert on disk while the running pulse keeps using the old code.
- **Multi-PID accumulation**: observed 2026-04-21 with 5 concurrent pulse PIDs because restarts never settle cleanly. The t2578 stale-lock fix exists and was merged, but users still have the old code running in memory.
- **Cross-runner drift**: remote runners pulling via `aidevops update` don't pick up pulse fixes either — same gap, wider surface.

Only the HOTFIX path (`_hotfix_auto_apply` in `aidevops-update-check.sh:408-443`) has restart logic, and it's inline/duplicated. Regular updates go through `cmd_update` → `setup.sh --non-interactive` → no restart.

## What

1. Create `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` as the canonical pulse lifecycle manager with subcommands:
   - `is-running` — exit 0 if any pulse PID, 1 otherwise
   - `stop` — SIGTERM all pulse instances, SIGKILL after grace window
   - `start` — nohup background start, check not already running
   - `restart` — stop + start (force, used for deploy scenarios)
   - `restart-if-running` — no-op if pulse not running, otherwise stop+start (used by update flow)
   - `status` — show PIDs + uptime (informational)

2. Call `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running` from:
   - `setup.sh` main() after `_setup_post_setup_steps` (catches all direct-setup paths, interactive and non-interactive)
   - `cmd_update` in `aidevops.sh` after setup succeeds (belt-and-braces)

3. Refactor `_hotfix_auto_apply` to call the shared helper instead of duplicating restart logic inline.

4. Honour `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1` env var as the opt-out (for active debugging sessions).

5. Add regression tests: `tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — verify each subcommand, the is-running check, env opt-out, and that restart survives a transient stop/start cycle.

## How

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — model on existing `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*-helper.sh` pattern (shebang, `set -euo pipefail`, subcommand dispatch, `main "$@"`).
- EDIT: `setup.sh` main() (after `_setup_post_setup_steps "$_os"`) — add single helper call.
- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` `cmd_update()` — add helper call after setup runs (both up-to-date-with-version-mismatch path and remote-ahead path).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` `_hotfix_auto_apply()` — replace inline restart block with helper call.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — update the "Pulse restart after deploying pulse script fixes" section to reflect that the behaviour is now actually implemented (keep the manual fallback documentation for developer hot-deploys).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — structural tests (subcommand dispatch, is-running detection, opt-out honoured, idempotent restart).
- Verification:
  - `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` → all pass
  - `bash setup.sh --non-interactive` with pulse running → pulse restarts (new PID, old PID gone)
  - `bash setup.sh --non-interactive` with pulse stopped → no-op, no pulse started (respects "not running" state)
  - `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1 bash setup.sh --non-interactive` with pulse running → pulse NOT restarted
  - `shellcheck` clean on all modified files

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` exists with the 6 subcommands and is executable
- [ ] `setup.sh --non-interactive` restarts pulse when one is running
- [ ] `aidevops update` restarts pulse when updating (verified end-to-end with a live merged pulse-script change)
- [ ] `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PULSE_RESTART=1` opts out cleanly
- [ ] `_hotfix_auto_apply` no longer duplicates restart logic
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Pulse restart after deploying pulse script fixes" section matches reality
- [ ] Regression test passes: `test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all modified files
- [ ] No new function exceeds the 100-line complexity gate

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `setup.sh`
- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`

## Session Origin

Interactive session (2026-04-21, maintainer) — user asked "how about we make it so aidevops update does that?" after observing t2578 (pulse stale-lock race) fix merged but 5 concurrent pulse PIDs still running because no restart happened. This is the canonical implementation of a long-documented-but-absent behaviour.

title: t2581: Task-ID Collision Guard false-positive on prose references in PR body
body:
The Task-ID Collision Guard CI check in .github/workflows/task-id-collision-check.yml scans PR title AND body for t-IDs, and reports a VIOLATION for any t-ID without a chore:claim commit on the PR branch.

False-positive scenario (observed in t2579 PR #20289): the PR body contained prose like "the t2574 REST fallback covers..." as narrative context. The guard saw t2574, could not find a claim commit for it on this PR branch (because t2574 was claimed on a prior merged PR), and blocked CI.

## Expected behaviour

t-IDs referenced in PR BODY prose (not in the PR title or commit subjects) should either:
- Be recognised as cross-references if preceded by Resolves/Closes/Fixes/Ref/For and followed by #NNN, OR
- Be allowed if they match an already-merged claim commit anywhere in repo history (git log --all), OR
- Be ignored in prose contexts and only enforced in PR titles and commit subjects.
