body:
Observed during an interactive Claude Code session on macOS (zsh host). Calling `gh_create_issue` (sourced from shared-constants.sh via shared-gh-wrappers.sh) prints four identical warning lines before the success URL:

```
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step:local:2: bad option: -n
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step:local:2: bad option: -n
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step:local:2: bad option: -n
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step:local:2: bad option: -n
https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/NNN
```

Creation succeeds. The wrapper is probably using a bashism like `local -n ref` (nameref, bash 4.3+) that zsh's `local` builtin doesn't recognise. Four lines suggests the step function runs four times during title extraction.

**Repro**: any invocation of `gh_create_issue` in a zsh-based interactive session after sourcing shared-constants.sh.

**Impact**: cosmetic, but clutters worker output logs and signals an incompatibility that may hide a real bug later. Should either (a) guard the nameref usage with `[[ -n ${ZSH_VERSION:-} ]]` branch, or (b) port to a portable pattern (global temp var, eval indirection).

**Framework files affected**: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (function `_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step`).

title: t2687: fix health-dashboard dedup: preserve cache on gh query errors to prevent duplicate supervisor issues under rate-limit pressure
body:
## Task

Harden `_find_health_issue` in `stats-health-dashboard.sh` so that `gh` query errors (rate limit, network timeout, connection reset) never cascade into duplicate issue creation. Add periodic dedup scan on cache hits and a one-shot migration to close the 19 orphaned duplicates across the fleet.

## Why

On 2026-04-21 04:00–13:30 UTC, a GraphQL rate-limit window caused `_find_health_issue` to silently treat `gh` query failures as "not found" and create duplicates. t2574/t2580 REST fallback for CREATE made the duplicate actually succeed where previously it would have also failed (no duplicate). Post-t2574, READ-side queries silently return empty while WRITE succeeds via REST → duplicate created.

**Fleet impact:** 19 orphaned duplicate supervisor/contributor issues across 7 repos (<webapp>/<webapp> ×4, marcusquinn/aidevops ×4, aidevops-routines ×3, others ×2). 84 rate-limit failures logged today.

**Evidence timeline (`~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log`):**

```text
31595: [stats] Health issue: failed to update body for #10944: GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded
30527-31908: [stats] Health issue: could not create for marcusquinn/aidevops (×5)
31990: [stats] Health issue: created #20267 (supervisor) for marcusquinn in marcusquinn/aidevops  <-- DUPLICATE
```

## How

Full brief: `todo/tasks/t2687-brief.md`. Summary:

1. **Layer 1 — Error discrimination in `_find_health_issue`**: distinguish `gh` command rc=0-empty (confirmed-not-found) from rc≠0 (query failed). On rc≠0, preserve cache, return `__QUERY_FAILED__` sentinel, abstain from creation this cycle.
2. **Layer 2 — Periodic dedup**: even on cache hits, run label-based dedup scan once per hour per repo. Closes duplicates that slipped in during prior rate-limit windows.
3. **Migration**: one-shot script closes the 19 existing duplicates and backfills `origin:worker` on #20298 (missing due to REST-fallback side effect).
4. **Tests**: stub-based test harness covers rate-limit-on-view, rate-limit-on-list, rate-limit-on-title, stale-cache-with-two-existing.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-find-health-issue-rate-limit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/migrate-health-issue-duplicates-t2687.sh`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t2687-brief.md`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Rate-limit simulation preserves cache (no `rm -f "$health_issue_file"`) and creates no duplicate
- [ ] Cache-hit path runs dedup scan ≥ 1×/hour and closes stale duplicates
- [ ] Migration closes 19 current duplicates with explanatory comments and dedup marker
- [ ] `shellcheck` zero violations on all modified files
- [ ] Post-merge fleet scan shows zero duplicate `[Supervisor:*]` issues per (repo, runner)

## Follow-ups (will be filed after merge)

- Framework-wide REST fallback for `gh issue view` and `gh issue list` (Layer 3 in the analysis)
- Pulse-level rate-limit circuit breaker (Layer 4)
- Root-cause investigation of `origin:worker` missing on #20298 (likely REST-fallback label-derivation gap)

title: Audit remaining local -n nameref usages for zsh-source compatibility gaps
body:
## Context

PR #20302 fixed one `local -n` nameref incompatibility in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (GH#20300). That fix exposed a broader question: which of the remaining 72 `local -n` usages across 6 deployed helpers are reachable from zsh-sourcing contexts, and therefore need the same pattern applied?

## Scope

This is a **research/audit task**, not a blanket rewrite. 72 sites is too many to fix indiscriminately — most will be reached only via shebang-invoked scripts where the re-exec guard in `shared-constants.sh:30-95` already kicks in (exec → Homebrew bash 4+ on macOS).

The question to answer: **which sites are sourced (not executed) from chains that could originate in zsh?**

That is the specific class of bug that caused GH#20300 — the re-exec guard relies on `BASH_VERSINFO` + `BASH_SOURCE[1]`, both unset when zsh sources a `.sh` file, so the guard never fires and the `local -n` declaration is then evaluated under zsh.

## Audit targets (accurate counts as of 2026-04-21, post-#20302-merge)

| File | Count | Initial reachability hypothesis |
|---|---:|---|
| `.agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh` | 43 | Heaviest user. Likely only executed (not sourced). Verify. |
| `.agents/scripts/email-delivery-test-helper.sh` | 12 | Likely only executed as a script; low risk. |
| `.agents/scripts/document-creation-helper.sh` | 11 | Check if sourced from any document workflows. |
| `.agents/scripts/setup/_tools.sh` | 2 | Sourced by `setup.sh` — verify `setup.sh` invocation origins. |
| `.agents/scripts/thumbnail-helper.sh` | 1 | Likely executed as a script. |
| `.agents/scripts/label-sync-helper.sh` | 1 | Likely executed as a script. |

## How

1. For each file, trace how it's invoked — shebang execution (safe, re-exec guard covers) vs. sourced from another script (potentially unsafe).
2. If a file is ever sourced, check whether that sourcing chain could originate from zsh (user's login shell sourcing `.sh` files via shell init, `aidevops` CLI wrapper chains, etc).
3. Apply the canonical module-globals pattern ONLY to sites that are demonstrably reachable from zsh-sourcing.
4. Document the reachability reasoning per file — "safe because X" is a valid outcome for most sites.

### Reference pattern

`.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh:638-770` — canonical module-globals pattern (`_BRIEF_*`). Key idea: the function sets module-level `_MODULE_VAR` globals; callers read them directly after invocation; no `local -n` declared inside the function body. Pattern-marker comments at `task-brief-helper.sh:643,757` and `linters-local.sh:1402` document this explicitly.

The specific transformation that PR #20302 applied to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:351-386`:

```bash
# Before (bash 4.3+ only — breaks under zsh):
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step() {
    local step="$1" input="$2"
    local -n _out_todo="$3" _out_title="$4"
    # ... sets _out_todo, _out_title via nameref
}

# After (bash 3.2 / zsh safe):
_GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TODO=""
_GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TITLE=""
_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title_step() {
    local step="$1" input="$2"
    _GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TODO=""
    _GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_TITLE=""
    # ... sets _GH_WRAPPER_EXTRACT_{TODO,TITLE} directly
}
```

### Verification per fix

Add a regression test modelled on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh` — exercise the function under zsh directly and assert the module globals are populated. Skip cleanly if `zsh` is not installed on the runner.

### macOS vs Linux coverage

- **macOS (bash 3.2 default, zsh as `/bin/sh`/login shell):** the highest-risk platform — the exact one GH#20300 surfaced on.
- **Legacy Linux (bash 3.2 containers):** same risk class without zsh, any `local -n` is a hard failure.
- **Modern Linux (bash 4+):** `local -n` works, no functional impact, but fixes are still valuable for uniformity.
- **Linux with zsh users:** same zsh-sourcing risk as macOS if they invoke framework helpers via sourced chains.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Per-file reachability analysis documented in follow-up comments or a dedicated decomposition doc
- [ ] Only genuinely-reachable sites get fixed (with documented justification per site)
- [ ] Unreachable sites documented as "safe — shebang-invoked only" with proof of how they're called
- [ ] Regression test per fixed file modelled on `test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh`
- [ ] The `bash 3.2 compatibility` regression gate counter drops by the number of sites fixed (from 82 post-#20302 down by N)

## Anti-scope

- **NOT** "rewrite all 72 sites." That's scope creep without evidence of reachability.
- **NOT** removing the canonical pattern-marker comments at `task-brief-helper.sh:643,757` or `linters-local.sh:1402` — those are the documentation of the pattern.
- **NOT** editing `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — already handled by PR #20302.

## Related

- Fix PR: #20302
- Original bug: #20300
- Re-exec guard (implementation): `shared-constants.sh:30-95`
- Canonical pattern: `task-brief-helper.sh:638-770`
- Regression test template: `test-gh-wrapper-zsh-compat.sh` (added in #20302)


## Children

- #20392 — Audit local -n nameref reachability for all 6 files (t2718, research phase)
- #20393 — Fix setup/_tools.sh local -n nameref usages, 2 sites at lines 96 and 126 (t2719, implementation phase)

_Decomposed by #20388. Hierarchy: audit first (documents which files are safe vs at-risk), then targeted fixes for at-risk files only._

title: t2685: harden gh signature-footer enforcement (PATH shim + plugin hook block)
body:
## What

The `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` output — with its `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` marker, runtime/version/model/token/session metadata, and canonical formatting — is the ONLY acceptable signature footer on GitHub writes. The framework has multiple enforcement paths, all defeatable:

1. **`gh_create_issue` / `gh_issue_comment` / `gh_create_pr` wrappers in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`** auto-inject the sig. Good when agents call these. Defeated by raw `gh` calls.
2. **OpenCode plugin hook `quality-hooks.mjs::checkSignatureFooterGate`** inspects tool calls before execution. Defeated by its current trust check: `cmd.includes("aidevops.sh")` — any string containing the literal domain passes, including hallucinated prose that mentions the domain.
3. **`build.txt` §8 prompt rule** instructs agents to call the helper and never compose inline. Prompt-layer rule only — no hard enforcement.

On 2026-04-21 an interactive cleanup session on a managed private repo (webapp) posted a human-readable footer (`"— interactive cleanup from marcusquinn runtime."`) with no `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` marker and no runtime metadata. All three layers silently allowed it through.

## Why

Hallucinated footers defeat the observability contract — without runtime/version/model fields, we can't trace issues to the session that produced them, correlate outcomes to model tiers, or identify regressions by runtime version. This is a correctness defect in the signature-footer enforcement system, not a cosmetic nit.

## How

Three structural fixes, in order of trust:

1. **PATH shim at `.agents/scripts/gh`** — intercepts `gh issue comment|create` and `gh pr comment|create`, auto-injects `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` output when body lacks the canonical marker. Bypass: `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`. Fast pass-through for all other subcommands.

2. **Tighten `checkSignatureFooterGate`** — replace loose `cmd.includes("aidevops.sh")` with marker-based detection (`<!-- aidevops:sig -->`). Transparent repair via `output.args.command` mutation. Throw mentoring Error on unparseable bodies (heredoc-sourced etc.).

3. **Reinforce `build.txt` §8** — anti-pattern section quoting the exact hallucinated prose structure.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/gh` (PATH shim, shellcheck clean)
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-shim.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs`
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks.mjs` (tighten gate logic)
- EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` §8 (add anti-pattern example)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/setup/_deployment.sh` (chmod +x shim after deploy)

## Acceptance

- [x] All three layers (shim, plugin hook, prompt rule) refuse a hallucinated footer body.
- [x] `gh-signature-helper.sh footer`-generated bodies pass all three layers unmodified.
- [x] Bypass env var (`AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`) works for local diagnosis.
- [x] Regression test coverage: existing `test-gh-wrapper-auto-sig.sh` still passes (30/30).

## Session Origin

- **Branch:** feature/t2685-gh-signature-enforcement
- **Runtime:** OpenCode v1.14.19
- **Conversation:** interactive, triggered by a hallucinated footer incident on a managed private repo during a duplicate-nudge cleanup session on 2026-04-21.

title: t2689: Extend t2574 REST fallback to gh issue view / gh issue list reads
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive. Follow-up to t2687 / PR #20308. See GH#20301 for root-cause context.

## What

Extend the t2574 REST fallback mechanism to cover GitHub `gh issue view` and `gh issue list` read paths — not just CREATE/EDIT writes.

## Why

During GraphQL rate-limit windows (observed 2026-04-21 at 0/5000 remaining for ~45 min), `gh issue view` and `gh issue list` calls fail with non-zero exit codes. t2574 (PR #20255) added REST fallback for CREATE/EDIT paths but NOT for READ paths. The asymmetry means under pressure: reads silently fail → callers treat "failure" as "not found" → duplicate creation.

t2687 (PR #20308) adds rc-aware classification at ONE call site (`_find_health_issue` in `stats-health-dashboard.sh`). That's Layer 1 of the defence-in-depth. Layer 3 is this task: make the READ fallback framework-wide so every caller gets resilience without per-site patches.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

title: t2690: Pulse-level circuit breaker when GraphQL rate-limit budget exhausted
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive. Follow-up to t2687 / PR #20308. Background context: GH#20301.

## What

Add a pulse-level circuit breaker that pauses worker dispatch when the GitHub GraphQL rate-limit budget is exhausted or nearly exhausted, preventing cascade failures across concurrent runners.

## Why

On 2026-04-21, marcusquinn/aidevops GraphQL budget hit 0/5000 for ~45 min. During that window:
- Every worker that tried to create an issue or edit a PR failed at step 1 (until t2574 added REST fallback for writes)
- Every worker that tried to READ an issue also failed (Layer 3 / t2689 will fix reads)
- Watchdogs killed stalled workers
- The pulse kept spawning MORE workers that also failed

Defence-in-depth: t2574 (CREATE/EDIT REST fallback), t2687 (READ rc-awareness at one site), t2689 (framework-wide READ REST fallback). All reactive. A circuit breaker would be proactive — pause dispatch when we know the budget is near-exhausted, so the pulse simply waits instead of burning worker cycles on doomed-to-fail dispatches.

## How (Approach)

### Design questions the worker needs to resolve

1. **Trigger threshold.** At what percentage of GraphQL budget remaining do we trip the breaker? Suggest 5% (250/5000). Configurable via `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` (default 0.05).
2. **Reset condition.** Does the breaker auto-reset when budget recovers (poll `gh api rate_limit` every pulse cycle)? Or require a configurable dwell time?
3. **Scope.** Does the breaker pause ALL dispatch, or just GraphQL-heavy operations (issue creation, PR creation)? REST-only operations (issue label edits, comments via REST fallback) could proceed.
4. **Multi-runner coordination.** Multiple runners share the same GraphQL budget. Should the breaker write a shared state file so all runners see the same signal? Or is per-runner polling acceptable (each sees the same API response)?
5. **Observability.** Log format, audit comment on skipped dispatches, metric counter (`pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` in `pulse-stats.json`).

### Files likely to change

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` — helper with `check | trip | reset | status` subcommands.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` OR `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch.sh` — check the breaker at the top of each dispatch pass.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — add the circuit-breaker as an additional layer before worker spawn (mirrors the t2424 pre-dispatch eligibility gate pattern).
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` — stub `gh api rate_limit`, assert breaker trips at threshold, asserts dispatch aborted.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` (document the breaker)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Circuit breaker helper exists with `check` / `status` subcommands returning exit codes honoured by the pulse.
- [ ] Pulse wrapper calls `check` before dispatching a worker — on trip, skip dispatch, log a `[INFO] pulse: GraphQL budget exhausted, deferring dispatch until next cycle` line.
- [ ] `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` counter in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json` increments on each skipped dispatch.
- [ ] `aidevops status` surfaces the counter and current breaker state.
- [ ] Test harness: stub `gh api rate_limit` to return 4/5000 remaining → breaker trips, dispatch aborts with the correct exit code.
- [ ] Test harness: stub 1000/5000 remaining → breaker does NOT trip, dispatch proceeds.
- [ ] Documentation in `.agents/AGENTS.md` under the "Worker Diagnostics" or "Pulse" section.
- [ ] Threshold configurable via `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` env var.

## Tier rationale

`tier:thinking` — requires design decisions (threshold, reset condition, scope, multi-runner coordination) with no directly-copyable existing pattern. Opus-class reasoning appropriate.

## Context

- Root-cause document: GH#20301
- Reactive layers: t2574 (PR #20255), t2687 (PR #20308), t2689 (GH#20309)
- Related pre-dispatch infrastructure: pre-dispatch-eligibility-helper.sh (t2424 pattern)

title: t2691: Root-cause origin:worker label missing on newly-created source:health-dashboard issues
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive. Follow-up to t2687 / PR #20308. Root-cause context: GH#20301.

## What

Investigate WHY issue #20298 (the health-dashboard duplicate that triggered the t2687 investigation) was created WITHOUT the `origin:worker` label. The t2687 migration script backfills it across the fleet, but the originating bug is unfixed.

## Why

Per `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Session origin labels" rule (t2200):

> `origin:interactive`, `origin:worker`, and `origin:worker-takeover` are mutually exclusive — an issue/PR has exactly one origin.

The health-dashboard runs exclusively from headless pulse context (`stats-health-dashboard.sh` invoked by pulse routines). EVERY health issue it creates MUST carry `origin:worker`. The fact that #20298 was missing it means:

- Either `_create_health_issue` is creating issues via a code path that doesn't apply origin labels,
- OR the REST fallback (t2574) omits labels that the GraphQL path normally includes,
- OR the `gh_create_issue` wrapper was bypassed for some reason.

This matters because:
- Pulse dispatch decisions key on origin labels (`origin:interactive` + assignee = block dispatch per GH#18352)
- Auto-merge gates key on origin (`origin:interactive` auto-merges, `origin:worker` follows different path per t2449)
- Audit trail fidelity — "who created this" is broken when labels don't reflect truth

## How (Investigation approach)

### Facts to gather

1. Read `_create_health_issue` in `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`. Confirm what labels it passes to `gh_create_issue`.
2. Read `gh_create_issue` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. Confirm origin-label application logic.
3. Read REST fallback in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`. Confirm label handling in REST-path issue creation — specifically the separate `POST /repos/.../issues/{N}/labels` call mentioned in AGENTS.md under t2574.
4. Re-read #20298's creation event timeline via `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20298/timeline` to see label application sequence.
5. Check `~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log` around the creation timestamp for any REST-fallback or label-skip log lines.

### Hypothesis to falsify first

**H1**: The REST fallback for `gh_create_issue` (t2574) does NOT apply the auto-detected `origin:*` label because that label is applied synchronously at GraphQL-path issue-creation time but the REST POST endpoint uses a separate labels-application step that may silently fail or skip the origin label specifically. AGENTS.md under "REST fallback for GraphQL-exhausted gh wrappers (t2574)" explicitly describes this: "labels are applied via a separate `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{pr_number}/labels` call since the pulls endpoint does not accept labels at creation time." This is for PR creation — **does the same pattern apply to ISSUE creation?** If yes, and if the separate label-apply call failed, we'd see exactly this symptom (issue created without origin label).

H1 is the most likely candidate. Validate by reading the code before committing to a fix direction.

### Possible remediations (depending on root cause)

- If H1 confirmed: add label-apply retry / error-surfacing in REST fallback.
- If the bug is upstream in `_create_health_issue`: ensure it explicitly passes `--label origin:worker`.
- If the bug is in `gh_create_issue` origin-detection (inferring from session context): make detection robust in headless paths (e.g. when `Claude_HEADLESS` is unset but the caller is clearly pulse-initiated).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh` (extend)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-create-health-issue-origin-label.sh` (new, if warranted)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented in PR body (which of H1/H2/etc. was correct, plus evidence).
- [ ] Code fix prevents recurrence.
- [ ] New or extended test harness reproduces the bug against pre-fix code and passes against post-fix code.
- [ ] Any affected fleet-wide state is surfaced (the migration in t2687 already backfilled; this task should confirm no re-occurrence by spot-checking health issues created after merge).
- [ ] Shellcheck zero violations on modified files.

## Tier rationale

`tier:standard` — investigation + targeted fix, follows existing patterns. If H1 is correct, it is a ~20-line fix in `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`.

## Context

- Root-cause document: GH#20301
- Triggering symptom (missing label): #20298
- Migration that backfilled fleet: PR #20308 (t2687)
- Related infra: t2574 (PR #20255 — REST fallback for writes)

title: bug: 'Prompt guard patterns: Nd old' warning never clears — rsync -a preserves source mtime, so 'aidevops update' is a no-op for the check
body:
## Description

The security startup check `check_prompt_guard_patterns` in
`security-posture-helper.sh` flags the deployed patterns YAML as stale whenever
its **file mtime** is >30 days old, and recommends `aidevops update` as the fix.

However, `deploy_aidevops_agents` (`setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh`) uses
`rsync -a`, which preserves source mtime on copy. If upstream hasn't modified
`.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` in >30 days, re-deploying
copies the same mtime back — and the warning fires again on the next session.

This creates a circular loop visible to any user whose system is fully up to
date during an upstream quiet period:

1. Session start warns: `Prompt guard patterns: 36d old (>30d)`
2. `aidevops security setup` offers: `Run: aidevops update`
3. Update reports: `Framework already up to date!` (correct — content matches)
4. mtime unchanged → warning fires again on next session

The user has no action they can take. The patterns file IS the current
upstream version; the staleness signal is measuring upstream release cadence,
not local drift.

## Expected Behavior

One of the following (maintainers to decide):

- **Option A — touch on confirmed-current deploy.** After `deploy_aidevops_agents`
  completes and the deployed SHA matches upstream HEAD, `touch` the patterns
  YAML so mtime reflects "last confirmed current" rather than "last upstream edit".
- **Option B — compare against upstream commit date, not mtime.** Use
  `git log -1 --format=%ct -- configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` from the
  canonical repo (or the `.deployed-sha` stamp at `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha`)
  as the reference point. If upstream itself hasn't shipped a patterns update
  in 30d, the check is informational at best.
- **Option C — reframe the warning.** "No upstream updates in 30d" is not an
  actionable staleness signal when the local copy already matches upstream.
  Suppress the warning when local == upstream, or promote it to an advisory
  (`[--]` rather than `[!!]`) rather than an action-needed item.

Option A is the smallest delta and preserves the "30 days since we refreshed
your patterns" semantic. Option B is the most correct (measures what it claims
to measure). Option C is the cheapest if the maintainers consider the check
low-value once the other signals (secret storage, gh auth, secretlint) are in.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
aidevops security setup
```

**Actual output**:

```
Security Setup
===============

Walking through pending security actions.

[1] Prompt guard patterns: 36d old (>30d)
    Run: aidevops update

    Run aidevops update now? [Y/n]

Updating AI DevOps Framework

[INFO] Current version: 3.8.88
[INFO] Fetching latest version...
[OK] Framework already up to date!
...
=======================================
Fixed: 1 action(s)
=======================================
```

Next `aidevops security setup` invocation reports the same `36d old` warning.
`Fixed: 1 action(s)` is itself misleading — nothing was fixed; the underlying
file mtime was not updated.

**Expected output**: either no staleness warning (file matches upstream HEAD),
or a warning that clears after a successful update.

**Causal code**:

`~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh` lines 947-983
(`check_prompt_guard_patterns`):

```bash
# Check staleness (>30 days old)
local file_age_days=0
if [[ "$(uname)" == "Darwin" ]]; then
    file_mod=$(stat -f %m "$yaml_file" || echo "0")
    now=$(date +%s)
    file_age_days=$(((now - file_mod) / 86400))
else
    file_age_days=$((($(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$yaml_file" || echo "0")) / 86400))
fi

if [[ "$file_age_days" -gt 30 ]]; then
    CHECK_LABEL="$label: ${file_age_days}d old (>30d)"
    CHECK_FIX="Run: aidevops update"
    return 1
fi
```

`~/Git/aidevops/setup-modules/agent-deploy.sh` line 141 and the
`_atomic_stage_and_deploy_agents` helper both use `rsync -a`, which preserves
source mtime.

No recent commits (last 2 weeks) touch either
`.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh` or
`.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `aidevops update` when upstream hasn't touched
   `.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` for >30 days (current
   upstream file was last touched 2026-03-15 by commit `c091cc6e1`).
2. Start a new session — security greeting says N actions needed.
3. Run `aidevops security setup` — offered fix is `Run: aidevops update`.
4. Accept; update reports "Framework already up to date!".
5. Re-run `aidevops security setup` — same warning, same offered fix.

## Workarounds Applied

None landed — there is no user-side workaround. A user could manually
`touch ~/.aidevops/agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` to suppress
the warning for another 30 days, but this is a local patch for a framework
bug and must not be recommended because it defeats the check's intent: any
real staleness after a subsequent upstream release would still be masked
until that file hits 30d again.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.88
- **Latest version**: 3.8.88
- **Install method**: `~/.local/bin/aidevops` → `~/Git/aidevops/aidevops.sh` (git symlink)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode v1.14.19 with claude-opus-4-7
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (VirtualBox guest)
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

## Additional Context

- Deployed file: `~/.aidevops/agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`
  mtime 2026-03-16 10:58, 27535 bytes.
- Source file: `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`
  mtime 2026-03-16 10:58, 27535 bytes. Content matches.
- Last upstream commit touching this file: `c091cc6e1` on 2026-03-15.
- `Change` time on the deployed file is 2026-04-21 11:16 (today's update),
  confirming rsync ran but preserved the source `Modify` time.
- Stamp file `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha` already exists for t2156 drift
  detection, so Option B can reuse it without new infrastructure.

title: pulse-batch-prefetch: remove unsupported headRefName JSON field from gh search prs calls
body:
## Description

`pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` requests `headRefName` from `gh search prs`, but the GitHub Search API doesn't expose that field — only `gh pr list` and `gh pr view` (the repo-specific REST endpoint) do. Every pulse cycle emits:

```
[pulse-batch-prefetch] gh search prs failed for owner=<owner>: Unknown JSON field: "headRefName"
[pulse-batch-prefetch] refresh complete: search_calls=2 cache_writes=2 errors=1
```

This is a direct sibling of t2577 (#20261), which removed the unsupported `reviewDecision` field from the same call but explicitly preserved `headRefName` — the partial fix missed that `headRefName` suffers from the same incompatibility.

## Expected Behavior

`gh search prs` call on line 268 of `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` should only request fields that the Search API actually supports. The PR prefetch should not log errors on every cycle.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (exact call the framework makes):

```bash
gh search prs --owner robstiles --state open --limit 1 \
  --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository,headRefName,createdAt,author
```

**Actual output**:

```
Unknown JSON field: "headRefName"
Available fields:
  assignees
  author
  authorAssociation
  body
  closedAt
  commentsCount
  createdAt
  id
  isDraft
  isLocked
  isPullRequest
  labels
  number
  repository
  state
  title
  updatedAt
  url
```

**Confirming call without `headRefName`** (succeeds):

```bash
$ gh search prs --owner robstiles --state open --limit 1 \
    --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository,createdAt,author
[]
```

**Causal code**:

```
$ git blame -L 266,270 .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
1868e8262d (Marcus Quinn 2026-04-20 02:38:32 +0100 266) 	pr_json=$(gh search prs --owner "$owner" --state open \
1868e8262d (Marcus Quinn 2026-04-20 02:38:32 +0100 267) 		--limit "$BATCH_SEARCH_LIMIT" \
6ae60e1bbc (Marcus Quinn 2026-04-21 04:59:18 +0100 268) 		--json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository,headRefName,createdAt,author 2>"$pr_err") || pr_json=""
```

Commit `6ae60e1bb` is t2577 (#20261) — the partial fix. Diff from that commit shows the intent was to remove unsupported fields, but it retained `headRefName`:

```diff
-		# PRs: preserve reviewDecision and headRefName if available
+		# PRs: preserve headRefName if available
 		jq '
 			...
-					reviewDecision: (.reviewDecision // null),
 					headRefName: (.headRefName // null),
 		...
-		--json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository,reviewDecision,headRefName,createdAt,author
+		--json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository,headRefName,createdAt,author
```

`gh search prs --help` confirms the supported `--json` fields; `headRefName` is not among them. The Search API returns issue-shaped results (because PRs are issues in GitHub's data model), so repo-head-specific fields like `headRefName` are not available.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `gh search prs --owner <any> --state open --limit 1 --json headRefName` → reproduces error.
2. Observe pulse logs after any cycle: `grep 'gh search prs failed' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` → recurring every refresh.

## Suggested Fix

Two surgical edits to `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`:

1. **Line 268** — drop `headRefName` from the `--json` list:
   ```
   --json number,title,labels,updatedAt,assignees,repository,createdAt,author
   ```
2. **Lines 156, 167** — drop the `headRefName` capture from the `jq` pipeline (the downstream consumer already uses `// null` so callers are tolerant of missing values):
   ```
   # PRs (comment) — update or remove
   # jq {} block — remove the 'headRefName: (.headRefName // null),' line
   ```

If downstream code (e.g. pulse-merge stacked-retarget) truly needs branch names, fetch them lazily via `gh pr view <N> --json headRefName` for the specific PRs that need it — not wholesale in the prefetch path.

## Workarounds Applied

None applied this session. The bug is non-fatal — the call falls through to per-repo GraphQL fetch when the search errors, so pulse continues to operate. The cost is log noise + increased GraphQL consumption (partially defeating the 50× reduction goal of the originating PR #20051 / GH#19963).

## Impact Assessment

- **Severity**: Low (non-fatal, graceful degradation).
- **Frequency**: Every batch prefetch cycle (every pulse tick, ~every 4 min under normal load).
- **Cost**: (a) log noise, (b) `errors=1` in every refresh summary, (c) forced fallback to per-repo GraphQL defeats part of the batch-prefetch optimisation goal.

## Related

- **Introducing PR**: #20051 (GH#19963) — "feat(pulse): batch prefetch via org-level gh search to reduce GraphQL consumption ~50x", merged 2026-04-20.
- **Partial fix PR**: #20261 (t2577) — "remove unsupported reviewDecision field from gh search prs calls", merged 2026-04-21. This is the same class of bug, one field missed.

title: core-routines: r910 (aidevops-skills-sync) script was never shipped — routine fails every 5 min
body:
## Description

Routine `r910` in `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh` is defined as enabled and points at `bin/aidevops-skills-sync`, but the script doesn't exist in either the source tree or the deployed tree. `git log --all -- '.agents/bin/aidevops-skills-sync'` returns zero commits — the script has never been committed to the repo.

Because the routine is scheduled every 5 minutes (`cron(*/5 * * * *)`), every pulse tick where evaluate_routines fires logs:

```
[pulse-wrapper] routine r910: script not found or not executable: /home/rob/.aidevops/agents/bin/aidevops-skills-sync
```

Per `pulse-routines.sh:106-113`, the routine is marked as failed and `_routine_update_state "r910" "failure"` runs — creating false-failure audit records on every cycle.

## Expected Behavior

One of the following:

1. The routine's declared script exists and performs the documented behaviour (refresh agent skills).
2. The routine is disabled (change `|x|` to `| |`) until a script exists.
3. The routine is removed from `core-routines.sh` if no longer planned.
4. `bin/aidevops-skills-sync` is a thin wrapper around the existing `aidevops skills` or `aidevops skill` CLI subcommand (both exist in v3.8.88).

## Reproducer

**Step 1 — routine definition** (`.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh:28`):

```
r910|x|Skills sync — refresh agent skills|repeat:cron(*/5 * * * *)|~15s|bin/aidevops-skills-sync|script
```

**Step 2 — script is missing from both trees**:

```
$ ls -la ~/.aidevops/agents/bin/
drwxrwxr-x  2 rob rob 4096 Apr 19 10:51 .
drwxrwxr-x 24 rob rob 4096 Apr 21 11:17 ..
-rwxrwxr-x  1 rob rob 1194 Apr 19 10:51 gh_create_issue
-rwxrwxr-x  1 rob rob 1179 Apr 19 10:51 gh_create_pr

$ ls -la ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/bin/
drwxrwxr-x  2 rob rob 4096 Apr 19 10:51 .
drwxrwxr-x 25 rob rob 4096 Apr 21 11:15 ..
-rwxrwxr-x  1 rob rob 1194 Apr 19 10:51 gh_create_issue
-rwxrwxr-x  1 rob rob 1179 Apr 19 10:51 gh_create_pr

$ git -C ~/Git/aidevops log --all --follow --oneline -- '.agents/bin/aidevops-skills-sync'
# (empty — never committed)
```

**Step 3 — live failure in pulse log** (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`):

```
[pulse-wrapper] routine r910 is due (expr=cron(*/5 * * * *), last_run_epoch=1776786570)
[pulse-wrapper] routine r910: script not found or not executable: /home/rob/.aidevops/agents/bin/aidevops-skills-sync
```

**Causal code**:

The handler at `.agents/scripts/pulse-routines.sh:106-113`:

```bash
local script_path="${agents_dir}/${run_script}"
if [[ ! -x "$script_path" ]]; then
    echo "[pulse-wrapper] routine ${routine_id}: script not found or not executable: ${script_path}" >>"$LOGFILE"
    _routine_update_state "$routine_id" "failure"
    return 1
fi
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.8.88.
2. Start pulse (`aidevops pulse start`).
3. Wait 5 minutes for routine evaluation.
4. Observe `grep r910 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` — the "script not found" line recurs every 5 minutes.

## Systemic Pattern

While investigating r910 I audited all r9xx core routines. **Four of fourteen** core routines reference scripts that don't ship in either tree:

```
r901 | scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh                          | OK
r902 | bin/aidevops-auto-update check                    | MISSING in source + deployed
r903 | scripts/process-guard-helper.sh kill-runaways     | OK
r904 | scripts/worker-watchdog.sh --check                | OK
r905 | scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh                | OK
r906 | bin/aidevops-repo-sync check                      | MISSING in source + deployed
r907 | scripts/contribution-watch-helper.sh scan         | OK
r908 | scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh update           | OK
r909 | scripts/screen-time-helper.sh snapshot            | OK
r910 | bin/aidevops-skills-sync                          | MISSING in source + deployed  ← this issue
r911 | scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh refresh              | OK
r912 | server/index.ts                                   | MISSING in source + deployed
r913 | scripts/opencode-db-maintenance-helper.sh auto    | OK
r914 | scripts/repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh run        | OK
```

Only r910 is currently noisy in logs because it runs every 5 minutes. The others are on 10-min / daily / persistent schedules and either haven't fired in the observed window or fail silently under less frequent evaluation. This suggests a process gap — routines were seeded without a pre-deploy check that verifies each `script` path resolves.

**Note**: the aidevops CLI has matching subcommands for three of the missing `bin/` scripts:

- `aidevops auto-update <cmd>` ↔ r902 expects `bin/aidevops-auto-update check`
- `aidevops repo-sync <cmd>` ↔ r906 expects `bin/aidevops-repo-sync check`
- `aidevops skill <cmd>` / `aidevops skills <cmd>` ↔ r910 expects `bin/aidevops-skills-sync`

This suggests the intended implementation was thin `bin/*` wrappers around the CLI subcommands, and those wrappers simply weren't written (or weren't committed) before the seeding PR merged.

## Workarounds Applied

None applied this session. The failure is non-fatal (pulse continues), but creates false failure records in the routine state file and recurring log noise.

## Impact Assessment

- **r910 specifically**: recurring log entry every 5 minutes; routine is recorded as "failed" in state updates, which pollutes `routine-log-helper.sh` history and could skew routine health dashboards.
- **Systemic (r902/r906/r910/r912)**: documented functionality (auto-update, repo-sync, skills-sync, dashboard server) is referenced but non-functional as declared. Users reading `describe_r910()` etc. in the docs will expect working routines.
- **Upstream tracking issue exists**: `robstiles/aidevops-routines#10` (`r910: Skills sync`) was auto-created by PR #17967 but hasn't been paired with an implementation.

## Suggested Fix Directions

Pick one of:

1. **Ship the scripts** — write `bin/aidevops-skills-sync` (and siblings) as the thin CLI wrappers the naming implies. `describe_r910()`'s documented behaviour (regenerate SKILL.md, update symlinks, process only changed files) is already close to what `aidevops skills` / `aidevops skill update` might do.
2. **Redirect to CLI subcommands** — change r910's `run:` field in `core-routines.sh` from `bin/aidevops-skills-sync` to `bin/aidevops skills update` (or whichever subcommand actually implements the sync). Same approach for r902, r906.
3. **Disable** — flip `|x|` to `| |` for the four affected routines until implementations land.
4. **Pre-deploy validation** — add an invariant check during `setup.sh` / `aidevops update` that resolves every `script` path in `core-routines.sh` and fails loudly if any is missing. This closes the process gap that allowed PR #17967 to merge with broken references.

Recommendation: combine #2 (immediate relief — redirect to existing CLI subcommands) with #4 (invariant) so the specific r910 symptom stops today and the pattern cannot recur.

## Related

- **Introducing PR**: #17967 — "feat: seed core routine descriptions and tracking issues into routines repo", merged 2026-04-08. PR body claims it seeded "12 core aidevops launchd routines (pulse, auto-update, process-guard, watchdog, memory-pressure, repo-sync, contribution-watch, profile-readme, screen-time, skills-sync, token-refresh, dashboard)" — four of the twelve have no backing script.
- **Auto-created tracking issue**: `robstiles/aidevops-routines#10` (private; created by `routine-log-helper.sh` during the seed run).
- **Documentation**: `.agents/scripts/routines/core-routines.sh` lines 534-569 (`describe_r910()`) describes expected behaviour but no script exists to perform it.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.88
- **Latest version**: 3.8.88

- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode

title: t2692: scrub private repo references from aidevops codebase
body:
## Session Origin

Flagged during the t2685 signature-footer session. The agent composed issue/PR/brief/commit content that referenced a managed private repo by its actual slug. User surfaced the leak; this issue tracks the remediation.

## What

Two coordinated fixes, already implemented in the worktree for this branch:

1. **Code-tree scrub** — replace every occurrence of the private slug and URL with the generic placeholder `webapp` across 20 files: `TODO.md`, 7 brief files (`t2685`, `t2434`, `t2112`, `t2113`, `t2114`, `t2031`, `t1968`), 1 research doc (`todo/research/optimize-brief-tiers.md`), 5 scripts (`post-merge-review-scanner.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`, `pulse-merge.sh`, `pulse-dep-graph.sh`, `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`), 6 tests.
2. **Privacy-guard config fix** (already applied out-of-band, not part of this PR) — `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` had `local_only: null` + `mirror_upstream: null`, so the guard treated the repo as public. Fixed by setting `mirror_upstream: true` AND creating `~/.aidevops/configs/privacy-guard-extra-slugs.txt` as a belt-and-braces backup.

## Why

Cross-repo privacy rule (`prompts/build.txt` + `.agents/AGENTS.md`): private repo names must never appear in the aidevops codebase. Leak surfaces scrubbed pre-PR:

- GitHub issue bodies (via REST PATCH)
- GitHub PR descriptions (via REST PATCH)
- Memory DB (121 rows, via SQL UPDATE with backup)

## How

- Ordered `perl -i -pe` pipeline applied per-file: URL form → pair form → bare slug → `webapp`.
- Manually edited `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1256` to replace `(GH#<slug>)` with `(observed downstream)` since `GH#webapp` would be a malformed ref.
- All 5 scrubbed scripts + 6 tests pass `bash -n`.
- `rg -c '<slug>' .agents/ todo/ TODO.md` returns zero matches in the worktree.

## Acceptance

- [x] Zero occurrences of the private slug in `.agents/`, `todo/`, `TODO.md` (verified).
- [x] All scrubbed shell scripts pass syntax check.
- [x] Remote public content already scrubbed (issue #20306 + PR #20307 body + release v3.8.89).
- [x] Privacy-guard config fixed so this cannot silently recur.
- [ ] PR merged and post-merge redeploy via `setup.sh --non-interactive`.
- [ ] Patch release cut so scrubbed scripts propagate to peers.

## Out of Scope

- 49 commit-message bodies across git history that leak the slug. Two are on `main` (t2685 squash + t2572 squash); the rest are on merged feature branches still reachable via PR head refs on GitHub. Scrubbing would require force-push on `main`, which is explicitly forbidden by the framework safety rules. Accepted as historical.
- Memory backup file `memory-backup-pre-<webapp>-scrub-20260421T173533Z.db` still contains the leak. Out of scope here; will be pruned in a follow-up once recent-history confidence is established.

title: t2694: bump pulse-wrapper canary test timeout from 30s to 60s
body:
## Session Origin

Flagged during the t2692 interactive session (2026-04-21). The canary test timed out at the 30s boundary on CI despite passing Test 1 in ~20s — the same flake also broke the t2685 main merge immediately before. Local runs complete in ~8-10s, so the flake is CI runner slowness near the timeout edge, not a regression.

## What

Change the `timeout 30` in the two subshell invocations inside `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh` (Tests 1 and 2 — `test_canary_exits_zero` and `test_canary_prints_checkpoint`) to `timeout 60`. The bump keeps the failure mode "fast" on actual regressions (max 60s wait instead of 30s) while eliminating the runner-slowness flake.

## Why

Framework Validation job failed on PR #20318 and again on the t2685 main merge — both with exit code 124 (timeout signal) after Test 1 passed at ~20s. The canary's purpose is to catch set -e exit-code propagation regressions by running pulse-wrapper.sh --canary — a 60s budget is still tight enough to catch a hung canary while being forgiving of runner jitter.

## How

Two `oldString`/`newString` replacements in the same file, identical in pattern:

File: \`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh\`

### Files to modify

- EDIT: \`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh\` — two \`timeout 30\` → \`timeout 60\` substitutions inside \`test_canary_exits_zero\` (around line 78) and \`test_canary_prints_checkpoint\` (around line 107).

Exact replacement block 1 (test_canary_exits_zero):

\`\`\`
	output=\$(
		HOME=\"\${sandbox}/home\" \\
			FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=1 \\
			timeout 30 bash \"\$WRAPPER_SCRIPT\" --canary 2>&1
	)
\`\`\`

becomes:

\`\`\`
	output=\$(
		HOME=\"\${sandbox}/home\" \\
			FULL_LOOP_HEADLESS=1 \\
			timeout 60 bash \"\$WRAPPER_SCRIPT\" --canary 2>&1
	)
\`\`\`

Replacement block 2 (test_canary_prints_checkpoint) is textually identical in the current file; use \`replaceAll=true\` or make the two edits separately with surrounding context to disambiguate.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Both \`timeout 30\` → \`timeout 60\` replacements applied.
- [ ] \`bash -n .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh\` passes.
- [ ] Local run \`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-canary.sh\` passes (all 4 tests green, exits 0, takes <30s wall clock).
- [ ] CI Framework Validation job passes on the PR.

title: bug: /log-issue-aidevops allows duplicate filings — search indexing lag + no idempotency in gh issue create
body:
## Description

The `/log-issue-aidevops` command and its backing `log-issue-helper.sh search` subcommand have a **race window** between the duplicate-check step and the issue-creation step that permits duplicate issue filings from a single user session. There is **no body-hash fingerprint**, **no idempotency on `gh issue create`**, and **no recent-by-author filtering** — dedup is entirely dependent on GitHub's search index having caught up, which it often hasn't.

The duplicate-check itself (Step 3 in the command doc) uses `gh issue list --search "KEYWORDS"`, which:

1. Hits GitHub's search index, which has a **2-10 second indexing lag** after an issue is created.
2. Is **agent-driven** — the LLM composes the keywords. Identical-body submissions with differently-chosen keywords will miss each other.
3. Is **not atomic with creation** — even if Step 3 returns zero hits, Step 6 runs `gh issue create` with no further check.

On a `gh issue create` transient failure (network timeout, 5xx), the agent or the user retrying will create a second issue — the first may have succeeded server-side. There is no reconciliation.

## Expected Behavior

One of the following (maintainers to decide — all three can coexist):

- **Option A — body-hash fingerprint file.** Before `gh issue create`, hash `(title + body + author)` and look it up in `~/.aidevops/state/log-issue-fingerprints.jsonl` (timestamp + issue number). If the same fingerprint was filed in the last N seconds (suggest 60), either (a) abort with "you filed this N seconds ago: #NNN" or (b) `gh issue comment` on the prior issue instead of creating a new one. Append on success. This is **deterministic** and not subject to search indexing lag.

- **Option B — `gh_create_issue` wrapper with built-in idempotency.** Wrap `gh issue create` in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` so that every call first runs `gh issue list --author @me --search "<title-verbatim>" --created ">$(date -d '-60s' --iso-8601=seconds)"` and short-circuits if a match exists. Opt-out flag for intentional sequential filings (`--allow-duplicate`).

- **Option C — recent-by-author pre-check in `/log-issue-aidevops`.** Step 3 currently does a keyword search across all issues/all states. Add a second check: `gh issue list --author @me --state open --created '>PT5M'` — anything this user filed in the last 5 minutes that has a >80% title match is a likely dup. Deterministic, no state file needed.

Option A is the most robust (works across sessions, surviving process crashes). Option B automates it at the API surface (wider blast radius — affects every `gh_create_issue` caller, not just `/log-issue-aidevops`). Option C is the cheapest and most targeted.

## Reproducer

**Live reproducer** (both open in repo, one now closed as dup):

- #20312 — created 2026-04-21T16:07:58Z by @robstiles
- #20313 — created 2026-04-21T16:08:10Z by @robstiles (closed as dup)

**Byte-identical bodies**. **12-second gap** between filings. Same session (identical signature-footer metadata: "13m and 29,474 tokens"). GitHub's search index did not surface #20312 when #20313 was about to be filed — OR the dedup check wasn't run — OR the first `gh issue create` returned an error that masked its server-side success.

**Ironically**, the `github-actions[bot]` auto-response on both issues says:

> Tip: For faster, higher-quality issue reporting, use `/log-issue-aidevops` in your AI assistant session. It gathers diagnostics automatically and checks for duplicates.

The "checks for duplicates" claim is the failure mode — dedup ran (or was supposed to run) and still produced two copies.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From an AI assistant session, invoke `/log-issue-aidevops` with any framework bug report.
2. After Step 4 composes the body, let the agent retry the `gh issue create` call twice in rapid succession (or simulate by running the same `gh issue create` command twice manually within 10 seconds).
3. Two issues are filed with identical bodies. The second Step 3 run, if done within indexing lag, does not find the first.

**Alternative reproducer** (explicit race): two concurrent sessions run `/log-issue-aidevops` on the same bug within 5 seconds. Both pass Step 3 (empty results) and both file. Not yet observed but structurally possible.

## Causal Code

**Command doc** — `.agents/scripts/commands/log-issue-aidevops.md`:

- Lines 115-121 (Step 3): agent-driven `gh issue list --search` with no post-creation verification.
- Lines 243-253 (Step 6): `gh issue create` with no idempotency wrapper.

**Helper** — `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh`:

- Lines 167-183 (`search_issues()`): thin wrapper over `gh issue list --search`, no fingerprint lookup.
- No `filed_recently()`, no `fingerprint_lookup()`, no `check_not_recently_filed()` subcommand exists.

**Wrapper** — `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (for Option B): `gh_create_issue` currently has no idempotency logic — if it did, Option B would be near-free.

## Workarounds Applied

During this session I hit two adjacent framework gaps while investigating:

1. **`isGhWriteCommand` false-positive** (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:47-55`): the regex `\bgh\s+(pr\s+(create|comment)|issue\s+(create|comment))\b` matches the literal text `gh issue create` inside a `--search` argument value, blocking legitimate read commands like `gh issue list --search "idempotency gh issue create"`. Workaround: reword the search string. Root cause: regex doesn't distinguish command body from quoted argument content. File as sibling issue if confirmed.

2. **Plugin module caching**: on first session attempt, the patched `quality-hooks.mjs` was on disk but OpenCode's cached module still had the broken version — bash was 100% blocked. Required a fresh process (not just a new session). Already addressed by t2693/#20320.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.91 (post-t2693 patch)
- **Observed duplicates**: #20312 and #20313 (see Reproducer)
- **OS**: macOS (investigation) — bug is OS-agnostic, platform doesn't matter for the race
- **Reporter of duplicates**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (per #20312 environment)

## Additional Context

- The `/log-issue-aidevops` command doc's Step 3 admonishes the agent to "present them and ask" when duplicates are found. This is a **soft gate** — the agent can skip it or miss matches. Any durable fix must be deterministic (file-system or API-level), not agent-driven.
- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` exists for worker dispatch and implements layered deterministic checks. An analogous `issue-create-dedup-helper.sh` with fingerprint + recent-window + author-filter would be the natural pattern match.
- Sibling issue territory (optional split-out):
  - `isGhWriteCommand` regex false-positive on quoted arguments
  - `gh issue create` idempotency in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (Option B above, as its own task)

title: t2696: extract standalone SYNC_PAT visibility step in sync-on-pr-merge to match the other three jobs
body:
## Session Origin

Discovered during the t2692 interactive session (2026-04-21) while investigating why the user thought SYNC_PAT wasn't set. It IS set and the other three jobs are using it correctly, but sync-on-pr-merge has an inconsistent visibility pattern that can mask the signal on common PR types.

## What

The t2166 brief (`todo/tasks/t2166-brief.md`) states the intent was to "add the same warning to all four jobs" of `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml`. Three of the four jobs — `sync-on-push` (line 68), `sync-on-issue` (line 206), `manual-sync` (line 282) — have an explicit, unconditional standalone step:

```
      - name: Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)
        env:
          SYNC_PAT_PRESENT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT != '' && 'true' || '' }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z "${SYNC_PAT_PRESENT:-}" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::SYNC_PAT secret is not set — TODO.md auto-sync push will be rejected by branch protection (GH006)."
            ...
          else
            echo "::notice::SYNC_PAT present — TODO.md push will use PAT"
          fi
```

The fourth job, `sync-on-pr-merge` (starts line 348), does NOT have this standalone step. Its visibility check is inlined deep inside the `Update TODO.md proof-log` step (lines 750-754) and is gated on THREE upstream conditions:

1. `steps.extract.outputs.task_id != ''` (line 678)
2. Not a range-syntax PR title (lines 725-728 early-exit)
3. Not a planning-only PR with For/Ref references (lines 740-743 early-exit)

If any of those gates fire, the visibility warning never emits — even when SYNC_PAT is unset. This is common: every `Ref #NNN` / `For #NNN` planning PR merge hits gate 3 and silently skips the signal.

## Why

Operator diagnosis path: when investigating "is SYNC_PAT configured?", operators look at the most recent issue-sync workflow run. If the most recent run is `sync-on-pr-merge` on a planning PR (common), they see no signal at all — neither `::notice::present` nor `::warning::unset`. The other three jobs give an unconditional signal on every run.

This also contradicts the t2166 brief's stated intent ("add the same warning to all four jobs"). The implementation shipped a partial fix.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` — insert a standalone `Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)` step at the top of the `sync-on-pr-merge` job (after line 361, before the `Extract task ID and collect linked issues` step at line 365).

The step is a verbatim copy of the existing step at lines 282-292 (from `manual-sync`, which has no `if:` gate and thus always runs). Paste it as the first step of `sync-on-pr-merge.steps`.

Exact insertion block (place between line 361 `steps:` and line 365 `- name: Extract task ID...`):

```yaml
      # t2166 / t2696: visibility check mirroring the other three jobs.
      # Ensures the warning/notice emits unconditionally on every merged PR,
      # not just when the downstream TODO.md proof-log path actually runs
      # (which is skipped by range-syntax titles and planning-only PR bodies).
      - name: Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)
        env:
          SYNC_PAT_PRESENT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT != '' && 'true' || '' }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z "${SYNC_PAT_PRESENT:-}" ]]; then
            echo "::warning::SYNC_PAT secret is not set — TODO.md auto-sync push will be rejected by branch protection (GH006)."
            echo "::warning::Fix: gh secret set SYNC_PAT --repo ${REPO} --body \"<FINE_GRAINED_PAT>\" (Contents: Read and write)"
          else
            echo "::notice::SYNC_PAT present — TODO.md push will use PAT"
          fi
```

Leave the existing inlined block at lines 750-754 in place — it's still useful as a close-to-the-push-attempt reminder when the proof-log path actually runs.

### Optional secondary fix (low priority, include if trivial)

The two `gh api` steps in `sync-on-pr-merge` — `Find issue by task ID` (line 418) and `Apply closing hygiene` (line 464) — use `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` only, no SYNC_PAT fallback. Functionally this is fine (they only read/comment, not push). For consistency with the other three jobs which uniformly use the fallback, consider changing both to `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`. Skip this if it's out of scope; the primary fix is the visibility step.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New standalone `Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)` step present at top of `sync-on-pr-merge` job.
- [ ] Step runs unconditionally (no `if:` gate, matching `manual-sync`).
- [ ] YAML syntax valid: `yq eval '.jobs."sync-on-pr-merge".steps[0].name' .github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` returns `Check SYNC_PAT visibility (t2166)`.
- [ ] Workflow file still passes `actionlint` if installed locally.
- [ ] On the next PR merge (this PR's own merge), the `Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` run emits either `::notice::SYNC_PAT present` or `::warning::SYNC_PAT secret is not set` at the top of the log. Verify by running `gh run view <run-id> --log | grep -iE "SYNC_PAT present|SYNC_PAT secret is not set"` and confirming one of them is printed within the first step of the job.

## Out of Scope

- Rewriting the inlined SYNC_PAT check at lines 750-754 — leave it in place.
- Any change to the 3 already-working jobs.
- Investigation of the `::warning::` vs `::notice::` threshold policy (separate design question).

## Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml`

title: t2697: Harden plugin re-export regression test to auto-discover all plugin .mjs files
body:
---
mode: subagent
---

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
# t2697: Harden plugin re-export regression test to auto-discover all plugin .mjs files

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `plugin reexport test auto-discover` → 0 hits — no prior lessons (expected; this test shipped in v3.8.91)
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 commit (7f504cefa, merge of PR #20320 that introduced the test) / 1 merged PR (#20320) / 0 open PRs touch target file in last 48h
- [x] File refs verified: 1 ref checked, present at HEAD (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs:128-133`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:simple` — single-file test change, exact diff block provided, no design decisions

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-21
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (post-v3.8.91 hardening)
- **Created by:** marcusquinn (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Conversation context:** After shipping v3.8.91 with a regression test for the re-export-only-used-locally pattern (PR #20320), we noted the test only covers 4 hardcoded files out of 47 plugin .mjs files. New plugin files with the same bug pattern would slip through silently. Store-a-lesson-in-memory protects only the session that recalls it; framework-wide protection requires shipping the fix in code.

## What

Replace the hardcoded `CANDIDATES` list in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs` with an auto-discovery loop that reads the plugin directory and runs the regression check against every `.mjs` file except `index.mjs`. After the change, all 46 non-entry-point plugin files are covered; any new plugin `.mjs` file added to the directory is automatically tested — no manual CANDIDATES maintenance required.

## Why

The hardcoded list (4 files) covers ~8.5% of the 47 plugin `.mjs` files. The re-export-only-used-locally bug is a silent runtime failure (`ReferenceError: X is not defined` at call time), and the test exists specifically to catch it at CI time. When a new plugin file lands with the same pattern, the hardcoded list does not protect against it — defeating the whole point of having the test. Auto-discovery closes this gap structurally.

This is the code counterpart to the meta-lesson: protections must ship in code (tests, lint rules, workflow checks) to reach all users of the framework — memory recall only benefits the session that queries for it.

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [x] **2 or fewer files to modify?** 1 file
- [x] **Every target file under 500 lines?** 144 lines
- [x] **Exact `oldString`/`newString` for every edit?** Yes — two small blocks below
- [x] **No judgment or design decisions?** Mechanical replacement; exclusion of `index.mjs` is the only filter
- [x] **No error handling or fallback logic to design?** None — `readdirSync` throws on missing dir, which is already a test-infrastructure error
- [x] **No cross-package or cross-module changes?** Single file
- [x] **Estimate 1h or less?** ~15 min including verification
- [x] **4 or fewer acceptance criteria?** 3 criteria

All checked = `tier:simple`.

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`

**Tier rationale:** Single-file test change with two verbatim oldString/newString blocks provided. No judgment required — auto-discovery pattern is `readdirSync(dir).filter(...).sort()`. Exclusion of `index.mjs` is a single equality check. Passes all simple-tier disqualifiers.

## PR Conventions

Leaf (non-parent) issue — PR body uses `Resolves #NNN` as normal.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs:22` — add `readdirSync` to the `node:fs` import
- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs:127-133` — replace hardcoded `CANDIDATES` array with auto-discovery call

### Implementation Steps

1. Add `readdirSync` to the existing `node:fs` import at line 22.

**oldString:**

```javascript
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
```

**newString:**

```javascript
import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";
```

2. Replace the hardcoded `CANDIDATES` array with an auto-discovery loop that enumerates all `.mjs` files in `pluginDir` except `index.mjs` (the plugin entry point, which re-exports everything and is the one file where re-export-only semantics are intended).

**oldString:**

```javascript
// Files known to use the re-export pattern — extend when new ones land.
const CANDIDATES = [
  "quality-hooks.mjs",
  "google-proxy.mjs",
  "oauth-pool.mjs",
  "agent-loader.mjs",
];
```

**newString:**

```javascript
// Auto-discover all plugin .mjs files except the entry point (index.mjs).
// Rationale: hardcoded lists silently miss new files that ship with the
// re-export-only-used-locally bug pattern. t2697 closes that gap by scanning
// the plugin directory on every test run. `index.mjs` is excluded because it
// is a pure re-export barrel — the pattern this test flags is legitimate there.
const CANDIDATES = readdirSync(pluginDir)
  .filter((name) => name.endsWith(".mjs") && name !== "index.mjs")
  .sort();
```

3. Run the test locally to confirm all 46 files pass (no regressions from v3.8.91's fix).

### Verification

```bash
# All 46 non-entry-point plugin .mjs files should be tested and pass.
cd /Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs 2>&1 | tail -20

# Expected: "tests 46" (not 4). Zero failures.
# Confirm test count bumped from 4 to 46:
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs 2>&1 | grep -E "^# tests"
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test count bumps from 4 to 46 (one per non-index `.mjs` plugin file).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "cd /Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops && node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qE '^# tests 46$'"
  ```

- [ ] All 46 tests pass (no regressions from the existing v3.8.91 fix).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "cd /Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops && node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs 2>&1 | grep -qE '^# fail 0$'"
  ```

- [ ] No hardcoded file names remain in the CANDIDATES definition.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: '"quality-hooks\.mjs"'
    path: ".agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs"
    expect: absent
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Why `index.mjs` is excluded:** `index.mjs` is the plugin entry point — it legitimately uses `export { X } from "./Y"` to re-export everything without needing local bindings. The test would false-positive on it.
- **Why sort():** Deterministic test ordering aids debugging when a specific file fails.
- **Why not glob:** `readdirSync` + `filter` is a single stdlib call, no dependency. Matches the test's existing "vanilla node" style.
- **Rejected alternative:** Adding a comment above the hardcoded list saying "remember to update this". That IS the current state; it has already failed once (only 4 of 47 files covered after v3.8.91 merged).
- **Not goals:** Refactoring the test's detection logic. Changing how `findReExportLocalUseViolations` works. Adding new detection rules. This task is scoped to the CANDIDATES enumeration only.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs:22` — import statement to extend
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-reexport-local-binding.mjs:127-133` — hardcoded array to replace
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — the one file correctly excluded from scanning
- `.github/workflows/plugin-import-check.yml` — runs this test; no changes needed (already invokes the test file)

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** nothing critical, but defensive for any future plugin file additions
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 2m | Read the 144-line test file |
| Implementation | 5m | Two small edits |
| Testing | 5m | Run `node --test` locally, confirm count is 46 and all pass |
| **Total** | **~15m** | |

title: t2698: enhance issue-sync-helper.sh pull to seed TODO.md entries for orphan GitHub issues
body:
## Task

Enhance `issue-sync-helper.sh pull` so that when it detects an orphan GitHub issue (an open issue with a parseable task ID that has no matching line in `TODO.md`), it **seeds a new `[ ]` entry in `TODO.md`** instead of only reporting the orphan via stderr.

## Why

`TODO.md` is the designated master source of truth for planned and in-progress work. Today `pull` already detects orphans and emits `ORPHAN: #NNNN ...` on stderr, ending with a summary like `Refs synced: 0 | Orphans open: 2 closed: 53`. It then stops — it does not write a TODO entry. That creates a silent gap:

- Issues opened via `claim-task-id.sh --no-issue` followed by a direct `gh issue create` never get a TODO entry.
- Issues created manually by maintainers via `gh issue create` likewise.
- Result: the task is invisible in `TODO.md` throughout its lifecycle. When the implementation PR merges, `sync-on-pr-merge` has no `[ ]` line to flip to `[x]`, so the task never appears in the historical record either.

Without this fix the "TODO.md is source of truth" invariant is load-bearing wrongly — orphans become permanent blind spots.

### Concrete failure evidence from the session that filed this issue

- `t2696` was claimed via `claim-task-id.sh --no-issue --title ...` (ID allocated, no issue created by helper).
- Issue `#20324` was then created manually via `gh issue create --body ...` with the `auto-dispatch` label.
- The next `sync-on-issue` workflow run (id `24736909933`) detected `#20324` as ORPHAN, logged `Refs synced: 0 | Orphans open: 2 closed: 53`, but did not seed any TODO entry.
- The filing session had to hand-seed a `[ ]` line in a follow-up planning PR to restore parity. This PR (the one that opens t2698) is doing exactly that for both `#20324` and for t2698's own entry.

## How

Target file: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh`

1. Locate the orphan-detection code path in `pull()` / the helper's pull command. Grep for the `ORPHAN:` log string to find the exact site (e.g. `rg -n 'ORPHAN:' .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh .agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh`).
2. When an orphan is detected (open issue whose task ID cannot be found in TODO.md), construct a `[ ]` line and append to the chronological tail of TODO.md's Tasks section.
3. **Task ID extraction** from the issue, in this priority order:
   - Title prefix `tNNN:` or `GH#NNN:` — use the existing extractor pattern `_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (read it; don't re-derive).
   - Fall back to a `tNNN` or `GH#NNN` token found in the issue body.
   - If neither is found, **skip and log** `ORPHAN (no task ID): #NNNN` — do not seed, not safely attributable.
4. **Line format** (must match existing entries exactly so `map_tags_to_labels` round-trips cleanly):
   ```
   - [ ] {task_id} {title_without_prefix} #{tag}#{tag}... ref:GH#{issue_number}
   ```
   - Labels → tags: reverse the forward map in `map_tags_to_labels()` (read `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` to find it; likely a paired forward-only function today). For each GitHub label that has a reverse mapping, emit `#{tag}`.
   - Preserve label ordering (stable sort by label name) so tests are deterministic.
   - Omit tags with no reverse mapping (e.g. `tier:simple`, `status:*` — these are derived at sync time, not source-of-truth in TODO.md).
5. **Placement**: append to the chronological tail of the open-tasks section of TODO.md. The file is loosely chronological by addition time, not strictly sorted. Follow the same append pattern that `claim-task-id.sh` uses when it pushes a freshly-claimed TODO line — grep `claim-task-id.sh` for `>> TODO.md` or similar append site.
6. **Idempotency**: if the issue already has any TODO line (even a stale `[x]`), do not duplicate. The existing orphan-detection logic already determines "no match found"; the seeding fires only inside that not-found branch.
7. **Dry-run safety**: if the helper already exposes a dry-run flag on `pull`, gate writes on it and emit `would seed: - [ ] tNNN ...` to stderr in dry-run mode. If no dry-run flag exists yet, add one — the existing tests likely need it.

### Pattern to copy (read these files first)

- **Task ID extraction**: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — search for `_gh_wrapper_extract_task_id_from_title`. That function already handles `tNNN:` and `GH#NNN:` prefixes; reuse it rather than writing a new regex.
- **TODO.md append**: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — search for the block that writes a new line to TODO.md after successful issue creation. Mirror its approach (atomic append, line-ending hygiene, blank-line separator).
- **Label-to-tag reverse map**: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` — find `map_tags_to_labels()`. Invert the pairs at call time (don't hardcode a second map — risk of drift).

### Edge cases to handle explicitly

- **Issue is CLOSED** but no TODO line exists → **do not seed**. Report-only. (The correction window has passed; seeding `[x]` lines for work nobody tracks pollutes the file.)
- **Issue is OPEN but task ID prefix is malformed** (e.g. `tABC:`, `T2698:`) → skip, log `ORPHAN (unparseable task ID): #NNNN`.
- **Issue has `parent-task` label** → seed as usual, but **do not** emit `#auto-dispatch` even if the label is also applied. Parents are never dispatched (see `prompts/build.txt` parent-task rule).
- **Issue title has no `tNNN:`/`GH#NNN:` prefix and no ref in body** → skip, log `ORPHAN (no task ID): #NNNN`.
- **Multiple task IDs in title** (rare, e.g. `tNNN/tMMM:`): take the first, log `ORPHAN (multi-ID, using first): #NNNN tNNN`.
- **Issue body is NULL** (unlikely but possible on deleted-then-restored issues): treat as empty, fall through to "no task ID" branch.

## Acceptance

1. `issue-sync-helper.sh pull` (default mode, not dry-run) on a repo with an open orphan → issue gets a `[ ]` TODO line with correct task ID, title, `#tag` labels, and `ref:GH#NNN`. `pull` exit code 0.
2. Running `pull` a second time with the same orphan now-seeded → no duplicate TODO line; line count unchanged.
3. `pull --dry-run` on a repo with an open orphan → stderr emits `would seed: - [ ] tNNN ...` with the full proposed line; TODO.md unchanged on disk.
4. New regression test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pull-seeds-orphans.sh` covers: (a) open orphan seeded, (b) closed orphan not seeded, (c) duplicate-run no-op, (d) malformed-title skip, (e) `parent-task` label does not get `#auto-dispatch`, (f) dry-run no write, (g) missing task ID skipped with correct log line.
5. The existing `Refs synced: N | Orphans open: M closed: K` summary line updates to include seeds: proposed new format `Refs synced: N | Orphans seeded: S | Orphans skipped: X`. Preserve the `Orphans open: M closed: K` decomposition in a second line if any tooling parses the current format (grep `Refs synced` across `.agents/` to check).
6. Manual end-to-end validation documented in the PR body: trigger a sync-on-issue run on this repo after the fix merges, confirm a freshly-orphaned issue is seeded on the next run. Include the run id and a diff snippet in the PR description.

- **EDIT** `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh` — factor the `_seed_orphan_todo_line` helper here if logic is reusable; otherwise keep it in the helper.
- **NEW** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pull-seeds-orphans.sh` — regression test covering the Acceptance matrix.
- **Possibly EDIT** `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` — only if a summary-comment step parses the `Refs synced` line; keep the format change compatible.

## Session origin

Filed interactively from a session that discovered the orphan-seeding gap while handling t2696 (the `SYNC_PAT` visibility fix in `issue-sync.yml`). Parent context: TODO.md serves as the master source of truth for planned and in-progress work; orphan issues silently bypass it. This task makes that invariant enforceable by closing the gap for all future auto-dispatch issues that are born without a TODO line.
