title: Research: SonarCloud rule tuning — S1481/S1066/S100 shell-idiom false-positive inventory
body:
## Session Origin

Interactive follow-up research task filed after t2717 / PR #20387 merged. While closing out that session, inventorying SonarCloud showed that 295 total issues on the dashboard are dominated by shell-idiom false positives, not real code-quality signal.

Parallel systemic fix lives in t2720 / PR #20400 (unrelated to rule tuning — fixes the PR-title extractor gap that kept the t2717 TODO checkbox unchecked).

## What

Inventory and remediate SonarCloud false positives from three shell-idiom rules. Together they account for ~99% of the dashboard count:

| Rule  | Name                    | Count | Typical shell false-positive pattern |
|-------|-------------------------|-------|--------------------------------------|
| S1481 | Unused local variables  | 178   | `local var=$(...)` declared to separate return-code capture from value for `set -e` safety; variable IS used via side effects |
| S1066 | Collapsible `if`        | 97    | Nested `if` kept readable, or outer block is a guard/early-exit pattern that would be obscured by `&&` |
| S100  | Function naming         | 18    | Framework convention uses `_leading_underscore` for private and `snake_case` throughout; SonarCloud defaults expect camelCase |
| **Total** |                     | **293 / 295 (~99%)** | |

Heaviest offenders observed (top 5, from t2717 session investigation):

- `.agents/scripts/mission-dashboard-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/email-compose-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/memory/recall.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/domain-research-helper.sh`

## Why

- Dashboard number (295) looks alarming but is mostly noise. Real debt is drowned.
- Every new shell script added to the framework bumps the count further — this has been a trailing headwind on every merge.
- Review bots (CodeRabbit, Gemini) occasionally cite these rules as "new issues introduced" when they're identical false positives that already exist 500 times elsewhere — wasting reviewer attention and agent token budget.
- Quality scanners should converge on real signal; paying the false-positive tax in perpetuity is the wrong default.

## How (proposed decomposition — to be filed as separate children)

### Phase 1 — Evidence gathering and classification (tier:thinking child)

- File-by-file inventory of S1481 / S1066 / S100 hits: file, line, pattern, three-way classification `{false-positive, legitimate smell, tactical exemption}`.
- Deliverable: ranked table in the Phase 1 brief (`todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md`) with counts, representative examples, and category assignments.
- Exit criterion: each of the 293 findings has a classification.

### Phase 2 — Configuration-level exemptions (tier:standard child)

- Tune `.sonarcloud.properties` (or `sonar-project.properties`) to exclude shell-idiom rules at the framework level, or scope them to non-shell language subsets.
- Alternative considered: suppress specific rules globally with a documented rationale file.
- Measure dashboard delta after the change and attach before/after screenshots to the phase's PR.

### Phase 3 — Per-site `# NOSONAR` pragmas for residual hits (tier:standard child)

- For remaining genuine-intent hits that can't be excluded at config level, add `# NOSONAR[<rule>]: <reason>` inline annotations.
- Create and maintain an exemption inventory at `docs/sonar-exemptions.md` so future reviewers can see the policy.

## Children

- #20453 — t2732: SonarCloud S1481/S1066/S100 false-positive inventory and classification (Phase 1, tier:thinking)
- #20454 — t2733: SonarCloud S1481/S1066/S100 config-level rule exclusions (Phase 2, tier:standard)
- #20455 — t2734: SonarCloud residual hits — per-site NOSONAR pragmas and exemption inventory (Phase 3, tier:standard)



## Acceptance (for this parent to close)

- [ ] Phase 1 child issue filed, brief written, inventory deliverable reviewed.
- [ ] Phase 2 child issue filed, config-level exemptions applied, dashboard count measurably reduced.
- [ ] Phase 3 child issue filed, residual pragmas in place, exemption inventory doc exists.
- [ ] Final SonarCloud dashboard total documented in closing comment alongside before/after numbers.

## Files to investigate

- `.sonarcloud.properties` (if present) or `sonar-project.properties` (create if absent)
- Top offenders listed above
- `docs/sonar-exemptions.md` (will be created in Phase 3)

## Do NOT dispatch a worker

This is a research parent-task. Implementation happens via the three child tasks filed separately. The `parent-task` label applies an unconditional dispatch block (per t2211). Removing `parent-task` without decomposing first is forbidden — it would allow a single worker to take a 293-finding problem and either give up or produce a scope-leaked PR.

title: t2721: remove auto-dispatch label and make dispatch the default behaviour
body:
## What

Remove the `auto-dispatch` label as a positive opt-in requirement for pulse dispatch. Invert to: pulse dispatches any open issue unless an explicit opt-out signal is present (blockers, decomposition markers, active claim, closed state).

**This is a `#parent` investigation-and-phased-implementation task.** Phases 1-7 below will each be filed as separate child issues as the prior phase lands. The parent stays open until Phase 7 merges.

## Why

The `auto-dispatch` label is a positive opt-in from an earlier era of the framework, when server-side pre-dispatch validators didn't exist. Today the pulse already treats a comprehensive set of labels as dispatch-blockers (`pulse-dispatch-core.sh:821` — `persistent | supervisor | contributor | quality-review | on hold | blocked | parent-task | meta`), plus label-based opt-outs (`no-auto-dispatch`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `hold-for-review`), plus claim state (`status:in-review/claimed/queued/in-progress` + assignee), plus server-side eligibility validators (`tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh`, t2424 pre-dispatch eligibility gate).

With all those opt-outs in place, the `auto-dispatch` label is redundant. Its only remaining function is ceremonial: "this issue has been reviewed and is worker-ready". But that ceremony now causes friction:

- Agents reading `plans.md:64` ("Add `#auto-dispatch` only when ALL inclusion criteria pass") vs `save-todo.md:31` ("Default to `#auto-dispatch`") get inconsistent signals.
- Issues filed without the tag sit dormant even when dispatchable, requiring manual backfill or re-filing.
- The doc gate duplicates server-side validators that already refuse dispatch on low-quality issues.
- Ceremony burden falls on the issue creator at a point where they have least context; the real quality gate happens at dispatch time when the pulse has more information.

Removing the label aligns the framework with GitHub's native issue semantics (open = work to be done) and eliminates a whole class of "did I remember the tag?" friction.

## Measured migration scope

Verified during t2721 investigation (session 2026-04-21):

- 92 total open issues across 14 pulse-enabled repos
- 4 issues would newly become dispatchable under the default-flip (not the initially-estimated "hundreds"):
  - `marcusquinn/aidevops#20391` — quality-debt finding, probably SHOULD dispatch (label missing is likely scanner bug)
  - `marcusquinn/aidevops#20341` — already has `status:in-review` → blocked by active-claim check anyway
  - `<webapp>/<webapp>#2598` — single unlabeled user TODO
  - `<webapp>/<webapp>#2531` — has `needs-brief` → fails existing pre-dispatch eligibility gate
- Of the 85 open issues lacking `auto-dispatch`, 81 are already blocked by other signals (`persistent`, `parent-task`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `contributor-insight`, `routine-tracking`, closed state, etc.)

Migration cost is effectively zero. This removes the primary risk justification for a phased vs one-shot approach — but phasing is still worthwhile for review isolation.

## Phases

Each phase is an independently reviewable PR. Children will be filed one at a time as the prior phase lands — not upfront — to keep the worker queue uncluttered and let each phase inform the next.

**Phase 1 — Inventory** (`tier:thinking`, ~1h)
Exhaustive file-level enumeration of every code path that reads, writes, or asserts on `auto-dispatch`. Deliverable: `todo/tasks/t2721-inventory.md` checked into the parent branch listing every script, every test, every doc, with call-site line numbers and semantic classification (writer, reader, assertion, doc). No behaviour changes. Signs off that Phase 2+ scope is complete.

**Phase 2 — Formalise opt-out vocabulary** (`tier:standard`, ~30min)
Add `needs-credentials` as a first-class GitHub label (currently described in docs but not enforced by a label). Document the canonical blocker set in a new `reference/dispatch-blockers.md` that becomes the single source of truth cross-referenced from `AGENTS.md`, `plans.md`, `new-task.md`, `save-todo.md`.

**Phase 3 — One-shot backfill** (`tier:standard`, ~30min)
Sweep the 4 at-risk issues from the "Measured migration scope" section. Hand-review each, apply appropriate opt-out labels OR add the positive `auto-dispatch` label to keep the pulse behaviour unchanged until Phase 4 ships. #20391 specifically: triage whether it should dispatch (file as `auto-dispatch`) or is gated for a reason.

**Phase 4 — Pulse behaviour flip** (`tier:standard`, ~1h)
Core change: `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` treats absence of blockers as dispatchable. Remove the `auto-dispatch` positive check. Behind feature flag `AIDEVOPS_AUTODISPATCH_DEFAULT=1` (default=0 until verified). First pulse cycle after deployment: verify candidate sets match the pre-flip list via audit logs. Second cycle: flip default to 1.

**Phase 5 — Remove label-adding from scanners and wrappers** (`tier:standard`, ~1h)
Remove `auto-dispatch` label-adding from: `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`, review-scanner issue generation, quality-debt issue generation, code-simplifier, `pulse-nmr-approval.sh` auto-approve path, `claim-task-id.sh`, `gh_create_issue` wrapper, `issue-sync-helper.sh` tag-to-label mapper. Retain label acceptance (no errors on its presence — backward compat for contributors reading old docs).

**Phase 6 — Self-assignment logic inversion** (`tier:standard`, ~1h)
t2157/t2218/t2406 currently skip self-assignment when `auto-dispatch` label is present. Invert: skip self-assignment UNLESS `assignee:` field present in TODO entry OR `--self-assign` flag. Update regression tests (`test-auto-dispatch-no-assign.sh`, `test-gh-create-issue-auto-dispatch-skip.sh`, `test-interactive-session-post-merge.sh`).

**Phase 7 — Doc + test sweep** (`tier:standard`, ~1h)
Remove "when to add `#auto-dispatch`" sections from `plans.md`, `new-task.md`, `save-todo.md`, `brief.md`, `log-issue-aidevops.md`, `autoresearch.md`, `autoagent.md`, `planning-detail.md`, `onboarding.md`, `orchestration-analysis.md`. Update all templates and examples. Invert test assertions that check for label presence. Close this parent when merged.

## Risks and mitigations

1. **Pulse dispatch storm after Phase 4 flip.** Mitigation: feature flag defaults to old behaviour for first cycle; audit log compares new vs old candidate sets before flipping default.
2. **Scanner regression — low-quality issues suddenly dispatching.** Mitigation: server-side validators (tier-simple-body-shape, pre-dispatch eligibility gate) already handle this. Phase 1 inventory will confirm coverage.
3. **Backward compat — old docs / contributor-filed issues.** Mitigation: Phase 5 retains label acceptance as a no-op. Phase 7 doc sweep stops teaching the label but doesn't error on it.
4. **Hidden coupling surfaces in Phase 1 that invalidates scope.** Mitigation: Phase 1 is an inventory PR with no behaviour change — if it finds unexpected coupling, the parent body gets updated and phases re-planned.
5. **Test churn > estimated time.** Mitigation: Phase 7 may be larger than 1h; update estimate when Phase 1 output lands.

## Acceptance (parent closes when)

1. All 7 phase PRs merged.
2. Pulse default behaviour is "dispatch open issues unless blocker present" (confirmed via audit log over 24h).
3. Zero new `auto-dispatch` labels added by framework code (scanners, wrappers, helpers).
4. Test suite passes with inverted assertions.
5. Docs have zero "when to add #auto-dispatch" guidance.
6. Label retained as recognised-historical-no-op for backward compat.

## Out of scope

- Removing other dispatch-gating labels (`parent-task`, `needs-maintainer-review`, `hold-for-review`, etc.) — these have distinct semantic purposes that `auto-dispatch` lacks.
- Changing the `origin:interactive` vs `origin:worker` model — orthogonal.
- Changing server-side pre-dispatch validators — they're the foundation this change relies on and should stay stable.

## Session Origin

Surfaced during t2705 shipping (2026-04-21). User observed friction from inconsistent `auto-dispatch` doc guidance and asked "do we even need an auto-dispatch label and logic?" Initial risk estimate was inflated ("hundreds of legacy issues"); actual measurement showed 4. Revised recommendation is radical removal rather than doc harmonisation.

## Children

Filed incrementally as each phase completes. Current state:

- Phase 1 — Inventory: filed as #20410 (merged via PR #20415, 2026-04-22)
- Phase 2 — Formalise opt-out vocabulary: filed as #20558 (available for pickup)
- Phases 3-7 — _filed after Phase 2 lands_

title: t2722: Phase 1 inventory of auto-dispatch references
body:
## Task

Phase 1 of the 7-phase parent task [#20402](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20402). Produce an exhaustive inventory of every code path, test, doc, workflow, and config that references the `auto-dispatch` label, classified by semantic role and mapped to the phase that will modify it.

**Behaviour change in this PR:** none — doc-only.

## Why

Phase 1 is the scoping gate for t2721. Without a complete inventory, Phase 2-7 (opt-out vocabulary formalisation, backfill, pulse behaviour flip, scanner strip, self-assignment inversion, doc sweep) cannot be confidently scoped. Any hidden reader, writer, or assertion that surfaces during Phase 4-6 would either break pulse dispatch, leave dormant-but-dispatchable issues, or require emergency revert.

The inventory PR lands in the repo as a reference document, not an ephemeral chat artifact. Subsequent phase PRs cite its tables and phase-assignment column.

## How

1. File enumeration: `rg -l "auto-dispatch|auto_dispatch" .agents/ .github/` plus top-level docs.
2. Per-file line-level classification into 6 roles: WRITER, READER, OPT-OUT (`no-auto-dispatch`), DOC, TEST, WORKFLOW.
3. Distinguish positive refs (`auto-dispatch`) from negative refs (`no-auto-dispatch`) per file.
4. Map doc inconsistency: 4 contradictory files, 17 teaching-but-consistent files, line-level evidence.
5. Map test assertion direction: positive (asserts label present) vs negative (asserts absent) vs incidental.
6. Assign each reference to a phase (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or `keep`).

title: t2724: route session-start framework status to TUI toast instead of message context
body:
## What

Render the session-start framework status as an OpenCode TUI toast via `client.tui.showToast()` instead of (or in addition to) injecting it as the first message in context. Phase 1 is additive — the toast appears alongside the existing message-context greeting so we can A/B the visual result. Phase 2 trims the human-only parts from the context version.

## Why

The current session greeting — version string, security advisories, pulse status, contribution count — is rendered by the model as the first message in every interactive session. This consumes 100-200 tokens of context per session (more when advisories are active), even though most of the content is status information the human needs but the model rarely acts on.

OpenCode 1.14 exposes `client.tui.showToast()` (SDK method `TuiShowToastData`, URL `/tui/show-toast`) with `variant: info|success|warning|error` and optional `duration`. Routing the banner through toasts frees that context entirely while keeping the human-visible information at session start.

## How

Phase 1 — additive plugin hook:

- NEW: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs` — module exporting `createGreetingHook({ scriptsDir, client })`. Handler fires on `event.type === "session.created"`, guarded by a `fired` flag so it runs once per plugin init. Runs `${scriptsDir}/aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive`, parses the output into up to 3 toasts (info for version/env, warning for pulse/contribution, error for security advisories), emits via `await client.tui.showToast({ body: { title, message, variant, duration } })`.
- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs` — import `createGreetingHook`, compose the greeting handler into the existing `event:` hook alongside the observability handler so both run on every event.
- Model pattern to follow: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/observability.mjs` (same event-subscription style; see `handleEvent` signature).
- Defaults: 3 toasts max, 10s duration (30s for errors), fire-once per plugin init.

Phase 2 — trim redundant human-only lines from model-rendered greeting (separate commit in same PR once Phase 1 is visually confirmed):

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh:47-…` — the "On interactive conversation start" instruction block. Reduce to: "If the user asks about version/advisories/status, Read `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt`." Remove the "greet with: Hi!..." scripted response entirely (toast handles it).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/index.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh`
- `todo/tasks/*-brief.md`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance

- Launching a fresh OpenCode session displays an info toast within 2s of first prompt render showing the aidevops version and runtime.
- When security advisories are present, a separate error-variant toast appears with the advisory summary.
- When the pulse is stalled or contributions need reply, a warning-variant toast appears.
- Message-context consumption from the greeting drops by ≥50 tokens (measured via `opencode stats` before/after a clean session start with no advisories).
- No regression: the existing observability `event:` handler still receives all events (verified via `~/.aidevops/logs/observability.sqlite` new rows on tool calls).
- Plugin init completes without errors in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` or OpenCode's own log.

## Session Origin

Interactive session, OpenCode v1.14.20, aidevops v3.8.91. Request from maintainer — "shall we add to toast first, see how that looks, then remove bit by bit that's for humans only?"

title: t2725: fix toast greeting update-check timeout (5s to 15s)
body:
## Task

Bump `execSync` timeout in the OpenCode plugin's toast greeting handler from 5000ms to 15000ms so the update-check script reliably completes before emission.

## Why

t2724 (PR #20420) shipped the Phase 1 toast greeting with a 5s execSync timeout on `aidevops-update-check.sh`. Runtime diagnosis inside the deployed plugin (file-based trace) showed the timeout consistently fires:

```text
runUpdateCheck-env {"OPENCODE":"1","OPENCODE_PROCESS_ROLE":"main",...}
runUpdateCheck-threw spawnSync /bin/sh ETIMEDOUT
runUpdateCheck-output length=0 preview=""
runGreeting-skip empty-output
```

**Root cause.** `aidevops-update-check.sh` forks background children (provenance notify — line 759; deploy drift check — line 895) that inherit stdout. Node's `execSync` waits for ALL inherited FDs to close, not just the main script exit. Observed wallclock on a standard macOS system: **~5.8s** — consistently over the 5s limit.

Standalone Bash tests complete the same script in 1-2s because the test process doesn't block on inherited FDs the same way. The plugin's execSync pipe inheritance is the critical difference.

Consequence: Phase 1 toasts **never emit in real sessions**. `runGreeting` returns early on empty output, the model-context greeting (AGENTS.md template fallback) is the only thing the user sees, and the Phase 2 token savings never actually apply.

## How

Single-file, single-value change:

- EDIT: `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs:61` — change `timeout: 5000` to `timeout: 15000`.
- Also extend the doc comment above `runUpdateCheck` to explain the FD-inheritance reason so future readers don't naively revert this as "too slow".

### Files Scope

- .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs

## Acceptance

- Fresh OpenCode TUI launch emits toasts for the session-start banner (error/warning/info/success bundles from update-check output).
- Plugin trace (when enabled) shows `handler-triggered -> runGreeting-start -> runUpdateCheck-output length>0 -> buildToasts -> emitToast-ok xN -> runGreeting-end`.
- Timeout still bounded — 15s gives headroom for slower hardware without hanging the handler indefinitely.

## Context

- Depends on: #20412 (t2724, merged in #20420).
- Related diagnostic: observed via file-based trace added to the deployed plugin during the t2724 session; trace left in the deployed copy for user verification, will be cleaned up once fix merges.

title: t2727: consolidate greeting toasts into single emit (opencode TUI shows only one)
body:
## Task

The opencode-aidevops plugin greeting emits four separate TUI toasts (error, warning, info, success) via `client.tui.showToast()`. OpenCode's TUI renders only one toast at a time — each new emit replaces the previous one before the user can read it. End-user reports seeing only the final `success` toast; errors, warnings, and info vanish.

Consolidate into a single toast with all categories combined, using the highest-severity variant and longest duration.

## Why

Matches the pre-t2724 prose greeting UX (all status visible at once) and works within opencode's single-slot toast model. Without this, higher-priority information (SECURITY ADVISORY, pulse stalled, external contributions) is invisible to the user — defeating the purpose of the toast migration.

Verified empirically by the end user after PR #20424 deployed: restarting opencode and sending "hi" showed exactly one toast (green "Security: all protections active"), not four.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs:145-185` — rewrite `buildToasts()` to return a single toast. Reuse the existing `classifyLines()` output for severity detection.

### Reference pattern

Current `buildToasts()` already has the right classification logic — just collapse the four `toasts.push()` calls into one assembly with:

- `variant`: first non-empty category in order `error → warning → info → success`
- `duration`: matching that variant (30s / 15s / 8s / 5s)
- `message`: lines concatenated in severity order `[...error, ...warning, ...info, ...success].join("\n")`
- `title`: `"aidevops"` (drop the per-variant "aidevops — attention required" string — severity is communicated via the toast color)

Rename `buildToasts` → `buildToast` (singular) and update the one call site in `runGreeting()` to emit once.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs`

## Acceptance

- Function returns `null` when all buckets are empty, `{ title, message, variant, duration }` otherwise.
- Variant derivation follows error > warning > info > success priority.
- Duration follows the variant's existing mapping (30s/15s/8s/5s).
- `runGreeting()` emits exactly one toast (or zero if `buildToast` returns null).
- End-to-end verification: restart opencode, confirm the consolidated toast shows all lines (version, env, security active, advisory, pulse stalled, external contribution) with the error variant color.
- Diagnostic trace (if `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG=1`) logs `emitToast-*` once, not four times.

## Context

- Preceding PRs: #20420 (t2724, Phase 1+2), #20424 (t2725, timeout fix).
- SDK type: `TuiShowToastData` at `~/.config/opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/sdk/dist/gen/types.gen.d.ts:3261` — no `id` field, confirming per-call replacement behaviour.
- The `classifyLines()` function already does the work; only `buildToasts()` needs to change.
- No test harness exists for the plugin; verification is manual via opencode restart.

title: t2728: toast UX polish — strip runtime-identity, add aidevops contributions subcommand, backtick commands
body:
## Task

Three UX polish items on the opencode greeting toast (follow-up to PR #20432 / t2727):

1. **Strip runtime-identity line from the toast.** The line `You are running in OpenCode. Global config: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (emitted by `_get_runtime_hint` in `aidevops-update-check.sh:256-269`) is useful as session prose for the model but clutters the toast. It should flow through the cached `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt` (so non-Bash agents still see it) but NOT into the toast message.

2. **Promote `contribution-watch-helper.sh status` to an `aidevops` subcommand.** The current toast says "run `contribution-watch-helper.sh status` to see them". Long helper paths are awkward in user-facing output. Add `aidevops contributions` (alias `aidevops contrib`) that defaults to `status` when called with no args, matching the pattern used for `aidevops pulse`, `aidevops doctor`, etc.

3. **Wrap commands in backticks in toast strings.** The advisory emit (`aidevops-update-check.sh:349`) and contribution-watch emit (`aidevops-update-check.sh:391`) both include bare command strings mid-sentence. Backticks make it obvious what's copy-pastable.

## Why

End-user verification of t2727's consolidated toast (PR #20432) surfaced these three polish items. Matches the "one glance, act on it" design goal for the greeting — identity chatter hides the actionable advisories; long helper paths discourage the user from running them; untagged commands blur what's shell vs. narrative.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:349` — wrap `aidevops security` and `aidevops security dismiss <id>` in backticks:

  ```bash
  entry=$(printf '%s Run in your terminal: `aidevops security` | Dismiss: `aidevops security dismiss %s`' "$first_line" "$adv_id")
  ```

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:391` — rename helper path to the new `aidevops` subcommand and backtick it:

  ```bash
  contribution_watch="${cw_count} external contribution(s) need your reply (run \`aidevops contributions\` to see them)."
  ```

- `EDIT: aidevops.sh:1728-1766` case dispatcher — add a `contributions | contrib` arm that defaults to `status` when bare:

  ```bash
  contributions | contrib)
      [[ $# -eq 0 ]] && set -- status
      _dispatch_helper "contribution-watch-helper.sh" "contribution-watch-helper.sh" "$@"
      ;;
  ```

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs:108-143` `classifyLines()` — skip runtime-identity lines from classification so they never enter any toast bucket:

  ```javascript
  // Runtime identity flows through the cached greeting file for model prose
  // but shouldn't clutter the toast — the user already knows which app they
  // launched. Filter at the classifier so cacheGreeting() still captures it.
  if (line.startsWith("You are running in ")) continue;
  ```

  Also update the top-of-file doc comment (lines 22-35) to mention this filter.

### Reference pattern

- CLI subcommand dispatch: `_dispatch_helper "pulse-session-helper.sh" ...` at `aidevops.sh:1742` is the canonical pattern.
- Default-to-subcommand pattern: `cmd_repos` at `aidevops.sh:1258` uses `local action="${1:-list}"` — we use the inline `[[ $# -eq 0 ]] && set -- status` form for parity with how `_dispatch_helper` already forwards `"$@"`.

### Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh aidevops.sh` passes.
- `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs` passes.
- `bash aidevops.sh contributions` = `bash aidevops.sh contributions status` (both show watched items).
- Restart opencode, send "hi", confirm the toast:
  - No longer contains "You are running in OpenCode. Global config: ..."
  - References `` `aidevops contributions` `` (backticked) instead of `contribution-watch-helper.sh status`
  - Advisory line has `` `aidevops security` `` and `` `aidevops security dismiss litellm-2026-03` `` in backticks

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs`
- `aidevops.sh`

## Acceptance

- Toast message no longer contains any `You are running in ...` line.
- `aidevops contributions` (bare) runs `contribution-watch-helper.sh status`.
- `aidevops contrib` alias works the same as `contributions`.
- Commands in toast body are surrounded by backticks (`` `aidevops security` ``, `` `aidevops security dismiss ...` ``, `` `aidevops contributions` ``).
- Cached greeting file (`~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt`) still contains the runtime-identity line so non-Bash agents get it.
- All three linters (shellcheck, node --check) pass on the modified files.

## Context

- Preceding merged PRs in this arc: #20420 (t2724, Phase 1+2), #20424 (t2725, timeout), #20432 (t2727, consolidation).
- `aidevops.sh` was recently split into sub-libraries (PR #20296, GH#20287) to get under the 2000-line complexity gate; the top-level dispatcher still lives in `aidevops.sh` at line 1728.
- `_dispatch_helper` at `aidevops.sh:1579` resolves helper location preferring `$AGENTS_DIR/scripts/` (deployed) over `$INSTALL_DIR/.agents/scripts/` (source).
- Out of scope for this PR: startup-latency reduction (user observed longer delay from enter-key to session start — the `execSync` update-check call blocks the session.created handler). Will be filed as a separate follow-up task once this ships.

title: t2729: fire greeting update-check async so session.created handler returns immediately
body:
## Task

Eliminate the 5-8s delay between first-message send and session start in opencode sessions introduced by the t2724 greeting-toast path.

## Why

End-user observation after t2727/t2728 shipped: "there's a longer delay from hitting enter on the first message to showing the session starting since implementing what's changed in this session". The delay is the `execSync` call in `greeting.mjs::runUpdateCheck()` blocking the plugin's `session.created` / `session.updated` handler.

Root cause is already documented in `greeting.mjs` lines 58-63 and reinforced by t2725 (timeout raised from 5s to 15s to accommodate the same FD-inheritance effect): `aidevops-update-check.sh` returns its own stdout in 1-2s but forks two background children (`aidevops-update-check.sh:759` provenance notify, `aidevops-update-check.sh:895` deploy drift check) that inherit stdout. Node's `execSync` waits for all inherited FDs to close, so observed wallclock is 5-8s on typical macOS hardware.

The fix is functionally orthogonal to the existing timeout: rather than wait 15s before giving up, wait zero seconds and let the toast emit when the subprocess eventually finishes.

## How

### Files to modify

**Option A (Node-side, recommended):**

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs:68-82` — replace the synchronous `execSync` call with a fire-and-forget `spawn` / `exec` (promise-wrapped) and change `runGreeting()` so the handler returns before the subprocess finishes. Emit the toast inside the promise's `then` / completion callback. The `fired = true` gate already at line 269 handles the one-shot semantics.

  Example shape:

  ```javascript
  import { exec } from "child_process";
  import { promisify } from "util";
  const execAsync = promisify(exec);

  // In runGreeting:
  execAsync(`bash ${JSON.stringify(script)} --interactive`, { timeout: 15000 })
    .then(({ stdout }) => {
      if (!stdout) return;
      cacheGreeting(stdout.trim());
      const buckets = classifyLines(stdout.trim());
      const toast = buildToast(buckets);
      if (toast) emitToast(client, toast);  // non-blocking
    })
    .catch((err) => {
      if (process.env.AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG) {
        console.error(`[aidevops] greeting: update-check failed: ${err.message}`);
      }
    });
  // runGreeting returns here (synchronously), handler promise resolves.
  ```

**Option B (shell-side, complementary):**

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:759` (provenance notify fork) and `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:895` (deploy drift check fork) — redirect stdout/stderr to `/dev/null` in the background invocations so they don't hold the parent's stdout open, even if a caller uses synchronous exec. Low-risk defence-in-depth even if Option A lands.

Option A alone solves the user-facing problem. Option B reduces blast radius for other synchronous consumers of `aidevops-update-check.sh` (there may be none, but it's cheap insurance).

### Reference pattern

title: t2730: restore runtime-identity line in generated opencode AGENTS.md
body:
## Task

Restore the **runtime-identity line** — `You are running in OpenCode. Global config: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` — to the generated `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` so the model sees it in first-response context. It was removed from the toast in t2728 (PR #20434) but never restored to the AGENTS.md template, leaving it visible only in the cached session greeting (which the model does not always read).

## Why

The runtime-identity line is operationally important prose — it tells the model which host app it's running in (OpenCode vs Claude Code vs headless) so runtime-aware operations (LSP restart commands, session databases, plugin paths) are scoped correctly.

t2724 Phase 2 trimmed this line from the heredoc template on the assumption the toast would carry it. t2728 then removed it from the toast (correctly — it's static info, not a session-state update). Result: the line now lives only in `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt`, which the model reads only when explicitly fetched. The user confirmed directly ("i'm just not seeing this message, which we need back in the session context first response") that the line is missing from their current session.

This is a regression in observability — the model no longer has a reliable way to know its host runtime without making additional tool calls.

## What

Add the runtime-identity line as permanent prose to the heredoc template that writes `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`.

**Deliverable:** A one-line addition (plus a blank line for markdown clarity) to the heredoc in `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh:42-58`.

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh:42-58` — add runtime-identity prose inside the `cat >"$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/AGENTS.md" <<'EOF' ... EOF` block, immediately after the first line (`Add ~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md to context...`) and before the `## aidevops Framework Status` heading.

### Reference pattern

### Edit detail

Inside the heredoc at the current position between line 43 and line 45, insert:

```markdown

**Runtime**: You are running in OpenCode. Global config: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.
```

The line belongs BEFORE `## aidevops Framework Status` so it's the first operational fact the model encounters after the `Add ~/.aidevops/agents/AGENTS.md to context...` bootstrap directive.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh`

## Acceptance

1. `.agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh` heredoc contains the literal string `You are running in OpenCode. Global config:`
2. Running `bash .agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh` (or its deployed copy) rewrites `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` to include the runtime-identity line as a top-level paragraph.
3. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/generate-opencode-agents.sh` passes with zero violations.

```bash

```

User feedback in active interactive session: "i'm just not seeing this message, which we need back in the session context first response: 'You are running in OpenCode. Global config: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json'". Part of the t2724 → t2728 → t2730 toast-vs-prose refactor arc.

- **Prior task arc**: t2724 (PR #20420 — initial toast wiring + template trim), t2725 (PR #20424 — execSync timeout), t2727 (PR #20432 — four-toast consolidation), t2728 (PR #20434 — toast UX polish that removed runtime-identity from the toast). All merged.

dispatch unconditionally in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` (`PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED`),
but the nudge comment is advisory-only — no automation actually
decomposes the parent.

This issue closes that loop. Implementing it clears the block on
#20368 by replacing it with tracked children.

## How

1. **Read the parent issue** at https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20368
   and identify logical phases, components, or sub-tasks. Look for
   explicit `## Phase` sections, bullet lists of work items, or

title: t2731: unfilter runtime-identity line from opencode toast (revert t2728 filter)
body:
## Task

Revert the **t2728 toast filter** that strips the runtime-identity line (`You are running in <app>. Global config: ...`) from the opencode toast bucket. User explicitly wants this line visible in the toast at session start.

## Why

- **t2728** (PR #20434) filtered the runtime-identity line from the toast on the premise "user already knows which app they launched".
- **t2730** (PR #20438) restored it as static prose in `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` — making it model-visible but NOT user-visible. The model reads AGENTS.md silently; it doesn't output it verbatim.
- User feedback after t2730 restart: "tried that, still not seeing it" — with screenshot confirming the model's first response is generic ("Hi! What would you like to work on?") and the toast contains only the short-form environment line (`aidevops v3.8.93 running in OpenCode v1.14.20 | aidevops/main`), not the long-form runtime-identity with config path.
- **Only the toast is a user-visible surface** at session start. AGENTS.md is model context. The cache file is fallback-only. Reverting the filter restores the line to the visible channel.

t2728's filtering of this specific line was a design error for users who value seeing the config path at session start. The rationale "clutters the toast" does not apply to a one-line addition — the toast already carries 5-6 lines in typical sessions.

## What

Remove the 8-line filter block in `greeting.mjs` that skips lines starting with `"You are running in "`. Update the top-of-file rationale comment to reflect the revert.

The runtime-identity line will re-enter the `info` bucket (as `classifyLines` already routes it there), adding one line to the consolidated toast body.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs:129-136` — delete the filter block (the `if (line.startsWith("You are running in "))` guard and its preceding 5-line comment).
- **EDIT:** `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs:37-40` — update the `Toast-only filters (t2728)` comment block to reflect the t2731 revert. Preserve the historical record but note the reversion rationale.

### Reference pattern

Two edits in one file. No new imports, no structural changes.

### Edit detail — filter block (lines 129-136)

```diff
     if (line.startsWith("UPDATE_AVAILABLE|") || line === "AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED") {
       continue;
     }

-    // Skip the runtime-identity line (t2728). "You are running in <app>.
-    // Global config: ..." is useful as session prose for the model but
-    // clutters the toast — the user already knows which app they launched.
-    // cacheGreeting(output) writes the raw output, so non-Bash agents still
-    // see the line via ~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt.
-    if (line.startsWith("You are running in ")) {
-      continue;
-    }
-
     // Order matters: errors first (most specific), then warnings, then
     // success, then info (catch-all for version/env lines).
```

### Edit detail — top-of-file rationale (lines 37-40)

Replace:

```
// Toast-only filters (t2728): lines matching `You are running in <app>.`
// are filtered in classifyLines() so they don't enter any toast bucket.
// The runtime-identity line is useful as session prose for the model but
// would clutter the toast — the cache file still captures it verbatim.
```

With:

```
// Toast filters: UPDATE_AVAILABLE|<...> and AUTO_UPDATE_ENABLED are the
// only lines suppressed — those are machine-readable sentinels. The
// runtime-identity line (`You are running in <app>. Global config: ...`)
// WAS suppressed from the toast by t2728 but restored by t2731 after
// user feedback that seeing the config path at session start is valuable.
// See also t2730 for the parallel AGENTS.md prose (model-only surface).
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs`

## Acceptance

1. `greeting.mjs` no longer contains `line.startsWith("You are running in ")`.
2. The top-of-file comment block accurately reflects the t2728 → t2731 history.
3. After redeploy and OpenCode restart, the toast body contains the line `You are running in OpenCode. Global config: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (as one of the info-bucket lines).
4. No other toast behaviour changes (severity ordering, duration, other filters unaffected).
5. `biome check` / lint passes for the edited file (no new violations).

## Verification

```bash
# From worktree after edit:
grep -n "You are running in" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs
# Should show ONLY the comment reference at ~line 37, NOT a filter guard.

# Visual: restart OpenCode and confirm the toast body has the line.
```

## Session Origin

User feedback in active interactive session after t2730 restart: screenshot showed first-response context still missing the expected line. User corrected the approach: "are you sure about editing ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md ? when aidevops setup/update should be copying from .agents/AGENTS.md to here?" — triggering a re-examination of the correct surface. Conclusion: toast is the user-visible surface; filter must be reverted.

## Context

- t2728 (PR #20434) — originally introduced the filter. Merged 2026-04-22T03:21:23Z.
- t2730 (PR #20438) — added AGENTS.md prose as static model-context. Merged 2026-04-22T03:51:57Z. Not being reverted — the AGENTS.md line is still useful for silent model context (answering "what runtime am I in?" without needing to read cache).
- Two surfaces serve two audiences: toast = user at session start; AGENTS.md = model in context.

title: t2732: SonarCloud S1481/S1066/S100 false-positive inventory and classification
body:
## Session Origin

Child of parent-task #20401 (SonarCloud rule tuning — S1481/S1066/S100 shell-idiom false-positive inventory). Filed by decomposition issue #20450.

## What

Inventory and classify all SonarCloud S1481, S1066, and S100 findings across the `.agents/scripts/` shell codebase. Produce a ranked table with file, line, rule, pattern type, and three-way classification: `{false-positive, legitimate-smell, tactical-exemption}`.

## Why

Parent #20401 documents ~293 SonarCloud findings dominated by shell-idiom false positives (S1481: 178, S1066: 97, S100: 18). Before applying config-level exclusions (Phase 2 / t2733), we need evidence that these are genuinely false positives — not legitimate code smells masked by convention. This inventory IS the evidence.

## How

### Approach

Use `rg` and pattern matching to find instances of each rule's triggering pattern in shell scripts:

1. **S1481 (Unused local variables)** — grep for `local var=$(...)` patterns where `var` is never referenced again in the function. Focus on the `set -e` safety pattern: `local rc=0; command || rc=$?` where the variable IS used but SonarCloud misses the indirect usage.
   - Pattern: `rg -n 'local \w+=' .agents/scripts/ --type sh | head -50` to get representative samples.
   - For each sample: check if the variable is used later in the same function scope.

2. **S1066 (Collapsible if)** — grep for nested `if` blocks inside `if` blocks.
   - Pattern: look for `if ...; then\n.*if` patterns.
   - Classify: is the outer `if` a guard/early-exit, or genuinely collapsible?

3. **S100 (Function naming)** — grep for function names not matching camelCase.
   - Pattern: `rg -n '^[a-z_]+\(\)' .agents/scripts/ --type sh` — the framework uses `snake_case` and `_leading_underscore` by convention.
   - Classify: ALL should be false-positives since the naming convention is `snake_case`.

### Deliverable

A ranked table in the PR body and a summary file at `todo/tasks/t2732-brief.md` containing:

```

|------|------|------|---------|----------------|
```

title: t2733: SonarCloud S1481/S1066/S100 config-level rule exclusions
body:
## Session Origin

Child of parent-task #20401 (SonarCloud rule tuning — S1481/S1066/S100 shell-idiom false-positive inventory). Filed by decomposition issue #20450. Depends on Phase 1 (t2732 / #20453) for evidence.

## What

Add config-level exclusions for SonarCloud rules S1481, S1066, and S100 in `sonar-project.properties`, scoped to shell scripts (`**/*.sh`). This eliminates ~293 false-positive findings from the dashboard in one change.

## Why

- S1481 (178 findings): `local var=$(...)` is idiomatic shell for `set -e` safety — SonarCloud doesn't understand the pattern.
- S1066 (97 findings): Nested `if` blocks are kept for readability as guard/early-exit patterns.
- S100 (18 findings): The framework convention is `snake_case` / `_leading_underscore`; SonarCloud defaults expect camelCase.
- These 293 findings are ~99% of the dashboard total, drowning real signal.
- Line 98-99 of `sonar-project.properties` currently says these are NOT excluded because "they catch real issues" — Phase 1's inventory (t2732) provides the evidence to override that decision.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `sonar-project.properties:44,98-99` — add 6 new exclusion entries (3 rules × 2 prefixes `shelldre:` / `shell:`) and update the comment at lines 98-99 to reference the inventory evidence.

### Reference pattern

Follow the existing exclusion pattern at `sonar-project.properties:46-70` — each rule gets a pair of entries (`shelldre:` and `shell:` prefix) with a comment block explaining the rationale. Model on the S7679 entry at lines 76-79.

### Implementation

Add after line 99 (replacing the "NOT excluded" comment):

```properties
# S1481: Unused local variables - shell `set -e` safety pattern
# `local var=$(cmd)` captures return code separately from value; variable IS used
# via side effects or in subsequent conditional checks. SonarCloud's data-flow
# analysis doesn't track shell variable usage across subshell boundaries.
# Evidence: t2732 inventory classified 178/178 as false-positive.
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e18.ruleKey=shelldre:S1481
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e18.resourceKey=**/*.sh

sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e19.ruleKey=shell:S1481
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e19.resourceKey=**/*.sh

# S1066: Collapsible if statements - intentional guard/early-exit pattern
# Nested ifs are kept for readability: outer block is a precondition guard,
# inner block is the actual logic. Collapsing with && obscures the control flow.
# Evidence: t2732 inventory classified 97/97 as false-positive or tactical-exemption.
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e20.ruleKey=shelldre:S1066
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e20.resourceKey=**/*.sh

sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e21.ruleKey=shell:S1066
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e21.resourceKey=**/*.sh

# S100: Function naming convention - framework uses snake_case by design
# All shell functions follow snake_case and _leading_underscore convention.
# camelCase would be inconsistent with 460+ existing scripts.
# Evidence: t2732 inventory classified 18/18 as false-positive.
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e22.ruleKey=shelldre:S100
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e22.resourceKey=**/*.sh

sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e23.ruleKey=shell:S100
sonar.issue.ignore.multicriteria.e23.resourceKey=**/*.sh
```


title: t2734: SonarCloud residual hits — per-site NOSONAR pragmas and exemption inventory
body:
## Session Origin

Child of parent-task #20401 (SonarCloud rule tuning — S1481/S1066/S100 shell-idiom false-positive inventory). Filed by decomposition issue #20450. Depends on Phase 2 (t2733 / #20454) — residual hits are those that survive config-level exclusions.

## What

For any SonarCloud findings that survive the Phase 2 config-level exclusions (t2733 / #20454), add per-site `# NOSONAR` inline annotations with rule ID and rationale. Create and maintain an exemption inventory document at `docs/sonar-exemptions.md`.

## Why

Config-level exclusions (Phase 2) blanket-suppress S1481/S1066/S100 for all shell scripts. If the Phase 1 inventory (t2732 / #20453) identifies any findings that are **legitimate smells** (not false-positives), those should NOT be config-excluded — they need per-site `# NOSONAR[<rule>]: <reason>` annotations instead, so the suppression is visible at the code site and the rationale is preserved for future maintainers.

Additionally, any new rules that surface after Phase 2's config change lands (SonarCloud may reanalyse with different rule sets) need a documented process for handling.

## How

title: Extend dirty-pr-sweep close window to 14d for origin:interactive referenced PRs
body:
## What

Extend the dirty-pr-sweep auto-close idle window from 7d to 14d for `origin:interactive` PRs that have a recognised issue reference (`For #NNN`, `Ref #NNN`, or closing keywords).

## Why

After t2708, `origin:interactive` PRs with issue references flow through the normal age/idle close heuristic in `_dirty_pr_classify`. This means a maintainer-authored planning PR linked to a tracked issue that goes DIRTY and sits idle for 7d gets auto-closed with `--delete-branch`.

This is problematic because:
- `origin:interactive` + referenced = maintainer deliberately linked this to tracked work
- 7d is short for planning PRs waiting on prerequisite work
- `--delete-branch` could lose incremental work
- `do-not-close` is available but must be applied proactively

A 14d window (double the default) gives maintainers more time while still cleaning up genuinely abandoned PRs.

Analysis: parent #20368, Question 2 verdict: NEEDS-FIX.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:66-76` — add new constant
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:459-477` — pass extended age to close check

### Implementation

1. Add a new configurable constant after line 76:

```bash
DIRTY_PR_CLOSE_MIN_AGE_INTERACTIVE="${DIRTY_PR_CLOSE_MIN_AGE_INTERACTIVE:-1209600}"  # 14d for origin:interactive + referenced
```

2. In `_dirty_pr_classify`, after the `origin:interactive` + reference check passes (line 468 "Has a reference — fall through"), pass the extended age threshold. Replace the current fall-through with:

```bash
    # Has a reference — use extended close window for interactive PRs.
    local close_decision
    close_decision=$(_dps_consider_close "$age" "$now" "$updated_epoch" "$created_epoch")
    # Override: if age < DIRTY_PR_CLOSE_MIN_AGE_INTERACTIVE, skip close
    if [[ "$age" -le "$DIRTY_PR_CLOSE_MIN_AGE_INTERACTIVE" && -n "$close_decision" ]]; then
        printf '%s|origin-interactive-referenced-not-yet-stale' "$_DIRTY_ACTION_NOTIFY"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$close_decision" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$close_decision"
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s|dirty-not-auto-resolvable' "$_DIRTY_ACTION_NOTIFY"
    return 0
```

Alternatively (simpler): just gate the fall-through with an age check before reaching `_dps_consider_close`:

```bash
    # Has a reference — use extended close window for interactive PRs (t2711 Q2).
    if [[ "$age" -le "$DIRTY_PR_CLOSE_MIN_AGE_INTERACTIVE" ]]; then
        printf '%s|origin-interactive-referenced-within-extended-window' "$_DIRTY_ACTION_NOTIFY"
        return 0
    fi
    # Beyond extended window — fall through to normal age-based close.
```

### Reference pattern

Model on the `origin:interactive` orphan check at lines 463-469.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dirty-pr-sweep.sh
```

## Acceptance

1. An `origin:interactive` PR with a valid issue reference that is DIRTY and 8d old classifies as `notify`, not `close`
2. The same PR at 15d old classifies as `close|stale-and-idle`
3. Non-interactive PRs are unaffected (still use 7d threshold)
4. `shellcheck` passes
5. New env var `DIRTY_PR_CLOSE_MIN_AGE_INTERACTIVE` is documented in the header comment

title: t2710 child: widen _dps_consider_rebase conflict allowlist to match planning allowlist
body:
## What

Widen the conflict allowlist in `_dps_consider_rebase` (`pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:355`) to match the headless planning allowlist from `pre-edit-check.sh`.

Currently, only exact `TODO.md` passes the rebase eligibility check. Planning files `todo/**` and `README.md` are incorrectly rejected, preventing auto-rebase for PRs with planning-only conflicts in those files.

## Why

The headless main-branch planning exception (t1990) allows direct-to-main writes for `TODO.md`, `todo/*`, and `README.md`. But `_dps_consider_rebase` only recognises `TODO.md` as rebase-safe. This mismatch means planning PRs conflicting on `todo/tasks/tXXX-brief.md` or `README.md` fall through to the notify/close path instead of being auto-rebased.

Filed as a child of the t2710 investigation (#20361). Analysis: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20361#issuecomment-4294270853

Ref #20361

## How

### Files to modify

### Reference pattern

The planning allowlist pattern is defined in `pre-edit-check.sh` function `is_main_allowlisted_path`. Model the filter on that function's path list.

### Implementation

Replace line 355:

title: t2710 child: extend rebase age window for planning-only conflicts in dirty-pr-sweep
body:
## What

Add a separate, longer age window for planning-only conflicts in `_dps_consider_rebase` (`pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:347`). Currently the fixed 48h `DIRTY_PR_REBASE_MAX_AGE` applies regardless of conflict scope, causing planning-only TODO.md PRs to age out of rebase eligibility and fall through to the close path.

## Why

The t2710 analysis (#20361, comment: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20361#issuecomment-4294270853) found that Gate 1 (age < 48h) is the primary blocker for `origin:interactive` planning PRs. All other gates pass for the common case of repo-owner-authored TODO-only PRs.

Planning-only conflicts (TODO.md, todo/**, README.md) are zero-risk to rebase at any age — the files are bookkeeping, not code. The 48h cap is appropriate for code conflicts (limit blast radius), but for planning-only conflicts it unnecessarily pushes PRs to the close path after 48h.

Reference PRs #20201, #20232, #20329 all touched only `TODO.md` and were `origin:interactive` by the repo owner. #20201 was closed without merge — likely because the 48h window expired before the sweep caught the DIRTY state.

Ref #20361

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh:343-360` — restructure `_dps_consider_rebase` to apply a two-tier age check

### Implementation approach

Add a new env-configurable constant:
```bash
DIRTY_PR_REBASE_PLANNING_MAX_AGE="${DIRTY_PR_REBASE_PLANNING_MAX_AGE:-604800}"  # 7d
```

Restructure `_dps_consider_rebase` to:
1. Check gates 2-4 first (author, parent-task, repo_path) — these are age-independent.
2. Compute conflicts and `non_planning` (using the widened allowlist from the sibling issue).
3. If `non_planning` is empty (planning-only conflict), apply `DIRTY_PR_REBASE_PLANNING_MAX_AGE` (7d).
4. If `non_planning` is non-empty, apply the existing `DIRTY_PR_REBASE_MAX_AGE` (48h) — but this path currently doesn't emit rebase at all (only planning-only conflicts get rebased), so this is a no-op guard for future extension.

```bash
_dps_consider_rebase() {
    local age="$1" rebase_author_ok="$2" has_parent_task="$3"
    local repo_path="$4" head_ref="$5"

    # Author and label gates (age-independent)
    [[ "$rebase_author_ok" -eq 1 ]] || return 0
    [[ "$has_parent_task" -eq 0 ]] || return 0
    [[ -n "$repo_path" && -d "$repo_path" ]] || return 0

    local conflicts non_planning
    conflicts=$(_dps_conflicting_files "$repo_path" "$head_ref" "origin/main" 2>/dev/null) || conflicts=""
    [[ -n "$conflicts" ]] || return 0
    non_planning=$(printf '%s\n' "$conflicts" | grep -vx 'TODO.md' | grep -v '^todo/' | grep -vx 'README.md' | grep -v '^\s*$' || true)

    if [[ -z "$non_planning" ]]; then
        # Planning-only conflict — use extended age window
        [[ "$age" -lt "$DIRTY_PR_REBASE_PLANNING_MAX_AGE" ]] || return 0
        printf '%s|planning-only-conflict' "$_DIRTY_ACTION_REBASE"
    fi
    # Non-planning conflicts: age gate + future extension point
    # Currently no rebase for mixed conflicts.
    return 0
}
```

### Dependencies

- Sibling issue #20463 (widen conflict allowlist) should land first or be combined. The `non_planning` filter and variable name from #20463 are assumed in this implementation.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh
# Verify: a 3-day-old TODO-only DIRTY PR is classified as rebase (not close/notify)
# Verify: a 3-day-old code-conflict DIRTY PR is NOT classified as rebase
```

## Acceptance

1. New `DIRTY_PR_REBASE_PLANNING_MAX_AGE` env var (default 604800 = 7d) is documented in the file's config section.
2. Planning-only conflicts use the extended age window.
3. Non-planning conflicts still use `DIRTY_PR_REBASE_MAX_AGE` (48h) as the ceiling.
4. Age gate is moved after conflict-scope detection (reorder within the function).
5. ShellCheck clean.

title: t2737: multi-runtime version freshness for framework status greeting
body:
## Session Origin

t2736 shipped a cache-read greeting for OpenCode that extracts version and runtime from `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting.txt` line 1. Post-merge verification exposed the fragility of the alternative approach (Option 1, setup-time literal interpolation in `AGENTS.md`): at Sonnet/Haiku tiers, the model substitutes "OpenCode" → "Claude Code" from its own identity prior and drops version numbers entirely. Only cache-read (observed data, not quoted instruction) survives the tier mix. This parent tracks generalising that proven pattern across all aidevops-supported runtimes so the greeting stays accurate without per-runtime drift.

## What

Provide an authoritative, auto-updating source of truth for `{runtime_display_name, runtime_version, aidevops_version}` that every runtime's AGENTS.md equivalent can read at session start. Single template, per-runtime population, zero hardcoded versions anywhere.

## Why

- **Correctness**: version literals in AGENTS.md files go stale within a release cycle. A centralised cache + read-from-file instruction kept t2736 green across Opus/Sonnet/Haiku; the same architecture should apply to every runtime.
- **Scalability**: aidevops supports a growing matrix of runtimes (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex, Droid, Aider, Cursor, Continue, …). Each one currently requires its own greeting handling; without a shared helper every new runtime re-invents the wheel.
- **Debuggability**: one canonical cache file per runtime makes "what did the framework report at session start" inspectable by humans and other agents without re-running scripts.

## How

Decomposition into three phases. Each phase is a separate child issue linked back here; this parent stays open until all phases merge.

### Phase A — foundation (blocking for B and C)

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runtime-registry.sh` — add `rt_version <runtime>` returning the runtime's installed version string (e.g. `opencode --version`, `claude --version`, `codex --version`), with graceful `unknown` fallback. Model on the existing `rt_*` dispatch functions in this file.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runtime-registry.sh` — add `rt_display_name <runtime>` (e.g. opencode→"OpenCode", claude-code→"Claude Code", codex→"Codex") for template interpolation.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/greeting-cache-helper.sh` — writes `~/.aidevops/cache/session-greeting-{runtime}.txt` with line 1 normalised as `aidevops vX running in {display_name} vY | {repo_slug}`. Called from the runtime's plugin / hook / wrapper at session start.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config.sh` — parameterise the heredoc in `_generate_agents_opencode()` so the cache-file path and display name are runtime-substituted; rename helper to `_generate_agents()` accepting a runtime arg. Preserves t2736 semantics for OpenCode, adds generality.

### Phase B — Claude Code rollout

- EDIT: `Claude-aidevops` plugin (`greeting.mjs` equivalent) — wire the new `greeting-cache-helper.sh` to write the per-runtime cache at session start.
- EDIT: `_generate_agents_Claude()` in `generate-runtime-config.sh` — emit the same cache-read instruction, substituted for Claude Code.
- VERIFY: `~/.config/Claude/AGENTS.md` gets regenerated by `setup.sh --non-interactive`; opening a fresh Claude Code session produces a greeting with correct version numbers at Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku tiers.

### Phase C — remaining runtimes (one child issue per runtime as needed)

- Codex, Droid, Aider, Cursor, Continue — file follow-up child issues only as user demand surfaces. Phase A's abstractions should reduce each to a ~50-line plugin + template addition.

## Files to modify (Phase A scope only; B and C in child issues)

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-registry.sh` — add `rt_version`, `rt_display_name`
- `.agents/scripts/greeting-cache-helper.sh` — NEW
- `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config.sh` — parameterise existing opencode generator

## Acceptance

Parent issue stays open until all three phases have merged PRs. Closure criteria:

1. Phase A helper functions exist and are invoked at session start by at least OpenCode (existing plugin) and Claude Code (new wiring).
2. Both runtimes' AGENTS.md files read from per-runtime caches, not hardcoded versions.
3. Running `aidevops update`, then opening a fresh session in each supported runtime, produces a greeting with the new version — no stale v-numbers, no "Claude Code" / "OpenCode" substitution at lower tiers.
4. `rt_version unknown-runtime` gracefully returns `unknown`, not a subshell failure.

## PR Conventions (parent-task rule)

- Each phase PR uses `For #<this-issue>` or `Ref #<this-issue>` in its body — never `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves`.
- Only the final phase PR (when all runtimes are wired and the parent is ready to close) uses `Closes #<this-issue>`.

## Scope

Framework-internal. No user-facing behaviour change beyond "greeting versions stay correct as aidevops/runtime versions bump." No dependencies on the open [upstream OpenCode feature request #23879](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/23879) (dismissible toasts) — that's a separate UX concern, not on this critical path.

title: t2738: extend _gh_auto_link_sub_issue to honour 'Parent:' line at create-time
body:
## What

Extend `_gh_auto_link_sub_issue` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` so it detects a `Parent: #NNN` / `Parent: GH#NNN` / `Parent: tNNN` line in the child issue body at create-time. Currently only dot-notation titles (`tNNN.M:`) trigger auto-linkage — non-dot-notation phase-style children never get the GitHub sub-issue relationship established.

## Why

Parent-child auto-linkage fires from two paths in the framework:

1. **Create-time** — `_gh_auto_link_sub_issue` (in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, called by `gh_create_issue`). Currently only catches dot-notation titles.
2. **Backfill-time** — `_detect_parent_from_gh_state` (in `issue-sync-relationships.sh`, called by `backfill-sub-issues`). Catches dot-notation + `Parent:` line + `Blocked by:` + parent-task label.

The create-time path is structurally narrower than the backfill path. Non-dot-notation phase children (e.g. `t2722: Phase 1 of t2721 parent`) never get linked at creation. Backfill recovers them eventually, unless GraphQL rate limit is exhausted — in which case the linkage is silently lost (Gap B, filed separately).

Observed in session 2026-04-22: parent #20402 (t2721) + child #20410 (t2722 phase 1) were created with narrative body prose only, no `Parent:` line. Create-time auto-link skipped on title regex miss; backfill skipped on rate-limit exhaustion. Sub-issue graph remained empty.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-auto-link-parent-line.sh
- todo/tasks/t{NEW}-brief.md

### Changes

1. `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:_gh_auto_link_sub_issue` — extend arg-parse loop to capture `--body` / `--body=` / `--body-file` / `--body-file=`. After the existing dot-notation title check, add a body-parse fallback that extracts `Parent: <ref>` using the same regex shape as `_detect_parent_from_gh_state` method 2 (plain, bold-markdown, backtick-quoted variants; `tNNN` / `#NNN` / `GH#NNN` ref forms). Resolve `tNNN` via a single `gh search issues` call (reuse `_resolve_task_id_via_gh_search` semantics inline — copy 6 lines rather than source the 900-line relationships module).
2. Add regression test `test-gh-auto-link-parent-line.sh` following the pattern of `test-backfill-sub-issues.sh`: stub `gh` on PATH, assert `addSubIssue` mutation fires for each body variant, assert no-op when neither title nor body signals present.
3. Brief file (this file).

## Acceptance

- Creating an issue whose body contains `Parent: #NNNN` triggers an `addSubIssue` mutation linking the new issue under `#NNNN`.
- Creating an issue whose body contains `Parent: tNNN` resolves the task ID to an issue number and links.
- Creating an issue whose body contains `**Parent:** \`tNNN\`` (bold-markdown variant) links.
- Creating an issue with neither dot-notation nor `Parent:` line produces no sub-issue mutation (existing behaviour preserved).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` clean.

- REST fallback for rate-limit-exhausted node-ID resolution — separate issue (Gap B).

title: t2739: extend REST fallback to sub-issue backfill node-ID resolution (Gap B)
body:
## Task

Extend the t2574 REST-fallback pattern to the sub-issue backfill path so that `backfill-sub-issues` no longer silently skips links when GraphQL budget is exhausted.

## Why

When the pulse runs `backfill-sub-issues` during a low-GraphQL-budget window:

- `_cached_node_id` in `issue-sync-relationships.sh` calls GraphQL to resolve issue numbers to node IDs.
- On rate-limit exhaustion, the GraphQL call returns empty silently.
- `_backfill_parent_children` receives an empty node ID, emits `log_verbose "could not resolve parent node ID"` (only visible with `VERBOSE=1`), and continues.
- The outer `cmd_backfill_sub_issues` loop reports a generic "Skipped" status — the caller cannot distinguish a true no-op (no parent signal in child) from a rate-limit skip.

Observed in session 2026-04-22: PR #20415 session had 0 GraphQL points remaining for ~20 minutes. Backfill ran during that window; parent #20402 and child #20410 never got linked until the rate limit reset. Net effect: the sub-issue graph is populated non-deterministically.

## How

### Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh` — `_cached_node_id`, `_backfill_parent_children`, `cmd_backfill_sub_issues`

### Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh:_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` and the REST fallback added in t2574 (PR #20255). That pattern: detect GraphQL remaining ≤ threshold via `gh api rate_limit`, fall through to a REST-equivalent path.

For node-ID resolution specifically: the REST endpoint `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}` returns a `node_id` field at the top level. No GraphQL needed.

### Changes

1. Add a REST path to `_cached_node_id`: if GraphQL returns empty AND `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` is true, call `gh api /repos/$OWNER/$REPO/issues/$NUM --jq .node_id` and cache that result.
2. Distinguish skip reasons in `cmd_backfill_sub_issues` outer loop: emit `RATE_LIMITED` instead of `SKIPPED` when `_cached_node_id` hit a rate-limit path. Callers (pulse) can then re-enqueue the issue for the next cycle instead of treating it as permanently uninterested.
3. Update `test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` with two scenarios:
   - REST-fallback path fires when GraphQL is exhausted (stub sets `_GH_SHOULD_FALLBACK_OVERRIDE=1`)
   - `RATE_LIMITED` status is emitted distinctly from `SKIPPED`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `shellcheck issue-sync-relationships.sh` clean (no new findings)
- [ ] New test scenarios pass; existing 21 backfill tests still pass
- [ ] Manual smoke: run `backfill-sub-issues --issue 20410 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops` under simulated rate-limit (`AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD=9999`) and confirm link is established via REST path

## Not In Scope

- Pre-emptive budget reservation / circuit breaker for backfill (orthogonal to REST fallback)
- Changes to GraphQL mutation paths (addSubIssue) — those require GraphQL by design; they already have a REST-equivalent (t2574) or can wait for budget recovery

## Session Origin

Identified in t2721/t2722 session during analysis of why #20410 was not linked to #20402. Gap B of four-gap audit. Gap A (create-time `Parent:` line detection) shipped in PR #20474.

title: t2740: auto-file next phase child when prior phase PR merges for parent-task issues (Gap C)
body:
## Task

When a phase child PR merges for a `parent-task`-labeled issue, auto-create the next phase's child issue from the parent's `## Phases` section. Eliminates the manual step of filing Phase 2, 3, 4... by hand after each prior phase ships.

## Why

Current parent-task decomposition lifecycle has a gap between phases:

1. Parent issue filed with `## Phases` section enumerating work.
2. Phase 1 child filed manually (via interactive session or `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` which fires once per parent per day).
3. Phase 1 PR ships, merges. Parent's `## Children` section gets updated.
4. **Phase 2 is NOT auto-filed.** `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` won't fire because the parent already has child(ren). Maintainer must manually notice and file Phase 2.

Net effect: long-running multi-phase parent tasks stall between phases. Maintainer has to remember. Workers cannot self-serve.

Observed in t2721 (7-phase auto-dispatch removal): Phase 1 shipped in PR #20415. Phases 2-7 require maintainer to file each in sequence.

## How

### Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — add a post-merge hook that inspects the merged PR's linked issue and the parent
- Possibly new `.agents/scripts/shared-phase-filing.sh` — extraction of phase-parsing + filing logic for reuse
- `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` — loosen the "zero children" gate OR coordinate with the new post-merge path

### Reference patterns

- `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` for parent `## Phases` parsing — same section extraction
- `pulse-merge.sh` existing post-merge hooks (e.g., `release_interactive_claim_on_merge` at merge time)
- `_extract_children_from_prose` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1053-1089` — identifies existing children via regex

### Design considerations (tier:thinking)

Non-trivial decisions:

1. **Closed-not-merged edge case**: if a phase PR closed without merging (cancelled, rejected), do we skip or re-queue the same phase?
2. **External-input-blocked phases**: some phases need maintainer decisions before starting (e.g., "after discussion, implement option X"). How does the auto-filer know to skip?
3. **Phase order enforcement**: should filing wait for Phase N-1 to merge, or auto-fill all remaining phases at once after Phase 1 merges?
4. **Brief generation for next phase**: does the post-merge hook generate a brief, or just the issue, leaving brief creation to the worker's first action?
5. **Parent issue state updates**: Children section (`Phase N filed as #NNN`) update, phase status markers (`(in progress)`, `(merged)`).

Recommend: MVP only fires for "next phase" (N+1 of merged N), uses a new `## Phases` marker like `- Phase 3 - NAME: [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]` to opt in per phase. Phases marked `[requires-decision]` never auto-file. This keeps blast radius tight.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Design doc or issue comment outlining closed-not-merged, external-input, and ordering strategy chosen
- [ ] Implementation lands behind a feature flag `AIDEVOPS_SEQUENTIAL_PHASE_AUTOFILE=0|1` (default 0 initially)
- [ ] Test coverage: merge phase 1 → phase 2 auto-fires when marked opt-in, skipped when not marked
- [ ] Closed-not-merged phase PR does NOT trigger next phase autofill
- [ ] Shellcheck clean on all modified files

## Not In Scope

- Auto-implementing the filed phase — the worker pickup path (pulse dispatch + `claim-task-id.sh`) continues to handle implementation
- Cross-repo phase chains (all phases must be in the same repo as the parent, initial version)
- Dynamic phase generation (parent body edited to add Phase 8 after the fact) — initial version uses static phase list at parent creation time

## Session Origin

Identified in t2721/t2722 session. Parent t2721 has 7 phases; Phases 2-7 must be filed manually by the maintainer after each prior phase merges. Gap C of four-gap audit. Gap A (create-time `Parent:` line detection) shipped in PR #20474; Gap B filed as #20475.

title: t2741: add aidevops parent-status CLI helper for decomposition inspection (Gap D)
body:
## Task

Add a read-only CLI helper `aidevops parent-status <issue-number> [--repo <slug>]` that shows the current decomposition state of a `parent-task`-labeled issue: phases planned, children filed, merged, in-flight, next action.

## Why

Currently the maintainer has to piece together parent decomposition state from three sources:

1. Parent issue body (`## Phases` section — what's planned)
2. `## Children` section in parent body (what's been filed — often stale)
3. `gh issue list --search "refs:NNN"` + manual cross-reference with PR merge state

Result: hard to answer "what's left on t2721?" without opening multiple browser tabs or running 3-4 commands. High-friction. Workers cannot self-serve either.

One command that prints a tidy table would collapse the friction.

## How

### Files to modify

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/parent-status-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/aidevops` (dispatch entry — add `parent-status` subcommand)

### Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/scripts/pulse-diagnose-helper.sh` (read-only helper with `--json` + `--verbose` output modes) and `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` (already parses `## Phases` section from parent body).

### Output format

Default (human):

    $ aidevops parent-status 20402
    Parent: #20402 t2721: Remove / invert auto-dispatch default
    Phases: 7 planned, 1 filed, 0 merged, 1 in-flight

    Phase 1 — Inventory: #20410 (PR #20415 OPEN mergeable)
    Phase 2 — needs-credentials label: NOT FILED
    Phase 3 — backfill 4 at-risk issues: NOT FILED
    Phase 4 — pulse-dispatch-core.sh flip: NOT FILED
    Phase 5 — strip label-adding: NOT FILED
    Phase 6 — invert self-assign carveouts: NOT FILED
    Phase 7 — doc sweep: NOT FILED

    Next action: merge PR #20415, then file Phase 2 child.

`--json` emits a structured version for programmatic use.

### Sources

For each phase line, the helper reads:

- Parent body `## Phases` section (planned phases with names)
- Children discovered via sub-issue graph (`gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/N/sub_issues`) AND via prose extraction (fallback for unlinked children) — matches `_extract_children_from_prose` behaviour
- For each child: its state (OPEN/CLOSED), linked PRs (via Development section), PR merge state
- Cross-reference phase name (from parent) with child title to map phases → issues

### Rate-limit considerations

Each invocation: ~1 REST call for parent body, 1 REST call for sub-issue list, 1 REST call per child for PR state. For a 7-phase parent: ~9 REST calls, 0 GraphQL points. Well within any budget.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `aidevops parent-status 20402` produces the table output shown above
- [ ] `aidevops parent-status 20402 --json` emits structured data
- [ ] Shellcheck clean on new helper and aidevops dispatch edit
- [ ] Test: unit test using stubbed `gh` (following `test-backfill-sub-issues.sh` pattern) with canned parent body + child payloads, assert output shape
- [ ] Exits 1 with a clear error when the target issue lacks `parent-task` label

## Not In Scope

- Mutation (filing next phase, closing parent) — that's Gap C
- Cross-repo parents — initial version scoped to single repo
- Historical analysis (time-in-phase, cycle time) — initial version is point-in-time only

## Session Origin

Identified in t2721/t2722 session. Observed self-friction during that session: counting phases filed vs planned took several `gh` calls and manual table building. Gap D of four-gap audit. Gap A (create-time `Parent:` line) shipped in PR #20474; Gap B filed as #20475; Gap C filed as #20476.
