title: t2742: Fix string-literal ratchet regex false positive on adjacent quoted shell arguments
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced during t2738 implementation (PR #20474) in an interactive session. The helper-extraction refactor added three `local tid="$1" repo="$2"` style declarations to `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, which tripped the string-literal ratchet in `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`. The refactor had to split every multi-var `local` into separate lines — a workaround, not a fix. The pattern itself is idiomatic shell and appears pre-existing in at least one location (line 1066 of the same file: `local op="$1" repo="$2" number="$3"`). The ratchet will keep catching legitimate patterns until the root cause in the extraction regex is addressed.

Follow-up to **#19739 (t2230)**, which converted the validators to ratchet-style (absolute-count → delta-count) and is CLOSED / `status:done`. t2230 reduced the blast radius (only NEW repeats block) but did not fix the underlying regex logic. This issue fixes the regex.

## What

Fix the false-positive class in `_count_repeated_literals` (`.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:270-280`) and its display companion `_show_repeated_literals` (`:283-293`) so the `"[^"]{4,}"` capture does not misinterpret the span between two adjacent shell-quoted arguments as a string literal.

## Why

The regex `"[^"]{4,}"` knows nothing about shell syntax. When a line contains two quoted var-refs separated by whitespace — a standard shell idiom:

```bash
local tid="$1" repo="$2"
```

— the regex captures `" repo="` as a 6-char "literal" using the `"` at the end of `"$1"` and the `"` at the start of `"$2"` as the outer quotes. The existing exclusion filter `grep -vE '^"\$'` only rejects literals that START with `"$` (direct var-refs like `"$agent_name"`). It cannot reject inter-argument spans, because the captured "literal" starts with whitespace, not `$`.

**Impact:**

- Punishes the idiomatic `local a="$1" b="$2" c="$3"` pattern (common for multi-param helpers and `while-case` arg parsers)
- Crosses the `≥3 occurrences` ratchet threshold quickly — any file that introduces 3-4 new helper signatures with this shape trips it
- Forces workaround patches that split every `local` declaration into single-var lines — bloats helper prologues and adds no information
- Affects WRITE-TIME enforcement (pre-commit-hook.sh runs on `git commit`), so every developer hits it on every multi-param helper they write
- Also affects the empty-init variant: `local title="" repo="" body=""` captures ` repo=` and ` body=` as spurious literals (noted in memory record from 2026-04-21 covering PR #20255)

**Confirmed in the wild** — PR #20474, commits `9de0fa355` → `1c128d3eb`:

```
[ERROR] NEW repeated string literals in .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh (new: 1, pre-existing: 3)
  4x: "
  4x: "interactive"
  5x: "true"
```

(The `4x: "` display is the `" repo="` literal truncated by the display pipeline — the captured string includes leading whitespace that breaks column alignment. Also a minor issue worth fixing.)

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` lines 270-293 — fix `_count_repeated_literals` and `_show_repeated_literals`
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` — regression test fixtures
- **EDIT** (optional, same PR): `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:274,287` — replace `grep -v '^\s*#'` with POSIX `grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#'` (see cross-platform section)

### Recommended approach: pre-strip shell-syntax tokens before the extraction regex

The fundamental issue is that `grep -oE '"[^"]{4,}"'` counts `"` characters without understanding shell argument-quoting. The most robust portable fix is to eliminate shell var-ref tokens BEFORE the literal extraction regex runs, so the `"` pairs that remain belong to true string literals.

Insert a `sed` pre-strip pass between the comment-filter and the literal extraction:

```bash
_count_repeated_literals() {
	local _ext_literal='"[^"]{4,}"'
	local _ext_numeric='^"[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*"$'
	local _ext_varref='^"\$'
	grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' |
		sed -E '
			s/"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"//g
			s/"\$\{[^}]*\}"//g
			s/"\$@"//g
			s/"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"//g
		' |
		grep -oE "$_ext_literal" |
		grep -vE "$_ext_numeric" |
		grep -vE "$_ext_varref" |
		sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 >= 3' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
	return 0
}
```

After the sed pre-strip, `local tid="$1" repo="$2"` reduces to `local tid= repo=` — no quote pairs remain, no false-positive literal captured. The existing `_ext_varref` filter stays as a second line of defense.

The four sed substitution patterns cover:

| Pattern | Matches |
|---|---|
| `"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"` | `"$var"`, `"$name"`, `"$_private"` |
| `"\$\{[^}]*\}"` | `"${var}"`, `"${var[0]}"`, `"${var:-default}"`, `"${#var}"` |
| `"\$@"` | special array-expansion token |
| `"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"` | `"$1"`, `"$*"`, `"$#"`, `"$?"`, `"$$"`, `"$!"`, `"$-"` |

Apply the same pre-strip in `_show_repeated_literals` so the display output matches what the counter saw.

### Cross-platform compatibility (MANDATORY)

The validator runs from `pre-commit-hook.sh`, invoked by git during `git commit`. It must work on:

- **macOS** with `/usr/bin/sed` (BSD sed) and `/usr/bin/grep` (BSD grep)
- **Linux** with GNU sed and GNU grep (Ubuntu, Debian, Alpine)
- **bash 3.2** (macOS default) through **bash 5.x** (GNU) — framework auto-upgrades to bash 4+ via Homebrew on macOS per `reference/bash-compat.md`, but pre-commit-hook.sh may run before that upgrade is active

**Verified safe constructs** (used in the recommended fix):

- `sed -E` (ERE mode): supported by both BSD sed (macOS 10.8+) and GNU sed
- Character classes `[A-Za-z0-9_]`: POSIX, works on both grep flavors
- Anchors `^`, `$`: POSIX
- `[[:space:]]`, `[[:alpha:]]`: POSIX character classes
- `{N,}` interval quantifier in ERE: both flavors when invoked with `-E`

**Forbidden constructs** (will break on at least one platform):

- `sed -i` without backup-extension argument: GNU accepts `sed -i 'script' file`, BSD requires `sed -i '' 'script' file`. This pipeline reads stdin / writes stdout — `-i` is not used, no conflict, but mention so the worker does not "improve" it into in-place mode.
- `\s`, `\w`, `\b`, `\d`: GNU grep extensions. BSD grep does NOT reliably honour them. The current line `274` uses `grep -v '^\s*#'` — likely a pre-existing cross-platform bug. Verify on a stock macOS shell:

  ```bash
  printf '  # comment\nreal line\n' | /usr/bin/grep -v '^\s*#'
  ```

  If BSD grep does not honour `\s`, the current validator is not actually filtering comment-only lines on macOS. Replace with POSIX `[[:space:]]*`.

- `[[:<:]]` / `[[:>:]]`: BSD word-boundaries, not supported on GNU
- `sed` with `-r` flag for ERE: GNU-specific. Use `-E` (portable to both since BSD sed 10.8 and GNU sed 4.2+)
- Perl-style lookaround `(?=...)` / `(?!...)`: not supported in POSIX ERE on either flavor

**Test on both platforms before merging** — see Verification below.

### Verification

Add a regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` covering these fixtures. Each test feeds a string through `_count_repeated_literals` (sourced from `pre-commit-hook.sh`) and asserts the expected count:

**1. Positive — genuine repeated literal IS caught:**

```bash
local msg="error: invalid input"
echo "error: invalid input" >&2
printf '%s\n' "error: invalid input"
```

Expect: 1 distinct literal at ≥3 count (`"error: invalid input"`).

**2. Negative — inter-argument spans are NOT counted (the bug this issue fixes):**

```bash
local tid="$1" repo="$2"
local body="$1" repo="$2"
local title="" repo="" body=""
local op="$1" repo="$2" number="$3"
```

Expect: 0 distinct literals at ≥3 count. Before fix: 1 (`" repo="`).

**3. Negative — repeated var-refs (already working, regression guard):**

```bash
echo "$var"
echo "$var"
echo "$var"
```

Expect: 0. The existing `^"\$` filter handles this — confirm still works after sed pre-strip.

**4. Negative — numeric-only strings (already working, regression guard):**

```bash
echo "3.14"
echo "3.14"
echo "3.14"
```

Expect: 0.

**5. Negative — `${var}` form inside quotes (new coverage):**

```bash
log "${msg}"
log "${msg}"
log "${msg}"
```

Expect: 0. The `s/"\$\{[^}]*\}"//g` sed pattern must strip this.

**6. Positive — prose literals with $ inside are still caught (boundary case):**

```bash
err="price is \$5.00"
err="price is \$5.00"
err="price is \$5.00"
```

Expect: 1. Escaped `\$` inside a quoted string is NOT a var-ref; must survive the sed pre-strip.

**7. Cross-platform smoke test** — run the test suite on both Linux and macOS:

- **Linux (CI)**: GitHub Actions `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` job runs it automatically if the test is under `.agents/scripts/tests/` (existing pattern)
- **macOS**: Run locally with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`. Also run under `/bin/bash` (v3.2) explicitly, not just Homebrew bash: `/bin/bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`
- **Alpine/BusyBox** (optional but recommended for hermetic verification):

  ```bash
  docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work alpine:3.19 \
    sh -c 'apk add --quiet bash grep sed && bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh'
  ```

  BusyBox sed/grep are stricter POSIX subsets than BSD or GNU — if the test passes on BusyBox, it passes everywhere.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_count_repeated_literals` and `_show_repeated_literals` no longer count the span between adjacent quoted shell-argument tokens as a string literal
- [ ] Regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` exists with all 7 scenarios above (4 negative, 2 positive, 1 boundary) and passes
- [ ] Running the ratchet against the pre-t2738 HEAD of `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` reports the same or FEWER repeated literals post-fix — never more (no new false positives introduced in existing files)
- [ ] Running the ratchet against the post-t2738 HEAD of the same file reports 0 NEW repeats compared to main (the current workaround commit `1c128d3eb` becomes unnecessary but harmless)
- [ ] Pre-existing use of `\s` at `pre-commit-hook.sh:274,287` is either confirmed safe on BSD grep across all supported macOS versions OR replaced with POSIX `[[:space:]]*`
- [ ] Test suite passes on both `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` CI jobs
- [ ] No new shellcheck violations introduced in `pre-commit-hook.sh`

## Context

title: t2743: Fix shared-gh-wrappers REST fallback to work in zsh (drops labels+assignees silently)
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced during t2742 filing. When an interactive session on macOS (default shell: zsh) sourced `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` + `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` and called `gh_create_issue` under GraphQL-exhausted conditions (forcing REST fallback), the created issue was missing its `--label` and `--assignee` values — applied via REST only after manual `gh api POST` remediation. Root cause: `IFS=',' read -ra _toks <<<"$val"` patterns throughout the REST fallback helper fail silently in zsh because zsh uses `read -A arr` for array reads, not `read -a arr`.

Direct evidence from t2742 / #20478 filing (PR #20479 session):

```
_gh_issue_create_rest:read:22: bad option: -a
_gh_issue_create_rest:read:24: bad option: -a
_gh_issue_create_rest:read:22: bad option: -a
https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20478  ← issue created, but with empty labels[] and assignees[]
```

Issue #20478 needed three follow-up REST calls to apply the 5 labels + 1 assignee the caller had already supplied via `--label` and `--assignee`.

## What

Make `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` work correctly when sourced by a zsh interactive shell (macOS default), not just when sourced by bash 4+ (headless worker default). The helper must tokenize `--label foo,bar,baz` into a `labels=(foo bar baz)` array using a shell-agnostic mechanism that works in bash 3.2+, zsh 5+, and BusyBox ash.

Secondary: fix two adjacent load-order issues in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` that surface only when the wrapper is sourced outside the pulse's canonical invocation path.

## Why

The REST fallback exists to keep issue/PR/comment operations alive when GraphQL is rate-limited (t2574). It's a safety net. When the safety net silently loses labels and assignees, the upstream claim-task-id / auto-dispatch pipeline sees un-tagged issues and either:

- Ignores them (missing `tier:*` → no dispatch tier routing)
- Mis-routes them (missing `origin:interactive` → pulse may treat as worker issue)
- Leaves them stuck pre-dispatch (missing `auto-dispatch` → never gets picked up)

Blast radius:

- **Production path (headless workers)**: unaffected. Workers invoke `/bin/bash` explicitly via `headless-runtime-helper.sh`, and `read -ra` works in bash 3.1+.
- **Interactive path (maintainer sessions)**: affected whenever macOS default shell (zsh) sources the wrappers and REST fallback fires. This is exactly the "offline / rate-limited" scenario the fallback was designed to handle, so it fails when the user needs it most.

Confirmed in the wild this session — t2742 (#20478) was filed with no labels and no assignee; three REST catch-up calls repaired the state. Every interactive issue-filing during GraphQL exhaustion hits this.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` — replace every `IFS=',' read -ra _toks <<<"$val"` with a shell-portable split
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh:56-58` — fix the conditional REST-fallback-source block so it works when `_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR` is unset (interactive sourcing)
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` (multiple lines) — ensure `print_info`/`print_warning` helpers are either sourced from `shared-constants.sh` or replaced with inline `printf`-to-stderr so they don't fail in contexts that haven't sourced the constants file
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-shell-compat.sh` — regression tests that exercise the wrapper functions under both `/bin/bash` and `/bin/zsh` explicitly

### Recommended approach: single portable split helper, one point of replacement

Define one helper function near the top of `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`:

```bash
# Portable CSV split. Emits one token per line to stdout.
# Works in bash 3.2+, zsh 5+, BusyBox ash — uses POSIX parameter expansion only.
# No `read -ra` (bash-only), no `read -A` (zsh-only), no IFS-clobber-and-split.
_gh_split_csv() {
	local _str="$1"
	local _delim="${2:-,}"
	while [[ -n "$_str" ]]; do
		if [[ "$_str" == *"$_delim"* ]]; then
			printf '%s\n' "${_str%%"$_delim"*}"
			_str="${_str#*"$_delim"}"
		else
			printf '%s\n' "$_str"
			_str=""
		fi
	done
	return 0
}
```

Then replace every line of the form:

```bash
--label) IFS=',' read -ra _toks <<<"${2:-}"; labels+=("${_toks[@]}"); shift 2 ;;
```

with:

```bash
--label) while IFS= read -r _tok; do [[ -n "$_tok" ]] && labels+=("$_tok"); done < <(_gh_split_csv "${2:-}"); shift 2 ;;
```

`< <(...)` process substitution works in both bash and zsh. `IFS= read -r _tok` works in both. The `[[ -n "$_tok" ]]` guard skips empty tokens (e.g., from trailing commas).

### Sites to convert

From `grep -n 'read -ra' .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` (14 occurrences):

| Line | Context |
|---|---|
| 138, 139 | `_gh_issue_create_rest` — `--label` / `--label=` |
| 140, 141 | `_gh_issue_create_rest` — `--assignee` / `--assignee=` |
| 304, 305 | `_gh_issue_edit_rest` — `--add-label` / `--add-label=` |
| 306, 307 | `_gh_issue_edit_rest` — `--remove-label` / `--remove-label=` |
| 308, 309 | `_gh_issue_edit_rest` — `--add-assignee` / `--add-assignee=` |
| 310, 311 | `_gh_issue_edit_rest` — `--remove-assignee` / `--remove-assignee=` |
| 522, 523 | `_gh_pr_create_rest` — `--label` / `--label=` |
| 685, 686 | (additional occurrence in a sibling function, verify context) |

All 14 sites use the same pattern and should be converted uniformly. No conditional — single replacement.

### Load-order fixes (sibling bugs surfaced during t2742 filing)

**Bug 2a**: `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:56-58` conditionally sources the REST fallback only if `_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR` is populated:

```bash
if [[ -n "$_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR" && -f "$_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh" ]]; then
	source "$_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh"
fi
```

When sourced via `source /absolute/path/to/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` from an interactive shell, `_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR` may not be set (depends on whether the caller also sourced `shared-constants.sh` first). Result: `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest`, `_gh_issue_create_rest`, `_gh_pr_create_rest` are all undefined, `gh_create_issue` fails with `command not found: _gh_should_fallback_to_rest`.

**Recommended fix**: derive the sibling path from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}` at source time and unconditionally attempt the sibling load:

```bash
# Derive sibling directory from this file's own path — works whether the
# caller has sourced shared-constants.sh or not.
_wrapper_self_dir="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}"
if [[ -f "$_wrapper_self_dir/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh" ]]; then
	# shellcheck source=shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh
	source "$_wrapper_self_dir/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh"
fi
unset _wrapper_self_dir
```

Note: `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` is bash-only. For zsh compat, use `${(%):-%x}` or normalize with a conditional. The wrapper is currently bash-shebanged (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`), and zsh sourcing of a bash script is a rare path — but this path IS hit in interactive AI sessions. Verify whether zsh populates `BASH_SOURCE` when sourcing (it does in recent zsh versions via compat mode) or provide a zsh branch.

**Bug 2b**: `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` at lines 501, 520, 528, 542, 650 (and more) calls `print_info` and `print_warning`. These functions live in `shared-constants.sh`, which is NOT auto-sourced. When the wrapper is used without the constants file sourced first, these calls produce `command not found: print_info` warnings. Not fatal (errors go to stderr, stdout still returns the URL), but noisy.

**Recommended fix**: at the top of `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, define minimal inline stubs if the real functions aren't defined yet:

```bash
# Minimal stub fallbacks. If shared-constants.sh is sourced later, its
# definitions will win (later sourcing overrides prior function definitions).
if ! declare -F print_info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	print_info() { printf '[INFO] %s\n' "$*" >&2; return 0; }
fi
if ! declare -F print_warning >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	print_warning() { printf '[WARN] %s\n' "$*" >&2; return 0; }
fi
```

This makes the wrapper self-contained without breaking the existing `shared-constants.sh` sourcing pattern.

### Cross-platform compatibility (MANDATORY)

The fix must work on:

- **macOS bash 3.2** — framework default shell before Homebrew upgrade; pre-upgrade setup scripts run here
- **macOS zsh 5+** — user's default interactive shell; AI sessions invoke wrappers from here
- **Linux bash 4+ / 5+** — GNU Ubuntu, Debian, Alpine; worker default
- **BusyBox ash** — Alpine Docker images used in hermetic CI

Verified portable constructs:

| Construct | bash 3.2+ | zsh 5+ | BusyBox ash | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `[[ -n "$x" ]]` | yes | yes | no (use `[ -n "$x" ]`) | Prefer `[[ ]]` since BusyBox ash doesn't source this helper |
| `[[ "$a" == *"$b"* ]]` | yes | yes | no | Same caveat |
| `${var%%pat*}` | yes | yes | yes | POSIX parameter expansion |
| `${var#*pat}` | yes | yes | yes | POSIX parameter expansion |
| `while IFS= read -r v; do ...` | yes | yes | yes | Universal |
| `< <(cmd)` process substitution | yes | yes | no | BusyBox ash doesn't support; wrapper isn't loaded in that path |
| `local _var="$1"` | yes | yes | yes | Universal inside functions |
| `declare -F fn` | yes | yes | no (use `command -v fn`) | Use `command -v` for broader compat if needed |
| `printf '%s\n' "$x"` | yes | yes | yes | Universal, prefer over `echo` |

Forbidden constructs (at least one target shell doesn't support):

- `read -a arr` — bash-only (bash 3.1+); zsh errors with `bad option: -a`
- `read -A arr` — zsh-only; bash errors with `invalid option`
- `mapfile -t arr` / `readarray -t arr` — bash 4.4+, not available on bash 3.2 or zsh
- `${(f)var}` — zsh-only array-from-newlines expansion
- `arr=($str)` with word-splitting — works in bash (with default IFS behaviour) but NOT in zsh by default (requires `setopt SH_WORD_SPLIT`)

### Verification

Add regression tests at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-shell-compat.sh`:

**1. Positive — `_gh_split_csv` tokenizes correctly under bash:**

```bash
/bin/bash -c '
  source .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh
  out=$(_gh_split_csv "a,b,c" ",")
  [[ "$out" == "$(printf "a\nb\nc")" ]] || exit 1
'
```

**2. Positive — same tokenization under zsh:**

```bash
/bin/zsh -c '
  source .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh
  out=$(_gh_split_csv "a,b,c" ",")
  [[ "$out" == "$(printf "a\nb\nc")" ]] || exit 1
'
```

**3. Negative — single token (no delimiter) returns the string unchanged:**

```bash
out=$(_gh_split_csv "solo" ",")
[[ "$out" == "solo" ]] || exit 1
```

**4. Negative — empty string returns nothing (no spurious empty line):**

```bash
out=$(_gh_split_csv "" ",")
[[ -z "$out" ]] || exit 1
```

**5. Boundary — trailing delimiter produces a trailing empty token, which the caller must skip (covered by the `[[ -n "$_tok" ]]` guard):**

```bash
out=$(_gh_split_csv "a,b," ",")
# raw split output includes the trailing empty token
lines=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
[[ "$lines" == "3" ]] || exit 1
```

**6. Integration — mock `gh api` call with labels+assignees under both shells, assert payload includes all tokens:**

```bash
# Stub gh to echo its POST body to a temp file, then invoke _gh_issue_create_rest
# with --label tier:standard,auto-dispatch,framework and --assignee marcusquinn,otheruser
# Assert the captured POST body includes labels=["tier:standard","auto-dispatch","framework"]
# and assignees=["marcusquinn","otheruser"]. Run once under /bin/bash, once under /bin/zsh.
```

**7. Load-order — source `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` from a bare shell with NO `_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR` set, confirm `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` is defined:**

```bash
/bin/bash -c '
  unset _SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR
  source .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh
  declare -F _gh_should_fallback_to_rest >/dev/null || exit 1
  declare -F _gh_issue_create_rest >/dev/null || exit 1
  declare -F _gh_pr_create_rest >/dev/null || exit 1
'
```

**8. CI coverage** — add the test suite to `.github/workflows/ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` so both shell matrices exercise it. macOS CI runs zsh natively; Ubuntu CI needs `apt-get install -y zsh` in the test setup step.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-shell-compat.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 14 occurrences of `IFS=',' read -ra _toks <<<"$val"` in `shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh` replaced with the `while read -r` + `_gh_split_csv` pattern
- [ ] `_gh_split_csv` helper defined once near the top of the file; shellcheck clean
- [ ] `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:56-58` REST-fallback-source block derives its path from `${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}` (or equivalent zsh-compat mechanism) and does not depend on `_SHARED_GH_WRAPPERS_DIR` being pre-set
- [ ] `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` defines inline `print_info` / `print_warning` stubs when the real functions aren't already in scope, so sourcing the wrapper alone doesn't produce `command not found` warnings
- [ ] Regression test `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-shell-compat.sh` exists with 7+ scenarios covering bash, zsh, load order, edge cases; passes on both `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` (with `apt-get install zsh`) and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` CI jobs
- [ ] End-to-end smoke: creating an issue via `gh_create_issue` in an interactive zsh session (with GraphQL exhausted to force REST) applies all `--label` values correctly — verified by comparing the returned issue's `labels` array to the `--label` CSV input
- [ ] No new shellcheck violations in either modified file; existing warnings count unchanged or lower
- [ ] Changelog / version bump not required (internal helper fix), but note in PR body that this restores correct labels-at-creation for interactive zsh sessions

## Context

- **Root cause discovery**: t2742 filing session, 2026-04-22. Created #20478 without labels; applied labels via `gh api POST repos/OWNER/REPO/issues/NNN/labels` as a 3-call remediation. Process demonstrated in [PR #20479 session comment] / memory record `mem_20260422184820_247ba78a`.
- **Related precedents**:
  - **t2574 (#20243)** — introduced REST fallback to handle GraphQL rate limits. This issue fixes a latent shell-compat bug in that same helper.
  - **t2689** — most recent refactor of the fallback; noted in file header. Did not surface the zsh bug because the test suite runs under bash only.
- **Memory records** (from `memory-helper.sh recall`):
  - `mem_20260422184820_247ba78a` (high): detailed diagnosis including workaround pattern (apply labels via direct `gh api POST` after the creation call)
- **Adjacent audits** (same PR or follow-up):
  - Check `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` and other sourced helpers for the same `read -ra` pattern — any CLI-parsing helper that does CSV tokenization is a candidate
  - Check `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — if it ever calls `read -ra` it should be fixed in the same sweep
  - Check shell-based plugin code under `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/` for equivalent bash-only constructs
- **Cross-platform framework rules** satisfied by this fix:
  - `prompts/build.txt` "Bash 3.2 Compatibility"
  - `reference/bash-compat.md`
  - `shared-constants.sh` "Shell style guide" (positional-param consolidation; this fix is consistent with that discipline)
- **Non-goal**: This issue does NOT change which operations use GraphQL vs REST. It does not change rate-limit thresholds. It does not add new wrapper functions. It fixes correctness of existing ones in a wider set of calling shells.

## Tier checklist

- [x] 2 files edit + 1 new test file (3 files total)

title: t2744: raise GraphQL throttle defaults and reduce pulse/stats cycle pressure
body:
# t2744 — Raise GraphQL throttle defaults and reduce pulse/stats cycle pressure

## Session Origin

Interactive session investigation triggered by user noting frequent "GraphQL budget exhausted" events. Diagnosis confirmed: per-cycle GraphQL cost (400-700 pts × 30 cycles/hr × 14 repos) chronically exceeds the 5000/hr budget by 2-4×. Existing protections fire too late — circuit breaker at 5% remaining (250/5000), REST fallback at 10 remaining — both engage after 95-99% of budget is already spent.

## What

Tier-1 (config-only) optimisations to GraphQL budget protection, addressing items 1-4 from the broader investigation:

1. Raise pulse circuit breaker default from 5% (`0.05`) to 30% (`0.30`) so worker dispatch pauses with headroom in reserve, not after the budget is gone.
2. Raise REST fallback default threshold from `10` to `1000` so read-heavy operations route through the separate 5000/hr REST core pool while GraphQL still has reserve.
3. Increase stats-wrapper interval from `900s` (15 min) to `3600s` (1 hour). Health dashboard data is not realtime; an hourly refresh cuts ~80% of stats-driven GraphQL spend.
4. Increase pulse cycle interval default from `120s` (2 min) to `180s` (3 min). 33% fewer cycles. Bonus: macOS launchd path currently hardcodes `120` and ignores `supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds` from settings (Linux/cron path already respects it) — fix that gap so the setting is honoured uniformly.

All four are env-overridable / config-overridable. Users wanting prior behaviour can revert via env vars or `aidevops settings set`.

## Why

Direct evidence at investigation time:

- GraphQL = `0/5000` remaining; REST core = `4044/5000` remaining (split-pool headroom is plentiful but unused).
- 21 distinct `[circuit-breaker-rl] GraphQL budget EXHAUSTED` events in current pulse log.
- Sawtooth pattern in log: breaker recovers to `4980/5000` then burns back to `0` within minutes.
- Circuit breaker tripping at `remaining=235` means ~95% of budget was already spent by the time the breaker fired.
- Worker dispatches were failing at step 1 (`gh issue read`, `gh pr create`) with `RATE_LIMIT_EXHAUSTED` errors, wasting $0.05-$0.25 per doomed dispatch + watchdog kill.

The existing layered protections (t2574, t2689, t2690) are correctly designed but tuned for "GraphQL exhaustion is rare". Reality: under realistic load (10+ pulse-enabled repos), exhaustion is the steady state. Raising the trip thresholds turns these from "last-ditch reactive" into "proactive headroom preservation", which is what the user actually wants from a circuit breaker.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh:87` — default `0.05` → `0.30`. Update header comment block (lines 24-28) accordingly.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh:34` — default `10` → `1000`. Update header comment.
- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:271` — `_read_pulse_interval_seconds` fallback `120` → `180`.
- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:535` — `_generate_pulse_plist_content` hardcoded `<integer>120</integer>` replaced with the value returned by `_read_pulse_interval_seconds` (so macOS plist respects settings.json the way Linux already does).
- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:587` — update "every 2 min" log message to be dynamic / accurate.
- EDIT: `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:977,998,1006-1011` — stats-wrapper `StartInterval` `900` → `3600`; cron schedule `*/15` → `0`; "every 15 min" message → "every hour".
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh:65` — default seed value `120` → `180`.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md:274` — update the t2690 doc line ("< 5% (250/5000)") to reflect the new default.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/settings.md:34` — update the default column for `supervisor.pulse_interval_seconds`.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/configuration.md:108,417` — update "every 2 minutes" prose and table default.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md:17` — "Pulse cycle (every 2 min)" → "Pulse cycle (every 3 min, configurable)".
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/planning-detail.md:25` — "Phase 0 picks these up every 2 minutes" → "every 3 minutes" or remove the time stamp (it's now a soft default).

### Reference patterns

- Model the macOS launchd interval wiring on the existing Linux path at `setup-modules/schedulers.sh:336-337` (`_pulse_interval_sec=$(_read_pulse_interval_seconds)`). The plist generator function takes the value as an argument and substitutes it into the heredoc the same way `${pulse_label}` is substituted today.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh`
- `setup-modules/schedulers.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `.agents/reference/settings.md`
- `.agents/reference/configuration.md`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`
- `.agents/reference/planning-detail.md`
- `todo/tasks/t2744-brief.md`
- `TODO.md`

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Lint the changed shell files
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh \
           .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh \
           .agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh \
           setup-modules/schedulers.sh

# 2. Confirm circuit breaker still trips correctly with new default (no env override)
unset AIDEVOPS_PULSE_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD
.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh status
# Expect: status line showing threshold=1500 (30% of 5000)

# 3. Run the existing circuit-breaker tests — they pass explicit thresholds
.agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh

# 4. Run the REST fallback tests
.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-issue-read-rest-fallback.sh

# 5. Confirm settings validation still accepts 180 in the existing range [30,3600]
.agents/scripts/settings-helper.sh validate

# 6. Smoke-test setup.sh dry-run (don't actually reload launchd)
```

title: t2745: Add pre-push guard to catch duplicate TODO entries from issue-sync orphan seed
body:
## Task

`_seed_orphan_todo_line` in `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh:1608` seeds a minimal TODO entry at the bottom of `TODO.md` when an orphan issue is detected. Its idempotency check at line 1618 only inspects `TODO.md` on `main` — it has no visibility into open planning PRs that add a rich TODO entry for the same task. When a planning PR eventually merges (or when a feature branch rebases), both entries coexist in `TODO.md` because they live at different line numbers and produce no merge conflict.

## Why

Concrete evidence from today's session (2026-04-22):

- Issue filed: `#20480` (t2743, REST fallback zsh compat fix) at 18:34 UTC via `gh api repos/.../issues POST` (direct, bypassing `gh_create_issue` due to the t2743 bug itself).
- `issue-sync.yml` detected the orphan and ran `_seed_orphan_todo_line`, appending `- [ ] t2743 Fix shared-gh-wrappers REST fallback to work in zsh (drops labels+assignees silently) #auto-dispatch #framework ref:GH#20480` as the last non-empty line in `TODO.md` (commit `70bc9e61b chore: sync ref:GH#20480 to TODO.md [skip ci]`).
- Meanwhile the feature branch `feature/t2743-rest-fallback-zsh-compat` added a rich 400-char entry near line 104 inside `## Ready` as part of planning PR #20481.
- On `git rebase main` at 19:34 UTC, both entries ended up in the file — no conflict because they were at different line numbers.
- `grep -c "^- \[.\] t2743" TODO.md` returned `2` instead of `1`.
- Same pattern hit t2742/#20478 earlier the same hour.

Impact:

- **Silent TODO.md duplicates.** Two entries for one task, only detectable via manual grep or by a reader noticing both.
- **Dispatch confusion surface.** Minimal entry has thin tags (`#auto-dispatch #framework`) while rich entry has full context (`#bugfix #framework #auto-dispatch #worker ~2h tier:standard` + file references + brief link). If the minimal entry survives the manual cleanup, the worker loses the rich context.
- **Workflow-dependent, not user-error.** The framework's own `claim-task-id.sh --create-issue` → planning-PR workflow triggers this pattern. Even with t2743 fixed (so `gh_create_issue` works), the race between issue-sync seeding and the planning PR merging persists.
- **Storable in memory but not systemically enforced.** Session memory stored (`mem_20260422193418_6b773cb1`), but memory recall is probabilistic — the next session may not query for it before pushing.

Follow-up to **t2698 (#20327, MERGED)** which introduced `_seed_orphan_todo_line` with forward-only idempotency (checks main, cannot see planning PRs).

## What

One of two fix options — option (A) is the recommended pre-push guard approach (cheaper, catches at the right moment, no network calls); option (B) is the seeding-side solution (more robust but higher network cost).

### Option A (RECOMMENDED): Pre-push guard for duplicate task IDs

Add a new pre-push check to the existing `install-pre-push-guards.sh` framework (alongside privacy, complexity, scope guards) that greps the pushed `TODO.md` for duplicate `^- \[.\] tNNN ` entries. Blocks the push with a clear error message pointing at the duplicate lines; suggests the `grep -c` self-check and manual removal.

- `.agents/hooks/pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` (NEW): extracts all `tNNN` task IDs from `TODO.md` on the branch being pushed, counts occurrences of each, exits 1 if any count > 1.
- `.agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh` (EDIT): register the new guard alongside privacy/complexity/scope. Default: enabled. Bypass: `git push --no-verify` OR `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_DUP_TODO_GUARD=1`.
- Existing pattern: `.agents/hooks/pre-push-privacy.sh`, `.agents/hooks/pre-push-complexity.sh`, `.agents/hooks/pre-push-scope.sh` — model on any of these for structure.

### Option B: `_seed_orphan_todo_line` queries open PRs before seeding

Before appending a minimal entry, query open PRs in the repo for any that touch `TODO.md` and contain `ref:GH#NNN` in the diff. If any match, skip the seed and log "ORPHAN has planning PR #NNN in flight — skipping seed".

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh:1608` `_seed_orphan_todo_line` (EDIT): insert query before line 1642 append.
- Implementation: `gh pr list --repo "$slug" --state open --search "ref:GH#${num} in:TODO.md" --json number --jq '.[]|.number' | head -1` — single REST call per orphan.
- Downside: extra API call per orphan check (issue-sync runs frequently). With ~2-10 orphans per cycle and GraphQL rate limits already tight (hit 0/5000 multiple times this week), this adds meaningful pressure.

### Recommendation

Ship **Option A only** as t2745. It catches the problem at the right moment (at push, when the user can fix it immediately), adds no network cost, and matches the existing pre-push-guard pattern. Option B is a defensible follow-up but not urgent given (A) catches the symptom deterministically.

Do NOT do both in one PR — A is a local/client-side guard, B is a server-side/GitHub-Actions change. They serve different layers.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/hooks/pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` — new hook script
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh` — register the new guard in the install/list/status paths
- **EDIT**: `.agents/reference/pre-push-guards.md` — document the new guard with bypass env var
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` — fixture test

### Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/hooks/pre-push-privacy.sh` — similar scope (single-file, one-check, one failure mode, clear error message). Model the install registration on how the three existing guards are registered in `install-pre-push-guards.sh` (search for `privacy`, `complexity`, `scope` in that file to find the three canonical registration points: install, list, status).

### Test fixtures

Create `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` with at minimum:

1. **Clean TODO.md** (no duplicates) → exit 0.
2. **Single duplicate** (`t2743` appears twice) → exit 1, error message cites line numbers.
3. **Multiple duplicates** (`t2743` AND `t2742` both duplicated) → exit 1, error message cites both.
4. **Completed + open pair** (`- [x] t2743 ...` + `- [ ] t2743 ...`) → exit 1 (must not silently allow the completed/open pair — it's still a duplicate that confuses scanners).
5. **Pseudo-duplicate** (`- [ ] t2743 ...` + `tests for t2743 ref:GH#...` where the second line is a different task mentioning t2743 in description) → exit 0 (the regex must be anchored to the checkbox-and-task-id pattern: `^- \[.\] tNNN `).
6. **Bypass env var** (`AIDEVOPS_SKIP_DUP_TODO_GUARD=1`) → exit 0 even with duplicates, with a warning logged to stderr.
7. **`--no-verify` path** (via the git hook wrapper, not the script directly) → bypassed, no warning (this is git's own bypass).

### Cross-platform requirements

- POSIX-only regex (no `\s`, no `[[:<:]]`, no `\b` — use `[[:space:]]`, `[^[:alnum:]]`).
- Bash 3.2 compatible (no `read -a`, no `mapfile`, no `[[ =~ ]]` without string-var indirection where needed).
- Must work on macOS BSD grep and GNU grep.

### Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/hooks/pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` — zero violations.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` — all 7 fixtures pass.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh` — zero violations (regression check).
- Manual: create a test branch with duplicate `t9999` entries in TODO.md, attempt `git push`, verify the hook blocks and emits the duplicate line numbers.
- Verify bypass: repeat with `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_DUP_TODO_GUARD=1 git push` — should succeed with stderr warning.

### Files Scope

- .agents/hooks/pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh
- .agents/scripts/install-pre-push-guards.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh
- .agents/reference/pre-push-guards.md

## Acceptance

1. Hook `pre-push-dup-todo-guard.sh` exists, shellcheck clean, POSIX-portable.
2. Hook blocks `git push` when pushed `TODO.md` contains two or more `^- \[.\] tNNN ` lines with the same `tNNN`.
3. Hook reports the offending task ID(s) AND the line numbers where duplicates appear.
4. Hook is bypassable via `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_DUP_TODO_GUARD=1` and `git push --no-verify`.
5. `install-pre-push-guards.sh install|list|status` each surface the new guard consistently with the three existing guards.
6. All 7 test fixtures pass.
7. `reference/pre-push-guards.md` documents the new guard including bypass paths.

## Session Origin

Discovered during interactive session 2026-04-22 while rebasing PR #20481 (t2743 planning) against `main`. The rebase pulled in `70bc9e61b chore: sync ref:GH#20480 to TODO.md [skip ci]` from issue-sync.yml's orphan seeding, producing a second `- [ ] t2743 ...` entry at the file bottom. Manual grep + removal was needed post-rebase. Same pattern hit t2742/#20478 earlier in the same session (both caught and cleaned up, but only because the session was alert to the pattern after the first occurrence).

title: shared-gh-wrappers.sh: gh_create_pr fails silently without shared-constants.sh sourced
body:
## Task

Make `gh_create_pr` (and the other wrappers in `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`) sourcing-safe — i.e., they should not silently fail with "command not found: print_info" when `shared-constants.sh` was not also sourced.

## Why

During t2744 (PR #20483 creation), I attempted to use `gh_create_pr` after sourcing only `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. The function failed silently because it depends on `print_info` (defined in `shared-constants.sh`) without auto-sourcing or guarding the dependency. The wrapper exited with a cryptic "print_info: command not found" stderr that was easy to miss in pipelined output.

Concrete impact: I had to fall back to raw `gh pr create`, which created a PR WITHOUT `origin:interactive`. Then I had to apply the label via `gh pr edit --add-label`, which (combined with the maintainer-gate `labeled`-trigger gap — separate issue) left the PR in a broken gate state.

This is a foot-gun for any caller that sources `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` standalone. The framework's "use the wrappers" rule (PROMPTS.md "Origin labelling MANDATORY") is undermined by the wrappers being unusable without ceremony.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` — add a guarded auto-source of `shared-constants.sh` near the top of the file, OR define minimal `print_*` fallbacks if the canonical functions aren't available.

### Reference pattern

Two options:

**Option A — auto-source guard (preferred for symmetry):**

```bash
# Top of shared-gh-wrappers.sh, after SPDX header
if ! declare -F print_info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _gh_wrappers_dir="${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  source "${_gh_wrappers_dir}/shared-constants.sh"
fi
```

**Option B — inline minimal fallbacks (preferred if shared-constants is heavy):**

Model on the pattern documented in `prompts/build.txt` "Quality Standards" §Shell helpers:

```bash
[[ -z "${RED+x}" ]] && RED=''
# ... etc for each color
print_info()  { printf '[INFO] %s\n'  "$*"; }
print_warn()  { printf '[WARN] %s\n'  "$*" >&2; }
print_error() { printf '[ERROR] %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
```

Wrap each fallback in `declare -F print_X >/dev/null 2>&1 ||` so callers that DID source shared-constants.sh first keep their canonical implementations.

### Verification

- New test under `.agents/scripts/tests/`: source ONLY `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` in a clean shell, call `gh_create_pr --help` (or a dry-run path), assert no "command not found" stderr.
- Existing tests still pass (sourcing both files should not double-define).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` is usable when sourced standalone (no canonical-shell-source ceremony)
- [ ] All `print_*` calls inside the file resolve without depending on caller's sourcing order
- [ ] Test added asserting standalone sourcing works
- [ ] `shellcheck shared-gh-wrappers.sh` clean
- [ ] Existing wrappers (`gh_create_issue`, `gh_create_pr`, `gh_issue_comment`, `gh_pr_comment`, `gh_issue_edit_safe`, `set_issue_status`) all still pass their existing tests

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`

title: pulse: suppress 'fatal: ambiguous argument origin/main' errors via default-branch detection
body:
## Task

Suppress / guard the `fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/main': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.` errors emitted by `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` (and likely `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh`) when operating on repos that lack a fetched `origin/main` ref or use a different default branch (`master`, `develop`, etc.).

## Why

Observed 33 occurrences of this error in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` over a single recent window (lines 48787-49231 of a 49000-line log = last ~5% of log). The errors are noise — they don't crash the pulse — but:

1. They mask real errors during log review (signal-to-noise degradation).
2. They suggest the fast-forward step is silently failing for affected repos, meaning those repos may stay on stale `main` instead of fast-forwarding as intended (defeats the purpose of `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh`).
3. Each failed `git rev-parse origin/main` is a wasted git invocation per pulse cycle per affected repo.

Repositories likely affected: any repo where `git fetch origin` hasn't been run recently, OR repos on a non-`main` default branch (some legacy WordPress plugins on `master`, etc.).

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` — replace hardcoded `origin/main` with detected default branch
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` — same (lines 255-637 reference `origin/main` ~10 times)

### Reference pattern

Use `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` to detect the actual default branch. Guard with existence check:

```bash
_get_default_branch() {
  local repo_path="$1"
  local default_ref
  # Try to read remote HEAD symbolic ref
  default_ref=$(git -C "$repo_path" symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "${default_ref#origin/}"
}
```

Then use:

```bash
local default_branch
default_branch=$(_get_default_branch "$repo_path") || {
  # Fallback: skip this repo with a single-line debug log instead of fatal stderr
  print_debug "Skipping ${repo_path}: no origin/HEAD set, run 'git remote set-head origin --auto'"
  return 0
}
local base_ref="origin/${default_branch}"
```

Alternatively, pre-fetch and verify before the rebase:

```bash
git -C "$repo_path" fetch --quiet origin "${default_branch}:refs/remotes/origin/${default_branch}" 2>/dev/null
git -C "$repo_path" rev-parse "origin/${default_branch}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
```

### Verification

- Run pulse cycle against a repo with `origin/master` (or no `origin/HEAD`) and observe NO `fatal: ambiguous argument` errors in the log.
- For a repo with a healthy `origin/main`, behavior is unchanged.
- New test under `.agents/scripts/tests/`: simulate both scenarios, assert no `fatal:` lines in stderr.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh` no longer emits `fatal: ambiguous argument` for repos without `origin/main`
- [ ] `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` similarly guarded
- [ ] Default-branch detection works for repos on `main`, `master`, `develop`, or other non-standard branches
- [ ] Test added covering both scenarios
- [ ] Full pulse cycle produces no `fatal: ambiguous argument` output for any of the 14 pulse-enabled repos

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-maintenance.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-default-branch-detection.sh`

## Task

Add `actionlint` (and optionally `yamllint`) checks for `.github/workflows/*.yml` to the pre-commit hook chain. Goal: catch YAML parse errors and workflow misconfigurations BEFORE they ship and silently break framework-wide gates.

On 2026-04-21 (PR #20311 / t2691), a one-extra-leading-space whitespace regression in `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate.yml` (lines 807-875) silently broke the Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate framework-wide. Symptoms:

- GitHub recorded "phantom" workflow runs on `push` events with `conclusion=failure` and zero jobs.
- The required `Maintainer Review & Assignee Gate` check NEVER posted to ANY commit.
- Every PR (worker and interactive) was stuck at `mergeable_state: blocked`.
- Invisible in the Actions UI — phantom failures look identical to "no run yet" to a casual glance.
- Detected only after t2744 PR #20483 mysteriously could not get its required check, requiring manual diagnosis with `python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)'` to find the parse error.

A pre-commit `actionlint` check would have flagged the indentation mismatch instantly during `t2691` work, preventing ~24 hours of framework-wide degradation.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh` (or wherever pre-commit hook installation logic lives — verify with `grep -l "pre-commit" .agents/scripts/install*.sh`)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` — add the actionlint check
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/lint-workflows-helper.sh` — wraps `actionlint` invocation, handles missing-binary case (degrade to `python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)'`)

### Implementation notes

1. Detect changed `.github/workflows/*.yml` files in staged set.
2. If any, run `actionlint` (or `python3 -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(f))'` fallback).
3. Block commit on errors with mentor-style message pointing to `.github/workflows/<file>:N`.
4. Allow bypass via `--no-verify` (standard pre-commit convention).
5. Skip if no workflow files changed (don't lint full directory on unrelated commits).

- Stage a valid workflow file edit → commit succeeds.
- Stage a non-workflow file → no actionlint invocation.

title: review-bot-gate: CI workflow duplicates helper logic and was not migrated by PR #19309 (t2139 settlement check bypassed at branch-protection layer)
body:
## Description

The t2139 fix (PR #19309, merged 2026-04-16) added a settlement check to `bot_has_real_review()` in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`, intended to defeat CodeRabbit's two-phase placeholder-then-edit posting pattern. The fix updated the helper and its in-agent callers (`pulse-merge.sh`, `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, etc.), but did NOT update `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml`, which contains its own independent inline implementation of the gate logic. The CI workflow was added before the helper existed (PR #2739, 2026-03-02) and has never been refactored to call the helper. PR #19309 therefore fixes the in-agent merge path but leaves the GitHub-enforced branch-protection gate entirely unfixed.

## Expected Behaviour

The `review-bot-gate` CI check should apply the same settlement logic as the helper — reject a PR for merge while any known review bot has an unsettled comment. Whether this is accomplished by calling the helper directly or by porting its logic inline, the two code paths should not diverge.

## Reproducer

**Symptom**: on a PR in a managed private repo, opened 2026-04-22, `origin:interactive` + OWNER author:

| T | Event |
|---|-------|
| T+0 (18:48:49Z) | PR opens |
| T+11s (18:49:00Z) | CodeRabbit posts Phase 1 placeholder comment |
| T+26s (18:49:15Z) | CI `review-bot-gate` job starts |
| T+34s (18:49:23Z) | CI `review-bot-gate` passes (8s total; no settlement awareness) |
| T+3m36s (18:52:25Z) | PR auto-merged via `origin:interactive` path |
| T+5m47s (18:54:36Z) | CodeRabbit edits placeholder with "Review failed — closed during review" |
| T+7m46s (18:56:35Z) | Gemini posts review — 4 minutes after merge |

CodeRabbit never completed its review. The review-feedback pipeline (t2093, t2123, t2139) received no signal because no review ever existed to signal about. A CodeRabbit rate-limit slot was consumed for zero reviewable output.

**Causal code**: `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml` lines 89-96 (inline `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` — note old variable name, pre-t2139) and lines 150-271 (inline `bot_has_real_review()` that duplicates helper logic without the settlement check added in t2139).

**Upstream commit history** (`.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml`):

```text
2026-04-08  7b227cf  GH#17671: remove unauthorized external code...
2026-03-21  c7081c5  fix: remove job name field...
2026-03-09  fe7054f  GH#4002: Fix OpenCode AI Agent and Review Bot Gate workflows...
2026-03-08  3286d3c  fix: add rate-limit grace period...
2026-03-07  cad8b10  fix: pin all GitHub Actions to SHA...
2026-03-06  d8e5b54  t1410: fix review-bot-gate status fallback...
2026-03-06  8caf94a  fix: review-bot-gate falls back to SUCCESS...
2026-03-06  265d36f  fix: review-bot-gate distinguishes rate-limit...
2026-03-06  3540dc8  fix: resolve CI check failures...
2026-03-02  2b9a32f  feat: enforce review bot gate before PR merge (t1382)
```

Last touch: 2026-04-08, 8 days before the t2139 helper fix. No t2139 touch on this file.

## Why this matters

Many users rely on the `review-bot-gate` CI check as a required status check in branch protection — that's the enforcement path the workflow was explicitly designed for ("To enforce: add 'review-bot-gate' as a required status check in GitHub branch protection settings for each repo", comment block at top of workflow). When the CI check runs its stale inline logic, it passes within ~8 seconds regardless of whether CodeRabbit has finished reviewing. Branch protection then permits the merge, and `pulse-merge.sh`'s subsequent helper call — which DOES have the t2139 settlement check — can still be defeated by the bug documented in the sibling issue (See-also). The net effect: on many auto-merge paths the entire CodeRabbit review is raced, and the review-feedback pipeline the framework was designed around never gets signal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.8.94 (current latest with t2139 fix)
2. Ensure `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml` from any aidevops-installed repo is present (same as upstream)
3. Configure CodeRabbit on the repo
4. Open a PR that CodeRabbit will review (any non-trivial code change)
5. Observe: CI `review-bot-gate` passes in 5-10 seconds; does not wait for CodeRabbit completion
6. If the PR qualifies for auto-merge (`origin:interactive` + OWNER, or other auto-merge path), the merge fires before CodeRabbit finishes; CodeRabbit posts "Review failed — Pull request was closed or merged during review" after the fact

## Considerations for the maintainer(s)

Architectural question with several viable paths — each with different second-order effects:

### Option A: Refactor workflow to call the helper via `wait` subcommand

```yaml
- run: bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh wait "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" "${{ github.repository }}"
```

**Pros**: single implementation; future helper fixes propagate to CI automatically; preserves poll-with-timeout semantics.

**Cons**: GitHub-hosted runners don't have `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` — the helper must be fetched or vendored into the repo. Possible via `actions/checkout` of marcusquinn/aidevops, or a lightweight install step. Either approach couples the workflow to framework availability and adds per-run cost.

### Option B: Refactor workflow to call helper via `check`, re-triggered by events

Event-driven re-runs: workflow triggers on `pull_request`, `issue_comment` (`created`, `edited`, `deleted`), `pull_request_review`. Each run makes one helper `check` call, exits with non-zero on WAITING (failure) or zero on PASS. Branch protection blocks merge until a subsequent event triggers a passing run.

**Pros**: simpler per-run; respects GitHub's event model; no polling.

**Cons**: users see `review-bot-gate` in FAILED state (red X) for the entire active-review window — functionally correct but confusing UX. Depends on event coverage being complete (does CodeRabbit's placeholder edit reliably trigger `issue_comment.edited`? Empirical testing needed).

### Option C: Port the settlement logic into the workflow inline

Duplicate `_comment_is_settled` + `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` into the workflow YAML's inline bash.

**Pros**: no runtime dependency on the framework; self-contained workflow; minimum delta.

**Cons**: continues the duplicate-implementation pattern that caused this bug. Next t2139-class fix faces the same propagation gap.

### Option D: Deprecate the CI workflow in favor of in-agent gating only

Remove the CI workflow; rely on `pulse-merge.sh` + other callers for helper-based enforcement with `--admin` bypass accepted.

**Pros**: no duplication; simplest mental model.

**Cons**: forfeits GitHub-native branch protection enforcement. PRs merged via `gh pr merge` from a developer's terminal (outside the pulse) no longer hit the gate. External contributors and manual maintainer merges lose the signal.

### Propagation mechanism (separate question)

Whichever option is chosen: **how should workflow updates reach existing repos?** `aidevops update` updates `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` but does NOT push files into `.github/workflows/` of any repo. Users who installed the workflow months ago carry stale inline logic even after `aidevops update` (my local copy in one managed private repo dates to 2026-02-10). An `aidevops workflow-sync` subcommand, or a pulse routine that checks upstream workflow versions and PRs updates into user repos, may be a necessary complement to whichever option above is chosen.

## Relationship to sibling issue

Paired with #20494 (Layer 2 — the settlement-check semantic bug in `_comment_is_settled`). Both failures occurred on the same private PR (timeline above):

- Layer 1 (this issue) failed first — CI check passed without settlement awareness at T+26s.
- Layer 2 (sibling) failed second — pulse-merge's direct helper call at T+3m36s also incorrectly classified the 205s-old unedited placeholder as "settled by age".

Both gates must agree before merge proceeds, so fixing either layer alone prevents the observed failure mode for `pulse-merge` admin-bypass paths. However:

- Layer 1 must be fixed for branch-protection-enforced non-admin paths (external contributors, manual merges).
- Layer 2 must be fixed for code paths that call the helper directly without a CI-status pre-check (e.g., `pr-loop.md`, future callers) and for diagnostic UX — Option B above leaves CI in FAILED state during the entire active-review window, which a correct Layer 2 would shorten.

Ideal resolution: address both. Prioritize Layer 1 for the architectural win; Layer 2 for semantic correctness.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.94
- **Latest version**: 3.8.94
- **Install method**: unknown (/home/rob/.local/bin/aidevops)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

## Additional Context

Related prior issues:
- #19251 (CLOSED) — bug report that triggered t2139 fix
- #19173 (CLOSED) — earlier discussion of review-feedback gap class
- #19309 (MERGED) — the t2139 fix (covered helper, not workflow)
- #19339 (CLOSED) — review-followup on t2139 PR

See-also: #20494 (Layer 2 — `_comment_is_settled` semantic bug)

title: review-bot-gate-helper: _comment_is_settled edit-criterion rejects fast legitimate edits; 30s default miscalibrated for CodeRabbit long-tail latency
body:
## Description

The t2139 settlement-check logic in `_comment_is_settled` (`.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:204-232`) has two independent semantic issues surfaced by real-world CodeRabbit behaviour:

1. **Edit criterion requires `edit_delta >= min_lag`** — a legitimate real-review edit that lands *before* the minimum-lag threshold is rejected. When `min_lag` is tuned up to cover CodeRabbit's long-tail latency (e.g., 600-900s), a CodeRabbit edit that lands quickly (T+180s) is explicitly classified as "not settled" even though the comment body IS the final review.

2. **Default `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS=30`** is far below the real distribution of CodeRabbit's edit latencies (empirical: 2s to 18+ minutes). A 30s threshold catches short non-review notices (walkthrough-skipped, rate-limit notices) but systematically allows "aged-in" unedited placeholders to be falsely classified as settled real reviews.

Together, these cause `bot_has_real_review` to false-positive on CodeRabbit Phase 1 placeholders that have aged past 30s but haven't yet been edited with Phase 2 real review content.

## Expected Behaviour

Given CodeRabbit's two-phase posting pattern (Phase 1 placeholder at ~T+15s → Phase 2 edit with real review content at variable T+X), `_comment_is_settled` should correctly classify comment state such that `bot_has_real_review` returns `true` only when real review content is actually present:

- The moment a real-review edit lands, the comment's body IS the final review — should be classified as settled immediately, regardless of how quickly the edit came.
- An unedited placeholder should not be promoted to "real review" status by aging alone, because its body is not review content.

## Reproducer

**Symptom**: same observation event as sibling issue (#20493 — Layer 1). On a PR in a managed private repo, 2026-04-22.

At pulse-merge decision time (T+3m36s after PR open), `bot_has_real_review("coderabbitai", <repo>, <pr>)` evaluated:

```text
CodeRabbit comment:
  created_at:  2026-04-22T18:49:00Z
  updated_at:  2026-04-22T18:49:00Z  (unedited at this point)
  body:        Phase 1 placeholder content (no "Review failed" yet)
  age at check: 205 seconds
  edit_delta:   0
  min_lag:     30 (default)

_comment_is_settled:
  (a) edit_delta (0) >= min_lag (30)?  NO
  (b) age (205)     >= min_lag (30)?  YES → settled

is_non_review_comment(body)?
  NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS match on placeholder body? NO
  (none of "Review failed", "Review skipped", "closed or merged during review",
   "Auto reviews are limited", or rate-limit variants match pre-edit placeholder)

bot_has_real_review: RETURNS TRUE → merge allowed → race condition fires
```

**Causal code**: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:204-232`:

```bash
_comment_is_settled() {
  # A comment is "settled" if EITHER:
  #   (a) it has been edited (updated_at >= created_at + min_lag), OR
  #   (b) it is old enough that the bot would have edited by now
  #       (now - created_at >= min_lag).
  ...
  if [[ "$edit_delta" -ge "$min_lag" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "$age" -ge "$min_lag" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}
```

Introduced in PR #19309 (t2139).

### Empirical data — CodeRabbit edit-delta distribution

Collected from 15 recent PRs on marcusquinn/aidevops (public repo, 2026-04-22):

| `edit_delta` | count | fraction | likely semantics |
|--------------|-------|----------|-----------------|
| < 30s | 10 | 67% | non-review notices (skipped, rate-limit, trivial) |
| 1-5 min | 2 | 13% | short real reviews |
| 7-18 min | 3 | 20% | deep real reviews |

The 30s default correctly catches the first bucket but systematically misclassifies the ~33% of real reviews that exceed 30s. Those real reviews either:
- Arrive as edits where `edit_delta >= 30s` — classified settled via edit (correct).
- Are preceded by an unedited placeholder aging past 30s — classified settled via age **before** the edit lands (the actual failure mode).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.8.94 with the t2139 fix.
2. Configure a repo with CodeRabbit enabled.
3. Open a PR that will trigger CodeRabbit review; note creation time (T+0).
4. Wait ~35s past CodeRabbit's Phase 1 placeholder post (typically T+45-60s total).
5. Before CodeRabbit's edit lands (typically T+1min-18min), run:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh check $PR $OWNER/$REPO
   ```

6. Observe: returns `PASS` despite CodeRabbit not having completed its review. The placeholder body is treated as a real review because it has aged past 30s without matching any `NON_REVIEW_PATTERN`.

## Considerations for the maintainer(s)

### Option A: Recognize Phase 1 placeholder body content

Add distinctive CodeRabbit Phase 1 placeholder patterns to `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` (or a separate `PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS` list). An unedited placeholder's body would then be recognized as "not a real review" regardless of age. Real review registers only after the edit changes the body.

**Pros**: semantically correct — detects what CodeRabbit is actually saying. Works regardless of timing.

**Cons**: requires empirically collecting and maintaining placeholder body patterns. CodeRabbit's exact placeholder text may change. Per-bot placeholder patterns needed (each bot has its own Phase 1 text).

### Option B: Relax the edit criterion — any edit means settled

Remove the `edit_delta >= min_lag` requirement. Any edit (regardless of delta) is treated as "comment reached final form" — the delta check was a safety net against flapping, but flapping isn't a real pattern for review bots.

```bash
if [[ "$updated_epoch" -gt "$created_epoch" ]]; then
  return 0   # edited at all → settled
fi
if [[ "$age" -ge "$min_lag" ]]; then
  return 0   # never edited but aged-in → settled
fi
return 1
```

**Pros**: one-line change. Trusts the bot's edit as authoritative.

**Cons**: doesn't fix the aged-in-unedited-placeholder false positive. The 30s default still lets unedited placeholders get promoted.

### Option C: Raise default `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS`

Increase the default from 30s to 600-900s (10-15 min) to cover CodeRabbit's 95th-percentile review duration.

**Pros**: minimum code delta. Tunes the existing knob to observed distribution.

**Cons**: 10-15 min merge delays on every CodeRabbit-reviewed PR. Still a threshold, still fragile against future latency drift. Doesn't address the edit-criterion semantic issue in Option B.

### Option D: Per-bot defaults in the helper

Make `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS` bot-aware with baked-in defaults (`coderabbitai=900, gemini-code-assist=120, copilot=60`), still user-overridable via `review_gate.tools.<bot>.min_edit_lag_seconds` in `repos.json`.

**Pros**: calibrates to each bot's empirical reality without user config burden.

**Cons**: maintenance of the bot-default table as bots evolve. Adds complexity to `_get_min_edit_lag` resolution order.

### Option E (recommended reading): Combine A + B

Phase 1 placeholder body recognition (A) + relaxed edit criterion (B):

- Unedited placeholder body matches PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS → classified as "non-review" → `bot_has_real_review` waits for edit.
- Edited comment → any edit counts as settled → body checked; real review → PASS; "Review failed" etc. → non-review.
- Age criterion becomes a fallback safety net for unforeseen states.

**Pros**: semantically robust; independent of `min_lag` tuning.

**Cons**: most change surface area; per-bot placeholder-pattern maintenance.

### Second-order effects to consider

- **Cycle time**: any solution that slows merges affects auto-merge cycle time for ALL `origin:interactive` + OWNER PRs, not just CodeRabbit-reviewed ones. Raising `min_lag` globally decreases worker productivity measurably.
- **Bot-evolution maintenance**: solutions with per-bot patterns introduce maintenance burden when bot behaviour changes (new bots, CodeRabbit placeholder redesign, etc.).
- **Layer interaction**: if Layer 1 (sibling #20493) is fixed first, Layer 2's false positive is masked by the CI-check gate — but only for paths that respect CI status. `pulse-merge.sh` does. `pr-loop.md` does not necessarily.
- **`wait` subcommand inheritance**: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` uses `review-bot-gate-helper.sh wait` (polls every 60s for up to 10 min). `wait` calls the same `check` logic → inherits Layer 2's bug. This is where the 30s default most directly causes workers to merge prematurely, independent of Layer 1.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.94
- **Latest version**: 3.8.94
- **Install method**: unknown (/home/rob/.local/bin/aidevops)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

## Additional Context

Related prior issues:
- #19251 (CLOSED) — original bug that triggered t2139
- #19309 (MERGED) — the t2139 fix; introduced `_comment_is_settled` and the 30s default
- #19339 (CLOSED) — review-followup on t2139 PR

See-also: #20493 (Layer 1 — architectural, CI workflow not migrated)
