title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20478 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20478

**Parent issue:** #20478 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2742: Fix string-literal ratchet regex false positive on adjacent quoted shell arguments
**Parent labels:** `auto-dispatch,origin:interactive,tier:standard,framework,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20478. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20478 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20478:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20478 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20478 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20478 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20478 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20478** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Session Origin

Surfaced during t2738 implementation (PR #20474) in an interactive session. The helper-extraction refactor added three `local tid="$1" repo="$2"` style declarations to `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, which tripped the string-literal ratchet in `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`. The refactor had to split every multi-var `local` into separate lines — a workaround, not a fix. The pattern itself is idiomatic shell and appears pre-existing in at least one location (line 1066 of the same file: `local op="$1" repo="$2" number="$3"`). The ratchet will keep catching legitimate patterns until the root cause in the extraction regex is addressed.

Follow-up to **#19739 (t2230)**, which converted the validators to ratchet-style (absolute-count → delta-count) and is CLOSED / `status:done`. t2230 reduced the blast radius (only NEW repeats block) but did not fix the underlying regex logic. This issue fixes the regex.

## What

Fix the false-positive class in `_count_repeated_literals` (`.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:270-280`) and its display companion `_show_repeated_literals` (`:283-293`) so the `"[^"]{4,}"` capture does not misinterpret the span between two adjacent shell-quoted arguments as a string literal.

## Why

The regex `"[^"]{4,}"` knows nothing about shell syntax. When a line contains two quoted var-refs separated by whitespace — a standard shell idiom:

```bash
local tid="$1" repo="$2"
```

— the regex captures `" repo="` as a 6-char "literal" using the `"` at the end of `"$1"` and the `"` at the start of `"$2"` as the outer quotes. The existing exclusion filter `grep -vE '^"\$'` only rejects literals that START with `"$` (direct var-refs like `"$agent_name"`). It cannot reject inter-argument spans, because the captured "literal" starts with whitespace, not `$`.

**Impact:**

- Punishes the idiomatic `local a="$1" b="$2" c="$3"` pattern (common for multi-param helpers and `while-case` arg parsers)
- Crosses the `≥3 occurrences` ratchet threshold quickly — any file that introduces 3-4 new helper signatures with this shape trips it
- Forces workaround patches that split every `local` declaration into single-var lines — bloats helper prologues and adds no information
- Affects WRITE-TIME enforcement (pre-commit-hook.sh runs on `git commit`), so every developer hits it on every multi-param helper they write
- Also affects the empty-init variant: `local title="" repo="" body=""` captures ` repo=` and ` body=` as spurious literals (noted in memory record from 2026-04-21 covering PR #20255)

**Confirmed in the wild** — PR #20474, commits `9de0fa355` → `1c128d3eb`:

```
[ERROR] NEW repeated string literals in .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh (new: 1, pre-existing: 3)
  4x: "
  4x: "interactive"
  5x: "true"
```

(The `4x: "` display is the `" repo="` literal truncated by the display pipeline — the captured string includes leading whitespace that breaks column alignment. Also a minor issue worth fixing.)

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` lines 270-293 — fix `_count_repeated_literals` and `_show_repeated_literals`
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` — regression test fixtures
- **EDIT** (optional, same PR): `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:274,287` — replace `grep -v '^\s*#'` with POSIX `grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#'` (see cross-platform section)

### Recommended approach: pre-strip shell-syntax tokens before the extraction regex

The fundamental issue is that `grep -oE '"[^"]{4,}"'` counts `"` characters without understanding shell argument-quoting. The most robust portable fix is to eliminate shell var-ref tokens BEFORE the literal extraction regex runs, so the `"` pairs that remain belong to true string literals.

Insert a `sed` pre-strip pass between the comment-filter and the literal extraction:

```bash
_count_repeated_literals() {
	local _ext_literal='"[^"]{4,}"'
	local _ext_numeric='^"[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*"$'
	local _ext_varref='^"\$'
	grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' |
		sed -E '
			s/"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"//g
			s/"\$\{[^}]*\}"//g
			s/"\$@"//g
			s/"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"//g
		' |
		grep -oE "$_ext_literal" |
		grep -vE "$_ext_numeric" |
		grep -vE "$_ext_varref" |
		sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 >= 3' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
	return 0
}
```

After the sed pre-strip, `local tid="$1" repo="$2"` reduces to `local tid= repo=` — no quote pairs remain, no false-positive literal captured. The existing `_ext_varref` filter stays as a second line of defense.

The four sed substitution patterns cover:

| Pattern | Matches |
|---|---|
| `"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"` | `"$var"`, `"$name"`, `"$_private"` |
| `"\$\{[^}]*\}"` | `"${var}"`, `"${var[0]}"`, `"${var:-default}"`, `"${#var}"` |
| `"\$@"` | special array-expansion token |
| `"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"` | `"$1"`, `"$*"`, `"$#"`, `"$?"`, `"$$"`, `"$!"`, `"$-"` |

Apply the same pre-strip in `_show_repeated_literals` so the display output matches what the counter saw.

### Cross-platform compatibility (MANDATORY)

The validator runs from `pre-commit-hook.sh`, invoked by git during `git commit`. It must work on:

- **macOS** with `/usr/bin/sed` (BSD sed) and `/usr/bin/grep` (BSD grep)
- **Linux** with GNU sed and GNU grep (Ubuntu, Debian, Alpine)
- **bash 3.2** (macOS default) through **bash 5.x** (GNU) — framework auto-upgrades to bash 4+ via Homebrew on macOS per `reference/bash-compat.md`, but pre-commit-hook.sh may run before that upgrade is active

**Verified safe constructs** (used in the recommended fix):

- `sed -E` (ERE mode): supported by both BSD sed (macOS 10.8+) and GNU sed
- Character classes `[A-Za-z0-9_]`: POSIX, works on both grep flavors
- Anchors `^`, `$`: POSIX
- `[[:space:]]`, `[[:alpha:]]`: POSIX character classes
- `{N,}` interval quantifier in ERE: both flavors when invoked with `-E`

**Forbidden constructs** (will break on at least one platform):

- `sed -i` without backup-extension argument: GNU accepts `sed -i 'script' file`, BSD requires `sed -i '' 'script' file`. This pipeline reads stdin / writes stdout — `-i` is not used, no conflict, but mention so the worker does not "improve" it into in-place mode.
- `\s`, `\w`, `\b`, `\d`: GNU grep extensions. BSD grep does NOT reliably honour them. The current line `274` uses `grep -v '^\s*#'` — likely a pre-existing cross-platform bug. Verify on a stock macOS shell:

  ```bash
  printf '  # comment\nreal line\n' | /usr/bin/grep -v '^\s*#'
  ```

  If BSD grep does not honour `\s`, the current validator is not actually filtering comment-only lines on macOS. Replace with POSIX `[[:space:]]*`.

- `[[:<:]]` / `[[:>:]]`: BSD word-boundaries, not supported on GNU
- `sed` with `-r` flag for ERE: GNU-specific. Use `-E` (portable to both since BSD sed 10.8 and GNU sed 4.2+)
- Perl-style lookaround `(?=...)` / `(?!...)`: not supported in POSIX ERE on either flavor

**Test on both platforms before merging** — see Verification below.

### Verification

Add a regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` covering these fixtures. Each test feeds a string through `_count_repeated_literals` (sourced from `pre-commit-hook.sh`) and asserts the expected count:

**1. Positive — genuine repeated literal IS caught:**

```bash
local msg="error: invalid input"
echo "error: invalid input" >&2
printf '%s\n' "error: invalid input"
```

Expect: 1 distinct literal at ≥3 count (`"error: invalid input"`).

**2. Negative — inter-argument spans are NOT counted (the bug this issue fixes):**

```bash
local tid="$1" repo="$2"
local body="$1" repo="$2"
local title="" repo="" body=""
local op="$1" repo="$2" number="$3"
```

Expect: 0 distinct literals at ≥3 count. Before fix: 1 (`" repo="`).

**3. Negative — repeated var-refs (already working, regression guard):**

```bash
echo "$var"
echo "$var"
echo "$var"
```

Expect: 0. The existing `^"\$` filter handles this — confirm still works after sed pre-strip.

**4. Negative — numeric-only strings (already working, regression guard):**

```bash
echo "3.14"
echo "3.14"
echo "3.14"
```

Expect: 0.

**5. Negative — `${var}` form inside quotes (new coverage):**

```bash
log "${msg}"
log "${msg}"
log "${msg}"
```

Expect: 0. The `s/"\$\{[^}]*\}"//g` sed pattern must strip this.

**6. Positive — prose literals with $ inside are still caught (boundary case):**

```bash
err="price is \$5.00"
err="price is \$5.00"
err="price is \$5.00"
```

Expect: 1. Escaped `\$` inside a quoted string is NOT a var-ref; must survive the sed pre-strip.

**7. Cross-platform smoke test** — run the test suite on both Linux and macOS:

- **Linux (CI)**: GitHub Actions `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` job runs it automatically if the test is under `.agents/scripts/tests/` (existing pattern)
- **macOS**: Run locally with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`. Also run under `/bin/bash` (v3.2) explicitly, not just Homebrew bash: `/bin/bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`
- **Alpine/BusyBox** (optional but recommended for hermetic verification):

  ```bash
  docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work alpine:3.19 \
    sh -c 'apk add --quiet bash grep sed && bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh'
  ```

  BusyBox sed/grep are stricter POSIX subsets than BSD or GNU — if the test passes on BusyBox, it passes everywhere.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_count_repeated_literals` and `_show_repeated_literals` no longer count the span between adjacent quoted shell-argument tokens as a string literal
- [ ] Regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` exists with all 7 scenarios above (4 negative, 2 positive, 1 boundary) and passes
- [ ] Running the ratchet against the pre-t2738 HEAD of `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` reports the same or FEWER repeated literals post-fix — never more (no new false positives introduced in existing files)
- [ ] Running the ratchet against the post-t2738 HEAD of the same file reports 0 NEW repeats compared to main (the current workaround commit `1c128d3eb` becomes unnecessary but harmless)
- [ ] Pre-existing use of `\s` at `pre-commit-hook.sh:274,287` is either confirmed safe on BSD grep across all supported macOS versions OR replaced with POSIX `[[:space:]]*`
- [ ] Test suite passes on both `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` CI jobs
- [ ] No new shellcheck violations introduced in `pre-commit-hook.sh`

- **Memory records** (from `memory-helper.sh recall`):
  - `2026-04-21` PR #20255 session: documented the empty-init variant `local a="" b="" c=""` tripping the same regex; prescribed split-to-one-per-line workaround. No root-cause fix filed at that time.
  - `2026-04-19` t2230 session: identified two known validator bugs — the `"[^"]{4,}"` var-ref capture (superseded by later `^"\$` filter addition) and warnings incrementing the violation counter. Second bug out of scope for this issue.

  - `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh:55,61` — comments reference "avoid repeated string literals" but use a different mechanism; confirm not vulnerable to the same false positive
  - `.agents/scripts/quality-fix.sh:216` — reports on the same literal counts; may need matching display fix

title: consolidated: Fix string-literal ratchet regex false positive on adjacent quoted shell arguments
body:
_Supersedes #20478 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix the false-positive class in `_count_repeated_literals` (`.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:270-280`) and its display companion `_show_repeated_literals` (`:283-293`) so the `"[^"]{4,}"` capture does not misinterpret the span between two adjacent shell-quoted arguments as a string literal.

Add a regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` covering 7 scenarios (2 positive, 4 negative, 1 boundary case).

## Why

The regex `"[^"]{4,}"` knows nothing about shell syntax. When a line contains two quoted var-refs separated by whitespace — a standard shell idiom:

```bash
local tid="$1" repo="$2"
```

— the regex captures `" repo="` as a 6-char "literal" using the `"` at the end of `"$1"` and the `"` at the start of `"$2"` as the outer quotes. The existing exclusion filter `grep -vE '^"\$'` only rejects literals that START with `"$` (direct var-refs like `"$agent_name"`). It cannot reject inter-argument spans, because the captured "literal" starts with whitespace, not `$`.

**Impact:**

- Punishes the idiomatic `local a="$1" b="$2" c="$3"` pattern (common for multi-param helpers and `while-case` arg parsers)
- Crosses the `≥3 occurrences` ratchet threshold quickly — any file that introduces 3-4 new helper signatures with this shape trips it
- Forces workaround patches that split every `local` declaration into single-var lines — bloats helper prologues and adds no information
- Affects WRITE-TIME enforcement (pre-commit-hook.sh runs on `git commit`), so every developer hits it on every multi-param helper they write
- Also affects the empty-init variant: `local title="" repo="" body=""` captures ` repo=` and ` body=` as spurious literals

**Confirmed in the wild** — PR #20474, commits `9de0fa355` → `1c128d3eb`:

```
[ERROR] NEW repeated string literals in .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh (new: 1, pre-existing: 3)
  4x: "
  4x: "interactive"
  5x: "true"
```

(The `4x: "` display is the `" repo="` literal truncated by the display pipeline — the captured string includes leading whitespace that breaks column alignment. Also a minor display issue worth fixing in `_show_repeated_literals`.)

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` lines 270-293 — fix `_count_repeated_literals` and `_show_repeated_literals`
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` — regression test fixtures
- **EDIT** (optional, same PR): `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh:274,287` — replace `grep -v '^\s*#'` with POSIX `grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#'`

### Recommended approach: pre-strip shell-syntax tokens before the extraction regex

Insert a `sed` pre-strip pass between the comment-filter and the literal extraction:

```bash
_count_repeated_literals() {
	local _ext_literal='"[^"]{4,}"'
	local _ext_numeric='^"[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*"$'
	local _ext_varref='^"\$'
	grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' |
		sed -E '
			s/"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"//g
			s/"\$\{[^}]*\}"//g
			s/"\$@"//g
			s/"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"//g
		' |
		grep -oE "$_ext_literal" |
		grep -vE "$_ext_numeric" |
		grep -vE "$_ext_varref" |
		sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 >= 3' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
	return 0
}
```

After the sed pre-strip, `local tid="$1" repo="$2"` reduces to `local tid= repo=` — no quote pairs remain, no false-positive literal captured.

The four sed substitution patterns cover:

| Pattern | Matches |
|---|---|
| `"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"` | `"$var"`, `"$name"`, `"$_private"` |
| `"\$\{[^}]*\}"` | `"${var}"`, `"${var[0]}"`, `"${var:-default}"`, `"${#var}"` |
| `"\$@"` | special array-expansion token |
| `"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"` | `"$1"`, `"$*"`, `"$#"`, `"$?"`, `"$$"`, `"$!"`, `"$-"` |

Apply the same pre-strip in `_show_repeated_literals` so display output matches what the counter saw.

### Cross-platform compatibility (MANDATORY)

Must work on macOS `/usr/bin/sed` (BSD sed) + `/usr/bin/grep` (BSD grep), Linux GNU sed/grep, and bash 3.2 through bash 5.x.

**Verified safe constructs:**
- `sed -E` (ERE mode): supported by BSD sed (macOS 10.8+) and GNU sed
- `[A-Za-z0-9_]`, `[[:space:]]`, `[[:alpha:]]`: POSIX character classes
- `{N,}` interval quantifier in ERE: both flavors with `-E`

**Forbidden constructs:**
- `\s`, `\w`, `\b`, `\d` in `grep`: GNU grep extensions, not reliable on BSD grep. The current `grep -v '^\s*#'` at line 274 may already be broken on stock macOS — verify and replace with `[[:space:]]*`.
- `sed -i` without backup-extension: BSD requires `sed -i '' 'script' file`
- `[[:<:]]` / `[[:>:]]`: BSD-only word boundaries
- `sed -r`: GNU-specific, use `-E` instead

### Verification

Test fixtures for `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`:

**1. Positive — genuine repeated literal IS caught:**
```bash
local msg="error: invalid input"
echo "error: invalid input" >&2
printf '%s\n' "error: invalid input"
```
Expect: 1 distinct literal at ≥3 count.

**2. Negative — inter-argument spans NOT counted (the bug this issue fixes):**
```bash
local tid="$1" repo="$2"
local body="$1" repo="$2"
local title="" repo="" body=""
local op="$1" repo="$2" number="$3"
```
Expect: 0. Before fix: 1 (`" repo="`).

**3. Negative — repeated var-refs (regression guard):**
```bash
echo "$var"; echo "$var"; echo "$var"
```
Expect: 0.

**4. Negative — numeric-only strings (regression guard):**
```bash
echo "3.14"; echo "3.14"; echo "3.14"
```
Expect: 0.

**5. Negative — `${var}` form inside quotes:**
```bash
log "${msg}"; log "${msg}"; log "${msg}"
```
Expect: 0.

**6. Positive — prose literals with escaped `\$` still caught (boundary case):**
```bash
err="price is \$5.00"; err="price is \$5.00"; err="price is \$5.00"
```
Expect: 1. Escaped `\$` is NOT a var-ref; must survive the sed pre-strip.

**7. Cross-platform smoke test:**
- Linux (CI): GitHub Actions `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` auto-runs tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/`
- macOS: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` AND `/bin/bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` (bash 3.2)
- Alpine (optional): `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work alpine:3.19 sh -c 'apk add --quiet bash grep sed && bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh'`

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_count_repeated_literals` and `_show_repeated_literals` no longer count the span between adjacent quoted shell-argument tokens as a string literal
- [ ] Regression test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-string-literal-ratchet.sh` exists with all 7 scenarios (4 negative, 2 positive, 1 boundary) and passes
- [ ] Running the ratchet against the pre-t2738 HEAD of `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh` reports the same or FEWER repeated literals post-fix — never more
- [ ] Running the ratchet against the post-t2738 HEAD of the same file reports 0 NEW repeats compared to main
- [ ] Pre-existing use of `\s` at `pre-commit-hook.sh:274,287` is either confirmed safe on BSD grep OR replaced with POSIX `[[:space:]]*`
- [ ] Test suite passes on both `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` CI jobs
- [ ] No new shellcheck violations introduced in `pre-commit-hook.sh`

## Context & Decisions

**Session origin:** Surfaced during t2738 implementation (PR #20474) — helper-extraction refactor added `local tid="$1" repo="$2"` style declarations to `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, tripping the ratchet. Workaround: commit `1c128d3eb` split every multi-var `local` into separate lines. The pattern is idiomatic and appears pre-existing at line 1066 of the same file (`local op="$1" repo="$2" number="$3"`).

**Follow-up to #19739 (t2230, closed):** t2230 converted validators to ratchet-style (absolute-count → delta-count), reducing blast radius. It did not fix the underlying regex logic. This issue fixes the regex.

**Per @marcusquinn (planning PR #20479 context):** The workaround in `1c128d3eb` is harmless but unnecessary once this fix lands. +Blocks pushes when the pushed commit's `TODO.md` contains two or more checkbox lines with the same task ID (t2745). title: parent: Tier-2/3 GraphQL optimization (conditional — re-evaluate after t2744 observation)
body:
## Task (parent-task, held)

Track Tier-2/3 GraphQL optimization work that was deliberately deferred during t2744 (PR #20483, merged `dbd1e9cb4`). **Do NOT dispatch automatically** — this issue exists to surface a re-evaluation decision after a 7-14 day observation window of Tier-1 effectiveness.

## Why deferred, not abandoned

t2744 shipped four Tier-1 config-only changes that should substantially reduce GraphQL consumption:

1. Circuit breaker threshold `0.05` → `0.30` (trip at 1500 remaining instead of 250)
2. REST fallback threshold `10` → `1000` (route reads earlier)
3. Pulse interval `120s` → `180s`
4. Stats-wrapper interval `900s` → `3600s`

Pre-deploy baseline: `168K-294K pts/hr against a 5K/hr ceiling` with repeated 0/5000 exhaustion events. Post-deploy first observation (within one rate-limit window): 1995/5000 remaining at mid-window, zero `circuit-breaker-rl GraphQL budget EXHAUSTED` events. Promising but insufficient evidence — need a full observation window to know if Tier-1 alone is enough.

Committing to Tier-2/3 work now would be scope expansion without evidence the original fix fell short. Defer.

## Re-evaluation criteria

Re-evaluate this parent-task on or after **2026-04-29** (7 days post-t2744 merge) OR earlier if ANY of the following are observed:

- [ ] `circuit-breaker-rl GraphQL budget EXHAUSTED` fires > 3 times per 24h window (check `grep -c "EXHAUSTED" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log`)
- [ ] GraphQL `remaining` drops below 500 during normal operation (not near reset) in >1 pulse cycle per hour
- [ ] Pulse cycles begin timing out or watchdog-killing due to `_gh_should_fallback_to_rest` rejections
- [ ] Worker dispatch throttles via `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken > 0` in `~/.aidevops/stats/pulse-stats.json`

If NONE of the above fire during the observation window: close this parent-task as `status:done` with rationale "Tier-1 sufficient — no structural changes needed". Memory `mem_20260422202420_*` captures the decision pattern for future reference.

If ANY fire: decompose into child phases below and dispatch in priority order.

## Phases (child candidates — DO NOT dispatch until trigger fires)

### Phase 1: Consolidate repeated `gh issue list` calls (Tier-2, ~4h)

Target: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` — each makes 8+ `gh issue list` calls per repo per pulse cycle (14 repos × 30 cycles/hr × ~16 lists each = >5000 point pressure on GraphQL before any other work). The existing batch-prefetch path (`pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` via `gh search`) already demonstrates the consolidation pattern — extend it to cover the reconcile and triage read paths.

**Model on:** `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh::_batch_search_issues_for_owner` — single `gh search issues` query covering multiple repos per owner.

**Expected reduction:** ~60-70% of current GraphQL load per cycle, based on `gh issue list` being the dominant consumer in `pulse-prefetch.sh::_prefetch_repo_prs` and reconcile paths.

### Phase 2: ETag / `If-None-Match` conditional requests (Tier-2, ~6h)

Cache `ETag` response headers from `gh api` GraphQL responses. On repeat query within cache TTL, send `If-None-Match: <etag>` and treat `304 Not Modified` as cost-0 (GitHub does not charge against the rate limit for 304s).

**Blocker check:** GitHub GraphQL API's ETag support surface needs verification — REST endpoints definitely support it, GraphQL is less universal. Research task as part of Phase 2 kickoff before implementation.

**Expected reduction:** ~40% additional reduction on top of Phase 1 IF the read pattern is repetitive (which pulse cycles are — same queries every 180s against mostly-unchanged issue state).

### Phase 3: Multi-token GraphQL rotation (Tier-3, ~8h)

Provision additional GitHub tokens (fine-grained PATs scoped per-repo) and rotate across a pool for GraphQL requests, bypassing the per-token 5000/hr ceiling. Phase 3 is the expensive, invasive path — only dispatch if Phases 1+2 did not return the system to headroom.

**Security note:** multi-token rotation requires secure pool storage (`gopass` preferred per framework security rules) and careful audit — tokens must be scoped minimally and rotated regularly. Full threat model in `tools/security/prompt-injection-defender.md` should be reviewed before proliferating tokens.

**Expected reduction:** linear with pool size (2x tokens → 2x effective budget). Use only if structural consolidation (Phases 1+2) is insufficient.

## Acceptance

This parent-task is `status:done` when either:

- **Path A (Tier-1 sufficient):** Observation window completes with NO trigger criteria met. Close with rationale comment linking to this issue's measurement data. No child issues filed.
- **Path B (Tier-1 insufficient):** Triggered criteria documented in a comment. Child issues for triggered phases filed (one per phase), each with its own brief, tier label, and measurement-evidence section. This parent closes when ALL filed children merge.

## Files Scope

None during the hold period. Files scope per child issue when decomposed.

## Session origin

t2744 (GraphQL throttle defaults) follow-up. Filed during interactive session 2026-04-22, after successful t2744 deploy (PR #20483 merged as `dbd1e9cb4`). Companion memory: `mem_20260422202420_*` captures the measurement-driven deferral pattern for reuse.

title: t2746: preserve worker assignee on merged PR for audit-trail visibility in issues list
body:
## Task

Preserve the worker assignee on issues that close via a merged linked PR, so the issues list unambiguously shows which runner machine's worker completed the work.

## Why

Workers run on user machines (the runner's gh-auth identity). The assignee on an issue is the visible signal for "which machine has (or had) a worker on this". Current `clear_active_status_on_release()` strips the assignee indiscriminately at worker exit, erasing the audit trail on successful merges.

Desired three-state semantics:

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| OPEN + assigned | Active claim — worker on @{assignee}'s machine is in flight |
| OPEN + unassigned | No claim (fresh, or released after worker failure) |
| CLOSED + assigned | Worker PR merged — @{assignee}'s machine did the work (audit trail) |
| CLOSED + unassigned | Closed without a worker (manual, wontfix, duplicate) |

Today rows 1, 2, 4 work; row 3 is broken — the assignee is stripped 10-60s after merge, making successful-merge-by-worker indistinguishable from manual-close.

## How

Edit `clear_active_status_on_release()` in `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:843-907`. Currently it only preserves assignee when an **OPEN** linked PR is found. Widen the preserve-check to also match **MERGED** linked PRs that reference this issue with a closing keyword.

### Files to modify

- **EDIT** `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh:860-880` — change the `gh pr list` call from `--state open` to `--state all`, then filter for `state == "OPEN" OR state == "MERGED"` with the existing closing-keyword regex (already anchored on `#NNN\b` to avoid cross-issue false positives).
- **NEW** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-merged-pr.sh` — mirrors the structure of `test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-pr.sh`, but with the linked PR in `MERGED` state.

### Reference pattern

Model the new test on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-pr.sh` (OPEN-PR preserve case) and `test-clear-active-status-on-release-no-pr.sh` (no-PR unassign case). Both already mock `gh` and exercise `clear_active_status_on_release` directly.

### Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — clean
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-merged-pr.sh` — passes (new)
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-pr.sh` — passes (unchanged)
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-no-pr.sh` — passes (unchanged — failure path still unassigns)

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-merged-pr.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] Worker that merges a PR leaves the issue CLOSED with assignee preserved (visible in `gh issue list --state closed`)
- [ ] Worker that fails without opening a PR leaves the issue OPEN with no assignee (unchanged)
- [ ] Worker that opens a PR but is still in flight keeps status:in-review + assignee (unchanged)
- [ ] New test covers merged-PR-preserve case
- [ ] Existing tests still pass

## Session origin

Interactive session diagnosing why recent worker-completed issues showed no assignee. Traced to `clear_active_status_on_release` dropping assignee when its OPEN-PR-check raced with the merge-then-close sequence.

title: Add aidevops review-gate CLI for configuring rate_limit_behavior
body:
## Task

Add an `aidevops review-gate` CLI subcommand for configuring `review_gate.rate_limit_behavior` in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` without requiring users to hand-edit JSON.

## Why

Surfaced during #20493 review (Layer 1 CI workflow fix). The `review_gate.rate_limit_behavior` field is the user-facing opt-in for "block merge when bots are rate-limited" — default `"pass"` preserves velocity (rely on daily code audit), opt-in `"wait"` provides strict review-before-merge semantics.

Current discovery path is:

1. Notice the workflow's behaviour doesn't match preference
2. Read `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`
3. Hand-edit `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`
4. Validate JSON with `jq . ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json > /dev/null`

This is discoverable only by users who read docs. A CLI subcommand makes the setting accessible from `aidevops --help`, the AI assistant's response path ("Want me to change this setting for you?"), and normal tab-completion.

The setting itself already exists and works correctly — this is pure UX plumbing, not new behaviour.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/review-gate-config-helper.sh` — new helper script following the pattern of existing config-mutation helpers (`secret-helper.sh`, `approval-helper.sh`).
- **EDIT**: `aidevops.sh:1751` — add a new dispatch line after the `secret` entry:
  ```bash
  review-gate | review_gate) _dispatch_helper "review-gate-config-helper.sh" "review-gate-config-helper.sh" "$@" ;;
  ```
- **EDIT**: `aidevops.sh` (around line 1387, the help output for subcommands) — add:
  ```bash
  echo "  review-gate <cmd>  Configure review_gate.rate_limit_behavior (list/set/unset)"
  ```
- **EDIT**: `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md` — add a line under the `review_gate` field description pointing to the new CLI: "CLI: `aidevops review-gate --help`".

### Reference patterns to copy

- **Helper file structure**: model on `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` — small helper with subcommand dispatch, `print_header`/`print_error` UX, `--help` output.
- **repos.json mutation pattern**: model on `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` or any helper that edits `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` via `jq`. Critical: re-validate after edit (`jq . ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json > /dev/null`) — see `.agents/AGENTS.md` "repos.json structure (CRITICAL)" note. A malformed file silently breaks pulse for ALL repos.
- **CLI dispatch**: model on the `secret | secrets)` and `approve)` lines at `aidevops.sh:1751-1752`.

### Subcommand surface

```bash
aidevops review-gate                              # Show current config for all registered repos
aidevops review-gate list                         # Same as above (explicit)
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug>                  # Show config for one repo
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug> pass             # Set per-repo default to "pass"
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug> wait             # Set per-repo default to "wait"
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug> unset            # Remove the per-repo override (fall back to env/default)
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug> --tool coderabbitai pass   # Per-tool override
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug> --tool coderabbitai wait
aidevops review-gate <repo-slug> --tool coderabbitai unset
aidevops review-gate --help                       # Usage
```

`<repo-slug>` accepts either an `owner/repo` slug (matched against `initialized_repos[].slug`) or a local path (matched against `initialized_repos[].path`). If the slug doesn't match any registered repo, error with a pointer to `aidevops repos`.

### Validation

- On set: validate that the value is one of `pass`, `wait` (reject anything else with a clear error).
- On set: validate that `--tool` value is one of the known bot logins (`coderabbitai`, `gemini-code-assist`, `augment-code`, `augmentcode`, `copilot`) — or at least warn if unknown (don't reject — allows forward-compat with new bots).
- After any write: `jq . ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json > /dev/null` must succeed, else bail and restore from backup. Keep a transient `.bak` before writing.
- Resolution summary on `list`: show the effective value after applying the precedence order (per-tool > per-repo > env var > `"pass"`).

### Verification

```bash
# Shellcheck the new helper
shellcheck .agents/scripts/review-gate-config-helper.sh

# Dry-run against a test repos.json
cp ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json /tmp/repos-backup.json
aidevops review-gate list
aidevops review-gate marcusquinn/aidevops wait
aidevops review-gate marcusquinn/aidevops --tool coderabbitai unset
aidevops review-gate list  # confirm the changes
aidevops review-gate marcusquinn/aidevops unset  # restore default
diff /tmp/repos-backup.json ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json  # should be identical (only transient changes)

# Integration: open an aidevops session, verify the setting flows through
bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh check <pr> <repo>
# (should respect whatever `aidevops review-gate` wrote)
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `.agents/scripts/review-gate-config-helper.sh` exists, is shellcheck-clean, and implements the subcommand surface above.
2. `aidevops review-gate` is registered in `aidevops.sh` dispatch and appears in `aidevops --help`.
3. `aidevops review-gate list` (or bare `aidevops review-gate`) shows effective config for every registered repo, with the resolved value clearly distinguished from the raw config value.
4. `aidevops review-gate <slug> pass|wait|unset` mutates `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` via `jq`, re-validates the file, and reports the change.
5. `--tool <bot-login>` scope is supported and applies per-tool overrides under `review_gate.tools.<login>.rate_limit_behavior`.
6. Invalid inputs (unknown slug, unknown value, malformed JSON) fail with a clear error and do NOT corrupt `repos.json`.
7. `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md` updated to cross-reference the new CLI.
8. The new subcommand is additive — existing JSON schemas, env vars (`REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMIT_BEHAVIOR`), and resolution order are unchanged.

## Tier

`tier:standard`. Multi-file change, new helper + dispatcher edit + doc update, reference patterns exist, acceptance criteria clear. Not `tier:simple` because JSON mutation + validation + subcommand surface design require judgment.

## Context

- Parent review: #20493 (the Layer 1 CI workflow fix)
- Sibling: #20494 (Layer 2 `_comment_is_settled` semantic bug)
- Field spec: `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md` "review_gate" field
- Helper implementation: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:129-159` (resolution order)
- Not a blocker for #20493 — that PR ships the workflow fix first. This follow-up is UX polish.

title: t2748: fix(scanner): post-merge-review-scanner emits issues without auto-dispatch + tier labels
body:
## What

`post-merge-review-scanner.sh` creates `review-followup` issues without the `auto-dispatch` and `tier:standard` labels. Pulse dispatch requires both. Result: scanner-emitted issues sit unworked indefinitely.

## Why

Observed 9 dispatchable review-followup issues (#20508, #20510-#20517) stalled for hours/days while pulse workers idled. Backfill of labels has been applied as a one-shot remediation; this PR fixes the source so it doesn't recur.

## How

Single-file change.

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh:614` — extend `label_list` to include `auto-dispatch,tier:standard` when `SCANNER_NEEDS_REVIEW != true`.
- Pattern: keep NMR-gated issues without dispatch labels (NMR auto-approval will add them when clearing). Only the non-NMR path needs the change.
- Reference: existing label_list construction at lines 614-620.

Proposed diff shape:

```bash
local label_list="$SCANNER_LABEL,source:review-scanner,origin:worker"
if [[ "$SCANNER_NEEDS_REVIEW" == "true" ]]; then
    gh label create "needs-maintainer-review" --repo "$repo" \
        --description "Requires human triage before worker dispatch" \
        --color "B60205" || true
    label_list="${label_list},needs-maintainer-review"
else
    # Scanner-emitted issues are dispatchable by default — without these
    # labels pulse cannot pick them up. NMR'd issues skip this path because
    # NMR auto-approval (pulse-nmr-approval.sh) adds auto-dispatch on clear.
    label_list="${label_list},auto-dispatch,tier:standard"
fi
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] New review-followup issues created by the scanner carry `auto-dispatch` + `tier:standard` labels
- [ ] NMR'd review-followup issues do NOT carry `auto-dispatch` (gating preserved)
- [ ] Scanner unit tests still pass: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh` (if present) or shellcheck clean

## Verification

```bash

SCANNER_DRY_RUN=1 ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh scan marcusquinn/aidevops 2>&1 | grep -E "(label|auto-dispatch|tier)"
```

title: auto-decomposer-scanner.sh: zero-delay thresholds + 1-day re-file for AI-throughput mode
body:
## Task

Update three default thresholds in `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` to reflect the AI-throughput operating model:

- `SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS`: 6 → 0
- `SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS`: 24 → 0
- `AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL`: 604800 → 86400 (7 days → 1 day)

## Why

The current thresholds encode "give a human author time to self-decompose before the bot intervenes" — which made sense when humans filed most parent-tasks. In the current AI-driven workflow:

1. Most parent-task issues are filed by AI sessions that immediately move on to other work. Waiting 6h for the author to come back is betting on a return that won't happen — the author's session is ended by the time the threshold fires.

2. The "aged parent" signal (≥1 non-nudge comment → use 24h instead of 6h) is polluted by review bots (CodeRabbit, SonarCloud, Codacy, github-actions) that comment within minutes of issue creation. The current logic treats those bot comments the same as a human actively engaging — which is not the intent.

3. The 7-day re-file interval is ~10-20x the typical `tier:thinking` decompose worker completion time (~30min-2h). 1 day is still >10x the worker duration, leaving ample headroom to avoid duplicate filings while allowing failed decompose attempts to retry within a reasonable window.

## Race-condition / false-dispatch analysis

The only realistic failure mode with 0-hour thresholds is the **relabel-then-edit race**: a maintainer applies `parent-task` to an existing issue, then types decomposition markers into the body over the next few minutes. Scanner fires on the next pulse cycle (≤3 min), files a decompose child, worker dispatches, session-start reads the now-updated parent body, sees `## Phases` present, closes Outcome A.

Total cost of this race: ~10K tokens (one false dispatch) + one dispatch slot + 30-60s of worker time.

Risk mitigations already in place:

- Worker-triager protocol (GH#18538): Outcome A close when premise falsified
- In-flight dedup in scanner: title-match + `source:auto-decomposer` label skips already-filed decompose children
- `SCANNER_MAX_ISSUES=3` per-repo per-run cap: prevents thundering herd

For **new** parent-task issues filed via `gh_create_issue` with `--label parent-task` + full body in a single call, there is no race — body markers are present at the moment the label is applied.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:66-72` — change the three default values

### Change

```bash
# Before (lines 66-72)
SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS="${SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS:-24}"
SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS="${SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS:-6}"
SCANNER_MAX_ISSUES="${SCANNER_MAX_ISSUES:-3}"
SCANNER_PARENT_LIST_LIMIT="${SCANNER_PARENT_LIST_LIMIT:-100}"
SCANNER_LABEL="source:auto-decomposer"
AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL="${AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL:-604800}"

# After
SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS="${SCANNER_NUDGE_AGE_HOURS:-0}"
SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS="${SCANNER_FRESH_PARENT_HOURS:-0}"
SCANNER_MAX_ISSUES="${SCANNER_MAX_ISSUES:-3}"
SCANNER_PARENT_LIST_LIMIT="${SCANNER_PARENT_LIST_LIMIT:-100}"
SCANNER_LABEL="source:auto-decomposer"
AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL="${AUTO_DECOMPOSER_INTERVAL:-86400}"
```

### Comparison logic — verify

Check that the nudge-age comparison in the scanner handles `threshold=0` correctly. The relevant function is around `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:144-`. If the comparison is `age_hours >= threshold_hours`, then 0 works fine (`age >= 0` is always true once a nudge has been posted). If there's an inadvertent `age_hours > threshold_hours` (strict), then 0 would never fire and we'd have a regression — add a test.

### Documentation updates

- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — search for "24h advisory nudge" and "7-day NMR escalation" phrasing; correct to reflect the new defaults AND the fact that the nudge posts immediately on the next cycle (the 24h/7d numbers were always about the scanner fire, not the nudge itself).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md` (if it exists; otherwise skip) — same correction.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:49-56` — update the `# Env:` doc block to reflect new defaults.

### Verification

- New test under `.agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-decomposer-scanner-zero-threshold.sh`:
  - Stub a parent-task issue with a nudge comment posted N seconds ago (where N < 60).
  - Run scanner with defaults.
  - Assert: decompose issue IS filed (not skipped for "too young").
  - Run scanner again immediately.
  - Assert: decompose issue is NOT filed a second time (in-flight dedup + 1-day re-file interval both apply).
- Existing test `tests/test-parent-decomposition-nudge-dedup.sh` still passes.
- Existing test `tests/test-pulse-reconcile-parent-task*.sh` still passes.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` clean.

### Enhancement (optional, can be a separate PR)

Make `_count_non_nudge_comments` in `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:84` exclude known review-bot logins (`coderabbitai`, `sonarcloud[bot]`, `codacy-production[bot]`, `github-actions[bot]`) so the fresh-vs-aged distinction remains a meaningful human-engagement signal even with 0-hour thresholds. This is useful for logging/observability and as a safety margin if a future operator wants to re-enable a small delay. Can be deferred — not required for this PR.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Three defaults changed in `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`
- [ ] Env-var overrides still honoured (backwards-compatible)
- [ ] Comparison logic verified to handle `threshold=0` correctly
- [ ] AGENTS.md and in-script env doc block updated
- [ ] New zero-threshold test added and passing
- [ ] Existing parent-task tests still passing
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `.agents/reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md` (if exists)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-auto-decomposer-scanner-zero-threshold.sh`

## Session origin

Filed during t2744 follow-up conversation 2026-04-22. Maintainer preference expressed: "since we're maximising ai use for throughput, i don't see the need for any delay in decomposition, then maybe 1-day refile to avoid duplicate decomposition". Related memory: `mem_20260422232622_6b6e1cbd` (timing model) and `mem_20260422232614_dd8f099d` (H2 heading requirement). See also parent-task #20518 which demonstrates the held-parent pattern compatible with these new defaults.

title: fix(pulse-batch-prefetch): detect GraphQL exhaustion and fall back to REST API
body:
## What

`pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` has TWO related bugs that cause silent prefetch failures during GraphQL rate-limit exhaustion (observed 17:36–18:45 UTC on 2026-04-22, recurring):

1. **Detection gap**: `_is_search_rate_limited` checks for "Search API rate limit exceeded" patterns but `gh search` uses GraphQL under the hood. The actual error message is "GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID …" which doesn't match any pattern. Result: rate-limit hits are logged as generic failures (`gh search prs failed for owner=…`).

2. **Fallthrough is a lie**: When `_is_search_rate_limited` DOES match, the helper logs "falling through to per-repo GraphQL" — but the function then returns 1 with no fallthrough code anywhere. There is no actual fallback path.

Combined effect: when GraphQL exhausts (which happens regularly per pulse-wrapper.log), batch-prefetch silently fails and the pulse loses owner-level issue/PR cache. Workers can't be dispatched accurately because the cache is empty/stale.

## Why

This is a primary contributor to the GraphQL exhaustion the framework already mitigated at the consumer side (t2574, t2744 added REST fallback to `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`). The batch-prefetch path was not migrated. User asked: "we should also fallback to rest api" — confirming the expected behavior.

## How

Two-part fix:

1. **Extend rate-limit detection**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh:100-103` — add GraphQL exhaustion patterns to `_is_search_rate_limited`:
   ```bash
   grep -qiE 'Search rate limit exceeded|search API rate limit|HTTP 422.*abuse detection|secondary rate limit|was submitted too quickly|GraphQL: API rate limit (already )?exceeded|API rate limit exceeded for user'
   ```

2. **Implement REST fallback for `gh search issues|prs`**: when rate-limited, fall through to per-repo `gh api repos/{slug}/issues` (REST). Pattern to follow: `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` `_use_rest_fallback` logic (t2574, t2744). The REST core pool is independent (5000/hr) so it's a real escape hatch.

   Affected functions:
   - `_refresh_owner_issues` (line 220-260)
   - `_refresh_owner_prs` (line 262-300)

   Per-repo fallback iterates repos in the owner group, calls REST issues/PRs, normalises to the same schema as `_normalize_search_to_prefetch_schema`. More gh-api calls but each is small and the REST bucket has headroom.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_is_search_rate_limited` returns true on observed "GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded" errors
- [ ] When rate-limited, batch-prefetch falls through to per-repo REST and writes the same per-slug caches
- [ ] Cache hits remain valid after GraphQL exhaustion — pulse log no longer shows extended periods of "gh search ... failed"
- [ ] Existing tests pass: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh`
- [ ] Add a new test case for the REST fallback path (mock GraphQL exhaustion)

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck ~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/tests/test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh
# Manual: artificially trigger by setting AIDEVOPS_GH_REST_FALLBACK_THRESHOLD=99999
# and observe batch-prefetch routes via REST
```

## Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-enrich-batch-prefetch.sh

## Context

- Related: #20518 (parent: Tier-2/3 GraphQL optimization, held for observation)
- Pattern: t2574, t2744 (shared-gh-wrappers REST fallback)
- Evidence: 1+ hour of `[pulse-batch-prefetch] gh search ... failed for owner=… GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded` lines in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` on 2026-04-22

title: auto-decomposer-scanner.sh: exclude known review-bot logins from fresh-vs-aged engagement signal
body:
## Task

Make `_count_non_nudge_comments` in `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:84-94` exclude known review-bot logins when counting "non-nudge comments" on parent-task issues. Restore the aged-vs-fresh distinction as a meaningful human-engagement signal.

## Why

The function currently counts ALL comments (except the `<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->` nudge marker) as "engagement evidence". This determines whether a parent is treated as **fresh** (0 comments → shorter threshold) or **aged** (≥1 comments → longer threshold).

Problem: review bots (CodeRabbit, SonarCloud, Codacy, github-actions, etc.) often post within minutes of issue creation — their comments are mechanical, not a signal that a human is actively engaging. Treating bot chatter the same as human comments means virtually every parent-task is instantly classified "aged" and gets the longer threshold, defeating the fresh/aged distinction.

Related PR #20532 reduces both thresholds to 0, which makes the classification moot in the **current** default. But this enhancement is still valuable:

1. **Observability / logging** — the scanner logs fresh vs aged classifications; clean classifications make diagnostics more useful.
2. **Future-proofing** — any operator who wants to re-enable a small delay (via env override) gets a meaningful signal again.
3. **Other callers** — if `_count_non_nudge_comments` is ever reused by another pulse component (e.g., for "has a human reviewed this issue?" checks), the bot-aware version is the correct semantics everywhere.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh:84-94` — update `_count_non_nudge_comments` to filter out bot logins
- OPTIONAL: `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` — if a shared bot-login list doesn't exist already, add one (check first with `grep -n "BOT_LOGINS\|bot_logins\|REVIEW_BOTS" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*.sh`)

### Change

Current:

```bash
_count_non_nudge_comments() {
	local repo="$1"
	local issue_num="$2"
	local count
	count=$(gh api --paginate "repos/${repo}/issues/${issue_num}/comments" \
		--jq '[.[] | select(.body | contains("<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->") | not)] | length' \
		2>/dev/null || echo "0")
	[[ "$count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || count=0
	printf '%s' "$count"
	return 0
}
```

Proposed:

```bash
# Known review-bot logins — these accounts post mechanical review comments
# (not a human-engagement signal). Extend as needed when new review bots
# are adopted.
REVIEW_BOT_LOGINS_JQ_FILTER='["coderabbitai", "coderabbitai[bot]", "sonarcloud[bot]", "sonarqubecloud[bot]", "codacy-production[bot]", "github-actions[bot]", "gemini-code-assist[bot]", "qodo-merge-pro[bot]", "codefactor-io", "socket-security[bot]"]'

_count_non_nudge_comments() {
	local repo="$1"
	local issue_num="$2"
	local count
	# Exclude both the nudge marker AND any comment authored by a known
	# review bot. The comparison is against user.login (lowercased) to
	# absorb the "[bot]" suffix variations.
	count=$(gh api --paginate "repos/${repo}/issues/${issue_num}/comments" \
		--jq "[.[] | select(
			(.body | contains(\"<!-- parent-needs-decomposition -->\") | not) and
			(.user.login as \$login | ${REVIEW_BOT_LOGINS_JQ_FILTER} | index(\$login) | not)
		)] | length" \
		2>/dev/null || echo "0")
	[[ "$count" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || count=0
	printf '%s' "$count"
	return 0
}
```

### Reference pattern

If `shared-constants.sh` (or another shared file) already has a bot-login list, use it. Check first:

```bash
grep -rn "BOT_LOGINS\|bot_logins\|REVIEW_BOTS\|coderabbitai" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/shared-*.sh ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*.sh | head
```

If a shared list exists, source it and reference rather than duplicating the login list. If not, define the list local to `auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` (this PR) and file a follow-up to extract it to `shared-constants.sh` if a second caller ever materialises.

### Verification

- New test under `.agents/scripts/tests/test-count-non-nudge-comments-bot-filter.sh`:
  - Stub a parent-task issue with: 1 human comment, 2 CodeRabbit comments, 1 SonarCloud comment, 1 nudge marker comment.
  - Call `_count_non_nudge_comments`.
  - Assert result == 1 (only the human comment counts).
- Existing scanner tests still pass.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh` clean.
- `jq` syntax valid — run a dry-run invocation with the new filter against a real issue (e.g., `marcusquinn/aidevops#20518`) and confirm the output is a non-negative integer.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_count_non_nudge_comments` excludes known review-bot logins
- [ ] Bot login list is maintainable (single location, clear to extend)
- [ ] New test added covering the bot filter
- [ ] Existing tests still pass
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean
- [ ] Semantically correct when combined with PR #20532's 0-hour thresholds (function still works, just less important)

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/auto-decomposer-scanner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` (if extracting the bot list)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-count-non-nudge-comments-bot-filter.sh`

## Session origin

Filed during t2744 follow-up conversation 2026-04-22. Companion PR #20532 zeroes the nudge thresholds; this PR makes the fresh-vs-aged signal meaningful for observability and future-proofing. Can merge in either order relative to #20532 — independent changes.

title: bug: _release_dispatch_claim fires with empty DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG due to late export
body:
## Description

`_release_dispatch_claim` in `headless-runtime-failure.sh:41` emits a non-fatal warning:

```
Cannot release claim: missing issue=6 repo=
```

The `repo=` field is empty because `DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG` is read from the environment (line 51) but is only exported later in the call chain — inside `_execute_run_attempt` (headless-runtime-helper.sh:878-882), which runs **after** the EXIT trap that calls `_release_dispatch_claim` is already set (line 1136 via `_cmd_run_prepare`).

## Root Cause

Ordering gap between trap setup and env export in `cmd_run`:

1. **Line 1260** — `_cmd_run_prepare()` sets an EXIT trap calling `_release_dispatch_claim '$session_key' 'process_exit'`
2. **Lines 1268-1294** — `resolve_headless_variant`, continuation config, etc.
3. **Line 1296+** — retry loop begins, eventually calling `_execute_run_attempt`
4. **Line 878-882** — `DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG` is finally exported (guarded by `role == "worker" && session_key == issue-*`)

Any exit between steps 1 and 4 triggers the trap with `DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG` unset. Under `set -euo pipefail` (line 18), an unhandled failure in steps 2-3 causes exactly this.

Additionally, the role guard at line 878 means non-`worker` roles (triage, research, pulse) that still use numeric-suffixed session keys will always hit the warning — the slug is never set for them, but the EXIT trap fires unconditionally.

## Considerations

Two independent gaps to address:

**Gap 1 — Late export:** `DISPATCH_REPO_SLUG` should be set before the EXIT trap is armed. Moving the `git remote get-url origin` extraction into `_cmd_run_prepare` (which already receives `$work_dir`) would close the timing window. The export is cheap (~2ms) and has no side effects if the release path isn't reached.

**Gap 2 — Unconditional trap vs conditional export:** The EXIT trap calls `_release_dispatch_claim` for all roles, but the slug is only set for `role == "worker" && session_key == issue-*`. Options:
  - (a) Make the trap conditional on role (only arm for workers)
  - (b) Set the slug for all roles and let `_release_dispatch_claim` decide whether to post the API comment
  - (c) Have `_release_dispatch_claim` silently return 0 without warning when called from a non-worker context (cheapest, but masks future bugs)

Option (b) is simplest — the slug extraction is role-independent (`git remote get-url origin` works regardless of session type), and `_release_dispatch_claim` already no-ops gracefully when both fields are empty.

## Impact

- **Severity:** Low. The warning is non-fatal (returns 0). The claim is not released via API comment, so the pulse relies on the 30-min TTL expiry instead of immediate re-dispatch.
- **Frequency:** Every worker dispatch where the process exits before `_execute_run_attempt`, plus every non-worker dispatch with a numeric-suffixed session key.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.94
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0

## File References

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:878-882` — move slug export earlier
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1136` — or make trap conditional
- `REF: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:41-56` — the warning-emitting function

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20494 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20494

**Parent issue:** #20494 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** review-bot-gate-helper: _comment_is_settled edit-criterion rejects fast legitimate edits; 30s default miscalibrated for CodeRabbit long-tail latency
**Parent labels:** `auto-dispatch,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20494. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20494 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20494:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20494 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20494 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20494 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20494 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20494** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Description

The t2139 settlement-check logic in `_comment_is_settled` (`.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:204-232`) has two independent semantic issues surfaced by real-world CodeRabbit behaviour:

1. **Edit criterion requires `edit_delta >= min_lag`** — a legitimate real-review edit that lands *before* the minimum-lag threshold is rejected. When `min_lag` is tuned up to cover CodeRabbit's long-tail latency (e.g., 600-900s), a CodeRabbit edit that lands quickly (T+180s) is explicitly classified as "not settled" even though the comment body IS the final review.

2. **Default `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS=30`** is far below the real distribution of CodeRabbit's edit latencies (empirical: 2s to 18+ minutes). A 30s threshold catches short non-review notices (walkthrough-skipped, rate-limit notices) but systematically allows "aged-in" unedited placeholders to be falsely classified as settled real reviews.

Together, these cause `bot_has_real_review` to false-positive on CodeRabbit Phase 1 placeholders that have aged past 30s but haven't yet been edited with Phase 2 real review content.

## Expected Behaviour

Given CodeRabbit's two-phase posting pattern (Phase 1 placeholder at ~T+15s → Phase 2 edit with real review content at variable T+X), `_comment_is_settled` should correctly classify comment state such that `bot_has_real_review` returns `true` only when real review content is actually present:

- The moment a real-review edit lands, the comment's body IS the final review — should be classified as settled immediately, regardless of how quickly the edit came.
- An unedited placeholder should not be promoted to "real review" status by aging alone, because its body is not review content.

## Reproducer

**Symptom**: same observation event as sibling issue (#20493 — Layer 1). On a PR in a managed private repo, 2026-04-22.

At pulse-merge decision time (T+3m36s after PR open), `bot_has_real_review("coderabbitai", <repo>, <pr>)` evaluated:

```text
CodeRabbit comment:
  created_at:  2026-04-22T18:49:00Z
  updated_at:  2026-04-22T18:49:00Z  (unedited at this point)
  body:        Phase 1 placeholder content (no "Review failed" yet)
  age at check: 205 seconds
  edit_delta:   0
  min_lag:     30 (default)

_comment_is_settled:
  (a) edit_delta (0) >= min_lag (30)?  NO
  (b) age (205)     >= min_lag (30)?  YES → settled

is_non_review_comment(body)?
  NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS match on placeholder body? NO
  (none of "Review failed", "Review skipped", "closed or merged during review",
   "Auto reviews are limited", or rate-limit variants match pre-edit placeholder)

bot_has_real_review: RETURNS TRUE → merge allowed → race condition fires
```

**Causal code**: `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:204-232`:

```bash
_comment_is_settled() {
  # A comment is "settled" if EITHER:
  #   (a) it has been edited (updated_at >= created_at + min_lag), OR
  #   (b) it is old enough that the bot would have edited by now
  #       (now - created_at >= min_lag).
  ...
  if [[ "$edit_delta" -ge "$min_lag" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "$age" -ge "$min_lag" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  return 1
}
```

Introduced in PR #19309 (t2139).

### Empirical data — CodeRabbit edit-delta distribution

Collected from 15 recent PRs on marcusquinn/aidevops (public repo, 2026-04-22):

| `edit_delta` | count | fraction | likely semantics |
|--------------|-------|----------|-----------------|
| < 30s | 10 | 67% | non-review notices (skipped, rate-limit, trivial) |
| 1-5 min | 2 | 13% | short real reviews |
| 7-18 min | 3 | 20% | deep real reviews |

The 30s default correctly catches the first bucket but systematically misclassifies the ~33% of real reviews that exceed 30s. Those real reviews either:
- Arrive as edits where `edit_delta >= 30s` — classified settled via edit (correct).
- Are preceded by an unedited placeholder aging past 30s — classified settled via age **before** the edit lands (the actual failure mode).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install aidevops v3.8.94 with the t2139 fix.
2. Configure a repo with CodeRabbit enabled.
3. Open a PR that will trigger CodeRabbit review; note creation time (T+0).
4. Wait ~35s past CodeRabbit's Phase 1 placeholder post (typically T+45-60s total).
5. Before CodeRabbit's edit lands (typically T+1min-18min), run:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh check $PR $OWNER/$REPO
   ```

6. Observe: returns `PASS` despite CodeRabbit not having completed its review. The placeholder body is treated as a real review because it has aged past 30s without matching any `NON_REVIEW_PATTERN`.

## Considerations for the maintainer(s)

### Option A: Recognize Phase 1 placeholder body content

Add distinctive CodeRabbit Phase 1 placeholder patterns to `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` (or a separate `PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS` list). An unedited placeholder's body would then be recognized as "not a real review" regardless of age. Real review registers only after the edit changes the body.

**Pros**: semantically correct — detects what CodeRabbit is actually saying. Works regardless of timing.

**Cons**: requires empirically collecting and maintaining placeholder body patterns. CodeRabbit's exact placeholder text may change. Per-bot placeholder patterns needed (each bot has its own Phase 1 text).

### Option B: Relax the edit criterion — any edit means settled

Remove the `edit_delta >= min_lag` requirement. Any edit (regardless of delta) is treated as "comment reached final form" — the delta check was a safety net against flapping, but flapping isn't a real pattern for review bots.

```bash
if [[ "$updated_epoch" -gt "$created_epoch" ]]; then
  return 0   # edited at all → settled
fi
if [[ "$age" -ge "$min_lag" ]]; then
  return 0   # never edited but aged-in → settled
fi
return 1
```

**Pros**: one-line change. Trusts the bot's edit as authoritative.

**Cons**: doesn't fix the aged-in-unedited-placeholder false positive. The 30s default still lets unedited placeholders get promoted.

### Option C: Raise default `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS`

Increase the default from 30s to 600-900s (10-15 min) to cover CodeRabbit's 95th-percentile review duration.

**Pros**: minimum code delta. Tunes the existing knob to observed distribution.

**Cons**: 10-15 min merge delays on every CodeRabbit-reviewed PR. Still a threshold, still fragile against future latency drift. Doesn't address the edit-criterion semantic issue in Option B.

### Option D: Per-bot defaults in the helper

Make `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS` bot-aware with baked-in defaults (`coderabbitai=900, gemini-code-assist=120, copilot=60`), still user-overridable via `review_gate.tools.<bot>.min_edit_lag_seconds` in `repos.json`.

**Pros**: calibrates to each bot's empirical reality without user config burden.

**Cons**: maintenance of the bot-default table as bots evolve. Adds complexity to `_get_min_edit_lag` resolution order.

### Option E (recommended reading): Combine A + B

Phase 1 placeholder body recognition (A) + relaxed edit criterion (B):

- Unedited placeholder body matches PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS → classified as "non-review" → `bot_has_real_review` waits for edit.
- Edited comment → any edit counts as settled → body checked; real review → PASS; "Review failed" etc. → non-review.
- Age criterion becomes a fallback safety net for unforeseen states.

**Pros**: semantically robust; independent of `min_lag` tuning.

**Cons**: most change surface area; per-bot placeholder-pattern maintenance.

### Second-order effects to consider

- **Cycle time**: any solution that slows merges affects auto-merge cycle time for ALL `origin:interactive` + OWNER PRs, not just CodeRabbit-reviewed ones. Raising `min_lag` globally decreases worker productivity measurably.
- **Bot-evolution maintenance**: solutions with per-bot patterns introduce maintenance burden when bot behaviour changes (new bots, CodeRabbit placeholder redesign, etc.).
- **Layer interaction**: if Layer 1 (sibling #20493) is fixed first, Layer 2's false positive is masked by the CI-check gate — but only for paths that respect CI status. `pulse-merge.sh` does. `pr-loop.md` does not necessarily.
- **`wait` subcommand inheritance**: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` uses `review-bot-gate-helper.sh wait` (polls every 60s for up to 10 min). `wait` calls the same `check` logic → inherits Layer 2's bug. This is where the 30s default most directly causes workers to merge prematurely, independent of Layer 1.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.94
- **Latest version**: 3.8.94
- **Install method**: unknown (/home/rob/.local/bin/aidevops)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

2. **Age-derived settlement** — the bot *would have edited by now* if it were going to. A proxy, and a bad one for bots whose edit latency exceeds the age threshold.

The 30s default is below the empirical 95th percentile of CodeRabbit edit latency (~10-18 min per the reporter's sample). An unedited placeholder aged 31s whose body doesn't match `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` is classified as a real review. The reporter's trace (PR at T+3m36s, edit at T+5m47s) is exactly this failure mode.

If a bot edits at T+5s with `min_lag=30`, the comment is not-settled for ~25s more, then becomes settled via the age branch. This is a bounded delay, not a rejection. The concern would bite only if `edit_delta` were the *only* criterion (AND, not OR). Reading the code, it isn't. Claim 1 is a misframing — the real issue is Claim 2.

## Implementation Plan — Option A' (two-phase bot list)

This comment pins the worker-ready implementation context referenced in my prior review. Option A' was selected over A/B/C/D/E because it fixes the semantic defect (Claim 2) without pattern-maintenance burden or cycle-time regression for non-two-phase bots.

### What

Require edit-observed settlement for CodeRabbit (and any future two-phase review bot) in `_comment_is_settled`; disable the age-derived fallback for those bots only. All other bots preserve existing OR-semantics.

### Why

`_comment_is_settled` currently treats "aged past `min_lag`" as equivalent to "bot has finished writing its review" — a proxy that breaks for bots whose Phase 2 edit latency exceeds the age threshold. CodeRabbit's empirical edit-delta distribution (67% < 30s, 33% at 1-18 min per reporter's sample) means a 30s default false-positives on any aged-in unedited Phase 1 placeholder. 1. **`.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:74-85`** — add constant near `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS`:

    ```bash
    # Bots that post a Phase 1 placeholder and later edit it with real review content.
    # For these, age-derived settlement is unreliable — require edit-observed settlement.
    readonly TWO_PHASE_BOTS=("coderabbitai")
    ```

2. **`.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`** — add `_is_two_phase_bot` helper (model on `_get_rate_limit_behavior` / `_get_min_edit_lag` resolver pattern at lines 129-186):

    ```bash
    _is_two_phase_bot() {
      local bot_login="$1"
      local b
      for b in "${TWO_PHASE_BOTS[@]}"; do
        [[ "$bot_login" == "$b" ]] && return 0
      done
      return 1
    }
    ```

3. **`.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:204-236`** — modify `_comment_is_settled` to accept `bot_login` as a 4th param. When `_is_two_phase_bot` is true, require `edit_delta > 0` and skip the age-derived branch:

    ```bash
    _comment_is_settled() {
      local created_epoch="$1"
      local updated_epoch="$2"
      local min_lag="$3"
      local bot_login="${4:-}"
      local edit_delta=$((updated_epoch - created_epoch))
      local now_epoch
      now_epoch=$(date -u +%s)
      local age=$((now_epoch - created_epoch))

      if _is_two_phase_bot "$bot_login"; then
        # Phase 2 edit is authoritative; Phase 1 placeholder is not a real review regardless of age.
        [[ "$edit_delta" -gt 0 ]] && return 0
        return 1
      fi

      # Non-two-phase bots: preserve existing OR semantics.
      [[ "$edit_delta" -ge "$min_lag" ]] && return 0
      [[ "$age" -ge "$min_lag" ]] && return 0
      return 1
    }
    ```

4. **`.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`** — update 3 call sites to pass `bot_login` as 4th argument:
    - `bot_has_real_review` (~line 380)
    - `_classify_bot_state` (~line 626)
    - Verify via `rg '_comment_is_settled' .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` — any additional call sites get the same treatment.

5. **`.agents/tests/test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh`** — update tests:
    - Preserve existing 6 cases (these now exercise the non-two-phase branch; rename assertions to reflect that).
    - Add ~4 two-phase cases:
        - `coderabbitai` aged-in unedited (`edit_delta=0`, `age=120`) → NOT settled
        - `coderabbitai` edited (`edit_delta=5`, any age) → settled
        - Unknown bot login behaves as before (falls through to OR semantics)
        - `REVIEW_BOT_MIN_EDIT_LAG_SECONDS` env override still respected for non-two-phase bots

### Files Scope

```text
- .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh
- .agents/tests/test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh
```

### Acceptance

- [ ] `TWO_PHASE_BOTS=("coderabbitai")` constant added; `_is_two_phase_bot` helper implemented.
- [ ] `_comment_is_settled` accepts `bot_login` (4th param, optional for backward-compat) and, for two-phase bots, requires `edit_delta > 0` with age branch skipped.
- [ ] All call sites of `_comment_is_settled` pass `bot_login`.
- [ ] Existing 6 `test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh` cases pass unchanged (non-two-phase behaviour preserved).
- [ ] New tests cover: coderabbitai aged-in-unedited → not-settled; coderabbitai edited (any delta) → settled; unknown bot → OR semantics; env override still honoured.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` exits clean.
- [ ] PR body includes Layer-1 note: "#20493 — CI workflow has its own inline copy of this logic; this PR does NOT reach it. Coordinate port-through."

### Verification

```bash

bash .agents/tests/test-review-bot-gate-completion-signal.sh

# Lint
shellcheck .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh

# Integration smoke against a recent CodeRabbit-reviewed PR (pick a known-settled PR to confirm no regression)

```

### Layer dependency

**#20493 (Layer 1 — architectural)** has its own inline copy of `_comment_is_settled` in a CI workflow. This PR does NOT reach that copy — the branch-protection gate stays broken on Layer 1 until #20493 is fixed or this change is ported through. Call this out explicitly in the PR body; do not claim the bug is fully resolved on merge of this PR alone.

### Tier

`tier:standard` — judgment required (test case design, call-site audit, layer coordination), >1 file. Not `tier:simple` eligible.

### Notes on design decisions

- **Why `edit_delta > 0` rather than `>= min_lag` for two-phase bots?** Review bots don't flap — the `>= min_lag` guard in the original logic was a defensive relic, not an observed pattern. Simplifying to "any edit is authoritative" reduces surface area. If flapping is ever observed for a two-phase bot, tighten at that point.
- **Why make `bot_login` optional (4th param with default)?** Keeps existing call sites in unit tests working without cascade edits; any production call that forgets it falls through to the non-two-phase branch (safe default — preserves old behaviour).
- **Why not add `_is_two_phase_bot` via per-bot `repos.json` override?** Two-phase posting is a bot-implementation fact, not a repo policy. Baking it into the helper avoids every repo re-declaring the same truth. If CodeRabbit ever abandons two-phase posting, remove from the list.
