title: t2768: pulse: consolidate circuit breaker threshold into single conf file
body:
## What

Consolidate the GraphQL circuit-breaker threshold into a single source-of-truth config file. Currently the value is defined in 4 places that disagree:

| File | Line | Value | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` | :345 | `0.05` | default when env unset |
| `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` | :92, :195 | `0.30` | default when env unset |
| `.agents/configs/plist-env-overrides.json.txt` | :8 | `0.30` | launchd override |
| `.agents/AGENTS.md` | :274 | `0.30` | docs |

Live effective value differs by launch path: 0.30 via launchd (override set before wrapper default), 0.05 via manual pulse start. The 17 `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` fires in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json` happen at 0.05, not 0.30 — evidence that manual starts are hitting the 5% threshold before the breaker trips.

## Why

Behaviour silently changes based on how the pulse was started. Docs and code disagree. One place to edit, one place to read, one place for docs to point at.

Follow the existing `.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` pattern — one KEY=VALUE file, inline change history, all consumers source from it, docs reference it.

## How

### Files to modify

- NEW: `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` — single source of truth. `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_THRESHOLD=0.30` with comment explaining rationale (reserve GraphQL budget for in-flight worker reads).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:345` — replace hardcoded `0.05` default with sourcing the new conf; fall back to `0.30` if conf file missing (graceful degradation).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh:92, :195` — replace hardcoded `0.30` defaults with same sourcing pattern.
- EDIT: `.agents/configs/plist-env-overrides.json.txt:8` — keep the override line (launchd plists can't source conf files at plist-parse time) but add a comment pointing to `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` as the canonical default. If the two ever drift, the conf is authoritative.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md:274` — replace the literal `(default 0.30; previously 0.05 — ...)` prose with a reference to `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` as the canonical default.

### Reference pattern

`.agents/configs/complexity-thresholds.conf` — KEY=VALUE format, inline comment/history, read by `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`. Mirror that exactly: sourceable by bash (`source .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf`), human-readable comments above each key, no quotes needed around values.

### Files Scope

- .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh
- .agents/configs/plist-env-overrides.json.txt
- .agents/AGENTS.md

## Verification

```

bash -n .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf  # should parse as bash

# Unit tests still pass:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All three scripts reference `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` as canonical; no hardcoded `0.05` or `0.30` fallback except in the conf file itself and the graceful-degradation fallback literal
2. Docs at `.agents/AGENTS.md:274` point to the conf file; literal threshold removed from docs
3. Manual pulse start and launchd-started pulse both use the same threshold value (0.30)
4. Existing tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` still pass

Filed interactively from a review of the pulse concurrency ceiling. Discovered the 4-place inconsistency while explaining why the breaker fires at 5% when docs say 30%.

Pulse-level `no_work` rate breaker: detect cross-issue `no_work` storms and pause worker dispatch temporarily with one operator-visible alert. But the 201-issue cluster across 4 repos reveals a different pattern: many DIFFERENT issues all crashing `no_work` at once — symptomatic of a cross-cutting infrastructure problem (auth, rate limit, opencode session hang). Per-issue thresholds don't catch this; a rate-window breaker does.

Pauses dispatch → one alert → operator investigates → auto-reset when storm clears.

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — in the dispatch loop, after reading pulse state, count `fast_fail_record … crash_type=no_work` lines in a rolling window from `pulse.log` (default: 10 events in 10 minutes). If exceeded, skip all dispatch this cycle, log one alert line, emit a counter.

title: t2771: pulse: deterministic phase-extractor for well-formed parent-task bodies
body:
## What

Deterministic phase-extractor scanner: when a `parent-task` issue body follows the well-formed phase template (explicit `### Phase N:` headings with required sub-sections), automatically file each phase as a standalone `tier:standard` child via verbatim text extraction. Zero LLM, zero paraphrasing.

Complements the existing auto-decomposer which handles the general case. The existing decomposer is an LLM pass; this scanner is a deterministic short-circuit for parent bodies that already contain a fully-written phase plan.

## Why

Canonical case: #20622 (GraphQL→REST routing). Parent body already contains 4 well-formed phases with `EDIT:` file paths, reference patterns, verification commands, and acceptance criteria. The existing auto-decomposer filed #20633 to do the work an LLM would need to invent — but the content is already written in the parent. Running an LLM over it adds hallucination surface for zero value.

This scanner detects the template, verifies completeness, and files each phase with verbatim content. If any required sub-section is missing for a phase, the scanner no-ops and falls back to the existing decomposer.

## How

### Files to modify

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/parent-task-phase-extractor.sh` — detect + verify + file. Deterministic: no LLM call.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — add a call to the new helper before the existing `auto-decomposer` dispatch. If the extractor fires (exit 0), skip the decomposer for this parent.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-extractor.sh` — unit tests covering detection, completeness check, and fail-safe fallback.

### Detection algorithm (deterministic, no LLM)

Parent body is eligible when it contains 2+ blocks matching ALL of:
- `^### Phase \d+:` heading line
- `^- EDIT:` or `^- NEW:` (≥1 line in the phase section)
- `^\*\*Reference pattern:\*\*` sub-section
- `^\*\*Verification:\*\*` sub-section
- `^\*\*Acceptance:\*\*` sub-section (with ≥1 criterion bullet)

If any phase is missing any of these, the scanner NO-OPs entirely — does not file partial children, does not fall halfway through. This is the fail-safe for reliability: either the template is complete and extraction is trivially safe, or we don't touch it.

### Action (pure text extraction)

For each qualifying phase:
1. Claim task ID: `claim-task-id.sh --repo-path <path> --title "<parent-title-prefix>: Phase <N> — <phase-heading>" --no-issue`
2. Compose body: verbatim copy of the phase section from parent + auto-generated `## Context` block linking parent via `For #<parent-num>` (NOT `Closes` / `Resolves` — parent-task keyword rule, see `.agents/AGENTS.md` "Parent-task PR keyword rule").
3. Call `gh_create_issue` (via `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`) with labels `auto-dispatch,tier:standard` plus whatever tier label the parent carries (if tier:thinking parent, phases inherit).
4. Append `## Children` section to parent body if not present, or append new child line if section exists.

### Reference pattern

Existing auto-decomposer pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` `reconcile_parent_tasks` path. Mirror its dispatch shape but with the deterministic check first.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/parent-task-phase-extractor.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-extractor.sh

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/parent-task-phase-extractor.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
# Test: synthetic parent body with each required sub-section missing individually
# assert scanner no-ops for each
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-extractor.sh
# Test: canonical #20622 body (snapshot as fixture)
# assert scanner files exactly 4 children with verbatim phase content
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Scanner detects all 4 phases in a #20622-shaped parent body
2. Scanner no-ops when any required sub-section is missing from ANY phase (all-or-nothing)
3. Child issues contain verbatim phase text, no paraphrasing
4. Parent body gets `## Children` section added with cross-links to all filed children
5. Unit tests cover each missing-sub-section case plus the happy-path canonical case

### Non-scope

- Do not modify the existing auto-decomposer. This is a short-circuit path, not a replacement.
- Do not attempt to LLM-guess missing sub-sections. Missing → no-op.
- Do not file children for parents carrying `no-auto-dispatch` — that's a user opt-out.

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive review of pulse concurrency blockers. User asked for a scanner that was reliable with no hallucination risk; this design is pure regex + verbatim copy.

title: aidevops check-workflows: detect drift in framework-owned workflows across registered repos
body:
## Task

Implement `aidevops check-workflows` (new subcommand) that reports drift between aidevops-shipped workflow YAMLs and the copies in registered downstream repos. Report-only, zero writes.

## Why

aidevops currently has no mechanism to detect drift between its own `.github/workflows/*.yml` files and copies checked into downstream repos that were bootstrapped at some prior point. GH#20637 was a real user-visible bug (stale `issue-sync.yml` missing the `For/Ref` guard from PR #19883) that would have been caught by this check.

Audit of this workspace at filing time: **3 of 31 registered repos have drifted `issue-sync.yml`, all missing the fix**:

- `<webapp>` — 659 lines vs 1331 canon
- `wpallstars/really-simple-ssl-multisite` — 681 lines
- `wpallstars/compressx-multisite` — 714 lines

The other 28 repos don't have the workflow at all, which is fine — absence is not drift.

## How

**New files:**

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh` — core drift detector. Model on `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` for argument parsing and output formatting.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows.sh` — unit tests. Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-pr-guard.sh`.

**Modify:**

- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` — add `cmd_check_workflows()` function and dispatch case in the main switch. Model on `cmd_update` around line 521 and the dispatch block around line 1732.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — document the subcommand in the Quick Reference / CLI section.

**Manifest of framework-owned workflows** (hard-coded array in `check-workflows-helper.sh`):

Include (14 workflows that might legitimately live in any aidevops-managed repo):

```
issue-sync.yml
issue-triage-gate.yml
pr-triage-gate.yml
linked-issue-check.yml
maintainer-gate.yml
ai-approved-label-gate.yml
nmr-hold-comment.yml
parent-ta[redacted-credential].yml
planning-pr-keyword-check.yml
planning-pr-redundancy-check.yml
review-bot-gate.yml
post-merge-verify.yml
postflight.yml
dedup-tier-labels.yml
```

Explicitly exclude (aidevops-repo-only — don't compare these in downstream repos):

```
auto-deploy-agents.yml, release.yml, publish-packages.yml, sync-wiki.yml,
update-website-docs.yml, plugin-import-check.yml, shellcheckrc-parity.yml,
test-harness-deps.yml, code-review-monitoring.yml, opencode-agent.yml,
code-quality.yml, qlty-regression.yml, qlty-new-file-gate.yml,
counter-stack-check.yml, counter-monotonic.yml, gh-wrapper-guard.yml,
shell-init-pattern-check.yml, shell-portability.yml, ratchet-post-merge.yml,
simplification-outcome-check.yml, complexity-bump-justification-check.yml
```

(These are aidevops-specific quality gates; not obviously applicable to arbitrary downstream repos. Keep the initial manifest conservative — can expand later.)

**Algorithm:**

```
for each entry in ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json .initialized_repos[]:
  resolve path (expand ~)
  skip if: path missing, local_only: true, or path == $INSTALL_DIR
  for each wf in FRAMEWORK_WORKFLOWS:
    local="$repo/.github/workflows/$wf"
    canon="$INSTALL_DIR/.github/workflows/$wf"
    if [[ ! -f "$local" ]]: status=NOT-PRESENT (skip — intentional absence)
    elif [[ "$(git hash-object "$local")" == "$(git hash-object "$canon")" ]]:
      status=CURRENT
    else:
      # Distinguish STALE (matches some historical aidevops commit)
      # from MODIFIED-LOCALLY (matches no aidevops commit)
      local_hash=$(git hash-object "$local")
      if git -C "$INSTALL_DIR" log --all --format='%H' -- ".github/workflows/$wf" | \
         xargs -I{} git -C "$INSTALL_DIR" show "{}:.github/workflows/$wf" 2>/dev/null | \
         git hash-object --stdin -w --no-filters | grep -q "^$local_hash$"; then
        status=STALE
      else:
        status=MODIFIED-LOCALLY
      fi
  aggregate per-repo summary
```

(Implementation note: the STALE vs MODIFIED distinction via blob-hash history scan may be expensive on large repos. An acceptable simplification for Phase 1 is to treat any non-matching hash as DRIFTED and defer the STALE/MODIFIED split to Phase 2 where it matters more. Decide based on perf measurements.)

**Output format** — model on `aidevops status` formatting:

```
Workflow drift audit:

  REPO                                   STATUS      DETAIL
  aidevops                               CURRENT     (canonical source)
  <webapp>                              DRIFTED     issue-sync.yml: 659 lines vs 1331 canon
  really-simple-ssl-multisite            DRIFTED     issue-sync.yml: 681 lines vs 1331 canon
  compressx-multisite                    DRIFTED     issue-sync.yml: 714 lines vs 1331 canon
  <28 other repos>                       OK          no framework workflows present

Summary: 3 of 31 repos with drift.
Next step: aidevops sync-workflows --apply (requires Phase 2).
```

## Acceptance

1. `aidevops check-workflows` runs in under 5s for 30 repos (no network calls — local hash comparison only).
2. Reports exactly one of `{CURRENT, DRIFTED, NOT-PRESENT}` per (repo, workflow) pair. STALE/MODIFIED-LOCALLY distinction optional for Phase 1 (see implementation note above).
3. Exits 0 when no drift, exits 1 when any repo has DRIFTED status (so CI can gate).
4. Running against current workspace correctly identifies the 3 known-drifted repos: `<webapp>`, `really-simple-ssl-multisite`, `compressx-multisite`.
5. Test file passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows.sh`.
6. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh` passes with zero violations.

## Verification

```bash
# Manual smoke test
aidevops check-workflows
# Expected: exit 1, lists exactly 3 DRIFTED repos

# Unit tests
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows.sh

# Static analysis
shellcheck .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh
```

## Session Origin

Filed from review of #20637 — the reporter correctly identified a symptom but couldn't see the root cause because aidevops has no drift visibility. Audit confirms 3 affected repos on the filer's workspace. Interactive session on main (2026-04-24).

## Related

title: aidevops sync-workflows: opt-in resync for drifted framework workflows in downstream repos
body:
## Task

Implement `aidevops sync-workflows` (new subcommand) — opt-in command that copies framework-owned workflows from `$INSTALL_DIR/.github/workflows/` into registered downstream repos, refusing on locally-modified files. Dry-run by default; `--apply` required for writes.

## Why

Phase 1 (`aidevops check-workflows`, filed separately) surfaces drift but requires the user to manually `cp` the file into every drifted repo. This phase provides the one-step remediation. Without it, users have read-only visibility into drift but no ergonomic fix path — the same cp-by-hand ceremony that let #20637's bug go undetected on 3 of 31 registered repos for weeks.

**Hard constraint: never silently overwrite local modifications.** Refuse (exit non-zero) if a workflow's local hash doesn't match either the current canon or any known historical canon hash from the aidevops git history.

## How

**Depends on Phase 1** — blocked-by:#20648. Must land after Phase 1's drift classifier helper (`check-workflows-helper.sh`) exists; this phase extends it with write operations.

**Modify:**

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh` — add `sync_workflows()` function + `--sync` subcommand flag dispatched from the same helper. Keep detection and remediation in one helper for shared primitives.
- EDIT: `aidevops.sh` — add `cmd_sync_workflows()` that invokes `check-workflows-helper.sh sync [flags]`. Dispatch case in main switch near `cmd_check_workflows`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows.sh` — extend with sync scenarios (dry-run, apply, modified-locally refusal, filter flags).
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — document both subcommands together under a "Workflow sync" subsection.

**Flags:**

```
aidevops sync-workflows                        # dry-run; print planned changes, exit 0
aidevops sync-workflows --apply                # actually copy files
aidevops sync-workflows --repo <slug>          # limit to one repo
aidevops sync-workflows --workflow <name>      # limit to one workflow file
aidevops sync-workflows --force                # bypass MODIFIED-LOCALLY refusal
                                               # (prints warning, still logs what was overwritten)
```

**Algorithm:**

```
reuse_classifier_from_phase1

for each repo with status=DRIFTED:
  for each workflow where local=STALE (or any non-CURRENT, if Phase 1 didn't split):
    if --apply:
      cp "$canon" "$local" (preserve mode via cp -p)
      log: "cp: $canon → $local"
    else:
      print: "would copy: $workflow in $repo ($bytes_before → $bytes_after)"
  for each workflow where local=MODIFIED-LOCALLY (only if Phase 1 detects this):
    if --force:
      cp anyway, log with WARNING
    else:
      print refusal diagnostic:
        "  $workflow in $repo has local modifications (hash doesn't match any
         known aidevops canon). To accept the aidevops version, either:
           (a) delete the local file, commit, then run sync-workflows --apply
           (b) inspect the diff and rebase your local mods onto the new canon
           (c) use --force to overwrite (not recommended)"
      exit 1 at end
```

**Output format:**

Dry-run:

```
Dry-run plan (aidevops sync-workflows):

  <webapp>:
    issue-sync.yml: DRIFTED → will replace
      diff: -659 +1331 lines, hash 3a7f2e1 → 48f57e5
  really-simple-ssl-multisite:
    issue-sync.yml: DRIFTED → will replace
      diff: -681 +1331 lines
  compressx-multisite:
    issue-sync.yml: DRIFTED → will replace
      diff: -714 +1331 lines

Apply with: aidevops sync-workflows --apply
No commits made — review and commit per-repo after applying.
```

Apply:

```
Applying (aidevops sync-workflows --apply):

  [1/3] <webapp>: cp .../aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml → .../<webapp>/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml
  [2/3] really-simple-ssl-multisite: cp ...
  [3/3] compressx-multisite: cp ...

Synced 3 workflows across 3 repos.

Next step: review, commit, and push each repo. The helper does NOT commit —
workflow changes should be reviewed per-repo since they affect CI.

Suggested commit message: "chore: resync issue-sync.yml from aidevops v$(cat $INSTALL_DIR/VERSION)"
```

## Acceptance

1. Default is dry-run; `--apply` flag required for writes.
2. Never overwrites MODIFIED-LOCALLY workflows without `--force`. Refusal path prints the three-option diagnostic and exits 1.
3. On apply: uses `cp -p` to preserve file modes. No git operations (user commits manually per-repo).
4. `--repo` + `--workflow` filters compose: `--repo <webapp> --workflow issue-sync.yml` limits to one pair.
5. Running `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` against the current workspace correctly resyncs the 3 known-drifted repos (`<webapp>`, `really-simple-ssl-multisite`, `compressx-multisite`), and subsequent `aidevops check-workflows` reports 0 DRIFTED.
6. Test file passes: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows.sh` with new sync test cases.
7. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh` passes with zero violations.

## Verification

```bash
# Dry-run
aidevops sync-workflows
# Expected: lists the 3 DRIFTED repos, exit 0

# Apply
aidevops sync-workflows --apply
# Expected: copies files, prints per-repo success

# Re-check
aidevops check-workflows
# Expected: exit 0 (all CURRENT)

# Filter
aidevops sync-workflows --repo <webapp> --workflow issue-sync.yml --apply

# Refusal test (simulate local mod)
echo "# local mod" >> /path/to/some-repo/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml
aidevops sync-workflows
# Expected: MODIFIED-LOCALLY diagnostic, exit 1 (without --force)

# Unit tests + shellcheck
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh
```

## Session Origin

Filed from review of #20637. Phase 1 provides visibility; this phase provides ergonomic fix. Interactive session on main (2026-04-24). Depends on Phase 1 landing first (shared helper file).

## Related

- Phase 1: `aidevops check-workflows` (drift detector) — this phase's blocker

title: t2773: pulse: route reconcile sub-stages through pulse-prefetch-cache (Phase 2 of #20622)
body:
## What

Route `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` reconcile sub-stages through the existing `pulse-prefetch-cache.json` instead of each sub-stage making its own `gh issue list` calls. The prefetch stage already fetches this data per-cycle — downstream stages duplicate the work.

This is **Phase 2 of parent-task #20622** (prefetch cache extension). Complements #20642 (Phase 1: route calls through REST-fallback wrappers). Phase 2 eliminates the calls entirely in the hot path.

For #20622.

## Why

Evidence in parent #20622:

- `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` contains **13 direct `gh issue list` / `gh pr list` call sites**.
- Each runs per-cycle, per-repo. At 3 pulse-enabled repos × 30 cycles/hour = 1,170 duplicate calls/hour.
- Meanwhile `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` already fetches the same issue lists and caches them at `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-prefetch-cache.json` (cache shape already includes `issues` array with `number`, `title`, `labels` per repo).
- Prior work (t2574, t2744) routed `gh_issue_list` wrapper calls through REST fallback, but reconcile stages bypass the wrapper because they invoke `gh issue list` directly with custom JSON queries.

Reading from the already-fetched cache is cheaper than any REST fallback — it's zero API calls.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — refactor the five reconcile sub-stages to accept a pre-fetched issue/PR list from the cache. Sub-stage list (verify with `grep -nE '^(reconcile_|close_issues_with_merged_prs)' .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`):
  - `close_issues_with_merged_prs` (line ~632)
  - `reconcile_stale_done_issues` (line ~738)
  - `reconcile_open_issues_with_merged_prs` (line ~846)
  - `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` (line ~1398)
  - `reconcile_labelless_aidevops_issues` (line ~1540)

  For each sub-stage: replace the local `gh issue list ... --json ...` call with a `jq` filter over `pulse-prefetch-cache.json`. The cache already contains `number`, `title`, `labels`, plus whatever the prefetch stage requested. If a sub-stage needs a field the prefetch doesn't fetch, extend the prefetch stage (see second bullet) rather than re-fetching here.

- **EDIT (if needed):** `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` — widen the `--json` field list on its `gh issue list` call to include every field the reconcile sub-stages read. Cost is one extra field per issue, paid once per cycle, vs N×5 `gh issue list` calls amortised across reconcile stages.

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh` or `pulse-prefetch-infra.sh` — ensure the cache file is populated BEFORE `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` runs. Verify with the existing pulse stage order (`rg 'pulse-prefetch|pulse-issue-reconcile' .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`).

### Reference pattern

`.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-infra.sh:487` — `tmp_file=$(mktemp "${cache_dir}/.pulse-prefetch-cache.XXXXXX")` shows the atomic-write pattern used by prefetch. Reading back in reconcile uses plain `jq` over `PULSE_PREFETCH_CACHE_FILE` (env var defined at `pulse-wrapper.sh:343`).

### Cache-miss fallback

If `pulse-prefetch-cache.json` is missing, stale (>10 minutes old), or lacks a repo's entry, fall back to the existing `gh_issue_list` wrapper (from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`) — NOT raw `gh issue list`. This preserves the REST fallback path from Phase 1 (#20642) as a safety net.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-infra.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh

# After fix: direct gh issue list calls in reconcile should drop sharply
rg -nE 'gh (issue|pr) list' .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh | wc -l
# Expect: near-zero (only the cache-miss fallback path remaining, and that goes
#         through gh_issue_list wrapper — not bare gh)

# Prefetch cache is read by reconcile
rg -n 'pulse-prefetch-cache|PULSE_PREFETCH_CACHE_FILE' .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
# Expect: multiple matches (one per sub-stage)

# Unit tests still pass
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh 2>&1 | tail -5

# Smoke test — live pulse run with cache present, confirm reconcile stages behave identically
pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh restart-if-running
tail -f ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep -E 'reconcile|close_issues'
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Each of the five reconcile sub-stages reads from `pulse-prefetch-cache.json` when the cache is fresh.
2. Cache-miss fallback goes through `gh_issue_list` / `gh_pr_list` wrappers — not bare `gh` calls.
3. `rg 'gh issue list|gh pr list' .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` returns no matches outside the fallback path.
4. No functional regression — the set of issues flagged/closed by reconcile before and after is identical on the same repo state.
5. `gh api rate_limit` graph: GraphQL `remaining` curve during a 30-minute pulse run trends noticeably higher than pre-change.

### Non-scope

- Do NOT expand the prefetch cache contents beyond what reconcile needs. Fields reconcile does not use stay out.
- Do NOT modify the five reconcile sub-stages' decision logic. This is a pure data-source swap.
- Do NOT reduce pulse cycle frequency — that's Phase 3 (#TBD).
- Do NOT collapse the five sub-stages into a single pass — that's Phase 4 (#TBD).

title: t2775: pulse: per-repo pulse_interval throttle for contributor-role repos (Phase 3 of #20622)
body:
## What

Add a per-repo `pulse_interval` (seconds) override to `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` and honour it in the pulse dispatch loop. Contributor-role repos don't need the same 120-second polling cadence as maintainer repos; widening the interval for low-activity repos linearly reduces GraphQL budget consumption.

This is **Phase 3 of parent-task #20622** (reduce cycle frequency). Independent of Phase 2 (prefetch-cache extension, #TBD) and Phase 4 (reconcile consolidation, #TBD) — can ship in parallel.

For #20622.

## Why

Evidence in parent #20622:

- Pulse timer is 120s (hardcoded default) = ~30 cycles/hour.
- With 3 pulse-enabled repos, each cycle fans out API calls per-repo across ~20 stages.
- Contributor-role repos (e.g. external projects we only monitor for PR review) don't need 2-minute polling. A 5 or 10-minute interval is sufficient for any human-driven signal.
- Existing `repos.json` already has `pulse_hours` (window) and `pulse_expires` (opt-out sunset). `pulse_interval` is the missing polling-cadence knob.

If a contributor repo moves from 120s to 600s intervals, its per-cycle API cost drops 5×. Three contributor repos at 600s saves ~1,000 GraphQL points/hour of headroom for maintainer repos and worker dispatch.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` schema — NO local edit needed in this PR (user-owned config). Document in reference docs that `pulse_interval` may be set per-repo. Do NOT ship a default value in repo entries — unset means "use `PULSE_INTERVAL_SECS` global default (120s)".

title: t2776: pulse: consolidate reconcile sub-stages into single-pass iterator (Phase 4 of #20622)
body:
## What

Consolidate the five reconcile sub-stages in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` into a single pass that fetches (or reads from cache) the issue list ONCE per repo, then runs all reconcile logic against that shared result.

This is **Phase 4 of parent-task #20622** (reconcile consolidation). Depends on **Phase 2 (#TBD)** landing first — Phase 2 establishes the cache-read pattern; Phase 4 is structural cleanup on top of it.

For #20622.

## Why

Evidence in parent #20622:

- Current shape: five sub-stages (`close_issues_with_merged_prs`, `reconcile_stale_done_issues`, `reconcile_open_issues_with_merged_prs`, `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks`, `reconcile_labelless_aidevops_issues`) each call `gh issue list` (or after Phase 2, read the cache) independently.
- Even after Phase 2 routes all of these to the cache, each sub-stage still iterates the full issue list independently. Five loops over N issues per repo = 5N iterations per cycle.
- Consolidating into one pass: one iteration over N issues per repo, applying all five reconcile checks per issue. 5N → N.
- Beyond the loop savings, consolidation also eliminates the shellcheck/maintenance cost of five near-duplicate prelude blocks (fetch cache, parse JSON, bail if empty, etc.).

This is structural cleanup — correctness-preserving, no behavioural change. Savings compound with Phase 2's cache-read savings.

## How

### Dependency gate

**Do not start this issue until Phase 2 (#TBD) is merged.** Phase 2 introduces the `pulse-prefetch-cache.json` read pattern into `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`; Phase 4 collapses the five call sites into one. Without Phase 2, this issue would duplicate the cache-migration work.

If Phase 2 is still in progress when this is dispatched, the worker should post a comment citing the dependency and exit BLOCKED (reason: `blocked-by:#<phase2-issue>`).

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — replace the top-level orchestrator (currently a sequence of function calls, one per sub-stage) with a single-pass iterator:

  ```
  # Pseudocode for the consolidated pass:
  issues = jq '.[].issues[]' pulse-prefetch-cache.json
  for issue in issues:
      if should_close_merged_pr(issue): close_merged_pr_action(issue)
      if should_reconcile_stale_done(issue): stale_done_action(issue)
      if should_reconcile_open_merged(issue): open_merged_action(issue)
      if should_reconcile_completed_parent(issue): completed_parent_action(issue)
      if should_reconcile_labelless(issue): labelless_action(issue)
  ```

  Each sub-stage becomes a `should_*` predicate + `*_action` pair. The existing function names stay as the action functions; new `should_*` predicates lift the `gh issue list --search` filter queries out of each sub-stage into inline JSON predicates over the already-fetched issue record.

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — extend to cover the consolidation: same input fixtures, same expected output set.

### Reference pattern

The consolidation pattern mirrors how `pulse-merge.sh` already orchestrates its per-PR checks (one PR list fetched, multiple checks applied per PR). Read that file for the idiom.

### Behaviour preservation

Per-predicate ordering must match the current sub-stage order. Some issues may match multiple predicates; in the current code each sub-stage runs in sequence, so an issue closed by sub-stage 1 (`close_issues_with_merged_prs`) is never seen by sub-stage 2. Preserve this: predicates are evaluated in the same order per issue, and an action that closes/modifies the issue short-circuits subsequent predicates for that issue.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh

## Verification

```
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh

# Unit test: fixture issue list exercising each of the five reconcile predicates;
#            assert the set of actions taken equals the pre-change set.
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh

# Line count: consolidated reconcile file should be shorter than pre-change
#             (target: ≥15% reduction from de-duplicated preludes)
wc -l .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh

# Smoke test — live pulse run, confirm same set of issues is reconciled before/after:
#   1. Take diff of gh api issues pre-change
#   2. Run pulse for one cycle
#   3. Diff gh api issues post-change
#   4. Run pulse for one cycle on the new script
#   5. Same issue-state deltas should result
```

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` has a single top-level orchestrator that iterates the issue list ONCE per repo.
2. Each of the five reconcile checks is expressible as a `should_*` predicate + `*_action` function pair.
3. Predicate evaluation order preserves pre-change sub-stage order for any given issue.
4. Unit tests pass with identical action set as pre-change.
5. No behavioural regression on a 1-hour live pulse run against a maintainer repo (same set of issues reconciled, same set closed).

### Non-scope

- Do NOT change the decision logic inside any individual reconcile check.
- Do NOT modify the prefetch cache shape (that's Phase 2).
- Do NOT adjust per-repo interval throttling (that's Phase 3).
- Do NOT parallelise the per-issue loop; sequential iteration preserves the short-circuit semantics.

title: Phase 3: refactor framework workflows to GitHub reusable-workflow pattern (eliminate drift class)
body:
## Task

Refactor aidevops's framework-owned GitHub Actions workflows into GitHub-native **reusable workflows** (`on: workflow_call:`), with downstream repos consuming them via tiny caller YAMLs. Eliminate per-repo script and workflow drift as an architectural class.

## Why

**Root cause we're correcting**: Framework logic was replicated per-repo instead of shared. Audit of 31 registered repos turned up 3 drifted `issue-sync.yml` copies at 659/681/714 lines vs canon 1331. Two of those 3 (`<webapp>`, `compressx-multisite`) are actively **failing every workflow run** because they have the workflow YAML but zero `.agents/scripts/` — the shell scripts the workflow calls don't exist. The third (`really-simple-ssl-multisite`) has drifted scripts too.

Phases 1 and 2 (#20648, #20649) patch the leak. This phase fixes the design so the leak can't reoccur.

**Architectural principle**: a framework that ships executable logic should have ONE source of truth for that logic. Downstream repos should opt in with configuration, not by cloning the implementation. Reusable workflows are GitHub's first-class mechanism for exactly this.

## How

### Design

**Current (replicated) model:**

```
aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← 1331 lines of logic
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh  ← framework shell
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh
aidevops/.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh

downstream-repo/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← copied, drifts
downstream-repo/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh  ← copied, drifts
downstream-repo/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh  ← copied, drifts
downstream-repo/.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh  ← copied, drifts
```

**New (reusable) model:**

```
aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml  ← 1331 lines, `on: workflow_call:`
aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← ~25-line caller for aidevops's own CI
aidevops/.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml  ← canonical caller template
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh  ← unchanged, framework source of truth
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh
aidevops/.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh

downstream-repo/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← ~25-line caller, stable
(no .agents/scripts/ needed — fetched at runtime)
```

### Implementation steps

**Step 1 — Refactor `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` into reusable + caller:**

- NEW: `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` — contains ALL current jobs from `issue-sync.yml`, with:
  - Top-level trigger changed to `on: workflow_call:` with `inputs:` and `secrets:` declared
  - Each job's existing `if: github.event_name == '<X>'` guards kept (they reflect the caller's event, which is correct behaviour in reusable workflows)
  - A new first step in every job: `actions/checkout@v4` with `repository: marcusquinn/aidevops, path: __aidevops, ref: <version>` — fetches framework scripts at runtime so downstream repos don't need them checked in
  - Every `bash .agents/scripts/...` call rewritten to `bash __aidevops/.agents/scripts/...`
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` — becomes a thin ~25-line caller that uses the reusable workflow via relative path: `uses: ./.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`. Preserves aidevops's own CI behaviour end-to-end.

**Step 2 — Create the canonical caller template:**

- NEW: `.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml` — the exact YAML downstream repos should carry. Model:

```yaml
# Managed by aidevops framework. Upstream logic: marcusquinn/aidevops.
# Do not edit — call aidevops check-workflows / sync-workflows to manage.
name: Issue Sync
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'TODO.md'
      - 'todo/PLANS.md'
      - 'todo/tasks/**'
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, closed, reopened]
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      command:
        description: 'Sync command'
        required: true
        default: 'status'
        type: choice
        options: [status, pull, push, close, reconcile, enrich]

jobs:
  sync:
    uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml@main
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      command: ${{ inputs.command || '' }}
```

- Include a commented-out pinned-version alternative at the top (`@v3.9.0` style) so users can opt into stable pinning.

**Step 3 — Integrate with `aidevops init`:**

- EDIT: `aidevops-init-lib.sh` — in `cmd_init`, add opt-in scaffolding for the caller YAML when `--features` includes `planning` (or a new `workflows` feature flag). Users can explicitly decline.
- EDIT: `.aidevops.json` feature schema — add `workflows` field alongside `planning`, `git_workflow`, etc. Default false (opt-in, not auto-added to existing repos).

**Step 4 — Documentation:**

- NEW: `.agents/reference/reusable-workflows.md` — architecture doc. Covers:
  - Why reusable workflows (this issue's Why section)
  - How the caller + reusable split works
  - Pinning strategies (`@main` vs `@vX.Y.Z` — tradeoffs and recommendation)
  - How `aidevops init`, `aidevops check-workflows`, `aidevops sync-workflows` interact with this model
  - Migration guide from old copied-workflow model
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — add a "Workflow architecture" subsection pointing at the new reference doc.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` lines around 69-79 — update the SYNC_PAT description to reflect the reusable-workflow model (still per-repo secret, but the workflow file is no longer per-repo).

**Step 5 — Phase 1 + Phase 2 alignment:**

- Phase 1 (#20648) detector needs to know that "canonical downstream state" = the caller template, NOT the full 1331-line workflow. Update its manifest.
- Phase 2 (#20649) resync action becomes "install caller template", which effectively migrates any drifted full-copy repo to the caller pattern. This replaces Phase 2's originally-scoped "cp to canon" action — it's actually a better Phase 2.

**Step 6 — Tests:**

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh` — validates the caller template is syntactically correct and references a real aidevops workflow.
- EXTEND: any existing CI that validates workflow YAML should cover the new reusable workflow + caller.

### Decisions this issue resolves

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Where does logic live? | Reusable workflow in aidevops | Single source of truth |
| How are scripts loaded? | Runtime `actions/checkout` of aidevops | Eliminates script drift as a class |
| Caller pinning strategy | Default `@main`, document `@vX.Y.Z` | Auto-update for power users, pinning available for stability |
| Downstream `.agents/scripts/` | Can be removed | No longer needed by the workflow |
| Secret handling | `secrets: inherit` in caller | SYNC_PAT still per-repo, but workflow code doesn't care |
| aidevops's own use | Thin caller pointing at reusable via relative path | Same pattern as downstream, single architecture |

### Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Runtime `actions/checkout` of aidevops slows workflow | Checkout is ~2s — negligible vs existing multi-minute sync runs |
| `@main` pinning exposes downstream to breaking changes | Caller template header documents `@vX.Y.Z` pinning option; aidevops keeps breaking changes behind feature flags |
| Reusable workflow can't see caller's `.agents/scripts/` customisations | Intentional — customisations should be upstreamed, not repo-forked |
| GitHub Actions secret `inherit` requires modern GH version | GHES 3.7+ and all GitHub.com — no issue in practice |

## Acceptance

1. `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` exists, has `on: workflow_call:`, and contains the 4 jobs currently in `issue-sync.yml`.
2. `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` becomes a thin caller (`< 50 lines`) that invokes the reusable workflow via `uses: ./.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`.
3. `.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml` exists and is copy-pasteable into any downstream repo.
4. aidevops's own `issue-sync` behaviour on CI is preserved end-to-end — verified by at least one full run on a PR that touches `TODO.md`.
5. `.agents/reference/reusable-workflows.md` exists and documents the architecture + pinning strategy.
6. `aidevops init` can scaffold the caller YAML as an opt-in feature.
7. Migrating the 3 known-drifted repos (`<webapp>`, `really-simple-ssl-multisite`, `compressx-multisite`) to the caller pattern: the caller YAML works; `aidevops check-workflows` reports OK after migration; at least one test run of the reusable workflow (e.g., a TODO.md push) succeeds in each migrated repo.
8. `shellcheck` passes on any new shell code.
9. Workflow YAML passes `actionlint` if available, or at minimum GitHub parses it (CI runs to completion).

## Verification

```bash
# Syntactic check on the reusable workflow
actionlint .github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml
actionlint .github/workflows/issue-sync.yml
actionlint .github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml

# End-to-end aidevops CI test
# (push a TODO.md change on a test branch and observe the sync workflow)

# Downstream migration test
cd ~/Git/<webapp>  # (or one of the drifted repos)
# Replace workflow with caller template, push, verify the reusable workflow fires
gh run watch

# Drift audit after migration
aidevops check-workflows
# Expected: 0 DRIFTED (all migrated repos now carry identical caller YAML)
```

## Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` (NEW)
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` (EDIT — becomes thin caller)
- `.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml` (NEW)
- `.agents/reference/reusable-workflows.md` (NEW)
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` (EDIT — add workflow-architecture subsection)
- `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` (EDIT — update SYNC_PAT context around lines 69-79)
- `aidevops-init-lib.sh` (EDIT — add opt-in caller scaffolding)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh` (NEW)

## Session Origin

Interactive session on main (2026-04-24). Filed as follow-up to review of #20637. Target architecture for workflow management across the 31+ registered repos in `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json`. Blocks clean completion of Phase 1 (#20648) and Phase 2 (#20649) — both should reference the new caller template once this lands.

## Related

- #20637 (symptom — closed as stale downstream)
- #20648 — Phase 1 drift detector (becomes "detect callers that don't match template")
- #20649 — Phase 2 opt-in resync (becomes "install caller template")
- Prior art: this is the first time aidevops adopts the reusable-workflow pattern. Future framework workflows (`maintainer-gate.yml`, `linked-issue-check.yml`, etc.) follow the same pattern.

title: t2780: sync-workflows-helper: rewrite on.push.branches filter to match downstream default branch
body:
## Task

`sync-workflows-helper.sh` installs the canonical `issue-sync-caller.yml` verbatim when migrating a repo from NEEDS-MIGRATION. The canonical template hardcodes `on.push.branches: [main]`, so any downstream repo with a non-`main` default branch ends up with a workflow that never fires.

Evidence: <webapp> (default branch `develop`) was migrated by v3.10.0 (PR #20673, GH#20649) — the installed workflow had `branches: [main]` and required a manual follow-up PR (<webapp>/<webapp>#2700) to change to `[develop]`.

## Why

The whole point of reusable-workflow migration is to eliminate drift and let downstream repos pick up framework updates for free. A trigger filter that doesn't match the default branch breaks the feature silently — `TODO.md` pushes don't trigger issue sync, and the repo looks healthy in `aidevops check-workflows` (post the upcoming detector fix).

## How

Two cooperating changes needed:

1. **`sync-workflows-helper.sh` at install/refresh time** — detect the downstream default branch (`git -C "$_path" symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD | sed 's|^origin/||'`, same call already used in `_sync_preflight`) and rewrite `branches: [main]` to `branches: [<actual-default>]` in the rendered content before writing. `_render_template_with_ref` already parameterises `@ref`; add a second `sed` pass for the branch filter.

2. **`check-workflows-helper.sh` when diffing** — normalise both sides of the comparison so a repo whose workflow references `branches: [develop]` and otherwise matches canonical is classified `CURRENT/CALLER`, not `DRIFTED/CALLER`. Simplest approach: both tools agree on a canonical "%%DEFAULT_BRANCH%%" placeholder or the detector substitutes the downstream default before diffing.

Model the rewrite on the existing `_render_template_with_ref` function in `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` — it already demonstrates the rewrite-on-install pattern for `@ref`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-sync-workflows-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-check-workflows-helper.sh

## Acceptance

- [ ] A repo with `default branch = develop` is classified `CURRENT/CALLER` (not DRIFTED) after `aidevops sync-workflows --apply`.
- [ ] <webapp> specifically returns `CURRENT/CALLER` after the upstream fix ships.
- [ ] New fixture test in `test-sync-workflows-helper.sh` covering a `develop` default branch.
- [ ] New fixture test in `test-check-workflows-helper.sh` covering a mock repo with `branches: [develop]` + otherwise canonical content returning CURRENT/CALLER.
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations; bash 3.2 parse; no function exceeds 100 lines.

## Session Origin

Surfaced during post-release verification of v3.10.0 workflow drift elimination (Phase 2, #20649). <webapp> workflow installed but didn't fire on develop pushes; manual follow-up PR (<webapp>/<webapp>#2700) shipped the one-line fix.

Ref: GH#20649 (Phase 2)
Related: `reference/reusable-workflows.md` (t2770)

title: t2781: pulse: worker retry-with-backoff on repeated rate_limit failures
body:
## What

Add per-issue rate_limit backoff to `dispatch_with_dedup` — track recent `rate_limit` exits per issue number, skip dispatch if cooldown is active, escalate to exponential backoff after Nth failure on same issue.

## Why

`headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` shows **407 rate_limit events totalling 1,894 min (~31.5h) of worker burn** in the recent tail. Same issues repeatedly dispatched on the same throttled account produce the same failure:

- `issue-20641` (2× rate_limit, 103 min total)
- `issue-2662` (3× rate_limit, 67 min total)
- `issue-15018` (6 retries), `issue-15087` (5 retries), `issue-15015` (4 retries)
- `supervisor-pulse` itself: 12 rate_limit events

No backoff means we pay the full token cost trying the same path on the same throttled account immediately after failure. This is the single largest token-saver available in the pipeline today.

## How

Model on the per-issue `no_work` circuit breaker (t2769, #20639 — merged). Same structure, different input signal.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `dispatch_with_dedup` function; add rate_limit history check as a new dedup layer BEFORE the dispatch call
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-backoff-helper.sh` — compute backoff window for a given issue from `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` (last N hours)
- Reference pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — grep for `no_work` circuit breaker call pattern and `_has_active_claim` style dedup-layer shape
- Optional integration: `model-accounts-pool-helper.sh` — if rate_limit was tied to a specific account, allow dispatch via a different account instead of blocking

Backoff schedule (suggested, tune after first observation):

| Nth failure | Cooldown |
|---|---|
| 1 | 5 min |
| 2 | 30 min |
| 3 | 2 h |
| 4+ | 24 h + apply `needs-maintainer-review` label |

## Acceptance

1. `dispatch-backoff-helper.sh check <issue_num> <slug>` returns exit 0 if clear, exit 1 if cooldown active; prints reason and next-eligible timestamp on stderr.
2. `dispatch_with_dedup` calls the helper as a dedup layer; blocked dispatches log `BACKOFF_ACTIVE reason=rate_limit_cooldown next=<ts>` to `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`.
3. Unit test: simulate 2 `rate_limit` exits on same issue within 5 min (append two lines to a fixture `.jsonl`), confirm 3rd dispatch is blocked for 30 min.
4. Verify in a live pulse cycle: `tail -100 ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | grep BACKOFF_ACTIVE` surfaces at least one entry within 24h of merging.
5. Counter added to `pulse-stats.json`: `dispatch_backoff_skipped`.

## Session Origin

Filed interactively by marcusquinn from pulse/worker productivity review (2026-04-24). Evidence: `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` analysis — 407 rate_limit events / 31.5h burn across recent history.

title: t2782: worker: cap watchdog_stall_continue duration and count per session
body:
## What

Cap maximum duration and count of `watchdog_stall_continue` events per worker session. Current behavior: activity watchdog warns on 300s silence but lets the worker continue indefinitely. Five stalls of 75+ min observed in a single 24h window.

## Why

Top token burns from `watchdog_stall_continue` (exit code 78, the "continue" variant):

| Session | Stall duration |
|---|---|
| pr-conflict-2669 | 89 min |
| issue-2455 | 86 min |
| issue-2650 | 77 min |
| issue-2461 | 75 min |
| supervisor-pulse | 25 min (ongoing) |

These are workers that lost tool-call activity for 300s, watchdog warned, worker kept running in a stalled state for 60+ more minutes burning context tokens but producing no output. Unbounded stall-continue is a pure token sink — the worker cannot recover autonomously once in this state.

## How

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — grep for `watchdog_stall_continue`, find the "continue" branch, add a per-session stall counter and cumulative-time tracker
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh` OR `.agents/scripts/worker-watchdog.sh` — the process-side monitor; escalate to SIGTERM on Nth event OR once cumulative stall time exceeds cap
- Reference pattern: look at the existing hard-kill path in `worker-watchdog.sh` — the signalling exists, we're just widening its trigger

### Config (new env knobs, validated via `_validate_int` in `pulse-wrapper.sh`)

- `WORKER_STALL_CONTINUE_MAX` — default 3. Max stall-continue events per session before hard-kill.
- `WORKER_STALL_CUMULATIVE_MAX_S` — default 1800 (30 min). Max cumulative stall time before hard-kill.

Either trigger fires: SIGTERM → 10s grace → SIGKILL.

## Acceptance

1. After Nth `watchdog_stall_continue` event OR cumulative stall time exceeds cap (whichever first), worker receives SIGTERM; SIGKILL after 10s if still running.
2. Exit recorded as `watchdog_stall_killed` (NOT `_continue`) in `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` with `exit_code` reflecting the kill signal.
3. Config knobs honored: env override works AND default fires when env unset. `_validate_int` guards bad values.
4. Unit test: simulate 4 stall events on a mock worker via injected fixtures, confirm kill fires at N=3.
5. Verify in live pulse: 24h after merge, no `watchdog_stall_continue` events over 35 min in `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`.

## Session Origin

Filed interactively by marcusquinn from pulse/worker productivity review (2026-04-24). Evidence: `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` showing 5 stalls >75 min in 24h.

title: t2783: pulse: post remediation comment when maintainer manually removes NMR label (ever-NMR block)
body:
## What

When a maintainer manually removes the `needs-maintainer-review` label from an issue WITHOUT using `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>`, post a one-shot explanatory comment noting the `ever-NMR` history flag is still set and dispatch will continue to skip until cryptographic approval lands.

## Why

Silent dispatch block creates avoidable confusion. Observed 2026-04-24: maintainer removed NMR labels from <webapp>#2639 and #2649, expected dispatch to resume, pulse continued to silently skip with:

```
[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_with_dedup: BLOCKED #2639 in <webapp>/<webapp> — requires cryptographic approval (ever-NMR)
```

IF label `needs-maintainer-review` is absent

title: t2788: Extend _parse_phases_section to accept narrative bold-heading form (Phase 1 of #20559)

## What

Extend `_parse_phases_section` in `shared-phase-filing.sh` to recognise `**Phase N — description**` bold-heading form (in addition to the existing `- Phase N - description` list form). Add support for an opt-in marker system for narrative phases.

Ref #20559 — Phase 1 of the parent-task phase-lifecycle automation fix.

## Why

Currently `_parse_phases_section` only matches list-form phase declarations (`- Phase N - desc`). Parent issues using bold-heading narrative form (`**Phase N — desc**`) — which is common in hand-authored issue bodies — are invisible to the parser. This means the sequential auto-file mechanism (t2740) cannot fire for narrative-format parents, and the Phase 2 close-guard (which depends on this parser) cannot count declared phases accurately.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-phase-filing.sh:122-179` — extend `_parse_phases_section` to also match lines like `**Phase N — description**` or `**Phase N — description [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]**`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-phase-filing.sh` — add test cases for bold-heading form

### Implementation steps

1. In `_parse_phases_section` (line 140 onwards), after the existing list-form match (`grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]+[Pp]hase[[:space:]]+[0-9]+'`), add an `elif` branch matching bold-heading form: `grep -qE '^\*\*[Pp]hase[[:space:]]+[0-9]+'`.

2. For bold-heading matches, extract the same 4 fields (phase_num, description, marker, child_ref):
   - `phase_num`: extract from `**Phase N` 
   - `description`: text between the separator (` — ` or ` - `) and the closing `**`, minus any trailing marker bracket
   - `marker`: default to `none` for narrative form (safe default). Support explicit trailing markers like `[auto-fire:on-prior-merge]` if present inside or after the `**...**`
   - `child_ref`: trailing `#NNN` after the closing `**` (same pattern as list form)

3. Support an HTML comment opt-in marker `<!-- phase-auto-fire:on -->` anywhere in the parent body that flips ALL narrative phases to `auto-fire` marker. Check for this before the per-line loop and set a default override.

4. Add tests in `test-shared-phase-filing.sh` covering:

   - Explicit `[auto-fire:on-prior-merge]` marker on bold form overrides default

title: t2786: Add phase-declaration-aware guard to _try_close_parent_tracker (Phase 2 of #20559)
body:
## What

Add a declared-vs-filed guard in `_try_close_parent_tracker` to prevent premature parent closure when some declared phases have not yet been filed as child issues.

Ref #20559 — Phase 2 of the parent-task phase-lifecycle automation fix.

## Why

Currently `_try_close_parent_tracker` counts closed children and closes the parent when all filed children are closed. But if the parent declares 3 phases and only 1 has been filed as a child issue, the parent gets closed prematurely when that single child merges. The guard must compare declared phases (from the parser) against filed children before closing.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1354-1396` — add declared-vs-filed guard in `_try_close_parent_tracker`, after the `all_closed` check and before `gh issue close`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-lifecycle.sh` — add test cases for the three scenarios

### Implementation steps

1. After the existing `all_closed` check in `_try_close_parent_tracker` (around line 1380), add a call to `_parse_phases_section` on the parent body to count declared phases.

2. Compare declared phase count against filed child count:
   - If declared > filed: skip close, post a one-time nudge comment with marker `<!-- parent-declared-phases-unfiled -->` listing unfiled phases
   - If declared <= filed OR no Phases section exists: proceed with close as today

3. Use idempotent marker check — search existing comments for `<!-- parent-declared-phases-unfiled -->` before posting to avoid duplicate nudges.

4. Add tests covering:
   - (a) No `## Phases` section → close as today (backward compat)
   - (b) All declared phases filed as children, all closed → close parent
   - (c) Some declared phases unfiled → skip close + post nudge

### Reference pattern

## Task

Sweep-fix all remaining `grep -c … || echo "0"` counter-stacking violations across the codebase and reset the ratchet guard to zero-tolerance.

Phase 2 of parent #20581. Phase 1 (guard + helper) was completed in #20594 (PR #20621, #20645).

## Why

Phase 1 landed `safe_grep_count()` in `shared-constants.sh` and the `counter-stack-check.sh` ratchet gate. The gate currently baselines ~106 violations across ~50 files. Until these are swept, the bug class remains latent — zero-match paths produce `"0\n0"` instead of `"0"`, breaking numeric comparisons, arithmetic, and interpolated text.

## How

1. **Shell script that sources `shared-constants.sh`**: replace with `count=$(safe_grep_count … args …)`.
2. **Shell script that cannot source** (bootstrap, standalone CLI, test harness): use inline form:

title: prompt-guard-helper: role_play false-positive on literal 'dark mode' / 'light mode' in UI content
body:
## Problem

`prompt-guard-helper.sh` flags the literal English phrase "dark mode" / "light mode" as a HIGH-severity `role_play: Evil twin persona attempt` whenever it appears in any scanned content.

### Reproduction

Tested against `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (a public repo of design-focused skill markdown) during a security review. The scanner produced 5 HIGH findings across 5 SKILL.md files, all for the exact same phrase:

| File | Matched text |
|---|---|
| `skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/redesign-skill/SKILL.md` | `dark mode` |
| `skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |
| `imagegenskills/frontendwebsiteimageskill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |

Context from one of the files (`skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md:424-427`) is a palette-preset list, not an injection:

```text
1. Pristine Light Mode
2. Deep Dark Mode
3. Bold Studio Solid
4. Quiet Premium Neutral
```

### Why this is a false positive

The `role_play` pattern is intended to catch jailbreak invocations of the form `<adjective> mode` — "DAN mode", "developer mode", "evil mode", "godmode", "jailbreak mode". "Dark mode" and "light mode" are UI colour-theme terms in near-universal use across CSS, Tailwind, `prefers-color-scheme`, design systems, and user-facing product settings. Any scan over design content, CSS, theming docs, accessibility guidance, or UX writing will trip this pattern.

### Impact

- Every design-related skill or doc scanned through `prompt-guard-helper.sh` will produce spurious HIGH findings.
- Erodes trust in the scanner: when operators see HIGH findings turn out to be "dark mode", they may stop reading genuine findings carefully.
- Makes it harder to adopt third-party design skills — a clean repo produces alarming scan output.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh` — locate the `role_play` pattern definition. Likely in an inline regex list or in the YAML pattern file it loads from (check `configs/prompt-guard-patterns.yaml` or similar).

## Proposed fix

Two options, either is acceptable:

title: t2789: claim-task-id.sh: apply status:available by default so new issues are dispatchable immediately
body:
## What

`claim-task-id.sh` creates GitHub issues without applying `status:available` label by default. Issues created this way are invisible to the pulse dispatcher (which filters on `label:"status:available"`) until a downstream mechanism (issue-sync workflow, manual edit) adds the label.

## Why

Direct symptom: during session on 2026-04-24, 4 tasks (t2781-t2784, #20680-#20683) were filed via `claim-task-id.sh --title ... --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:standard,bug,framework,pulse"`. All 4 were created without `status:available`, making them invisible to `preflight_early_dispatch`. Required manual `gh issue edit --add-label "status:available"` intervention after 45 minutes of diagnosis.

Context: `claim-task-id.sh` is the canonical, recommended entry point for creating tasks (per AGENTS.md "Task IDs: `/new-task` or `claim-task-id.sh`. NEVER grep TODO.md for next ID"). It's used by `/new-task`, interactive agents, and directly by maintainers. Any issue created through it should be immediately dispatchable.

Root cause: the label-application logic (lines 294-339 of `claim-task-id.sh`) normalizes user-supplied labels via `map_tags_to_labels` but has no default baseline. Contrast with `issue-sync-helper.sh:621` which applies `status:available` on sync — but only when the TODO.md push triggers the workflow, which is a downstream event.

Impact: every `claim-task-id.sh`-created issue has a dispatch dead zone between creation and next issue-sync run (up to 60 min). If the user then commits TODO.md and pushes, issue-sync will re-apply the label — but the initial window is lost.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — after the label normalization block (after line ~340, where `TASK_LABELS` is finalized), add a default status label application before passing to `gh issue create`:

```bash
# Apply default status:available if no status label was provided (t2785)
if [[ ",${TASK_LABELS}," != *",status:"* ]]; then
  if [[ -n "$TASK_LABELS" ]]; then
    TASK_LABELS="${TASK_LABELS},status:available"
  else
    TASK_LABELS="status:available"
  fi
fi
```

- Reference pattern: `issue-sync-helper.sh:621` (`local status_label="status:available"`) shows the canonical label.
- Exclusion: `--status-label` flag override or explicit `status:blocked` / `status:queued` in `--labels` should be preserved (the check above handles this via the substring match).
- The fix MUST NOT apply to issues that already carry a `status:*` label from user input.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Issues created via `claim-task-id.sh --title "test"` have `status:available` applied from the `gh issue create` call itself (no race with downstream sync).
2. Issues created via `claim-task-id.sh --title "test" --labels "status:queued"` retain `status:queued` and do NOT get `status:available` added.
3. Existing behavior preserved: `--labels "auto-dispatch,tier:standard"` still results in auto-dispatch + tier:standard + status:available.
4. No duplicate labels applied (check idempotency).
5. Smoke test via dry-run flag or direct invocation, observing the resulting issue's labels.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` (label application block, ~line 340)

## Verification

```bash
# Dry-run or direct invocation in test repo
./claim-task-id.sh --title "test-status-default" --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:standard"
# Verify the created issue has status:available applied
gh issue view <N> --repo <slug> --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | sort'
# Should include: auto-dispatch, status:available, tier:standard
```

## Session Origin

Direct observation during interactive session on 2026-04-24T04:41Z. Filed 4 tasks (t2781-t2784) via `claim-task-id.sh`, observed they were invisible to pulse dispatcher for 45 min until manual `gh issue edit --add-label "status:available"` was applied. Root-caused via `grep -rn "status:available" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*.sh` — no auto-apply mechanism in claim-task-id.sh path.

title: t2796: worker_complete emitted on zero-output exit — classify as worker_noop to trigger cascade
body:
## What

`headless-runtime-helper.sh::_cmd_run_finalize` emits `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete` whenever the worker process exits with `ledger_status != "fail"` (i.e., exit code 0 after the orchestration runs). This classification does NOT check whether the worker produced any tangible output — it only checks that the process exited cleanly.

A worker that silently no-ops (zero commits, no branch pushed to remote, no PR opened) is reported as `worker_complete` — indistinguishable from a worker that genuinely shipped a PR. Downstream:

- Fast-fail counter is NOT incremented → tier escalation does not fire.
- No audit signal distinguishes "succeeded" from "no-op exit".
- The issue remains in dispatch limbo until a human or stale-recovery cycle intervenes.

## Why

**Evidence from t2789 incident (2026-04-24T14:10-14:19Z, issue #20713):**

- Worker dispatched (PID 14566, haiku tier) at 14:10:53Z.
- Worker released claim at 14:19:53Z with `reason=worker_complete`.
- No remote branch for `feature/auto-20260424-145010-gh20713` existed post-release.
- No PR was created linking to #20713.
- Orphan worktree `/Users/marcusquinn/Git/aidevops-feature-auto-20260424-145010-gh20713` had zero local commits on the feature branch.
- The claimed fix (adding `status:available` default to `claim-task-id.sh`) was absent from both source and deployed trees.

Effect: issue #20713 required manual recovery — an interactive session had to reimplement the fix (PR #20720). Without that intervention, the task would have sat indefinitely in a "looks complete per audit trail, actually zero output" state.

This is not unique to t2789. Any worker that:

1. Reads the issue and concludes "already fixed" (false positive — the fix isn't there).
2. Runs out of tokens before the commit stage but after model inference started.
3. Hits a logic branch in `/full-loop` that returns early without committing.
4. Creates a worktree but fails silently during the implementation phase.

...will emit `worker_complete` and appear in the audit trail as a successful run.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1102-1147` — `_cmd_run_finalize` block that emits `worker_complete` / `worker_failed`.

### Reference pattern

Check the worker's workspace (`$work_dir`) before emitting success classification:

1. Are there commits on the feature branch beyond the base (i.e., `git rev-list --count <base>..HEAD` > 0)?
2. Was a PR opened that links to this issue (i.e., `gh pr list --search "gh-<N>" --json number` returns results)?
3. Was a branch pushed to remote (i.e., `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>` returns output)?

If NONE of these hold, the worker did no tangible work. Emit a new classification:

```
_release_dispatch_claim "$session_key" "worker_noop"
_report_failure_to_fast_fail "$session_key" "worker_noop_zero_output" "no_work"
```

This triggers the fast-fail counter (so cascade dispatch fires on the next pulse cycle) and leaves a distinct audit signal (`worker_noop` vs `worker_complete`) for operators investigating stuck issues.

Alternative design: promote the check into a new helper `_worker_produced_output()` that returns 0/1 based on the three signals, so the classification branch stays readable.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh

### Discovery command

```bash
# Find current emission point:
grep -n "worker_complete\|worker_failed" .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh

# Find the base-branch resolution pattern used elsewhere:
grep -n "rev-list --count\|git log.*\.\." .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
```

## Verification

```bash
# Unit test: mock a worker that exits 0 with no commits → expect worker_noop
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh

# Shellcheck:
shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
```

Live verification will come on the next real worker dispatch: a successful PR-creating worker continues to emit `worker_complete`; a silent no-op worker emits `worker_noop` and fires fast-fail → cascade escalation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_cmd_run_finalize` emits `worker_noop` (not `worker_complete`) when the worker's work_dir has zero new commits AND no PR linking to the issue AND no pushed branch.
2. `worker_noop` increments the fast-fail counter (triggers cascade dispatch on next pulse cycle).
3. `worker_complete` is still emitted when ANY of the three output signals is present (commits OR PR OR pushed branch).
4. Test coverage in `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` for both paths (no-output → noop, any-output → complete).
5. Shellcheck zero violations on modified file.

## Non-scope

- Do NOT redefine `worker_failed` classification — its semantics (ledger_status="fail") are correct.
- Do NOT touch the `crash_type` classification in the fail path — that's orthogonal.
- Do NOT modify the TTL-based claim GC path — that's a different safety net.

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive session that diagnosed and manually recovered t2789 (PR #20720). The worker dispatched for #20713 exited `worker_complete` with zero output, making the failure invisible until the interactive session audited the remote branch state. This classification gap is the root cause — the fix ensures the audit trail reflects reality.

Related prior work:

- t1927/t2042: fast-fail counter and recovery (the mechanism this task plugs into).
- t2420: CLAIM_RELEASED label-clearing (the adjacent lifecycle signal).
- t2781: rate_limit backoff (another worker-lifecycle classification refinement).

Tested against `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (a public repo of design-focused skill markdown) during a security review. The scanner produced 5 HIGH findings across 5 SKILL.md files, all for the exact same phrase:

3. Bold Studio Solid

The `role_play` pattern is intended to catch jailbreak invocations of the form `<adjective> mode` — "DAN mode", "developer mode", "evil mode", "godmode", "jailbreak mode". Option A is more robust because it generalises to other UI terms (e.g., "focus mode", "presentation mode" in apps) without needing an ever-growing allow-list.

**Option preference:** Option A (remove `mode` from the noun alternation) is preferred over Option B (allow-list). Rationale:
- `mode` is the problematic noun — `dark twin`, `dark version`, `dark side`, `dark alter ego` remain jailbreak-specific and should still match.
- The existing inline pattern at `prompt-guard-helper.sh:272` already handles the legitimate jailbreak mode phrases: `Jailbreak|Unfiltered\s+mode|God\s+mode|Uncensored\s+mode`.
- "evil mode" / "shadow mode" as bare phrases are not common enough in adversarial prompts to justify the false-positive rate across all design/UI content.
- Contextual gating (reporter's alternative Option A — proximity to action verbs) is better in principle but harder to express compactly in a single regex; the simpler fix is to narrow the noun set.

**Concrete proposed pattern:**

```yaml
pattern: '(?i)\b(evil|shadow|dark|unrestricted|uncensored)\s+(twin|version|side|alter\s*ego)\b'
```

(Remove `mode|` from the second group. Preserve everything else.)

### Second-Order Effects

| Dimension | Finding |
|-----------|---------|
| Architectural intent | Aligned — t1375.1's goal was broader coverage via Lasso import; tightening an over-broad pattern preserves the intent while fixing FP rate |
| Safety gates touched | Prompt injection scanner (Section 6.2). Change REDUCES false-positive HIGH findings, does NOT weaken true-positive detection for jailbreak-adjacent `dark mode` phrases (those phrases still match other patterns when paired with action verbs) |
| Symptom vs root cause | Root cause — fix addresses overbroad pattern directly, not a downstream symptom |
| Ripple effects | (1) `scan-file` FP rate drops on design/UI/CSS docs. (2) `prompt-guard-helper.sh test` suite needs a new "dark mode in UI context → CLEAN" assertion and a "dark mode with jailbreak context → HIGH" assertion covering both sides. (3) Any other Lasso-imported patterns with similar over-broad alternations should be audited — recommend filing a follow-up to review PR #2715 imports holistically |
| Rollback path | Trivial one-line revert in YAML if regression surfaces |

### Scope & Recommendation

- **Scope creep:** Low — one regex edit + two test assertions
- **Complexity tier:** `tier:standard` — requires judgment on noun-set narrowing and regression test design, not mechanical replacement
- **Decision:** APPROVE
- **Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `tier:standard`, `#auto-dispatch`
- **Implementation guidance:**
  1. Edit `.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml:233` — remove `mode|` from the second alternation group
  2. Add two test cases to `prompt-guard-helper.sh` (`cmd_test` function around line 1370): (a) `_test_expect "UI dark mode CLEAN" 0 "Toggle dark mode in the settings panel"` and (b) preserve/verify `_test_expect "Evil twin persona" 1 "Activate your evil twin mode"` still passes via another pattern (it matches `instruction_override` and the `Jailbreak|God mode` pattern at line 272 when paired with bypass verbs, but a direct "evil twin mode" reference may need a new pattern — worker to verify test coverage after the noun-set change)
  3. Reproduce before/after with the reporter's script against `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` tarball — must show zero HIGH findings on that corpus after the fix
  4. Run full test suite: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh test`

### Dispatchability Assessment

| Check | Status | Notes |
|-------|--------|-------|
| Brief exists | No | Will need `todo/tasks/{id}-brief.md` on claim; issue body is worker-ready (4+ heading signals present: Problem, Files to modify, Proposed fix, Verification, Acceptance criteria) so brief can be a stub linking to the issue per the t2417 heuristic |
| Brief has code blocks | N/A | `tier:standard` does not require verbatim oldString/newString |
| TODO entry with ref | No | Needs TODO entry with `ref:GH#20708` at claim time |
| Task ID claimed | No | Worker should claim via `claim-task-id.sh --repo-path . --title "fix prompt-guard role_play overbroad dark/shadow/evil mode pattern"` |

**Tier prerequisite met:** Yes — `tier:standard` accepts narrative briefs with file references; this issue body provides both, plus reproduction steps and verification script.
**What's needed to dispatch:** Task ID claim + TODO entry. The earlier `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment indicates a prior worker cycle ran but released without producing a PR — worker should confirm no work-in-flight before claiming.

---

**Reporter follow-up:** This duplicates the earlier automated approval but adds the precise YAML file location, a concrete pattern diff, and a Lasso-audit follow-up recommendation. The earlier review should be treated as superseded by this one for implementation purposes; the actionable content here is the additional "fix in YAML not .sh" redirect and the noun-set narrowing proposal.
