title: review-bot-gate: helper-SHA pin in downstream workflows goes stale with no release-time bump mechanism
body:
## Description

`.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml` is distributed to downstream repos as a **vendored copy** with a hard-coded SHA pin on the `actions/checkout` step that fetches `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` from this repo. When the helper changes, the pin does not auto-update — and the framework's own workflow file is itself pinned, so there is no release-time trigger that cascades a new SHA to downstream installations.

Result: a substantive helper fix (e.g. [#20550](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20550) / [PR #20572](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20572), the two-phase-bot Option A' settlement check) does nothing for downstream repos until someone manually edits the workflow file in each repo. The stale pin observed today (`73b664a`, 2026-04-22 23:19Z) is carried both by a downstream project repo and by `marcusquinn/aidevops` itself, despite #20572 having merged at 2026-04-23 02:11Z.

## Observed symptom (downstream)

On a qs-agency PR batch (10 merged PRs across 2026-04-24), 4 carried a CodeRabbit "Review failed — pull request was closed or merged during review" marker. Example PR #1868 timeline:

| T | Event |
|---|---|
| T+0s | PR opens |
| T+12s | CR posts Phase 1 placeholder |
| T+21s | `review-bot-gate` CI runs helper, classifies CR as `rate-limited (not a real review)` |
| T+33s | Helper returns `PASS_RATE_LIMITED`, gate passes |
| T+32s | PR merges |
| T+73s | CR edits comment to "Review failed — closed during review" |

The pre-fix helper uses a shared `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` list as both the "this is not a real review" detector **and** the `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` alias (`review-bot-gate-helper.sh:87`). A Phase 1 placeholder (that hasn't yet been edited with walkthrough) reads as "not a real review" and therefore as "rate-limited", triggering the `PASS_RATE_LIMITED` shortcut under the default `review_gate.rate_limit_behavior=pass`.

[#20550](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20550) / [#20572](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20572) is exactly the fix for this symptom — but it only reaches downstream repos if they manually bump the pin. Most users will not know to do this.

## Reproducer

```bash
# 1. On any downstream repo with a vendored review-bot-gate.yml:
rg "^\s*ref:" .github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml
# → ref: 73b664a8d7417e0da4a076eb80ef72609188399e

# 2. Compare against post-fix aidevops main:
gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/main --jq '.sha'
# → f145379881e057c5f6a6956db72ad21663cd539b (drift > 2 days)

# 3. Confirm the fix is in main but not in pinned SHA:
git -C ~/Git/aidevops log 73b664a..f145379 -- .agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh | head -20
# → shows commits including GH#20550 Option A' fix
```

The same pin is carried in `marcusquinn/aidevops` itself:

```bash
rg "^\s*ref:" ~/Git/aidevops/.github/workflows/review-bot-gate.yml
# → ref: 73b664a8d7417e0da4a076eb80ef72609188399e
```

## Scope — how widespread

The downstream repo effectively uses whatever SHA was embedded at `aidevops init` / `setup.sh` time, and never changes unless a human edits the workflow. Every repo that ran init before 2026-04-23 02:11Z and has not been manually bumped is exposed.

Context that shapes the fix:

- `issue-sync.yml` already moved to the reusable-workflow architecture (t2770) — downstream carries a ~45-line caller with `@main` or a version pin, helpers fetched at runtime. `aidevops check-workflows` + `aidevops sync-workflows` detect/heal drift. `review-bot-gate.yml` has not been migrated — no template under `.agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml`, no reusable callee under `.github/workflows/review-bot-gate-reusable.yml`.
- Some consumers may prefer a pin (supply-chain posture) over a floating ref. Any fix should probably expose both modes, matching the `@main` vs `@vX.Y.Z` vs `@<sha>` tradeoffs documented for `issue-sync.yml`.
- The framework repo itself hits the same issue — whatever mechanism ships must be able to fix the aidevops repo, not just downstream.

## Considerations for the maintainers

Not prescribing the fix; the right answer depends on framework direction. A few paths surfaced during analysis:

1. **Migrate `review-bot-gate.yml` to the reusable-workflow architecture.** Matches the `issue-sync.yml` pattern. Single source of truth in `marcusquinn/aidevops`, downstream carries a thin caller. `aidevops check-workflows` / `sync-workflows` already scaffolding exists and could be extended. Main cost: migration PR + downstream caller template. Main benefit: pin management reduced to a single `@ref:` at the caller level, with the existing drift detector already built.

2. **Keep vendored workflow, add release-time pin bump.** `setup.sh` / `aidevops update` could detect that `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` has changed since the pin and rewrite the `ref:` line automatically. Requires no architectural change; main cost is a reliable "is this repo's pin older than helper's last touch" check that has to handle the framework repo's own workflow file too. Lower ceiling than option 1 because every new vendored workflow would need the same treatment.

3. **Drop the pin entirely, use `ref: main`.** Simplest; auto-picks up fixes. Main cost: supply-chain posture — downstream now runs whatever aidevops `main` is at job-runtime. Probably undesirable without a canary story.

4. **Do nothing; document the bump as an operational task.** Acceptable if the frequency of breaking helper changes is genuinely low and the existing advisory system can surface "bump your pin" nudges. Today's observation suggests the frequency is not low: a multi-day drift produced a visible downstream merge-quality regression between two consecutive helper changes (#19309 → #20572, both in the same week).

A fifth path, orthogonal to the above: the `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` / `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` aliasing in the helper is itself a semantic foot-gun that made this particular regression visible. #20550 fixes the CR-specific case; the broader "non-review is not the same as rate-limited" split may be worth a follow-up regardless of which distribution mechanism is chosen.

## Workarounds applied (downstream)

Manually edited the pin in `qs-agency`'s workflow, in [PR #1872](https://github.com/robstiles/qs-agency/pull/1872), bumping from `73b664a` → `f145379`. Expected to resolve the symptom on that repo only; every other downstream repo that was initialised before 2026-04-23 02:11Z needs the same manual step until the framework ships a sync mechanism.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.10.2 (up to date)
- **Install method**: unknown (`/home/rob/.local/bin/aidevops`)
- **AI Assistant**: Claude Code
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21
- **gh CLI**: 2.91.0

## References

- [#19251](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/19251) — original Phase 1 placeholder false-positive report
- [PR #19309](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/19309) — t2139 settlement check (first attempt)
- [PR #20547](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20547) — CI workflow migration to helper-delegate (GH#20493)
- [#20550](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20550) / [PR #20572](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20572) — Option A' two-phase-bot settlement (the fix that needs to reach downstream)
- `reference/reusable-workflows.md` — the t2770 architecture used for `issue-sync.yml`

title: t2797: backfill status:available on auto-dispatch issues missing status labels (pre-t2789 heal)
body:
## What

Create a one-shot (and optionally scheduled) backfill helper that applies `status:available` to dispatchable issues missing any `status:*` label. Covers pre-t2789 issues that the PR #20720 fix does not retroactively heal.

## Why

PR #20720 (t2789) made `claim-task-id.sh` apply `status:available` as default on **new** issues. But dozens of existing `auto-dispatch` issues filed before the fix lack any `status:*` label, so the pulse deterministic fill-floor enumerator never considers them as candidates. Today's audit required manual backfill for 8 issues across aidevops + <webapp>. Automating this closes the heal gap.

Evidence from 2026-04-24 audit session:
- aidevops: #20708, #20703, #20677, #20723 were stuck — no `status:*` label
- <webapp>: #2717, #2716, #2692, #2647 same pattern
- All had `auto-dispatch` and appropriate tier labels; pulse simply skipped them

## How

### Files to create

- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh` — one-shot helper, safe to re-run
  - Model on: `.agents/scripts/reconcile-origin-labels.sh` (structure, cross-repo iteration, dry-run flag, signature footer)
  - Uses `~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` `initialized_repos[]` with `pulse: true` for target repos
  - Skip `local_only: true` repos (no GitHub remote)

### Files to edit

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md` — add brief mention that backfill runs opportunistically via maintenance cycle (1-2 lines in routine cleanup section)

### Candidate selection query (the core logic)

For each pulse-enabled repo, list OPEN issues matching:

```bash
gh issue list --repo "$slug" --state open --limit 200 \
  --search "label:auto-dispatch \
    -label:status:available -label:status:queued -label:status:in-progress \
    -label:status:in-review -label:status:blocked -label:status:done \
    -label:parent-task -label:persistent -label:consolidation-task \
    -label:routine-tracking -label:no-auto-dispatch" \
  --json number,title,labels
```

Then for each result:
1. Apply `status:available` via `gh issue edit N --repo SLUG --add-label "status:available"`
2. If no `tier:*` label present, apply `tier:standard` as safe default (tier-simple-body-shape-helper will downgrade if it qualifies)
3. Log each action to stdout with format `[backfill] <slug>#<num> → status:available [+tier:standard]`

### Flags

- `--dry-run` — print would-modify list, no changes (default when no flag)
- `--apply` — actually apply labels  
- `--repo OWNER/REPO` — limit to single repo
- `--json` — machine-readable output

### Safety

- Exclusion set MUST include: `parent-task`, `persistent`, `consolidation-task`, `routine-tracking`, `no-auto-dispatch` (these are intentionally not dispatchable)
- Never remove any existing labels — purely additive
- Emit signature footer via `gh-signature-helper.sh footer` on any comments (none in default path — we don't comment on issues, just label them)
- `set -euo pipefail`, standard helper skeleton

## Acceptance

- [ ] `backfill-status-available.sh --dry-run` lists candidates across all pulse repos without modifying anything
- [ ] `backfill-status-available.sh --apply` applies `status:available` to all candidates and reports count per repo
- [ ] Pre-existing backfilled issues (e.g., if any remain at review time) get picked up by pulse on next cycle and dispatch to workers
- [ ] Shellcheck clean: `shellcheck .agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh`
- [ ] No existing `status:*` label is ever overwritten (idempotent — re-running is safe)
- [ ] Dry-run output format suitable for use in CI status comments

## Verification

```bash
# Build and verify
shellcheck .agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh

# Dry-run on a single repo
.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --dry-run

# Cross-repo dry-run
.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh --dry-run

# Apply (only after maintainer review of dry-run output)
.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh --apply
```

## Context

- PR #20720 fix: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:446-458` injects `status:available` for new issues
- Pulse candidate enumeration: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` (build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json, dispatch_deterministic_fill_floor)
- Investigation session: interactive session 2026-04-24 manually backfilled 8 issues (aidevops #20708/#20703/#20677/#20723, <webapp> #2717/#2716/#2692/#2647), each subsequently dispatched successfully
- Related: t2789 (PR #20720), t2796 (#20721 silent-failure classifier)

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/backfill-status-available.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md`

title: t2798: catch status:available default leak on bypass-path issue creation (defence-in-depth for t2789)
body:
## Task

Catch the remaining `status:available` default-injection gap: issues created via bare `gh issue create` (bypassing `claim-task-id.sh`) still ship without a `status:*` label, leaving them invisible to the pulse's dispatch fill-floor until healed manually.

## Session Origin

Filed interactively 2026-04-24 during a backlog audit that unblocked 8 pre-t2789 issues. Observed while filing #20728 (t2797): `gh issue create --label auto-dispatch,...` produced an issue without `status:available` because PR #20720's fix lives in `claim-task-id.sh`, not in a GitHub workflow. Manual `gh issue edit --add-label status:available` was required post-creation.

## What

Add a tiny `issues.opened` workflow that applies `status:available` when:

1. The issue carries `auto-dispatch`, AND
2. No `status:*` label is already present, AND
3. The issue is not excluded (`parent-task`, `persistent`, `consolidation-task`, `routine-tracking`, `no-auto-dispatch`).

This is a server-side safety net — the `claim-task-id.sh` path remains the primary source of the default; this workflow catches the bypass path (direct `gh issue create`, `gh_create_issue` wrapper calls from scripts that pre-date t2789, external tooling).

## Why

The pulse's deterministic fill-floor enumerates dispatchable candidates by `auto-dispatch` + `status:available`. An auto-dispatch issue without any `status:*` is invisible — the pulse simply doesn't see it. Before PR #20720, this was the norm; after PR #20720, it's a bypass-path leak. The audit that surfaced this had to manually label 8 stranded issues across 2 repos; without a server-side guard, every future bypass creates another manual heal.

Defence-in-depth: application-layer fix (claim-task-id.sh) + platform-layer fix (workflow). Either alone is incomplete — the workflow also catches issues filed via GitHub web UI with `auto-dispatch` applied by template.

## How

### Files

- **NEW**: `.github/workflows/apply-status-available-default.yml` — model on `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml` (`issues.opened` trigger, `actions/github-script@f28e40c7f34bde8b3046d885e986cb6290c5673b`, concurrency group per-issue, 2-minute timeout).

### Pattern

Copy the shape of `issue-triage-gate.yml`:

```yaml
name: Apply status:available Default

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened, labeled]

permissions:
  issues: write

jobs:
  apply-default:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    concurrency:
      group: apply-status-default-${{ github.event.issue.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@f28e40c7f34bde8b3046d885e986cb6290c5673b # v7
        with:
          script: |
            const issue = context.payload.issue;
            const labels = (issue.labels || []).map(l => l.name);

            // Gate 1: must have auto-dispatch
            if (!labels.includes('auto-dispatch')) return;

            // Gate 2: already has a status label? skip
            if (labels.some(l => l.startsWith('status:'))) return;

            // Gate 3: excluded label classes
            const excluded = ['parent-task', 'persistent', 'consolidation-task',
                              'routine-tracking', 'no-auto-dispatch'];
            if (labels.some(l => excluded.includes(l))) return;

            await github.rest.issues.addLabels({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: issue.number,
              labels: ['status:available']
            });
            console.log(`Applied status:available to #${issue.number}`);
```

Listening on `labeled` as well as `opened` handles the case where `auto-dispatch` is added post-creation (user tags an existing issue). The gates are idempotent — re-runs on already-labeled issues are no-ops.

### Interaction with t2797 backfill (#20728)

These two tasks complement each other:

- **t2797 (#20728)**: one-shot heal of EXISTING pre-t2789 issues across all pulse repos.
- **t2798 (this)**: server-side prevention of NEW bypass-path leaks.

Order doesn't matter — both should land. Neither blocks the other.

### Deployment

This is a per-repo workflow. Initially land in `marcusquinn/aidevops`. Subsequent rollout to other pulse repos can use `aidevops sync-workflows` (the t2779 helper) — or just copy the file manually since it's trivial.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New file `.github/workflows/apply-status-available-default.yml` created with the pattern above (adjust timing/wording at worker's discretion).
2. Workflow triggers on `issues.opened` AND `issues.labeled`.
3. Gates correctly handle: no auto-dispatch → skip; existing status:* → skip; excluded label → skip; otherwise → add status:available.
4. Verified by filing a test issue via `gh issue create --label auto-dispatch --title "test status-available workflow" --body "test"`, confirming the workflow fires and adds `status:available` within ~30s. Close the test issue after verification.
5. Documentation: add a one-line mention under "Auto-Dispatch and Completion" in `.agents/AGENTS.md` pointing to the workflow as the safety net for the bypass path.

## Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/apply-status-available-default.yml`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

## Verification

```bash
# After PR merges:
gh workflow list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops | grep "Apply status:available"

# Smoke test — file and observe:
gh issue create --repo marcusquinn/aidevops \
  --title "test: status-available workflow smoke" \
  --body "Automated smoke test for status:available default workflow. Close after verification." \
  --label auto-dispatch
# Wait 30s, then:
# gh issue view <N> --json labels | jq -r '.labels[].name' | grep status:available
# Close: gh issue close <N>
```

## Tier

`tier:standard` — single new workflow file plus a one-line doc edit, no judgment calls beyond gate ordering which is already specified.

title: t2799: review-bot-gate-helper: rename RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS alias and split rate-limit vs non-review pattern sets
body:
## Session Origin

Orthogonal finding surfaced during review of #20727 (migrate `review-bot-gate.yml` to reusable-workflow pattern). The SHA-pin staleness and the pattern-array semantic mismatch both touch the same helper but are independent fixes.

**Blocked by #20727** — that migration rewrites the workflow that sources this helper. Merge #20727 first to avoid conflicts on the same file set.

## What

Clean up the misleading `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` alias in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`. After t2139 (GH#19251) expanded the array beyond rate-limit notices to include `"Review failed"`, `"Review skipped"`, and `"closed or merged during review"`, the legacy alias `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` became semantically wrong — callers that want only rate-limit patterns get non-review patterns too.

## Why

- The name `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` implies rate-limit-only but the array now contains non-rate-limit review-failure markers.
- Any downstream `custom/scripts/` caller that still references `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` for true rate-limit logic (e.g. grace-period handling via `RATE_LIMIT_GRACE_SECONDS`) is silently getting wrong behaviour — a "Review skipped" comment will trip rate-limit branches.
- Inside the framework itself there are **zero** callers of `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` (confirmed: `rg -n "RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS" .agents/ .github/` returns only the definition at line 87). Safe to retire.

## How

Two-step cleanup:

1. **Split the arrays by intent** in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:74-87`:
   - `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` (restored to original semantics): entries 1-6 above (`"rate limit exceeded"` through `"has exceeded the limit for..."`). Used by grace-period logic.
   - `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` (broader set, current behaviour): `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS + ("Review failed" "Review skipped" "closed or merged during review" "Auto reviews are limited")`. Used by `is_rate_limit_comment` / comment classification.
   - Build `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` as a union of `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` + the non-rate-limit entries so the two sets stay consistent.

2. **Audit the three current call sites** (`:352`, `:355`, `:626`) to confirm each is using the correct array. Line 352's comment (`# is_rate_limit_comment for accuracy — see NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS.`) suggests the classification logic wants the broader set — verify and document.

3. **Deprecate, don't delete, the alias** for one release cycle: replace `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS=("${NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS[@]}")` with a sourcing-time warning that tells downstream `custom/scripts/` callers to switch names, then remove in the next minor version. Track removal as a follow-up `ref:GH#NNN` before merging.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` contains only the 6 rate-limit entries; `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` contains the 10-entry union.
- All three existing call sites (`:352`, `:355`, `:626`) audited and using the array that matches their intent (documented in a comment if the choice is non-obvious).
- Grace-period logic (`RATE_LIMIT_GRACE_SECONDS`) exercised only by rate-limit matches, not by "Review skipped"-type matches.
- Deprecation warning emitted when a downstream caller references the alias (a follow-up issue filed to remove it in the next minor version).
- Existing tests pass; if any test relied on the old unified behaviour, update with a comment explaining the semantic split.

## Reference

- Review comment that surfaced this: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20727#issuecomment-4314595759
- Original expansion rationale: t2139 / GH#19251 (CodeRabbit false-positive fix)

title: t2800: claim-task-id: pre-flight validate --labels to prevent claimed-ID orphans when issue creation fails
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced during an interactive session filing GH#20732. The call `claim-task-id.sh --labels "debt,tier:standard,origin:interactive"` produced:

```text
[OK] Claimed t2799 (attempt 1, 0s)
[OK] Allocated task ID: t2799
[WARN] issue-sync-helper.sh push returned no issue number, falling back to bare creation
[WARN] Failed to create GitHub issue: could not add label: 'debt' not found
[WARN] Issue creation failed for t2799 (non-fatal — ID is secured)
task_id=t2799
ref=none
```

`debt` isn't a valid label in this repo (canonical names are `quality-debt`, `refactor`, etc.). The counter advanced to 2800, t2799 was consumed, but no issue was created — the claim is stranded. The operator then had to fall back to the issue-creation wrapper manually and inject the task ID into the title by hand to keep the trail. This happens to be meta-appropriate: the orphan t2799 was recycled into #20732, but in a worker dispatch the ID would be fully lost.

## What

Add pre-flight label validation (or graceful label drop) to `claim-task-id.sh` so that invalid `--labels` arguments either (a) abort the claim BEFORE the counter advances, or (b) strip unknown labels with a warning and proceed. The current behaviour — claim first, discover invalid label during issue creation, strand the ID — is the worst of both worlds.

## Why

- **Existing scope gap.** t2548 / #20180 / PR #20213 fixed TODO.md orphans AFTER successful issue creation. This bug is upstream of that fix: issue creation never succeeds, so the TODO append path doesn't even run. Same root category (counter / issue / TODO trio getting out of sync), different branch.
- **Silent failure.** The warnings are marked "non-fatal" and the exit code is 0. A scripted caller (headless worker, automation) sees success and moves on while the task ID is lost.
- **Collision risk.** An orphan t-ID pollutes the task-ID-collision guard (`install-ta[redacted-credential].sh`) — future commits referencing a "claimed but never issued" ID look identical to legitimate task IDs. The dedup check in claim-task-id (fuzzy PR title search) won't flag reuse because there was never a PR.
- **Easy interactive mistake.** `debt` vs `quality-debt`, `tier:std` vs `tier:standard`, `origin:int` vs `origin:interactive` — trivial typos that cost a counter slot each.

## How

Two viable approaches. Recommend **(A) Pre-flight validation** with **(B) as fallback** for the rare case where label listing itself is rate-limited.

### (A) Pre-flight validation (primary)

Insert after tag normalisation at `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:298`, before the CAS claim loop. New helper `_validate_labels_exist` that:

1. Runs the repo's label-list query once, caches the names in a session-local temp file.
2. Splits `--labels` on comma, trims whitespace, checks each against the cache with `grep -Fxq`.
3. On any missing label: logs which labels are invalid, logs the lookup command the operator should run, returns non-zero.
4. On API failure during the list query: fail-open (skip validation, let option B handle it).

Call site adds an early exit with a new exit code `3` (invalid-labels) before the CAS claim:

```text
if ! _validate_labels_exist "$PLATFORM_REPO_SLUG" "$TASK_LABELS"; then
  log_error "Claim aborted — counter NOT advanced"
  exit 3
fi
```

Cost: one label-list query per claim (~200-400ms). Skippable with `--skip-label-validation` for the bulk `--count N` path where pre-flight is redundant after the first claim.

### (B) Graceful degradation fallback

If the label-list query itself fails (rate limit, network), don't block — move label application from the create call into a second add-label step so a bad label doesn't kill the create. Current behaviour is already close to this; the fix is to reorder: create first, label second, so a label failure is recoverable instead of fatal.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh` (if label-passing logic lives in the sub-library after PR #20247)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-ta[redacted-credential].sh` (add regression)

## Acceptance

- Calling the helper with a nonexistent label returns non-zero BEFORE advancing `.task-counter` (option A).
- Regression test: invalid label → exit 3, counter unchanged. Valid label → exit 0, counter advances by 1.
- Existing `test-claim-ta[redacted-credential].sh` remains passing.
- `--skip-label-validation` flag works for bulk allocation.
- Fail-open branch (API error during validation) is exercised by a test: simulated list-query failure → validation skipped, claim proceeds, any label failure in issue creation falls back to option B's label-separate-step path.

## Reference

- Prior related orphan fix: t2548 / #20180 / PR #20213 (covers post-creation orphans).
- Claim-task-id architecture: PR #20247 (split into counter + issue sub-libraries).
- Key call sites: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh:219` (flag parse), `:290-298` (tag normalisation via `map_tags_to_labels`), `:433-457` (issue-create args assembly).

title: t2801: signature-footer hook: false positives on heredoc bodies and quoted-arg matches push operators toward bypass
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced during the same interactive session that filed GH#20732 and GH#20734. The signature-footer enforcement hook (t2685 / PR #20307, refined in t2707 / PR #20352 and #20379) is doing its job on actual `gh` invocations, but its detection regex matches the pattern anywhere in the raw command string — including quoted string arguments of unrelated tools, heredoc body content, and search patterns. Three false positives in one session:

**Failure 1 — heredoc body containing narrative reference:**

The command `cat > /tmp/issue-body-claim.md <<'BODY' ... BODY` wrote a markdown draft. The body contained the phrase `call the issue-creation wrapper` and elsewhere named `the gh create invocation` as narrative. Hook blocked with:

```text
aidevops: gh write command missing signature footer (t2685).
Hook auto-repair could not parse the command — likely a heredoc...
```

No gh command is being executed. The hook is pattern-matching prose.

**Failure 2 — `memory-helper.sh store --content "..."`:**

The memory payload described the bug and cited the prior failure mode. The content string contained the literal `the gh create step fails on label validation`. Hook blocked identically.

**Failure 3 — `rg -n "... the relevant gh issue create string ..." file`:**

Searching for call sites in source code. The ripgrep pattern literally contains `gh issue create` as the search query. Hook blocked.

Each case was worked around by substituting the trigger phrase or using the `Write` tool instead of heredoc — but every workaround is a step closer to an operator reaching for `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`, which would defeat the signature audit trail entirely.

## What

Tighten the detection regex in `quality-hooks-signature.mjs` (and the shim `.agents/scripts/gh`) so the check fires on actual `gh` invocations only, not on the same token sequence appearing inside:

- Heredoc bodies (`<<EOF ... EOF`, `<<-EOF`, `<<'EOF'`)
- Quoted string arguments of non-`gh` commands (`rg "gh issue create"`, `memory-helper.sh store --content "... gh issue create ..."`, `echo "gh pr comment"`)
- Search-tool arguments generally (`rg`, `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `find -name`)

Zero regression on legitimate enforcement: any real `gh pr|issue create|comment` invocation (at a command boundary, outside quoted strings/heredocs) must still block without `gh-signature-helper` output.

## Why

The signature footer carries the runtime, app version, model ID, token count, and session duration. That metadata is the only way to correlate a later-surfaced bug to the specific worker version that produced the comment — critical when a bug is fixed in v3.6.190 but a user reports it still happening and we need to know whether the reporting comment was written by v3.6.188. Losing footers is a diagnostic-blindness bug.

The enforcement intent is therefore correct and must not be relaxed. The problem is the false-positive rate: each one pushes the operator toward bypass (`--no-verify`, `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1`). Once bypass becomes muscle memory, real unsigned gh calls slip through unrelated to the false-positive trigger. The fix must be sharper detection, not looser enforcement.

Current detection (`quality-hooks-signature.mjs:47-55`):

```javascript
const ghWritePattern = /\bgh\s+(pr\s+(create|comment)|issue\s+(create|comment))\b/;
return cmd.split("\n").some((line) => {
  const trimmed = line.trim();
  if (trimmed.startsWith("#")) return false;
  if (/\bgit\s+commit\b/.test(trimmed)) return false;
  return ghWritePattern.test(trimmed);
});
```

The `\b` boundaries allow the pattern to match mid-line inside any quoted string or heredoc content. Line-splitting + `#`-comment filtering is too weak to distinguish "line inside a heredoc body" from "line executing a command".

## How

Three complementary tightening layers. Recommended order: (1) command-boundary anchor, (2) heredoc tracking, (3) quoted-string detection.

### (1) Command-boundary anchor (highest impact)

Require the `gh` match to be preceded by a shell command boundary: start-of-line, `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `(`, `$(`, or backtick. Not any whitespace.

```javascript
// Match gh only when it starts a command segment
const ghWritePattern = /(^|[;&|(`]|\$\()\s*gh\s+(pr\s+(create|comment)|issue\s+(create|comment))\b/;
```

Eliminates Failures 2 and 3 (where `gh` appears mid-argument after whitespace inside a quoted string).

### (2) Heredoc tracking

Before the `.split("\n").some(...)` check, strip heredoc bodies from the command string. Track `<<TAG` / `<<-TAG` / `<<'TAG'` / `<<"TAG"` openers and their matching terminator line; remove the enclosed lines from the input the regex sees.

Eliminates Failure 1.

### (3) Quoted-string stripping (defense in depth)

For each line, strip content inside balanced single and double quotes before running the regex. Avoids matches on literal `gh ...` substrings inside any quoted arg that survived layer (1) — e.g., when chained after `&&` but still quoted.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-signature-footer-gate.mjs` — add regression cases for all three false-positive classes.
- `.agents/scripts/gh` (PATH shim) — mirror the same regex if it duplicates the detection logic rather than sourcing the plugin's.

## Acceptance

Regression tests must cover, at minimum, these positive and negative cases:

**Must pass (real gh invocations — continue to block without footer):**

- `gh issue create --title X --body Y` (bare, no footer) → BLOCK
- `foo && gh issue create --title X --body Y` (chained, no footer) → BLOCK
- `$(gh issue comment 123 --body Y)` (command substitution, no footer) → BLOCK

**Must pass (real gh invocations with footer — allow):**

- `gh issue create --body "$(gh-signature-helper.sh footer)"` → ALLOW
- `gh issue comment N --body-file "$BODY"` where `$BODY` contains the marker → ALLOW

**Must NOT block (false positives):**

- `cat > file <<EOF\n...gh issue create...\nEOF` → ALLOW (heredoc body)
- `memory-helper.sh store --content "... gh issue create ..."` → ALLOW (quoted arg of non-gh tool)
- `rg "gh issue create" src/` → ALLOW (search pattern)
- `echo "to file a comment, run gh issue comment N"` → ALLOW (echoed prose)
- `grep -n "gh pr create" --include="*.md"` → ALLOW (grep pattern)

Test format: follow the existing `test-signature-footer-gate.mjs` pattern with labelled `ALLOW`/`BLOCK` expectations per case.

## Reference

- Original t2685 hardening: PR #20307 (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-signature.mjs:47-80`)
- t2707 shim extension: PR #20352
- Recent iteration: PR #20379 (shim api-endpoint detection)
- Current detection regex: `quality-hooks-signature.mjs:48`
- Command-start check in shim: `.agents/scripts/gh` (verify whether it shares logic or re-implements)

## Related

- GH#20732 — review-bot-gate helper rename (surfaced during same session)
- GH#20734 — claim-task-id label validation (surfaced during same session)

title: t2802: worktree-helper.sh add: explicitly base new branches on origin/<default> to prevent scope-leak PRs
body:
## What

`worktree-helper.sh cmd_add` creates new branches from the canonical repo's current HEAD rather than explicitly basing them on `origin/<default>`. When the canonical's HEAD is anything other than the remote default (stale local `main`/`develop`, long-running feature branch, post-checkout leftover), every new worktree inherits that stale state. Worker PRs then open with a diff surface proportional to the canonical's drift — sometimes hundreds of unrelated files.

## Why

**Canonical failure mode — <webapp>/<webapp>#2716 (scope-leaked PR #2733, 100 files for a 2-line fix):**

1. Dispatched worker created branch `feature/auto-20260424-072814-gh2716` via `worktree-helper.sh add`.
2. `cmd_add` ran `git worktree add -b "$branch" "$path"` without a base ref. Git defaulted to HEAD of the canonical repo.
3. Canonical's HEAD happened to be on stale `main` (commit `c9b8e66c`, "merge develop into main" from April 11 — behind `origin/develop` by many commits).
4. PR opened against `develop` (repo default). Diff = everything `develop` had that `main` didn't + the 2-line fix = 100 files.
5. PR was closed as `CONFLICTING`. Successive cherry-pick retry workers (sonnet → opus-4.6 → opus-4.7) ran out of tokens trying to cherry-pick the 100-file monster into a clean branch. All died at `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` / `no_work` before engaging with the actual 2-line fix.
6. Eventually NMR'd after 2 stale-recovery ticks. Required interactive maintainer intervention to resolve.

**Total cost**: 5+ worker dispatches, opus tokens, maintainer context-switch — to fix a 2-line review comment.

The reuse path in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:293-305` *does* reset existing worktrees to `origin/<default>` explicitly. The **create** path at `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:317-320` → `worktree-helper.sh:938` has no equivalent safeguard.

## How

### 1. `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`

Extend `_parse_cmd_add_args` to accept `--base <ref>`:

- New global `_ADD_BASE`.
- New case branches for `--base` and `--base=*`.
- Usage string updated.

In `cmd_add` (new-branch path, around line 938), resolve base ref with precedence:

1. `--base <ref>` if provided (explicit user intent — stacked PR, test fixture, etc.)
2. `origin/$(get_default_branch)` if that ref resolves (`git rev-parse --verify`)
3. `<default_branch>` (local) if remote-tracking doesn't exist
4. Fall back to HEAD (current behaviour) with a `print_warning` if none of the above resolve — surface the degradation so users notice.

Pass the resolved base as the 3rd positional to `git worktree add -b "$branch" "$path" "$base"`.

Log the base used (stderr, `print_info`) so pulse/worker dispatch traces show which base was chosen — critical for future scope-leak debugging.

### 2. `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`

No code change required — the helper change propagates automatically. Verify by reading the call at line 320 and confirming it doesn't need `--base`.

### 3. Tests

Add a shellcheck verification pass (already covered by CI). For integration, a manual verification matrix:

- Canonical on default branch → worktree branch parent = `origin/<default>` tip. ✔
- Canonical on feature branch → worktree branch parent = `origin/<default>` tip (not feature branch). ✔
- `--base some/other-branch` passed → worktree branch parent = `some/other-branch` tip. ✔
- No `origin` remote (local-only repo) → falls back to local default, logs warning. ✔
- No default branch detectable → falls back to HEAD + loud warning. ✔

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` (only if a log line is added for clarity)

## Acceptance

1. `worktree-helper.sh add <branch>` without `--base` creates the new branch on top of `origin/<default>`, regardless of canonical HEAD.
2. `worktree-helper.sh add <branch> --base <ref>` respects the explicit base.
3. When `origin/<default>` can't be resolved, falls back gracefully and warns.
4. Existing `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` behaviour preserved — pre-created worktrees are rooted at `origin/<default>` tip.
5. `shellcheck` clean.
6. No regressions in existing worktree usage (local dev, full-loop, stacked PRs).

title: t2803: brief-template: add Complexity Impact section to prevent function-complexity gate surprises
body:
## What

Add a **Complexity Impact** section to the brief template (and its `new-task.md` / `task-brief-helper.sh` companions) so task briefs flag upfront when a change is likely to trip the function-complexity, nesting-depth, or file-size regression gates. Brief must require the worker to plan an extract-helpers refactor BEFORE writing code when projected growth pushes a function past ~50% of threshold.

## Why

Canonical failure: issue #20702 / PR #20705 / plus 7 subsequent worker dispatch attempts all hit the same Complexity Analysis wall on `_parse_phases_section`. The function was already ~60 lines; adding a bold-heading parser inline pushed it to ~120, well over the 100-line `function-complexity` threshold. Because the issue body said only "add an elif branch" without mentioning the complexity gate or the extract-helpers precedent (GH#20496 / PR #20503 on the same file), every worker copied the shape and got the same red build. Eventually PR #20736 resolved it by extracting four helpers — an approach that takes 10 min to design but workers couldn't discover from the brief.

This is a preventable class of waste: one brief update saves N worker dispatches across every future "grow existing function" task.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` — add a `### Complexity Impact` subsection under `## How`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/commands/new-task.md` — add Complexity Impact step to interview flow
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh` — if helper validates section presence, add Complexity Impact to checklist
- EDIT or CREATE: `.agents/reference/large-file-split.md` cross-reference OR new `reference/complexity-impact-briefing.md`

### Reference pattern

### Verification

1. Run `/new-task` interactively on a shell-modifying task, confirm it prompts for Complexity Impact.
2. Create a test brief that grows a function past threshold without the Complexity Impact section — `task-brief-helper.sh` should flag it as incomplete.
3. Check `templates/brief-template.md` renders correctly (markdown lint passes).

`tier:standard` — concrete edits, clear file scope, no novel design.

title: t2804: pulse: diagnose launch_recovery:no_worker_process dispatch stalls (#20702 evidence)
body:
## What

Investigate and remediate the `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` dispatch failure mode. Observed: 7 consecutive pulse worker dispatch attempts on issue #20702 (t2788) failed before a worker process ever spawned. Cascade escalation from `tier:standard` → `tier:thinking` (opus) kept happening but the underlying worker never executed code. Separate from coding-failure loops; this is an orchestration-layer defect.

## Why

Observable evidence (from #20702 issue timeline, 2026-04-24):
- Multiple dispatch claims stamped by runner `alex-solovyev` within minutes
- Each attempt ends with `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` — launch-recovery subsystem observed no live worker
- Cascade tier escalation fired (standard → thinking) as if the worker had failed, but there was no worker to fail
- Interactive takeover via `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` unblocked the issue instantly; human-authored PR landed in ~15 min

This symptom is invisible to the cost-circuit-breaker (no tokens spent since no worker ran) but wastes dispatch slots and triggers NMR escalation incorrectly. If this pattern affects more than one issue or one runner, it's a dispatch-pool availability bug hiding behind "worker failed" classification.

## Decomposition (parent-task)

Investigation first, then phase PRs:

- **Phase 1 — Instrumentation & triage** [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]: collect all `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` events from pulse logs across all runners for last 14 days; classify by runner, issue, tier. Build reproducer or confirm transient.
- **Phase 2 — Root cause** [requires-decision]: inspect `pulse-wrapper.sh` dispatch → spawn path. title: t2805: pulse-merge: rebase MERGEABLE PRs with CI failures before routing to fix-worker
body:
# t2805 — pulse-merge: rebase MERGEABLE PRs with CI failures before routing to fix-worker

## Session Origin

Interactive triage session 2026-04-24 on `<webapp>/<webapp>#2684` (PR #2750). A correct worker-authored fix sat blocked for ~5 hours despite all code-relevant CI passing, because E2E shards 1-4 failed on **unrelated planner tests** that were fixed in a separate PR (#2772 / t443) that merged to `develop` ~3h after PR #2750 was created. Manual `git rebase origin/develop && git push --force-with-lease` immediately resolved the E2E failures on re-run — zero re-implementation needed.

## What

`pulse-merge.sh::_attempt_pr_merge` currently only triggers `gh pr update-branch` (the cheap server-side fast-forward) when `mergeable == "CONFLICTING"` (t2116 path, line 1292). When a PR is `MERGEABLE` but has failing required checks, it is routed directly to `_route_pr_to_fix_worker "$pr_number" ... "ci"` (line 1358) — which spawns a fresh worker session to diagnose and fix CI.

The problem: the failing checks are often on **base-drift**, not on the PR's own code. Examples observed:

- PR #2750 (this session): E2E shards failed on `planner.spec.ts` tests. The PR only touched `packages/api/src/modules/org/rewards/queries.ts` + a new test file. Failures were caused by a pre-existing planner bug later fixed in PR #2772.
- PR #2703 (`t418`, same base): same 4 E2E shards failing. Completely unrelated to its stat-card CSS change.
- PR #2702 (`t413`): same 4 E2E shards failing. This is the planner fix PR itself — it can't fix itself without the test seed fix landing.

Spawning a CI-fix worker on these is token-waste. The worker will read the failing test files, conclude they're not related to the PR's diff, and either rebase (success) or escalate (failure). The rebase path is a ~1-second `gh pr update-branch` call that GitHub already provides server-side.

## Why

The `t2116` comment explicitly notes update-branch is *"idempotent and cheap"* and fires when the conflict is *"purely due to base advancement"*. The same reasoning applies to CI failures: if the PR's HEAD is behind base and CI is failing, there is a non-zero chance base-advancement fixed it. We should try the cheap fix before spawning a $0.10-$2.00 fix-worker session.

Observable cost of the gap (24h window on my runner):

- PR #2750: 6 dispatch/release cycles, ~5 hours stuck, one worker actually created the fix successfully but then continued running after PR creation and was killed at `worker_failed` — likely trying to fix the "failing" CI it had no way to diagnose as base-drift.
- 2 unique PRs blocked by t2449 bot-author gate in the same window (both had the same pattern).

Root cause class: the merge pipeline treats `CONFLICTING` and `CI-failing-but-MERGEABLE` as separate branches, even though the remediation (update-branch) is the same for the common base-drift case.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1347-1360` — before calling `_route_pr_to_fix_worker "ci"`, attempt `gh pr update-branch`. If HEAD is already at base, or update-branch fails, fall through to routing.

### Implementation Steps

1. Extract a new helper `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry <pr_number> <repo_slug>`:
   - Query GraphQL for `pullRequest { headRefOid, baseRef { target { oid } }, mergeable, behindBy }` (or `gh pr view --json baseRefName,headRefOid` + `gh api repos/.../compare/...`).
   - If `behindBy == 0`, return 1 (nothing to rebase, don't retry).
   - Call `gh pr update-branch "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug"` — idempotent server-side fast-forward.
   - Return 0 on success (caller re-checks CI on next cycle), 1 on failure.

   Model on the existing `_attempt_pr_update_branch` at `pulse-merge.sh:660`.

2. In `_attempt_pr_merge` (around line 1354):

   ```bash
   if ! _pr_required_checks_pass "$pr_number" "$repo_slug"; then
       # NEW: try cheap rebase first if PR is behind base — pre-existing
       # failures in unrelated tests are often fixed by base advancement.
       # If rebase succeeds, skip fix-worker routing — next pulse cycle
       # will re-check CI on the rebased HEAD.
       if _attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry "$pr_number" "$repo_slug"; then
           echo "[pulse-merge] PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug}: rebased on base via update-branch before CI-fix routing (t2805)" >>"$LOGFILE"
           return 1
       fi
       # Fall through to existing fix-worker routing
       local _ci_linked_issue
       _ci_linked_issue=$(_extract_linked_issue "$pr_number" "$repo_slug")
       _route_pr_to_fix_worker "$pr_number" "$repo_slug" "$_ci_linked_issue" "ci" || true
       return 1
   fi
   ```

3. Rate-limit guard: reuse the same per-PR cooldown already present for update-branch (one call per CONFLICTING PR per pulse cycle — see t2116 comment at line 669). The same mechanism should cover CI-drift rebase too; no new state needed if the cooldown is keyed on PR number, not on reason.

4. Audit log: emit `[pulse-merge] PR #N: attempting CI-drift rebase (t2805)` on entry, `succeeded` or `failed` on exit. Parallels the existing t2116 log lines.

### Verification

- Local sanity: `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- Regression: existing t2116 tests should still pass (same helper, same rate-limit).
- Integration: dry-run against `PR #2703` (same base-drift pattern) — the pulse log should show a rebase attempt before any fix-worker dispatch.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] When a PR with `mergeable:MERGEABLE` has failing required checks AND is behind its base, `pulse-merge.sh` attempts `gh pr update-branch` before routing to a CI-fix worker.
- [ ] When update-branch succeeds, the CI-fix worker is NOT spawned that cycle (next pulse cycle re-checks).
- [ ] When update-branch fails (true behind + semantic conflict in CI-relevant files), fall through to the existing fix-worker routing.
- [ ] Rate-limit honours the existing per-PR per-cycle cap — no duplicate update-branch calls in one cycle.
- [ ] Audit log entries `[pulse-merge] ... CI-drift rebase (t2805)` appear in `pulse.log`.
- [ ] No regression on existing t2116 CONFLICTING path.

## Context

**Related, intentionally NOT scoped into this task** — file separately if needed:

- t2449 bot-author gate blocking auto-merge of worker PRs whose linked issue was created by `github-actions[bot]` (issue-sync without SYNC_PAT). Separate problem, separate fix — this task only addresses the CI-drift rebase.
- `security-posture-helper.sh` Phase 7 SYNC_PAT detection skips when classic branch-protection API returns 404, which mis-reports rulesets-based protected repos (e.g. `<webapp>/<webapp>`) as "not needing SYNC_PAT". Separate fix.
- Pre-existing `no_work` / `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` worker stall cluster (already tracked at `marcusquinn/aidevops#20560` / t2756). This rebase-before-routing change does NOT replace that work — it is a complementary optimisation.

**Evidence artifacts:**

- `<webapp>/<webapp>#2684` (stuck issue) / `<webapp>/<webapp>#2750` (stuck PR)
- `<webapp>/<webapp>#2703`, `#2702` (same base-drift pattern, same cycle)
- Pulse log excerpts captured during triage show ~6 dispatch/release cycles on #2684 before dedup caught up.

Tier: `tier:thinking` — introduces a new branch in the merge pipeline and must not regress existing t2116 semantics. Standard-tier could implement once the design is locked, but the initial cut benefits from an opus review of the rate-limit and audit-log interactions.

title: t2806: security-posture-helper Phase 7 SYNC_PAT check misses rulesets-based branch protection
body:
# t2806 — `security-posture-helper.sh`: detect SYNC_PAT need under rulesets-based branch protection

## Session Origin

Surfaced during triage of `<webapp>/<webapp>#2684` (2026-04-24). Verified: `<webapp>` is rulesets-protected (`GET /repos/<webapp>/<webapp>/branches/develop` returns `"protected": true`), yet the issue-sync workflow creates issues as `github-actions[bot]` with `author_association=NONE`, which trips the t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge gate.

Root cause: `SYNC_PAT` is not configured on the repo. Expected behaviour: `aidevops security check <webapp>/<webapp>` should surface this as an advisory. Actual behaviour:

```
Phase 7: SYNC_PAT Detection (issue-sync)
[SKIP] No GitHub remote — SYNC_PAT check skipped
```

Incorrect — the repo has a remote. The underlying detector returns "not needed" silently because the legacy branch-protection API returns `404 Branch not protected` on repos that use **rulesets** (the modern GitHub replacement for classic branch-protection rules).

## What

`security-posture-helper.sh::_check_sync_pat_need` (line 665-) uses only the classic endpoint:

```bash
protection_json=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/branches/${default_branch}/protection" 2>/dev/null) || true
if [[ -z "$protection_json" || "$protection_json" == *"Not Found"* || "$protection_json" == *"Branch not protected"* ]]; then
    print_pass "No branch protection — SYNC_PAT not needed for $slug"
    ...
    return 0
fi
```

Repos migrated to **rulesets** (Settings → Rules → Rulesets) return `{"protected": true, ...}` on `GET /repos/{slug}/branches/{branch}` but `404` on `/protection`. The detector's third-branch fallback never fires, so the repo is mis-classified as "no protection" and SYNC_PAT is declared unnecessary. A subsequent `gh secret set SYNC_PAT` advisory is never emitted.

This is a silent gap: users following the `aidevops security check` output conclude their repo is fine, but every worker-briefed PR created from an issue-sync'd TODO entry on that repo will be blocked from t2449 auto-merge.

Evidence matrix (this session):

| Repo | `protected` | Classic API | Rulesets API | SYNC_PAT set | Current detection |
|------|-------------|-------------|--------------|--------------|-------------------|
| `marcusquinn/aidevops` | true | 200 | ? | yes | PASS (correct) |
| `<webapp>/<webapp>` | true | 404 | present | no | **SKIP (incorrect — should WARN+advise)** |
| `essentials-com/essentials.com` | ? | ? | ? | no | not tested here |

## Why

The migration path from classic branch protection to rulesets is deliberate GitHub policy — rulesets are more flexible (multi-branch, bypass actors, different rule types), so many repos will move. The SYNC_PAT detector was written before rulesets existed; the gap is real and will grow.

Downstream effect chain, from weakest to most painful:

1. `aidevops security check <slug>` reports PASS — false clean health signal.
2. No advisory emitted → user never sets SYNC_PAT.
3. Every issue-sync-created issue on the repo is authored by `github-actions[bot]` with `author_association=NONE`.
4. t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge refuses to merge (correctly, since it has no way to know the underlying TODO commit was maintainer-authored).
5. Worker PRs sit in `BLOCKED` state even when CI passes; dispatch loops continue until dedup catches up; eventual manual merge.

Fixing detection closes the loop without any framework change to t2449 — users who act on the advisory set the PAT, issues become MEMBER-authored, auto-merge works.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh:665-` — in `_check_sync_pat_need`, when the classic protection endpoint returns 404, ALSO query `/repos/{slug}/rulesets` and check for a ruleset that targets the default branch with a `pull_request` rule or `required_status_checks`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a helper `_branch_is_rulesets_protected <slug> <default_branch>` that:
   - `gh api "repos/${slug}/rulesets" --jq '.[] | {id, target, enforcement, conditions}'`
   - For each enabled ruleset (`enforcement == "active"`), fetch details: `gh api "repos/${slug}/rulesets/${id}" --jq '{conditions:.conditions.ref_name.include, rules:[.rules[].type]}'`
   - Return 0 if any active ruleset matches `${default_branch}` (or `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` / `refs/heads/*`) AND includes a `pull_request` rule.
   - Fail-open: if the rulesets API errors or is empty, return 1.

2. Modify `_check_sync_pat_need` at line 682-690:

   ```bash
   # Existing legacy check — keep as primary
   protection_json=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/branches/${default_branch}/protection" 2>/dev/null) || true

   local protected="false"
   if [[ -n "$protection_json" && "$protection_json" != *"Not Found"* && "$protection_json" != *"Branch not protected"* ]]; then
       # Classic protection active — existing path
       protected="classic"
       # ... existing required_reviews extraction ...
   elif _branch_is_rulesets_protected "$slug" "$default_branch"; then
       # NEW: Rulesets-based protection
       protected="rulesets"
   fi

   if [[ "$protected" == "false" ]]; then
       print_pass "No branch protection — SYNC_PAT not needed for $slug"
       ...
       return 0
   fi
   # Proceed to Step 3: Is SYNC_PAT set?
   ```

3. Keep the existing `required_reviews -eq 0` optimisation for the `classic` path only. For the `rulesets` path, assume PR reviews are required (conservative — false positives here just result in an advisory that the user can ignore; false negatives leave real silent gaps).

4. Update the advisory text emitted by `_emit_sync_pat_advisory` to reference "branch protection rules or repository rulesets" (neutral wording).

### Verification

- Local unit: add `.agents/scripts/tests/test-security-posture-sync-pat.sh` that mocks both API endpoints and asserts detection in four cases: `classic`, `rulesets-only`, `both`, `neither`.
- Integration: `security-posture-helper.sh check <webapp>/<webapp>` after the fix should produce:

  ```
  Phase 7: SYNC_PAT Detection (issue-sync)
  [WARN] SYNC_PAT not set for <webapp>/<webapp> (rulesets-based protection)
         → gh secret set SYNC_PAT --repo <webapp>/<webapp>
  ```

- Regression: `marcusquinn/aidevops` (classic protection, SYNC_PAT set) should still PASS.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-security-posture-sync-pat.sh`
- `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` (one-line note: "detector handles rulesets" if current doc claims specific API)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_check_sync_pat_need` detects rulesets-protected repos via `/repos/{slug}/rulesets` API and emits the advisory.
- [ ] Regression: classic-protection repos still detected correctly; SYNC_PAT-set repos still PASS.
- [ ] Unit tests cover all four detection cases (classic / rulesets / both / neither).
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh` clean.
- [ ] On <webapp> (real repo), the advisory fires and the suggested `gh secret set SYNC_PAT` command is actionable.

## Context

- Detector lives in Phase 7 of `security-posture-helper.sh` (t2374 addition).
- Advisory infrastructure is already set up (`_emit_sync_pat_advisory`, `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync_pat_*.advisory`). No new infra needed.
- **Not a security hole** — classic API failure means "skip advisory", not "incorrectly authorise something". But it IS a silent health-check gap that cascades into auto-merge blockage downstream.

Related framework context (not in scope):

- `t2805` (GH#20743) — separate fix for the same downstream symptom (CI-drift rebase before fix-worker routing). Compatible fixes; either alone improves the situation.
- t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge gate semantics are unchanged by this task — we just ensure the upstream setup step is advertised correctly.

Tier: `tier:standard` — scoped single-file change, clear acceptance, existing test scaffolding.

title: t2808: migrate tools/design/library examples to DESIGN.md spec v0.1.0 format
body:
## What

Migrate the aidevops design library (55 brand examples + 12 style archetypes) from the legacy prose-only 9-section format to the spec-compliant two-layer format (YAML front matter tokens + canonical 8-section Markdown + aidevops §9/§10 extensions) defined by Google Labs DESIGN.md spec v0.1.0.

## Why

PR #20749 (t2807) brought the `design-md` agent and `aidevops init` template into line with the formal spec at [google-labs-code/design.md](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md). The library examples still use the pre-spec prose-only format. This makes them:

- Invisible to the `@google/design.md` CLI (`lint`, `diff`, `export`) — no YAML tokens to validate.
- Unable to export to Tailwind / DTCG / `tokens.json` for real projects.
- Inconsistent with the template we now ship to new users.

The spec tolerates prose-only files (unknown sections preserved, missing YAML produces warnings not errors), so this is a **quality upgrade, not a correctness fix** — it can be done incrementally and partial progress is shippable.

## How

### Reference pattern

Copy the YAML front matter structure from the updated template:

- **Template**: `.agents/templates/DESIGN.md.template` (PR #20749 — see YAML block at top)
- **Agent doc**: `.agents/tools/design/design-md.md` (PR #20749 — "YAML Front Matter Schema" and "Canonical Section Order")
- **Upstream example**: Google Labs ships three reference examples at [github.com/google-labs-code/design.md/tree/main/examples](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md/tree/main/examples) — `atmospheric-glass` is the most comprehensive

### Migration procedure per file

For each `tools/design/library/brands/{brand}/DESIGN.md` and `tools/design/library/styles/{archetype}/DESIGN.md`:

1. Extract existing colour hex values from §2 prose → populate `colors:` in YAML front matter using canonical token names (`primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `neutral`, `surface`, `on-surface`, `error`).
2. Extract typography specs from §3 hierarchy table → populate `typography:` using recommended level names (`headline-display`, `headline-lg`, `headline-md`, `body-lg`, `body-md`, `body-sm`, `label-lg`, `label-md`, `label-sm`).
3. Extract spacing values from §5 Layout → populate `spacing:` with canonical scale (`xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `gutter`, `margin`).
4. Extract radius values from §5 Border Radius Scale → populate `rounded:` with canonical scale (`none`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `full`).
5. Extract component specs from §4 → populate `components:` using token references (`{colors.primary}`, `{rounded.md}`, `{typography.label-md}`). Each variant (hover/active/disabled) is a sibling key, not nested.
6. Reorder prose sections to canonical order: Overview → Colors → Typography → Layout → Elevation & Depth → **Shapes** (new, extract from current §5) → Components → Do's and Don'ts → Responsive Behaviour (aidevops) → Agent Prompt Guide (aidevops).
7. Rename sections per the spec: `Visual Theme & Atmosphere` → `Overview`; `Colour Palette & Roles` → `Colors`; `Typography Rules` → `Typography`; `Component Stylings` → `Components`; `Layout Principles` → `Layout`; `Depth & Elevation` → `Elevation & Depth`.
8. Validate: `npx @google/design.md@0.1.1 lint .agents/tools/design/library/{path}/DESIGN.md` — must produce **0 errors** for every file. Warnings are acceptable (orphaned tokens are expected in examples that show off colour palettes without wiring every hue into a component).

### Chapter-file variants

Some brands use a chapter-file structure (`01-visual-theme.md`, `02-color-palette.md`, etc.) with a manifest `DESIGN.md` that indexes them — see `tools/design/library/brands/apple/` and `claude/`. For these:

- Put the YAML front matter on the **manifest** `DESIGN.md`, not on individual chapter files.
- Chapter files stay as prose-only detail documents — the manifest is the linter-visible artifact.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/design/library/brands/**/DESIGN.md`
- `.agents/tools/design/library/styles/**/DESIGN.md`

Do NOT modify:

- `.agents/tools/design/library/_template/DESIGN.md.template` (handled by t2807)
- `.agents/tools/design/library/_template/preview.html.template` (not affected by spec)
- Chapter files `01-*.md` through `09-*.md` (metadata lives on manifest only)

### Decomposition

Spec-compliant files are independent — no cross-file references exist. Migration can be done in batches:

1. **Batch 1** — 12 archetype styles (`styles/*.md`) — smaller set, consistent shape
2. **Batches 2-5** — 55 brand examples in groups of ~15, alphabetised (`brands/a*-c*`, `brands/d*-h*`, etc.)

Each batch is an independent PR. Workers should claim a follow-up task ID for each batch (`claim-task-id.sh --title "GH#20750 batch N: migrate library {group}"`).

## Acceptance

- [ ] All 12 `styles/*/DESIGN.md` files carry valid YAML front matter and pass `npx @google/design.md lint` with 0 errors.
- [ ] All 55 `brands/*/DESIGN.md` files (or their manifest equivalents) carry valid YAML front matter and pass `npx @google/design.md lint` with 0 errors.
- [ ] Section order matches the canonical spec (Overview → Colors → Typography → Layout → Elevation & Depth → Shapes → Components → Do's and Don'ts → [aidevops §9 Responsive] → [aidevops §10 Agent Prompt Guide]).
- [ ] Token references use `{colors.primary}`-style syntax in the `components:` block; no hardcoded hex values in components.
- [ ] No existing prose content is silently dropped during migration — if a section has no clean mapping (e.g. legacy "Distinctive Components" prose), preserve it as a final `## Notes` section (unknown sections are valid per spec).
- [ ] README at `tools/design/library/README.md` updated to note the library now ships spec-compliant YAML-enabled examples.

## Session Origin

- Parent task: t2807 (PR #20749) — agent + template alignment
- Interactive discussion: April 24, 2026 — user asked to compare aidevops `design-md` agent against [github.com/google-labs-code/design.md](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md); gap analysis identified YAML token layer + CLI validator + canonical section order as missing; user directed splitting into "agent+template now, library later"

## Context

- **Spec**: [google-labs-code/design.md @ v0.1.0](https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md), format version `alpha`
- **CLI**: `@google/design.md@0.1.1` on npm (Apache 2.0)
- **DTCG**: underlying token schema inspired by [W3C Design Tokens Format Module](https://tr.designtokens.org/format/)
- **Worked example**: Google Labs' `atmospheric-glass` reference DESIGN.md at `gh api repos/google-labs-code/design.md/contents/examples/atmospheric-glass/DESIGN.md --jq '.content' | base64 -d`

title: t2810: upstream-watch: file GitHub issues on detected updates
body:
## What

Extend `upstream-watch-helper.sh check` so that when a watched upstream transitions `updates_pending: 0 → 1`, the helper files a GitHub issue against the local aidevops repo describing the update. When a user runs `ack <slug>`, the corresponding issue is closed with a comment linking the adoption decision (merged PR, "no action needed", or "deferred").

Closes the audit-trail gap: today, detected updates live in `~/.aidevops/logs/upstream-watch.log` and runtime state only. A v1 release of `google-labs-code/design.md` — or any watched repo — would be silently noted and sit there until someone manually runs `status`.

## Why

Framework mission rule (prompts/build.txt): *"every change discoverable — what, who/what, why. Git is the audit trail; non-git work is invisible."*

Current flow violates that rule:

1. `auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:762` calls `upstream-watch-helper.sh check` once per 24h
2. Output is redirected to log: `"$upstream_watch_script" check >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1` (line 792)
3. `updates_pending: 1` is written to `~/.aidevops/cache/upstream-watch-state.json`
4. **No git-tracked artifact, no GitHub surface, no pulse notification**

By contrast, `skill-update-helper.sh` already solves the analogous problem for imported skills (creates one PR per skill when upstream changes). Upstream-watch should have the same level of integration into the task lifecycle.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT: `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper.sh`** — add issue-filing to the check path (two locations: `_check_github_repo` body inside the loop starting around line 400, and `_check_non_github_upstream` body around line 560); add close-on-ack in the `ack` command (search for `handle_ack` or the existing ack function).

### Reference pattern

Model on `skill-update-helper.sh` lines 873-964 (`_create_github_pr_for_skill`) — it demonstrates the same "detect upstream change → create GitHub artifact → include rich context" pattern. Key techniques to copy:

- Conventional-commit-style title with truncated version hash
- Body composed with heredoc including relevance prose + diff summary + explicit action link
- Dedup via `gh issue list --search`
- Use `gh_create_issue` wrapper (sourced from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`) — NOT raw `gh issue create`

### Specific changes

1. **New function** `_file_upstream_update_issue(slug_or_name, kind, old_value, new_value, entry_json)`:
   - Look up the local aidevops repo slug via `jq -r '.initialized_repos[] | select(.is_framework_dir == true) | .slug' ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json` (fallback: `marcusquinn/aidevops`)
   - Dedup: `gh issue list --repo <slug> --state open --search "source:upstream-watch slug:<slug>" --json number` — if one exists, update the existing issue body instead of creating a new one
   - Otherwise create a new issue with:
     - **Title**: `upstream: {slug} {kind:release|commit} → {new_value_short} (review adoption)`
     - **Body**: markdown with sections: Summary (relevance from config), What Changed (old→new with upstream compare URL), Affects (files from config `affects` array if present, else "see relevance text"), Action (instructions to review diff, propose PR, run `upstream-watch-helper.sh ack`), plus the hidden marker `<!-- aidevops:generator=upstream-watch -->` and `<!-- upstream-watch:slug=<slug> -->`
     - **Labels**: `source:upstream-watch`, `auto-dispatch`, `tier:standard`, `origin:worker`
     - **Signature footer**: via `gh-signature-helper.sh footer`

2. **Modify `_check_github_repo`** (~line 400) — after the existing `UPDATE DETECTED` echo, and ONLY when the state transitions 0→1 (check `$updates_pending_before != 1 && $has_update == true`), call `_file_upstream_update_issue`. Do NOT file on every check — only on the transition.

3. **Modify `_check_non_github_upstream`** (~line 560) — same pattern for non-GitHub entries.

4. **Modify `ack` command** (search for the function handling `ack`) — after marking state, look up the open issue via the same search query, comment with `> Acked by user. Adoption: <user-supplied optional arg>` (add optional `--note "text"` flag), then `gh issue close` with reason `completed`.

5. **Pre-dispatch validator** — add `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validators/upstream-watch-validator.sh` that re-runs the state check before a worker spawns on the issue: if `updates_pending == 0` (user has already acked), exit 10 (close the issue as no-longer-applicable). Register by matching the `source:upstream-watch` marker in `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh`.

### Edge cases

- **First-time add** of a watched repo: `add` sets `last_release_seen` to current release, so no spurious 0→1 transition on first check. Verify in the existing `_add_repo` function that the initial state is `updates_pending: 0`.
- **Re-detection** after an unmerged review (user ran check, issue exists, doesn't ack, next 24h check fires): dedup must prevent duplicate issues. Update the existing issue body if the current value has advanced further than what's in the body.
- **Offline/rate-limited `gh`**: if `gh_create_issue` fails, log a warning and continue — don't break the check loop. The retry happens next cycle.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/upstream-watch-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validators/upstream-watch-validator.sh` (NEW)
- `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` (add validator dispatch for `upstream-watch` marker)

Do NOT modify:

- `.agents/configs/upstream-watch.json` (user-level config)
- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh` (scheduling layer — issue-filing is the helper's responsibility, not the scheduler's)

## Acceptance

- [ ] `upstream-watch-helper.sh check` files a GitHub issue on `updates_pending: 0 → 1` transition for both GitHub repos and non-GitHub upstreams.
- [ ] Issue title, body, labels, and signature footer match the spec above.
- [ ] Dedup: running `check` twice without an `ack` in between does NOT create a second issue. Second run either updates the existing body (if the upstream advanced further) or is a no-op.
- [ ] `upstream-watch-helper.sh ack <slug>` closes the open matching issue with an ack comment.
- [ ] `ack <slug> --note "adopted in PR #NNNN"` includes the note in the close comment.
- [ ] Pre-dispatch validator closes the issue as no-longer-applicable if `updates_pending: 0` at worker-spawn time.
- [ ] Offline `gh` doesn't break the check loop — warning logged, state still updated, retry on next cycle.
- [ ] New shellcheck runs clean on modified files.

## Verification

Integration test in a disposable state directory:

```bash
# Prep — fake upstream state with an "old" release
export AIDEVOPS_UPSTREAM_WATCH_STATE=/tmp/uwtest-state.json
echo '{"github":{"google-labs-code/design.md":{"last_release_seen":"0.0.9","updates_pending":0}}}' > "$AIDEVOPS_UPSTREAM_WATCH_STATE"

# Check — should file one issue
upstream-watch-helper.sh check google-labs-code/design.md
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --search "source:upstream-watch slug:google-labs-code/design.md" --state open  # expect 1

# Second check — should dedup
upstream-watch-helper.sh check google-labs-code/design.md
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --search "source:upstream-watch slug:google-labs-code/design.md" --state open  # still expect 1

# Ack — should close
upstream-watch-helper.sh ack google-labs-code/design.md --note "test close"
gh issue list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --search "source:upstream-watch slug:google-labs-code/design.md" --state closed  # expect 1
```

## Session Origin

- Task t2807 / PR #20749 added `google-labs-code/design.md` to upstream-watch
- User asked: "will upstream watch file its own issues on upstream updates?"
- Investigation: `upstream-watch-helper.sh` has NO issue-filing paths. `grep -E "gh_create_issue|gh issue create"` in the helper returns 0 matches. Detection lands in `~/.aidevops/logs/upstream-watch.log` only.
- Confirmed this violates the framework's mission rule ("every change discoverable; non-git work is invisible")
- Filed this task to close the gap

## Context

- **Reference implementation**: `.agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh` lines 873-964 (per-skill PR creation with dedup)
- **Scheduling layer** (do not modify): `.agents/scripts/auto-update-freshness-lib.sh:762-800` calls `check` once per 24h
- **Pre-dispatch validator pattern**: `.agents/reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`
- **Signature footer**: `prompts/build.txt` §"#8 Signature footer hallucination" — use `gh-signature-helper.sh footer`
- **gh wrapper**: `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` provides `gh_create_issue`, `gh_issue_edit_safe`, `gh_issue_comment`
