title: planning-commit-helper.sh: log_warning: command not found (function-name mismatch; shared-constants.sh defines log_warn)
body:
## Description

`planning-commit-helper.sh` calls `log_warning` at 6 sites but `shared-constants.sh` only defines `log_warn`. Every invocation of those branches fails with `log_warning: command not found`. The helper then proceeds (no `set -e` around the call), so the observable symptom varies by branch:

- Line 561 branch (offline/push-failed fallback) — memory note from a prior session reports a silent commit failure here: files remain staged, no commit lands, no non-zero exit.
- Lines 164, 205, 211, 304, 525 — warning text is lost, execution continues.

Six independent /new-task worker sessions hit this on 2026-04-24 in the qs-agency repo while creating tasks t283–t288. All fell back to manual `git commit` + `git push` successfully, but the error polluted logs and signals a broader problem: this is not specific to `planning-commit-helper.sh`.

**Scope (call-site sweep):**

```
rg -c "log_warning\b" .agents/scripts/ → 60 callsites
rg -c "\blog_warn\b"  .agents/scripts/ → 485 callsites
```

Affected helpers that call `log_warning` WITHOUT defining a local fallback (will fail at runtime on those branches):

- `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` — 6 callsites (164, 205, 211, 304, 525, 561)
- `.agents/scripts/virustotal-helper.sh` — 3 callsites (456, 563, 681)
- `.agents/scripts/plugin-loader-helper.sh` — 7 callsites (55, 68, 189, 216, 240, 269, 295, 621, 641)
- `.agents/scripts/tech-stack-helper.sh` — 4 callsites (305, 1257, 1269, 1276, 1279)

Helpers that work around it with a local definition (not broken, but divergent — cosmetic output only):

- `.agents/scripts/generate-skills.sh:75` defines `log_warning()`
- `.agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh:84` defines `log_warning()`

## Expected Behavior

One of:

1. **Rename callsites** — change all `log_warning` to `log_warn` in the non-self-defining helpers. Smallest diff, fewest side effects.
2. **Add alias in `shared-constants.sh`** — define `log_warning() { log_warn "$@"; }` so both names work. Removes the divergence with `generate-skills.sh` / `skill-update-helper.sh`'s local definitions (they could then drop their locals).

Option 2 is probably the intent — `log_warning` is the more common English name and two helpers already carry local definitions of it; the absence of an alias in `shared-constants.sh` looks like an oversight.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh next_task_id --title "test probe"
```

Any code path that hits one of the six `log_warning` callsites — e.g., running offline will exercise line 525 via `claim-task-id.sh`.

**Actual output** (as observed by six independent sessions on 2026-04-24):

```
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh: line 561: log_warning: command not found
```

…and, per the 2026-04-23 memory note for the line-561 branch: files remain staged, no commit lands, no non-zero exit code.

**Expected output**: a yellow `[WARN]` log line via `log_warn`, execution continuing cleanly.

**Causal code**:

```
git blame .agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh -L 561,561
a8ac72c704 (Marcus Quinn 2026-02-12 13:55:16 +0000 561) 		log_warning "Committed locally (push failed after retries - will retry later)"

git blame .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh -L 590,590
6dd285c6aa (Marcus Quinn 2026-02-27 02:37:37 +0000 590) log_warn() {
```

The `log_warning` callsites predate or diverge from the `log_warn` definition. No rename migration was run across callsites.

**Source-chain check**: Deployed (`~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`) and source (`~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`) have identical mtime and size — this is NOT a stale deploy. The source itself is broken.

**Framework rule check**: `planning-commit-helper.sh:22` correctly sources `shared-constants.sh`. The problem is purely the function name mismatch; the "source shared-constants.sh" rule from build.txt is already satisfied.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `/new-task` in any repo via an interactive Claude Code / Claude Code session (dispatched via Task tool).
2. Worker runs `planning-commit-helper.sh` to commit the brief and TODO.md update.
3. One of the 6 branches fires (any push retry, any `next_task_id` allocation path, any `--verified` call, etc.).
4. Shell emits `log_warning: command not found`; on line 561 the commit may silently fail to land even though the message suggests local success.
5. Worker falls back to manual `git add` + `git commit` + `git push`.

## Workarounds Applied

Six /new-task sessions on 2026-04-24 (creating t283–t288 in qs-agency) and at least one prior session on 2026-04-23 applied this workaround:

- After `planning-commit-helper.sh` exits, check `git status` and `git log --oneline -1` — if the commit didn't land, run `git add <brief> TODO.md`, `git commit -m <msg>`, `git push` manually.

This is entirely manual; there is no framework-side workaround other than duplicating the fallback logic in each session. Stored as a memory note on 2026-04-23, but memory alone doesn't fix the helper.

## Siblings (candidate follow-ups)

None filed yet — the same root cause affects 3 other helpers listed above. If this issue fixes the name mismatch globally (Option 2 alias), no siblings are needed. If Option 1 (rename callsites), siblings should be filed for `virustotal-helper.sh`, `plugin-loader-helper.sh`, and `tech-stack-helper.sh`.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.10.2
- **Latest version**: 3.10.2
- **Install method**: /home/rob/.local/bin/aidevops
- **AI Assistant**: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.7) — diagnostics script reported "OpenCode" due to env var fingerprint; actual runtime is Claude Code.
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo at time of observation**: qs-agency (main)
- **gh CLI**: 2.91.0

## Additional Context

- Memory note from 2026-04-23 (high confidence) documenting the same symptom + extra detail on silent commit failure at line 561.
- Six independent workers on 2026-04-24 reported the error identically without coordination — rules out a local-env issue.
- `log_warn` is called 485 times framework-wide and works. `log_warning` is called 60 times; the only ones that "work" are in files that shadow the missing function with a local definition.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decide Option 1 (rename callsites) or Option 2 (alias in `shared-constants.sh`) — Option 2 recommended for minimal diff and lowest regression risk.
- [ ] Apply fix to `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` and/or affected helpers.
- [ ] If Option 2: consider dropping local `log_warning()` definitions in `generate-skills.sh` and `skill-update-helper.sh` for cleanliness (not required for the fix).
- [ ] Verify with a test `/new-task` invocation that `log_warning: command not found` no longer appears.
- [ ] Verify the line-561 branch specifically — simulate a push failure and confirm the warning is logged AND the commit still lands locally.
- [ ] No regression in logging output (yellow [WARN] prefix preserved).

Suggested labels: `bug`, `shell-helpers`, `low-severity`.

title: t2811: Release interactive claim on Ref/For-keyword planning PR merges (claim-stamp leak)
body:
## What

Extend `release_interactive_claim_on_merge()` in `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` so it fires when a merged PR uses `Ref #NNN` or `For #NNN` keywords (planning-only PRs), not just closing keywords (`Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves`).

Currently, planning-only PRs from interactive sessions deliberately use `Ref #NNN` / `For #NNN` to avoid auto-closing the linked issue — but `release_interactive_claim_on_merge()` depends on `_extract_linked_issue()` which ONLY matches closing keywords. Result: every planning-PR merge leaves the interactive claim stamp stranded, requiring manual release.

## Why

**Canonical occurrence (2026-04-24):** PR #20754 (t2809 plan refresh) merged cleanly but required manual `interactive-session-helper.sh release 20753 marcusquinn/aidevops` because the PR body used `Ref #20753` per the planning-PR keyword rule (`templates/brief-template.md` "PR Conventions", `.github/workflows/planning-pr-keyword-check.yml`).

**Not catastrophic** — stamps are released at session end or by `scan-stale`. But it's:

- **Predictable** (every planning-only interactive PR hits this path)
- **Avoidable** (the design already separates "release claim" from "close issue")
- **Visible** to the user as "PR merged but claim still active" confusion until next `scan-stale` runs

**Why `_extract_linked_issue` should NOT be extended:** the strict closing-keyword regex there is load-bearing for the auto-close path in `_handle_post_merge_actions` (pulse-merge.sh). Extending it would close issues on planning-only PRs — the exact bug t2108/t2204 guards against. So the fix belongs in the release path, not the extractor.

## How

### Option A (recommended): Permissive fallback inside release function

EDIT `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:64-99` — `release_interactive_claim_on_merge()`:

When Guard 1 would return 0 (linked_issue empty), attempt a permissive extraction before giving up:

```bash
# Before Guard 1 early-return, try permissive fallback.
# Strict `_extract_linked_issue` already checked in caller and came back empty.
# Permissive match covers `Ref #NNN` / `For #NNN` on planning-only PRs
# that carry an interactive claim stamp.
if [[ -z "$linked_issue" ]]; then
    local pr_body
    pr_body=$(gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo_slug" --json body --jq '.body // empty' 2>/dev/null) || pr_body=""
    # Match close/fix/resolve (defence in depth) + ref/refs/for.
    # Keeps the authoritative set narrow: only keywords that ALREADY carry
    # an issue-reference convention in aidevops PRs.
    linked_issue=$(printf '%s' "$pr_body" | grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?|ref(s|erences?)?|for)\s+#[0-9]+' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
fi
[[ -z "$linked_issue" ]] && return 0
```

**Precedent pattern** — `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh:850-858` uses a similar wider regex (`resolves|closes|fixes|for`) in `_isc_extract_pr_linked_issues`. Model on that.

**Placement rationale** — put the fallback inside `release_interactive_claim_on_merge` rather than in callers (`pulse-merge.sh:1185`, `full-loop-helper.sh:1468`) so both call sites get the fix without duplication.

### Option B (rejected): Extend `_extract_linked_issue`

Would break auto-close semantics. Do NOT do this.

### Option C (rejected): Stamp-driven scan

Scan `CLAIM_STAMP_DIR` for stamps matching PR's author+repo+recency, release any. More robust but increases API surface and fights the existing guard architecture. Reserve for a future pass if Option A proves insufficient.

### Edge case: false-positive release

A PR body that says `Ref #999` as context (not as the PR's primary linkage) would spuriously match and release claim #999 from a different session. Mitigations:

- Guards 2-4 already constrain scope to `origin:interactive` + existing claim stamp (rare combo for unrelated issues).
- `interactive-session-helper.sh release` is idempotent (re-claim if still needed).
- Accept the risk — the alternative (leaving stamps stranded) is worse and more predictable.

If the team judges the false-positive risk too high, narrow the fallback to `head -1` on the first paragraph of the PR body only (typical planning-PR convention places the `Ref #NNN` in the first few lines).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `release_interactive_claim_on_merge()` fires when PR body contains `Ref #NNN` / `For #NNN` and all other guards (origin:interactive, stamp file exists) pass
- [ ] `release_interactive_claim_on_merge()` still short-circuits silently when guards fail (no breaking change to existing success path)
- [ ] New unit test in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-auto-release.sh` covering the Ref/For fallback path — model on existing test cases at `:144-270`
- [ ] Existing unit tests in `test-full-loop-merge-auto-release.sh` + `test-pulse-merge-auto-release.sh` still pass
- [ ] `_extract_linked_issue` in `pulse-merge.sh:1607` unchanged — strict closing-keyword semantics preserved

## Verification

```bash
# Unit tests pass:
```

title: pulse-nmr-approval: scanner-label creation-default check defeats circuit-breaker gate → ever-NMR trap
body:
## Summary

`_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` runs the **creation-default signature** check before the **circuit-breaker trip** check. The creation-default branch matches on any issue that carries a scanner-provenance label (`source:review-feedback`, `source:review-scanner`, `review-followup`) **regardless of when NMR was applied** — those labels persist for the life of the issue. This short-circuits the circuit-breaker check for every scanner-generated issue that subsequently trips a breaker (stale-recovery, cost, no_work_loop). Auto-approval strips NMR, the `ever-NMR` history flag remains set, and the issue is trapped: `auto-dispatch` label ON, NMR removed, dispatch permanently blocked by `ever-NMR` until a human runs `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>`.

This is the **incomplete half of the t2386 fix** (#19756 post-mortem). t2386 removed breaker markers from the **comment-marker** branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature`, but left the **label-based** branch which is always co-temporal because labels never expire.

## Canonical Evidence

`<webapp>/<webapp>#2717` — a `source:review-feedback` quality-debt issue.

| Time (UTC) | Event | Comment/Log |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-24 04:06:53 | Issue created by `quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged`, labelled `source:review-feedback`, `tier:standard`, `auto-dispatch` | — |
| 04:26:08 | Worker #1 (alex-solovyev runner) crashed before engaging — `no_work` | stale recovery tick 1/2 |
| 04:41:10 | CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_failed | — |
| 04:55:46 | Worker #2 crashed same way | stale recovery tick 2/2 |
| 05:07:24 | **Label `needs-maintainer-review` applied by `stale-recovery-tick:escalated` path** | (label event) |
| 05:07:32 | Comment posted: `<!-- stale-recovery-tick:escalated (threshold=2) -->` | +8s from label event — well inside the ±60s breaker-trip window |
| ~05:07:40 | `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` runs → `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` returns 0 (because `source:review-feedback` label present) → auto-approval **removes NMR** | `[pulse-wrapper] Auto-approved #2717 — maintainer is author, NMR applied by automation` |
| ~05:07:45 | Next dispatch attempt | `[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_with_dedup: BLOCKED #2717 — requires cryptographic approval (ever-NMR)` |
| (ongoing) | Pulse posts `ever-nmr-remediation` comment once; user must manually run `sudo aidevops approve issue 2717` | — |

The circuit-breaker comment at 05:07:32 falls perfectly inside the `label_at ± 60s` window checked by `_nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip`. **That check is never reached** because the label-based branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` returns 0 first.

## Root-cause code reference

`.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`

- **The bug site:** `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (lines 416-456) checks automation-signature **before** circuit-breaker-trip:

    ```bash
    if _nmr_application_has_automation_signature "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
        return 1   # auto-approve OK
    fi
    if _nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
        return 0   # PRESERVE NMR
    fi
    ```

- **The root cause:** the label-based branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (lines 321-329) does not check timing:

    ```bash
    has_bot_label=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/issues/${issue_number}" \
        --jq '[.labels[].name] | map(select(. == "review-followup" or . == "source:review-scanner" or . == "source:review-feedback")) | length' ...)
    if [[ "$has_bot_label" -gt 0 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    ```

    These labels persist for the life of the issue. So any NMR application on a scanner-labelled issue is misclassified as a "creation default" regardless of whether the label event was actually co-temporal with issue creation.

- **The t2386 comment block (lines 253-262) explicitly warns about this failure mode** but only for the marker-based branch. The label-based branch added later (labelled t2686 in the code) re-opened the same hole for a different class of co-temporality violations.

## Fix (recommended)

Invert the check order AND tighten the label-branch to be co-temporal. Defense in depth.

**1. Invert in `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (lines 444-453):**

    if [[ -n "$nmr_at" ]]; then
        # Circuit-breaker check FIRST — the co-temporal marker is a stronger
        # signal than label persistence. Scanner-labelled issues that trip a
        # breaker MUST preserve NMR regardless of creation provenance.
        if _nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
            echo "[pulse-wrapper] ... — circuit breaker tripped — PRESERVING NMR ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
            return 0
        fi
        if _nmr_application_has_automation_signature "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
            echo "[pulse-wrapper] ... — creation-default signature detected ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
            return 1
        fi
    fi

**2. Tighten the label-branch in `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (lines 321-329):** only match the scanner label when NMR was applied within N seconds of issue creation — e.g. 5 minutes. Any later NMR event on the same issue is either manual or a breaker trip, not a creation default.

    # Scanner label alone is not sufficient — require the NMR event to have
    # been co-temporal with issue creation (within 300s). Later NMR events
    # on scanner-labelled issues are manual holds or breaker trips.
    local issue_created_at
    issue_created_at=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/issues/${issue_number}" --jq '.created_at' 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ -n "$issue_created_at" && -n "$label_at" ]]; then
        local gap
        gap=$(python3 -c "from datetime import datetime; \
            c=datetime.fromisoformat('$issue_created_at'.replace('Z','+00:00')); \
            l=datetime.fromisoformat('$label_at'.replace('Z','+00:00')); \
            print(int((l-c).total_seconds()))" 2>/dev/null) || gap=999999
        if (( gap <= 300 )); then
            if [[ "$has_bot_label" -gt 0 ]]; then
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    fi

(Approximation — the helper may already have a more idiomatic time-diff utility; prefer that.)

Either fix alone closes this specific case. Both together makes the intent explicit and resilient to future ordering changes.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:444-453` — invert check order in `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:321-329` — add creation-time co-temporality guard to label-based branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh` — regression test

## Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh` — already covers the marker-based classification matrix. The new regression test should extend this pattern with scenarios where a scanner-labelled issue subsequently trips a circuit breaker.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A mock issue with `source:review-feedback` label + NMR applied +60s after a `stale-recovery-tick:escalated` comment → `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` returns 0 (PRESERVE NMR).
2. A mock issue with `source:review-feedback` label + NMR applied at creation time (no breaker comment in window) → still returns 1 (auto-approve OK) — no regression on the happy path.
3. A mock issue with `source:review-feedback` label + NMR applied with neither a creation-time signature nor a breaker marker (pure manual hold at ± 1h from creation) → returns 0 (PRESERVE — manual hold).
4. Existing `test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh` continues to pass unchanged.
5. No-work-loop breaker (`cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop`) on a scanner-labelled issue preserves NMR.

## Verification

    bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh
    bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh   # new
    shellcheck ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh

## Blast-radius check

One-shot sweep for other trapped issues across all pulse-enabled repos:

    for slug in $(jq -r '.initialized_repos[] | select(.pulse==true and (.local_only//false)==false) | .slug' ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json); do
      gh issue list --repo "$slug" --state open --label "auto-dispatch" --json number,title,labels \
        | jq -r --arg slug "$slug" '.[] | select(.labels | map(.name) | contains(["source:review-feedback"]) or contains(["source:review-scanner"]) or contains(["review-followup"])) | "\($slug)#\(.number) \(.title)"'
    done

For each match, check `aidevops approve verify <N>` — if unverified AND pulse logs show `BLOCKED ... ever-NMR`, it's a survivor of the same trap and needs manual approval.

## Why this wastes user tokens

Every `ever-NMR`-trapped issue requires the maintainer to: (a) notice the ever-nmr-remediation comment, (b) diagnose whether the worker crashes were legitimate infra issues or unimplementable scope, (c) run the crypto-approval command OR pick the issue up interactively (as I'm doing now). Scanner-generated issues are THE most common class of issue in this framework — every quality-debt ticket, every review-followup, every post-merge scanner finding. The trap is likely firing hundreds of times across the network of repos running this framework, each time pulling a human out of flow to crypto-approve a trivial fix whose body already contained the full instructions.

This is also why the symptom is invisible in pulse stats: the wasted tokens aren't worker tokens (workers died pre-engagement), they're **maintainer tokens** — human cognitive load plus the interactive session that unblocks each trapped issue. The framework's token metering doesn't capture this cost.

## Companion investigation

The upstream `no_work` worker crashes that triggered the stale-recovery escalation in the first place need their own investigation (see also #20702 / t2804). That's a separate issue — filing alongside, not blocking this one.

## Session origin

Interactive session against `<webapp>/<webapp>#2717` on 2026-04-24. PR #2781 (idempotent DO-block wrap) ships the user-visible fix; this issue ships the framework-level fix so future occurrences of the same pattern self-recover without manual crypto-approval.

## How

1. Read `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (lines 416-456) and `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (lines 284-332) — confirm the call graph and the comment intent.
2. Review the t2386 post-mortem commentary at lines 253-267 — the marker-only fix is explained there; this is the companion label-path hole.
3. Apply both fixes (order inversion + label co-temporality).
4. Write the regression test covering the 5 acceptance scenarios.
5. Run existing NMR test suite for regression.
6. Sweep for trapped issues per the Blast-radius section above; post a remediation comment linking this PR on any survivors.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh`

title: t2815: Phase 4 — prevent cascade tier escalation on infra failures
body:
## What

Prevent `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` from triggering cascade tier escalation. Infrastructure failures (worker never spawned) must be classified distinctly from coding failures (worker spawned but failed to implement) and handled with same-tier retry or bail — not tier upgrade.

Child of parent-task #20740 (t2804). Ref #20740. Blocked by t2814 (Phase 3 fix).

## Why

The current cascade escalation treats all dispatch failures uniformly: `tier:standard` → `tier:thinking` → `needs-maintainer-review`. When a worker never spawned (infra failure), escalating to a more expensive model is wasteful — the problem is not that the model couldn't solve the task, but that the worker process never started. An opus dispatch for an infra failure burns budget without any possibility of success.

Observable evidence from #20702: cascade went `standard` → `thinking` (opus) multiple times, each attempt ending with `no_worker_process`. Every tier upgrade was wasted.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — modify the cascade escalation logic to check the failure classification before upgrading tiers. Specifically:
  - Find the cascade escalation function/section (search for `cascade`, `tier.*escalat`, `launch_recovery`)
  - Add a guard: if failure type is `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` (or any infra-class failure), retry at the SAME tier or bail after N retries — do NOT escalate to a higher tier
  - New failure signature: `launch_recovery:spawn_exec_failed` or `launch_recovery:infra_failure` (distinct from coding failure)

### Reference pattern

- READ: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — find the cascade escalation logic. Look for where `tier:standard` is upgraded to `tier:thinking` and what conditions trigger it.
- READ: `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — lifecycle documentation for the dispatch → recovery path

### Implementation steps

1. Locate the cascade escalation code in `pulse-wrapper.sh`
2. Identify where `launch_recovery` outcomes feed into the escalation decision
3. Add a conditional: if `launch_recovery:no_worker_process`, skip tier upgrade, retry same tier (max 2 retries), then bail with `DISPATCH_INFRA_FAILURE` status
4. Update the `launch_recovery` classifier to output distinct signatures:
   - `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` → infra failure (no escalation)
   - `launch_recovery:worker_timeout` → coding failure (escalation allowed)
   - `launch_recovery:worker_crashed` → coding failure (escalation allowed)
5. Run `shellcheck` on all modified scripts

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
# Verify the cascade escalation logic correctly skips tier upgrade for infra failures
grep -n "no_worker_process\|infra_failure\|spawn_exec_failed" .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Cascade tier escalation does NOT trigger for `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` failures
- [ ] Infra failures retry at the same tier (max 2 retries) before bailing
- [ ] Distinct failure signatures exist for infra vs coding failures
- [ ] All modified scripts pass `shellcheck`
- [ ] `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` updated with the new classification scheme

## Problem

`prompt-guard-helper.sh` flags the literal English phrase "dark mode" / "light mode" as a HIGH-severity `role_play: Evil twin persona attempt` whenever it appears in any scanned content.

### Reproduction

Tested against `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (a public repo of design-focused skill markdown) during a security review. The scanner produced 5 HIGH findings across 5 SKILL.md files, all for the exact same phrase:

| File | Matched text |
|---|---|
| `skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/redesign-skill/SKILL.md` | `dark mode` |
| `skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |
| `imagegenskills/frontendwebsiteimageskill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |

Context from one of the files (`skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md:424-427`) is a palette-preset list, not an injection:

```text
1. Pristine Light Mode
2. Deep Dark Mode
3. Bold Studio Solid
4. Quiet Premium Neutral
```

### Why this is a false positive

The `role_play` pattern is intended to catch jailbreak invocations of the form `<adjective> mode` — "DAN mode", "developer mode", "evil mode", "godmode", "jailbreak mode". "Dark mode" and "light mode" are UI colour-theme terms in near-universal use across CSS, Tailwind, `prefers-color-scheme`, design systems, and user-facing product settings. Any scan over design content, CSS, theming docs, accessibility guidance, or UX writing will trip this pattern.

### Impact

- Every design-related skill or doc scanned through `prompt-guard-helper.sh` will produce spurious HIGH findings.
- Erodes trust in the scanner: when operators see HIGH findings turn out to be "dark mode", they may stop reading genuine findings carefully.
- Makes it harder to adopt third-party design skills — a clean repo produces alarming scan output.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh` — locate the `role_play` pattern definition. Likely in an inline regex list or in the YAML pattern file it loads from (check `configs/prompt-guard-patterns.yaml` or similar).

## Proposed fix

Two options, either is acceptable:

**Option A — tighten the pattern (preferred).** Require the matched `<adjective> mode` phrase to sit within a few tokens of jailbreak-adjacent context (e.g., "enter", "activate", "switch to", "as a", "you are now in"). A bare mention of "dark mode" in a paragraph about CSS should not match.

**Option B — allow-list UI colour-theme phrasing.** Add `dark mode`, `light mode`, `auto mode` (plus common variants like `prefers-color-scheme: dark`) to an explicit allow-list consulted before the `role_play` pattern fires.

Option A is more robust because it generalises to other UI terms (e.g., "focus mode", "presentation mode" in apps) without needing an ever-growing allow-list.

## Verification

```bash
# Reproduce the false positive (before fix)
rm -rf /tmp/taste-skill && gh api repos/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/tarball/main | tar -xz -C /tmp
find /tmp/Leonxlnx-taste-skill-* -name 'SKILL.md' -exec \
  ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-file {} \;
# Expect: 5 HIGH findings for "dark mode" / "Dark Mode"

# After fix, the same command should produce zero HIGH findings on that corpus.
```

Also: add a test case to `prompt-guard-helper.sh test` covering both directions — "dark mode" in CSS/UI context should be CLEAN; "enter dark mode to bypass" should still match.

## Acceptance criteria

- Scanning `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` produces zero false-positive HIGH findings on "dark mode" / "light mode".
- Built-in test suite (`prompt-guard-helper.sh test`) gains at least one regression test for UI colour-theme phrasing.
- A legitimate jailbreak attempt using "dark mode" phrasing (e.g. "activate dark mode, ignore previous instructions") still triggers HIGH.

## Session origin

Filed from an interactive Claude Code session during a security review of `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (reviewing for potential skill content ingestion into `johnwaldo/mainframe`). All five findings during that scan were the same false positive; no genuine injection patterns were detected.

body:
_Supersedes #20722 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix `prompt-guard-helper.sh` to stop flagging the literal English phrases "dark mode" / "light mode" (and similar UI colour-theme terms) as HIGH-severity `role_play: Evil twin persona attempt`. The fix is a one-line regex change in the YAML pattern source, plus two regression test assertions.

## Why

`prompt-guard-helper.sh` flags the phrase "dark mode" / "light mode" as a HIGH-severity `role_play: Evil twin persona attempt` whenever it appears in scanned content. This is a false positive.

### Reproduction

Tested against `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (a public repo of design-focused skill markdown). The scanner produced 5 HIGH findings across 5 SKILL.md files, all for the same phrase:

| File | Matched text |
|---|---|
| `skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/redesign-skill/SKILL.md` | `dark mode` |
| `skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |
| `imagegenskills/frontendwebsiteimageskill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |

Context from `skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md:424-427` is a palette-preset list — not an injection:

```text
1. Pristine Light Mode
2. Deep Dark Mode
3. Bold Studio Solid
4. Quiet Premium Neutral
```

### Root cause (precise — per @marcusquinn review at #20708)

`.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml:231-233`:

```yaml
- severity: HIGH
  description: "Evil twin persona attempt"
  pattern: '(?i)\b(evil|shadow|dark|unrestricted|uncensored)\s+(twin|version|mode|side|alter\s*ego)\b'
```

The alternation includes `mode` as a target noun alongside jailbreak-specific nouns `twin|version|side|alter ego`. A bare `dark mode` matches `dark` + `mode` with no contextual gate. This pattern was originally imported from the Lasso pattern set (PR #2715, t1375.1) without the narrowing needed for a codebase that routinely scans design content and CSS docs.

**Important fix target note:** The issue body of #20708 lists `prompt-guard-helper.sh` as the edit target. The actual fix site is `.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml:231-233` (YAML is the primary pattern source per `_pg_load_yaml_patterns()`, line 158). The inline patterns at `prompt-guard-helper.sh:270-301` do NOT contain this rule — the inline `role_play` set is narrower and correctly does not trip on "dark mode".

### Why it matters

- Every design-related skill or doc scanned through `prompt-guard-helper.sh` produces spurious HIGH findings.
- Erodes trust in the scanner: when operators see HIGH findings turn out to be "dark mode", they may stop reading genuine findings carefully.
- Makes it harder to adopt third-party design skills — a clean repo produces alarming scan output.
- `dark mode`, `light mode`, `auto mode` are universal UI colour-theme terms in CSS (`prefers-color-scheme: dark`), Tailwind (`dark:` variants), macOS/iOS/Windows system settings, and every modern design system.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml:231-233` — remove `mode|` from the second alternation group in the `role_play` evil-twin pattern
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh` — add two regression test cases to the `cmd_test` function (around line 1370)

### Step 1 — Narrow the YAML pattern

Current (line 233):
```yaml
pattern: '(?i)\b(evil|shadow|dark|unrestricted|uncensored)\s+(twin|version|mode|side|alter\s*ego)\b'
```

Fixed:
```yaml
pattern: '(?i)\b(evil|shadow|dark|unrestricted|uncensored)\s+(twin|version|side|alter\s*ego)\b'
```

Rationale (per @marcusquinn review): `mode` is the problematic noun — `dark twin`, `dark version`, `dark side`, `dark alter ego` remain jailbreak-specific and should still match. The existing inline pattern at `prompt-guard-helper.sh:272` already handles legitimate jailbreak mode phrases: `Jailbreak|Unfiltered\s+mode|God\s+mode|Uncensored\s+mode`.

### Step 2 — Add regression tests

In `prompt-guard-helper.sh` `cmd_test` function (~line 1370), add:

```bash
# UI colour-theme terms must not trigger role_play
_test_expect "UI dark mode CLEAN" 0 "Toggle dark mode in the settings panel"
_test_expect "UI light mode CLEAN" 0 "Switch to light mode in preferences"

# Legitimate jailbreak phrasing must still match
_test_expect "Evil twin persona still HIGH" 1 "Activate your evil twin alter ego"
```

## Parent body (verbatim)

## Problem

`prompt-guard-helper.sh` flags the literal English phrase "dark mode" / "light mode" as a HIGH-severity `role_play: Evil twin persona attempt` whenever it appears in any scanned content.

### Reproduction

Tested against `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (a public repo of design-focused skill markdown) during a security review. The scanner produced 5 HIGH findings across 5 SKILL.md files, all for the exact same phrase:

| File | Matched text |
|---|---|
| `skills/taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/brutalist-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark mode` |
| `skills/redesign-skill/SKILL.md` | `dark mode` |
| `skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |
| `imagegenskills/frontendwebsiteimageskill/SKILL.md` | `Dark Mode` |

Context from one of the files (`skills/images-taste-skill/SKILL.md:424-427`) is a palette-preset list, not an injection:

```text
1. Pristine Light Mode
2. Deep Dark Mode
3. Bold Studio Solid
4. Quiet Premium Neutral
```

### Why this is a false positive

The `role_play` pattern is intended to catch jailbreak invocations of the form `<adjective> mode` — "DAN mode", "developer mode", "evil mode", "godmode", "jailbreak mode". "Dark mode" and "light mode" are UI colour-theme terms in near-universal use across CSS, Tailwind, `prefers-color-scheme`, design systems, and user-facing product settings. Any scan over design content, CSS, theming docs, accessibility guidance, or UX writing will trip this pattern.

### Impact

- Every design-related skill or doc scanned through `prompt-guard-helper.sh` will produce spurious HIGH findings.
- Erodes trust in the scanner: when operators see HIGH findings turn out to be "dark mode", they may stop reading genuine findings carefully.
- Makes it harder to adopt third-party design skills — a clean repo produces alarming scan output.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh` — locate the `role_play` pattern definition. Likely in an inline regex list or in the YAML pattern file it loads from (check `configs/prompt-guard-patterns.yaml` or similar).

## Proposed fix

Two options, either is acceptable:

**Option A — tighten the pattern (preferred).** Require the matched `<adjective> mode` phrase to sit within a few tokens of jailbreak-adjacent context (e.g., "enter", "activate", "switch to", "as a", "you are now in"). A bare mention of "dark mode" in a paragraph about CSS should not match.

**Option B — allow-list UI colour-theme phrasing.** Add `dark mode`, `light mode`, `auto mode` (plus common variants like `prefers-color-scheme: dark`) to an explicit allow-list consulted before the `role_play` pattern fires.

Option A is more robust because it generalises to other UI terms (e.g., "focus mode", "presentation mode" in apps) without needing an ever-growing allow-list.

## Verification

```bash
# Reproduce the false positive (before fix)
rm -rf /tmp/taste-skill && gh api repos/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/tarball/main | tar -xz -C /tmp
find /tmp/Leonxlnx-taste-skill-* -name 'SKILL.md' -exec \
  ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/prompt-guard-helper.sh scan-file {} \;
# Expect: 5 HIGH findings for "dark mode" / "Dark Mode"

# After fix, the same command should produce zero HIGH findings on that corpus.
```

Also: add a test case to `prompt-guard-helper.sh test` covering both directions — "dark mode" in CSS/UI context should be CLEAN; "enter dark mode to bypass" should still match.

## Acceptance criteria

- Scanning `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` produces zero false-positive HIGH findings on "dark mode" / "light mode".
- Built-in test suite (`prompt-guard-helper.sh test`) gains at least one regression test for UI colour-theme phrasing.
- A legitimate jailbreak attempt using "dark mode" phrasing (e.g. "activate dark mode, ignore previous instructions") still triggers HIGH.

## Session origin

Filed from an interactive Claude Code session during a security review of `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` (reviewing for potential skill content ingestion into `johnwaldo/mainframe`). All five findings during that scan were the same false positive; no genuine injection patterns were detected.

Model test additions on existing `_test_expect` calls in the `cmd_test` function of `prompt-guard-helper.sh`.

- [ ] Scanning `Leonxlnx/taste-skill` produces zero false-positive HIGH findings on "dark mode" / "light mode"

- [ ] A legitimate jailbreak attempt using related phrasing (e.g. "activate your evil twin") still triggers HIGH
- [ ] Existing `prompt-guard-helper.sh test` suite passes with no regressions on genuine jailbreak patterns

```bash

rm -rf /tmp/taste-skill && gh api repos/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/tarball/main | tar -xz -C /tmp
```

- **Original report** (parent #20708 body): Identified the false positive with 5 specific files from `Leonxlnx/taste-skill`, proposed two options (A: contextual gating, B: allow-list), and cited "dark mode" / "light mode" as universal UI terms.

title: issue-sync mislabels open sibling task as status:done when same PR completes a different task
body:
## Symptom

When a PR completes one TODO.md task (e.g. t306 marked `[x]`) and references a different sibling task in the body (e.g. `Ref #1893` for t291, which remains `[ ]`), the post-merge issue-sync run applies `status:done` to the **referenced** issue, not just the resolved one.

Concrete failure: robstiles/qs-agency PR #1941 (merge commit `cf3e03d`).

- PR body: `Resolves #1929` (t306, marked `[x]` on merge) + `Ref #1893` (t291, still `[ ]` in TODO.md)
- Expected post-merge labels on #1893: unchanged (still `status:available`)
- Actual post-merge labels on #1893: `status:done` added by `github-actions[bot]` at 2026-04-24T23:21:21Z, ~16s after merge
- Concurrent (correct) action on same issue at 23:21:31Z: `auto-dispatch` label added (matching new TODO.md tag)

The TODO.md line for t291 was `[ ]` both before and after the merge — there is no signal in the working tree that justifies `status:done`.

## Reproduction

1. Have two open TODO.md entries: A (`[x]`-on-merge) and B (`[ ]`, still pending).
2. Open a PR that closes A via `Resolves #<A-issue>` and merely references B via `Ref #<B-issue>` or `For #<B-issue>`.
3. Merge the PR. Wait for `issue-sync` to run.
4. Observe: B's issue gets `status:done` applied even though B's TODO.md line is still `[ ]`.

## Why this is P2

Wrong `status:done` poisons several pulse paths:

- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` may treat the issue as complete and skip dispatch.
- Cross-repo health dashboards count `status:done` issues as resolved — understates outstanding work.
- Manual triage trusts `status:done` and may close the issue prematurely.

In the concrete case, t291 (#1893) is a real pending production-touching task held behind `needs-maintainer-review`. The incorrect `status:done` would have caused the pulse to skip it entirely once the maintainer cleared NMR.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` — TODO ↔ GitHub label sync logic
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` (or its reusable workflow per t2770) — what triggers and what arguments are passed on `pull_request: closed` events
- Look for any path that iterates `closingIssuesReferences` AND any other body refs (`#NNN` mentions) without distinguishing closing keywords (`Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`) from non-closing keywords (`Ref`/`For`).

The likely culprit: a code path that resolves "all issues referenced in the PR body" and applies `status:done` to all of them, rather than only the issues whose TODO.md line was flipped to `[x]` in the merged commit.

## Expected behaviour

`status:done` should be applied only when:

1. The TODO.md line for that task ID flips from `[ ]` to `[x]` in the merged commit, OR
2. The PR body uses a closing keyword (`Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`) for the issue.

Mere `Ref #N` / `For #N` references must NOT trigger label changes on N.

## Workaround

Manual fix after merge: `gh issue edit <N> --remove-label status:done --add-label status:available`.

## Reference pattern

`scripts/pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue` already implements the correct closing-keyword-only extraction (per the build.txt rule on `Resolves` vs `Ref`/`For`). Whatever path in `issue-sync-helper.sh` is making this mistake should adopt the same regex semantics: `grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh`
- Reproduce on a test repo: open PR with `Resolves #A` + `Ref #B`, merge, confirm B's labels unchanged
- Existing test pattern at `.github/workflows/parent-task-keyword-check.yml` covers the closing-keyword-vs-reference distinction for parent tasks; mirror that test surface for issue-sync.
<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---

title: t2816: /setup-git slash command — guided per-repo platform secret setup with toast surfacing (Phase 1)
body:
# t2816 — `/setup-git` slash command: guided per-repo platform secret setup

## Session Origin

Surfaced from interactive triage of `<webapp>/<webapp>#2684` (2026-04-25). The PR #2750 was stuck for ~5h because:

1. Worker created a correct fix → PR opened
2. PR sat with E2E base-drift failures while the planner-fix on `develop` lagged behind
3. t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge gate refused to merge because the linked issue was authored by `github-actions[bot]` (`author_association: NONE`)
4. Bot authorship was caused by **`SYNC_PAT` not being set on `<webapp>/<webapp>`** — the issue-sync workflow falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` and creates issues as the bot
5. `aidevops security check <webapp>/<webapp>` reports "no branch protection — SYNC_PAT not needed" (FALSE — repo uses **rulesets**, missed by the legacy `/protection` API)

The detector gap is fixed by t2806 (#20745). The discoverability gap remains — even with the advisory firing, the operator gets a one-line `[ADVISORY]` toast and is expected to know to set `SYNC_PAT`. There's no guided path from "I see the advisory" to "the secret is set and verified".

User feedback (verbatim):

> we use the opencode toast to advise how many repos need SYNC_PAT setup, and create/give a command /setup-git or something like that, that will give the instructions for the git platform setup, asking for a list of repo slugs from ~/Git to add to repos.json, what git platform(s) to setup and push those to, and giving links to each repo platform url to add the SYNC_PAT token, remind them to save a copy of the tokens to their password manager, and any other ideas to make sure this setup gets done.

## What

Ship Phase 1 of a guided per-repo platform secret setup flow:

1. **`/setup-git` slash command** (`scripts/commands/setup-git.md`) that walks the operator through fixing per-repo platform secret debt. The command reads existing advisories from `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory`, surfaces the count and slugs, generates platform-specific PAT-creation URLs with required scopes pre-encoded, and walks the operator through `gh secret set` in a separate terminal (NEVER accepts secret values in conversation).

2. **Toast aggregation** — `aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive` emits ONE `[WARN]` summary line aggregating SYNC_PAT-missing repo count when ≥1 advisory exists. The OpenCode plugin's `classifyLines` (`greeting.mjs:172-185`) already buckets `[WARN]` as warning-tier (15s display) — the existing per-repo `[ADVISORY]` lines fall back to info-tier as before. Result: the toast escalates to warning whenever there's setup debt, with a clear `/setup-git` call to action.

3. **`setup-debt-helper.sh`** — small aggregator that reads `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` files, returns the count, slugs, and JSON for both human consumption (slash command) and machine consumption (toast emit, future tests). Subcommands: `summary`, `list-sync-pat-missing`, `verify-secret`, `help`.

4. **Platform matrix reference** (`reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`) — canonical doc with PAT-creation URL templates, scope vocabularies, and `gh`/`glab`/`tea` secret-set commands per platform. GitHub primary; GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket as stubs that point at platform docs (Phase 2 fills these in).

5. **Cross-references** — update `aidevops/onboarding.md` to clarify scope split (`/onboarding` = per-account auth setup; `/setup-git` = per-repo platform secrets), and update `.agents/AGENTS.md` to register `/setup-git` under "Repo registration" and Quick Reference.

6. **Advisory body update** — existing SYNC_PAT advisory body in `security-posture-helper.sh::_emit_sync_pat_advisory` gains one line: "For a guided fix, run `/setup-git` in OpenCode or Claude Code."

## Why

**Discoverability gap.** Today the only path from "I see a SYNC_PAT advisory" to "the PAT is set" is reading the advisory body, then the AGENTS.md "Known limitation — issue-sync TODO auto-completion" section, then the GitHub fine-grained PAT docs, then constructing the right URL with the right scopes by hand. Each step is documented but discoverable only if the operator knows to look. The recurring failure mode (missing SYNC_PAT, bot-authored issues, t2449 blocks auto-merge, PRs sit BLOCKED) is preventable but invisible until something stalls.

**Operational cost.** PR #2750 stalled ~5h before manual takeover. Multiplied across N repos × T months, the unset-PAT class of incident is the dominant cost-of-not-having-a-guided-flow.

**Scaling argument.** Today: 3 repos confirmed at SYNC_PAT issue (`<webapp>/<webapp>`, `essentials-com/essentials.com` missing; `marcusquinn/aidevops` set). At the rate of new-repo creation, this debt grows monotonically without an onboarding path that makes setup the default.

**Existing surface fits.** The integration points already exist:

- Plugin toast (`greeting.mjs`) already classifies `[WARN]` lines.
- Advisory infra already writes `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` files (t2374).
- `opencode-github-setup-helper.sh` already detects platform (GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket) and sets up workflows.
- `aidevops/onboarding.md` already covers per-account auth — `/setup-git` is its per-repo complement.

This task composes existing pieces; it doesn't introduce a new architecture.

## How

### Files to modify (Phase 1)

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/setup-debt-helper.sh` (~150 LOC) — aggregator. Subcommands:
  - `summary [--format=human|toast|json]` — count + slug list
  - `list-sync-pat-missing` — one slug per line (one-line stdout, easy to consume)
  - `verify-secret <slug> <name>` — exit 0 if `gh secret list --repo SLUG | grep NAME` finds it
  - `help`
  - Reads `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` (existing format from `_emit_sync_pat_advisory`); applies dismissed-list filter; resolves slug from filename.

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md` (~150 LOC) — slash command spec. Sections:
  - Quick reference (one-line description + invocation)
  - When to use (after a SYNC_PAT advisory toast, after creating a new repo, when onboarding a new operator)
  - Cross-reference to `/onboarding` (different scope)
  - Step-by-step flow for the agent: load setup-debt summary, walk the operator through each gap, generate platform PAT URL, instruct on `gh secret set`, request `verify <slug>` confirmation, write manifest entry (Phase 2).
  - Per-platform URL templates (cross-ref to `reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`)
  - Security posture: never accept secret values in the conversation; never run `gh secret set NAME --body "$VALUE"`; always direct to a separate terminal.

- **NEW**: `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md` (~100 LOC) — platform matrix:
  - GitHub fine-grained PAT URL with query-string scope encoding
  - GitLab personal-access-tokens URL + scope list
  - Gitea / Bitbucket stubs with platform doc links (Phase 2)
  - SecLevel guidance: per-repo over org-wide, expiry rotation, password manager reminder

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh` (~60 LOC) — tests for `summary`, `list-sync-pat-missing`, `verify-secret`. Mocks `~/.aidevops/advisories/` directory; covers zero-advisory, single-advisory, multi-advisory, dismissed-advisory cases.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:325-360` (`_check_advisories`) — before the per-advisory loop, prepend ONE aggregated `[WARN]` line if `setup-debt-helper.sh summary --format=toast` returns non-empty. The aggregated line is the warning-tier signal; the per-advisory `[ADVISORY]` lines remain as info-tier follow-up detail.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh:631-656` (`_emit_sync_pat_advisory`) — add one line at the top of the advisory body: "For a guided fix, run `/setup-git` in OpenCode or Claude Code."

### Reference patterns


## Acceptance

title: framework-routing-helper bypasses fingerprint dedup; body fingerprint not normalized (root cause of #20808 duplicate)
body:
## Task

Close the cross-path duplicate-issue-creation gap exposed when `framework-routing-helper.sh log-framework-issue` fires concurrently with `/log-issue-aidevops` (or any other path that uses `log-issue-helper.sh`'s fingerprint dedup).

Two cooperating fixes:

1. **Wire `framework-routing-helper.sh::log_framework_issue` into the canonical fingerprint dedup** — call `log-issue-helper.sh::check_recent_filing` before creating, and `record_filing` after.
2. **Normalize body before fingerprinting** in `log-issue-helper.sh::_compute_issue_fingerprint` so that cosmetic suffixes (source-context blocks, sig footer) don't defeat dedup across paths.

## Why

Live failure: GH#20807 and GH#20808 were filed in the **same OpenCode session 36s apart** about the same root cause (`enrich_metadata_block` adds `Resolves #N` to PR-merge close-comments). #20808 was closed as a duplicate.

Two parallel issue-creation paths fired:

- 23:24:19 — `/log-issue-aidevops` → #20807 (no source trailer)
- 23:24:55 — `framework-routing-helper.sh log-framework-issue` from `robstiles/qs-agency` → #20808 (auto-appended `*Detected by framework-routing-helper in robstiles/qs-agency.*` trailer)

The GH#20322 fingerprint dedup didn't catch #20808 because:

- The two paths don't share fingerprint state at all — `framework-routing-helper.sh:319-332` rolls its own ad-hoc dedup via `gh issue list --search` (subject to GitHub indexing lag, the exact GH#20322 problem).
- Even if `framework-routing-helper.sh` called `check_recent_filing`, the body hash would differ because the source trailer is appended *after* the dedup search (`framework-routing-helper.sh:339-345`) — so on the receiving side, the cached fingerprint for #20807's body wouldn't match #20808's body-with-trailer.

This is the same class of bug as GH#20322 (search-indexing lag) plus a fingerprint-normalization gap that GH#20322's fix didn't address.

## How

### Fix 1 — `framework-routing-helper.sh::log_framework_issue`

**EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/framework-routing-helper.sh:319-332` (replace ad-hoc `gh issue list --search` block) and `:354-360` (after `gh_create_issue` succeeds).

**Pattern to copy:** the existing `log-issue-helper.sh::file_issue` flow that calls `check_recent_filing` → create → `record_filing`. Source `log-issue-helper.sh` and call its functions directly (it already provides `check_recent_filing` and `record_filing` as library functions — see `log-issue-helper.sh:231` and `:270`).

Sketch:

```bash
# Build full body INCLUDING source trailer first, then fingerprint-check
# (matches what will actually be created — trailer is part of the issue identity)
if [[ -n "$source_repo" ]]; then
    body="${body}

---
*Detected by framework-routing-helper in \`${source_repo}\`.*"
fi

# Source canonical dedup
# shellcheck source=./log-issue-helper.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/log-issue-helper.sh"

local dedup_result
dedup_result=$(check_recent_filing "$title" "$body" || true)
if [[ "$dedup_result" == DUPLICATE:* ]]; then
    local dup_num="${dedup_result#DUPLICATE:}"
    dup_num="${dup_num%%:*}"
    log_info "Fingerprint duplicate within window: #${dup_num}"
    echo "https://github.com/${slug}/issues/${dup_num}"
    return 2
fi

# ... existing gh_create_issue call ...

# After successful creation:
record_filing "$title" "$body" "$issue_number"
```

The existing `gh issue list --search` block at `:319-332` can stay as a *secondary* check (it catches duplicates outside the dedup window). But the fingerprint check must come first.

### Fix 2 — `log-issue-helper.sh::_compute_issue_fingerprint` body normalization

**EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh:207-226`

Strip cosmetic suffixes before hashing so the same issue identity hashes the same regardless of which path filed it:

- The signature footer block (everything from `<!-- aidevops:sig -->` to end of body, or last `---` separator + `aidevops.sh` line)
- Source-context trailers (lines matching `*Detected by framework-routing-helper in \`...\`.*` and similar `*Detected by .*`)

Sketch:

```bash
_normalize_body_for_fingerprint() {
    local body="$1"
    # Strip aidevops sig footer (HTML marker delimited)
    body=$(printf '%s' "$body" | awk '
        /<!-- aidevops:sig -->/ { skip=1 }
        !skip { print }
    ')
    # Strip "*Detected by .* in \`...\`.*" trailers (framework-routing source context)
    body=$(printf '%s' "$body" | sed -E '/^\*Detected by [^*]+\*$/d')
    # Trim trailing blank lines and `---` separator that preceded the trailer
    body=$(printf '%s' "$body" | sed -e :a -e '/^\s*$/{$d;N;ba' -e '}' -e 's/\n*---\n*$//')
    printf '%s' "$body"
}

_compute_issue_fingerprint() {
    local title="$1"
    local body="$2"
    local normalized_body
    normalized_body=$(_normalize_body_for_fingerprint "$body")
    local input="${title}|${normalized_body}"
    # ... rest unchanged ...
}
```

This must apply on **both** `check_recent_filing` and `record_filing` (they both call `_compute_issue_fingerprint`, so the change is centralized).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/framework-routing-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tests/log-issue-helper.bats` (or new tests file if absent)

## Acceptance

1. `log_framework_issue` calls `check_recent_filing` before `gh_create_issue` and `record_filing` after success — verifiable via `grep -n 'check_recent_filing\|record_filing' .agents/scripts/framework-routing-helper.sh` returning 2+ matches.
2. `_compute_issue_fingerprint` normalizes the body via a helper that strips the aidevops sig footer marker block and `*Detected by ... in ...*` source trailers before hashing.
3. Test: simulate two filings of the same `(title, body)` 30s apart, one through `/log-issue-aidevops` and one through `framework-routing-helper.sh log-framework-issue` (with `--source-repo X`). The second call returns the URL of the first issue (exit 2) and does not call `gh issue create`.
4. Test: same `(title, body)` filed via two paths within window, where one body has the source trailer appended and the other does not. Both fingerprints match (normalized body) — second call dedups.
5. Existing `log-issue-helper.sh` and `framework-routing-helper.sh` callers continue to work unchanged (no new required arguments).
6. `bats .agents/tests/log-issue-helper.bats` passes.

## Session Origin

Interactive OpenCode session reviewing GH#20807 and GH#20808 (the duplicate). Diagnosis emerged from comparing the two issue creation timestamps (23:24:19 vs 23:24:55), the source trailer presence/absence, and reading both helper scripts at `.agents/scripts/framework-routing-helper.sh:299-365` and `.agents/scripts/log-issue-helper.sh:191-296`.

Verified at code level (per t2204):

- `framework-routing-helper.sh:319-332` does its own `gh issue list --search` dedup, does NOT call `check_recent_filing`/`record_filing`.
- `log-issue-helper.sh:210` hashes `"${title}|${body}"` directly with no body normalization.
- Both confirmed by reading the files; no inference required.

Related: GH#20322 (original search-indexing-lag fix), GH#20807 (the bug that prompted the duplicate filing), GH#20808 (the duplicate).

title: t2817: post-merge-review-scanner: extend NOOP_RE to catch Gemini mid-sentence LGTM phrasing + zero-findings gate
body:
## What

Extend `NOOP_RE` in `post-merge-review-scanner.sh` to catch Gemini's mid-sentence LGTM phrasing, and add a belt-and-braces zero-findings gate that skips issue creation when both review summaries and inline comments are empty.

## Why

PR #18947 (t2086, MERGED 2026-04-14) added `NOOP_RE` as a deny-list to suppress Gemini LGTM reviews that substring-matched `ACT_RE` (e.g. `"refactors"` matching the `refactor` keyword). The original pattern was anchored to end-of-string (`[[:space:][:punct:]]*$`). The comment at `post-merge-review-scanner.sh:104-113` explicitly documents the tradeoff: "phrases are specific enough that false positives (a real review that also contains 'no feedback to provide' in a sub-clause) are rare in practice."

On 2026-04-24, PR #20759 exposed the hole. Gemini's review said:

> "This pull request updates the documentation in `.agents/AGENTS.md` to include a description of a new server-side safety net workflow… **I have no feedback to provide as there were no review comments.**"

Three failures stacked:

1. The noop phrase `"I have no feedback to provide"` is followed by `" as there were no review comments."` — the end-anchor fails.
2. `"no review comments"` isn't in `NOOP_RE` at all.
3. `"updates"` matches `ACT_RE` (`should|consider|fix|change|update|refactor|missing|add`), so the review passes the actionability filter and a followup issue is created.

Result: issue #20792 was filed with no actionable finding. A worker was dispatched (launch-recovery crashed the first attempt, the second ran an Outcome A "premise falsified" close). Net cost: ~30K tokens burned for zero finding.

Gemini's phrasing is deterministic — every empty review produces this exact sentence. So the saving is per empty-review PR, not one-off.

A sibling library already has the right pattern: `quality-feedback-findings-lib.sh:347-352` in `_check_empty_review_guard` uses an unanchored regex that includes `"no review comments"`. We can converge on it.

## How

**Layer 1 — extend `NOOP_RE` in `post-merge-review-scanner.sh:113`:**

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh:113` — modify the `NOOP_RE` constant
- Add `no review comments` to the alternation list
- Drop the `[[:space:][:punct:]]*$` end-anchor. The alternatives (match-last-sentence, multiline mode) are more fragile. The phrases in the list are distinctive enough that mid-sentence false positives are rare in practice, and losing a genuine finding because the reviewer wrote "I have no feedback to provide on X, but…" is much less common than missing an actual LGTM.
- Update the rationale comment at lines 104-112 to reflect the new tradeoff: we now prefer false negatives (occasional missed issue creation for a real finding whose phrasing happens to include a noop substring) over false positives (issue created for LGTM). Cite issue #20792 as the triggering incident.

**Reference pattern:** `.agents/scripts/quality-feedback-findings-lib.sh:347-352` — proven unanchored regex in `_check_empty_review_guard`:

```jq
"no feedback|no review comments|no issues found|lgtm|looks good to me|" +
"nothing to flag|no further|no comments|nothing actionable|" +
"i have no (feedback|issues|comments|concerns)|" +
"no (issues|problems|concerns|suggestions|recommendations) (found|detected|identified)|" +
"(found|identified|detected) no (issues|problems|concerns|suggestions)"
```

Don't copy this wholesale (the bash regex dialect is POSIX ERE via `test()`, not PCRE). Adapt the relevant clauses into the existing `NOOP_RE` alternation.

**Layer 2 — zero-findings gate at the create-issue call site:**

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh` — in the flow around line 535 where `fetch_review_summaries_md` is called, after both summaries and inline comments are computed, add an explicit check: if BOTH are empty strings, log a skip reason and do NOT create the issue. Model on the existing skip-logging pattern in the same function.
- This catches future bot phrasings we haven't seen yet. Defence in depth.

**Test additions:**

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh` — add fixtures:
  1. Gemini's exact phrasing from PR #20759: `"This pull request updates the documentation... I have no feedback to provide as there were no review comments."` — assert `fetch_review_summaries_md` returns empty.
  2. Bare `"no review comments"` phrase — assert it's filtered.
  3. Positive control: real finding with the word `"feedback"` in prose (e.g. `"Some feedback: the function name should be..."`) — assert it's preserved.
- Existing "Gemini ## Code Review is preserved" test at line 359 must still pass.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/post-merge-review-scanner.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh`

## Acceptance

1. `NOOP_RE` extended: includes `no review comments`, end-anchor removed, rationale comment updated to cite #20792.
2. Zero-findings gate added at the create-issue call site in `post-merge-review-scanner.sh`.
3. New test fixture with Gemini's exact phrasing from PR #20759 passes (review is filtered, no issue would be created).
4. New test fixture with bare `no review comments` phrase passes.
5. Positive-control test for review bodies that coincidentally contain noop substrings in the middle of actionable prose passes (not over-filtered).
6. All existing tests in `test-post-merge-review-scanner.sh` pass.
7. `shellcheck` clean on modified files.
8. `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` passes.

## Session Origin

Interactive session with maintainer 2026-04-25. The maintainer noticed review-followup issue #20792 closed without a PR, asked whether some were closed by cross-referencing. Investigation found #20792 was correctly closed (Outcome A, premise falsified) but should never have been created — Gemini's review was an empty LGTM that slipped through the existing `NOOP_RE` filter because the phrase isn't at end-of-string and `"no review comments"` isn't in the deny-list. Maintainer asked whether we should improve the filter. This issue captures the fix.

## References

- Original filter: t2086 / PR #18947 (MERGED 2026-04-14)
- Triggering incident: issue #20792 (closed 2026-04-24, Outcome A)
- Triggering PR: #20759 (t2798 — status:available default workflow)
- Gemini review: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/20759#pullrequestreview-4172507084
- Sibling pattern: `_check_empty_review_guard` at `.agents/scripts/quality-feedback-findings-lib.sh:329`

title: t2818: fix(lifecycle): detect worker_branch_orphan — pushed branch without PR is currently misclassified as worker_complete
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced 2026-04-25 while unsticking <webapp>/<webapp>#2647 (t397). The headless worker on 2026-04-23 committed and pushed `feature/t397-delete-org-from-switcher` (matching the brief precisely), then posted `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete` 56 seconds after the push — but **never opened a PR**. The branch sat orphaned for ~24h. The pulse couldn't recover it because:

- `_worker_produced_output` returned TRUE (Signal 2: branch pushed) → classified as `worker_complete`, not `worker_noop` → no fast-fail, no re-dispatch.
- `ever-NMR` flag was set during the earlier infra crashes → pulse refused to re-dispatch even when stale-recovery fired.
- No code path in the framework looks for "branch exists but no PR" as a stuck state.

A maintainer had to manually rebase + open the PR (#2806). The work was already done — it just had no PR to land it.

## What

Add a fourth lifecycle classification — `worker_branch_orphan` — for the case where a worker pushed commits on a feature branch but did not open a PR. Implement two complementary fixes:

1. **Detect the orphan state at session-end** (in `_cmd_run_finish`): when commits/branch are present (Signal 1 or 2) but no PR exists (Signal 3 absent), classify as `worker_branch_orphan` instead of `worker_complete`.

2. **Auto-recover the orphan**: try `gh pr create --head <branch> --base <default> --body "$(orphan_recovery_body)"` once. If success → release as `worker_complete` with a note that the PR was auto-recovered. If failure → release as `worker_branch_orphan`, post a structured comment on the issue surfacing the branch path so the next dispatch can pick it up.

3. **Counter + audit**: increment `worker_branch_orphan_count` in `pulse-stats.json`. Post the existing `<!-- ops:start ... ops:end -->` style audit comment so the lifecycle is visible.

## Why

- The current OR-merged signal short-circuits on the first positive — pushed branch is treated as equivalent to a PR. They are not equivalent: a pushed branch is invisible to the merge pipeline (no review, no auto-merge, no retarget).
- The failure mode is silent: audit trail says "worker_complete" but the issue stays open and the next pulse won't re-dispatch (claim was released cleanly).
- Real cost observed on <webapp>#2647: ~17h stuck + 64K tokens spent + 14 pulse comments + manual maintainer intervention to land work the worker had already finished.
- Auto-recovering at session-end is cheaper and safer than detecting the orphan at pulse cycle time (no race against ever-NMR, no need for new pulse-side scanner).

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1106-1162` — refactor `_worker_produced_output` to return a classification (`pr_exists`, `branch_orphan`, `noop`) instead of a boolean. Keep the existing fail-open semantics.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh:1219-1245` — update `_cmd_run_finish` to switch on the new classification: emit `worker_complete`, `worker_branch_orphan` (with auto-PR attempt), or `worker_noop`.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` (or extend if exists) — add `_attempt_orphan_recovery_pr "$session_key" "$work_dir" "$branch_name" "$repo_slug"` returning 0 on PR-created, 1 on failure.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh:157-298` — add cases for: `(commits + branch + PR) → pr_exists`, `(commits + branch + no PR) → branch_orphan`, `(no signals) → noop`. Cover auto-recovery success and failure paths.

### Reference patterns

- **Existing 3-signal check**: `_worker_produced_output` at `headless-runtime-helper.sh:1106` — keep all three signals, just split the return shape.
- **Counter increment pattern**: `pulse-stats.json` writes elsewhere in pulse-wrapper.sh (see `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` for the canonical jq update).
- **Auto-PR creation**: `gh_create_pr` wrapper from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh` already auto-applies origin label + signature footer. Pass `--label origin:worker-takeover` for orphan-recovery PRs to distinguish from normal worker output.
- **Audit comment shape**: copy the `<!-- ops:start ... ops:end -->` block from `pulse-wrapper.sh` worker-dispatch path.
- **Pre-edit-check**: this work is in `.agents/scripts/`. Use a worktree per the t1990 interactive-session rule (canonical aidevops dir stays on main).

### Tier checklist

- 4 files, ~150 lines diff. Touches lifecycle code (high blast radius).
- Requires designing the orphan-recovery PR body, deciding draft vs ready (recommend non-draft so existing review/merge gates apply), choosing whether to inherit the failed worker's commit history as-is or rebase. → tier:standard with possible thinking-tier escalation if the worker hits ambiguity around the rebase question.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` (if it exists; otherwise extend the headless test)
- `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` (only if a new env var like `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_ORPHAN_RECOVERY` is added)

## Acceptance

1. `_worker_produced_output` (or its successor) returns one of 3 classifications, not a boolean.
2. New test case proves: when commits exist, branch is pushed, but no PR exists for the issue → classification is `branch_orphan`.
3. New test case proves: orphan-recovery attempts `gh pr create` with the right `--head`, `--base`, and `--label origin:worker-takeover`. Mock the gh call.
4. New test case proves: on auto-PR success, lifecycle emits `worker_complete` with an audit-trail note. On auto-PR failure, emits `worker_branch_orphan` and a structured issue comment.
5. `worker_branch_orphan_count` counter increments in `pulse-stats.json` on each orphan recovery attempt (success or failure).
6. Existing `worker_noop` and `worker_complete` paths are unchanged behaviourally — only the classification call site is restructured.
7. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` passes. ShellCheck clean. No new function-complexity / nesting-depth regressions (the regression gates apply).
8. Manual verification: simulate the <webapp>#2647 case in a sandbox (push a branch with no PR for an open issue, run `_cmd_run_finish` with `ledger_status=success`) → expect a draft/non-draft PR auto-created against the issue's default branch, OR a structured "branch orphan, please review" comment on the issue.

## Context

- **The trigger**: <webapp>/<webapp>#2647 → resolved by manually-rebased PR #2806. Memory entry stored 2026-04-25T00:50:19Z (`mem_20260425005019_0b52428d`).
- **Related design docs**: `prompts/build.txt` §"Pre-implementation discovery (t2046)" — this is the cherry-pick-first principle applied at the framework layer instead of the worker layer.
- **Related lifecycle comments**: `headless-runtime-helper.sh:1219-1235` already calls out that worker_noop was added because "exit 0 with no commits, no pushed branch, no PR" was misclassified. This task extends the same logic: "exit 0 with commits/branch but no PR" should also be classified separately.
- **Why not a pulse-side scanner instead**: a pulse-side detector would race against `ever-NMR` blocks (the very thing that made #2647 unrecoverable for 24h). Detecting and recovering at session-end happens before the NMR gate engages.
- **Edge case to think through during implementation**: what if the worker exited because the linked issue was closed (premise falsified per the t1900 worker triage rule)? In that case, the branch is genuinely orphaned and shouldn't auto-PR. Check `gh issue view <N> --json state` before the auto-PR attempt; skip recovery if state == "CLOSED".

title: t2819: pulse: pre-dispatch tier override for self-hosting dispatch-path tasks
body:
## What

Add a pre-dispatch tier-override step that detects self-hosting tasks (those modifying the worker dispatch/spawn path) and applies `model:opus-4-7` at issue creation time, bypassing the `tier:thinking` (opus-4-6) → opus-4-7 cascade.

## Why

Issues that modify the dispatch path (`pulse-wrapper.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-*.sh`, `headless-runtime-*.sh`, `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`, `shared-dispatch-dedup.sh`) have an unusual self-referential property: the very workers dispatched to fix them run through the code being fixed. When the dispatch path is broken, those workers fail to spawn (`no_worker_process`) or stall (`worker_failed`), triggering cascade escalation.

Observed on #20765 (t2814 — Phase 3 of the no_worker_process investigation):

| Attempt | Model | Runtime | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | opus-4-6 | ~60s | `worker_failed` |
| 2 | opus-4-6 | ~75s | `no_worker_process` (the exact bug being fixed) |
| 3 | opus-4-7 (after cascade) | ~18min | `worker_failed` |
| 4 | opus-4-7 (after stale-recovery) | in progress at file time | completed successfully |

Two opus-4-6 attempts (~40K wasted tokens combined) before the cascade reached the tier that was always required for this task size (1780+ lines, 4 independent semantic changes, 3 interacting scripts).

These tasks already carry `tier:thinking` — the gap is the **cascade-starts-at-opus-4-6** default within that tier. Applying `model:opus-4-7` upfront (the label the cascade would eventually reach anyway) eliminates 1-2 wasted attempts for this specific class of self-referential issue.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` — add a new validator that runs BEFORE the existing ones, inspects the target issue body's `## Files to modify` / `## How` sections for dispatch-path patterns, and applies `model:opus-4-7` as a side effect (not a blocker). Exit 0 always; label mutation is an advisory pre-step, not a dispatch block.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-self-hosting-detector.sh` — regression test covering positive detection (`pulse-wrapper.sh`), negative detection (docs-only change), mixed-scope (dispatch file + unrelated file → still triggers), idempotency (re-run on already-labeled issue is a no-op).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document the self-hosting short-circuit in the cascade section.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md` — add the new validator to the inventory.

### Self-hosting file patterns (canonical list)

Trigger when the issue body's `Files to modify` / `How` section references any of:

- `pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `pulse-dispatch-*.sh` (core, engine, worker-launch, decision, cleanup)
- `pulse-cleanup.sh`
- `headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`
- `shared-dispatch-dedup.sh`
- `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
- `worker-activity-watchdog.sh`

Maintain the list as a shell array constant in the validator so future additions are one-line edits.

### Reference pattern

Model on existing validators in `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh` — same command signature (`validate <issue-number> <slug>`), same exit-0-on-pass semantics, side-effect label application via `gh_issue_edit_safe` (from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`).

The existing validator architecture (GH#19118, documented in `reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`) is the right extension point. This is a NEW validator, not a modification to an existing one. Skip it with `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1`.

Audit comment on label application: wrap in `<!-- provenance:start -->` markers explaining the auto-upgrade rationale and linking back to this task. Follow the pattern in `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` (t2389).

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-self-hosting-detector.sh
# Positive-path smoke test (dry run against a known dispatch-path issue):
AIDEVOPS_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR_DRY_RUN=1 \
  .agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh validate 20765 marcusquinn/aidevops
```
