title: t2820: pulse: extend no_work reclassification to worker_failed using Phase 3 log-tail data
body:
## What

Extend the `no_work` classification — which currently triggers only on `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` — to also cover `worker_failed` events where the worker log shows no actual implementation progress (no tool calls, no file edits, no commits). Use the log tail that Phase 3 (t2814, #20765) surfaces to make the decision.

## Why

The current fast-fail classification has two buckets:

1. `no_worker_process` — worker never spawned. t2387 skips tier escalation. Phase 4 (#20766, t2815) will harden the cascade-skip enforcement.
2. `worker_failed` — everything else. Triggers cascade escalation.

But `worker_failed` is a false-merge: it conflates two distinct failure modes that demand opposite responses:

- **Real coding failure**: worker spawned, loaded context (~20K tokens), executed tool calls, produced bad code. Escalation to opus-4-7 is the correct response.
- **Late infra failure**: worker spawned, ran canary, canary passed, then hit a mid-session blip (auth refresh timeout, provider rate limit, plugin hook deadlock) BEFORE any code was produced. Escalation wastes opus tokens on a model that cannot help.

Evidence from #20765:

- Attempt 1 (opus-4-6): `worker_failed` at ~60s — too fast to have written real code; likely an early exit masquerading as coding failure
- Attempt 3 (opus-4-7): `worker_failed` at ~18min — ran but stalled; log tail would reveal whether it produced any file edits

Phase 3 (t2814) lands the log-tail collection in the `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment (`_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` in `pulse-cleanup.sh`). That same log-tail data can drive an automatic reclassification: if the tail shows no tool-call frames after N seconds of runtime, reclassify as `no_work` and trigger the existing t2387 skip-escalation path.

## How

### Prerequisites (blocked-by)

- **Phase 3 (#20765 / t2814)** must merge — delivers the worker-log tail visibility that Fix 1 (`_post_launch_recovery_claim_released`) provides.
- **Phase 4 (#20766 / t2815)** must merge — delivers the distinct `launch_recovery:*` failure signatures and the cascade-skip enforcement that this fix extends.

Do NOT dispatch a worker on this issue until both prerequisites merge. The `no-auto-dispatch` label enforces this.

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — extend `escalate_issue_tier()` (current line ~951) with a reclassification helper that inspects the worker log tail before deciding escalation vs skip.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — extend `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` (current line ~816) to emit the distinct reason it was reclassified (e.g. `no_tool_calls_in_log`, `canary_failure_post_spawn`).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` — extract the log-tail reader from Phase 3's `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` into a shared helper (`_read_worker_log_tail_classified` or similar) so reclassification and claim-released comment share the same parsing logic (DRY).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh` — regression test with fixture log tails for each shape (real-coding-failure, early-exit, mid-session-hang, canary-post-spawn).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document the reclassification signatures.

### Reclassification rules

When fast-fail reason is `worker_failed` AND runtime is under `NO_WORK_RECLASS_ELAPSED_MAX` (default 180s, env-overridable) AND log tail contains **no** `"tool_use"` or `"edit"` step-frames → reclassify as `no_work` with subtype `no_tool_calls_in_log`.

When log tail contains only canary-test output or `[t2814:early_exit]` markers (from Phase 3 Fix 2) → reclassify as `no_work` with subtype `canary_post_spawn_failure`.

When either subtype fires, call the existing `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` path (t2387) with the subtype passed through so the emitted comment explains why escalation was skipped (and which reclassification rule fired).

### Reference pattern

- Model on `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` (worker-lifecycle-common.sh:816) — same output shape, same circuit-breaker integration, same `source:auto-reclassify` provenance marker.
- Log parsing: reuse the log-tail reader from Phase 3 Fix 1 by extracting into `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`. Parsing logic to locate: the body of `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` in `pulse-cleanup.sh` after Phase 3 lands (file path: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`, function added by PR that closes #20765).

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh
# After deploy: observe that worker_failed events under 3 minutes with clean log tails no longer escalate to opus-4-7
# Audit query:
gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/<N>/comments --jq \
  '.[] | select(.body | test("no_work.*(no_tool_calls_in_log|canary_post_spawn_failure)")) | .body' | head -20
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Phase 3 (#20765) and Phase 4 (#20766) merged first (prerequisite check — do not implement until both are deployed)
- [ ] `escalate_issue_tier()` inspects log tail when fast-fail reason is `worker_failed` and runtime is under threshold
- [ ] Distinct reclassification subtypes: `no_tool_calls_in_log`, `canary_post_spawn_failure`
- [ ] Shared log-tail reader extracted to `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` (DRY with Phase 3 Fix 1)
- [ ] Regression test covers all 4 log shapes (real coding failure / early exit / mid-session hang / canary-post-spawn)
- [ ] Env var override `NO_WORK_RECLASS_ELAPSED_MAX` works
- [ ] `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` updated with the reclassification matrix

## Session Origin

Interactive session with maintainer. Derived from dispatch-history analysis of #20765 during Phase 3 follow-up. Companion to (A) self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override (t2819) and (C) dispatch-path `#parent` default policy (t2821). All three target the tautology-loop failure mode surfaced by t2804 (#20740).

title: t2821: policy: dispatch-path tasks default to #parent + no-auto-dispatch for interactive implementation
body:
## What

Establish a framework-level rule: tasks whose `## Files to modify` section hits the worker dispatch/spawn path default to `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` unless explicitly overridden. Maintainers implement these interactively rather than through auto-dispatched workers.

## Why

Self-hosting tasks (fixing the worker dispatch path from within worker-dispatched sessions) have a tautology failure mode: broken dispatch kills workers fixing dispatch. Observed on #20765 (t2814):

- 3 worker attempts across ~90 minutes before one succeeded
- 2 attempts failed with `worker_failed`, 1 with `no_worker_process` (the exact bug being fixed)
- Estimated ~40-60K opus tokens burned on failed attempts before the successful opus-4-7 run

Issues A (t2819 — self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override) and B (t2820 — no_work reclassification extension) mitigate the cost **per failed attempt**. This rule addresses the decision to **attempt dispatch at all** for this task class.

1. Human context available for judgment calls about dispatch-path design trade-offs

- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` — document the default and the manual override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — cross-link the new rule in the "Auto-Dispatch and Completion" section.

1. Brief's `Files Scope` or `## How` references any file in the self-hosting set (same canonical list as Issue A — keep it in one place, reference it from both) → recommend `#parent`, `no-auto-dispatch`, and `origin:interactive`.

- The `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` server-side auto-downgrade (t2389) is the closest architectural analogue: detects a mis-classification from the brief shape and adjusts labels with a provenance-wrapped audit comment. Model the brief-helper side-effect on this pattern.

title: issue-sync auto-close ignores parent-task label, repeatedly closes parent issues
body:
## Problem

`issue-sync.yml` (the reusable workflow at `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`) auto-closes a linked GitHub issue when the corresponding TODO.md entry is marked `[x]`, regardless of whether the issue carries the `parent-task` label.

This breaks the parent-task lifecycle: a `#parent` task should stay open until ALL phase children merge, with only the final phase PR closing it. But if the parent's TODO entry is marked `[x]` for ANY reason (e.g. an audit-report PR shipped while the implementation roadmap is still in progress), issue-sync closes the parent issue and applies `status:done`. Manually reopening doesn't help — the next sync run closes it again.

## Reproduction

Observed in `robstiles/qs-agency`:

1. Parent issue #1877 created with `parent-task` label tracking an implementation roadmap (11 phase children).
2. TODO.md had `- [x] t288 ... pr:#1888 completed:2026-04-24` — the `[x]` reflected that the audit-report PR shipped, not that the parent task itself was complete.
3. `issue-sync` ran, saw `[x]` t288 → close GH#1877, apply `status:done`. Twice in 4 hours.

Workaround in qs-agency PR #1946: change `[x]` to `[ ]`, rename `pr:` to `audit-pr:` to disambiguate.

## Proposed fix

Before applying the `[x]` → close mapping, check whether the linked issue has the `parent-task` label. If yes, skip the close + skip the `status:done` label. The parent stays open until its closing PR merges with `Closes #NNN` (which only the final phase PR uses, per the t2046 parent-task PR keyword rule already enforced in `parent-task-keyword-check.yml`).

Consistent with existing parent-task protections (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED`, `_is_protected_label`, `parent-task-keyword-check.yml`). The issue-sync auto-close path is the missing layer.

## Files likely involved

- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` (or whichever helper performs the auto-close)
- Discriminator: `gh issue view <N> --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | contains(["parent-task"])'`

## Verification

- Unit/integration test: input TODO has `[x]` on entry whose linked issue carries `parent-task` → expect issue to remain OPEN and `status:done` not applied.
- Ratchet test: scan for `parent-task`-labelled CLOSED issues with `state_reason == "completed"` that don't have a merged PR with `Closes #NNN` → flag as bug-1 false closures.

## Background

Discovered while landing the planning PR for the t288 implementation roadmap in qs-agency. Full context: robstiles/qs-agency#1877, robstiles/qs-agency#1942 (planning PR), robstiles/qs-agency#1946 (workaround).

title: t2823: auto-emit blocked-by from predecessor references in claim-task-id.sh
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced while triaging #20732 dispatch friction. The recovery cycle that produced PR #20817 was triggered by sibling PR #20776 (issue GH#20774) merging in parallel and breaking PR #20775's diff. Both PRs touched `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`. GH#20774's body explicitly self-described as a "Follow-up from t2799 (GH#20732) ... after one release cycle" but emitted no `blocked-by` marker. Both went dispatchable simultaneously.

## What

Close the sibling-task scheduling gap: when a follow-up issue body explicitly references a predecessor task, automatically emit a `blocked-by:<predecessor>` marker so the dispatch dedup engine serialises them.

Two complementary fixes — choose one or both:

1. **Light (recommended first):** `claim-task-id.sh` regex-detects predecessor references in the brief body and emits a `blocked-by:tNNN` tag in the TODO.md entry it writes.
2. **Heavier:** `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` consults `Files Scope` across open issues and defers dispatch when an active issue claims the same path.

## Why

The dispatch dedup engine has six layers of overlap protection (origin labels, status labels, assignee+status combo, etc.) but no awareness of:

- semantic predecessor/successor relationships expressed in prose
- file-level scope overlap between two open issues

So when two issues touching the same file are both `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` + unassigned, the pulse will dispatch both. If the work order matters (which it does for follow-up cleanups, deprecation removal, two-step refactors), the second-merger wins the file and the first-merger gets a mechanical conflict.

Concrete cost on #20732/GH#20774:

- 1 wasted opus-tier worker session (PR #20775 → closed with conflict)
- 1 conflict-feedback recovery cycle (cherry-pick into PR #20817)
- ~25K extra opus tokens
- ~3.5h additional wall time

This pattern will recur whenever a brief explicitly says "after X ships" / "follow-up to Y" but the author forgot the `blocked-by` tag.

## How

### Light fix (Option 1) — files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — add a `_detect_predecessor_refs` function that scans `--description` (or the linked brief body if `--description` is empty) for these patterns and extracts the predecessor task IDs:
  - `Follow-up from (t[0-9]+|GH#[0-9]+)`
  - `tracked in (GH#[0-9]+|#[0-9]+)`
  - `blocked-by:?\s*(t[0-9]+|GH#[0-9]+)` (already-explicit form — pass through)
  - `after (t[0-9]+) (?:ships|merges|lands)`
- When detected, emit `blocked-by:<refs>` as a TODO.md tag (same form as `ref:GH#NNN`).
- Emit a stderr advisory comment on the issue itself: "Detected predecessor reference; auto-emitting blocked-by:tNNN. Override with `--no-blocked-by`."

### Heavier fix (Option 2) — files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` — extend `is-assigned` (or add a new `has-active-scope-overlap` predicate) to:
  - Parse `Files Scope` (or `### Files Scope`) section from open issues.
  - Build the set of paths claimed by active dispatched issues (those with `status:in-progress` / `status:in-review` / non-self-assigned).
  - Return `OVERLAP_BLOCKED` when the candidate issue's Files Scope intersects.
- This is more powerful but needs careful design — Files Scope globs must be deterministic.

### Reference patterns

- Regex idiom: `_derive_pr_title_prefix` at full-loop-helper.sh:932 uses the same `t[0-9]+` boundary pattern.
- TODO.md tag emission: see how `claim-task-id.sh` writes `ref:GH#NNN` today (search `ref:GH#`).
- Files Scope parsing: brief-readiness-helper.sh already tokenises brief sections — extend that helper.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
# Light path:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-blocked-by-detection.sh  # NEW
# Smoke test: file an issue whose --description references "Follow-up from t2799" and verify the TODO entry has blocked-by:t2799
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-blocked-by-detection.sh` (new)
- (option 2 only) `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

1. **Light path**: when `--description` contains a predecessor reference matching one of the documented patterns, `claim-task-id.sh` emits a `blocked-by:tNNN` tag in the TODO entry it writes.
2. Multiple predecessors detected → all emitted as comma-separated `blocked-by:t1,t2`.
3. Already-explicit `blocked-by:tNNN` in description → pass through, no duplicate.
4. `--no-blocked-by` flag suppresses detection (escape hatch for legitimate parallel work).
5. Regression test covers each pattern variant + the no-match case (no tag added) + the override case.
6. ShellCheck clean.
7. Optional Option 2 work tracked as a child issue, not in scope here.

## Context

- Bug instance: GH#20774 was filed at 19:22 UTC explicitly as "Follow-up from t2799 ... after one release cycle"; no blocked-by tag; both dispatched in parallel; PR #20776 merged first; PR #20775 conflicted; recovery via PR #20817.
- The pulse already serialises strictly via `is_blocked_by_unresolved` (see #20732 actually being held by `blocked-by:#20727` correctly — that part of the chain works). The gap is on the TAG-EMISSION side: when the author writes prose that *implies* blocked-by but doesn't write the tag, the pulse can't infer it.
- Tier: standard. ~150 lines of bash + test. Not in the dispatch-path file set (claim-task-id.sh is dispatch-adjacent but not the worker-spawn path).

title: t2824: diagnose pre-push hook 60s timeout that forces --skip-hooks bypass
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced while triaging #20732 dispatch friction. The successful recovery worker (session that produced PR #20817) hit:

```
[ERROR] Push timed out after 60s — likely a pre-push hook stalling.
```

It worked around the timeout with `git push --no-verify` followed by `commit-and-pr --skip-hooks`. The PR landed without privacy/complexity/scope/dup-todo guard verification on the final diff. Worker log: `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-20732.log` (push-timeout block at lines 108-116, --no-verify push at line 112).

## What

Two-phase task:

1. **Phase 1 — diagnose**: instrument the four pre-push guards (`privacy-guard-pre-push.sh`, `complexity-guard-pre-push.sh`, `scope-guard-pre-push.sh`, `dup-todo-guard-pre-push.sh`) with `time` measurements and run them against the diff that triggered the original timeout. Identify which guard exceeds 60s.

2. **Phase 2 — fix**: based on Phase 1 findings, file a child issue with the targeted fix (likely one of: optimise the slow guard, raise the timeout, add a fast-path for known-safe diffs, or split the slow guard's work).

This issue covers Phase 1 only. Phase 2 is filed as a child once the diagnosis lands.

## Why

`commit-and-pr --skip-hooks` defeats the safety net the four guards exist to provide:

- **privacy-guard**: blocks private repo slugs leaking into public commits
- **complexity-guard**: blocks new function-complexity / nesting-depth / file-size violations
- **scope-guard**: blocks out-of-scope file changes per brief Files Scope
- **dup-todo-guard**: blocks duplicate task-ID checkboxes in TODO.md

When a worker bypasses with `--no-verify`, none of these run. The current escape hatch is necessary (workers must be able to push when blocked) but it's also routine — every worker that hits the timeout strips the guards from that PR. Untracked, this drifts toward "guards run nowhere".

The 60s timeout in `full-loop-helper.sh` is reasonable for a fast-path. The fix is either to make the slow guard fast, or to give it a longer budget without raising the global timeout for all four.

## How

### Phase 1 — diagnostic-first (THIS ISSUE)

Files to modify: NONE. This is pure investigation.

Steps:

1. Reproduce the timeout: check out the PR #20817 diff in a worktree, run each guard standalone:
   ```bash
   cd ~/Git/aidevops-feature-auto-20260425-004525-gh20732
   for g in privacy-guard-pre-push.sh complexity-guard-pre-push.sh scope-guard-pre-push.sh dup-todo-guard-pre-push.sh; do
       echo "=== $g ==="
       time ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/$g
       echo
   done
   ```
2. Record the timing in this issue's body as a comment.
3. If the slow guard is reproducible, profile it (`bash -x`, identify hot loops or external calls).
4. If the slow guard is NOT reproducible (transient), add diagnostic logging to each guard so the next timeout instance leaves a breadcrumb.
5. File Phase 2 child issue with the targeted fix and link back to this issue with `Resolves` once Phase 2 lands.

### Reference patterns

- Pre-push hook architecture: `reference/pre-push-guards.md`
- Existing guard scripts: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*-guard-pre-push.sh`
- Timeout location in full-loop-helper: search `Push timed out after 60s` (~line 730)

### Verification

```bash
# Phase 1 success criterion: this issue carries a comment with measured timings for all four guards on a reproducer diff.
# Phase 2 will be a separate PR with code changes.
```

### Files Scope

(Phase 1 only — investigation)

- No files modified in this phase.

## Acceptance (Phase 1 only)

1. Issue carries a comment with `time` measurements for all four pre-push guards on a reproducer diff (the #20732 diff or any large multi-file diff where the timeout has been observed).
2. The slow guard is identified by name, with its measured wall time and the dominant cost (CPU loop / external command / network / disk IO).
3. If the slow guard is reproducible, this issue also carries a brief profiling note (which line / which subprocess dominates).
4. Phase 2 child issue filed with: target file, proposed fix, estimated diff size, regression test sketch.

## Context

- Worker log evidence (PR #20817 cherry-pick session, ~21:18 UTC 2026-04-24): `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-20732.log` lines 108-120 — `commit-and-pr` push timed out at 60s, worker fell back to `git push --no-verify`, second invocation with `--skip-hooks` succeeded.
- Tier: standard. Investigation only — should not need thinking-tier.
- Not in dispatch-path file set. Auto-dispatch is fine.
- Tag as `parent-task` so the Phase 2 child can be filed cleanly underneath.

title: t2825: idempotent task-ID prefix in commit-and-pr (PR title double-prefix fix)
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced while triaging #20732 dispatch friction (5 attempts → merge). PR #20817 (the recovery PR that closed #20732) ended up titled `t2799: t2799: split RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS from NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS in review-bot-gate-helper` — task-ID prefix appears twice. Cosmetic but visible in the merged-PR audit trail.

## What

In `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`, make the auto-derived PR title prefix idempotent: when `--message` already starts with `t[0-9]+:` or `GH#[0-9]+:`, skip the auto-prefix instead of prepending again.

## Why

`full-loop-helper.sh:1078-1080` currently does:

```bash
if [[ -z "$pr_title" ]]; then
    pr_title="$(_derive_pr_title_prefix "$issue_number"): ${commit_message}"
fi
```

When the worker conscientiously prefixes `--message` with the task ID (the natural form the brief asks for, and the form most workers default to), `_derive_pr_title_prefix` resolves the same prefix from TODO.md and prepends it a second time. Result: `tNNN: tNNN: <description>`.

The issue-sync auto-completion regex (`^tNNN`) tolerates the double-prefix and still extracts a task_id correctly, so the merge-time TODO checkbox flip still works. But the PR title is published in this state, surfaces in `git log --oneline`, and ends up in any audit query that surfaces the title.

This is in the t2821 (#20827) "dispatch-path file" set — `full-loop-helper.sh` is the canonical headless commit/PR pipeline. The proposed t2821 policy says these should default to interactive implementation, which is what this issue does.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1078-1080` — guard the auto-prefix with a regex check.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-title-prefix-idempotent.sh` — regression test covering all branches.

### Implementation

Replace lines 1078-1080 with:

```bash
if [[ -z "$pr_title" ]]; then
    if [[ "$commit_message" =~ ^(t[0-9]+|GH#[0-9]+): ]]; then
        # Message already carries a task-ID prefix — use as-is.
        pr_title="$commit_message"
    else
        pr_title="$(_derive_pr_title_prefix "$issue_number"): ${commit_message}"
    fi
fi
```

### Reference patterns

- Regex idiom matches the form already used in `_derive_pr_title_prefix` (line 932) for grep-extracting task IDs from TODO.md.
- Test pattern: model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id.sh` for the `setup_test_env` / `cleanup_test_env` / `print_result` shape.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-title-prefix-idempotent.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-title-prefix-idempotent.sh`

## Acceptance

1. When `commit_message="t2799: split foo"` and `issue_number=20732` (TODO has `t2799 ... ref:GH#20732`), `pr_title="t2799: split foo"` (no double prefix).
2. When `commit_message="GH#20774: remove alias"` and `issue_number=20774`, `pr_title="GH#20774: remove alias"`.
3. When `commit_message="split foo"` (no prefix) and `issue_number=20732`, `pr_title="t2799: split foo"` (existing behaviour preserved).
4. When `--title "explicit override"` is passed, the new code path is bypassed (existing behaviour preserved — the `[[ -z "$pr_title" ]]` outer guard already handles this).
5. Regression test covers all four cases plus the existing GH#-fallback path.
6. ShellCheck clean.

## Reference

- Bug instance: PR #20817 title `t2799: t2799: split RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS from NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS in review-bot-gate-helper`
- Related: t2720 (existing tNNN-vs-GH# preference work) at full-loop-helper.sh:886-944

title: t2826: test-label-invariants: retarget WORKFLOW_FILE to issue-sync-reusable.yml after t2770 migration
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced 2026-04-25 while landing PR #20838 (GH#20828 parent-task close gate). Running `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-label-invariants.sh` against the worktree showed two pre-existing failures unrelated to the PR:


title: t2827: nesting-depth pre-push guard: change-scoped scan to fix 60s timeout
body:
## Session Origin

Filed by diagnostic worker session for issue #20835 (Phase 1 complete). This is the Phase 2 fix.

## Task

Implement change-scoped scanning in `complexity-regression-helper.sh` so the `check` command only scans files that changed between base SHA and head SHA, instead of scanning the entire repository.

## Why

The `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` hook currently times out at 60 seconds on every push that modifies any `.sh` file, because `complexity-regression-helper.sh check` scans **all 949 `.sh` files** in the repo regardless of how many files were actually changed:

- Phase 1 measurements (issue #20835 comment): `nesting-depth` metric takes **98s** (2 × 48.5s for base + head worktree full scans)
- Workers routinely fall back to `git push --no-verify` / `--skip-hooks` to bypass the timeout, defeating all four pre-push guards
- Root cause: `scan_dir` is called on the full worktree root, not on just the changed files

Correctness is preserved by the regression model: `new_violations = violations(head) - violations(base)`. We only need to compute those two sets for the changed files.

## How

### Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh` — `_check_regression` function (lines ~862-919) and `scan_dir` / metric-specific scanners

### Implementation

**Option A — diff-scoped worktrees (recommended):**

In `_check_regression`, before creating worktrees, compute the changed `.sh/.py` files:

```bash
_changed_sh=$(git diff --name-only "$_base_sha" "$_head_sha" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '\.(sh|py)$' || true)
if [[ -z "$_changed_sh" ]]; then
    log "[$_metric] no .sh/.py changes — skipping"
    exit 0  # no new violations possible
fi
```

Then in each metric scanner (`scan_dir_function_complexity`, `scan_dir_nesting_depth`, `scan_dir_file_size`), accept an optional `--files-filter <file>` argument (newline-separated list of relative paths to restrict scanning to). When present, skip `_collect_files` entirely and iterate only over the filtered list.

The `check` subcommand passes the changed-file list down to `_check_regression`. The `scan` subcommand (CI use case) remains unchanged — full-repo scan for CI is correct since CI isn't running against a local diff.

**Reference patterns:**
- Fast-path in `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh:143-148` — already computes `_changed_source` for the doc-only skip; this logic needs to be extended to restrict the actual scan
- `_collect_files` at line ~105 — the replacement for this in the scoped path is simply iterating over the filter list after resolving abs paths from the worktree root

### Acceptance criteria

1. Running `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` on a 2-file `.sh` change completes in **under 10 seconds** (vs current 98s)
2. Running it on a 0-file `.sh` change still exits 0 immediately (doc-only fast path)
3. Full-repo scan via `complexity-regression-helper.sh scan <dir>` is unchanged (no regression in CI use)
4. Verification: `time bash ~/.aidevops/agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh origin git@github.com:marcusquinn/aidevops.git` on the test branch completes under 10s

### Regression test sketch

```bash
# In .agents/scripts/tests/test-complexity-regression-helper.sh:
# Add a test case: create 2 modified .sh files in a temp worktree,
# verify _check_regression completes under 15s wall-clock for function-complexity,
# nesting-depth, and file-size metrics.
time complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base "$BASE" --metric nesting-depth
# Expected: < 15s (vs ~98s before fix)
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-complexity-regression-helper.sh` (regression test)
- `.agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh` (if filter flag plumbing needs changes)

## Acceptance

1. `time bash ~/.aidevops/agents/hooks/complexity-regression-pre-push.sh origin ...` on a 2-file `.sh` diff completes **under 10 seconds**
2. Full-repo `scan` subcommand unchanged (CI correctness preserved)
3. Regression test added to test suite
4. No new `qlty smells` introduced

## Context

- Parent issue: #20835 (Phase 1 diagnosis)
- Phase 1 diagnostic comment: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20835#issuecomment-4317404507
- Measured baseline: `nesting-depth` check = 98.2s, `function-complexity` = 8.3s, `file-size` = 5.2s, all on 949 total `.sh` files vs 1-2 changed files
- Do NOT use `parent-task` label here — this is a leaf implementation task

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #20827 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #20827

**Parent issue:** #20827 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** t2821: policy: dispatch-path tasks default to #parent + no-auto-dispatch for interactive implementation
**Parent labels:** `status:queued,no-auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,model:opus-4-7`

> You do **NOT** need to read #20827. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #20827 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #20827:**

```bash
gh issue comment 20827 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 20827 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 20827 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #20827 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #20827** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

Establish a framework-level rule: tasks whose `## Files to modify` section hits the worker dispatch/spawn path default to `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` unless explicitly overridden. Maintainers implement these interactively rather than through auto-dispatched workers.

## Why

Self-hosting tasks (fixing the worker dispatch path from within worker-dispatched sessions) have a tautology failure mode: broken dispatch kills workers fixing dispatch. Observed on #20765 (t2814):

- 3 worker attempts across ~90 minutes before one succeeded
- 2 attempts failed with `worker_failed`, 1 with `no_worker_process` (the exact bug being fixed)
- Estimated ~40-60K opus tokens burned on failed attempts before the successful opus-4-7 run

Issues A (t2819 — self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override) and B (t2820 — no_work reclassification extension) mitigate the cost **per failed attempt**. This rule addresses the decision to **attempt dispatch at all** for this task class.

The pattern is already encoded for the parent meta-task #20740 (t2804), which uses `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive`. Child phases auto-inherit tier but not this combination — #20765 (Phase 3) carried `auto-dispatch` by default, which kicked off the tautology loop.

Maintainers implementing these interactively have several concrete advantages over auto-dispatched workers:

1. Human context available for judgment calls about dispatch-path design trade-offs
2. Bypass the broken dispatch path entirely (interactive sessions don't spawn workers through the pulse)
3. Unlimited context budget (interactive Claude/OpenCode sessions vs ~200K soft-ceiling for workers)
4. Faster iteration on canary/FD/session-lock logic that requires visibility into the running system
5. The visibility fixes from Phase 3 (Fix 1 worker-log tails in `CLAIM_RELEASED` comments) are most valuable to maintainers debugging live, not to a worker being blocked by the bug

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — add a new section describing the dispatch-path default. Place after "Pre-implementation discovery (t2046)" or within "Worker triage responsibility". Document the trigger file set (shared with Issue A) and the override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` — add a "Dispatch-path classification" row to the Tier Assignment Validation checklist. If the files-scope section hits the self-hosting set, the tier-checklist flags it and prompts for `#parent`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh` — when the brief's `Files Scope` or `How` section references a dispatch-path file, auto-recommend `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` in the TODO entry emitted.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — when the `--description` or linked brief hits dispatch-path patterns AND the `--labels` argument includes `auto-dispatch`, emit a stderr warning (not a block) so the user knows what they are overriding.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-path-parent-default.sh` — regression test for brief-helper + claim-task-id behaviour (positive/negative/override cases).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` — document the default and the manual override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — cross-link the new rule in the "Auto-Dispatch and Completion" section.

### Default decision tree (new)

1. Brief's `Files Scope` or `## How` references any file in the self-hosting set (same canonical list as Issue A — keep it in one place, reference it from both) → recommend `#parent`, `no-auto-dispatch`, and `origin:interactive`.
2. User can override with a `#dispatch-path-ok` tag in the TODO entry (maps to a new label, also `dispatch-path-ok`) — documented as "I have read the rationale and want auto-dispatch anyway, the self-hosting pre-dispatch detector (Issue A) is my safety net". Tracked for observability.
3. The self-hosting pre-dispatch validator from Issue A (t2819) remains active as a safety net when the override is used, so `model:opus-4-7` is still applied before dispatch.

### Reference pattern

- The `parent-task` label + `no-auto-dispatch` label pattern is already in place — used by #20740 (parent t2804), documented in `reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`. This rule automates application for a specific file-pattern class.
- The `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` server-side auto-downgrade (t2389) is the closest architectural analogue: detects a mis-classification from the brief shape and adjusts labels with a provenance-wrapped audit comment. Model the brief-helper side-effect on this pattern.
- Canonical file-set source: share the same shell array / config file used by Issue A (t2819) so both helpers stay in sync when new dispatch-path files are added. Consider `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf` with a newline-separated list sourced by both helpers.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-path-parent-default.sh
# Observe: filing a new task via /new-task that references pulse-wrapper.sh in Files Scope
# produces #parent + no-auto-dispatch in the TODO entry emitted
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `build.txt` and `brief-template.md` updated with the dispatch-path default rule
- [ ] `task-brief-helper.sh` recommends `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` when self-hosting files detected in brief
- [ ] `claim-task-id.sh` emits stderr warning when `auto-dispatch` is requested on a dispatch-path task (non-blocking)
- [ ] Override path (`#dispatch-path-ok` tag → `dispatch-path-ok` label) works and is documented
- [ ] Shared canonical file-set between Issue A (t2819) and Issue C (this task) — single source of truth
- [ ] Regression test covers positive/negative/override cases
- [ ] `reference/auto-dispatch.md` updated
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` cross-link added

## Session Origin

Interactive session with maintainer. Companion policy-level fix to (A) self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override (t2819) and (B) no_work reclassification extension (t2820). All three derived from #20765 dispatch-history analysis.

This issue is intentionally filed with `no-auto-dispatch` — policy changes that modify the dispatch-routing rules should be reviewed by the maintainer before landing.

Extend the `no_work` classification — which currently triggers only on `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` — to also cover `worker_failed` events where the worker log shows no actual implementation progress (no tool calls, no file edits, no commits). title: consolidated: t2821: policy: dispatch-path tasks default to #parent + no-auto-dispatch for interactive implementation
body:
_Supersedes #20827 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Establish a framework-level rule: tasks whose `## Files to modify` section hits the worker dispatch/spawn path default to `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` unless explicitly overridden. Maintainers implement these interactively rather than through auto-dispatched workers.

## Why

Self-hosting tasks (fixing the worker dispatch path from within worker-dispatched sessions) have a tautology failure mode: broken dispatch kills workers fixing dispatch. Observed on #20765 (t2814):

- 3 worker attempts across ~90 minutes before one succeeded
- 2 attempts failed with `worker_failed`, 1 with `no_worker_process` (the exact bug being fixed)
- Estimated ~40-60K opus tokens burned on failed attempts before the successful opus-4-7 run

Issues A (t2819 — self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override) and B (t2820 — no_work reclassification extension) mitigate the cost **per failed attempt**. This rule addresses the decision to **attempt dispatch at all** for this task class.

The pattern is already encoded for the parent meta-task #20740 (t2804), which uses `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive`. Child phases auto-inherit tier but not this combination — #20765 (Phase 3) carried `auto-dispatch` by default, which kicked off the tautology loop.

Maintainers implementing these interactively have several concrete advantages over auto-dispatched workers:

1. Human context available for judgment calls about dispatch-path design trade-offs
2. Bypass the broken dispatch path entirely (interactive sessions don't spawn workers through the pulse)
3. Unlimited context budget (interactive Claude/OpenCode sessions vs ~200K soft-ceiling for workers)
4. Faster iteration on canary/FD/session-lock logic that requires visibility into the running system
5. The visibility fixes from Phase 3 (Fix 1 worker-log tails in `CLAIM_RELEASED` comments) are most valuable to maintainers debugging live, not to a worker being blocked by the bug

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — add a new section describing the dispatch-path default. Place after "Pre-implementation discovery (t2046)" or within "Worker triage responsibility". Document the trigger file set (shared with Issue A) and the override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` — add a "Dispatch-path classification" row to the Tier Assignment Validation checklist. If the files-scope section hits the self-hosting set, the tier-checklist flags it and prompts for `#parent`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh` — when the brief's `Files Scope` or `## How` section references a dispatch-path file, auto-recommend `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` in the TODO entry emitted.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — when the `--description` or linked brief hits dispatch-path patterns AND the `--labels` argument includes `auto-dispatch`, emit a stderr warning (not a block) so the user knows what they are overriding.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-path-parent-default.sh` — regression test for brief-helper + claim-task-id behaviour (positive/negative/override cases).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` — document the default and the manual override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — cross-link the new rule in the "Auto-Dispatch and Completion" section.

### Default decision tree

1. Brief's `Files Scope` or `## How` references any file in the self-hosting set (same canonical list as Issue A — keep it in one place, reference it from both) → recommend `#parent`, `no-auto-dispatch`, and `origin:interactive`.
2. User can override with a `#dispatch-path-ok` tag in the TODO entry (maps to a new label, also `dispatch-path-ok`) — documented as "I have read the rationale and want auto-dispatch anyway, the self-hosting pre-dispatch detector (Issue A) is my safety net". Tracked for observability.
3. The self-hosting pre-dispatch validator from Issue A (t2819) remains active as a safety net when the override is used, so `model:opus-4-7` is still applied before dispatch.

### Reference pattern

- The `parent-task` label + `no-auto-dispatch` label pattern is already in place — used by #20740 (parent t2804), documented in `reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`. This rule automates application for a specific file-pattern class.
- The `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` server-side auto-downgrade (t2389) is the closest architectural analogue: detects a mis-classification from the brief shape and adjusts labels with a provenance-wrapped audit comment. Model the brief-helper side-effect on this pattern.
- Canonical file-set source: share the same shell array / config file used by Issue A (t2819) so both helpers stay in sync when new dispatch-path files are added. Consider `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf` with a newline-separated list sourced by both helpers.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-path-parent-default.sh
# Observe: filing a new task via /new-task that references pulse-wrapper.sh in Files Scope
# produces #parent + no-auto-dispatch in the TODO entry emitted
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build.txt` and `brief-template.md` updated with the dispatch-path default rule
- [ ] `task-brief-helper.sh` recommends `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` when self-hosting files detected in brief
- [ ] `claim-task-id.sh` emits stderr warning when `auto-dispatch` is requested on a dispatch-path task (non-blocking)
- [ ] Override path (`#dispatch-path-ok` tag → `dispatch-path-ok` label) works and is documented
- [ ] Shared canonical file-set between Issue A (t2819) and Issue C (this task) — single source of truth
- [ ] Regression test covers positive/negative/override cases
- [ ] `reference/auto-dispatch.md` updated
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` cross-link added

## Context & Decisions

**per @alex-solovyev (original issue body):** The policy was derived from root-cause analysis of #20765 (t2814), where 3 worker attempts over ~90 minutes and ~40-60K opus tokens were burned before one succeeded. The tautology failure mode — dispatch breaking tasks meant to fix dispatch — is the core motivation.

**per @alex-solovyev:** The self-hosting pre-dispatch detector (Issue A, t2819) and no_work reclassification (Issue B, t2820) are companion mitigations. This rule (Issue C) addresses whether to dispatch at all. All three reference the same canonical self-hosting file set (proposed: `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`), keeping it as a single source of truth.

**Comment thread note:** Both comments on #20827 were automated operational messages (no_work tier escalation skip and self-hosting tier override applied by the pulse). No substantive scope modifications, corrections, or clarifications were added by human commenters. The original issue body is the complete spec.

title: t2828: pulse: split merge pass into dedicated 60s launchd plist (decouple from dispa...
body:
## What

Extract the pulse merge pass (`pulse-merge.sh`) into a dedicated launchd plist running every 60 seconds, decoupled from the main dispatch cycle. Currently `pulse-merge.sh` is invoked as a phase inside `pulse-wrapper.sh`, so PRs that go green at the start of a cycle wait for the full cycle (~28 min average, max 3.5h observed) before landing.

## Why

Empirical evidence over last 100 cycles (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`):

- Median cycle duration: **1411s (23.5 min)**, mean **1703s (28.4 min)**
- 33% of cycles merge anything; total 65 PRs merged in waves of up to 6 PRs/cycle
- Plist `StartInterval=180s` is fictional — cycles overlap so consecutive ticks land back-to-back at ~23 min cadence

Result: a PR can sit MERGEABLE + green for 28 minutes after CI completes before the merge gate sees it. Decoupling drops that to ~60s deterministically, eliminates the "batchy waves" perception, and reduces user-visible latency by 20-25x.

This is independent of dispatch concurrency — even with the worker cap raised, the merge bottleneck remains.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/templates/launchd/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-merge.plist` — model on existing `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` shape, but with `StartInterval=60` and `ProgramArguments` invoking `pulse-merge.sh` directly (not pulse-wrapper.sh).
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/install-launchd-helper.sh` (or wherever the supervisor plist install lives) — add the merge plist to the install/uninstall flow alongside the pulse plist.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add an env-gated skip for the merge phase: when `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_PHASE_DISABLED=1` (set by setup.sh when the dedicated merge plist is installed), the dispatch cycle's merge phase is a no-op. Avoids double-execution race.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — ensure the entry point can be invoked standalone (not just sourced from pulse-wrapper). Add an `flock` on a separate lockdir (`~/.aidevops/locks/pulse-merge.lock`) so merge passes don't overlap themselves.
- **EDIT**: `setup.sh` and/or `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — install both plists and toggle `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_PHASE_DISABLED` accordingly.

### Reference pattern

title: t2829: pulse: aggressive stale-lock breaker for wedged cycles holding lockdir for hours
body:
## What

Add aggressive stale-lock breaking to `pulse-wrapper.sh` is-running check: when the lockdir holder PID has been alive but idle (no log activity) for >30 min, OR the PID is dead but the lockdir wasn't cleaned up, kill the process group and reclaim the lock. Surface stalled-cycle counter in `pulse-stats.json`.

## Why

Empirical evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log`:

```
[2026-04-25T05:06:59Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] refresh complete  ← cycle ends
[pulse-wrapper] Starting pulse at 2026-04-25T06:52:50Z (trigger=stall)  ← 1h46m gap
[2026-04-25T09:53:44Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] issues refresh ← 3h gap before next prefetch
```

Cycles are wedging for **1-3 hours** at a time. The 180s plist tick fires every 3 min and gets "Pulse already running (PID: X), skipping" rejections — it never reclaims the lock. The stall watchdog from GH#20613/20614 added stale-lock detection at acquire time, but evidence shows it's not aggressive enough: the watchdog detects after multiple hours, when the work backlog is severe.

During these multi-hour wedges, ZERO dispatch happens. This is the largest single contributor to "broad interval" perception — worse than cycle elongation, worse than circuit-breaker fires.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — `is_pulse_running` (or equivalent lockdir-check function): replace simple PID-alive check with three-tier check:
  1. PID dead → reclaim immediately (already exists)
  2. PID alive AND lockdir age <`PULSE_STALE_LOCK_THRESHOLD` (default 1800s = 30 min) → respect the lock (current behavior)
  3. PID alive AND lockdir age ≥ threshold AND no log activity since lockdir created → kill the process group (`kill -TERM -<pgid>`, wait 5s, `kill -KILL -<pgid>`), remove lockdir, increment `pulse_stale_lock_broken` counter, log the kill.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh` — add `PULSE_STALE_LOCK_THRESHOLD` (default 1800s), `PULSE_STALE_LOCK_BREAKER_ENABLED` (default 1).
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — also detect "alive but idle" by checking last log line timestamp in `pulse-wrapper.log` against current time — if >`PULSE_STALE_LOCK_THRESHOLD`, trigger the same breaker.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-lock-breaker.sh` — synthetic test: write a fake lockdir with old timestamp, verify breaker fires; spawn a real process holding the lock, verify breaker does NOT fire when lock is fresh.

### Reference pattern

Existing stale-lock handling in `pulse-wrapper.sh` from GH#20613/20614 — extend that path with the age check + process-group kill. Process-group killing is established in `worker-watchdog.sh` (used to kill stuck workers).

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-lock-breaker.sh

### Complexity Impact

- `pulse-wrapper.sh` is already at file-size-debt (2000+ lines tracked in #20801). Mitigation: extract the new logic into a small helper function (`_check_and_break_stale_lock`) at the bottom of the file, ~30 lines. Does not exceed function-complexity gate.

### Verification

```bash
# Synthetic test:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-lock-breaker.sh
# Expected: PASS

# Manual verification:
# 1. Wedge a cycle: from a separate shell, hold the lockdir
mkdir ~/.aidevops/locks/pulse-wrapper-instance.lock
echo $$ > ~/.aidevops/locks/pulse-wrapper-instance.lock/pid
# 2. Backdate the lockdir mtime by 31 min
touch -mt $(date -v-31M +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S) ~/.aidevops/locks/pulse-wrapper-instance.lock
# 3. Trigger pulse manually
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
# 4. Expect: log entry "stale lock detected, breaking", lockdir removed, cycle proceeds.

# Counter populated:
jq '.counters.pulse_stale_lock_broken | length' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stats.json
# Expected: increments on each break event

# 24h soak test:
# Watch for sustained dispatch — no >30 min gaps between cycle starts in pulse-wrapper.log
```

## Acceptance

1. Stale-lock breaker fires when lockdir age >30 min AND no log activity in same window.
2. Living, active cycles are NEVER broken (test: long but actively-logging cycle keeps lock).
3. `pulse_stale_lock_broken` counter populated in `pulse-stats.json`.
4. Synthetic test passes (`test-pulse-stale-lock-breaker.sh`).
5. Post-deploy 24h: no `>30 min` gap between cycle starts in `pulse-wrapper.log` (current evidence shows multiple 1-3h gaps).
6. ShellCheck clean.

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive concurrency analysis (2026-04-25). Discovered 1h46m and 3h gaps in `pulse-wrapper.log` between cycle ends and next start, indicating wedged cycles holding the instance lock for hours. Highest-leverage fix for the "long quiet stretches" component of the user-perceived batchy behaviour.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — Sonnet. Process-group killing requires care to not nuke active work; needs synthetic test design; touches the lock contention path. Not simple.

title: t2830: pulse: L1 events-ETag tickle layer above batch prefetch (skip search calls when nothing changed)
body:
## What

Add an L1 "events tickle" cache layer above the existing L3 batch prefetch in `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`. Use `gh api /users/{owner}/events` (or `/orgs/{owner}/events` for orgs) with stored ETag and `If-None-Match` conditional GET — costs **0 rate-limit points on 304 Not Modified**. If the owner's events ETag hasn't changed since the last cycle, skip the batch prefetch's 2 search calls for that owner entirely.

## Why

Currently every pulse cycle runs L3 batch prefetch unconditionally:

```
[2026-04-25T05:06:50Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] issues refresh for owner=webapp
[2026-04-25T05:06:51Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] prs refresh for owner=webapp
[2026-04-25T05:06:52Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] issues refresh for owner=essentials-com
[2026-04-25T05:06:55Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] issues refresh for owner=marcusquinn
[2026-04-25T05:06:56Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] prs refresh for owner=marcusquinn
[2026-04-25T05:06:58Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] issues refresh for owner=wpallstars
[2026-04-25T05:06:59Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] prs refresh for owner=wpallstars
[2026-04-25T05:06:59Z] [pulse-batch-prefetch] refresh complete: search_calls=8 cache_writes=18
```

8 search calls (~1.2GraphQL points each = ~10 points) per cycle, 30+ cycles/h = ~300 GraphQL points/h on prefetch alone, even when **nothing changed** in any owner. Most cycles dispatch zero workers (only 35% of cycles have workers, evidence from cycle-index).

`/events` endpoint:
- REST API (separate 5000/h pool from GraphQL — t2574 / t2744 framework already routes some calls there)
- Conditional GET via ETag → 304 = 0 rate-limit charge
- Returns "any push, issue, PR, comment, label change, etc." within ~30s of the event happening on GitHub
- Per-owner aggregation (one call covers all repos under that owner)

Expected behavior: ~80% of cycles get 304 on all 4 owners = 0 search calls. Active period (you're working on a repo): tickle returns 200, batch prefetch runs as today.

This is the cheapest possible "is anything new?" gate. Complements the existing L2 idle-skip (which detects fingerprint changes per repo) by eliminating the L3 calls that build the fingerprint in the first place.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh` — single function `events_tickle <owner>` that:
  1. Reads stored ETag from `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-events-etag/{owner}.json`
  2. Calls `gh api -i /users/{owner}/events?per_page=1 -H "If-None-Match: <etag>"` (or `/orgs/...` based on owner type, cached)
  3. On 304: returns "fresh" (exit 0)
  4. On 200: parses new ETag from response headers, writes back to cache, returns "stale" (exit 1)
  5. On rate-limit / network error: returns "unknown" (exit 2) — caller treats as stale (fail-open, never falsely skip work)
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` — at the top of the per-owner loop, call `events_tickle "$owner"`. If exit 0 (fresh), increment `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_HITS` counter and `continue` to next owner without running search calls.
- **NEW**: `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-events-etag/` directory created at first run (mkdir -p in helper).
- **EDIT**: `.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf` — add `PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_ENABLED=1` env override.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh` — mocks `gh api` to return 304/200, verifies the helper does the right thing.

### Reference pattern

The existing batch-prefetch loop in `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` at line ~280-350 (look for the `for owner in` loop). The tickle is a cheap pre-check inserted at the top of each iteration. Follow the existing `_PULSE_HEALTH_BATCH_CACHE_HITS` counter pattern for the new `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_HITS` / `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_FRESH` / `_PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_STALE` counters.

`gh api -i` returns headers; parse with `awk '/^etag:/i {print $2}' | tr -d '\r"'`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
- .agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh

### Complexity Impact

- New file ~80 lines, single function, no nesting issues.
- `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` adds ~10 lines (single conditional + counter), no function-complexity gate impact.

### Verification

```bash
# Synthetic test:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh
# Expected: PASS

# Live verification:
# 1. Force a tickle for an owner you haven't touched in days:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh marcusquinn
# Expected: prints "stale" first time (no cache), "fresh" second time (304 hit)

# 2. Verify cache file populated:
cat ~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-events-etag/marcusquinn.json
# Expected: {"etag": "...", "last_check": "..."}

# 3. Run batch prefetch and observe skip:
PULSE_EVENTS_TICKLE_ENABLED=1 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh refresh-all
# Expected: log entries "events tickle fresh for owner=X, skipping search calls" for quiet owners

# 4. After 1h soak, count search-call reduction:
grep -c "search_calls=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log  # before vs after
# Expected: total search_calls drop ~70% (assumes typical activity pattern)

# 5. GraphQL budget over 1h pulse run:
watch -n 60 'gh api rate_limit --jq ".resources.graphql.remaining"'
# Expected: stays >3000 most of the time (was dipping below 1500 firing circuit breaker)
```

## Acceptance

1. `events_tickle` returns "fresh" on 304, "stale" on 200, "unknown" on error (fail-open).
2. ETag stored per owner, sent on subsequent requests.
3. Batch prefetch skips search calls for owners returning "fresh".
4. Synthetic test passes.
5. Post-deploy 24h: total batch search calls drop ≥60%.
6. Post-deploy 24h: zero new `pulse_dispatch_circuit_broken` events (currently 29 in 72h).
7. ShellCheck clean.
8. Counter `pulse_events_tickle_fresh` / `pulse_events_tickle_stale` populated in pulse-stats.json.

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive concurrency analysis (2026-04-25). User insight: "most repos won't have any issues or work needed for long periods of time, and a few will be continual work. maybe there's some method of 'is there anything new' on each repo that checks less frequently, and only if there is, does the more detailed analysis runs". The events ETag mechanism is GitHub's canonical primitive for exactly this — designed for polling change detection.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — Sonnet. New file with HTTP semantics (header parsing, conditional GET, fail-open error handling), integration into existing prefetch flow, synthetic test design. Not simple.

## Merge Conflict Feedback (from PR #21270)

The previous worker's PR #21270 (`t2830: pulse: L1 events-ETag tickle layer above batch prefetch`) developed merge conflicts with
`main` that could not be resolved by `gh pr update-branch` (server-side fast-forward).
The conflicts are semantic — the same files were modified on both branches (7 files touched).

### Files in the conflicting PR

```
.agents/configs/pulse-rate-limit.conf
.agents/scripts/pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-events-tickle.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch.sh
.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh
.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-events-tickle.sh
```

### Worker guidance

The prior PR's head commit is `7eb0f584940c21cdecdf8918ac5aaccbbe13c104`. Choose the cheapest path that works:

1. **Cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`** (~10x cheaper than rewriting, works when the prior implementation was correct-but-stale):

   ```bash
   git fetch origin pull/21270/head:recovered-21270
   # Explicit base on origin/main — NOT canonical HEAD (t2802).
   git worktree add -b fresh-branch ../fresh-worktree origin/main
   cd ../fresh-worktree
   git cherry-pick 7eb0f584940c21cdecdf8918ac5aaccbbe13c104
   # run tests — if clean, proceed to PR
   ```

2. **If cherry-pick surfaces conflicts**, resolve them. The conflict surface IS the semantic overlap between the two branches — resolve those specific hunks rather than rewriting untouched logic.

3. **If the scope-leak warning above fired** (prior PR >20 files but the issue describes a focused fix), **skip cherry-pick entirely** and rebuild from scratch using the issue body as the spec. Do NOT try to cherry-pick-then-drop-files — too error-prone. A clean rewrite from the 2-line spec is cheaper than surgery on a 100-file branch.

4. **Only rewrite from scratch (scope-OK case)** if the prior approach was rejected in review. Check PR #21270's review comments for `CHANGES_REQUESTED` or rejection keywords before assuming the approach was wrong.

Do NOT reuse the old PR's branch directly — always cherry-pick onto a fresh branch off current `origin/main`.

_Routed by deterministic merge pass (pulse-merge.sh)._

title: t2831: pulse: per-repo adaptive cadence (hot/warm/cold tiers based on 7-day activity)
body:
## What

Classify pulse-enabled repos into 3 activity tiers (`hot`, `warm`, `cold`) based on rolling 7-day GitHub activity (event count + PR throughput), and use the tier to control how often each repo is evaluated. Hot repos check every cycle (~60s with the merge plist split landed), warm every 3 cycles, cold every 10 cycles.

## Why

All 14 pulse-enabled repos currently get equal attention every cycle, regardless of whether they've had any activity for weeks. Empirically (~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-batch-prefetch logs):

- Owner `webapp`: continual issue/PR activity, multiple per day
- Owner `marcusquinn`: 8 repos, 3-4 active, the rest mostly idle
- Owner `wpallstars`: 4 repos, mostly idle
- Owner `essentials-com`: 1 repo, mostly idle

Even with the L1 events tickle (sister task in this concurrency-improvement batch), an active owner means ALL its repos get evaluated. Per-repo tiering finishes the job: an active owner with 1 hot repo and 7 cold repos shouldn't pay the L4 delta-prefetch cost on the cold ones every cycle.

This is independent and additive to the events-tickle work — events-tickle eliminates owner-level work; tiering eliminates per-repo work within active owners.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-tier.sh` — two commands:
  1. `classify` — for each pulse-enabled repo, query last 7 days of activity (`gh api /repos/{slug}/events?per_page=100` REST, paginated until 7d boundary), count events, classify:
     - **hot**: ≥30 events in 7 days, OR has open PR with `status:in-progress` label
     - **warm**: 5-29 events in 7 days
     - **cold**: <5 events in 7 days
     Write to `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-repo-tiers.json`. Re-run hourly.
  2. `tier-of <slug>` — read cached tier for one repo. If cache miss or >2h old, return "warm" (safe default).
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-tier-classifier-routine.sh` — runs hourly via launchd (separate plist), invokes `pulse-repo-tier.sh classify`.
- **NEW**: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-repo-tier-classify.plist` — `StartInterval=3600`.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` — in the per-repo loop, call `pulse-repo-tier.sh tier-of "$slug"`. Read corresponding minimum check interval from config:
  - hot: every cycle (no skip)
  - warm: skip if last full check <180s ago
  - cold: skip if last full check <600s ago
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh` — add `PULSE_TIER_HOT_INTERVAL=0`, `PULSE_TIER_WARM_INTERVAL=180`, `PULSE_TIER_COLD_INTERVAL=600`, `PULSE_TIER_CLASSIFICATION_ENABLED=1`.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-repo-tier.sh` — mocks event counts, verifies classification thresholds.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/install-launchd-helper.sh` — install the new tier-classifier plist.

### Reference pattern

The L2 idle-skip helper `_prefetch_single_repo_idle_skip` in `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` is the right pattern — it short-circuits per-repo work based on cache state. The new tier check happens before L2: if tier=cold AND last_check<600s, skip even the L2 check.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-repo-tier.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-repo-tier-classifier-routine.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh
- .agents/scripts/install-launchd-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-repo-tier.sh
- ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-repo-tier-classify.plist (template version under .agents/templates/launchd/)

### Complexity Impact

- New helper ~150 lines, classifier routine ~40 lines, single new conditional in prefetch (~8 lines). No file-size or function-complexity issues.

### Verification

```bash
# Initial classification:
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-repo-tier.sh classify
cat ~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-repo-tiers.json | jq
# Expected: { "marcusquinn/aidevops": "hot", "webapp/webapp": "hot", ... rest "warm" or "cold" }

# Test classification:
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-repo-tier.sh
# Expected: PASS

# Live behavior:
# Watch a cold repo's check pattern in pulse-wrapper.log — should appear once per ~10 cycles
grep "prefetch.*marcusquinn/some-quiet-repo" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log | head -20
# Compare timestamps; gaps should be ~10x cycle interval

# Active repos uninterrupted:
grep "prefetch.*marcusquinn/aidevops" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log | head -20
# Should appear every cycle

# Cycle-time reduction:
# Before: median 1411s. After: expect 30-50% reduction on quiet hours.
jq -r '.duration_s' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl | tail -50 | sort -n | awk 'NR==25 {print "median: " $1 "s"}'
```

## Acceptance

1. `pulse-repo-tier.sh classify` populates `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-repo-tiers.json` with valid tier assignments.
2. `tier-of` returns cached tier OR "warm" on stale cache.
3. Classifier routine runs hourly via dedicated launchd plist.
4. Prefetch flow respects tier-based skip intervals (verified via log grep).
5. Hot repos check every cycle (no regression).
6. Cold repos check ~10x less often (verified via log timestamps).
7. Synthetic test passes.
8. Post-deploy 24h: median cycle duration drops ≥30% during low-activity hours.
9. ShellCheck clean.

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive concurrency analysis (2026-04-25). User insight: "most repos won't have any issues or work needed for long periods of time, and a few will be continual work" — the tier model directly implements this. Sister task to events-tickle (filed in same batch): events-tickle eliminates owner-level redundant work, tier eliminates per-repo redundant work within active owners.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — Sonnet. New helper script, classifier logic, launchd plist, multiple integration points, synthetic test. Not simple.

title: t2832: fix(dispatch-dedup): honour no-auto-dispatch label as unconditional block (parity with parent-task)
body:
## What

Add `no-auto-dispatch` to the unconditional dispatch block list in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, alongside the existing `parent-task` / `meta` checks. Currently the label is honoured by enrichment, decomposition, and backfill paths, but **not by the dispatch path itself** — workers get dispatched to issues carrying the label.

## Why

Observed live on #20827 (the very issue establishing the dispatch-path policy that uses this label):

- Issue created at 2026-04-25T00:16:34Z with `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive` + `tier:standard`
- `alex-solovyev`'s runner stripped `origin:interactive`, added `origin:worker` + `status:queued` at 00:46:13Z
- 6 worker dispatches over 2 hours (00:46 → 02:39), all failing (`no_worker_process` × 2, `worker_failed` × 3, escalated to `tier:thinking` then `model:opus-4-7`)
- Issue eventually consolidated into #20852 and closed `not-planned`
- Estimated ~30-50K opus tokens burned across failed attempts

The bug is that `no-auto-dispatch` is treated as a *don't-modify* signal by some pulse paths but not as a *don't-dispatch* signal by the dispatch path. Static evidence:

```bash
git ls-files '.agents/scripts/pulse*.sh' '.agents/scripts/dispatch*.sh' \
  '.agents/scripts/worker-*.sh' | xargs rg -n 'no-auto-dispatch'
# (no output — zero call sites in the dispatch path)
```

By contrast `parent-task` IS in the unconditional block at `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:644`, which is why the consolidated #20852 policy (t2821) currently has to combine `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` to actually block dispatch. The `#parent` half is doing all the real work; `no-auto-dispatch` alone is an audit-trail signal with no enforcement bite.

This makes `no-auto-dispatch` a footgun: maintainers, agents, and helpers (e.g. `interactive-session-helper.sh lockdown`) reasonably believe it blocks dispatch — and the documentation reinforces that reading — but in practice it only blocks enrichment and decomposition.

## How

### Files to modify

title: _parse_phases_section over-counts via ### Phase N detail subsections (parent-task auto-close bug)
body:
## Task

Fix `_parse_phases_section` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1336-1346` to stop at `### Phase` subsection headings, not just `##` top-level headings. The current awk emits the canonical `## Phases` list AND every following `### Phase N detail` subsection, double-counting phases when the parent body uses both forms.

## Why

Surfaced during interactive verification of #20559 (the parent-task lifecycle parent itself, ironically — see "manual close" rationale on that issue). All 3 phase children merged + closed; sub-issue graph manually completed; `_try_close_parent_tracker` invoked directly — but skipped close with `declared=6 filed=4`.

The `## Phases` list declares 3 phases:

```text
## Phases

- Phase 1 - Extend _parse_phases_section ...
- Phase 2 - Add phase-declaration-aware guard ...
- Phase 3 - Flip AIDEVOPS_SEQUENTIAL_PHASE_AUTOFILE ... #20768
```

Then prose detail subsections follow:

```text
### Phase 1 detail

Extend `_parse_phases_section` ... [contains "Phase 1" matches]

### Phase 2 detail

Add a declared-vs-filed guard ... [contains "Phase 2" matches]

### Phase 3 detail

Flip default in ... [contains "Phase 3" matches]
```

The awk parser at `:1336-1346` only stops at `^##\s` (top-level), so all the `### Phase N detail` subsections get included in `_phases_section`. The grep at `:1466` then matches "Phase N" in BOTH the canonical list AND the heading lines — declared count balloons to 6.

Net effect: parents with `## Phases` + `### Phase N detail` body shape can never auto-close even when all children are filed and merged. The very issue establishing this auto-close path (#20559) was its own first victim.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1336-1346` — narrow the awk exit condition to also stop at `^###[[:space:]]+Phase[[:space:]]+[0-9]+` headings, OR (cleaner) count phases from the canonical list-item shape only (e.g., `^-[[:space:]]+Phase[[:space:]]+[0-9]+` or `^[*-][[:space:]]+\*\*Phase[[:space:]]+[0-9]+`). The structured output of `shared-phase-filing.sh::_parse_phases_section` (loaded earlier in the source chain) does this correctly — consider delegating to it instead of the duplicate-named local awk.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-guard.sh` (or equivalent) — add a regression test for the "Phases list + detail subsections" body shape. Source body from #20559 verbatim is the canonical case.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md` — clarify that `### Phase N detail` subsections under `## Phases` are valid and must not double-count.

### Reference pattern

`shared-phase-filing.sh::_parse_phases_section` (loaded first) returns structured `N\tdesc\tmarker\tchild` lines and correctly stops at the first non-list-shaped line. Two functions with the same name shadow each other across sources — the `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` local definition wins because it sources later. Either rename the local one or delegate.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-guard.sh
- .agents/reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md

### Complexity Impact

`_parse_phases_section` is ~10 lines. Adding one awk condition or replacing with a delegation is minimal. Stays well under any complexity gate.

### Verification

```bash
source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
body=$(gh issue view 20559 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --json body -q .body)

count=$(printf '%s' "$phases" | grep -cE '(^|[[:space:]])Phase[[:space:]]+[0-9]+')
# Expected: 3 (was 6 pre-fix)

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-guard.sh
# Expected: PASS, including the new regression case
```

## Acceptance

1. `_parse_phases_section` returns only the canonical `## Phases` list, not the `### Phase N detail` subsections
2. Regression test added and passing for the "list + detail subsections" body shape
3. Counted phase declarations match the canonical list count for #20559's body shape (3, not 6)

title: _fetch_subissue_numbers / _try_close_parent_tracker: union graph+body children, not first-non-empty (parent-task auto-close bug)
body:
## Task

Make `_fetch_subissue_numbers` (or its caller `_try_close_parent_tracker`) **union** GraphQL sub-issue results with body `## Children` extraction, instead of short-circuiting when GraphQL returns any non-empty result. Today the body fallback only fires when GraphQL returns zero — which means a partially-populated sub-issue graph silently masks correctly-listed children in the body.

## Why

Surfaced during interactive verification of v3.11.1 deploy. Two parent-task issues (#20559, #20581) had all their phase children merged + closed, but `_try_close_parent_tracker` skipped them with `child_count < 2`:

- #20559 body declared 4 children (#20768, #20702, #20703, #20704). GraphQL graph had only #20768 (the only auto-filed phase). The 3 manually-filed children (#20702/3/4) were not registered.
- #20581 body declared 2 children (#20594, #20707). GraphQL graph had only #20594.

Per `_try_close_parent_tracker:1427-1456`, the early-exit `[[ "$child_count" -ge 2 ]] || return 1` blocks close. Per `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1953-1971`, child detection is graph→body→prose with first-non-empty-wins. So a graph with 1 entry beats a body with 4.

Fix produced manual-close (with audit comment) for #20559. Manual GraphQL backfill (`gh api repos/{slug}/issues/{n}/sub_issues -X POST -F sub_issue_id={db_id}`) was needed to test the close path. This is fragile — auto-filed phase children get registered, manually-filed ones don't, and the body listing ground truth is bypassed.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1953-1971` — change graph→body→prose first-wins to graph∪body∪prose union, deduplicated. Or pass body-extraction result alongside graph result into a merge step before the `child_count` check.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1427-1456` — `_try_close_parent_tracker` — accept the unioned set; treat any source as authoritative.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-guard.sh` — add regression test where GraphQL returns subset of body-listed children. Expected: parent closes when ALL children (from union) are closed, not just GraphQL ones.

### Reference pattern

`_fetch_subissue_numbers` returns a sorted-uniq list. Body extraction (the existing `### Phases` or `## Children` parser) returns same shape. `sort -un` over the concatenation produces the union. `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1962-1965` (commented-out body fallback path that used to fire only on empty graph) shows the pre-existing extraction logic — un-gate it.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-guard.sh

### Complexity Impact

`_try_close_parent_tracker` is currently ~50 lines. Adding a union step adds 3-5 lines. Stays under any complexity gate.

### Verification

```bash
# Reproduce against #20559 body shape with partial graph
source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
# Mock graph returning subset
# Verify _try_close_parent_tracker uses union for child_count

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-task-phase-guard.sh
# Expected: all cases pass, including partial-graph regression
```

## Acceptance

1. `_try_close_parent_tracker` uses the union of (graph, body, prose) child sets, not first-non-empty
2. Regression test added for partial-graph + complete-body case
3. Both #20559 and #20581 body shapes (had they remained open) would auto-close cleanly
4. ShellCheck clean

## Session Origin

Filed during v3.11.1 deploy verification. Companion issue to #20871 (parser over-counting). Together these two block parent-task auto-close on real-world parent body shapes — which is exactly what t2755/t2786/t2787/t2788 set out to make robust.
