title: shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:218 SC2215 — aidevops-allow comment on line continuation breaks shellcheck (release pre-flight blocker)
body:
## Task

Fix SC2215 in `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:218`. The line `gh pr create \ # aidevops-allow: raw-gh-wrapper` puts a comment on the same line as a backslash line continuation, which makes shellcheck think `# aidevops-allow:...` is the next argument and `--repo` becomes an unrelated command. The pre-flight blocked v3.11.1 release on this — needed `--skip-preflight` to ship.

## Why

SC2215 ("This flag is not handled. Use a `--` to demarcate the end of options"): the shell treats everything after `\` literally, so `\ # aidevops-allow: raw-gh-wrapper` is `\` followed by space-` ` followed by `#...`. Shellcheck reads the trailing `#` as the start of an option-like token and the surrounding context confuses option parsing on the wrapped `gh pr create`. Triggers on every linter-local run after t2818 landed the `aidevops-allow:` exemption marker.

Concretely:

```bash
gh pr create \ # aidevops-allow: raw-gh-wrapper
    --repo "$repo_slug" \
    ...
```

The `# aidevops-allow:` marker exists to whitelist this raw `gh pr create` call (worker-takeover branch can't use the wrapper because the wrapper auto-applies `origin:worker`, conflicting with `origin:worker-takeover`). The marker is correct; placement is wrong.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:215-218` — move the `# aidevops-allow:` comment to its own line ABOVE `gh pr create`, then the line continuation `\` becomes unambiguous. Pattern: comment-above-statement is the canonical shellcheck-clean form.

### Reference pattern

Other `# aidevops-allow:` markers in the codebase live above their target line. Example: search `rg -n 'aidevops-allow:' .agents/scripts/` for clean placements.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh

### Complexity Impact

One-line edit. No complexity impact.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh
# Expected: clean

.agents/scripts/version-manager.sh release patch --dry-run
# Expected: pre-flight passes (no SC2215)
```

## Acceptance

1. SC2215 cleared in `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`
2. `aidevops-allow:` marker still effective (still on/near the `gh pr create` line for the regex/scanner that consumes it)
3. ShellCheck clean across `.agents/scripts/`
4. Future `version-manager.sh release patch` does not require `--skip-preflight` for this reason

## Session Origin

Surfaced during v3.11.1 release. Pre-flight failed:

```text
.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh:218:2: warning: This flag is not handled. Use a -- to demarcate the end of options [SC2215]
```

Worked around with `--skip-preflight`. This issue tracks the proper fix.

title: t2835: ops: manual single-issue dispatch CLI for smoke-testing pulse worker dispatch
body:
## What

Add a new helper `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` that dispatches a single GitHub issue as a headless worker without going through the full pulse cycle. Useful for smoke-testing newly-filed issues, debugging dispatch failures, and validating brief worker-readiness.

## Why

There is currently no clean way to manually dispatch a worker against a specific issue. The dispatch chain (`pulse-wrapper.sh` → capacity calc → `pulse-dispatch-engine.sh` → `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` → `headless-runtime-helper.sh`) is wrapped in a long-running cycle. Smoke-testing requires either:

- Waiting up to 30 min for the next pulse cycle to scan the target repo, or
- Killing the running pulse PID (which orphans active workers), or
- Replicating the launch chain manually (brittle, undocumented).

This gap was hit in the t2828–t2831 batch when wanting to validate that the briefs were worker-ready before committing pulse capacity to four parallel attempts. A focused CLI closes the gap.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/commands/dispatch-issue.md`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/t2835-brief.md`

### Implementation

**NEW: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`** — model on `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` for the subcommand+CLI shape, and on `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:557-602` for the actual worker launch invocation.

Subcommand surface:

```text
dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <issue_number> <owner/repo> [--model <id>] [--no-claim] [--dry-run]
dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status <issue_number> <owner/repo>
dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh help
```

`dispatch` flow:

1. Source `shared-constants.sh`, `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`, `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh`, `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`.
2. Validate prerequisites:

title: t2836: aidevops badges CLI subcommand + init hook + cross-repo drift detection
body:
## Task

Wire the Phase 1 badge artifacts (#20879 / PR #20883) into a CLI surface and `aidevops init` so badge syncing is one-command across all managed repos.

## Why

Phase 1 ships the workflow, helpers, and template, but nothing ties them together yet:

- New repos created via `aidevops init` don't get the caller workflow installed
- Existing repos have no one-command way to run a drift check or apply the canonical block
- Cross-repo drift detection (`aidevops check-workflows`-style) has no analogue for README badges

This phase is the user-facing layer that makes the system usable at scale.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `bin/aidevops` — add `badges` subcommand with delegations:
  - `aidevops badges render <slug>` → calls `readme-badges-helper.sh render <slug>`
  - `aidevops badges check [--repo OWNER/REPO]` → iterates `repos.json` (or single repo) and reports drift
  - `aidevops badges sync [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--apply]` → injects the canonical block (dry-run by default)
  - `aidevops badges install [--repo OWNER/REPO] [--apply]` → installs the loc-badge caller workflow (mirror of `sync-workflows`)
  - Model on the existing `check-workflows` / `sync-workflows` dispatch in `bin/aidevops`
- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/badges-check-helper.sh` — cross-repo iterator that runs `readme-badges-helper.sh check` per repo, classifying as `CURRENT` / `DRIFTED` / `NO-README` / `LOCAL-ONLY`. Output shape: mirror `aidevops check-workflows` (text + `--json` + `--verbose`). Exit 1 if any repo is `DRIFTED`.
- **NEW:** `.agents/scripts/badges-sync-helper.sh` — sync iterator. Default `--dry-run`; `--apply` writes, commits to a branch, opens a PR per repo. Skip dirty trees and non-default-branch worktrees. Mirror `aidevops sync-workflows` exactly.
- **EDIT:** `aidevops init` flow (likely in `setup.sh` or an `init`-helper script — locate first via `grep -rn "aidevops init" bin/aidevops`) — append a step that, when invoked in a fresh repo:
  1. Copies `loc-badge-caller.yml` template into `.github/workflows/loc-badge.yml`
  2. Calls `readme-badges-helper.sh inject README.md <slug>` to seed the canonical block
  3. Reminds the user about `SYNC_PAT` if the repo isn't `local_only`
- **EDIT:** `.agents/AGENTS.md` — add a "Badge management" section near the existing workflow drift detector / sync sections (search for `check-workflows` to find the right spot). Document the four subcommands and link to `.agents/aidevops/badges.md`.

### Reference patterns to copy

- Cross-repo iterator: `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh` (or wherever `aidevops check-workflows` is implemented; locate via `grep -rn "check-workflows" .agents/scripts/ bin/`)
- PR-creating sync: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` (same locate flow)
- CLI dispatch in `bin/aidevops`: look at how `check-workflows` and `sync-workflows` cases are wired

### Verification

```bash
# Cross-repo drift detection works and respects --json
aidevops badges check
aidevops badges check --json | jq '.[] | select(.classification == "DRIFTED")'

# Single-repo render
aidevops badges render marcusquinn/aidevops | head -10

# Dry-run sync of all pulse-enabled repos
aidevops badges sync

# Apply sync to a single repo, opens a PR
aidevops badges sync --repo marcusquinn/some-repo --apply

# Init flow installs both the workflow and the README block
cd /tmp/test-repo && aidevops init
ls .github/workflows/loc-badge.yml
grep -c 'aidevops:badges:start' README.md  # expect 1

# All helpers shellcheck-clean
shellcheck .agents/scripts/badges-*.sh

# CLI integration test
aidevops badges --help  # shows subcommand summary
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `badges-check-helper.sh` outputs match `check-workflows` format (text default, `--json` + `--verbose`); exit 1 on drift
- [ ] `badges-sync-helper.sh` opens PRs in dry-run-default mode mirroring `sync-workflows`

title: t2837: document BSD awk and ratchet hazards from t2834 in reference docs
body:
## Task

Document three hazards surfaced during t2834 / PR #20883 in the reference docs so future shell-helper authors don't re-hit them.

## Why

These three hazards each cost a debug round-trip during PR #20883:

1. BSD awk (macOS default) silently rejects gawk-only constructs that pass linting and look correct
2. The string-literal ratchet trips on every new SVG/HTML/XML codegen helper
3. The positional-parameter ratchet baselines at zero for new files — existing helpers using `case "$1"` are grandfathered, new ones aren't

Memory recall catches these only if a worker queries the right keywords. Reference-doc rules survive context resets.

## How

Three exact-text edits across two reference docs. Worker may apply via `Edit` tool.

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md` — extend the GNU/BSD command-portability table (around line 164, the existing `awk dynamic regex` row) with two new rows for the awk hazards
- **EDIT:** `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md` — add a new section after the existing "Counter Safety" section (around line 158, before "Migration checklist") documenting the string-literal ratchet pattern for code-generators and the new-file ratchet behavior

### Edit 1 — bash-compat.md

**oldString:**

```text
| `awk` dynamic regex `match($0, var)` | BSD awk rejects non-literal regex | Use `gsub()` with literal patterns, or switch to `perl`. Caught production bug t1983. |
```

**newString:**

```text
| `awk` dynamic regex `match($0, var)` | BSD awk rejects non-literal regex | Use `gsub()` with literal patterns, or switch to `perl`. Caught production bug t1983. |
| `awk` 3-arg `match(str, regex, capture_array)` | BSD awk has no capture-array form (gawk-only) | Use 2-arg `match(str, regex)`, then read `RSTART`/`RLENGTH` and slice with `substr()`. Caught during t2834 / PR #20883. |
| `awk -v key="$multi_line_value"` | BSD awk rejects embedded newlines in `-v` values | Stage the multi-line content to a temp file and slurp via `BEGIN { while ((getline line < f) > 0) arr[n++] = line; close(f) }`. Caught during t2834 / PR #20883. |
```

### Edit 2 — shell-style-guide.md

**oldString:**

```text
## Migration checklist
```

**newString:**

```text
## Code-generators and the string-literal ratchet (t2834)

The string-literal ratchet (`pre-commit-hook.sh::validate_string_literals`) flags any `"..."`-quoted substring of 4+ chars that appears 3+ times in a single file, with the ratchet baselined at zero for **new** files (existing files are grandfathered at HEAD). Helpers that emit SVG, HTML, XML, or any other attribute-rich markup trip this trivially because every element repeats `width="`, `height="`, `fill="`, etc. as boundary fragments.

### Banned pattern — inline attribute fragments

Multiple `printf` calls (or one heredoc with many elements) each containing inline `attr="value"` fragments:

```bash
# Trips the ratchet — `" fill="`, `" width="`, `" height="` count >= 3
printf '  <rect x="%s" y="%s" width="%s" height="%s" fill="%s"/>\n' "$x" "$y" "$w" "$h" "$c"
printf '  <text x="%s" y="%s" font-family="%s" fill="%s">%s</text>\n' "$x" "$y" "$f" "$c" "$t"
```

### Allowed pattern — attribute-builder helpers

Build attribute strings via a single `'%s="%s" '` format template, eliminating inline fragments entirely:

```bash
_ATTR_FMT='%s="%s" '

_svg_attrs() {
    local _out=""
    while [[ $# -ge 2 ]]; do
        local _k="$1" _v="$2"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2059  # _ATTR_FMT is a trusted constant
        _out+=$(printf "$_ATTR_FMT" "$_k" "$_v")
        shift 2
    done
    printf '%s' "${_out%% }"
    return 0
}

_svg_elem() {
    local _tag="$1"; shift
    local _attrs; _attrs=$(_svg_attrs "$@")
    printf '  <%s %s/>\n' "$_tag" "$_attrs"
    return 0
}

# Usage — no inline attr= fragments, no ratchet trip
_svg_elem rect x "$x" y "$y" width "$w" height "$h" fill "$c"
```

Canonical implementation: `.agents/scripts/loc-badge-helper.sh::_svg_attrs / _svg_elem / _svg_open / _svg_close / _svg_text_elem`.

### Ratchet baseline-at-zero for new files

Every ratchet-style validator (string-literal, positional-parameter, function-complexity, nesting-depth, file-size) compares HEAD content vs staged content. For an **existing** file with pre-existing violations, the ratchet only blocks when the staged count exceeds HEAD — pre-existing debt is grandfathered.

For a **new** file, HEAD count is zero. Every violation is "new" and blocks the commit.

**Practical rule:** in a new file, follow the strict pattern from line 1. The "fix later" approach available to maintenance commits on legacy files is not available to new files.

Examples of strict patterns required from line 1 of every new shell helper:

- Positional parameters: `local _arg="$1"` always (never bare `case "$1" in` or `VAR="$2"`)
- Function arguments: `local _msg="$1"` at the top of every function body
- Repeated string fragments: extract to constants OR build via a helper template (see attribute-builder pattern above)

### Detection

Reproduce the validator locally before committing a new helper:

```bash
# Show literals that would trigger the ratchet (after the canonical sed pre-strip)
grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' your-helper.sh | sed -E '
  s/"\$[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*"//g
  s/"\$\{[^}]*\}"//g
  s/"\$@"//g
  s/"\$[0-9*#?$!-]"//g
' | grep -oE '"[^"]{4,}"' | grep -vE '^"[0-9]+\.?[0-9]*"$' | grep -vE '^"\$' | sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 >= 3' | sort -rn

# Show direct positional-parameter usage that would trigger
awk '
  { line = $0
    gsub(/\047[^\047]*\047/, "", line)
    if (line ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) next
    sub(/[[:space:]]+#.*/, "", line)
    if (line ~ /local[[:space:]].*=.*\$[1-9]/) next
    if (line ~ /\$[1-9]/) print NR ": " $0
  }
' your-helper.sh
```

Both must be empty before commit.

## Migration checklist
```

### Verification

```bash
# Files exist after edit
test -f .agents/reference/bash-compat.md
test -f .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md

# bash-compat has the two new rows
grep -c "3-arg \`match(str, regex, capture_array)\`" .agents/reference/bash-compat.md  # expect 1
grep -c "BSD awk rejects embedded newlines" .agents/reference/bash-compat.md  # expect 1

# shell-style-guide has the new section
grep -c "Code-generators and the string-literal ratchet (t2834)" .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md  # expect 1
grep -c "Ratchet baseline-at-zero for new files" .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md  # expect 1

# Markdown still lints clean
npx --yes markdownlint-cli2 .agents/reference/bash-compat.md .agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `bash-compat.md` table extended with two new awk-portability rows
- [ ] `shell-style-guide.md` has a new "Code-generators and the string-literal ratchet (t2834)" section before the existing "Migration checklist" section
- [ ] Both files lint clean with `markdownlint-cli2`
- [ ] No other files modified (Files Scope is exactly these two)

## Session Origin

interactive — followup of t2834 / PR #20883

## Files Scope

- `.agents/reference/bash-compat.md`
- `.agents/reference/shell-style-guide.md`

## Context

- Tier rationale: `tier:simple` because the brief contains verbatim oldString/newString blocks, target files are under 500 lines, and there's no design judgment — just append two table rows and one section.
- The exact patterns to document are crystallized in this issue body; the worker should not re-invent or paraphrase. Apply the diffs as written.

body:
Two-part fix to make GitHub parent-task issues consistently use the sub-issue relationship field. (A) New pulse stage runs cmd_backfill_sub_issues --issue N for every open parent-task issue per cycle, gated by AIDEVOPS_PARENT_BACKFILL_INTERVAL (default: every 6th cycle ~hourly). (B) New --parent-issue flag on claim-task-id.sh injects 'Parent: #N' into the generated body so the existing _gh_auto_link_sub_issue wrapper picks it up at create time. Together: B is the primary path, A is the self-healing safety net. Idempotent — _gh_add_sub_issue suppresses duplicate-relationship errors.

title: t2839: dispatch-issue CLI follow-ups: status PID liveness + model inference scope alignment
body:
## Task

Address two **additive** suggestions surfaced by bot reviews on PR #20887 (the manual single-issue dispatch CLI from t2835). These were correctly classified as scope-expansion (not correctness bugs in PR #20887's own code), so per the t1382 review-bot gate they were filed as a follow-up rather than expanding the parent PR.

Two independent improvements:

1. **`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status` should verify PID liveness** (gemini-medium)
2. **`_dsi_resolve_model_for_issue` should align with pulse model-inference logic** (augmentcode-medium)

## Why

**(1) PID liveness:** Today `cmd_status` reads the dispatch ledger and prints whatever PID is recorded, with no signal that the worker actually died. A user running `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status <session-key>` after a worker crash will see `pid: 12345` and assume the worker is running. The pulse's own `dispatch-ledger-helper.sh check-issue` performs `kill -0` for liveness; the manual CLI's status view should do the same so the human and the pulse agree on what's running.

**(2) Model inference alignment:** `_dsi_resolve_model_for_issue` (in `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`) reads `model:opus-4-7` / `tier:thinking` / `tier:standard` / `tier:simple` labels and returns a model id. The pulse uses a richer resolution chain (cascade context, NMR overrides, t2819 dispatch-path safety net via `dispatch-path-detector-helper.sh`, conflict-feedback re-routing). If the two paths diverge, manual dispatch can pick a different tier than what the pulse would have chosen for the same issue — defeating the goal of "make manual dispatch behave the same as pulse dispatch, just bypassing dedup."

Both are quality-of-life fixes that make the manual CLI a faithful peer of pulse dispatch. Neither blocks PR #20887 (the CLI is functional without them); both improve operator trust and reduce the "why does manual dispatch behave differently?" surface area.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
  - `cmd_status` (~line 540) — extend to check `kill -0 <pid>` and display `running` / `dead (exit ?)` / `unknown`
  - `_dsi_resolve_model_for_issue` (~line 320) — replace the local label-walking logic with a call to (or extraction from) the pulse's model-resolution code path
- **REFERENCE:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — find the model-resolution call site (`_resolve_model_for_dispatch`, `_pulse_select_model_for_issue`, or similar — locate via `grep -n "model:opus-4-7" .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`)
- **REFERENCE:** `.agents/scripts/dispatch-path-detector-helper.sh` — the t2819 safety net that bumps dispatch-path tasks to opus-4-7
- **REFERENCE:** `.agents/scripts/dispatch-ledger-helper.sh` — `check_issue` and `cmd_check_issue` already implement PID-liveness; copy that pattern (look for `kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null`)

### Approach for (1) — PID liveness in status

Current `cmd_status` flow (rough):

```bash
session_key="$1"
ledger_entry=$(dispatch-ledger-helper.sh get --session-key "$session_key")
pid=$(echo "$ledger_entry" | jq -r '.pid')
echo "PID: $pid"
```

Extend to:

```bash
if [[ -n "$pid" && "$pid" != "null" ]]; then
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        liveness="running"
    else
        liveness="dead"
    fi
    echo "PID: $pid ($liveness)"
fi
```

If the ledger has a `worker_log` path, also tail the last few lines to give the operator immediate context (`Dispatched PID:` line, last error, etc.).

### Approach for (2) — model inference alignment

Investigate the pulse's resolution path first:

```bash
grep -n "anthropic/claude" .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
grep -n "tier:" .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh | head -20
```

Likely candidates: `_pulse_select_model_for_issue`, `_resolve_dispatch_model`, or inline in `dispatch_with_dedup`. The function may be in a sourced sub-library (e.g., `pulse-dispatch-resolution.sh`).

Best-case fix: extract the pulse's resolution logic into a shared helper (`shared-model-resolution.sh` or similar) that both pulse and manual CLI source. Worst-case: have `_dsi_resolve_model_for_issue` invoke `dispatch-path-detector-helper.sh classify <files>` to mirror the t2819 safety net, then walk labels using the same precedence as pulse.

If pulse-side resolution is too tangled to share cleanly, document the divergence in `commands/dispatch-issue.md` with a warning that manual dispatch may pick a different model than pulse would.

### Verification

- `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status <key>` against a known-dead worker shows `dead` (verify by killing a worker mid-run, then running status)
- `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh status <key>` against a live worker shows `running`
- For (2): pick an issue with `tier:standard` + dispatch-path files, verify both `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <issue> --dry-run` and `pulse-wrapper.sh` (in dry-run mode if it has one, else trace the model selection) pick the SAME model
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` clean
- Existing dry-run tests in PR #20887 still pass

## Acceptance

- [ ] `cmd_status` reports PID liveness (`running` / `dead`) using `kill -0`
- [ ] `_dsi_resolve_model_for_issue` matches pulse's model selection for the same issue (or divergence is documented in `commands/dispatch-issue.md` with rationale)
- [ ] If model resolution is extracted into a shared helper, pulse-wrapper.sh sources it instead of duplicating logic
- [ ] shellcheck clean on changed files
- [ ] Brief at `todo/tasks/t2839-brief.md` references this issue

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/commands/dispatch-issue.md`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-model-resolution.sh` (NEW, optional — only if extraction is the chosen approach)
- `todo/tasks/t2839-brief.md`

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive session t2835 (PR #20887 — manual single-issue dispatch CLI). Surfaced by gemini-code-assist + augmentcode review on PR #20887. Per t1382 (Review Bot Gate § "Additive suggestion decision tree"), correctness bugs in PR's own code → fix in PR; additive scope → file as follow-up. The 5 correctness bugs were addressed in commits `ade9f42ab` and `85991f44e`; these 2 additive concerns are this issue.

Ref PR #20887.

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

Extract the pulse merge pass (`pulse-merge.sh`) into a dedicated launchd plist running every 60 seconds, decoupled from the main dispatch cycle. Currently `pulse-merge.sh` is invoked as a phase inside `pulse-wrapper.sh`, so PRs that go green at the start of a cycle wait for the full cycle (~28 min average, max 3.5h observed) before landing.

## Why

Empirical evidence over last 100 cycles (`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`):

- Median cycle duration: **1411s (23.5 min)**, mean **1703s (28.4 min)**
- 33% of cycles merge anything; total 65 PRs merged in waves of up to 6 PRs/cycle
- Plist `StartInterval=180s` is fictional — cycles overlap so consecutive ticks land back-to-back at ~23 min cadence

Result: a PR can sit MERGEABLE + green for 28 minutes after CI completes before the merge gate sees it. Decoupling drops that to ~60s deterministically, eliminates the "batchy waves" perception, and reduces user-visible latency by 20-25x.

This is independent of dispatch concurrency — even with the worker cap raised, the merge bottleneck remains.

## How

### Files to modify

- **NEW**: `.agents/templates/launchd/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-merge.plist` — model on existing `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` shape, but with `StartInterval=60` and `ProgramArguments` invoking `pulse-merge.sh` directly (not pulse-wrapper.sh).
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/install-launchd-helper.sh` (or wherever the supervisor plist install lives) — add the merge plist to the install/uninstall flow alongside the pulse plist.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — add an env-gated skip for the merge phase: when `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_PHASE_DISABLED=1` (set by setup.sh when the dedicated merge plist is installed), the dispatch cycle's merge phase is a no-op. Avoids double-execution race.
- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — ensure the entry point can be invoked standalone (not just sourced from pulse-wrapper). Add an `flock` on a separate lockdir (`~/.aidevops/locks/pulse-merge.lock`) so merge passes don't overlap themselves.
- **EDIT**: `setup.sh` and/or `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` — install both plists and toggle `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_PHASE_DISABLED` accordingly.

### Reference pattern

The existing supervisor pulse plist at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse.plist` is the template — same `Label` reverse-domain convention (`com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-merge`), same logging pattern (`StandardOutPath`/`StandardErrorPath` to `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge.log`), same `EnvironmentVariables` block.

### Files Scope

- .agents/templates/launchd/com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-merge.plist
- .agents/scripts/install-launchd-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh
- setup.sh

### Complexity Impact

- `pulse-wrapper.sh`: adds ~10 lines (env-gated phase skip). Already 2000+ lines, file-size-debt issue tracking. Mitigation: skip block is small and self-contained.
- `pulse-merge.sh`: adds standalone-invocation guard + flock setup (~15 lines). Currently ~1500 lines, well under any threshold.
- No function exceeds the 100-line `function-complexity` gate.

### Verification

```bash
# After install:
launchctl list | grep aidevops-supervisor
# Expected: both pulse and merge entries

# Confirm merge plist runs every 60s:
tail -f ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge.log
# Should see entry every ~60s

# Measure latency improvement (ground-truth):
# Pick a PR that just went green. Measure (mergedAt - last_check_completed_at).
# Pre-change: distribution skewed toward 5-28 min.
# Post-change: distribution clustered at 0-90 sec.

# No double-execution:
grep "merge_pass already in flight" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-merge.log
# Expected: zero (the lock prevents this)

# Pulse cycles drop merge work:
grep -c "phase=merge" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log
# Expected: zero new entries after the AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_PHASE_DISABLED flag is set
```

## Acceptance

1. Dedicated `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-merge` plist installed by `setup.sh` and runs every 60s.
2. Pulse-wrapper merge phase is no-op when `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_MERGE_PHASE_DISABLED=1` is set.
3. Independent flock prevents overlapping merge passes (test: trigger two manual merge-pass invocations, second blocks/skips cleanly).
4. Average time from PR-green to PR-merged drops to ≤90s (measured over 24h post-deploy via PR mergedAt vs last CI conclusion timestamp).
5. ShellCheck clean on all modified scripts.
6. Pulse cycle median duration drops by ≥20% (merge work removed from cycle).

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive concurrency analysis (2026-04-25). User question: "pulse & workers seem to be closing issues in batches in broad intervals — i'd have thought we'd use more concurrency if the dispatching was continuous." Quantified analysis confirmed cycles average 28 min, merges concentrate in waves. This is the highest-ROI fix: small surface change, immediate visible improvement.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — Sonnet. Touches multiple files (plist + 3-4 scripts), needs flock design judgment, end-to-end install integration. Not simple (>2 files, >1h estimate).

**`pulse-merge.sh` is NOT a standalone script.** Its own file header (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:30-35`) explicitly says: *"This module is sourced by pulse-wrapper.sh. It MUST NOT be executed directly — it relies on the orchestrator having sourced shared-constants.sh, worker-lifecycle-common.sh and having defined all PULSE_* configuration constants in the bootstrap section."*

The merge entry point is the function `merge_ready_prs_all_repos` (defined in pulse-merge.sh, called from `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline` at `pulse-wrapper.sh:1042`).

Skip all other phases (canary, prefetch, dispatch, sweeps, etc.).
3. The new plist `com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-merge.plist` runs `pulse-wrapper.sh --merge-only`.

title: t2840: knowledge / cases / matter framework planes (MVP)
body:
## What

Establishes a standardised framework primitive — `_knowledge/`, `_cases/` and supporting infrastructure — applicable to any aidevops-managed repo. Serves multiple matter types (code projects, business cases, limited companies, asset portfolios, customer relationships, investigations, research projects) via the same engine, parallel to existing `.agents/`, `TODO.md`, `todo/`.

**MVP scope (this parent):** 6 phases, 16 children covering knowledge plane skeleton, sensitivity classification + LLM routing, kind-aware enrichment, cases plane, email channel, and AI comms agent.

**Full design context:** see `todo/tasks/t2840-brief.md` (committed on branch `feature/t2840-knowledge-planes-mvp`, planning PR pending).

## Why

The same ingestion-index-retrieve pattern serves any long-running matter with documents around it. Building one engine means:

- Technical agents get queryable knowledge (vendor docs, recurring decisions, industry patterns)
- Business cases get evidence management + AI-drafted comms (disputes, complaints, breaches, debts)
- Limited companies get statutory document storage with audit trails
- Asset portfolios get maintenance + incident histories
- webapp t357 (file post-processing pipeline) becomes a thin SaaS layer over the same engine

Without this primitive: every repo needing document-shaped data invents its own ingestion + index + retrieval. With it: standardised, audit-trailed, sensitivity-aware, retrievable across all aidevops-managed repos via one CLI surface.

## Phases & Children (20 total)

Phases pre-filed (not auto-fired) for parallelism within phases. Cross-phase dependencies enforce ordering.

### P0 — knowledge plane skeleton (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2844 / #20896 | P0a: knowledge plane directory contract + provisioning |
| t2843 / #20895 | P0b: knowledge CLI surface (add/list/search) + platform abstraction |
| t2845 / #20897 | P0c: knowledge review gate routine + NMR integration |

### P0.5 — sensitivity + LLM routing layer (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2846 / #20899 | P0.5a: sensitivity classification schema + detector |
| t2847 / #20900 | P0.5b: LLM routing helper + audit log |
| t2848 / #20901 | P0.5c: Ollama integration + local LLM substrate |

### P1 — kind-aware enrichment (2 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2849 / #20902 | P1a: kind-aware enrichment + structured field extraction |
| t2850 / #20903 | P1c: PageIndex tree generation across corpus |


### P2 — `_inbox/` capture & triage (4 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2866 / #20930 | P2a: `_inbox/` directory contract + per-repo provisioning |
| t2867 / #20931 | P2b: inbox capture CLI + watch folder + audit log |
| t2868 / #20932 | P2c: inbox triage routine: sensitivity gate → classification → routing |
| t2869 / #20933 | P2d: pulse digest of stale inbox items + weekly review surface |

### P4 — cases plane (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2851 / #20904 | P4a: case dossier contract + `aidevops case open` |
| t2852 / #20905 | P4b: case CLI surface (attach/status/close/archive/list) |
| t2853 / #20906 | P4c: case milestone + deadline alarming routine |

### P5 — email channel (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2854 / #20908 | P5a: `.eml` ingestion handler (kind=email) |
| t2855 / #20909 | P5b: IMAP polling routine + `mailboxes.json` registry |
| t2856 / #20910 | P5c: email thread reconstruction + filter→case-attach |

### P6 — AI comms agent (2 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2857 / #20911 | P6a: `aidevops case draft` agent (RAG, human-gated, provenance) — `tier:thinking` |
| t2858 / #20912 | P6b: `aidevops case chase` (template-only, opt-in auto-send) |

## MVP Exit Criteria (when all 20 children merged)

- [ ] `aidevops knowledge add <path>` works for a PDF, a URL, an `.eml`
- [ ] `aidevops inbox add <path>` captures into `_inbox/` with audit-log entry
- [ ] `aidevops inbox triage` routes items to planes with sensitivity-first gating; privileged content never reaches cloud LLM
- [ ] `aidevops case open <slug>` creates a case dossier
- [ ] `aidevops case draft <case>` produces a draft with provenance footer (human-gated)
- [ ] `aidevops case chase <case> --template <name>` sends a template-only chaser (opt-in)
- [ ] Sensitivity classification stamps every source's `meta.json`
- [ ] LLM routing fails hard if no compliant provider for a tier
- [ ] Provisioning works in a `local_only: true` repo (no GitHub)
- [ ] Standard skeleton provisions in any new aidevops-init repo

## Cross-Phase Dependencies

- P0.5 children blocked by P0a (need plane substrate to stamp meta.json)
- P1 children blocked by P0a + P0b (need directory contract + CLI before structured extraction)
- P2a/P2b can ship in parallel with P0 (independent directory contract)
- P2c blocked by P0.5a + P0.5c (sensitivity-first triage requires local detector + Ollama)
- P2d blocked by P2c (digest reads from triage.log)
- P4 children blocked by P0a + P0b + P0.5a (cases plane uses sensitivity stamps)
- P5 children blocked by P0a + P0b + P1a (email is a kind of knowledge ingestion)
- P5c blocked by P4a + P4b (filter→case-attach uses case CLI)
- P6 blocked by P4 + P1c + P0.5b/c (drafts use cases, RAG, LLM routing)

Within each phase, children that don't depend on each other can run in parallel; children depending on others wait.

## Out of MVP Scope (post-MVP follow-on)

Filed under separate parent after MVP exit:

- **`_campaigns/` plane** — marketing/ads/outreach work. Filed as **t2870 / #20929** (peer parent-task, decomposes into 6 future phases).
- **Structured tag format (Markdoc-style)** — crosscutting content format for inline semantic tags (`{% sensitivity %}`, `{% citation %}`, `{% case-attach %}`, `{% provenance %}`) across all planes. Filed as **t2874 / #20966** (peer parent-task, 7 future phases). t2849 + t2850 ship forward-compat hooks (draft tag emission + tag-aware tree metadata) so phase 4-5 of t2874 swap parsers without re-wiring producer/consumer.
- P1b: auto-transcription pipeline (manual `.md` drops work without it)
- Additional ingestion channels: URL fetching, GH-issue ingestion (separate from `_inbox/` triage which IS in MVP)
- `_performance/` plane (KPI tracking, metrics, dashboards)
- `_feedback/` plane (capability-gap mining)
- `_projects/` plane
- `_contacts-index/` and `_accounts-index/` adapters
- Gitea/GitLab adapter implementation (abstraction layer ships in MVP, gh-only impl)
- webapp t357 SaaS layer (thin wrapper over framework engine)

## Reference

- Full design: `todo/tasks/t2840-brief.md`
- Per-child briefs: `todo/tasks/t2843-brief.md` through `todo/tasks/t2858-brief.md` (skipping t2841/t2842 which other sessions claimed); P2 phase children at `todo/tasks/t2866-brief.md` through `todo/tasks/t2869-brief.md`
- Planning PR: pending — uses `For #20892` keyword (parent stays open until all phase children merge)
- Final phase child PR: uses `Closes #20892` to close this parent

title: t2841: pulse-issue-reconcile: _b_nums unbound when issue body has no children-section
body:
## Task

Fix unbound variable error in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh::_extract_child_numbers` (line 2007). The `_b_nums` local is only assigned when the issue body contains a `## Sub-issues` (or similar) section. When the section is absent, the conditional branch at line 1997-2000 is skipped, leaving `_b_nums` unset. Line 2006-2007 then references `$_b_nums` under `set -u`, killing the function.

## Why

Observable failure in the deployed pulse log:

```
/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh: line 2007: _b_nums: unbound variable
/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh: line 2007: _b_nums: unbound variable
/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh: line 2007: _b_nums: unbound variable
```

(Three back-to-back hits, same instance — every parent-task reconcile pass for an issue without a children-section dies.)

Impact: parent-task reconciliation silently fails for any parent issue whose body lacks a `## Sub-issues` (or equivalent) section. The function returns mid-execution, so:

- Parent-task auto-close (t2442) may not detect that all children are merged
- Parent-task nudge/escalate flow (t2771/t2388) may not fire
- Source-label tracking (`graph+body+prose`) is incomplete

This is a regression — the comment at line 1990 introduced the dash-joined source-label tracking, and the `if [[ -n "$children_section" ]]` guard was added to avoid running the body-extractor on empty input. The local declaration includes `_b_nums` but never initialises it.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1990` — initialise `_b_nums=""` at declaration

### The fix (one line)

Change line 1990 from:

```bash
local _g_nums _b_nums _p_nums child_nums
```

to:

```bash
local _g_nums="" _b_nums="" _p_nums="" child_nums=""
```

This matches the pattern used elsewhere in the file (e.g., `local _src_parts=""` on line 1991) and ensures all three extractors-output variables have a defined value when the union concat runs at line 2006.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Source the script with set -u and a stubbed call
bash -c 'set -u; source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh; _extract_child_numbers 1 owner/repo "Body without children section"' 2>&1
# Should NOT output "unbound variable" — should return cleanly

# 2. Watch pulse log after deploy — no more _b_nums errors
tail -f ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log | grep _b_nums
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_b_nums`, `_g_nums`, `_p_nums`, `child_nums` all initialised to `""` at declaration
- [ ] No `unbound variable` errors in pulse-wrapper.log after deploy
- [ ] shellcheck clean on changed file

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`

## Session Origin

Discovered in interactive session t2835 (PR #20887) while investigating <webapp> PR pile-up. Bug visible in pulse-wrapper.log timestamped 2026-04-25. Three back-to-back errors per cycle suggest every reconcile pass against an issue without a children-section is hitting this.

title: t2842: full-loop-helper commit-and-pr: run project linters/formatters/typecheck before push (close worker-CI-failure gap)
body:
## Task

Add a `_run_project_validators` step to `full-loop-helper.sh::cmd_commit_and_pr` that runs the project's standard format/lint/typecheck commands BEFORE the rebase-and-push, with auto-fix where possible. Eliminates the "worker pushes code that fails CI" failure mode.

## Why

**Observable failure (interactive triage of 16 stuck <webapp> PRs, 2026-04-25):**

12 of 16 stuck PRs have at least one of `Format`, `Lint`, or `Typecheck` failing. Pattern:

| PR | Failures |
|---|---|
| #2948 | Lint, Typecheck |
| #2984 | Lint, Typecheck |
| #2991 | Lint, Typecheck |
| #3014 | Format, Lint, Typecheck |
| #3017 | Typecheck |
| #3022 | Lint |
| #3024 | Format |
| #3025 | Format |
| ... | ... |

**Root cause:** <webapp>'s `.git/hooks/pre-commit` only flushes `bd` (beads) state — it does NOT run prettier/eslint/tsc. Workers commit unvalidated code through `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`, push, CI fails 5+ minutes later. The pulse has no auto-redispatch for CI-failure-only PRs (different from conflict-feedback), so these accumulate indefinitely.

**Cost so far:** 8 PRs sitting 0-10h, each consumed 1 worker session worth of tokens to produce, all need fix-up touch from a human or another worker. Net loss of ~8 worker-sessions of work.

**Why this is the right layer:** the framework already runs through `cmd_commit_and_pr` for every worker-produced PR. Adding the validator step here catches the gap once for ALL projects, regardless of whether they have project-specific pre-commit hooks. Project-side hooks remain correct as defense-in-depth, but framework can't assume they exist.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1119` (`cmd_commit_and_pr`) — insert `_run_project_validators` call between `_stage_and_commit` (line 660) and `_rebase_and_push` (line 688)
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — add new function `_run_project_validators` near `_stage_and_commit`
- **REFERENCE:** `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` — existing aidevops linter runner; same pattern but project-aware

### Approach

Add `_run_project_validators "$skip_hooks"` step. The function:

1. **Detect project type** by file presence:
   - `package.json` with `scripts.format`/`scripts.lint`/`scripts.typecheck` → npm/pnpm/yarn project
   - `Cargo.toml` → Rust → `cargo fmt && cargo clippy && cargo check`
   - `pyproject.toml` → Python → `ruff format && ruff check && mypy` (if configured)
   - `*.go` files → `gofmt -w . && go vet`
   - None → log `[validators] no project detected, skipping` and return 0
2. **Run available auto-fixers first** (format:fix, lint:fix). Re-stage if files changed.
3. **Run check-only validators** (typecheck). Failures → return 1 with clear error pointing to the failing command and suggesting `--skip-hooks` for known-safe doc-only changes.
4. **Detect package manager** from lockfile presence (`pnpm-lock.yaml` → pnpm; `yarn.lock` → yarn; `package-lock.json` → npm).

Detection heuristic for npm-style script names (try in order, use first that exists in `package.json::scripts`):
- Format: `format:fix`, `format:write`, `prettier:fix`, `format`
- Lint: `lint:fix`, `lint:eslint:fix`, `lint`
- Typecheck: `typecheck`, `tsc`, `check:types`

### Skip / opt-out

- `--skip-hooks` arg (existing) — bypasses entirely
- `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1` env — global bypass for emergency cases
- Auto-skip if commit message starts with `wip:` (intermediate WIP commits don't need full validation)
- Auto-skip if only docs changed (`*.md`, `*.txt`, `LICENSE`) — same logic as Qlty regression gate's docs-only path

### Verification

```bash
# In <webapp> worktree, intentionally introduce a lint error
echo 'const x="bad"' >> apps/web/src/test.ts
full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 1234 --message "test: validator should catch this"
# EXPECTED: commit succeeds (auto-fix applies), or push blocked with clear error if typecheck fails

# Test bypass
full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 1234 --message "test: skip" --skip-hooks
# EXPECTED: no validator step, push proceeds

# Test no-project
cd /tmp/empty && git init && touch foo
full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 1234 --message "test: no project"
# EXPECTED: log "no project detected, skipping" and proceeds
```

### Release path

- Bump version: `version-manager.sh release patch`
- Deploy: `setup.sh --non-interactive` (auto-restarts pulse t2579)
- Monitor: watch <webapp> PRs over 24h — new PRs from workers should NOT have Format/Lint/Typecheck failures

- [ ] Typecheck step runs check-only and blocks push on failure with mentor error
- [ ] `--skip-hooks` and `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1` both bypass
- [ ] WIP commits and docs-only PRs auto-skipped

- [ ] No regression on aidevops own commits (the script already runs without project-side npm scripts)

## Why

Without a review gate, untrusted content lands directly in versioned `_knowledge/sources/` — no audit trail, no opportunity to redact PII or reject malicious payloads. The trust ladder lets self-drops and trusted sources flow without friction (95% of cases), while still gating untrusted submissions through the existing NMR + crypto-approval infrastructure (no new approval primitives — reuses what's already battle-tested).

Inbox content is gitignored; staging content is gitignored too. Only after promotion does anything enter git. This is privacy-by-default: even a momentary gitignore misconfig won't leak inbox content.

## How (Approach)

1. **Trust ladder spec** — in `_config/knowledge.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "trust": {
       "auto_promote": { "from_paths": ["~/Drops/maintainer-knowledge/"], "from_emails": ["maintainer@example.com"], "from_bots": ["my-internal-bot"] },
       "review_gate":  { "from_emails": ["partner@example.com"] },
       "untrusted":    "*"
     }
   }
   ```
2. **Review helper** — new `scripts/knowledge-review-helper.sh`:
   - `tick` subcommand: scan `_knowledge/inbox/*/meta.json`, for each:
     - Read `trust` field (set by adder per source); if `maintainer` or `trusted` → auto-promote (move to `staging/` then to `sources/`, log audit)
     - If `untrusted` → file GH issue with NMR label, move to `staging/`
   - `promote <source-id>` subcommand: explicit promotion (used by approve hook)
   - `audit-log <action> <source-id>` — append to `_knowledge/index/audit.log` (JSONL)
3. **NMR issue body template** — embed source kind, sha256, size, ingested_by, and a snippet of extracted text (first 500 chars) so reviewer can decide without leaving GitHub
4. **Crypto-approval hook** — extend `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>` (or its dispatch path in `pulse-nmr-approval.sh`) to detect knowledge-review issues (label `kind:knowledge-review`) and call `knowledge-review-helper.sh promote <source-id>` after approval
5. **Pulse integration** — append routine to `TODO.md` Routines section; pulse picks it up on next cycle. Verify with `routine-helper.sh dry-run r040`
6. **Tests** — covers auto-promotion path, NMR-file path, crypto-approval promotion, audit log correctness, idempotent tick (re-run doesn't double-process)

body:
P1c: PageIndex tree generation across corpus #framework parent:t2840

## Worker Guidance


1. **Per-source tree generation** — `knowledge-index-helper.sh build-source <id>`:
   - Read `_knowledge/sources/<id>/text.txt` (extracted text from `document-extraction-helper.sh`)
   - Call `pageindex-generator.py` with appropriate model (route via `llm-routing-helper.sh` with source's sensitivity tier)
   - Write `_knowledge/sources/<id>/tree.json`
2. **Corpus-wide aggregation** — `build` subcommand:
   - List all sources with `tree.json`; for each, take the top 2-3 levels
   - Build a meta-tree where root is "corpus" and children are sources, grouped by document kind (invoices, contracts, …) when explicit, else flat
   - Write `_knowledge/index/tree.json`
3. **Incremental rebuild** — `_should_rebuild()`:
   - Hash all source IDs + their `tree.json` mtimes; if hash matches `_knowledge/index/.tree-hash`, skip
   - Otherwise rebuild changed-only (delegating to `build-source` per changed source) and re-aggregate
4. **Query subcommand** — `knowledge-index-helper.sh query <intent>`:
   - Use `pageindex_helpers.py` tree-walk routine; the helper already returns ranked nodes with anchors
   - Output JSON: `{matches: [{source_id, score, anchor, excerpt}, …]}`
5. **Routine `r042`** — `repeat: cron(*/60 * * * *)` (hourly), `run: scripts/knowledge-index-helper.sh build`, idempotent
6. **CLI upgrade** — extend `knowledge-helper.sh search` to detect tree existence; if present, route to `knowledge-index-helper.sh query`; otherwise fall back to grep
7. **Tests** — covers per-source build, corpus build, incremental rebuild skip path, query result shape, sensitivity routing, fallback to grep when tree absent

## Task Brief


# t2850: PageIndex tree generation across corpus

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `pageindex tree rag retrieval` → existing `pageindex-generator.py` and `pageindex_helpers.py` plus skill `tools/context/pageindex.md`
- [x] Discovery: PageIndex skill is production-quality for single-document trees
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/tools/context/pageindex.md`, `.agents/scripts/pageindex-generator.py`, `.agents/scripts/pageindex_helpers.py`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — wraps existing PageIndex skill, generalises from per-doc to corpus-wide tree

## Origin

- Created: 2026-04-25
- Parent task: t2840 / GH#20892
- Phase: P1 (kind-aware enrichment)

## What

Generate a PageIndex tree over the entire `_knowledge/sources/` corpus per repo (and per personal plane). The tree gives the AI comms agent (P6a) a vectorless RAG over all promoted knowledge — query intent → tree-walk → relevant excerpts. Tree regenerates on corpus change via a routine; the v1 implementation is a thin wrapper over the existing per-document PageIndex generator.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/knowledge-index-helper.sh build` — reads all `_knowledge/sources/*/extracted.json` and `_knowledge/sources/*/text.txt`, writes a corpus-wide tree to `_knowledge/index/tree.json`
2. `scripts/knowledge-index-helper.sh query <intent>` — given a natural-language intent, walks the tree and returns ranked source IDs + excerpt anchors
3. Per-source PageIndex tree: each source gets `_knowledge/sources/<id>/tree.json` (per-doc); corpus tree at `_knowledge/index/tree.json` aggregates the top levels
4. Incremental rebuild: only rebuild when source list changes (sha-based change detection — pattern from `pulse-simplification.sh`)
5. Routine `r042` on pulse loop, runs every hour, idempotent
6. CLI integration: `aidevops knowledge search <query>` (from t2843) upgrades from substring grep to tree-walk when tree exists
7. Personal plane: separate tree at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/knowledge/index/tree.json`

## Why

Without a corpus-wide index, querying knowledge is grep — fine for v1 in t2843, useless at scale. PageIndex is vectorless (no FAISS, no embeddings infrastructure) which fits the framework's "lightweight tools first" principle. The tree-walk approach means an LLM can navigate the corpus the way a human would — by topic, then sub-topic, then document.

Building corpus-wide tree on top of per-doc trees lets an LLM agent (P6a) ask "where in the corpus is X" without scanning every document — a meaningful efficiency gain at 1000+ sources.

## How (Approach)

1. **Per-source tree generation** — `knowledge-index-helper.sh build-source <id>`:

   - Write `_knowledge/index/tree.json`

# t2853: case milestone + deadline alarming routine

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse routine cron alarming reminder` → existing pulse routines pattern in `TODO.md` `## Routines`
- [x] Discovery: `pulse-wrapper.sh` is the routine integration point; sibling routines like nightly triage already work
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`, `.agents/reference/routines.md`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — routine + reminder logic; pulse-driven, no daemon

## Origin

- Created: 2026-04-25
- Parent task: t2840 / GH#20892
- Phase: P4 (cases plane)

## What

A pulse-driven routine that reads all open cases' deadlines, classifies each by urgency (red ≤7d, amber ≤30d, green >30d), and alarms via configurable channel (default: GH issue + ntfy notification + audit log). Sub-minute latency on legal deadlines is theatre — pulse polling (5-15min) is sufficient and avoids a daemon.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh tick` — pulse-driven routine: scan all open cases' deadlines, classify, alarm if not already alarmed at this stage
2. Stage memory: `_cases/.alarm-state.json` records last-alarmed stage per (case-id, deadline-label) so re-runs don't spam
3. Config in `_config/case-alarms.json`: stages (default: `[7, 30]` days), channels (default: `["gh-issue", "ntfy"]`), per-case overrides
4. Alarm channels:
   - `gh-issue` — open a GH issue tagged `kind:case-alarm` with case-id + deadline + days-remaining; auto-close on next tick if deadline now passed or removed
   - `ntfy` — push notification (uses existing `aidevops` ntfy infrastructure if present)
   - `email` — stub for MVP (full email send arrives in P5)
5. Routine `r043` in `TODO.md` `## Routines`, repeat: `cron(*/15 * * * *)`, run: `scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh tick`
6. Manual: `aidevops case alarm-test <case-id>` — re-fires alarms once for a case (testing/debug)

## Why

Cases without deadline visibility get missed. Filing deadlines, statute-of-limitations dates, contractually-required notice periods — missing one of these has tangible cost (a dispute conceded, a contract auto-renewed, a regulatory penalty). The framework's job is to make missing them require active dismissal, not passive forgetfulness.

Pulse-based alarming (rather than a separate daemon) reuses existing infrastructure: the pulse already runs every 5 min, has lifecycle and lock primitives, and can dispatch alerts via existing channels. A separate alarm daemon would be parallel infrastructure for no functional gain.

## How (Approach)

1. **Alarm config** — `.agents/templates/case-alarms-config.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "stages_days": [30, 7, 1],
     "channels":    ["gh-issue", "ntfy"],
     "ntfy_topic":  "aidevops-case-alarms",
     "per_case_overrides": { "case-2026-0001-foo": { "stages_days": [60, 14, 3] } }
   }
   ```
2. **Alarm helper** — `scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh`:
   - `tick`: list all `_cases/case-*` (not archived); for each, read `dossier.toon.deadlines`; for each deadline, compute `days_until = (deadline_date - now)`; classify against stages (`green` if > max stage, `amber/red` between stages); for each `(case-id, deadline-label)` not yet alarmed at current stage, fire alarm; record in `.alarm-state.json`
   - `alarm-test <case-id>`: bypass stage memory, fire alarms for all deadlines once
   - `_alarm_gh-issue <case-id> <deadline> <days>` — opens GH issue, returns issue number; subsequent calls update or close the issue
   - `_alarm_ntfy <case-id> <deadline> <days>` — POST to configured ntfy topic
3. **Stage memory** — `_cases/.alarm-state.json`:
   ```json
   { "case-2026-0001-foo": { "filing-deadline-2026-08-31": "amber" } }
   ```
   On re-tick: only fire if computed-stage > recorded-stage (escalation). Auto-close GH alarm issues when deadline passes (timeline entry; alarm record cleared).
4. **GH issue lifecycle** — alarm issues use a stable title pattern (`Case alarm: <case-id> deadline <label>`) so re-tick updates rather than duplicates; closed when deadline passes or alarm cleared
5. **Routine `r043`** — append to `TODO.md` `## Routines`; pulse picks up automatically; lock-protected (only one alarm tick per cycle)
6. **Tests** — covers stage classification, no-spam (re-tick same stage), escalation (amber→red), gh-issue lifecycle, ntfy stub send, per-case override, archived cases ignored

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/templates/case-alarms-config.json`
- EDIT: `.agents/cli/aidevops` (add `case alarm-test` subcommand)
- EDIT: `TODO.md` (add `r043` routine entry — done in this task's PR)
- NEW: `.agents/tests/test-case-alarm.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/cases-plane.md` (alarming section)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `case-alarm-helper.sh tick` finds all open cases with future deadlines and classifies each by stage

## Worker Guidance


1. **`mailboxes.json` schema**:
   ```json

     "mailboxes": [
       {
         "id": "personal-icloud",
         "provider": "icloud",
         "host": "imap.mail.me.com",
         "port": 993,

   - For each configured mailbox: connect, login, select folder
   - `UID FETCH <last+1>:* (RFC822 UID)` to get new messages since last-seen UID
   - For each fetched message: write `.eml` to `_knowledge/inbox/email-<mailbox-id>-<uid>.eml`
   - Update state with new high-watermark UID
   - Bash wrapper `email-poll-helper.sh tick` orchestrates iteration over all mailboxes, error handling, lock-protection
3. **Credential resolution** — `_resolve_password(password_ref)`:
   - If `password_ref` starts with `gopass:` → call `gopass show <path>` (silent, no echo)
   - Otherwise treat as a literal env-var name to look up
   - Never log resolved password value

   - `add` — interactive: prompt for provider (auto-fill host/port from `email-providers.json.txt`), user, gopass path; tests connection
   - `list` — table of mailboxes with last-polled-at, last-error
   - `test <id>` — fetch 1 message without committing state (dry-run)
   - `remove <id>` — un-register
5. **Routine `r044`** — pulse picks it up; lock-protected (one poll per cycle); errors fail open (log + continue, don't crash pulse)

body:
P5c: email thread reconstruction + filter to case-attach #framework parent:t2840

## Worker Guidance


1. **Thread reconstruction** — `email_thread.py`:
   - For each email source, read `meta.json` for `message_id`, `in_reply_to`, `references`
   - Build threads via JWZ: parent-link from `in_reply_to`, fall back to last `references` entry; subject-merge for orphans (normalise: strip `Re:`, `Fwd:`, lowercase, trim)
   - Each thread gets `_knowledge/index/email-threads/<thread-id>.json`: `{thread_id, root_subject, participants, sources: [{source_id, message_id, date, from}, …]}`
   - Re-runs are incremental: re-thread only sources whose meta changed since last build (via mtime)
2. **Filter ruleset** — `_config/email-filters.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "rules": [
       {
         "name": "Dispute counsel correspondence",
         "match": {
           "from_contains": "dispute-counsel@example.com",
           "subject_contains_any": ["Re: Dispute"]
         },
         "actions": [
           { "attach_to_case": "case-2026-0001-dispute-acme", "role": "evidence" },
           { "set_sensitivity": "privileged" }
         ]
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
3. **Filter helper** — `scripts/email-filter-helper.sh`:
   - `tick`: list email sources promoted since last filter run; for each, evaluate rules; on match, run actions (call `case-helper.sh attach`, optionally `sensitivity-detector-helper.sh override`); audit-log per case
   - `add` — interactive add of new filter rule
   - `test <rule-name>`: against last 50 email sources, show what would match without actions firing
   - `list`: show all rules with hit counts
4. **Filter state** — `_knowledge/.email-filter-state.json` records last-processed source ID per filter run (no double-processing)
5. **Routine `r045`** — pulse picks up; lock-protected; idempotent
6. **Match semantics** — start simple: `from_contains`, `from_equals`, `subject_contains_any`, `subject_matches_regex`, `body_contains`, `has_attachment_kind: <doc-type>`. Combine with `AND` semantics (all conditions must match). Negation operators come post-MVP.
7. **Tests** — covers thread reconstruction (orphan, root, multiple branches), filter match (each predicate kind), filter actions (attach, sensitivity override), no-double-process, filter `test` dry-run mode

# t2856: email thread reconstruction + filter→case-attach

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `email thread reconstruction in-reply-to references` → no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery: existing sieve config at `.agents/configs/email-sieve-config.json.txt`; thread semantics standard (RFC 5322 + JWZ algorithm)

## Origin

- Created: 2026-04-25
- Parent task: t2840 / GH#20892
- Phase: P5 (email channel)

## What

Two related capabilities that together close the email→cases loop:

1. **Thread reconstruction** — given the corpus of email sources, build a thread index using `In-Reply-To`, `References`, and subject heuristics (JWZ algorithm). Each thread becomes a queryable entity at `_knowledge/index/email-threads/<thread-id>.json` listing constituent source IDs in chronological order
2. **Filter → case-attach** — sieve-style rules in `_config/email-filters.json` that match incoming emails (post-ingestion) against rules; matching emails get attached to the configured case via `case-helper.sh attach` automatically. Audit-logged.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/email-thread-helper.sh build` — JWZ-style thread reconstruction over all email sources
2. `scripts/email-thread-helper.sh thread <message-id>` — returns thread ID + ordered constituent source IDs
3. `scripts/email-filter-helper.sh tick` — pulse-driven routine: scan recently-promoted email sources, match against filter rules, auto-attach to cases
4. `_config/email-filters.json` — sieve-style ruleset: `from`, `subject_contains`, `body_matches`, → `attach_to_case: <case-id>`, `set_role: evidence|reference`, `set_sensitivity: <tier>`
5. Routine `r045` in `TODO.md`, repeat: `cron(*/15 * * * *)`, run: `scripts/email-filter-helper.sh tick`
6. Audit log at `_cases/<case-id>/comms/email-attach.jsonl` per case
7. CLI: `aidevops email thread <message-id>`, `aidevops email filter add|list|test`

## Why

Without thread reconstruction, an email corpus is a flat list of disconnected messages — useless for case work where the conversation arc matters. JWZ-style threading is the de-facto standard (used by Thunderbird, Gmail, etc.) and works on `In-Reply-To` + `References` + subject normalisation.

Filter-based auto-attach is the productivity killer: a maintainer can configure "any email from `dispute-counsel@example.com` mentioning case slug XYZ → attach to case XYZ as evidence" and never manually attach again. Without filters, every incoming email needs human triage; with them, only the unmatched residue does.

The sieve-style ruleset format is familiar to anyone who's used Procmail/Sieve/Gmail filters; reusing the mental model lowers learning cost.

## How (Approach)

1. **Thread reconstruction** — `email_thread.py`:
   - For each email source, read `meta.json` for `message_id`, `in_reply_to`, `references`
   - Build threads via JWZ: parent-link from `in_reply_to`, fall back to last `references` entry; subject-merge for orphans (normalise: strip `Re:`, `Fwd:`, lowercase, trim)
   - Each thread gets `_knowledge/index/email-threads/<thread-id>.json`: `{thread_id, root_subject, participants, sources: [{source_id, message_id, date, from}, …]}`
   - Re-runs are incremental: re-thread only sources whose meta changed since last build (via mtime)
2. **Filter ruleset** — `_config/email-filters.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "rules": [
       {
         "name": "Dispute counsel correspondence",
         "match": {
           "from_contains": "dispute-counsel@example.com",
           "subject_contains_any": ["Re: Dispute"]
         },
         "actions": [
           { "attach_to_case": "case-2026-0001-dispute-acme", "role": "evidence" },
           { "set_sensitivity": "privileged" }
         ]
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
3. **Filter helper** — `scripts/email-filter-helper.sh`:
   - `tick`: list email sources promoted since last filter run; for each, evaluate rules; on match, run actions (call `case-helper.sh attach`, optionally `sensitivity-detector-helper.sh override`); audit-log per case
   - `add` — interactive add of new filter rule
   - `test <rule-name>`: against last 50 email sources, show what would match without actions firing
   - `list`: show all rules with hit counts
4. **Filter state** — `_knowledge/.email-filter-state.json` records last-processed source ID per filter run (no double-processing)
5. **Routine `r045`** — pulse picks up; lock-protected; idempotent
6. **Match semantics** — start simple: `from_contains`, `from_equals`, `subject_contains_any`, `subject_matches_regex`, `body_contains`, `has_attachment_kind: <doc-type>`. Combine with `AND` semantics (all conditions must match). Negation operators come post-MVP.
7. **Tests** — covers thread reconstruction (orphan, root, multiple branches), filter match (each predicate kind), filter actions (attach, sensitivity override), no-double-process, filter `test` dry-run mode

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/email-filter-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/templates/email-filters-config.json` (default `_config/email-filters.json`)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `email-thread-helper.sh build` reconstructs threads across email corpus and writes `_knowledge/index/email-threads/<id>.json`
- [ ] `aidevops email thread <message-id>` returns thread ID + chronological source list
- [ ] Orphan emails (no `In-Reply-To`/`References`, unique subject) get their own single-source thread
- [ ] Subject-merged threading: emails with `Subject: Foo` and `Re: Foo` link as same thread when no `In-Reply-To`

Drafts are **always human-gated** — the helper writes to `_cases/<case-id>/drafts/<timestamp>-<intent-slug>.md` and never auto-sends.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/case-draft-helper.sh draft <case-id> --intent "..." [flags]` — generates draft, writes to drafts/, opens preview
2. Default scope: only `_knowledge/sources/<id>/` for sources in this case's `sources.toon`. Cross-case access via `--include-case <id>` (logged in `_cases/<case-id>/comms/cross-case-access.jsonl` for audit)

Cross-case privilege firewall is critical for matters with multiple unrelated cases — bleed of one case's privileged content into another case's draft is a discovery nightmare. Requiring explicit `--include-case` opt-in + audit log makes cross-case retrieval a deliberate, traceable act.

P6b: aidevops case chase (template-only, opt-in auto-send) #framework parent:t2840

## Worker Guidance


1. **Template format** — `_config/case-chase-templates/payment-reminder.eml.tmpl`:
   ```
   From: {{sender_email}}
   To: {{recipient_email}}
   Subject: Reminder: invoice {{invoice_number}} dated {{invoice_date}}
   
   Dear {{recipient_name}},
   
   This is a reminder that invoice {{invoice_number}} dated {{invoice_date}} for {{currency}} {{amount}} 
   remains outstanding. The original due date was {{due_date}}.
   
   Please advise on the status of this payment.
   
   Regards,
   {{sender_name}}
   ```
2. **Field resolution** — `case-chase-helper.sh _resolve_fields(case-id, template, recipient)`:
   - From dossier: `parties`, `kind`, `case_id`, `parties_self`, `parties_recipient`
   - From attached invoice (if any in `sources.toon` with `kind: invoice`): `invoice_number`, `invoice_date`, `due_date`, `amount`, `currency` (read from invoice's `extracted.json` from t2849)
   - From mailbox config: `sender_email`, `sender_name`
   - From `--to` flag or auto-detected recipient party email: `recipient_email`, `recipient_name`
   - Validate ALL fields resolved before substitution; missing field → exit 1 with explicit list
3. **Opt-in check** — read `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled`; if missing or false, exit 1 unless `--force` (which still requires `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled: false-with-force-allowed` — even more deliberate)
4. **SMTP send** — Python script `email_send.py` using stdlib `smtplib` + `email` module:
   - Connect to SMTP host (from `mailboxes.json` mailbox-id), STARTTLS
   - Auth with credentials from gopass
   - Compose `EmailMessage` from substituted template
   - Send, capture message-id
   - Return `{message_id, sent_at}` JSON
5. **Audit + timeline** — on success:
   - Append to `_cases/<case>/comms/sent.jsonl`: full record
   - `case-helper.sh _timeline_append <case> "comm" "{kind: chase, template, recipient, message_id}"`
6. **Failure handling** — bounce/SMTP error:
   - First failure: log to `comms/sent.jsonl` with `status: error`, `error: <message>`, retry-allowed
   - Configurable retry: `case-chase-helper.sh retry <case-id> <message-id>` for manual retry
   - Two consecutive failures on same case: set case status to `hold` and fire alarm via t2853 via direct `case-alarm-helper.sh fire <case-id> --reason "chase send failure"`
7. **Template management** — `chase-template add|list|test`:
   - `add` opens editor on a fresh template, validates RFC 5322 + placeholder syntax
   - `test --case <case-id> --template <name>`: dry-run substitution, output to stdout (no send)
   - `list`: shows all templates with description (first comment line)
8. **Tests** — covers happy path send (with mocked SMTP), missing-fields rejection, opt-in gating, dry-run no-send, retry, bounce-failure → hold transition

- Created: 2026-04-25
- Parent task: t2840 / GH#20892
- Phase: P6 (AI comms agent)

## What

`aidevops case chase <case-id> --template <name>` sends a routine chaser email built from a template (no LLM at send time, only verified-data field substitution). Per-case opt-in via `dossier.toon: chasers_enabled: true`. Template library in `_config/case-chase-templates/<name>.eml.tmpl`. Send routes through SMTP credentials in gopass. Sent chasers are recorded in case timeline + `comms/sent.jsonl`.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/case-chase-helper.sh send <case-id> --template <name> [--to <email>] [--dry-run]` — substitutes data fields, sends via SMTP, records timeline
2. Templates at `_config/case-chase-templates/<name>.eml.tmpl` — RFC 5322 format with `{{field}}` placeholders
3. Field substitution: only verified data from dossier (parties, deadlines, attached invoice numbers, amounts, dates) — NEVER LLM-generated content
4. Opt-in gating: `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled` must be `true`; otherwise `chase` exits 1 with message
5. SMTP integration: credentials from gopass per `_config/mailboxes.json` (reuse t2855 mailbox config)
6. Send audit: `_cases/<case-id>/comms/sent.jsonl` records timestamp, template, recipient, message-id, sent-via mailbox-id; timeline entry too
7. CLI: `aidevops case chase <case-id> --template <name>`; `aidevops case chase-template add|list|test`
8. Bounce handling (MVP): if SMTP send fails, log error + retry once; second failure marks case status:hold + alarms via t2853

## Why

Most case work has routine touchpoints — "where's the invoice", "deadline reminder", "have you received this", "please confirm receipt". AI-drafted comms (P6a) for these is overkill and risks template drift. Template-only chasers handle the boring 80% with zero risk of LLM-introduced errors, and free human attention for the strategic 20% that P6a serves.

Opt-in per case is critical: some cases (e.g., active dispute) the user might not want auto-chase. Defaults are `chasers_enabled: false`, so explicit enabling is required.

LLM-free at send time is the safety guarantee: the human reviewed the template once when authoring it, the substitution is deterministic, the send is reproducible. No "LLM generated unexpected text in chaser" failure mode.

## How (Approach)

1. **Template format** — `_config/case-chase-templates/payment-reminder.eml.tmpl`:
   ```
   From: {{sender_email}}
   To: {{recipient_email}}
   Subject: Reminder: invoice {{invoice_number}} dated {{invoice_date}}
   
   Dear {{recipient_name}},
   
   This is a reminder that invoice {{invoice_number}} dated {{invoice_date}} for {{currency}} {{amount}} 
   remains outstanding. The original due date was {{due_date}}.
   
   Please advise on the status of this payment.
   
   Regards,
   {{sender_name}}
   ```
2. **Field resolution** — `case-chase-helper.sh _resolve_fields(case-id, template, recipient)`:
   - From dossier: `parties`, `kind`, `case_id`, `parties_self`, `parties_recipient`
   - From attached invoice (if any in `sources.toon` with `kind: invoice`): `invoice_number`, `invoice_date`, `due_date`, `amount`, `currency` (read from invoice's `extracted.json` from t2849)
   - From mailbox config: `sender_email`, `sender_name`
   - From `--to` flag or auto-detected recipient party email: `recipient_email`, `recipient_name`
   - Validate ALL fields resolved before substitution; missing field → exit 1 with explicit list
3. **Opt-in check** — read `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled`; if missing or false, exit 1 unless `--force` (which still requires `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled: false-with-force-allowed` — even more deliberate)
4. **SMTP send** — Python script `email_send.py` using stdlib `smtplib` + `email` module:
   - Connect to SMTP host (from `mailboxes.json` mailbox-id), STARTTLS
   - Auth with credentials from gopass
   - Compose `EmailMessage` from substituted template
   - Send, capture message-id
   - Return `{message_id, sent_at}` JSON
5. **Audit + timeline** — on success:
   - Append to `_cases/<case>/comms/sent.jsonl`: full record
   - `case-helper.sh _timeline_append <case> "comm" "{kind: chase, template, recipient, message_id}"`
6. **Failure handling** — bounce/SMTP error:
   - First failure: log to `comms/sent.jsonl` with `status: error`, `error: <message>`, retry-allowed
   - Configurable retry: `case-chase-helper.sh retry <case-id> <message-id>` for manual retry
   - Two consecutive failures on same case: set case status to `hold` and fire alarm via t2853 via direct `case-alarm-helper.sh fire <case-id> --reason "chase send failure"`
7. **Template management** — `chase-template add|list|test`:
   - `add` opens editor on a fresh template, validates RFC 5322 + placeholder syntax
   - `test --case <case-id> --template <name>`: dry-run substitution, output to stdout (no send)
   - `list`: shows all templates with description (first comment line)
8. **Tests** — covers happy path send (with mocked SMTP), missing-fields rejection, opt-in gating, dry-run no-send, retry, bounce-failure → hold transition

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/case-chase-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/email_send.py`
- NEW: `.agents/templates/case-chase-templates/{payment-reminder,deadline-reminder,receipt-acknowledge}.eml.tmpl` (3 starter templates)
- EDIT: `.agents/cli/aidevops` (add `case chase` and `case chase-template` subcommand groups)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/case-helper.sh` (initialise dossier with `chasers_enabled: false` by default)
- NEW: `.agents/tests/test-case-chase.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/cases-plane.md` (chasing section + opt-in policy)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `aidevops case chase <case-id> --template payment-reminder` substitutes fields, sends email, records timeline + sent.jsonl
- [ ] Case with `chasers_enabled: false`: chase exits 1 with friendly message
- [ ] Missing dossier field (e.g., no invoice attached, template needs invoice_number): chase exits 1 with explicit list of missing fields, NO partial send
- [ ] `--dry-run` outputs the substituted email to stdout, no SMTP call
- [ ] Sent email records full message_id in audit log; recoverable in case timeline `show`
- [ ] LLM is never invoked during send (no `llm-routing-helper.sh` calls in this helper)
- [ ] SMTP send failure: first failure logs error + retry-allowed; second failure transitions case to `hold` + fires alarm
- [ ] `aidevops case chase-template test --case <id> --template <name>`: dry-run substitution shows the would-send email
- [ ] `aidevops case chase-template list` shows all templates with description
- [ ] Adding new template: opens editor, validates RFC 5322 + placeholder syntax before saving
- [ ] Credentials never logged or appear in any output (verifiable by grep over logs)
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations; Python `py_compile` passes
- [ ] Tests pass: `bash .agents/tests/test-case-chase.sh`
- [ ] Documentation: chasing + opt-in policy in `.agents/aidevops/cases-plane.md`

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** t2851 (P4a — dossier with `chasers_enabled` field), t2852 (P4b — case-helper.sh timeline functions), t2849 (P1a — extracted.json invoice fields), t2855 (P5b — `mailboxes.json` for SMTP creds), t2853 (P4c — alarming integration on consecutive failures)
- **Soft-blocked by:** none (template-only, no RAG dependency)
- **Blocks:** none (final P6 leaf — closes MVP)

## Reference

- Parent brief: `todo/tasks/t2840-brief.md` § "AI comms agent" → strategic vs routine split
- Email config substrate: `.agents/configs/email-providers.json.txt` (SMTP host/port; reuse for sending)
- Pattern: similar to git hook templates — known structure, opt-in placement, deterministic firing
- Counterpart: t2857 (P6a) handles the LLM-drafted strategic side; this is the deterministic routine side
