## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-25
- **Session:** Claude Code interactive session (t2840 P2 phase)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Parent task:** t2840 / GH#20892
- **Conversation context:** GTD-failure-mode mitigation. Without active surfacing of stale items, `_inbox/` becomes a dumping ground that never gets sorted (the canonical "inbox zero" failure). Pulse digest pushes the user the oldest items so they don't get lost.

## What

Implements `aidevops inbox digest [--age-days N]` — reports the oldest unsorted/needs-review items in `_inbox/` across all repos plus the workspace-level inbox. Runs as a pulse routine producing a weekly digest (configurable interval) that surfaces in the session greeting / stale-claim scan output.

Two surfaces:

1. **CLI:** `aidevops inbox digest` — interactive query, returns top N stale items.
2. **Pulse routine:** runs weekly; if stale items > threshold, posts an advisory in `~/.aidevops/advisories/inbox-stale-{repo-slug}.advisory` so the next interactive session greeting includes a nudge.

After completion:

- Items in `_inbox/_drop/` or `_inbox/_needs-review/` older than `age-days` (default 7) surface as stale.
- Pulse posts advisories in repos with stale items.
- User running `aidevops inbox digest` sees a list with file path, age, sub-folder, and any prior triage attempt notes.

## Why

Inbox without escalation = abandoned items. Users need a passive nudge ("you have 14 items > 7 days old in `_inbox/`") rather than having to remember to check.

Advisory mechanism reuses the existing `~/.aidevops/advisories/` flow already used for security and update advisories — consistent UX, no new surface.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`. Pure reporting on existing data — no LLM calls, no destructive operations.

## PR Conventions

Child of parent-task t2840. Use `For #20892`.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/inbox-helper.sh` — add `digest` subcommand.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/inbox-digest-routine.sh` — pulse-callable; writes advisories.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops` — wire `aidevops inbox digest`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` — surface inbox advisories in session greeting alongside existing advisory types.

### Implementation Steps

1. `inbox-helper.sh digest [--age-days N] [--repo PATH] [--include-workspace] [--json]`:
   - Walk `_inbox/_drop/` and `_inbox/_needs-review/` for files older than `--age-days`
   - Cross-reference with `triage.log` to get any prior routing attempt notes
   - Output sorted by age desc, columns: `age_days  sub_folder  file_path  prior_attempts`
   - `--json` for machine-readable output (used by routine)

2. `inbox-digest-routine.sh`:
   - Iterate all `pulse: true` repos in `repos.json` plus workspace inbox
   - For each, run `inbox-helper.sh digest --json --age-days 7 --include-workspace`
   - If count > 0: write `~/.aidevops/advisories/inbox-stale-{repo-slug}-{ts}.advisory` with the digest
   - If count == 0: clean up any existing stale advisories for that repo (resolved)
   - Schedule: weekly default (configurable via env `AIDEVOPS_INBOX_DIGEST_INTERVAL_HOURS`, default 168)

3. Greeting integration:
   - `aidevops-update-check.sh` already reads `~/.aidevops/advisories/*.advisory` for session greeting
   - Inbox advisories follow the same format (just a different filename prefix)
   - Dismiss mechanism: `aidevops security dismiss inbox-stale-{slug}` (reuses existing advisory dismissal)

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** none (new file + small CLI extension)
- **Estimated growth:** ~150 lines total
- **Action required:** None.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/inbox-helper.sh .agents/scripts/inbox-digest-routine.sh

# Sanity: drop a stale file, run digest
touch -t 202604010000 _inbox/_drop/old.txt  # 25+ days old
aidevops inbox digest --age-days 7
# Expected: shows old.txt with age ~25 days

# Pulse routine produces advisory
.agents/scripts/inbox-digest-routine.sh
ls ~/.aidevops/advisories/inbox-stale-*.advisory
# Expected: at least one file
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/inbox-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/inbox-digest-routine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `aidevops inbox digest` lists stale items sorted by age.
- [ ] `--age-days N` and `--include-workspace` flags work.
- [ ] Pulse routine runs weekly and writes advisories when stale items exist.
- [ ] Advisories surface in session greeting alongside existing types.
- [ ] Advisories self-clear when stale items go to zero.
- [ ] Dismissal via existing `aidevops security dismiss` mechanism works.
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean.

## Context & Decisions

- **Why advisory reuse vs new mechanism:** consistent UX. Users already know how to dismiss advisories. Inbox-stale is just another kind.
- **Why weekly default:** daily nudges are noise; monthly is too easy to ignore. Weekly matches the GTD weekly-review cadence.
- **Why include workspace inbox:** captures-not-tied-to-repo can otherwise vanish. Including the workspace inbox in digest closes that gap.
- **Why surface count, not contents in greeting:** privacy. Greeting may be visible to others; just shows count + slug. User runs `aidevops inbox digest` to see actual filenames.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` — advisory reader
- `~/.aidevops/advisories/` — advisory store
- `.agents/configs/repos.json` — pulse-enabled repo iteration
- `t2867-brief.md` — capture produces files; this surfaces unprocessed ones

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** t2868 (P2c — needs `triage.log` populated to cross-reference prior attempts; can ship without if we accept "no prior attempts" for items)
- **Blocks:** none directly; closes the inbox-zero failure-mode mitigation
- **External:** none

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 30m | review existing advisory mechanism |
| Implementation | 2h | digest subcommand + routine + advisory wiring |
| Testing | 1h | manual verification + smoke test |
| **Total** | **~3.5h** | |

title: <webapp> canonical worktree conflict — manual intervention required
body:
## Issue redacted for privacy (t2871)

This issue was auto-filed by `pulse-canonical-recovery.sh` (introduced in PR
#20928) and contained a filesystem path that exposed information about the
affected user's local machine — username, drive topology, and a local repo
name. That advisory describes user-local state (a stash conflict on the
user's canonical worktree) which **only the affected user can resolve** —
maintainers cannot act on it, so cloud filing was the wrong channel as
well as a privacy bug.

The body has been redacted to remove the leaked paths and prevent further
indexing by GitHub search.

## Fix

PR #20945 switches `pulse-canonical-recovery.sh` to write to the local
advisory channel (`~/.aidevops/advisories/canonical-recovery-<repo>.advisory`)
which is surfaced in the session-start TUI toast — the same channel used
for security advisories and SYNC_PAT setup hints. Subsequent canonical-
recovery failures will appear in the affected user's own terminal, never
on GitHub.

A `_pcr_sanitise_path` helper was added as defence-in-depth: any future
code path that handles `${repo_path}` for non-local output will substitute
`$HOME/...` → `~/...`, `/Users/<name>/...` → `/Users/<user>/...`, and
similar — so a regression that re-introduces cloud filing won't re-leak
the same data.

## What to do if you saw the original advisory

Run the recovery commands in your **own terminal** (not in an AI chat):

```bash
# Replace <path> with your canonical repo path — DO NOT paste into chat:
cd <path>
git status
git merge --abort 2>/dev/null || true
git stash list | grep pulse-auto-stash
git stash pop          # or: git stash drop
git fetch origin
```

title: TBD: pulse-canonical-recovery: handle stale-UU state without active merge
body:
## Session Origin

Discovered while resolving the t2865 advisory at #20934. The recovery script worked as designed for the canonical "UU + active merge" case but failed at `stash-push-failed` when the conflict was a stale UU state with no active merge (`.git/MERGE_HEAD` already absent — git crashed mid-resolve).

## What

Add stale-UU recovery branch to `pulse-canonical-recovery.sh`:

When `_pcr_check_state()` returns `unmerged` AND `.git/MERGE_HEAD`, `.git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `.git/REBASE_HEAD` are all absent, the index has stale unmerged entries from a crashed prior op. Try `git merge --abort` (no-op if no merge; clears UU otherwise), then `git reset --merge HEAD` as fallback, then retry stash + pull.

## Why

The first manual recovery I did was `git reset --hard origin/develop` after exhausting safer options, which is a content-loss path (would have nuked uncommitted local work). Adding the stale-UU branch gives the script a content-safe recovery path for this specific failure mode without escalating to advisory-only when an automatic resolution exists.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-recovery.sh::_pcr_recover_repo` — add stale-UU detection and `git merge --abort` retry before the existing stash branch
- EDIT: `~/Git/aidevops/.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery.sh` — add synthetic test that creates UU state via `git update-index --index-info` without `MERGE_HEAD`

### Reference pattern

The existing `_pcr_recover_repo` function already handles the `unmerged` state path. New logic inserts BEFORE the stash attempt:

```bash
if [[ "$state" == "unmerged" ]]; then
    if [[ ! -e "${repo_path}/.git/MERGE_HEAD" \
       && ! -e "${repo_path}/.git/CHERRY_PICK_HEAD" \
       && ! -e "${repo_path}/.git/REBASE_HEAD" ]]; then
        # Stale UU from a crashed merge. Safe to abort.
        _pcr_log "stale-UU detected (no active merge); attempting merge --abort"
        if git -C "$repo_path" merge --abort 2>/dev/null \
           || git -C "$repo_path" reset --merge HEAD 2>/dev/null; then
            _pcr_log "stale-UU cleared via merge --abort"
            # Re-check state — should now be "dirty" or "clean"
            state=$(_pcr_check_state "$repo_path")
        fi
    fi
fi
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-recovery.sh`

### Verification

```bash
# Synthetic stale-UU test
cd /tmp && rm -rf stale-uu-test && mkdir stale-uu-test && cd stale-uu-test
git init && echo "v1" > foo && git add foo && git commit -m "init"
# Create stale UU state without MERGE_HEAD
git update-index --index-info <<EOM
100644 $(echo "v1" | git hash-object -w --stdin) 1	foo
100644 $(echo "v2" | git hash-object -w --stdin) 2	foo
100644 $(echo "v3" | git hash-object -w --stdin) 3	foo
EOM
# Verify UU exists but no MERGE_HEAD
git status --short  # expect: UU foo
ls .git/MERGE_HEAD  # expect: not exist

# Run recovery — should succeed via merge --abort path
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-canonical-recovery.sh /tmp/stale-uu-test
# Expected: "stale-UU cleared via merge --abort" then "no recovery needed"
```

### Complexity Impact

`_pcr_recover_repo` is currently ~40 lines. Adding stale-UU branch: +~12 lines. Will land at ~52 lines, well below 100-line gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_pcr_recover_repo` detects stale-UU state (unmerged + no merge head files) and attempts `git merge --abort` before stash
2. Synthetic test creates and recovers from stale-UU without manual intervention
3. Existing tests still pass (no regression on active-merge path)
4. Audit log shows distinct event for stale-UU recovery vs standard stash recovery

#framework #pulse #reliability #priority:medium #no-auto-dispatch #interactive

title: [REDACTED] request-handler canonical worktree conflict — manual intervention required
body:
## Issue redacted for privacy (t2871)

This issue was auto-filed by `pulse-canonical-recovery.sh` (introduced in PR
#20928) and contained a filesystem path that exposed information about the
affected user's local machine — username, drive topology, and a local repo
name. That advisory describes user-local state (a stash conflict on the
user's canonical worktree) which **only the affected user can resolve** —
maintainers cannot act on it, so cloud filing was the wrong channel as
well as a privacy bug.

The body has been redacted to remove the leaked paths and prevent further
indexing by GitHub search.

## Fix

PR #20945 switches `pulse-canonical-recovery.sh` to write to the local
advisory channel (`~/.aidevops/advisories/canonical-recovery-<repo>.advisory`)
which is surfaced in the session-start TUI toast — the same channel used
for security advisories and SYNC_PAT setup hints. Subsequent canonical-
recovery failures will appear in the affected user's own terminal, never
on GitHub.

A `_pcr_sanitise_path` helper was added as defence-in-depth: any future
code path that handles `${repo_path}` for non-local output will substitute
`$HOME/...` → `~/...`, `/Users/<name>/...` → `/Users/<user>/...`, and
similar — so a regression that re-introduces cloud filing won't re-leak
the same data.

## What to do if you saw the original advisory

Run the recovery commands in your **own terminal** (not in an AI chat):

```bash
# Replace <path> with your canonical repo path — DO NOT paste into chat:
cd <path>
git status
git merge --abort 2>/dev/null || true
git stash list | grep pulse-auto-stash
git stash pop          # or: git stash drop
git fetch origin
git pull --ff-only
```

Closing as not-planned — the underlying recovery condition is real but
should now be reported via your local advisory channel.

See PR #20945 and t2871 for the channel switch and the path-sanitiser helper.

Scripts that auto-file framework advisories to public marcusquinn/aidevops (notably pulse-canonical-recovery.sh) interpolate raw repo paths and basenames into title and body via gh_create_issue. The existing privacy-guard-pre-push.sh hook only covers git pushes — not GitHub API calls — so private repo names leak when pulse files an advisory about a private canonical repo. title: interactive-session-helper.sh::_isc_cmd_claim() missing auto-dispatch guard — creates permanent dispatch block
body:
## Description

`_isc_cmd_claim()` applies `status:in-review` + self-assignment unconditionally. When called on an issue that carries the `auto-dispatch` label, this creates the `(origin:interactive + assignee)` combination that `_has_active_claim()` in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:522` treats as an active claim — permanently blocking pulse dispatch per GH#18352/t1996.

Three creation-time guards already correctly skip self-assignment and auto-claim for auto-dispatch issues:

| Guard | Location | Task ID |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `_auto_assign_issue()` | `claim-task-id-issue.sh:66` | t2218 |
| `_interactive_session_auto_claim_new_task()` | `claim-task-id-issue.sh:239` | t2132 |
| `gh_create_issue()` | `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:537` | t2157/t2406 |

The direct `claim` subcommand bypasses all three. The post-merge heal (`_isc_post_merge_heal_stale_self_assign`) also cannot fix the resulting state — it explicitly skips issues with `status:in-review` (line 1335), which `claim` applies.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:**
```bash
interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug>
# where issue <N> carries the auto-dispatch label
```

**Actual output:** Claim applied — `status:in-review` + self-assignment stamped on an `auto-dispatch` issue.

**Expected output:** Warning that the issue has `auto-dispatch`, claim skipped.

**Causal code:**
`interactive-session-helper.sh:410-427` — no label inspection before applying `set_issue_status "in-review"`.

**Call-site sweep:** The only unguarded path. All other paths (`_auto_assign_issue`, `_interactive_session_auto_claim_new_task`, `gh_create_issue`) have guards.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From an interactive session, create an auto-dispatch issue via `claim-task-id.sh --labels auto-dispatch`
2. Creation-time guards correctly skip self-assign and auto-claim
3. Agent then calls `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug>` on the same issue
4. `status:in-review` + self-assignment applied — issue permanently blocked from dispatch

## Workarounds Applied

Three-step manual release required:
```bash
interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <slug>
gh issue edit <N> --repo <slug> --remove-assignee <user>
gh issue edit <N> --repo <slug> --remove-label origin:interactive --add-label origin:worker
```

## Context

Observed in a managed private repo. An interactive session created two issues in one flow: a parent-task (interactive) and an auto-dispatch sibling (cascade-unlock). The agent called `claim` on both per the AGENTS.md mandate ("MUST immediately call claim when engaging with a GitHub issue"). The mandate is correct for the parent-task but overly broad for the auto-dispatch sibling.

Contributing factor: AGENTS.md line 126 ("Implementing a `#auto-dispatch` task interactively") correctly distinguishes "implementing" from "creating," but the broader interactive claim mandate (line 193) uses "engaging with" which the agent interpreted as including creation-only.

## Environment

- aidevops 3.11.4, Claude Code, Ubuntu 24.04, bash 5.2, gh 2.91.0

title: t2873: comment out OpenCode→Claude Code substitution after empirical A/B verification
body:
## Task

In `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/provider-auth-request.mjs`, the `sanitizeSystemPrompt` function applies a `OpenCode → Claude Code` text substitution to every system-prompt block. Empirical A/B testing against `api.anthropic.com` confirms this substitution is unnecessary. Comment it out (do not delete — keep the line as a comment so it can be restored if Anthropic ever adds name-based detection).

## Why

The substitution was added in the original t1543 OAuth pool plugin commit (2025-09) with the comment "Anthropic server blocks 'OpenCode' string" — but it was never empirically verified. The later thorough investigations found the actual triggers are different:

- t2040 (2026-04-09): XML tags `<directories>`, `<env>`, `<available_skills>` — handled by `TAG_RENAMES`.

## How

```js
// before
let text = item.text.replace(/OpenCode/g, "Claude Code").replace(/opencode/gi, "Claude");

// after
// let text = item.text.replace(/OpenCode/g, "Claude Code").replace(/opencode/gi, "Claude");
let text = item.text;
```

Add a block comment above the change documenting the empirical test, history, cost, and re-enable instructions.

- Module imports cleanly under Node ES modules.

Six independent tests against the live Anthropic API all returned 200 OK with the literal word "OpenCode" in the system prompt at sizes from 380 bytes to 36KB. Test harness lives at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/aidevops/third-party-name-test/`.

title: t2874: structured tag format for knowledge planes (Markdoc-style peer parent)
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
# t2874: structured tag format for knowledge planes (Markdoc-style peer parent)

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: "structured content format markdown tags schema" — no prior aidevops work on this; BaseHub uses Markdoc for similar problem (audited 2026-04-26 in t2840 design session)
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch any `markdoc-*` path or tag-validator surface — greenfield primitive
- [x] File refs verified: pattern source `t2870-brief.md` (peer parent-task), `t2849-brief.md` (P1a kind-aware enrichment — produces tagged content), `t2850-brief.md` (P1c PageIndex — consumes tagged content)
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — architecture-level decomposition; child phases will be `tier:standard`

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-26
- **Session:** Claude Code interactive session
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (per user request — peer parent to t2840)
- **Parent task:** none (this IS a parent)
- **Conversation context:** During t2840 follow-up review, user asked whether BaseHub-style headless content patterns (Markdoc tags, structured fields, schema validation) could apply to our knowledge planes. Analysis concluded: format matters for agent reliability even within a file+git architecture — loose markdown gives no validation, no agent-stable extraction surface, no schema-driven consumers. PageIndex (t2850) already provides the navigation skeleton; Markdoc-style tags provide the inline semantic layer that lifts to navigation metadata. The two compose. Filed as separate parent so MVP scope (t2840) ships first; tag format follows once foundation is live and a real consumer (P1c) is wired to receive tag attributes.

## What

Establishes a Markdoc-compatible tag format as the canonical structured-content layer across all knowledge planes (`_knowledge/`, `_cases/`, `_projects/`, `_performance/`, `_feedback/`, `_campaigns/`, `_inbox/`). Tags declare semantic regions (sensitivity stamps, citations, case-attach edges, provenance, redaction, draft status) inside otherwise-prose markdown files. A schema-driven validator runs at write time (pre-commit + CLI), an extractor produces a tag-position JSON sidecar for agent consumption, and existing planes consume tag attributes via dedicated read paths (PageIndex node metadata, retrieval filters, draft provenance footers).

**This is a planning-only parent.** No code changes ship from this issue directly — children file individual implementation tasks once t2840 MVP foundation is live (P0a/P0b/P0c minimum + P1a/P1c so there's a real consumer to wire).

## Why

Loose markdown gives the agent no reliable surface for:

- **Sensitivity stamps inline** — today sensitivity lives in `meta.json`; a region within a longer document inherits the file-level stamp. Markdoc tags let a single source carry multiple sensitivity scopes (a public document quoting one privileged paragraph), which the routing layer (t2847) can honour exactly.
- **Citation graph** — drafts need to cite source IDs verbatim with confidence + page anchors. Today this is a regex pass over text. Markdoc `{% citation %}` blocks make citations structurally explicit, parser-friendly, and round-trippable.
- **Case-attach edges** — content that lives in `_knowledge/` but is relevant to one or more cases needs an edge structure that survives renames and forks. Tag attributes give that.
- **Schema enforcement at write time** — a worker drafting a `case chase` template can be blocked at commit if the template lacks `{% draft-status status="..." /%}` and `{% provenance %}`. No retroactive cleanup; bad tags never enter the corpus.
- **Indexing-by-tag** — t2850 PageIndex already builds a per-document tree with summaries; tag attributes promote to per-node metadata so retrieval can filter by `sensitivity=privileged AND case=acme-dispute` without re-reading bodies.
- **Format migration** — when the schema evolves (new sensitivity tier, new tag), a migration tool can rewrite tag attributes deterministically. With loose markdown, migration is regex + human review.

PageIndex (t2850) is the navigation skeleton; Markdoc tags are the inline semantic labels. Together they give the agent a structured queryable corpus without leaving file+git. Without this layer, every consumer reinvents extraction (and they will all do it differently).

**Concrete trigger:** P1a (t2849) currently emits `text.txt + meta.json`. Without a tag format, structured fields extracted at ingestion time (sender, receipt date, sensitivity classification) are split between the prose body (extracted text) and the sidecar JSON — two sources of truth, drift-prone. With tag format, P1a emits one canonical `source.md` with tags for what was extracted, and `meta.json` becomes a slim sidecar for non-tag-suitable fields (file hash, byte size, blob pointer).

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking` — this is decomposition design. Children will be `tier:standard` (validators, extractors, schema migrations are mechanical once shape is set).

## PR Conventions

This is a parent-task. Initial planning PR uses `For #` keyword (planning only). Children's PRs use `For #THIS-ISSUE` until the final phase, which uses `Closes #THIS-ISSUE`.

## Phases

Decomposition planned as 7 phases. Children file when t2840 MVP exits (specifically: P0a + P0b + P0c + P1a + P1c must be merged so there is a real producer-consumer pair to wire tags through).

- **Phase 1 — tag schema** — define namespace and JSON schemas under `.agents/tools/markdoc/schemas/`. Initial set: `sensitivity`, `provenance`, `case-attach`, `citation`, `redaction`, `draft-status`, `link`. Each schema declares attributes (required + optional + types), scope rules (file / section / inline), and example.
- **Phase 2 — validator** — `scripts/markdoc-validate.sh validate <file>` — parses tagged file, checks well-formed tags + schema conformance + scope rules; pre-commit hook integration; CI gate. Detailed error context (file:line:column + which schema rule failed).
- **Phase 3 — extractor** — `scripts/markdoc-extract.sh extract <file>` — outputs tag-stripped plain text + JSON sidecar of `[{tag, attrs, scope, char_start, char_end}, ...]`. Optional `--tree` produces hierarchical tag tree (file scope → section scope → leaf scope) for structural traversal.
- **Phase 4 — migration** — port P0a (t2843) `meta.json + text.txt` layout onto `source.md` (tagged) + slim `meta.json`. Backwards-compat reader so existing sources keep working until migrated.
- **Phase 5 — PageIndex consumer** — wire P1c (t2850) to lift Markdoc tag attributes into PageIndex node `metadata`. Tag scope rules: file-level → root + all descendants; section-level → that node + descendants; inline → leaf node attribute. Citation tags become tree-level cross-references.
- **Phase 6 — retrieval consumer** — wire P5/P6 retrieval (`aidevops case draft`, `aidevops knowledge search`) to filter and rank by tag attributes (e.g. `--sensitivity privileged --case acme-dispute`).
- **Phase 7 — tooling** — IDE LSP for tag autocomplete + schema validation in editor; gh comment renderer that pretty-prints or strips tags when reproducing source content in PR/issue threads.

Children NOT pre-filed — files when t2840 MVP exits and the producer-consumer pair (P1a → P1c) is live. Each phase will get its own brief + GH issue + auto-dispatch tag at that point. This parent stays open as a tracker.

## Out of Scope (for this parent)

- Markdoc runtime adoption (the JS library) — we want the syntax + schema discipline, not the JS dependency. Validator + extractor are shell + jq + python.
- Rich rendering (HTML, MDX, React components) — content stays as markdown for human + agent consumption; rendering is a phase 7 niche concern.
- Tag-namespace versioning + deprecation semantics — handled when first breaking schema change lands; not pre-emptive.
- Cross-runtime tag discovery (Gitea, GitLab) — relies on platform abstraction in t2840 P0b, which already exists in MVP.
- Bidirectional sync with structured-content CMSes (BaseHub, Sanity, Storyblok) — separate parent if ever needed.

## Cross-Plane Connections

- `_knowledge/sources/<id>/source.md` (post-migration) — tagged canonical text; `meta.json` slimmed to non-tag fields
- `_cases/<id>/timeline/*.md` — tagged with `{% case-attach %}`, `{% citation %}`, `{% draft-status %}`
- `_inbox/staging/*.md` — provisional `{% sensitivity tier="unverified" /%}` until P2c triage reclassifies
- `_campaigns/active/<id>/creative/*.md` — tagged with `{% sensitivity tier="competitive" /%}`, `{% draft-status %}`, `{% link target="..." kind="brand-asset" /%}`
- `_feedback/captures/*.md` — tagged with `{% provenance %}`, `{% sensitivity %}` so retention policy can scope by tag

## How (decomposition only — no code changes)

This parent ships:

- Decomposition plan in this brief
- Phase headings in the issue body so the auto-decomposer recognises it as decomposed
- Cross-references to t2840 dependencies (P0a/P1a/P1c specifically) so each child knows its prerequisites

Phase implementation follows once t2840 MVP foundation lands and the producer-consumer pair (t2849 + t2850) is live.

### Files Scope

- `todo/tasks/t2874-brief.md` (this file — for the planning PR)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Issue filed with `parent-task` label, `## Phases` heading, `no-auto-dispatch` label.
- [ ] Brief committed at `todo/tasks/t2874-brief.md`.
- [ ] TODO entry with `ref:GH#NNN`.
- [ ] Phase children NOT yet filed (deliberate — wait for t2840 MVP exit + P1a/P1c live).
- [ ] Cross-references to t2849 (P1a producer) and t2850 (P1c consumer) documented in brief.
- [ ] Forward-compat hooks documented in t2849 + t2850 briefs (so when phase 4 + phase 5 land, the wiring already has named extension points).

## Context & Decisions

- **Why a separate parent vs P-phase of t2840:** scope discipline. t2840 is already 20 children + a peer parent (t2870 campaigns). Folding tag format into t2840 would push delivery further out and re-open scope on already-filed children. Cleaner to ship MVP loose-markdown, then upgrade to structured tags as v2 once consumers exist.
- **Why filed now if not implemented now:** architectural intent is fragile and forward-compat hooks need to be designed in BEFORE producers/consumers freeze their interface. Documenting tag-aware extension points in t2849 (producer) and t2850 (consumer) now keeps them additive when phase 4 + phase 5 land.
- **Why phases not pre-filed:** children would block on t2840 MVP exit + age in backlog. File them when foundation lands and prerequisites (P1a + P1c live) are concrete.
- **Why Markdoc syntax specifically vs invented tags:** Markdoc has well-documented `{% tag attr="value" %}` and `{% /tag %}` block grammar with mature parsers (JS, Ruby), MIT licence, and stable schema-validation semantics. Adopting the syntax convention costs nothing and lets us inherit the parsing precedent without taking on the JS runtime. Inventing a new format costs design + parser + documentation.
- **Why `source.md + meta.json` not single-file `.bshb`-style:** BaseHub uses single-file-per-item (binary + metadata + content together). That fights our binary/text-separation design (large blobs route to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/knowledge-blobs/`, binary diffs are git-hostile). Directory-per-source with `source.md` + `meta.json` + `extracted.json` + `tree.json` keeps each artefact diff-friendly and tool-friendly.
- **Why validator-first not extractor-first:** extractor without validator means malformed tags silently produce empty extractions (RAG looks like it works but has missing data). Validator-first means malformed tags fail loudly at write time; extractor only sees well-formed input.
- **Why migration is its own phase:** a flag-day migration of all sources is risky on a corpus we haven't sized yet. Phase 4 ships migration tooling + a backwards-compat reader; sources migrate incrementally as they're re-touched, with a deadline tracked in TODO.

## Relevant Files

- `t2840-brief.md` — MVP foundation; tag format builds on its directory contract (`_knowledge/sources/<id>/`)
- `t2843-brief.md` (P0a directory contract) — current `meta.json + text.txt` layout that phase 4 migrates
- `t2849-brief.md` (P1a kind-aware enrichment) — producer; phase 4 makes it emit `source.md` instead of (or alongside) `text.txt`
- `t2850-brief.md` (P1c PageIndex tree) — consumer; phase 5 makes node `metadata` carry tag attributes
- `t2870-brief.md` (campaigns peer parent) — same peer-parent shape (parent-task, no-auto-dispatch, ## Phases, children-not-pre-filed)
- `.agents/tools/document/extraction-schemas/10-classification.md` — taxonomy reference; tag schemas may align with kind-classification

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** t2840 MVP foundation (specifically t2843 + t2849 + t2850 must merge — directory contract + producer + consumer)
- **Blocks:** none directly (post-MVP work; existing planes work fine with loose markdown until phase 4 migrates them)
- **External:** none in MVP; Markdoc syntax reference: <https://markdoc.dev/> (canonical spec, MIT)

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| This planning PR | ~30m | brief + issue + TODO |
| Future Phase 1-7 children | TBD | sized when filed (estimate ~30-40h total across 7 phases — schema design dominates phase 1, validator + extractor ~6-8h each, migration is the big one at ~8-12h) |
| **Planning total** | **~30m** | |

title: bug: reusable workflow caller templates missing permissions block — startup_failure on repos with default_workflow_permissions: read
body:
## Description

The canonical caller templates (`issue-sync-caller.yml`, `review-bot-gate-caller.yml`) shipped by the reusable workflow migration (t2770, PR #20664) do not include a `permissions:` block. This causes `startup_failure` (zero jobs, immediate rejection) on any downstream repo whose `default_workflow_permissions` is set to `"read"` — the GitHub-recommended restrictive default.

The aidevops self-caller also lacks a `permissions:` block, but works because the aidevops repo presumably uses the permissive `"write"` default. The gap was not caught because the three downstream repos identified for migration (<webapp>, really-simple-ssl-multisite, compressx-multisite) had not yet been migrated when the first external consumer hit it.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**: Any event trigger (issues, pull_request, push, workflow_dispatch) on the caller workflow.

**Actual output**: GitHub Actions `startup_failure`, `conclusion: startup_failure`, zero jobs created. The run completes in <1 second.

```
$ gh run view <id> --json conclusion,jobs
{"conclusion":"startup_failure","jobs":[]}
```

**Expected output**: Jobs created and routed to the reusable workflow.

**Causal code**:

`.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml` — no `permissions:` key at workflow or job level. Same gap in `review-bot-gate-caller.yml`.

**Root cause chain**:

1. Downstream repo has `default_workflow_permissions: "read"` (the secure default GitHub recommends).
2. Caller workflow declares no `permissions:` → inherits repo default → GITHUB_TOKEN ceiling is read-only.
3. Reusable workflow's per-job `permissions:` declarations (e.g. `contents: write`, `issues: write`) cannot exceed the caller's ceiling.
4. GitHub validates this at startup and refuses to create the jobs.

**Why the old inline workflow worked**: Per-job `permissions:` in a single-file workflow override the repo default directly. The reusable workflow architecture changes the trust model — the CALLER sets the ceiling, the CALLEE's permissions are capped.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a repo with `default_workflow_permissions: "read"` (check via `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow --jq .default_workflow_permissions`).
2. Run `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` to install the canonical caller template.
3. Trigger any event (open an issue, push to TODO.md, manual workflow_dispatch).
4. Observe `startup_failure` with zero jobs.

## Suggested Fix

Add a `permissions:` block to both caller templates covering the union of their reusable workflow's job-level permissions:

**`issue-sync-caller.yml`**:
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
```

**`review-bot-gate-caller.yml`**:
```yaml
permissions:
  pull-requests: read
  contents: read
  statuses: read
```

The `review-bot-gate` case only needs read permissions, but should still declare them explicitly so it's not silently capped by a restrictive default.

Also update `sync-workflows-helper.sh` to inject the permissions block when generating callers, and add a test to `test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh` that validates every caller template includes a `permissions:` block.

## Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml` — add `permissions:` block
- EDIT: `.agents/templates/workflows/review-bot-gate-caller.yml` — add `permissions:` block
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` — inject permissions when generating callers (if not already template-driven)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh` — add invariant: every caller template declares `permissions:`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/reusable-workflows.md` — document the `default_workflow_permissions` interaction

## Workarounds Applied

Manually added a `permissions:` block to the downstream repo's `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml`. Verified the fix resolves the startup_failure.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.11.5
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.91.0 (2026-04-22)

title: t2876: gh PATH shim: privacy-scan layer to fail-closed on private-slug references when posting to public repos
body:
Block private-repo-name leaks at the systemic layer.

## Why
Today's session redacted 70+ historical issues/PRs in marcusquinn/aidevops that contained the private repo basename 'awardsapp'. Source: prose typed by maintainer/workers when describing real bugs. The existing privacy-guard-pre-push.sh only covers git push, not gh API calls (gh issue/pr create|comment|edit), so the gap allows arbitrary leaks every time a session writes to a public repo.

## What
Add a privacy-scan layer to .agents/scripts/gh (the PATH shim) that:
1. Detects when the gh subcommand is a write to a public repo (issue/pr create/comment/edit, or gh api POST/PATCH to issues/comments/pulls).
2. Extracts --body / --body-file / --title content (and -f body= for gh api).
3. Scans content against private slugs from privacy_enumerate_private_slugs (already exists).
4. Fail-closed with a mentoring error message when a private slug is detected.
5. Bypass via AIDEVOPS_GH_PRIVACY_BYPASS=1 with audit log.
6. Fail-open on missing helper / unauthenticated gh / unparseable args.

## How
- Add privacy_scan_text(content, slugs_file) function to privacy-guard-helper.sh — scans free-form text (vs the existing privacy_scan_diff which scans git diffs). Match full slug forms (owner/basename) always; match bare basenames only when length ≥ 6 chars to limit false positives.
- Extend .agents/scripts/gh to gate write operations through privacy_scan_text after signature footer injection. Use privacy_is_target_public to determine if the target is public-and-needs-protection.
- Add tests: .agents/tests/test-privacy-guard-shim.sh — covers (a) public + private slug → block, (b) public + alias → allow, (c) private target → skip, (d) bypass env var → skip with audit, (e) missing helper → fail-open.

## Acceptance
- gh issue create --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --body 'mentions awardsapp' → blocked, exit 1, error message
- gh issue create --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --body 'mentions <webapp>' → allowed
- gh issue create --repo private/repo --body 'mentions awardsapp' → allowed (private target)
- AIDEVOPS_GH_PRIVACY_BYPASS=1 gh issue create … 'awardsapp' → allowed with stderr audit notice
- All existing shim tests still pass (signature footer behaviour unchanged)
- Tests pass: bash .agents/tests/test-privacy-guard-shim.sh

title: fix(cli): aidevops issue subcommand missing from dispatch table (regression of #19042)
body:
## Description

`aidevops issue release <N> <slug>` (and `claim`, `status`, `scan-stale`) are documented in `prompts/build.txt` and `AGENTS.md` as the canonical CLI fallback for releasing stale interactive claims, but the `issue)` case is not present in the dispatch table at `aidevops.sh:1731-1779`. Calling any `aidevops issue ...` subcommand falls through to the `*)` catch-all (line 1773), which prints `Unknown command: issue` followed by the full help text — including the bottom "Installation:" block, which can be mistaken for unrelated promo output if the error message scrolls off the visible terminal.

This is a regression of #19042 (t2105). That issue was filed 2026-04-15 with the exact two-line fix specified, and was auto-closed by PRs #19052 and #19057. **Neither of those PRs touched `aidevops.sh`** — both modified `pulse-cleanup.sh` and `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` only. The fix described in the t2105 brief has never landed on `aidevops.sh` (verified via `git log -S "interactive-session-helper.sh" -- aidevops.sh` returning empty across all branches).

## Expected Behavior

`aidevops issue <subcommand> ...` reaches `interactive-session-helper.sh <subcommand> ...` via the same `_dispatch_helper` plumbing that 30+ other subcommands use. Specifically:

- `aidevops issue release <N> <owner>/<repo>` → `[interactive-session] release: #N → status:available`
- `aidevops issue claim <N> <owner>/<repo>` → claim stamp + status:in-review applied
- `aidevops issue status [<N>]` → helper status output
- `aidevops issue scan-stale` → helper's full stale-claim report

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
aidevops issue release <NNNN> <owner>/<private-repo>
```

**Actual output** (truncated at 10 lines, but tail of full output is the framework "Installation:" banner):

```
[ERROR] Unknown command: issue

AI DevOps Framework CLI v3.11.5

Usage: aidevops <command> [options]

Commands:
  init [features]    Initialize aidevops in current project
  init-routines      Scaffold private routines repo (--org <name> | --local)
  upgrade-planning   Upgrade TODO.md/PLANS.md to latest templates
```

**Expected output**:

```
[interactive-session] release: #<NNNN> → status:available
```

**Causal code** — `aidevops.sh` dispatch table (lines 1755-1779), showing `approve)` present at line 1757 but no `issue)` case before the `*)` fallthrough at line 1773:

```bash
secret | secrets) _dispatch_helper "secret-helper.sh" "secret-helper.sh" "$@" ;;
approve) _dispatch_helper "approval-helper.sh" "approval-helper.sh" "$@" ;;
signing) _dispatch_helper "signing-setup.sh" "signing-setup.sh" "$@" ;;
# ... no issue) case anywhere in the table ...
*)
    print_error "Unknown command: $command"
    echo ""
    cmd_help
    exit 1
    ;;
```

Help text at `aidevops.sh:1383` similarly shows `approve <cmd>` but no `issue <cmd>` line.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. From any session with stale interactive claims (or any working aidevops install): `aidevops issue release 9999 owner/repo` (issue number doesn't need to exist — the dispatch fails before any GitHub call).
2. Observe `[ERROR] Unknown command: issue` followed by full help text.
3. Confirm dispatch table absence: `grep -n "issue)" ~/Git/aidevops/aidevops.sh` returns empty.
4. Confirm the helper itself works: `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh release 9999 owner/repo` reaches the correct path (will report "not found" on a non-existent issue, but proves the helper is functional and only the CLI plumbing is missing).

## Workarounds Applied

In the observing session, after `aidevops issue release <N>` failed silently for two stale claims, I called the helper directly:

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh release <N> <owner>/<repo>
```

Both releases succeeded. The workaround required knowing the helper's path (`.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`) and its argument signature (`<issue> <slug>`), neither of which is discoverable from the CLI's help output.

The `scan-stale` output does suggest `aidevops issue release <N>` as the remediation command — meaning the framework actively guides users to a command that doesn't work.

## Proposed Fix

Same as the original t2105 brief, with line numbers updated for the current (restructured) `aidevops.sh`:

**File 1: `aidevops.sh:1757` — add dispatch case after `approve)`**:

```bash
issue) _dispatch_helper "interactive-session-helper.sh" "interactive-session-helper.sh" "$@" ;;
```

**File 2: `aidevops.sh:1383` — add help line after `approve <cmd>`**:

```bash
echo "  issue <cmd>        Interactive issue ownership (claim/release/status/scan-stale)"
```

`_dispatch_helper` (defined around line 1582) handles path resolution between `$AGENTS_DIR/scripts/` and `$INSTALL_DIR/.agents/scripts/`. The helper already implements all subcommands (claim, release, status, scan-stale per t2056).

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck aidevops.sh
bash aidevops.sh issue 2>&1 | grep -v "Unknown command"  # should reach helper, not fallthrough
bash aidevops.sh issue release 9999 owner/repo            # should reach helper output, not CLI help banner
bash aidevops.sh help | grep "issue <cmd>"                # should match
```

## Tier

`tier:simple` — same shape as the original t2105: 2 files, exact verbatim line additions, no design. **Caveat**: t2105 was also `tier:simple` and was auto-closed by PRs that didn't touch the claimed file. Recommend the assigned worker run the verification commands above before declaring done; this is the cheapest defense against a repeat of the original false-closure.

## Additional Context

- **Original issue**: #19042 (t2105) closed 2026-04-15.
- **PRs that closed #19042 without delivering the fix**: #19052 (`pulse-cleanup.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`) and #19057 (`pulse-cleanup.sh`). Neither modified `aidevops.sh`.
- **Sibling issue worth filing separately**: the auto-close mechanism (PR body keyword → issue close) does not validate that the closing PR's diff overlaps the files claimed in the closed issue's brief. This is a class of false-closure that produces phantom-fixed bugs. Cheapest validation gate: when `_extract_linked_issue` matches a closing keyword on a PR merge, also verify the PR's `files[].path` includes at least one path mentioned in the closed issue's body (or at least one path under a directory mentioned in the brief). Skip when the issue body has no file references.
- **Documentation that references the broken command**: `prompts/build.txt` "Interactive issue ownership", `AGENTS.md` Git Workflow section, `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale` runtime output.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.11.5
- Latest: 3.11.5 (current)
- Install method: symlink at `~/.local/bin/aidevops` → `~/Git/aidevops/aidevops.sh`
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21
- gh CLI: 2.91.0

title: t2877: parse parent-task body cross-phase dependency declarations into blocked-by markers
body:
## What

A new pulse stage that parses prose phase-ordering declarations from parent-task issue bodies and emits the equivalent `blocked-by:tNNN` markers in TODO.md (and corresponding GitHub `blockedByIssue` relationships). Closes the gap surfaced during t2875 manual backfill.

## Why

Parent-task authors naturally encode cross-phase dependencies as narrative prose in the issue body (e.g., t2840/#20892 had 8 dependency lines like `P1 children blocked by P0a + P0b`). The framework's relationship sync (issue-sync-relationships.sh) only reads explicit `blocked-by:tNNN` from TODO.md, so prose declarations never reach GitHub. Result: rich dependency graphs declared in parent bodies but invisible to GitHub Projects, the issues UI, and external tooling.

t2875 manually backfilled 15 entries (42 blocked-by edges) for the t2840 decomposition. Automating closes the gap permanently.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh
- .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-parent-phase-dep-parser.sh

### Approach

1. Add `_parse_parent_phase_deps <issue-body>` helper to issue-sync-relationships.sh that locates lines matching `P[0-9.]+[a-z]? (children|blocked) by ...`, extracts phase IDs, resolves each to a child issue number via the parent body's children table.
2. Add a new pulse-issue-reconcile stage (next to the t2838 backfill stage) that calls the parser per open parent-task and emits `blocked-by:` markers + GraphQL `addBlockedByRelationship`. Rate-limited via state file mirroring t2838 pattern.
3. Tests for prose edge cases, table extraction, idempotency, no-declarations case.

### Verification

- New parser tests pass
- Dry-run against #20892 produces 0 net changes (already backfilled)
- End-to-end on a fresh parent decomposition

## Acceptance

- [ ] Parser handles all 8 dependency line shapes from t2840 parent body
- [ ] Idempotent on re-run
- [ ] Rate-limited via state file like t2838
- [ ] Tests cover simple/multi-blocker/sub-phase/transitive cases
- [ ] Verified end-to-end on a fresh decomposition

## Session origin

t2838 → t2875 follow-up. t2838 shipped GraphQL sub-issue backfill; t2875 added cross-phase blocked-by markers manually because no parser exists. This task automates t2875's work.

title: bug: canonical issue-sync caller template uses `secrets: inherit` — fails to pass SYNC_PAT to reusable workflow on cross-account consumers
body:
## Description

The canonical issue-sync caller template at `.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml` uses `secrets: inherit` to pass `SYNC_PAT` to the reusable workflow. For consumers in a **different account/org from `marcusquinn`** (which is every downstream user — this is a public framework), `secrets.SYNC_PAT` evaluates to an empty string inside the reusable workflow at runtime, even when the secret is correctly set on the caller repo and the reusable workflow declares it as an optional secret input.

Result: every push/issue/PR-close event triggers an issue-sync run that warns "SYNC_PAT not set", falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and is rejected by branch protection with `GH006: Protected branch update failed`. Operators receive a cascade of run-failure emails and assume their secret is misconfigured — re-set it, see the same failure, file a ticket. The framework's own `marcusquinn/aidevops` repo is the only one where this works, because there it's same-repo `secrets: inherit`.

## Sister-bug context

This surfaced immediately after #20967 (caller template missing `permissions:` block) was fixed via PR #2087 in `robstiles/qs-agency`. The `permissions:` fix made the workflow actually start; this bug is what it now fails on. Both bugs share the same root cause class: the canonical caller template was authored against the framework's own self-test scenario (`marcusquinn/aidevops` calling itself) and assumes co-located, same-account semantics that don't hold for downstream consumers.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (any push to `TODO.md` on a downstream consumer repo, or manual dispatch):

```
gh workflow run "Issue Sync - Bi-directional TODO.md ↔ GitHub Issues" --repo robstiles/qs-agency -f command=push
```

**Actual output** (from `gh run view <id> --log-failed`):

```
##[warning]SYNC_PAT secret is not set — TODO.md auto-sync push will be rejected by branch protection (GH006).
##[warning]Fix: gh secret set SYNC_PAT --repo robstiles/qs-agency --body "<FINE_GRAINED_PAT>" (Contents: Read and write)
...
remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main.
remote: 
remote: - Required status check "review-bot-gate" is expected.
To https://github.com/robstiles/qs-agency
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch hook declined)
error: failed to push some refs to 'https://github.com/robstiles/qs-agency'
All push attempts failed
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

**Expected output**: the push step uses `SYNC_PAT` (which IS set on the repo), bypasses branch protection via `enforce_admins: false`, and the TODO.md update lands on `main`.

**Causal evidence** that the secret IS set but unreachable:

- `gh secret list --repo robstiles/qs-agency` returns `SYNC_PAT  2026-04-19T22:06:10Z` (set, value present, not expired in storage)
- The runtime `Check SYNC_PAT visibility` step computes `SYNC_PAT_PRESENT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT != '' && 'true' || '' }}` and consistently logs `SYNC_PAT_PRESENT: ` (empty) across every job (push-triggered, issue-triggered, manual `workflow_dispatch`)
- All 15+ touchpoints to `secrets.SYNC_PAT` inside `issue-sync-reusable.yml` (lines 71, 91, 117, 125, 140, 148, 178, 217, 233, 252, 300, 315, 332, 396, 789, 827) receive empty
- The user's prior local `issue-sync.yml` (pre-migration, t237 / commit `4b54bcb` in `robstiles/qs-agency`) had the **same** `${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` expression INLINE in the same repo and worked correctly. The migration to the reusable-workflow pattern (PR #2083, generated by `aidevops sync-workflows --apply`) is when the secret resolution broke.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a repo NOT in the `marcusquinn` org/account, set `SYNC_PAT` as a repo secret (`gh secret set SYNC_PAT --repo <owner>/<repo>`)
2. Configure classic branch protection on `main` with at least one required status check, `enforce_admins: false`
3. Run `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` to install the canonical caller template (or use the equivalent `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` from `.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml`)
4. Push a change to `TODO.md`
5. Observe: workflow runs, `SYNC_PAT_PRESENT` logs as empty, push step fails with GH006

## Why this matters

1. **Affects every downstream consumer.** The framework's own `marcusquinn/aidevops` repo is the only one where `secrets: inherit` works for this reusable workflow — because there it's same-repo. Every other consumer using the canonical template (per `aidevops check-workflows`) is silently broken.

2. **Misleading error message.** The reusable workflow's existing `Check SYNC_PAT visibility` step warns "SYNC_PAT secret is not set" — but in this scenario the secret IS set on the caller. Operators chase a phantom misconfiguration instead of the actual cross-account inherit limitation.

3. **`aidevops sync-workflows` will overwrite local fixes.** A consumer who manually patches their caller to use explicit `secrets: SYNC_PAT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT }}` will have it stomped on the next `sync-workflows --apply` (which is also auto-suggested by `aidevops update`).

4. **Sister-bug pattern continues.** This is the second instance in 24 hours where the canonical caller template's framework-self-test assumption breaks for downstream consumers (see #20967). The class of bug deserves a structural mitigation, not just a per-bug patch.

## Considerations for the fix

The framework devs to choose the path. Some options to consider — these are not exhaustive:

**Option A: switch the canonical template to explicit secret pass-through**

```yaml
jobs:
  sync:
    uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml@main
    secrets:
      SYNC_PAT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT }}
    with:
      command: ${{ inputs.command || '' }}
```

- Works for cross-account/cross-org consumers
- Requires the template to enumerate every secret the reusable workflow declares; adding a new optional secret upstream becomes a breaking change for callers (they need to resync)
- `secrets:` and `secrets: inherit` cannot be mixed in the same job — choosing this means committing to explicit enumeration forever

**Option B: keep `secrets: inherit` but document the cross-account limitation**

- Document in `reference/reusable-workflows.md` that `secrets: inherit` requires same-org/same-enterprise membership
- Suggest consumers in different orgs use a forked / vendored copy of the reusable workflow
- Doesn't fix the bug; just shifts the burden

**Option C: better pre-flight diagnostic**

- The reusable workflow's existing "SYNC_PAT not set" warning is wrong in this scenario (the secret IS set on the caller, just not reaching the called workflow)
- Detect the cross-account case (caller-side secret present indicator vs called-side empty) and emit a more actionable warning naming the inherit limitation
- Doesn't fix the bug, but reduces wasted-triage cost
- Would require the caller template to do a pre-flight visibility check before calling the reusable workflow — adds template surface area

**Option D: investigate whether GitHub Actions has changed `secrets: inherit` semantics**

- Worth confirming the actual current GitHub Actions behavior by reading current docs and running a controlled cross-org test before assuming the limitation is the cause
- Possibility: the limitation is real per docs, OR there's something specific to how the framework's reusable workflow declares the secret that's interacting with inherit (e.g., a quirk in how `required: false` is handled)
- A 30-min controlled test would confirm or rule this out before committing to Option A's enumeration tax

## Workarounds Applied

In the observing session (`robstiles/qs-agency`), no workaround has been applied yet — the user wanted the upstream issue filed first so the canonical fix lands in the framework rather than drifting locally. Candidate consumer-side workaround (subject to being stomped by next `sync-workflows --apply`):

```yaml
jobs:
  sync:
    uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml@main
    secrets:
      SYNC_PAT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT }}
    with:
      command: ${{ inputs.command || '' }}
```

## Cross-references

- Sister bug **#20967** (caller template missing `permissions:` block) — same template, same root cause class (framework self-test passes, downstream broken)
- Prior framework SYNC_PAT work: t2048 (#18643, fine-grained PAT path), t2166 (#19488, extend SYNC_PAT to all four jobs), t2696 (#20324, extract visibility step), t2806 (#20745, rulesets-based protection detection)
- Workflow drift system: t2778 (`aidevops check-workflows`), t2779 (`aidevops sync-workflows`) — the canonical template is what consumers will keep getting reset to
- Live reproduction case: `robstiles/qs-agency` (secret set, workflow runs, push fails — available for verification of any candidate fix)

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml` — canonical caller template (the file to fix)
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` — reusable workflow declaring the secret input (15+ touchpoints to `secrets.SYNC_PAT`)
- `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh` (or wherever `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` lives) — needs to ship the corrected template

## Acceptance criteria

1. Canonical caller template passes `SYNC_PAT` in a way that works for cross-account/cross-org consumers
2. `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` on a downstream consumer (different account from `marcusquinn`) produces a caller that successfully resolves `secrets.SYNC_PAT` inside the reusable workflow at runtime
3. Decision documented (in `reference/reusable-workflows.md` or equivalent) on `secrets: inherit` vs explicit pass-through and why
4. Diagnostic message in the reusable workflow updated so it doesn't claim "SYNC_PAT not set" when the actual issue is cross-account inherit failure
5. Regression test or guidance that catches the next "framework self-test passes, downstream broken" instance of this class

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.11.5
- **Latest version**: 3.11.5
- **AI Assistant**: Claude Code
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Observing repo**: robstiles/qs-agency (main)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.91.0

title: test-interactive-session-claim: t2148 stub fixtures missing labels field after GH#20048 filter
body:
## Description

Three t2148 stampless-primitive tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh` fail on `origin/main` because the test stub's `STUB_ISSUE_LIST_JSON` fixtures are missing a `labels` field. After GH#20048 added `_filter_non_task_issues` to `_isc_list_stampless_interactive_claims` (interactive-session-helper.sh:262), the function jq-filters every issue through `.labels | map(.name) | any(. as $n | $ntl[] | . == $n) | not` — which errors on `null` labels and silently returns `[]` via the `|| echo "[]"` fallback.

Surfaced during PR #20977 verification. Failures pre-exist; not introduced by that PR.

## Reproducer

```bash
cd ~/Git/aidevops
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh 2>&1 | grep "t2148"
```

**Actual output:**

```
FAIL t2148: stampless primitive detects zombie claims (positive case) (rc=0, rows=)
FAIL t2148: stampless primitive excludes stamped claims (negative case) (rc=0, rows=)
FAIL t2148: scan-stale Phase 1a surfaces stampless claims (rc=0, out=No stale interactive claims.||...|No stampless interactive claims.|...)
```

**Expected:** all three pass.

## Root cause

`_filter_non_task_issues` at `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh:1509-1516` requires every issue object to have a `labels: [{name: "..."}]` shape:

```jq
[.[] | select(.labels | map(.name) | any(. as $n | $ntl[] | . == $n) | not)]
```

When `.labels` is `null` (because the stub omits the field), `null | map(.name)` raises a jq error, the whole expression errors, and the fallback `|| echo "[]"` collapses the array to empty. Downstream the function returns 0 with no stdout — exactly what the failing tests observe.

The test stub in `test-interactive-session-claim.sh:470-473` defines:

```bash
export STUB_ISSUE_LIST_JSON='[
  {"number": 91001, "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
  {"number": 91002, "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
]'
```

No `labels` field. Real `gh issue list ... --json labels` always returns the field, so the filter works in production — only the stub is stale.

## Worker Guidance

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh:470-473` (Test 12 fixture) and `:537` (reset fixture)
  - Add `"labels": []` to each issue object in `STUB_ISSUE_LIST_JSON`. The empty array is sufficient — neither test issue (`91001`, `91002`) needs to carry a non-task label since the test asserts they pass through the filter.
  - Final fixture shape:

    ```bash
    export STUB_ISSUE_LIST_JSON='[
      {"number": 91001, "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z", "labels": []},
      {"number": 91002, "updatedAt": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z", "labels": []}
    ]'
    ```

  - The reset on line 537 (`export STUB_ISSUE_LIST_JSON='[]'`) is already valid — empty top-level array, no objects to update.

### Reference pattern

- **Filter contract**: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers.sh:1509-1516` (`_filter_non_task_issues`) — jq predicate `.labels | map(.name) | ...` requires `labels: [...]` on every input object.
- **`gh issue list --json labels` real-world shape**: each issue object is `{"number": N, "updatedAt": "...", "labels": [{"name": "..."}, ...]}`. Test stubs that mock this endpoint must include the field even when empty.
- **Sibling test that gets it right**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stampless-non-task-filter.sh:7+` — that test's fixture (`FIXTURE_JSON`) already includes proper `labels` arrays on every issue, which is why it passes.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh 2>&1 | tail -10
# Expected: 25 tests run, 0 failed (currently 25 run, 3 failed)
```

## Acceptance

1. All three `t2148:` tests pass.
2. No other test regresses (currently 22 of 25 pass; new total should be 25 of 25).
3. `shellcheck` clean on the modified file.

## Why this matters

The t2148 stampless-primitive scan is the safety net for zombie interactive claims (issues left as `origin:interactive` + self-assigned with no stamp file). When the test silently fails, regressions in the production scan path (e.g. another stub-shape change after GH#20048) won't be caught — the test suite reports green except for these three lines that anyone reading the suite mentally categorises as "known broken". That's exactly the failure mode prompts/build.txt §"Self-modifying tooling test discipline" warns about.

## Surfaced from

PR #20977 (GH#20946 fix) verification. This issue is the follow-up promised in that PR's "Note: 3 pre-existing test failures unrelated to this PR" section.

title: t2879: docs(README): add per-repo platform setup section pointing to /setup-git
body:
## Why

`README.md` has zero mentions of `SYNC_PAT`, `/setup-git`, or per-repo platform setup. Operators following README onboarding (line 197 onwards) discover `/onboarding` but never learn about the per-repo affordance — leaving issue-sync workflow silent failures (TODO sync stops at branch protection, often diagnosed only when the workflow's remediation comment appears).

The canonical explanation already exists at `.agents/aidevops/onboarding.md:35,45-50` ("Scope: Per-Account vs Per-Repo"). The gap is README-only — new users land there first, find no breadcrumb to `/setup-git`, and have to discover it via failure.

This was surfaced during review of #20976 (canonical caller template uses `secrets: inherit`). Even after that bug fix lands, operators need to know *that* per-repo SYNC_PAT exists and *how* to set it up.

## What

Add a "Per-repo platform setup" subsection to `README.md` between the Quick Start (line 150) and the existing Configuration / Onboarding content. Section explains:

- What `SYNC_PAT` does (lets `issue-sync.yml` push TODO.md auto-completion past branch protection)
- Why it's per-repo (GitHub Actions secrets are scoped per-repo; cross-org `secrets: inherit` doesn't work — see #20976)
- How to set it up (run `/setup-git` in your AI assistant after `gh auth login` succeeds)
- When to set it up (after `aidevops init` registers a new repo, or when a SYNC_PAT advisory appears in the session greeting toast)

Should be ~10-20 lines — short, link-heavy, mirrored from the canonical onboarding.md wording.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `README.md` — add new `### Per-repo platform setup` (or `## Per-repo platform setup`) subsection. Insertion point: after the existing Quick Start section ends (around the current "## Configuration" or near line 197 where `/onboarding` is mentioned). Follow the README's existing heading hierarchy.

### Reference content

`.agents/aidevops/onboarding.md` lines 35-50 contains the canonical per-account vs per-repo split — copy/adapt that wording. Don't invent new framing; the onboarding wizard already establishes the mental model.

### Files Scope

- README.md

### Suggested wording outline

```markdown
### Per-repo platform setup

After `aidevops init` registers a new repo, run `/setup-git` in your AI assistant
to apply per-repo platform secrets. Most notably, this sets `SYNC_PAT` — a
GitHub Actions secret that lets `issue-sync.yml` push TODO.md auto-completion
past branch protection.

This is distinct from `/onboarding` (per-account credentials like `gh auth login`):
GitHub Actions secrets are scoped per-repo, so each repo needs its own.

If you skip this step, `issue-sync.yml` will post a remediation comment when it
hits branch protection. Run `/setup-git` to walk through the gap.
```

The bug review surfaced that `/setup-git` and `/onboarding` infrastructure already exists (t2816 / #20812) and onboarding.md correctly documents the per-account vs per-repo split — but README has no breadcrumb, so operators following README never see the affordance. Companion to #20976 (template fix) and the cross-account-inherit detection follow-up.

title: t2880: feat(setup-debt): detect cross-account secrets:inherit pattern in issue-sync.yml
body:
## Why

#20976 fixes the canonical caller template (`.agents/templates/workflows/issue-sync-caller.yml`) to map `SYNC_PAT` explicitly instead of using `secrets: inherit` — which fails silently across org/account boundaries (GitHub policy: `secrets: inherit` only propagates within the same org/enterprise).

Repos that re-run `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` after the fix lands will pick up the corrected template. But repos that don't re-sync still ship the broken pattern — and crucially, this is **invisible to existing tooling**:

- `aidevops check-workflows` only detects drift *from* the canonical template, not bugs *in* the canonical template at the time of caller install
- `setup-debt-helper.sh` currently aggregates `SYNC_PAT-missing` advisories (~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory) — but here `SYNC_PAT` IS set, just unreachable due to the cross-account inherit pattern
- Operators won't know their setup is broken until issue-sync silently fails on a real TODO push

This is a hidden setup debt class that needs explicit detection.

## What

Add a new debt class to `setup-debt-helper.sh` that scans each registered repo's `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` for the cross-account `secrets: inherit` pattern. When found, emit an advisory and surface via `setup-debt-helper.sh summary`. `/setup-git` walks the operator through `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` to remediate.

## How

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/setup-debt-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md
- .agents/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh

### Reference pattern

Existing `_emit_sync_pat_advisory` in `security-posture-helper.sh` (referenced from `setup-debt-helper.sh:8-15` header comment) is the model. Mirror that pattern: emit `~/.aidevops/advisories/cross-account-inherit-<slug-with-dashes>.advisory` with the same dismissal semantics.

`setup-debt-helper.sh` already has `summary`, `list-sync-pat-missing`, and `verify-secret` commands — add parallel `list-cross-account-inherit` and extend `summary` to aggregate both classes.

### Approach

1. **Detector** (`security-posture-helper.sh`): add `_detect_cross_account_inherit(slug)` that:
   - Fetches `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` via `gh api repos/<slug>/contents/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml --jq .content | base64 -d`
   - Returns 0 if file contains BOTH `uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/...` (caller pattern) AND `secrets: inherit` (the broken pattern)
   - Returns 1 if no broken pattern (correctly maps `SYNC_PAT:` explicitly, OR not a marcusquinn/aidevops caller)
   - Returns 2 if file missing or unfetchable (skip silently — not this class's concern)
2. **Advisory writer** (`security-posture-helper.sh`): `_emit_cross_account_inherit_advisory(slug)` writes to `~/.aidevops/advisories/cross-account-inherit-<slug>.advisory` mirroring `_emit_sync_pat_advisory` shape.
3. **Aggregator** (`setup-debt-helper.sh`): add `list-cross-account-inherit` command and extend `summary`'s human/toast/json formats to include the new class. Toast format: `[WARN] N repos need workflow re-sync — run /setup-git`.
4. **Slash command** (`commands/setup-git.md`): add a new step in the walk-through that detects this class and runs `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` (already exists from t2779).
5. **Tests** (`.agents/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh`): create new test file covering:
   - (a) cross-account caller (`uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/...` + `secrets: inherit`) → detected
   - (b) same-account caller (e.g., owner-internal aidevops fork) → NOT detected
   - (c) explicit `secrets: SYNC_PAT: ${{ secrets.SYNC_PAT }}` mapping → NOT detected (post-#20976 shape)
   - (d) missing workflow file → no false positive, exit cleanly
   - (e) summary aggregation reports both `sync-pat-*` and `cross-account-inherit-*` classes

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup-debt-helper.sh .agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh
bash .agents/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh
# Manual smoke against a registered repo:
setup-debt-helper.sh summary
setup-debt-helper.sh list-cross-account-inherit
```

## Acceptance

1. `setup-debt-helper.sh` detects cross-account `secrets: inherit` in `issue-sync.yml` workflows of registered repos
2. Advisory file written to `~/.aidevops/advisories/cross-account-inherit-<slug>.advisory` (with dismissal support via existing `dismissed.txt`)
3. `setup-debt-helper.sh summary` reports the new class alongside `sync-pat-missing`
4. `/setup-git` slash command walks operator through `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` when this class is detected
5. New tests in `.agents/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh` cover the 5 cases above (`bash .agents/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh` passes)
6. Existing setup-debt advisories unaffected (no regression in `sync-pat-*` aggregation)
7. `shellcheck` passes on modified shell scripts
8. Helper NEVER reads, accepts, or emits secret values — only checks for presence/pattern in workflow YAML

## Session Origin

Filed from interactive review of #20976 (canonical caller template uses `secrets: inherit`). The fix in #20976 silently leaves not-yet-resynced repos in the broken state — `aidevops check-workflows` only catches drift *from* the canonical, not bugs *in* the canonical at caller-install time. Companion to #20976 (template fix) and README per-repo setup follow-up.

Blocked-by: #20976 (need the fix to land + `aidevops sync-workflows --apply` flow available before this detector is useful for remediation).

title: t2881: Harden against external scanner-spam reports filed as 'responsible disclosure'
body:
## Task

Decomposition tracker for hardening aidevops against external scanner-spam reports — issues filed by drive-by external authors that mix marketing CTAs (`pip install <product>`) with high-FP scanner output, dressed as "responsible disclosure". Canonical example: this repo's issue #20978 (closed `invalid` / `not planned` 2026-04-26).

## Why

The threat is encountered by every aidevops user with a public repo, not just the maintainer of this one. The triage path discovered for #20978 is reproducible — verify each cited finding against actual code, treat external-domain links as untrusted, refuse install commands sourced from the body — but it is currently undocumented in framework code and undetected by automation.

Three concrete gaps the framework exposes today:

1. The existing prompt-injection YAML pattern store (`.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml`) has 10 categories covering injection attacks (instruction override, role-play, encoding tricks, DNS exfil, etc.) but **no category for unsolicited-disclosure marketing** — install solicitation, false-positive out-clauses, and disclosure marketing footers are not detected.
2. The `triage-review.md` sandboxed agent (no Bash/network) **cannot verify cited file:line evidence** against actual code, so fabricated correlations like the GITHUB_TOKEN→Stripe claim in #20978 would not be caught by the sandboxed path.
3. Build.txt §7 documents instruction-override immunity but **does not explicitly forbid executing install commands, fetching URLs, or contacting emails sourced from non-collaborator issue/PR bodies** — a gap that this incident's CTAs (`pip install pentesterra-devguard`) directly probed.

These three artifacts must ship via `aidevops update` so all framework users benefit. Per-user memory does not scale across the user base — confirmed during triage of #20978.

## How

Decomposition into three child phases (filed separately as sub-issues of this tracker):

### Phase A — Pattern category in YAML store

EDIT: `.agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml` — add a new `unsolicited_disclosure_marketing` category with patterns for install-command solicitation (`pip install`, `npm install`, `curl … | bash`, `brew install`), false-positive out-clauses ("if you believe this is a false positive"), and disclosure marketing footers. Patterns are PCRE-compatible regex per the existing schema. Reference shape: any existing category in the file.

### Phase E — Build.txt rule

EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — extend §7b "Worker scope enforcement" with an explicit rule that workers MUST NOT execute install commands, fetch URLs, or contact emails sourced from non-collaborator issue/PR bodies, even when the body invites it. Reference pattern: existing §7a "Instruction override immunity" prose style.

### Phase C — Structural detector

NEW: `.agents/scripts/external-content-spam-detector.sh` — combines the new pattern category from Phase A with structural checks (author association via `gh api`, single-domain repetition count) and emits a verdict + suggested labels for `needs-maintainer-review`. Depends on Phase A landing first. Reference pattern: `prompt-guard-helper.sh` integration with `content-classifier-helper.sh` for two-tier scoring; helper-script style follows `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`.

### Files Scope

- .agents/configs/prompt-injection-patterns.yaml
- .agents/prompts/build.txt
- .agents/scripts/external-content-spam-detector.sh
- todo/tasks/<task_id>-brief.md (per phase, if needed)

## Acceptance
